# Code Index

## `(root)` — The project root of SE3 (Software Engineering 3.0), a program-as-supervisor framework whose single `se3` Python package provides a Typer CLI, persistent state-machine flow engine, pluggable agent-runner adapters, and an optional daemon/central-server control plane, packaged with Hatchling and surrounded by framework specs (.claude/), bilingual docs and README, utility scripts, a broad pytest/Node test suite, and root configuration (se3.yaml, pyproject.toml). <!--#10c822701a7197d0|07a7c39b2681dbc7-->

### `.gitignore` (text) — Root ignore file using a deny-by-default policy (`/*`) that whitelists specific top-level project entries and SE3 committed artifacts (code-index, charter, issues, version-intents) while excluding runtime state, build/cache output, browser-test libs, and local config overrides. <!--#8be855da3c960c0a|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `LICENSE` (text) — The Apache License 2.0 full legal text under which the project is licensed, defining terms, conditions, and grants for use, reproduction, and distribution of the work. <!--#2f8292753ff1e47a|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `NOTICE` (text) — The project's attribution/copyright NOTICE file, declaring SE3 as copyright 2026 Zhendong Zhang (CRE) and crediting software developed by him. <!--#91852f8ef9e63e30|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `README.md` (markdown) — The project README presenting SE3 (Software Engineering 3.0) as a program-as-supervisor framework — a CLI engine plus persistent state machine and code-first knowledge system (code-index + charter + why-comments) that governs an AI coding agent across sessions and machines — covering its design philosophy, installation, quick-start, operating modes, full command reference, on-disk layout, and licensing. <!--#673898375854fc61|c68bb328c3783ed6-->
- `SE3 — Software Engineering 3.0 Framework` (heading) — Top-level README for SE3, positioning it as a CLI engine, persistent cross-session state machine, and code-first knowledge system (code-index + charter + why-comments) that supervises an AI coding agent until work is finished, with version/license badges and links to the Chinese README. <!--#1bcda1f6d091dda8-->
  - `Design Philosophy` (heading) — Parent heading grouping the rationale behind SE3's program-as-supervisor paradigm. <!--#77e6f8f8921f18d9-->
    - `1. A different paradigm: program-as-supervisor, human out-of-the-loop` (heading) — Argues that SE3's unit of work is a multi-session project task supervised by the engine rather than a human-watched single turn, contrasted in a tool-class table. <!--#c9555f96a940c05d-->
    - `2. The real pain: attention is all you need` (heading) — Frames human attention as the true bottleneck and describes the ideal prompt → discover → fire-and-forget → pick-up session that minimizes it. <!--#44bce7dd4e3df92b-->
    - `3. The four moats that make this paradigm work` (heading) — Lists the four capabilities — cross-session state machine, code-first knowledge system, built-in failure recovery, portable substrate — that in-session tools cannot provide. <!--#0904a695288fd8d5-->
    - `se3 vs Claude Code Dynamic Workflows (complementary, not competing)` (heading) — Distinguishes SE3's cross-session governance from Dynamic Workflows' in-session parallelism and explains how the two compose. <!--#3c9f8941e07f7a20-->
  - `The knowledge system: code-index + charter + why-comments` (heading) — Explains how SE3 replaced the old spec-mirror corpus and its sync governance machine with three code-colocated artifacts. <!--#a37585c7f445f66c-->
    - `The three pieces` (heading) — Describes SE3's three code-first knowledge pillars: code-index (a committed, fingerprinted structure map auto-summarized bottom-up), charter (a slimmed high-altitude spec injected in full every step), and why-comments (colocated intent-only comments maintained as a soft prompt convention). <!--#da8e286de1f7c7c7-->
    - `What actually got better (an honest accounting)` (heading) — Honestly accounts for the refactor's real gains — source of truth back in code, eliminated staleness, collapsed governance surface, explicit knobs, higher failure floor. <!--#6791cf42e2126b06-->
    - `A concrete before/after — and why spec-index could never win this` (heading) — Uses the retired spec_index.py to argue code-index wins on navigation because its source of truth is the code, cashing out the coverage-over-depth bet. <!--#c2fda17f39a3a1c0-->
  - `Installation` (heading) — Pip install instructions for the core CLI and the optional server and browser extras. <!--#131c9eece23a2cbf-->
  - `Quick Start` (heading) — A quickstart walkthrough showing the core commands to initialize a project, optionally run discovery, run/resume a full task flow end-to-end, and navigate the codebase via the code-index map. <!--#fc732be510ce6649-->
    - `Three operating modes` (heading) — Describes the --loop worktree mode, the resident daemon, and the central se3-server web console. <!--#c8f7660b10e8560d-->
      - `Web console authentication` (heading) — Outlines the multi-tenant first-run auth flow: break-glass admin token, login, user creation, and daemon-key binding. <!--#04d11c5004095aab-->
  - `Command Reference` (heading) — Parent heading introducing the full CLI command catalog as of the documented version. <!--#572ee8f7044e277a-->
    - `Top-level commands` (heading) — A reference table of SE3's top-level CLI commands (run, init, code-index, migrate, guardrails, merge, merge-respond, salvage) with their purposes and key flags. <!--#25a76810e5ca6a53-->
    - ``se3 history` — flow history` (heading) — Reference table for the `se3 history` command group, documenting its subcommands for listing flows (`list`), inspecting step-by-step details (`show`), resuming a flow by ID (`restore`), and listing archived flows (`archived`), along with their flags. <!--#3e81db08ca44209a-->
    - ``se3 issue` — project issues` (heading) — Reference table for the `se3 issue` command group, documenting subcommands to list issues (`list`, with `--all` and `--type` filters), render one (`show`), interactively create one (`create`), and reset an in-progress issue back to `open` (`reset`). <!--#33de25e8833392bc-->
    - ``se3 daemon` — resident control plane` (heading) — Reference table for the `se3 daemon` command group, documenting `start` (with `--foreground`, `--server-url`, and `--daemon-key` options), `stop`, and `status` for running and inspecting the resident daemon control plane. <!--#a5d50611985cec9b-->
  - `Directory Layout` (heading) — Documents the on-disk project layout under `se3/`, distinguishing git-tracked artifacts (code-index, charter, issues, prompts, version-rules) from gitignored runtime state and logs. <!--#7cf08ea68bc7e931-->
  - `Navigating the codebase` (heading) — Explains how to use the code-index as the primary navigation tool — drilling from the adaptive root map down to file-level symbols — and how it plus the charter are auto-injected into every flow step. <!--#2f772ef9c876139a-->
  - `Version & License` (heading) — States that the version lives in pyproject.toml and is engine-bumped, the Apache-2.0 license, and points to the changelog. <!--#999f2a2712e62082-->

### `README.zh.md` (markdown) — The Chinese-language README for the SE3 (Software Engineering 3.0) framework, laying out its program-as-supervisor design philosophy, the code-index/charter/why-comments knowledge system, installation and quick-start, the three run modes, a full command reference (v10.8.1), directory layout, and versioning/licensing. <!--#e7029b1d8f83632f|fd226a66f0ab7707-->
- `SE3 — Software Engineering 3.0 框架` (heading) — Title/banner section with version, Python, and license badges plus the tagline positioning SE3 above session-level tools as a persistent CLI engine + state machine + code-first knowledge system. <!--#f6025367ed3a8ad0-->

    - `2. 真正的痛点：attention is all you need` (heading) — Argues the real bottleneck is human attention and lays out the ideal fire-and-forget SE3 session (prompt → discover → walk away → collect deliverable). <!--#86c7cbd54fc3ec35-->
    - `3. 撑起这种范式的四件套护城河` (heading) — Lists the four pillars that make program-as-supervisor viable: cross-session state machine, code-first knowledge system, built-in failure recovery, and provider-neutral portability. <!--#3f4f12c0a105cc57-->
    - `se3 vs Claude Code Dynamic Workflows（互补，而非竞争）` (heading) — Distinguishes SE3 (cross-session project governance) from Dynamic Workflows (in-session parallel orchestration) and frames them as composable rather than competing. <!--#b2a83509c7f8e397-->
  - `知识体系：code-index + charter + why-注释` (heading) — Section introducing how the three colocated, code-as-source-of-truth artifacts replaced the old parallel spec corpus and its anti-drift governance machinery. <!--#8ecfda556e767049-->
    - `三件套` (heading) — Describes SE3's three-part orientation system: code-index (the deterministic, version-controlled structure map with embedded fingerprints), charter (high-altitude project conventions injected into every step), and why-comments (colocated intent notes updated only when the why changes). <!--#53526fd8b0fda6e4-->
    - `真正变好了什么（诚实的账）` (heading) — Honest accounting of the refactor's real gains (source-of-truth returns to code, staleness eliminated, governance surface shrinks, explicit knobs, decoupled charter size, higher failure floor) while conceding semantic accuracy is unchanged. <!--#5501353ee7d43418-->
    - `一个具体的前后对照——以及 spec-index 为何永远赢不了这一局` (heading) — Concrete before/after using the retired spec_index.py to argue code-index wins because its source of truth is the code itself, realizing the coverage-over-depth bet. <!--#20a9bcddeb628963-->

  - `快速上手` (heading) — A quick-start walkthrough showing the core CLI flow: `se3 init`, optional `--discover`, end-to-end `se3 run`, `--resume`, and navigating the codebase via `se3 code-index`. <!--#887ed3499a62e78e-->
    - `三种运行形态` (heading) — Describes the three execution modes—--loop (isolated worktree runs), se3 daemon start (resident supervisor), and se3-server (multi-machine central server). <!--#b7f29278060cfa34-->
      - `网页控制台鉴权` (heading) — Explains the central server's multi-tenant auth onboarding flow: bootstrap break-glass admin token, log in, create users, and issue per-owner daemon keys. <!--#dba033d164603542-->
  - `命令清单` (heading) — Heading introducing the command reference tables for version 10.8.1. <!--#09d18905dc6eff15-->
    - `顶层命令` (heading) — A reference table of SE3's top-level commands (run, init, code-index, migrate, guardrails, merge, merge-respond, salvage) with their purposes and key flags. <!--#6827bb3388ddba70-->
    - ``se3 history` — flow 历史` (heading) — Documents the `se3 history` command group with a table of subcommands (`list`, `show`, `restore`, `archived`) for listing, inspecting, and resuming past flows across active, archived, and history-only storage. <!--#bf47dd27483c9e01-->
    - ``se3 issue` — 项目 issue` (heading) — Documents the `se3 issue` command group with a table of subcommands (`list`, `show`, `create`, `reset`) for browsing, viewing, interactively creating, and reopening project issues. <!--#513bbae758ad378f-->
    - ``se3 daemon` — 常驻控制面` (heading) — Documents the `se3 daemon` command group with a table of subcommands (`start`, `stop`, `status`) for running the resident control-plane daemon, optionally registering it with a central server via `--server-url` / `--daemon-key`. <!--#60ae88b4da414295-->

  - `在代码库里导航` (heading) — Explains how to navigate the codebase top-down via the code-index map, opening source files only for implementation details, and notes the same root map plus charter are injected into every flow step. <!--#097744bdf4edad85-->
  - `版本与许可证` (heading) — States that pyproject.toml is the sole version source (auto-bumped by the engine), the Apache-2.0 license, and points to VERSIONS.md for the changelog. <!--#36724c39513a1cb4-->

### `VERSIONS.md` (markdown) — The SE3 framework's changelog, listing release entries in reverse-chronological order (from 11.22.1 back through earlier versions) with the fixes, features, and behavioral changes shipped in each version. <!--#c1ea3972b6820c35|9edcd8e3c225f14e-->
- `SE3 Framework Version History` (heading) — The top-level title of the SE3 framework's version history changelog, under which individual release entries are listed. <!--#bbd829c99d86a815-->
  - `11.22.1 - 2026-07-13` (heading) — Changelog entry for patch release 11.22.1, a fix for issue #287 restoring worktree-session discovery chat history in the WebUI by rejecting empty/shrinking full-history frames in the server cache, adding a registry-walk fallback in the daemon history read path, merging main-root and worktree-root records for paused worktree flows, guarding the frontend against zero-record deliveries clearing a rendered chat, and adding regression tests. <!--#39e387461ae6115a-->
  - `11.22.0 - 2026-07-13` (heading) — Changelog entry for version 11.22.0, describing the adjudicate step's new isomorphic-surface sweep: an optional `covered_surfaces` field on the ruling schema (validated, persisted to step outputs, and surfaced in the WebUI/CLI confirmation gate) plus a requirement that a single ruling fix both description and plan clauses at once. <!--#46cd183d01473f46-->
  - `11.21.0 - 2026-07-12` (heading) — Changelog entry for release 11.21.0 introducing the extensible i18n framework (zh-CN + en-US locale packs with en-US fallback), localizing all CLI and WebUI user-visible text, defining the CLI/WebUI language resolution and persistence rules, and unifying `language.language` for UI/LLM output while repurposing `language.spec_language` for knowledge assets. <!--#661c629bb52c6a8a-->
  - `11.20.1 - 2026-07-11` (heading) — Patch release (2026-07-11) fixing multi-round worktree discovery chat history visibility by giving daemon history records globally unique stepId#ordinal identities across worktree/main/sidecar files, stabilizing physical-copy selection and server relay/self-heal, hardening WebUI console deduplication, and adding daemon-to-e2e regression tests. <!--#5bb7f9232bfd459e-->
  - `11.20.0 - 2026-07-11` (heading) — Changelog entry for v11.20.0 describing the shift to a self-closing charter_freshness step that proposes, gates, and atomically applies charter.md updates, guarded by anchored-patch checks and an admission gate, plus a new invariant_check hard guard against silent deletion/rewrite of WHY:/INVARIANT: why-comments with an advisory LLM loss channel, read-only flag flips for CHARTER_FRESHNESS, and surfacing of charter diffs and why-comment losses in the summarize step and WebUI. <!--#f31bb66f26b1e1b6-->
  - `11.19.0 - 2026-07-11` (heading) — Release notes for 11.19.0 (2026-07-11): merge_integrate now auto-commits dirty SE3 self-managed state before merging, resolves .next_id/code-index conflicts deterministically, adds a dirty_working_tree failure reason (with file listing and CLI rendering), and fixes _abort_merge to treat a missing MERGE_HEAD as success. <!--#0e71be3ebcfe3b34-->
  - `11.18.0 - 2026-07-11` (heading) — Changelog entry for release 11.18.0 documenting daemon/WebUI traffic-reduction work: lightweight hash-gated status frames, delta HISTORY_INDEX and chat self-heal updates, on-demand REST detail fetching, gzip/permessage-deflate compression, and per-message-type wire byte counters for observability. <!--#16c26b5d3e11d891-->
  - `11.17.2 - 2026-07-10` (heading) — Changelog entry: makes se3 work out of the box by PATH-probing built-in agents (claude, then codex) to build the default agent chain, erroring clearly when none are found while leaving explicitly configured agents fail-loud. <!--#dd7bfdcac139a35e-->
  - `11.17.1 - 2026-07-10` (heading) — Changelog entry: fixes the WebUI self_check report card showing a false green PASSED badge by deriving the issue count from outputs.issues when actionable_count is absent, with neutral wording and front-end regression tests bridged into pytest. <!--#bcb8f2bb3f7f4c3c-->
  - `11.17.0 - 2026-07-10` (heading) — Changelog entry: adds a deterministic conflict-resolver framework that mechanically resolves code-index.md and .next_id merge conflicts before any LLM call, bounds the LLM conflict prompt size, and improves failure reporting after agent rotation. <!--#4998647e2add42ff-->
  - `11.16.0 - 2026-07-10` (heading) — Changelog entry: automatically creates an annotated git tag vX.Y.Z on major/minor releases (patches untagged), covering both normal and --worktree/reconcile commit flows with honest, fail-loud error reporting and re-entry-safe tagging. <!--#ee82f01ad5f41c83-->
  - `11.15.3 - 2026-07-08` (heading) — Changelog entry for release 11.15.3, listing fixes that stop the chat pane freezing during multi-round discovery, keep the commit step's code-index progress card updating in place, and make chat/history rendering self-heal and idempotent by periodically re-pulling flow history, hardening dedup, WS-increment recovery, the server full/incremental latch, and daemon engine.json rewrite detection. <!--#3588f3393ae7ae13-->
  - `11.15.2 - 2026-07-08` (heading) — Changelog entry for release 11.15.2 (2026-07-08) documenting fixes that stop archived roots from producing phantom flow-less '(untitled flow)' cards in the WebUI, with frontend flow_id filtering and new aggregator contract tests. <!--#ca63d45c34cfd6a5-->
  - `11.15.1 - 2026-07-08` (heading) — Changelog entry for release 11.15.1 recording the fix that makes commit prefixes, work-summary Type, and version-analyze output show the real analyze-inferred task type instead of the 'discovery' run mode, via a persisted analyzed_type and a single effective_task_type resolution source. <!--#974c0b1ae7192d2c-->
  - `11.15.0 - 2026-07-08` (heading) — Changelog entry for release 11.15.0 documenting the addition of a no-op `-n`/`--line-number` flag to `se3 code-index search` for grep compatibility, with preserved existing flag semantics, help-text documentation, and tests. <!--#5a33231d05871736-->
  - `11.14.0 - 2026-07-07` (heading) — Changelog entry for release 11.14.0 describing the shift to version-intent metadata and merge-time version reconciliation for worktree sessions, eliminating VERSIONS.md merge conflicts and concurrent version collisions via a merge library, merge lock guards, and end-to-end regression tests. <!--#e5703acd247db897-->
  - `11.13.1 - 2026-07-06` (heading) — Release notes for version 11.13.1 covering test-suite isolation from real project state, suppression of noise history entries, self-healing of the daemon project registry, and new cleanup scripts for leaked history and stale project-root entries. <!--#6655a7314320e017-->
  - `11.13.0 - 2026-07-06` (heading) — Changelog entry for release 11.13.0 introducing the `se3 code-index search <pattern>` subcommand with grep-consistent flags, exit codes, and one-line-per-match output, plus updated step prompts recommending it over raw grep of the code-index. <!--#c0007d107c6217e1-->
  - `11.12.1 - 2026-07-06` (heading) — A patch-release entry fixing live-chat delivery across the discovery→analyze boundary — correcting daemon disk-cache stale parsing, active-flow/read-cursor advancement, and the server history relay's self-healing broadcast — plus a periodic WebUI silent-rebuild fallback, scroll-anchor stability, and added end-to-end/fallback tests. <!--#cdff18ec3ac25a4c-->
  - `11.12.0 - 2026-07-06` (heading) — Changelog entry for release 11.12.0 introducing concurrent code-index summary generation (via code_index.max_concurrency) with preserved resumability, per-node NDJSON build progress, and live WebUI index-build progress while keeping engine/server isolation intact. <!--#556ec195c75d187a-->
  - `11.11.2 - 2026-07-06` (heading) — Patch-release changelog entry describing fixes to `--from-issue --worktree` flow finalization so source issues resolve based on persisted flow state and landed commits (across resume/daemon/merge paths) rather than the wrapper process exit code, with added regression tests. <!--#9d7965fcdd56c622-->
  - `11.11.1 - 2026-07-05` (heading) — Changelog entry for release 11.11.1 describing frontend progression-refresh changes that defer conversation rebuilds to the WS incremental path with a 5-second grace-period fallback, avoiding scroll jumps and stale token-usage badges, plus updated tests and retained gated diagnostics. <!--#9cf8964e6c0bc859-->
  - `11.11.0 - 2026-07-05` (heading) — Release entry for version 11.11.0 documenting the new `se3 worktree gc` command that archives old completed/failed worktree runs, prunes stale git worktrees, preserves and warns about unmerged branches, deletes already-merged branches, reports space reclaimed, and runs automatically as a low-frequency daemon tick. <!--#a2fee562f8595d07-->
  - `11.10.1 - 2026-07-04` (heading) — Patch release notes fixing the spec-write guard so it no longer clobbers the agent's --settings (model/permissions/effort), now delivering the guard hook via a generated --plugin-dir plugin while preserving spec-write denial behavior and the post-step spec-diff snapshot. <!--#dd0bbf96224faac9-->
  - `11.10.0 - 2026-07-04` (heading) — Release entry for v11.10.0 (2026-07-04) making adjudicate rulings auto-pass by default, adding opt-in human/LLM review via a `confirmation.steps.adjudicate` config entry, preserving the plan-only never-human-gated carve-out, updating docs/scaffold, defaulting config-resolution failures to auto-pass, and adding covering tests. <!--#42111c69eb0e06fd-->
  - `11.9.0 - 2026-07-04` (heading) — Changelog entry for release 11.9.0 documenting webui confirm-chip enhancements: approve/reject buttons with a note box returning a structured {approved, feedback} payload, an adjudicate review panel showing rationale and description diff, a CALL_KIND_CONFIRM data contract, Chinese approval/rejection word recognition, and a second-confirmation prompt for ambiguous free-text replies while keeping the free-text channel backward compatible. <!--#f5647f2bea46fc98-->
  - `11.8.1 - 2026-07-04` (heading) — Changelog entry for patch release 11.8.1 documenting a fix so daemon/webui-initiated flows no longer hang at human confirm gates—CONFIRM pauses now set engine.json to PAUSED and exit 0, honor JSON output non-interactively, preserve interactive behavior, and are covered by a new regression test. <!--#d414f659dcfcb3e9-->
  - `11.8.0 - 2026-07-04` (heading) — Changelog entry for release 11.8.0 introducing a daemon disk-JSON parse cache, off-event-loop parsing, a hot/cold split engine.json format with incremental per-step persistence, and backward-compatible read paths across resume/history/export/webui. <!--#867a507da5deaafe-->
  - `11.7.1 - 2026-07-03` (heading) — Changelog entry for version 11.7.1 splitting the ADJUDICATE step's LLM ruling into two phases so only genuine spec contradictions take the patch/reflow path while benign review-divergence rulings pass through as a transparent, audit-only no-op. <!--#e4eb112808c5cf0c-->
  - `11.7.0 - 2026-07-03` (heading) — Release notes for v11.7.0 introducing the ADJUDICATE step that resolves specification contradictions in the fix loop via a cross-iteration fingerprint ledger, oscillation triggers, priority override patches (adjudicated > refined > original), adjusted self_check validation, and a human/LLM confirmation gate. <!--#c0cc738cc823d2c3-->
  - `11.6.0 - 2026-07-02` (heading) — Release notes for version 11.6.0 describing the `se3 merge` never-lost/never-collide issue guarantee, automatic renumbering of duplicate incoming issue IDs coordinated via the `.next_id` counter, library-wide rewriting of attributable `#old`→`#new` cross-references, and alignment of the runtime-sync `adopt_issue` path with the git-merge channel. <!--#af4955bbbdfcb75b-->

  - `11.4.0 - 2026-07-01` (heading) — Changelog entry for v11.4.0 injecting recency context (recent session summaries and latest non-merge git commit subjects) into the discovery step's round-0 prompt to resolve cross-session references, gated to round 0 and applied in worktree mode while silently skipping missing sources. <!--#4e1a5a7c6ac2df3f-->

  - `11.2.0 - 2026-06-30` (heading) — Changelog for release 11.2.0, which hardens gitignore handling by generating root `/*` default-deny plus per-artifact whitelists for new projects, extends `migrate` to apply this default-deny idempotently while re-allowing already-tracked paths, and adds a non-blocking commit-time WARNING when a new top-level path is excluded. <!--#ecc8b082bd3d4f66-->

### `progress.md` (markdown) — A reverse-chronological session log for the SE 3.0 project, recording per-session Done/Changes/Open Issues/Next Steps entries that track feature work such as loop branch and collab modes, requirement-capture intake, CLI toolization (se3 lint/sync/verify/status), spec cleanup, and versioned protocol updates. <!--#e1332e31ececfbc4|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `pyproject.toml` (text) — Hatchling-based packaging and tooling manifest for the `se3` package (v11.22.1, a pure-CLI flow engine): declares core runtime deps (typer/pyyaml/rich/prompt-toolkit/psutil/pexpect), optional `server` and `browser` extras, the `se3` and `se3-server` console scripts, wheel artifacts for bundled static/i18n resources, and pytest config (testpaths including engine-colocated tests, `src` on pythonpath, and a deselect of the Chromium e2e test). <!--#5a635fa4344f08cd|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `se3.yaml` (yaml) — The root SE 3.0 framework configuration file that wires together the whole engine — the agent registry, per-step LLM caller and confirmation/review policies, human-call escalation, session bookkeeping, version bumping, language policy, e2e/critical-test verification, fix-loop workflow limits, and project preset prompts. <!--#6651ca5d6ed64ad8|ee539914ac0fcae4-->
- `human_call` (yaml-key) — Configuration for the human-in-the-loop call mechanism, specifying that call files live under `se3/calls` and expire after a 7-day timeout. <!--#aabec566b81e7d19-->
- `session` (yaml-key) — Session bookkeeping settings naming the progress log file and capping how many progress entries are retained. <!--#c067eb90db8bd1a7-->
- `agents` (yaml-key) — Top-level agent registry mapping logical names (primary/backup/low) to claude-code commands and priorities, resolved by name everywhere else in the config. <!--#2f9b309d4148ee7b-->
- `llm_caller` (yaml-key) — Defines the default agent caller chain plus hard per-step overrides for which agents run the implement and summarize steps. <!--#5e4a39a06783b3ed-->
- `confirmation` (yaml-key) — Configuration key setting confirmation behavior for workflow steps, capping the 'plan' step at a maximum of 3 iterations. <!--#664dfa6489595c1d-->
- `version` (yaml-key) — Automatic version-bumping settings controlling whether commits bump the version, auto-detect the version file, and embed the version in the commit message. <!--#8864db448db15952-->
- `language` (yaml-key) — Language policy separating the language used for human-facing steps from the language used when writing specs. <!--#fae409e34c1f163b-->
- `e2e` (yaml-key) — Optional end-to-end/visual-regression testing settings for baseline storage, pixel diff threshold, viewport, and URL paths to test. <!--#460af1d4687117b0-->
- `test` (yaml-key) — Registers critical acceptance tests that must genuinely run, so a skipped or missing test marks the verification run as unverified rather than passing. <!--#95f606ea092ea271-->
- `workflow` (yaml-key) — Workflow loop controls setting the fix-iteration backstop cap (max_fix_iterations: 100) and the adjudicate step's periodic safety-net interval (adjudicate_period: 10 iterations). <!--#40aef48cce75ad25-->
- `presets` (yaml-key) — Declares project-level preset prompts (e.g., doc-sync) that override built-in presets and are runnable via `se3 run --preset`. <!--#8cddb0680aac6aaa-->

## `.claude/` — The read-only framework-spec directory for the SE3 self-bootstrapping project, holding the published SE3 specs and root CLAUDE.md instructions (project purpose, the `se3 run` entry point, the `se3/` runtime layout, and optional per-step confirmation/review config) plus a session-state file tracking whether a Claude session is active. <!--#9622d82f73f44a00|ee9fa220890c234d-->

### `.claude/.session.json` (json) — A session-state file recording whether a Claude session is currently active, when it started (ISO 8601 timestamp), and the OS process ID used to detect if the session is still alive. <!--#75a1e2b905ccc3f1|97f010ab8e013eb0-->
- `status` (json-key) — Marks whether the session is currently active. <!--#5768e3a2fd58cd66-->
- `started_at` (json-key) — ISO 8601 timestamp recording when the session began. <!--#6cd43ee6b2d1a12c-->
- `pid` (json-key) — Operating-system process ID of the running session, used to detect whether it is still alive. <!--#6184dd5c70a9c3ce-->

## `docs/` — User-facing documentation directory holding the SE3 daemon-and-server guide in English and Chinese, covering the optional resident control plane (`se3 daemon` and central `se3-server`): quickstart, deployment/operations, architecture internals, mandatory multi-tenant authentication, TLS reverse-proxy deployment, and the bundled web frontend. <!--#87089fadeadac9f5|4039ef902670e18a-->

    - `The `se3-server` command` (heading) — Documents the standalone `se3-server` entry point, its CLI options/defaults, the `bootstrap-token` subcommand, and the mandatory-auth caveat. <!--#b51f88d8f81432c1-->
    - `A typical session` (heading) — End-to-end shell walkthrough of standing up a server, minting tokens/keys, and starting a worker daemon that dials in. <!--#77108cef308c4671-->

  - `Authentication & Multi-Tenant Access` (heading) — Section intro establishing the server as a multi-tenant control plane where every request and daemon must resolve to an owner, with a setup-motion overview. <!--#cb022cc70dbc930b-->
    - `Why authentication is mandatory` (heading) — Explains the fail-closed auth model: the configurable provider chain, `AuthNotConfigured` startup refusal, and HTTP 401 for ownerless requests. <!--#782723d85b178b36-->
    - `The persistence layer (`~/.se3/server.db`)` (heading) — Details the embedded sqlite store and the identity-only facts it persists (owners, bindings, password hashes, daemon-key/break-glass hashes), excluding live state. <!--#49cbf78253e40d42-->
    - `Bootstrapping the first admin (`bootstrap-token`)` (heading) — Describes the re-runnable one-time break-glass admin token as the IdP-independent first entrance into a fresh server. <!--#0dd5fe92e8fe2c99-->
    - `Logging in and creating users` (heading) — Documents the human login ceremony (login/logout/me endpoints) and admin-only user creation, noting no public self-registration in v1. <!--#49803a3994826103-->
    - `Issuing daemon keys and binding machines` (heading) — Explains owner-self-serviced daemon keys, the HELLO handshake that binds a machine to an owner, and WELCOME accept/reject behavior. <!--#f1fd2ca28ef64806-->
    - `Deploying behind a TLS reverse proxy (wss)` (heading) — Explains that `se3-server` speaks plaintext and needs a reverse proxy to terminate TLS and forward both static HTTP and upgraded WebSocket traffic. <!--#1b1d14307a1a3895-->
      - `nginx` (heading) — Provides a concrete nginx reverse-proxy config for WebSocket upgrade (the `map`, HTTP/1.1, long read timeout) with common-pitfall notes. <!--#375efbcea68f4501-->
      - `Caddy` (heading) — Provides the minimal Caddy reverse-proxy config that handles TLS and WebSocket upgrades automatically, plus an optional idle-timeout variant. <!--#adf7a3bf3e207711-->
      - `Verifying the proxy: a `curl --http1.1` handshake probe` (heading) — Shows how to confirm the proxy upgrades a WebSocket end-to-end via a raw `curl` handshake, interpreting the `101` and expected-404 results. <!--#da3245a99a200a4c-->
    - `Owner isolation` (heading) — Describes how both the UI/REST channel and the daemon `/ws` channel are owner-scoped, with cross-owner targets reading as 404 and additive provider linking. <!--#b7529003bf01a4e6-->
  - `The Web Frontend` (heading) — Documents the bundled build-step-free static frontend: login requirement, the `/ws/ui` real-time push channel, and watch/publish/respond capabilities. <!--#893626419c1e6172-->

### `docs/daemon-and-server.zh.md` (markdown) — Chinese user-and-operations guide for SE3's optional resident control plane — the per-machine `se3 daemon` and the central `se3-server` — covering quickstart (install, commands, a typical session), deployment/operations (outbound WebSocket model, foreground vs detached mode, runtime files, process supervision), architecture internals and the end-to-end task-publishing flow, mandatory owner-scoped auth/multi-tenancy (bootstrap token, sqlite identity store, daemon keys, TLS reverse-proxy deployment), and the bundled web frontend. <!--#ee3ec771277db2d9|9d439bcd17c0dfa0-->

    - `端到端:从远端机器发布任务` (heading) — Traces the full chain of publishing a task from the frontend through SPAWN_FLOW to a remote daemon's spawner, plus the mirror path for responding to a call via RESPOND_CALL. <!--#d17668f6e26dbd99-->

    - `为什么鉴权是强制的` (heading) — Explains the fail-closed auth model: the server refuses to serve without an available provider (default `local`), throwing AuthNotConfigured at startup and returning HTTP 401 for unresolvable requests. <!--#1fe9f0fb37aa236f-->

## `scripts/` — A directory of standalone operational scripts for the se3 project — one-time maintenance/cleanup passes (purging test-leak residue from se3/history/ and the daemon's project_roots.json), a data migration (backlog markdown → issue YAML), and a userspace shell helper that installs the system libraries headless-browser acceptance tests need. <!--#30c4f3afb45b3d74|561a977c0ef29768-->

### `scripts/cleanup_history_leak.py` (python) — A one-time maintenance script that scans se3/history/ and deletes (or dry-run lists) test-leak residue — empty dirs, single bare-`.jsonl` leak dirs, and known test-fixture residue names — while hard-protecting real flow, recovery-snapshot, and uuid-style history directories, exposing a `--dry-run`/`--history-dir` CLI. <!--#6aa0c884873661dc|42358c5eed1e937d-->
- `_project_root` (function) — Returns the project root directory (two levels up from this script's file path). <!--#515f3ee622c6e172-->
- `_is_leak_jsonl_file` (function) — Reports whether a path is a file literally named `.jsonl` — the name-only signature of an empty-step_id test leak, regardless of content. <!--#8e81921bac079a9b-->
- `_is_protected_name` (function) — Reports whether a directory name denotes a real flow (valid flow-id) or a `recovered_` snapshot that must never be deleted. <!--#6a5379f5e6be4cc6-->
- `_is_residue_name` (function) — Reports whether a directory name matches known test-fixture residue names (`se3`, `test-flow*`, `prompt_history*`) never used by real flows. <!--#abe133cbd5304a72-->
- `classify_dir` (function) — Classifies a history subdirectory into a leak category (empty / single-`.jsonl` / residue-name) or None to keep it, letting content signals override name protection but never deleting real uuid-style flow dirs by name. <!--#45c870fb4386af61-->
- `cleanup` (function) — Scans the history directory, deletes (or in dry-run lists) leak dirs and stray root files by category while preserving real flows and uuid dirs, then prints a summary report and returns an exit code. <!--#e58a7cd10e6fe0a1-->
- `main` (function) — CLI entry point that parses `--dry-run` and `--history-dir` arguments (defaulting to `<project_root>/se3/history`) and invokes `cleanup`. <!--#8c923a7c5c9f5f0e-->

### `scripts/cleanup_project_roots.py` (python) — A one-time maintenance CLI script that scrubs the daemon's project_roots.json registry of pytest-tempdir residue (and optionally vanished paths) leaked into it by test-spawned `se3 run` stubs, atomically rewriting the file (unless --dry-run) while preserving real project roots. <!--#fde91a1012f8d835|c64ce9ab7db4dcff-->
- `_default_registry` (function) — Resolves the path to the daemon's project_roots.json registry, honoring the SE3_DAEMON_DIR override and falling back to ~/.se3. <!--#f4bd2951eb4fb929-->
- `_is_pytest_residue` (function) — Predicate that returns whether a project-root path matches the pytest-residue regex (i.e., a leaked temp path from test runs). <!--#3ed4f14b96ddca01-->
- `cleanup` (function) — Loads the registry, drops pytest-residue (and optionally missing) project-root entries, atomically rewrites the file unless dry-run, and prints a cleanup report. <!--#063b65147aadad9d-->
- `main` (function) — CLI entry point parsing --dry-run/--registry/--prune-missing flags and invoking cleanup on the resolved registry path. <!--#1b63029c7edf6cf8-->

### `scripts/install_browser_test_libs.sh` (text) — A userspace bash fallback script that downloads and extracts (via `apt-get download`/`dpkg -x`, no root needed) the system shared libraries headless Chromium requires into a gitignored `.browser-libs/lib`, so the Playwright-based headless-browser acceptance test can run on hosts where `playwright install --with-deps` isn't possible. <!--#fe72f339a1f471d9|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `scripts/migrate_backlog.py` (python) — A one-time migration script that converts se3/specs/_backlog/*.md files into Issue YAML records by parsing each file's title, phase/status, and description, creating a tagged issue via IssueManager (with type inferred from phase), deleting the source markdown, and printing a migration report. <!--#a0845babfc6d9712|760a7a4bef36feb3-->
- `_extract_title` (function) — Returns the first markdown '# ' heading as the issue title, or 'Untitled' if none is found. <!--#5831f459c0a33fa4-->
- `_extract_phase` (function) — Finds and returns the markdown line containing both 'status' and 'backlog' to capture the phase/status info. <!--#5713b308209b36b0-->
- `_infer_type` (function) — Maps a phase/status line to an issue type (phase 1→task, phase 2/3→feature, phase 4/future→idea, default feature). <!--#c7e5b6978408cc9f-->
- `_extract_description` (function) — Collects body text under the Idea/Goal/Motivation section as the issue description, falling back to a default string. <!--#a6e466f1c2d9273a-->
- `migrate` (function) — Main entry point that iterates backlog markdown files, creates a tagged issue for each, deletes the source file, and prints a migration report. <!--#ce12a1e953eb33a1-->

## `src/` — The source root, holding the single `se3/` package: the entire SE 3.0 framework — its Typer CLI, state-machine flow engine, pluggable agent-runner adapters, shared config/core modules, optional daemon and central-server control plane, and project-scaffolding templates. <!--#0cfde6ce03e8c066|5f64bb0e9d734a3d-->

## `src/se3/` — The root package of the SE 3.0 framework — a state-machine-driven, LLM-agent-orchestrating engineering CLI — bundling the Typer CLI entry point and command layer, the flow engine (steps, prompts, code-index, fix-loop, DAG scheduler, merge), pluggable agent-runner adapters (Claude CLI, interactive Claude PTY, OpenAI Codex), layered project configuration, i18n catalogs, project-scaffolding templates, and the optional daemon/server control plane with its bundled web UI. <!--#2f15888ab419253a|7d45d2ea74ded979-->

### `src/se3/__init__.py` (python) — Package init for the SE 3.0 framework CLI that resolves and exposes the package version (via `__version__` / `SE3_FRAMEWORK_VERSION`) from installed metadata with a pyproject.toml fallback. <!--#9ea621a32fa204c4|52ccc8955ede7d6c-->
- `_get_version` (function) — Helper that determines the package version, preferring installed package metadata and falling back to parsing the `version` field from pyproject.toml, returning 'unknown' if all attempts fail. <!--#ac46b5e4fb58631f-->

### `src/se3/__main__.py` (python) — Package entry point that lets `python -m se3` launch the CLI by importing and calling the Typer `app`, serving as a robust fallback the daemon's spawner uses when the `se3` console script isn't on PATH. <!--#d004d4b47395e15f|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/se3/agent_runner.py` (python) — Defines the abstract AgentRunner base class and its contract (run, monitored run, arg-building, infra-error detection) that LLMCaller uses to drive any concrete agent runner, along with the InfraErrorType enum classifying rotation-worthy infrastructure failures and the RunResult dataclass bundling exit code, stdout, stderr, and detected error type. <!--#b3fac1acf22f6957|2d4ad19e73310e39-->
- `InfraErrorType` (class) — Enum classifying infrastructure-level failures (usage limit, timeout, hang, startup failure) that warrant rotating to a different agent. <!--#b4559b2f7002857f-->
- `RunResult` (class) — Dataclass bundling a runner execution's exit code, stdout, stderr, and detected infrastructure-error type. <!--#d425154633ceb3f4-->
- `AgentRunner` (class) — Abstract base class defining the runner contract LLMCaller uses to drive any agent implementation (Claude Code CLI, Codex, API-based), with abstract methods for synchronous run, monitored run, intent-to-CLI-args translation, and infrastructure-error detection. <!--#bdc46458d24e4cac-->
  - `AgentRunner.run` (method) — Abstract method to run the agent synchronously with optional timeout/cwd/env and a retry callback, returning a CompletedProcess. <!--#36ae2f398d60a19e-->
  - `AgentRunner.run_with_monitor` (method) — Abstract method to run the agent under wall/inactivity timeouts with output and activity callbacks, returning a monitored result. <!--#b42f4e02affb6ec5-->
  - `AgentRunner.build_call_args` (method) — Abstract method each runner subclass overrides to translate caller intent (effective prompt, read-only flag, context files, optional spec-guard plugin) into that agent's concrete CLI argument list. <!--#0b39227ae8198bb2-->
  - `AgentRunner.detect_infra_error` (method) — Abstract method that inspects a run's exit code and output to classify whether an infrastructure error occurred. <!--#9da392a3d03fdbc7-->

### `src/se3/claude_interactive_runner.py` (python) — The interactive-Claude AgentRunner adapter module: a third `AgentRunner` implementation that spawns the interactive `claude` TUI inside a lazily-imported pexpect PTY (feeding the prompt as simulated typing and supervising its wall/inactivity-timeout lifecycle), while a companion transcript watcher locates and incrementally tails the session's JSONL to emit stream-json NDJSON, accumulate usage tokens, and derive turn-completion/inactivity signals from combined PTY-and-JSONL activity. <!--#0868daa0828bded6|344f409d8cb91096-->
- `_import_pexpect` (function) — Lazily imports the optional pexpect dependency, raising a friendly install hint if it is missing, so the module loads without pexpect installed. <!--#95b977a55b4eb9b4-->
- `_safe_isalive` (function) — Returns whether the PTY child handle is still running, swallowing errors from a dead/reaped handle. <!--#98bcb81ff0b06817-->
- `_ActivityClock` (class) — Thread-safe last-activity timestamp bumped by the drain thread and read by the supervisor to drive inactivity timeouts. <!--#e8dd8801beac4cb5-->
  - `_ActivityClock.__init__` (method) — Initializes the clock to the current time with a lock for thread-safe access. <!--#34f4d6294c29498a-->
  - `_ActivityClock.update` (method) — Sets the stored timestamp to now under the lock (called on each activity tick). <!--#e2f01023ef425bb5-->
  - `_ActivityClock.last` (method) — Returns the last-recorded activity timestamp under the lock. <!--#fc964925b709c931-->
- `_normalize_pty_lines` (function) — Strips ANSI/TUI noise and collapses volatile digits and whitespace so cosmetic spinner/footer re-renders normalize to identical strings while real streamed text stays distinct. <!--#f917aa24c44496b4-->
- `_MeaningfulContentTracker` (class) — Degraded-mode progress detector that, when no transcript JSONL is available, advances an activity clock only on genuinely new PTY content so cosmetic TUI re-renders cannot keep the inactivity timer alive forever. <!--#c7186a35fb511d1e-->
  - `_MeaningfulContentTracker.__init__` (method) — Initializes the tracker's clock, chunk cursor, residual buffer, and bounded seen-line set. <!--#65310c3c1a5b2386-->
  - `_MeaningfulContentTracker.scan` (method) — Consumes newly-appended PTY chunks, holding back partial lines, and bumps the clock only when a normalized line hasn't been seen before. <!--#c5a7dc16b28cd47c-->
- `munge_cwd` (function) — Reproduces Claude Code's cwd→projects-subdir-name munging (replacing non-alphanumeric chars with dashes) to derive the per-project transcript directory. <!--#06a85a49aa34fe85-->
- `claude_projects_dir` (function) — Returns the ~/.claude/projects transcript directory, honoring the CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR override. <!--#2e8a3a47b034eaf4-->
- `_safe_mtime` (function) — Returns a path's modification time, or 0.0 if it cannot be stat-ed. <!--#f2c9d08de602063a-->
- `snapshot_session_files` (function) — Best-effort recursive snapshot of all *.jsonl transcript files under the projects tree, used for the pre/post-launch diff. <!--#b3cc6a37d00c01eb-->
- `_file_cwd_matches` (function) — Second-pass check that reads a candidate transcript's leading records to confirm/deny its cwd field matches the target, distinguishing concurrent-flow files. <!--#058ab205a169f36b-->
- `locate_session_file` (function) — Locates this launch's transcript file, binding deterministically to the explicit session-id filename when given, else diffing against the pre-launch snapshot with cwd-match isolation. <!--#8ad402673acf6dbd-->
- `tail_new_records` (function) — Incrementally reads complete JSON records appended past a byte cursor (leaving partial lines unconsumed, resetting on truncation) and returns them with the advanced cursor. <!--#9b6d210df49bb20b-->
- `to_stream_json_ndjson` (function) — Converts one JSONL transcript record into the stream-json NDJSON shape upstream consumers expect, filtering by type and dropping sidechain/non-meaningful records. <!--#a9cebac1c0ff43a0-->
- `extract_usage_from_record` (function) — Reads the four token-count fields from a record's nested or top-level usage payload, defaulting to zeros on any parsing surprise. <!--#d372c353fba00548-->
- `synthesize_result_line` (function) — Builds a terminal stream-json type:"result" line from accumulated usage so interactive-mode tokens flow through the existing usage-accounting chain. <!--#bc3e6e4b7b2cf681-->
- `_is_terminal_record` (function) — Decides whether a record marks turn-end (a result line or an assistant message with a terminal stop_reason), excluding tool_use/tool_result. <!--#f9e8edfb9ee3de7a-->
- `turn_complete` (function) — Single-turn completion check combining a terminal last JSONL record with the transcript having gone idle, deliberately ignoring PTY idleness. <!--#ffa31ba5172c2976-->
- `SessionTranscriptWatcher` (class) — Stateful watcher that snapshots, locates, and incrementally tails one session transcript JSONL, producing stream-json NDJSON, accumulating usage, and exposing write-activity for the turn-end/inactivity signals. <!--#e8241b7e9aff8b46-->
  - `SessionTranscriptWatcher.__init__` (method) — Initializes the watcher's cwd, projects dir, session id, file path, cursor, snapshot, record state, and usage accumulator. <!--#10cfb0fd9b41a77d-->
  - `SessionTranscriptWatcher.snapshot` (method) — Captures the pre-launch *.jsonl file set (called before spawning the PTY). <!--#a0b057e7f237a0b9-->
  - `SessionTranscriptWatcher.locate` (method) — Attempts to locate this launch's transcript file, idempotently caching it once found. <!--#211931ea8b3151e9-->
  - `SessionTranscriptWatcher.poll` (method) — Reads new records, advancing the cursor and state, accumulating usage, emitting a leading init line on first model sighting, and returns their stream-json NDJSON lines. <!--#4813007e9cc6466a-->
  - `SessionTranscriptWatcher.usage` (method) — Property returning a copy of the token counts accumulated across all assistant messages seen. <!--#670ae7e99550c5a2-->
  - `SessionTranscriptWatcher.write_activity` (method) — Returns the best timestamp of the last JSONL write (file mtime, falling back to last record-yielding poll) driving inactivity and turn-idle signals. <!--#a0974012f0252f9d-->
  - `SessionTranscriptWatcher.synthesize_result` (method) — Mints the terminal result line from the watcher's accumulated usage. <!--#6dde706e00fdf4ac-->
- `ClaudeInteractiveRunner` (class) — An AgentRunner adapter that drives the interactive Claude Code CLI (TUI) over a PTY, wrapping one CLI command per instance while feeding the effective prompt as simulated user input rather than embedding it in argv, and isolating concurrent flows via a per-launch session id and configurable --setting-sources. <!--#1b9a303754a4f513-->
  - `ClaudeInteractiveRunner.__init__` (method) — Initializes the runner with a single Claude command, setting-sources config, project root, and per-launch prompt/session-id slots. <!--#385aa73c8852e7ff-->
  - `ClaudeInteractiveRunner.build_call_args` (method) — Translates call intent into interactive-mode launch flags — stashing the prompt for later PTY input, adding read-only tool restrictions via --disallowedTools, and exposing context files through deduplicated --add-dir parent directories — while ignoring the spec_guard_plugin argument kept only for interface parity. <!--#dc49503e6c55083c-->
  - `ClaudeInteractiveRunner._build_full_cmd` (method) — Composes the launch argv, injecting --dangerously-skip-permissions, --setting-sources, and the explicit --session-id prefix flags. <!--#ca23609984994b62-->
  - `ClaudeInteractiveRunner._spawn_pty` (method) — Spawns the interactive claude inside a PTY as a session/process-group leader (via pexpect) so the whole group can later be killed. <!--#4b8a493ca1c400c9-->
  - `ClaudeInteractiveRunner._feed_prompt` (method) — Background-thread feeder that waits for input-box readiness, then delivers the full multi-line prompt as one bracketed paste followed by an Enter to dispatch the turn. <!--#215fc9a01efb85f5-->
  - `ClaudeInteractiveRunner._await_input_ready` (method) — Blocks until the PTY has rendered output and gone quiet for the settle window (input box ready) or the readiness timeout elapses. <!--#dec5ee493e266727-->
  - `ClaudeInteractiveRunner._write_text` (method) — Writes text to the PTY master via a byte-level full-delivery loop on the child fd, falling back to handle.send for test stubs. <!--#f41046c33dca8162-->
  - `ClaudeInteractiveRunner._write_all_bytes` (method) — Writes every byte of a payload to a fd, retrying the unwritten remainder in chunks with tiny pauses to avoid truncation/overrun. <!--#c7fde4aa2a021e36-->
  - `ClaudeInteractiveRunner._drain_pty` (method) — Background-thread reader that continuously drains PTY output, bumping activity clocks, buffering, logging, and firing output/activity callbacks until EOF or stop. <!--#d16fff172457c9fa-->
  - `ClaudeInteractiveRunner._terminate` (method) — Force-terminates the PTY child's whole process group (SIGTERM, grace, SIGKILL) and reaps it via pexpect close, best-effort on every step. <!--#fe6d7710e2b42015-->
  - `ClaudeInteractiveRunner.run` (method) — Runs one interactive turn synchronously via the shared monitored path and returns a CompletedProcess carrying the stream-json NDJSON output. <!--#a1823559b550eee5-->
  - `ClaudeInteractiveRunner.run_with_monitor` (method) — Launches interactive claude in a PTY and supervises its full lifecycle (wall/inactivity timeouts, force-kill, reclamation), returning a MonitoredResult with the captured output. <!--#5e0acfb93bb5b043-->
  - `ClaudeInteractiveRunner._make_watcher` (method) — Constructs the SessionTranscriptWatcher for the run, returning None (degraded PTY-only mode) when cwd is unknown; overridable in tests. <!--#0915cd3f68f49c15-->
  - `ClaudeInteractiveRunner._run_single_with_monitor` (method) — Core method that spawns the PTY, runs feed/drain threads and the composite PTY+JSONL supervisor loop until turn-complete or a timeout, and guarantees teardown/reclamation in a finally block. <!--#192e1a8f30049e77-->
  - `ClaudeInteractiveRunner._compose_output` (method) — Selects the output payload, preferring captured stream-json NDJSON and falling back to raw PTY capture when none was produced. <!--#a7dc47d241852098-->
  - `ClaudeInteractiveRunner._compose_output_with_limit_marker` (method) — Composes the output and appends a usage-limit marker after scanning the raw PTY buffer, so the keyword survives for downstream USAGE_LIMIT classification on timeout paths. <!--#2189ff68cdfcada1-->
  - `ClaudeInteractiveRunner._exit_code` (method) — Derives a best-effort exit code from a finished pexpect handle (exit status, 128+signal, or 0/1 fallback). <!--#46e170d535bbd994-->
  - `ClaudeInteractiveRunner._detect_usage_limit` (method) — Scans the output tail for usage/rate-limit keywords on failed runs only. <!--#b846f24a2be97871-->
  - `ClaudeInteractiveRunner._detect_startup_failure` (method) — Detects whether the output carries a PTY-spawn or never-created-transcript startup-failure marker. <!--#a5d76a6d9e6a9a4e-->
  - `ClaudeInteractiveRunner.detect_infra_error` (method) — Classifies infrastructure errors (USAGE_LIMIT, TIMEOUT, STARTUP_FAILURE, or NONE) for LLMCaller agent rotation, drawing on PTY output and JSONL transcript state. <!--#0c761ec5e68d6538-->
- `MonitoredResult` (class) — Dataclass result of run_with_monitor carrying the return code, output, command metadata, and interrupted/success state. <!--#b12f4f609b402674-->
  - `MonitoredResult.success` (method) — Property reporting whether the return code is zero. <!--#787b46b245897e2b-->
- `_SingleRunResult` (class) — Internal dataclass result of a single monitored PTY run (return code, output, success, should_retry, interrupted). <!--#7fd76b6e9948c7f4-->

### `src/se3/claude_runner.py` (python) — AgentRunner adapter that executes a single Claude Code CLI command as a subprocess — assembling permission/setting-source argv (with large prompts auto-piped to stdin to dodge E2BIG), running either synchronously or under real-time activity monitoring with confirmation-prompt handling, and reporting usage-limit/timeout infra errors for LLMCaller's retry logic. <!--#ab8aace3246cc409|8abf5e983b2a7a07-->
- `_spawn_stdin_writer` (function) — Module helper that writes a large prompt payload to the child's stdin from a daemon thread (then closes it) to avoid pipe-buffer deadlock on the large-prompt path. <!--#19dde2ba6f7be9f0-->
- `_spawn_stderr_reader` (function) — Module helper that drains the child's stderr in a daemon thread, optionally logging to a file and echoing to the parent's stderr, keeping stdout NDJSON clean. <!--#8e701338eb2971f4-->
- `detect_confirmation_prompt` (function) — Module function that conservatively detects an interactive CLI confirmation prompt in a line of child output, returning the prompt text and any inline numeric option labels (or None). <!--#5c28f457ef473dae-->
- `_write_stdin_response` (function) — Module helper that writes a confirmation answer (newline-terminated) back to the child's stdin, swallowing failures so undeliverable answers degrade to a no-op. <!--#a2717e89116de7e9-->
- `ClaudeCodeRunner` (class) — A single-command Claude Code CLI adapter (subclass of AgentRunner) that wraps one specific `claude`-family command, injects `--setting-sources` isolation into spawned subprocesses, and reroutes oversized `-p` prompts to stdin — leaving list-traversal and fallback logic to LLMCaller. <!--#1e499464290562ab-->
  - `ClaudeCodeRunner.__init__` (method) — Initializes the runner from a single command (with legacy `commands` support) and resolves the Claude CLI setting-sources list from explicit args or project config. <!--#b59445d42c87ca93-->
  - `ClaudeCodeRunner._resolve_args` (method) — Static method that rewrites oversized `-p`/`--prompt` argv values to stdin (preserving `@file` references) to avoid execve E2BIG limits. <!--#181b40b864d27e84-->
  - `ClaudeCodeRunner.run` (method) — Runs Claude synchronously via subprocess.run for a single command, assembling the full argv, feeding any stdin prompt, and returning a CompletedProcess (124 on timeout). <!--#4f8bee1df17dbf47-->
  - `ClaudeCodeRunner.get_command` (method) — Returns the command string at the given index in the backward-compatibility commands list (clamping to the last entry). <!--#55afbbe111e290a0-->
  - `ClaudeCodeRunner.get_next_command` (method) — Returns the command following a given one in the commands list, or None if it is last or not found. <!--#0f38633a0bb6a7c2-->
  - `ClaudeCodeRunner.build_call_args` (method) — Builds the Claude Code CLI argv from intent-level parameters (prompt, read-only flag, context files, optional spec-guard plugin), emitting the stream-json base flags plus read-only tool restrictions, an additive `--plugin-dir` guard, and per-file `--file` context args. <!--#ec3ed4965fc0fce4-->
  - `ClaudeCodeRunner.detect_usage_limit` (method) — Static method that inspects the tail of failed-command output for known usage/rate-limit keywords to detect quota exhaustion. <!--#f864b51cf98d6564-->
  - `ClaudeCodeRunner.detect_timeout` (method) — Static method that reports whether a return code (124) indicates a timeout failure. <!--#3e76609d6d367ce6-->
  - `ClaudeCodeRunner.detect_infra_error` (method) — Combines usage-limit and timeout detection into a single InfraErrorType verdict for LLMCaller's retry logic. <!--#b63bfc06170b32ad-->
  - `ClaudeCodeRunner.run_with_monitor` (method) — Runs Claude with real-time activity-based monitoring (stuck/hang detection, logging, output and confirmation callbacks) and returns a MonitoredResult. <!--#c345b548e48f0a50-->
  - `ClaudeCodeRunner._run_single_with_monitor` (method) — Internal worker that spawns the child via Popen and runs the monitoring loop — handling stdin feeding, stderr draining, wall/inactivity timeouts, and confirmation-prompt answering. <!--#f6f5b52ec49fdef8-->
- `MonitoredResult` (class) — Dataclass holding the outcome of run_with_monitor (return code, output, command used, retry/interrupt flags) with a `success` property. <!--#c1d4bf7467c22e70-->
  - `MonitoredResult.success` (method) — Property returning True when the monitored run's return code is zero. <!--#787b46b245897e2b-->
- `_SingleRunResult` (class) — Internal dataclass capturing the result of a single monitored command run (return code, output, success, should-retry, interrupted). <!--#3382b4f182bfe583-->

### `src/se3/cli.py` (python) — The Typer-based SE3 CLI entry point that defines all top-level commands — run, init, guardrails, daemon start/stop/status, merge (plus merge-respond/merge-unlock), salvage, and end-session — wiring user input, display setup, and version handling to the underlying engine flows. <!--#e35d4b48f8bbd8c4|5b9ccdf6646ee539-->
- `_version_callback` (function) — Typer eager callback for `--version` that echoes the localized version string and exits immediately. <!--#1daa43ccf5bfdbde-->
- `main` (function) — Root Typer callback that initializes the display console, wires the `--version` option, and prints help when no subcommand is given. <!--#b4f9f0eb2adc72b2-->
- `_init_display` (function) — Initializes the global Rich console for consistent CLI output. <!--#bc1892294d2bdfda-->
- `_read_multiline_input` (function) — Reads multiline user input from stdin, using prompt_toolkit (with Ctrl+D-to-accept bindings and history) when interactive and a plain read when piped, returning None on cancel. <!--#9941ab8d25f9a95a-->
- `run_cmd` (function) — The `se3 run` command — the unified flow-engine entry point that resolves the project root, applies preset/discovery/--from-issue/--worktree modes, and dispatches to the run/resume flow handlers. <!--#104a3dd1304ca2a4-->
- `init_cmd` (function) — The `se3 init` command that scaffolds a new SE3 project (se3.yaml plus the specs directory structure) at the given root. <!--#fe4af52f23d71113-->
- `_run_spec_size_guardrails` (function) — Runs spec volume-governance size checks and renders a report, exiting 1 under the `enforce` tier and 0 under `warn` or when clean. <!--#c85d9f6026d5700e-->
- `guardrails_cmd` (function) — The `se3 guardrails` command that checks a spec file's diff against its git/original version for weakening or deletion violations and also reports spec-size governance results, exiting non-zero on blocking violations. <!--#791dfb244a991b75-->
- `_project_root_for_spec` (function) — Helper that walks up from a spec file to locate the owning SE3 project root for size governance. <!--#40c3c36bb5ef4490-->
- `_precheck_websockets` (function) — Warns on the CLI when the `websockets` package is missing so the user knows a `--server-url` daemon would silently fall back to local-only mode. <!--#ce7c7d98cc33fa03-->
- `_report_connection_result` (function) — Polls the daemon status file after a detached start and reports the real server-connection outcome, trusting only status written by the fresh daemon and treating early errors as transient. <!--#784e4427a440b106-->
- `daemon_start_cmd` (function) — The `se3 daemon start` command that launches the daemon detached (or in the foreground), resolves the daemon key from flag or environment, and reports the resulting connection state. <!--#cd92a1f90509fdd6-->
- `daemon_stop_cmd` (function) — The `se3 daemon stop` command that stops the running daemon and reports stopped / not-running / stop-timeout outcomes with matching exit codes. <!--#4579fb698e0918f4-->
- `daemon_status_cmd` (function) — The `se3 daemon status` command that prints (or emits as JSON) the daemon's PID, machine, configured server, real connection state, and tracked flows. <!--#fe248f8d79b8de72-->
- `merge_cmd` (function) — The `se3 merge` command — a thin adapter that validates branch names, resolves strategy/delete-merged from flags and config, and runs the merge integrate+reconcile pipeline, signalling failure via exit code. <!--#2222de51aead4c30-->
- `merge_respond_cmd` (function) — The `se3 merge-respond` command that executes the conflict decisions recorded in an edited merge call-response file. <!--#cd592352d348f648-->
- `merge_unlock_cmd` (function) — The `se3 merge-unlock` command that inspects and reports the project's merge lock, auto-clears stale locks, and refuses a live holder unless `--force`. <!--#b7fe019b6eccb1cc-->
- `salvage_cmd` (function) — The `se3 salvage` command that best-effort recovers an abnormally terminated session by committing changes, filing issues for unfinished work, and archiving the session. <!--#ce1db9ff7cfef95f-->
- `end_session_cmd` (function) — The `se3 end-session` command that terminates a live run process and archives its session (including worktree cleanup) without merging uncommitted work. <!--#bf6970dad2f6c55f-->

### `src/se3/codex_runner.py` (python) — OpenAI Codex CLI adapter that wraps a single `codex exec --json` command as an AgentRunner subclass, translating codex's JSONL events into Claude-compatible stream-json NDJSON (via CodexEventConverter) and running codex synchronously or under activity-based monitoring with stdin routing, stderr draining, timeout enforcement, and infrastructure-error classification. <!--#7368c158c96ec664|90b98d81ec878b0d-->
- `_detect_shell_snapshot_failure` (function) — Module-level helper that returns True if the given stderr text contains any known shell-snapshot validation failure pattern. <!--#285b07575c27a81d-->
- `CodexEventConverter` (class) — Stateful converter that turns codex `--json` JSONL events into zero or more Claude stream-json NDJSON lines over the lifetime of one codex invocation, never raising. <!--#ebdd6c4cac5d6f89-->
  - `CodexEventConverter.__init__` (method) — Initializes the converter's internal state: accumulated agent messages, terminal-seen flag, tool-id counter, and touched-files set. <!--#23192a4eaaf62e01-->
  - `CodexEventConverter.touched_files` (method) — Property exposing the set of file paths collected from `file_change` items for dependency tracking. <!--#21dde3ceae6fa2d8-->
  - `CodexEventConverter._next_tool_id` (method) — Generates a unique synthetic tool-use id (`codex_tool_N`) when an event lacks its own call id. <!--#abc4b1e4bae8e685-->
  - `CodexEventConverter.convert_line` (method) — Parses one codex JSONL line and dispatches by event type to the appropriate handler, returning the resulting NDJSON lines. <!--#f5413ff755d808ce-->
  - `CodexEventConverter._handle_item_event` (method) — Converts `item.updated`/`item.completed` events (agent_message, command_execution, file_change, mcp_tool_call) into Claude tool_use/tool_result/assistant NDJSON events. <!--#6a72f173946f2fae-->
  - `CodexEventConverter._map_tool_name` (method) — Maps codex's generic tool/function names (shell, apply_patch, etc.) to the closest Claude tool names for display. <!--#24273fa0354b0a63-->
  - `CodexEventConverter._handle_turn_completed` (method) — Handles `turn.completed` by emitting a Claude `type: result` event built from accumulated agent messages, extracted usage, and cost. <!--#ae84f50b3fd4238f-->
  - `CodexEventConverter._handle_turn_failed` (method) — Handles `turn.failed`/`error` by emitting an error `type: result` event with the extracted error message and usage. <!--#5a23f07f8c5e81ff-->
  - `CodexEventConverter.finalize` (method) — Emits a synthesized terminal `result` event after the process exits if no `turn.completed`/`turn.failed` was ever seen. <!--#0a250218c729af5c-->
- `_spawn_stdin_writer` (function) — Launches a daemon thread that writes a prompt payload to the subprocess stdin and closes it, avoiding pipe-buffer deadlock. <!--#136c5b7ec66b9827-->
- `_spawn_stderr_reader` (function) — Launches a daemon thread that drains the subprocess stderr, optionally logging to a sidecar file and capturing the tail into a bounded buffer. <!--#af4e0e85a2eb715f-->
- `CodexRunner` (class) — An AgentRunner adapter that executes single `codex exec --json` CLI commands, building sandbox-aware argv, inlining context files into the prompt, and converting codex's JSONL events into Claude-compatible stream-json NDJSON for unchanged upper-layer consumers. <!--#22003ad0421b2726-->
  - `CodexRunner.__init__` (method) — Initializes the runner with a single command dict, defaulting to `{cmd: codex, priority: 0}`. <!--#c5b52427c53670a9-->
  - `CodexRunner.build_call_args` (method) — Translates intent-level parameters into codex CLI argv—prefixing `exec --json --skip-git-repo-check`, choosing read-only vs. danger-full-access `--sandbox`, inlining context-file contents into the prompt, and appending the prompt positionally or as a `-` stdin marker when it exceeds `_MAX_ARG_BYTES`. <!--#ab3777d59a7f51b9-->
  - `CodexRunner.run` (method) — Runs codex synchronously to completion and returns a CompletedProcess whose stdout is codex output converted to Claude NDJSON. <!--#a659dadfbc8ababd-->
  - `CodexRunner.run_with_monitor` (method) — Runs codex with activity-based monitoring, streaming converted NDJSON to buffer/log/callbacks and returning a MonitoredResult. <!--#a4ed41c0d1b0f6de-->
  - `CodexRunner._run_single_with_monitor` (method) — Core monitoring loop that spawns the codex process, streams and converts stdout, drains stderr, and enforces wall/inactivity (hang) timeouts. <!--#549f31a7c3cfe1be-->
  - `CodexRunner.detect_infra_error` (method) — Classifies a codex run's exit code and output tail into an InfraErrorType (timeout, usage/auth limit, shell-snapshot startup failure, or none). <!--#d00ad55f4e702f64-->
- `MonitoredResult` (class) — Dataclass holding the outcome of `run_with_monitor` (return code, output, command, retry/interrupt flags, stderr tail) with a `success` property. <!--#6ac9ba61952cbdea-->
  - `MonitoredResult.success` (method) — Property returning True when the return code is zero. <!--#787b46b245897e2b-->
- `_SingleRunResult` (class) — Internal dataclass capturing the result of a single monitored command run (return code, output, success, retry/interrupt flags, stderr tail). <!--#25c02f14463c799c-->

### `src/se3/config.py` (python) — SE3's configuration management module, defining the project config filenames and layered config dataclasses/loading, plus a cached git probe (`probe_main_repo_root` / `_resolve_main_repo_root`) that resolves whether a project root is a linked worktree and where the main repository checkout lives. <!--#93a62575a22b6d61|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/se3/preset_loader.py` (python) — Loads and resolves SE3 'preset prompts' from a dual-layer registry — built-in markdown templates plus project-local overrides from se3/prompts and se3.yaml — exposing listing and name-to-(task_type, prompt, layer) resolution with explicit errors for unknown presets or missing prompt files. <!--#6b084d3aa7add2b9|d2564ec60747f605-->
- `PresetError` (class) — Base exception for any preset resolution failure (e.g. a declared prompt file that does not exist). <!--#6030b307aeecbc5f-->
- `PresetNotFoundError` (class) — Exception raised when a requested preset name is absent from the registry. <!--#58c5c0d2faa5b1d9-->
- `PresetEntry` (class) — Dataclass representing one resolved preset registry entry (name, task type, on-disk prompt file path, and source layer). <!--#02e2f636bc038da6-->
- `_scan_builtin_presets` (function) — Enumerates built-in presets by globbing the packaged templates/prompts directory and attaching declared metadata. <!--#8fc5ae2abd3383b6-->
- `_load_project_presets` (function) — Enumerates project-local presets from se3/prompts/*.md and overlays metadata/path overrides from se3.yaml's presets section. <!--#2e2c97c767f5d773-->
- `load_registry` (function) — Builds the merged name→PresetEntry registry, loading built-ins first then letting project presets override same-named entries. <!--#6fface6d1a6916f9-->
- `list_presets` (function) — Returns all available presets (built-in plus project) sorted by name. <!--#1039d20edae71e6c-->
- `resolve` (function) — Resolves a preset name to its (task_type, prompt_text, layer) tuple, raising explicitly on unknown names or missing prompt files. <!--#e9990726bc48d1f3-->

### `src/se3/utils.py` (python) — A shared utility module for the SE3 framework providing spec discovery/parsing, output and change discovery, file copy/mtime helpers, scenario verification-marker search, framework version extraction, documentation-consistency and git-change checks, and status.md parsing. <!--#dd440553a674550f|bbb61607537f6fe4-->
- `_resolve_specs_dir` (function) — Resolves the specs directory by preference order: se3/specs/, then specs/, then legacy openspec/specs/. <!--#50cfb7c3c9bc1885-->
- `discover_specs` (function) — Returns a sorted list of absolute paths to spec.md files found in the resolved specs directory. <!--#92b1149753063b4b-->
- `parse_spec` (function) — Parses a spec.md file into structured data (title, purpose, requirements, and WHEN/THEN scenarios). <!--#264118a9b806c560-->
- `get_exit_code` (function) — Maps a list of validation results to a CLI exit code (0 success, 1 errors, 2 runtime error). <!--#61082e083fb6cc05-->
- `discover_outputs` (function) — Lists all regular files directly inside a given directory. <!--#ec09c48061154c4d-->
- `get_file_mtime` (function) — Returns a file's modification timestamp, or None if it doesn't exist. <!--#730f41c0d4c2440a-->
- `copy_file` (function) — Copies a file to a destination, creating parent directories as needed. <!--#78cd0cb36fae02a0-->
- `get_source_mappings` (function) — Returns the (now empty) source-to-output file sync mappings, since runtime files are no longer synced. <!--#6f5c472251f28ed0-->
- `discover_changes` (function) — Discovers changelog/change entry names from se3/specs/_changelog with legacy fallbacks. <!--#ca576176987c4adb-->
- `discover_specs_in_change` (function) — Legacy helper that finds spec.md files nested within a named change directory. <!--#0870a4e8ac7c9751-->
- `find_verification_markers` (function) — Searches Python files for pytest markers or comments verifying a given scenario ID. <!--#7dbaf5c1ee6b6e20-->
- `get_framework_version` (function) — Extracts the SE3 framework version string from pyproject.toml. <!--#1d5ec79da290223b-->
- `check_documentation_consistency` (function) — Validates that README.md and VERSIONS.md exist, cross-reference each other, and reflect the current framework version. <!--#5401b568afd9afa1-->
- `has_framework_file_changes` (function) — Checks git's staged files for changes to known framework source paths. <!--#dbfdb9481646fa39-->
- `parse_status_md` (function) — Parses status.md into structured fields (active change, current task, status, blockers). <!--#2c4ec321050f973f-->

## `src/se3/commands/` — The SE3 3.0 CLI command layer, housing the Typer command implementations that drive the tool's user-facing workflows — running/resuming flows (`run`), merging and conflict resolution (`merge`, `merge-respond`), session lifecycle (`end-session`, `salvage`, `history`, `worktree gc`), project setup and migration (`init`, `migrate`), issue and code-index management — over a shared merge-infrastructure subpackage that supplies locking, tracing, redaction, and typed result/failure models. <!--#7242a917d13e1bd4|107f5c7a6ed4f963-->

### `src/se3/commands/__init__.py` (python) — Package initializer for the SE 3.0 CLI commands module, containing only a docstring and marking the directory as the namespace that holds the individual command implementations. <!--#7bf1513a2bce3e63|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/se3/commands/code_index_cmd.py` (python) — Defines the Typer `se3 code-index` command family that lets humans and the LLM navigate the project's structure map — the adaptive budgeted root view plus literal drill-in (`index`), single-file detail (`show`), regex/literal grep of item lines (`search`), incremental/full (re)build (`rebuild`), and on-disk health stats (`inspect`) — all reading render-only from the authoritative `se3/code-index.md` except `rebuild`, which writes it. <!--#22e6fe9d96f9b6da|2fda5866aca58b78-->
- `get_project_root` (function) — Walks up from the cwd to find the project root (a `.git` dir or SE3 config), rebinding the i18n language to that root before returning it. <!--#6bb957ad4b0017c5-->
- `_render_adaptive_map` (function) — Renders the bare `se3 code-index` adaptive root view — the budgeted, auto-expanding orientation map injected into every flow step — erroring out if the index has not been built. <!--#f75bc16ba26279c7-->
- `code_index_main` (function) — Typer callback for the `code-index` command group that renders the adaptive root view when invoked with no subcommand and otherwise dispatches to its drill-in/rebuild/inspect subcommands. <!--#475c3ea7659eb429-->
- `index_cmd` (function) — The `index` subcommand: prints the literal, non-expanding drill-in view of exactly one level at the given path (or the root level when no path is given). <!--#5e072ceec3fc46b9-->
- `show_cmd` (function) — The `show` subcommand: prints one file's full summary plus every class/function/method from the code-index (or the file one-liners under a directory prefix). <!--#ab73eb6098443ac8-->
- `search_cmd` (function) — The `search` subcommand: a grep drop-in over the code-index item lines, supporting -i/-F/-m (and a no-op -n) and mirroring grep's 0/1/2 exit codes. <!--#829b979add860e84-->
- `_build_matcher` (function) — Compiles a search pattern into a per-line predicate — literal substring under `-F`, otherwise a regex — exiting 2 on an invalid regex. <!--#4894c9fafcd9565d-->
- `rebuild_cmd` (function) — The `rebuild` subcommand: re-enumerates the tree and LLM-summarises changed nodes (or everything with `--force`), writing the authoritative `se3/code-index.md` and reporting the resulting counts. <!--#2c79962407cf9769-->
- `inspect_cmd` (function) — The `inspect` subcommand: prints health-check stats of the on-disk index — file, symbol, and degraded counts plus a per-kind file breakdown — without dumping the map. <!--#fba429197e62b7e3-->

### `src/se3/commands/end_session_cmd.py` (python) — Implements the `se3 end-session` command: terminates a running `se3 run` flow's live process tree and archives the session — reusing the merge-cleanup machinery for `--worktree` sessions (archive worktree, promote engine state, sync history, delete branch/worktree, clear snapshot) or simply clearing engine state for main-branch sessions — running each step as an independently fault-tolerant unit and rendering a Rich summary table with an aggregate exit code. <!--#cebfefe151a4927b|eb726bbf0fd6ee8a-->
- `end_session` (function) — Top-level entry point for the `end-session` pipeline: resolves the main project root and flow id, finds any worktree session, kills the live `se3 run` process tree, archives the session (worktree or main-branch), prints a results table, and returns an aggregate exit code. <!--#af4089b15dfa3b59-->
- `_find_project_root` (function) — Walks up from the current directory to locate the project root via a `.git` dir or an SE3 config file. <!--#3c8eb6032ea041a2-->
- `_resolve_main_root` (function) — Resolves the main project root, normalizing a worktree-copy path back to its owning main root so archival writes land outside the worktree being deleted. <!--#62178ee8d8722eaf-->
- `_read_main_flow_id` (function) — Best-effort reads the active `flow_id` from the main project's `se3/state/engine.json`. <!--#811a4a97d453d48b-->
- `_find_worktree_session` (function) — Scans `se3/worktrees/*/.../engine.json` for a worktree session matching the given flow_id (regardless of status), returning its path/branch metadata or None for a main-branch session. <!--#c84340e517fd8c27-->
- `_proc_alive` (function) — Returns whether a pid names a live, non-zombie process (using psutil when available, else `os.kill(pid, 0)`). <!--#afc851908ba03f0c-->
- `_collect_descendants` (function) — Returns the given pids plus all their live recursive descendants, captured up front so a whole process tree can be signalled before the parent is killed and children orphaned. <!--#ef2fff3b2e9e0231-->
- `_any_alive` (function) — Returns whether any pid in the given collection is currently alive. <!--#325a42539d7156fa-->
- `_terminate_one` (function) — Kills a pid and its entire descendant tree with SIGTERM → grace period → SIGKILL, returning (ok, detail) where ok is True only when every process is confirmed dead, so callers can refuse destructive cleanup while a session is still running. <!--#b07a28e92b058f4c-->
- `_read_run_pidfile` (function) — Reads the live-flow pid recorded in `<state_root>/se3/state/run.pid`, returning None if absent/unreadable/empty. <!--#0cb62ebd8d238460-->
- `_pid_is_live_se3_run` (function) — Guards the run.pid marker against staleness by checking the pid is both alive and (via psutil cmdline) actually an `se3 run` process. <!--#b7281b12398e0885-->
- `_proc_has_descendant_in_dir` (function) — Returns whether a process's tree is anchored inside a worktree path (a descendant cwd or any open file under it), used to identify a `--worktree` flow's parent that stays at the main root. <!--#5e59f4d695e1cf19-->
- `_discover_pids_for_flow` (function) — Discovers live `se3 run` pids belonging to a flow via the run.pid marker, an `--flow-id` cmdline arg, matching cwd + on-disk flow_id, or a tree anchored in the worktree path. <!--#baf6b5daf9fa7b8e-->
- `_terminate_session_process` (function) — Resolves the session's target pid(s) — from the caller's hint or by discovering them from the flow id — terminates each via `_terminate_one`, and reports whether all were confirmed dead plus a joined per-pid detail summary. <!--#6086cdc5f12ecb3c-->
