- `_archive_worktree_session` (function) — Archives a worktree session by reusing merge-cleanup machinery: copies the worktree into the archive dir, promotes its engine state, syncs its history, clears the resumable snapshot, and deletes the isolation branch/worktree — each sub-step fault-tolerant, with the destructive branch/worktree removal skipped unless the archive copy succeeded. <!--#7dc967d2bd36d882-->
- `_archive_main_session` (function) — Archives a main-branch (non-worktree) session by clearing the main engine state and the flow's resumable snapshot, refusing the destructive clear unless the main engine.json is positively confirmed to belong to the requested flow. <!--#c725b5b470852516-->
- `_infer_worktree_branch` (function) — Infers the branch checked out at a worktree path by parsing `git worktree list --porcelain`, used when engine.json did not record a worktree_branch. <!--#c0d9e792ab67fa0a-->
- `_sync_worktree_history` (function) — Copies a worktree's per-flow history files into the main project append-only, never overwriting (collisions become `.from-<branch>` sidecars) and skipping byte-identical files for idempotency. <!--#118816cd79f47b90-->
- `_same_file` (function) — Fault-tolerantly returns whether two files have byte-identical content via filecmp. <!--#43129f0a76c9cfd1-->
- `_resolve_history_target` (function) — Resolves where to copy a history file without overwriting, returning the primary path, a uniquified `.from-<branch>` sidecar, or None if an identical copy already exists. <!--#cd2db7cff1fe7516-->
- `_clear_resumable` (function) — Clears the resumable snapshot for a flow_id within a worktree via PersistenceManager. <!--#46bde5cf369c8f72-->
- `_display_results` (function) — Renders the collected (step, status, detail) rows as a styled Rich table with localized headings and OK/SKIP/FAIL status styling. <!--#3d2b950c6b36e0a5-->

### `src/se3/commands/history_cmd.py` (python) — Implements the `se3 history` Typer command group for viewing and managing past flow sessions — listing active/archived/history-only flows, showing detailed flow info (including per-step LLM sessions and JSON output), and restoring flows — with helper functions for datetime/duration formatting, Rich status coloring, and reconstructing flow details from persistence, archive files, and chat history. <!--#bf535102cc02a47a|a350823ac8891575-->
- `get_project_root` (function) — Walks up from the cwd to find the enclosing project root (a `.git` dir or SE3 config) and rebinds the i18n language to that root before returning it. <!--#7f65c0c23bdaba9f-->
- `format_datetime` (function) — Converts an ISO datetime string into a human-readable `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM` format, falling back to the raw string on error. <!--#0f5d25170fb3009a-->
- `format_duration` (function) — Computes and formats the elapsed duration between two ISO timestamps as minutes/hours/days. <!--#212868504b98e854-->
- `list_all_flows` (function) — Returns all flows from every data source via the PersistenceManager. <!--#6ed7050a4e181cb1-->
- `list_archived_flows_from_disk` (function) — Scans `se3/state/archive/engine_*.json`, parsing each archive's timestamp (with mtime fallback) and reading only its header keys, to return a list of archived flow summary dicts, skipping malformed files. <!--#3b5c3967a9474f97-->
- `_detail_from_flow` (function) — Builds a detailed info dict (metadata, progress, steps, chat session count) from a live FlowInstance object. <!--#eeccd00f334be5a5-->
- `_load_archived_flow` (function) — Loads a full FlowInstance for a given flow_id from the archive by delegating to PersistenceManager's split-aware, size-guarded loader, resolving externalized cold step payloads and returning None when a legacy archive can only be read degraded so callers fall back to history-only detail. <!--#9bfb7cbac7889b19-->
- `_detail_from_history` (function) — Builds a minimal flow-detail dict from history-only directory data, reconstructing timestamps and self_check pass numbering. <!--#d657d101098e50a4-->
- `get_flow_detail` (function) — Retrieves a flow's detail dict by searching active, archived, then history-only data sources in order. <!--#f197f9de0c0a77c9-->
- `_status_color` (function) — Maps a flow status string to a Rich display color. <!--#d24adeb7ceeee4ff-->
- `_step_status_color` (function) — Maps a step status string to a Rich display color. <!--#8bb2cea2c4630c05-->
- `_render_flows_table` (function) — Prints a list of flow dicts as a colour-coded Rich table (id, status, truncated description, progress, updated time, source) plus a hint line. <!--#a4ac2cfcb1d583d9-->
- `default_cmd` (function) — The `se3 history` callback that, when no subcommand is given, lists all flows with optional `--active-only`/`--archived-only` filtering and JSON or table output. <!--#83b1fb3853154c77-->
- `list_cmd` (function) — The explicit `history list` subcommand: same as the default callback, listing all/active/archived flows as JSON or a Rich table. <!--#8e030e18e2d18738-->
- `show_cmd` (function) — The `history show` subcommand that resolves a flow id (exact or unique prefix) and prints its details — info table, per-step table with self_check pass numbering, and optionally full LLM call sessions — as text or JSON. <!--#5a86c8bfad1035a0-->
- `_show_detailed_sessions` (function) — Loads a flow's chat history, interleaves the sessions for display, and prints each one's rendered LLM call detail under a rule header. <!--#1e705327054f02e8-->
- `_show_detailed_json` (function) — Outputs a flow's detail plus full chat history as JSON. <!--#3757b11347d645fd-->
- `restore_cmd` (function) — The `history restore` subcommand that validates/resolves a flow id then shells out to `se3 run --resume --flow-id <id>` (or just prints the command under `--dry-run`). <!--#4b8fb2f960cfdd80-->
- `archived_cmd` (function) — The `history archived` subcommand that lists only on-disk archived flows as JSON or a Rich table with status colouring and archive timestamps. <!--#7f63e5d869ada8f7-->

### `src/se3/commands/init_cmd.py` (python) — Implements the `se3 init` CLI command, providing the testable run_init routine and helpers that scaffold a new SE3 project's artifacts (charter, VERSIONS.md, spec templates), initialize a git repository, and manage the .gitignore rules for se3.local.yaml. <!--#ac716f25919f11cb|7949f85b71a6f43b-->
- `_render_template` (function) — Loads a named template file from TEMPLATES_DIR and substitutes `{key}` placeholders via literal string replacement (not str.format) to avoid choking on incidental braces. <!--#760a3c5ebb7fdbb8-->
- `is_git_repository` (function) — Returns True if the given path lies inside an existing git repository by walking up parents looking for a .git directory. <!--#0d770de078464a79-->
- `init_repository` (function) — Runs `git init` in the given directory and returns a (success, message) tuple, handling git-not-installed and command-failure cases. <!--#6268849a7cbf7dd5-->
- `_normalize_gitignore_pattern` (function) — Strips gitignore anchor/recursive-glob/directory markers (`/`, `**/`, trailing `/`) from a pattern so it can be matched with fnmatch. <!--#a6b579bdc1df51ec-->
- `_gitignore_has_local_pattern` (function) — Returns True when an existing .gitignore already ignores se3.local.yaml via a literal or covering glob line, skipping comments and negations. <!--#d075bf1a25d3b705-->
- `_gitignore_has_local_negation` (function) — Returns True when .gitignore contains a narrow `!se3.local.yaml`-style negation that specifically un-ignores the file (but not se3.yaml), signalling a conflicting append should be refused. <!--#75d9f94ea11cafdf-->
- `create_gitignore` (function) — Ensures the project's .gitignore ignores se3.local.yaml, returning a (status, message) pair for one of five outcomes — created, appended, negated (an explicit `!se3.local.yaml` exists, so it refuses to add a conflicting rule), unchanged, or error. <!--#ceb7a4457a705dbc-->
- `_get_charter_template` (function) — Builds the initial se3/charter.md content by delegating to charter.render_charter_template with placeholder fill-in prompts for a fresh project. <!--#6d0eb88f593c231f-->
- `_get_versions_md_template` (function) — Renders the initial VERSIONS.md from the versions_md.md template, filling in project name and current date. <!--#80b454c638f9ac34-->
- `run_init` (function) — Testable core of project initialization: scaffolds se3.yaml, the se3/ runtime dir, se3/charter.md and VERSIONS.md, initializes git if needed, updates .gitignore, and returns a dict of created/skipped paths plus git, gitignore, and se3.local.yaml-shadowing status flags. <!--#ebb27b46d1c6ebaa-->
- `init_cmd` (function) — Typer CLI entry point for `se3 init` that resolves the project root and name, delegates to run_init, and echoes localized results (created/skipped files, VERSIONS.md, git, .gitignore, local-override warning, and next steps). <!--#7919084434aa7ab9-->

### `src/se3/commands/issue_cmd.py` (python) — Defines the Typer CLI command group for issue management (list, show, create, edit, close, reset), backed by IssueManager, with helpers for project-root resolution, Rich color/datetime formatting, external-editor YAML round-tripping, and description resolution from args/stdin/prompt. <!--#379f5cff9540fd3e|491264dd703bea1f-->
- `get_project_root` (function) — Walks up from the cwd to find the project root (a `.git` dir or SE3 config) and rebinds the i18n language to that root before returning it. <!--#7f65c0c23bdaba9f-->
- `_status_color` (function) — Maps an IssueStatus enum value to a Rich color string for table/detail rendering. <!--#440d3dc2ee8afeb2-->
- `_priority_color` (function) — Maps a priority string (critical/high/medium/low) to a Rich color for display. <!--#decc56c974d7023c-->
- `_type_color` (function) — Maps an issue type string (bug/feature/etc.) to a Rich color for display. <!--#bd6f4aa758834f96-->
- `_format_datetime` (function) — Formats a datetime as `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM`, falling back to its string form on error. <!--#622e5ed38538305d-->
- `_get_editor` (function) — Resolves the editor command from $EDITOR, defaulting to `vi` when unset or malformed. <!--#6da17e089dc60c09-->
- `EditorError` (class) — Exception raised when the external editor binary cannot be found or launched. <!--#5e3c13fe86988091-->
- `_open_editor_with_content` (function) — Writes the given text to a temp YAML file, opens it in the user's `$EDITOR`, and returns the edited content (None if the editor exits non-zero, raising `EditorError` if it can't be launched). <!--#98c16e9f3627f5b0-->
- `_issue_to_editor_yaml` (function) — Renders an existing Issue as a human-editable YAML template containing only editable fields plus a read-only id. <!--#b0abf28b8150969b-->
- `_new_issue_editor_yaml` (function) — Generates a blank YAML template for creating a new issue via the external editor. <!--#f32e849fd690fa51-->
- `_parse_edited_issue_yaml` (function) — Parses editor-returned YAML into a dict, raising `ValueError` if it is malformed, empty, or missing a non-blank description. <!--#b0bc2963e0175f06-->
- `default_cmd` (function) — Default callback that lists open issues when no subcommand is invoked. <!--#78df7f33146891ba-->
- `list_cmd` (function) — The `issue list` command: validates the `--source` filter, queries `IssueManager`, and renders matching issues as a colour-coded Rich table. <!--#069c51df462c5f38-->
- `show_cmd` (function) — The `issue show` command: loads one issue by id and prints its full details in a colour-coded block, exiting 1 if not found. <!--#fa4bc9120a3d8a64-->
- `create_cmd` (function) — The `issue create` command: builds a new human-sourced issue from a `--editor` YAML template or from a positional/stdin/interactive description plus metadata options. <!--#6533f3ebd5b4bf04-->
- `_resolve_description` (function) — Resolves an issue description from (in priority order) the positional argument, piped stdin, or an interactive multiline prompt, returning None on cancellation and raising `ValueError` when empty. <!--#b14899d61ce9b0e5-->
- `edit_cmd` (function) — The `issue edit` command: round-trips an existing issue through `$EDITOR` as YAML and applies every editable field back via `update_fields`, treating removed keys as cleared. <!--#84fcb082db8fcf51-->
- `close_cmd` (function) — The `issue close` command: closes an issue by id with an optional `--reason`, exiting 1 on error. <!--#4befdf6b1706c9ed-->
- `reset_cmd` (function) — The `issue reset` command: moves an in-progress issue back to open status, exiting 1 on error. <!--#d55b458abfe4d14a-->

### `src/se3/commands/merge_cmd.py` (python) — The `se3 merge` CLI command module that validates branch names and a clean/idle working tree, drives the sequential integrate()→reconcile() flow to merge branches, reconcile the release version, and optionally stash/deferred-clean/backfill resolved source issues, with a suite of git and reporting helpers that surface partial-sync signals, human-escalation artifacts, and failure titles. <!--#8c7f14dcc6fa5909|6558dc9931761215-->
- `_run_git` (function) — Thin wrapper that runs a git subcommand in a given project root via subprocess, capturing output with configurable check/timeout. <!--#8bdb8c6f53ca2c0b-->
- `_resolve_git_dir` (function) — Resolves the real git directory (handling linked worktrees where .git is a pointer file) via `git rev-parse --git-dir`, returning None if unavailable. <!--#39d970125e3b9d76-->
- `_is_working_tree_clean` (function) — Returns whether the working tree has no uncommitted tracked changes and no in-progress git operation, ignoring untracked files. <!--#0b796ef88d8b0242-->
- `_git_operation_in_progress` (function) — Detects whether git is mid-merge/cherry-pick/revert/rebase by checking for the corresponding marker files in the git directory. <!--#bfe6f2d49513bda6-->
- `_branch_exists` (function) — Checks whether a local branch exists via `git show-ref`, failing closed (False) on any infrastructure error so indeterminate refs are refused. <!--#e9891f12d3b59534-->
- `validate_branch_names` (function) — Validates user-supplied branch names before any git command runs, rejecting empty/leading-dash/shell-metachar/git-ref-invalid names and raising a ValueError that lists each rejected name and the rule it broke. <!--#f281be8158f162ea-->
- `_append_runtime_sync_lines` (function) — Renders all runtime-sync signals (skipped branches/files, idempotent bypasses, discarded tier-B, tier-A collisions) plus committed issue renumbers and ambiguous issue references into the merge summary lines, on both success and failure paths. <!--#d17adf52b3eb8264-->
- `_append_human_call_lines` (function) — Renders the human-escalation recovery block for a failure report — the real se3/calls/ file path in normal mode, or the recorded escalation payload plus a 'rerun se3 merge' instruction in suppress/library mode where no call file exists. <!--#c847fdd1b88c9f6a-->
- `_split_merged_buckets` (function) — Splits a merge report's merged branches into newly-merged versus already-an-ancestor buckets, with a git-ancestry fallback for legacy reports. <!--#85e42d3a5d245a8d-->
- `_append_split_branch_lines` (function) — Appends the per-bucket listings of newly-merged versus already-ancestor branches to the summary lines. <!--#b2b30c538c4b00fc-->
- `_has_user_uncommitted_changes` (function) — Returns whether the user has genuine working-tree WIP (tracked or untracked), filtering out SE3's own runtime artifacts, to decide if a fast-strategy pre-stash is needed. <!--#bf31679b6ab5f671-->
- `_fast_stash_dirty` (function) — Stashes a dirty working tree under a labeled se3-pre-fast-merge stash before a fast-strategy merge, returning the stash label or None (best-effort; failures only warn). <!--#57aa3f6ed62d0ec4-->
- `_fast_stash_pop` (function) — Pops the labeled pre-merge stash through the shared no-data-loss recovery path (archive-before-drop, LLM conflict resolution, audit issue on incomplete recovery), returning True when recovery did not finalize so the caller must not report clean success. <!--#6b38b8eb21612c0c-->
- `_map_branches_to_source_issues` (function) — Captures a {branch: source_issue_id} mapping (via a lazy run.py worktree scanner) before the merge runs, so the link survives after --delete-merged removes each worktree's engine.json; best-effort, never raises. <!--#e2e3917a9c4cece0-->
- `_backfill_resolved_source_issues` (function) — The single idempotent choke point that transitions the source issues of successfully-merged (newly-merged or already-ancestor) branches from IN_PROGRESS to RESOLVED, swallowing all errors so it can never alter the merge exit code. <!--#ba318c9bd4d86fe9-->
- `_acquire_merge_lock_with_callbacks` (function) — Helper that acquires the main-worktree merge lock in blocking mode, optionally probing non-blocking first so it can fire 'waiting'/'acquired' callbacks only when the caller must genuinely queue behind a live holder (never for a free or stale lock), swallowing callback exceptions. <!--#7316d471e91dc742-->
- `_run_deferred_branch_cleanup` (function) — Deletes the merged source branches only after the reconcile half has settled, so a reconcile fault leaves branches intact and the whole command stays re-runnable. <!--#86d3e1b62769e143-->
- `run_merge` (function) — Top-level entry point of the `se3 merge` command: validates branches and working-tree state, then drives the orchestrator's integrate() -> reconcile() sequence (merge invariants then version release), renders the summary, runs deferred cleanup, and returns the exit code. <!--#f61d726c7633e302-->
- `_failure_title_and_summary` (function) — Maps a merge failure_reason code (including compound prefixes like `fast_abort: <stderr>`) to the localized (title, first summary line) pair so the operator sees which category of failure occurred. <!--#96819c5c2aad20e0-->

### `src/se3/commands/merge_respond.py` (python) — The `se3 merge-respond` command module that processes MCP call/response files for paused merge conflicts, dispatching on the user's accept/abort/manual choice under a project-wide merge lock while enforcing spec guardrails, version-bump, and strict-placeholder checks. <!--#c497396171b2cff5|36ad4e88dda4d061-->
- `_is_spec_path` (function) — Thin wrapper that delegates se3 spec-file path detection to the canonical implementation in `se3.engine.merge.guardrails` so the merge subsystem shares one detector. <!--#92631e060c96b704-->
- `_first_parent_sha` (function) — Returns the first-parent SHA of HEAD via `git rev-list --parents`, treating octopus merges like 2-parent merges and raising RuntimeError on git failure or a parentless root commit. <!--#b8325d34356dfe2f-->
- `_head_parent_count` (function) — Returns HEAD's parent count for octopus-merge detection, distinguishing a legitimate `0` (root commit) from `None` (undetermined due to a transient git failure). <!--#a7aa6eaf6327be38-->
- `_extract_version_from_string` (function) — Parses a version string out of TOML (`pyproject.toml`) or JSON (`package.json`) content, returning None (and warning on TOML parse failure) when no version can be extracted. <!--#0322f245c4574684-->
- `_check_version_unchanged` (function) — Compares the version field in pyproject.toml/package.json between a pre-merge SHA and HEAD, returning a localized error message when the version was left unchanged or the version file became unparseable, and None otherwise. <!--#560120142d8ca4e5-->
- `process_merge_response` (function) — Public entry point for `se3 merge-respond`: resolves the project root and the main-repo merge lock, acquires it in blocking mode, and delegates to the locked handler, rendering localized errors for a missing call file or lock busy/stale conditions. <!--#d4373784e32adc94-->
- `_verify_pending_guardrails` (function) — Handles re-entry on a parked manual-resolution merge by reading the .pending_guardrails marker, checking the user actually made exactly one new commit, running MergeGuardrailsCheck against it, and either clearing the marker on success or stashing work and hard-resetting HEAD to the pre-merge SHA on violation. <!--#fc5ebfb99e551e6e-->
- `_process_merge_response_locked` (function) — Under the merge lock, dispatches a merge-conflict response: routes pending-guardrails re-entries, parses and validates the call/.response files and the accept/abort/manual choice, refuses strict-mode placeholder or orphan-spec-violating content, and writes the resolved file contents back to the working tree. <!--#cf0cd5601f00a1db-->

### `src/se3/commands/migrate_cmd.py` (python) — Implements the `se3 migrate` command as a registry-based, fault-tolerant migration channel whose shipped `spec-to-new-system` migrator runs a salvage-first pipeline that assembles a charter, colocates why/intent comments into source, builds the code-index, then deletes the retired `se3/specs/` tree and rewrites `.gitignore` — all as one uncommitted, git-revertable working-tree change. <!--#f6158628771df1a0|89764abbafbff369-->
- `ColocatedWhy` (class) — Dataclass pairing a project-relative source file path with a prose why/intent fragment to be inserted into that file as a comment. <!--#cfd51d5498faf0ca-->
- `SalvageInput` (class) — Dataclass bundling everything the salvager needs (project root, base spec text, non-base spec corpus, admission standard, charter template, project name) so the salvager does no discovery of its own. <!--#a03d93eb1581a162-->
- `SalvageResult` (class) — Dataclass holding the salvaged product: the full assembled charter body, the code-bound colocations, and advisory notes for the reviewer. <!--#a748fffc532da172-->
- `Migrator` (class) — A dataclass describing one registered migration: its id, an i18n key for its human-readable description, and the callable that runs it and returns a MigrationReport. <!--#0de3df9b26a5406a-->
- `register_migrator` (function) — Registers a migrator under its unique id in the MIGRATORS registry, raising on duplicate ids. <!--#29ecb08e2108fe0e-->
- `get_migrator` (function) — Looks up and returns a registered migrator by id, or None if not found. <!--#f654e0789ae24328-->
- `list_migrators` (function) — Returns all registered migrators sorted by id. <!--#f112e419974b0265-->
- `StepOutcome` (class) — Dataclass recording one pipeline step's name, status (OK/SKIP/FAIL), and detail string. <!--#b595caa244d380a1-->
- `MigrationReport` (class) — Dataclass accumulating per-step outcomes and notes, exposing overall success (`ok`) and a process `exit_code`. <!--#624b9b55c9e82f75-->
  - `MigrationReport.add` (method) — Appends a StepOutcome with the given name, status, and detail to the report. <!--#5b0f45dfab323d34-->
  - `MigrationReport.ok` (method) — Property that is True only when no recorded step has FAIL status. <!--#c434422828d4983f-->
  - `MigrationReport.exit_code` (method) — Property returning process exit code 0 on success, 1 on any failure. <!--#4299b082776eeaeb-->
- `_load_spec_corpus` (function) — Tolerantly loads the spec corpus from a specs directory, returning the base spec text and a {name: text} map of non-base specs while skipping unreadable, hidden, and underscore-prefixed entries. <!--#1727d96aa1f76583-->
- `_project_name_from_base` (function) — Best-effort extraction of the project name from the base spec's title line, with a fallback. <!--#4208a2781e9fec9b-->
- `_make_llm_salvager` (function) — Builds the default LLM-backed salvager closure that assembles the charter from the base spec plus a digest of other specs (pass A) and extracts file-bound why/intent from each non-base spec (pass B), degrading gracefully on any LLM failure. <!--#9d88188a314e8079-->
- `_strip_code_fence` (function) — Strips a single wrapping triple-backtick code fence from a text body if present. <!--#620f4e9b5e0d1c5d-->
- `_fallback_charter` (function) — Produces a degraded but lossless charter — the rendered template plus the base spec verbatim under a loud review banner — when LLM assembly is unavailable. <!--#13cb999b7c39d7eb-->
- `_comment_prefix` (function) — Returns the line-comment prefix for a file based on its extension, defaulting to `#`. <!--#edaf021548cf685e-->
- `_render_why_comment` (function) — Renders a why/intent fragment into a list of commented lines prefixed by the WHY marker. <!--#4017fdd2f97275ce-->
- `_insert_why_comment` (function) — Inserts a rendered why-comment block at a safe top-of-file location, preserving any leading shebang. <!--#0385c973b5aaea6c-->
- `_apply_colocations` (function) — Writes each salvaged why-comment into its target source file, returning how many were applied plus reasons for any skipped (missing or unreadable) targets instead of aborting. <!--#35856e640a3e605f-->
- `_write_charter_once` (function) — Writes the fully-assembled charter body to se3/charter.md in a single atomic write with no overwrite window. <!--#5542c0bfe1b1099e-->
- `_tracked_toplevel_whitelists` (function) — Helper that runs `git ls-files` to enumerate all tracked top-level paths and returns `!/<name>` whitelist lines (dirs with trailing slash, .gitignore first), or None if git is unavailable so callers won't add a root default-deny without existence protection. <!--#a1fd1234efe43966-->
- `_rewrite_gitignore` (function) — Idempotently rewrites the project's .gitignore to whitelist code-index/charter, drop the retired specs whitelist, and switch the root to default-deny (`/*`) guarded by explicit whitelists for every currently-tracked top-level path. <!--#f96317d5e262f4ad-->
- `run_spec_to_new_system` (function) — Runs the one-shot spec→new-system migration pipeline (charter assembly, why-comment colocation, code-index build, spec deletion gated on confirmed salvage, .gitignore rewrite), each step tolerant, leaving all changes uncommitted in the working tree. <!--#9df84c42b1df1df3-->
- `_display_report` (function) — Renders a MigrationReport as a Rich table of step/status/detail rows plus any accumulated notes. <!--#1d18b5d52d53ae61-->
- `list_command` (function) — CLI subcommand that prints a table of the registered migrations (id and description), or a message when none exist. <!--#7d771de463846e0a-->
- `run_command` (function) — CLI subcommand that resolves the project root (binding the UI language), looks up the named migrator, runs it with the --no-delete-specs flag, displays the report, and exits with the report's status code. <!--#8d1c2bf9d7e0fd75-->

### `src/se3/commands/run.py` (python) — Implements the `se3 run` CLI command — SE3 3.0's unified entry point that creates or resumes a flow, then drives it step-by-step through the state machine (dispatching step handlers, handling CONFIRM gates and interactive/web-console answers, emitting events to CLI/history/JSON sinks, and handling Ctrl-C interrupts). <!--#db314fe11de97381|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/se3/commands/salvage_cmd.py` (python) — The SE3 `salvage` command that rescues work from abnormally terminated sessions by running a fault-tolerant pipeline — tolerantly loading session state, assessing the git diff, committing uncommitted changes, creating tracking issues for unfinished work, and archiving the session — then reports per-step outcomes in a Rich table. <!--#57ec66f0bd7c74e6|c03e0c8fc18c4581-->
- `salvage` (function) — Entry point for the `salvage` command: locates the project root, re-binds the i18n language to it, then runs five independently error-guarded recovery steps (read session state, assess git diff, commit changes, create salvage issues, archive the session), prints a summary table, and returns 1 if any step failed. <!--#41f5d396f4efd5dd-->
- `_find_project_root` (function) — Walks up from the current directory to locate the project root by finding a .git directory or an SE3 config file. <!--#3c8eb6032ea041a2-->
- `_load_session` (function) — Tolerantly loads the persisted flow/session state via PersistenceManager, returning the FlowInstance (or None) plus any warnings. <!--#8c64b4dd4cc982ab-->
- `_assess_git_diff` (function) — Runs git status/diff to collect a dict of uncommitted-change info (status lines, changed file count/list, diff stat, truncated diff summary). <!--#c6bf085dac297a44-->
- `_commit_changes` (function) — Stages and commits all uncommitted changes with a generated `[salvage]` message, returning the new commit hash (or None if nothing to commit). <!--#2047b9ff2adde17e-->
- `_create_salvage_issues` (function) — Creates tracking issues for unfinished work, summarizing flow step history, interruption point, and changed files (or just changed files when no session state exists). <!--#782c49e6c54a7315-->
- `_archive_session` (function) — Clears the persisted session state and its per-flow resumable snapshot so the dispositioned flow is no longer resumable, returning whether anything was archived. <!--#1a0e70dd930dbfb2-->
- `_display_results` (function) — Renders the collected (step, status, detail) tuples from the salvage pipeline as a localized Rich table with colour-styled OK/SKIP/FAIL statuses. <!--#4c27b4a953753f03-->

### `src/se3/commands/worktree_cmd.py` (python) — The `se3 worktree gc` CLI command group — a thin render/exit-code shell over the engine's worktree garbage collector that reclaims leaked terminal `se3 run --worktree` runs and prints a three-part Rich report (archived/reclaimed, retained-unmerged branches, skips/errors), with a byte-formatting helper. <!--#c50c25387a0323d3|0f35a4dcafa2f080-->
- `_format_bytes` (function) — Helper that formats a raw byte count into a compact human-readable size string using binary (1024-based) units from B up to TB. <!--#9cafc2a1079fcdba-->
- `gc_command` (function) — Typer CLI command `se3 worktree gc` that sweeps leaked terminal `run --worktree` runs (archiving them, reclaiming space, and deleting only provably-merged branches), renders the resulting report as localized Rich tables covering archived/retained-unmerged/skipped/errored runs, and exits non-zero when any run errored. <!--#f0090f983c63f8ea-->

## `src/se3/commands/merge/` — Foundation infrastructure package for the SE3 merge subsystem, bundling intentionally import-light building blocks — typed Result/report models, a typed failure-reason enum with legacy-string converters, an fcntl-based exclusive merge lock, an append-only JSONL LLM-call tracer, a secret redactor for logs/traces, and post-condition assertions — that the merge orchestrator, CLI entry points, and engine internals reuse. <!--#62f77092011b0a9b|57c639818844852a-->

### `src/se3/commands/merge/__init__.py` (python) — Package init for the SE3 merge subsystem's foundation infrastructure, re-exporting the lightweight (no heavy git/LLM import cost) building blocks—typed Result models, failure-reason enums, concurrency locking, per-LLM-call tracing, secret redaction, and post-condition assertions—consumed by the merge orchestrator, CLI entry points, and engine internals. <!--#cf78c40f0e1bc931|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/se3/commands/merge/failure_reason.py` (python) — Defines the FailureReason IntEnum (a typed, subsystem-grouped catalog of every merge-orchestration failure/pause mode) plus bidirectional converters (from_legacy_string/to_legacy_string and a legacy_string property) that translate between the enum and the orchestrator's older compound 'prefix: detail' string surface, backed by a legacy-string map and a longest-first-ordered compound-prefix table guarded by a defensive ordering assertion. <!--#3d617f82135b7ccd|216dcac12bc54b0b-->
- `FailureReason` (class) — IntEnum cataloguing every way a merge orchestration can fail or pause, with gap-aware numeric codes grouped by subsystem (git merge, LLM conflict resolution, guardrails, rollback, postconditions, repo state, locking) and a `legacy_string` property yielding the stable lower-cased name for persistence. <!--#00323225ea3dd422-->
  - `FailureReason.legacy_string` (method) — Property returning the canonical legacy-string spelling of a reason as its lower-cased enum name, without any compound diagnostic detail. <!--#c0b7d910ff47c044-->
- `_assert_compound_prefix_order_longest_first` (function) — Test-importable defensive assertion that verifies the _COMPOUND_PREFIXES list is ordered longest-first so no shorter prefix can silently shadow a longer one during matching. <!--#a215f7b873024d92-->
- `from_legacy_string` (function) — Translates a legacy failure_reason string (None, empty, bare reason, or compound 'prefix: detail' form) into a (FailureReason, detail) tuple, falling back to UNEXPECTED with the raw text preserved as detail. <!--#14977706905a8d7c-->
- `to_legacy_string` (function) — Renders a FailureReason back into its legacy string form, mapping None to None and FailureReason.NONE to an empty string to preserve round-trip semantics. <!--#6e4cedb31364c905-->

### `src/se3/commands/merge/llm_trace.py` (python) — Defines an append-only JSONL LLM-call tracer for the merge command, pairing an `LLMCallRecord` dataclass (per-call metadata plus dict serialization) with a thread-safe `LLMTrace` writer that opens, size-rotates, batch-fsyncs, and closes trace files while recording each call as a line, usable directly or as a context manager. <!--#8150d7f2ad960f9f|cd3eec9a59d5ee7c-->
- `LLMCallRecord` (class) — Dataclass capturing a single LLM call's metadata (sequence, timestamp, agent, token estimate, prompt/response previews, duration, outcome, error, and arbitrary meta). <!--#6f024f9b4e32d840-->
  - `LLMCallRecord.to_dict` (method) — Serializes the call record into a plain dict ready for JSON encoding into a trace line. <!--#66bd42648a913924-->
- `LLMTrace` (class) — Thread-safe (single-process) append-only JSONL writer that records LLM calls, rotating files by size and batching fsync for durability without IO amplification. <!--#37656d149fdecb08-->
  - `LLMTrace.__init__` (method) — Configures the trace writer with project root, target directory, max file size, and fsync batching thresholds, initializing counters and the lock. <!--#a4d8a0e7c57bdd80-->
  - `LLMTrace._ensure_dir` (method) — Creates the trace output directory (and parents) if it does not yet exist. <!--#bcc55e51d2a7b05f-->
  - `LLMTrace._new_file_path` (method) — Generates a unique rotation-counter-suffixed, UTC-timestamped JSONL file path for a new trace file. <!--#dc1884017308886f-->
  - `LLMTrace._rotate_if_needed` (method) — Closes and reopens a fresh trace file once the current one exceeds the configured size limit. <!--#41851d34db6d1884-->
  - `LLMTrace._open_file` (method) — Ensures the directory exists and opens a new trace file for writing at a freshly generated path. <!--#3f16d51fc8ed6b8e-->
  - `LLMTrace._fsync_now` (method) — Forces a flush plus os.fsync of the current file and resets the fsync throttle counters. <!--#585ae5672b2847f9-->
  - `LLMTrace._close_file` (method) — Flushes the tail to disk via fsync and closes the current trace file so no buffered record is lost. <!--#9b59062c89518c78-->
  - `LLMTrace.start` (method) — Idempotently opens the initial trace file and marks the writer as started. <!--#6d6bb5dfdab16afe-->
  - `LLMTrace.stop` (method) — Closes the trace file (forcing a final fsync) and marks the writer as stopped. <!--#e7137789ab5bc682-->
  - `LLMTrace.record` (method) — Appends one LLM call as a JSONL line (truncating previews, rotating if needed, flushing, and conditionally fsyncing) and returns its sequence number. <!--#ca81df8dded5e875-->
  - `LLMTrace.__enter__` (method) — Context-manager entry that starts the trace and returns the instance. <!--#d1285a98c0961099-->
  - `LLMTrace.__exit__` (method) — Context-manager exit that stops the trace, ensuring the file is closed and synced. <!--#53eaf3af0d2e4827-->

### `src/se3/commands/merge/merge_lock.py` (python) — An fcntl.flock-based exclusive merge lock module providing the MergeLock dataclass (blocking/non-blocking acquire, PID-record management, stale-lock detection and breaking) plus BusyStale exceptions, inspection/release helpers, and an acquire_merge_lock convenience factory. <!--#fdec46d96355d4a4|56091478ba86b620-->
- `is_lock_held_in_process` (function) — Advisory check (no syscalls) that returns whether the current process already holds the merge lock, by consulting an in-memory registry of resolved lock paths. <!--#2bb6fc9e0e7d60d8-->
- `_stale_break_jitter` (function) — Returns a random fraction in [0,1) for stale-break backoff jitter, wrapped as a function so tests can monkeypatch it deterministically. <!--#8652290c3ab2f41a-->
- `MergeLockBusy` (class) — Exception raised when another live process currently holds the merge lock (non-blocking mode), carrying the lock file path and optional holder PID. <!--#1210b7f477ae2254-->
  - `MergeLockBusy.__init__` (method) — Stores the lock file and holder PID and builds a human-readable message that appends the PID when known. <!--#aafc5beb7625e77f-->
- `MergeLockStale` (class) — Exception signaling the lock file appears stale (holder PID absent, no PID recorded, or unparseable/corrupt), letting callers decide whether to break and retry. <!--#4e18a8971b831131-->
  - `MergeLockStale.__init__` (method) — Records the lock file, optional holder PID, and corrupt flag, composing a message that distinguishes dead-holder, empty-record, and corrupt-record cases. <!--#3058bbf691add9d9-->
- `MergeLock` (class) — Dataclass representing an exclusive merge lock over a file via fcntl.flock, providing acquire/release, blocking/non-blocking modes, PID record management, and stale-lock breaking. <!--#71bb3a553ee7ee70-->
  - `MergeLock.__post_init__` (method) — Resolves the configured lock_path against the project root (unless already absolute) into the instance's _resolved_path. <!--#0949665977013300-->
  - `MergeLock.held` (method) — Property reporting whether this specific instance currently owns an open, acquired lock file descriptor. <!--#69f47245bd20560f-->
  - `MergeLock._read_holder_pid` (method) — Reads the fixed-width PID record from the lock file (using O_NOFOLLOW, capped length), returning the holder PID or None and setting _last_read_corrupt when the bytes are unparseable. <!--#cc09b99d86e82597-->
  - `MergeLock._write_pid` (method) — Writes the current process's fixed-width PID record into the held lock fd via pwrite-then-truncate-then-fsync, avoiding any transient empty state for concurrent readers. <!--#04b2b4102bf2452e-->
  - `MergeLock._is_pid_alive` (method) — Probes whether a PID exists using signal 0, treating ESRCH as dead and EPERM (and success) as alive, to drive stale-lock decisions. <!--#009ece408997f3a8-->
  - `MergeLock._try_break_stale_and_acquire` (method) — Encapsulates the bounded, jittered unlink-then-reacquire retry loop for breaking a stale lock, returning the new fd or raising MergeLockBusy/OSError on failure. <!--#9693dfe29daac6dc-->
  - `MergeLock.acquire` (method) — Acquires the exclusive lock, choosing blocking LOCK_EX queueing or non-blocking fail-fast with stale detection and optional break_stale recovery, then records this process's PID. <!--#28984568b2a7ed6e-->
  - `MergeLock.release` (method) — Releases the flock, closes the file descriptor, and removes the path from the in-process held-locks registry, idempotently. <!--#60e5949e76255cfe-->
  - `MergeLock.__enter__` (method) — Context-manager entry that acquires the lock using the instance's configured blocking default and returns self. <!--#4b90db2205610f11-->
  - `MergeLock.__exit__` (method) — Context-manager exit that releases the lock. <!--#8f781b847877252c-->
- `LockStatus` (class) — Read-only snapshot dataclass of the lock file's state (existence, holder PID, liveness, staleness, corruption) shared by inspection and release logic. <!--#713c00e0cca2a814-->
- `ReleaseOutcome` (class) — Result dataclass of a manual release decision, holding an exit code, the observed LockStatus, and a categorical action label. <!--#ecd40e485c6e7e55-->
- `inspect_lock` (function) — Performs a write-free probe of the lock file, reusing MergeLock's PID-read and liveness checks to produce a LockStatus snapshot. <!--#358862de19df1f56-->
- `break_lock_file` (function) — Unlinks the lock file (the only way an external process can clear an flock-held lock), returning whether a file was actually removed. <!--#fcf13b779b14aba0-->
- `release_merge_lock` (function) — Pure decision logic for a manual lock release that inspects state and removes the file for stale or force cases while refusing to evict a live holder without force. <!--#8b93ee87f470279b-->
- `_lock_file_removed` (function) — Removes the lock file and re-probes the path to confirm it is actually gone, distinguishing real removal from a swallowed permission error. <!--#81738d415b225947-->
- `acquire_merge_lock` (function) — function acquire_merge_lock <!--#345e208a00ddaf0b-->

### `src/se3/commands/merge/postcondition.py` (python) — Post-condition assertions verifying every merge the orchestrator deems successful: that the branch is an ancestor of HEAD, that HEAD is a merge commit (allowing no-ops and optional fix-up commits), and that the version file was bumped to the expected value, each violation raising a typed PostConditionViolated with hardening (bounded version-file reads, git timeouts, parent-count safety caps) so failures route to the correct diagnostic bucket. <!--#b734fc587adf0d52|53dfd51b51cc4b95-->
- `_bounded_read_version_file` (function) — Reads a version file with size, duration, and regular-file-only guards so a pathological or streaming version file cannot hang or OOM the post-merge check. <!--#b4ca393bdf6263b1-->
- `PostConditionViolated` (class) — RuntimeError raised when a post-condition fails, carrying a typed FailureReason plus the offending branch and diagnostic detail so callers can route the failure. <!--#0da431b628261e1a-->
  - `PostConditionViolated.__init__` (method) — Constructs the exception from a FailureReason, optional branch, and detail string, assembling them into a human-readable message. <!--#f70bb7761adb86d6-->
- `CorruptCommitGraphError` (class) — RuntimeError signalling that a commit's parent count hit the safety cap, indicating a malformed commit graph rather than a non-merge commit. <!--#1294b6b69466ee14-->
  - `CorruptCommitGraphError.__init__` (method) — Builds the corrupt-graph error from the offending ref and the parent-count cap that was exceeded. <!--#fb3fa4e6616ab5a0-->
- `_run_git` (function) — Helper that runs a git subcommand in the project root with captured output, a timeout, and disabled stdin, returning the CompletedProcess. <!--#aec14a50bb4519da-->
- `assert_branch_merged` (function) — Post-condition that a branch is an ancestor of HEAD via git merge-base --is-ancestor, distinguishing a definitive not-merged verdict from unresolvable git errors. <!--#4596f5a4b25b218b-->
- `_resolve_parent_count_cap` (function) — Returns the parent-count safety cap, defaulting to 64 but honoring the SE3_MERGE_PARENT_COUNT_CAP environment override with validation. <!--#a59ca6631aa99934-->
- `_count_parents` (function) — Counts a ref's parents via repeated rev-parse --verify ref^N, reporting whether the ref itself resolves and raising CorruptCommitGraphError past the safety cap. <!--#c41f49fe5bd6b316-->
- `assert_head_is_merge_commit` (function) — Post-condition that HEAD is a merge commit (enough parents), with opt-in tolerance for fix-up commits stacked on top of the merge up to a configurable depth. <!--#1fa9b990dc66c18d-->
- `assert_version_bumped` (function) — Post-condition that the version file contains the expected version, parsing TOML/JSON to avoid substring false-positives and optionally cross-checking the committed HEAD tree. <!--#2da0110c10472f23-->
- `_assert_committed_version_matches` (function) — Verifies HEAD's committed version file matches the expected version, distinguishing transient git-plumbing failures from positive commit-hook tampering signals. <!--#5a603880f7db03aa-->
- `check_all` (function) — Convenience entry-point that runs all applicable post-condition checks (ancestry, merge-commit shape when not a no-op, and version bump when expected) for a merged branch. <!--#4252328eeb6514ee-->

### `src/se3/commands/merge/result_model.py` (python) — Defines the typed result models for the merge orchestrator — EvidenceRecord for fail-fast guardrail-violation evidence, MergeOutcome for a single branch's terminal result, and MergeReport as the typed successor to the legacy orchestrator.MergeReport with semantically split branch buckets, typed failure reasons, backward-compatibility aliases, and legacy-dict serialization. <!--#68890edcfe15c5a4|c206b4a2bd0ae05b-->
- `EvidenceRecord` (class) — A dataclass enumerating every recognized guardrail-violation evidence field (pairing, deletion, topology, size, etc.) that fails fast on unknown keys and round-trips to/from plain dicts for backward compatibility. <!--#bcfcb240c97cf3e0-->
  - `EvidenceRecord.to_dict` (method) — Serializes the evidence record to a plain dict, omitting fields whose value is None, for JSON-persisted call files and log entries. <!--#a62c823b0bddf6a4-->
  - `EvidenceRecord.from_dict` (method) — Classmethod that constructs an EvidenceRecord from a dict (returning None for empty input), letting unknown keys raise TypeError as the fail-fast behavior. <!--#05d79f59c6187865-->
- `MergeOutcome` (class) — A dataclass holding the terminal outcome of a single branch merge attempt, including success, typed failure reason, ancestor/warning flags, merge commit SHA, and the git_merge_succeeded distinction. <!--#7cb496de0e157739-->
- `MergeReport` (class) — A dataclass capturing the full result of a merge orchestration run — the typed successor to the legacy orchestrator.MergeReport — with semantically split branch-outcome buckets, a typed FailureReason, per-branch outcomes, version aggregation, cleanup, runtime-sync, committed-issue renumbering, and rollback/bump diagnostics. <!--#8d0b1e902862f801-->
  - `MergeReport.failure_reason_enum` (method) — Property returning the typed FailureReason for the report, parsing a legacy string (or passing through an existing enum) and mapping unknown strings to UNEXPECTED. <!--#ee363d13b2f99528-->
  - `MergeReport.add_outcome` (method) — Appends a branch outcome and routes it into the appropriate summary bucket (already-ancestor, newly-merged, with-warnings) while recording the first failed branch. <!--#938bedc6b8a3486a-->
  - `MergeReport.newly_merged` (method) — Backward-compatibility alias property returning newly_merged_branches. <!--#2ddc24cb4dd75dff-->
  - `MergeReport.already_merged` (method) — Backward-compatibility alias property returning already_ancestor_branches. <!--#7aa051f1613716f0-->
  - `MergeReport.all_merged_branches` (method) — Returns the combined backward-compatible view of all branches that were newly merged, already ancestors, or merged with warnings. <!--#cd3e3997fa557f3e-->
  - `MergeReport.call_file_str` (method) — Returns the human-call file path as a string or actual None, avoiding the legacy 'Call file: None' rendering bug. <!--#9ece35c501a4547a-->
  - `MergeReport.to_legacy_dict` (method) — Serializes the typed MergeReport into a plain dict matching the legacy orchestrator.MergeReport shape (normalizing FailureReason enums to legacy strings and flattening records) for JSON persistence, test fixtures, and un-migrated log consumers. <!--#9e8556acf438cce8-->

### `src/se3/commands/merge/secret_redact.py` (python) — A secret-redaction utility that detects and masks common secret patterns (API keys, bearer/GitHub/PyPI tokens, password fields) in text and git diffs before they are written to merge logs and traces, via a configurable thread-safe SecretRedactor class, an allowlist for intentional fake secrets, and module-level convenience functions backed by a cached default redactor. <!--#b643e520097c799f|d4452133f4d3d1d7-->
- `RedactConfig` (class) — Dataclass holding redaction configuration — an allowlist of exempt strings, extra regex/replacement patterns, and a preview length. <!--#59b0056d5d87e29e-->
- `SecretRedactor` (class) — Stateful, thread-safe redactor that applies the built-in plus configured patterns to mask secrets in text and diffs, restoring allowlisted fakes. <!--#c18072db25b8f560-->
  - `SecretRedactor.__init__` (method) — Initializes the redactor with a config and combines the default patterns with any configured extra patterns. <!--#85ccebb496ffc9a9-->
  - `SecretRedactor.redact` (method) — Applies all redaction patterns to a string, then restores any allowlisted values that were accidentally masked. <!--#fa9c0623cedad71a-->
  - `SecretRedactor._mask_fake` (method) — Static helper that runs the default patterns over a single known-fake value to compute its masked form for allowlist restoration. <!--#4fdd627f585d7c01-->
  - `SecretRedactor.redact_diff` (method) — Redacts secrets in a git diff line-by-line so diff markers and structure are preserved. <!--#eadedc33a38bbaa8-->
- `_get_default` (function) — Lazily constructs and caches a module-level default SecretRedactor singleton. <!--#a18335149677cff0-->
- `redact_text` (function) — Module-level convenience function that redacts secrets from text using the default redactor. <!--#ae56d65c5e441865-->
- `redact_diff` (function) — Module-level convenience function that redacts secrets from a git diff using the default redactor. <!--#c2475d3670220c02-->

## `src/se3/core/` — SE3's shared core utilities package, currently housing a small text-formatting helper (truncate_preview) for consistent console previews, providing a home for cross-cutting utility functions used framework-wide. <!--#cd265b7e389a08e3|45daffb5f1e58451-->

### `src/se3/core/__init__.py` (python) — Package initializer marking `src/se3/core` as the home for SE3's shared core utilities, containing only a module docstring and no runtime code. <!--#48e466c636635268|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/se3/core/utils.py` (python) — A shared SE3 core utilities module providing truncate_preview, which shortens overlong text to a maximum length with an appended ellipsis for consistent console preview formatting. <!--#e3c9d16af367d231|63fffa8987576585-->
- `truncate_preview` (function) — Truncates a string to a maximum length and appends an ellipsis indicator, returning the text unchanged when it already fits, for consistent text previews in console output. <!--#ae15e4e349281ce9-->

## `src/se3/daemon/` — The SE3 daemon package — a resident asyncio control-plane process that bridges one-shot `se3 run` flows and the central server, composing a supervisor and spawner (to discover, launch, track, and reap local flow processes), an aggregator plus disk-JSON cache and history reader (to poll on-disk flow/issue/history artifacts into serializable machine-status and session snapshots), and a NAT-friendly outbound WebSocket client speaking a versioned wire protocol (with per-type traffic metrics) to push status and route inbound spawn/respond/interject/issue/history commands. <!--#a4df89cd68f41c4f|77a2e61f24bde101-->

### `src/se3/daemon/__init__.py` (python) — Package entry point for the SE3 daemon (the resident control-plane process that bridges one-shot `se3 run` flows and the central server), re-exporting the public API from its supervisor, spawner, aggregator, daemon, client, and protocol sub-modules. <!--#6949b9b6bea420b2|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/se3/daemon/aggregator.py` (python) — Defines the SE3 daemon's DaemonAggregator plus its snapshot dataclasses (PendingCall, FlowSnapshot, IssueSnapshot, MachineStatus), which poll on-disk flow artifacts (engine.json, summaries, calls, resumable snapshots, issues) across project roots and fold them into a single serializable MachineStatus describing the whole local machine without touching any flow process. <!--#00b3cd9944ad734f|e71e5b6b67c73ed7-->
- `PendingCall` (class) — A dataclass modeling one queued human-in-the-loop interaction mirrored from a project's se3/calls/ file, whose kind field tells the UI how to render it (MCP call, interjection, retry decision, CLI confirm, or discovery gate). <!--#a82a6a33d2650497-->
  - `PendingCall.to_dict` (method) — Serializes a PendingCall to a plain dict, optionally clipping the (potentially large) prompt body to the history _DESC_CLIP length so full prompts don't inline into every STATUS_UPDATE snapshot. <!--#c6134464beb5db49-->
- `FlowSnapshot` (class) — A dataclass capturing one flow's aggregated state read from its engine.json, including progress, pending calls, a waiting-for-lock flag, and a daemon-computed resumable eligibility signal. <!--#a306a8939fb15f6f-->
  - `FlowSnapshot.to_dict` (method) — Serializes a FlowSnapshot to a dict, clipping each pending call's prompt so the wire carries only a preview while the full body is fetched on demand. <!--#801769a89269b7e1-->
- `IssueSnapshot` (class) — A dataclass holding one issue's webui-relevant summary fields (with a truncated description preview) for inclusion in a MachineStatus snapshot. <!--#182f28645c52b177-->
  - `IssueSnapshot.to_dict` (method) — Serializes the IssueSnapshot to a dict, omitting optional fields (title/priority/type) when unset. <!--#ac44a97529a64719-->
- `MachineStatus` (class) — A dataclass representing a full status snapshot of one SE3 machine — its flows, machine-wide pending calls, project roots, and issues. <!--#39c2520ab9a2cd38-->
  - `MachineStatus.to_dict` (method) — Serializes a MachineStatus to a dict, clipping machine-wide pending-call prompts (the largest redundant STATUS_UPDATE surface) so full bodies are fetched on demand. <!--#993d745498a11978-->
- `_stable_machine_id` (function) — Returns a process-stable machine id composed of the hostname plus a short uuid/node tail. <!--#e773a1e1eb387919-->
- `DaemonAggregator` (class) — The engine that periodically polls on-disk flow artifacts (engine.json, calls, issues) across tracked project roots into a MachineStatus snapshot, managing a persistent root registry, worktree→main normalization, live-process resumable gating, and a TTL cache for historical-root enumeration. <!--#90c2e2c816aeb1f5-->
  - `DaemonAggregator.__init__` (method) — Constructs the aggregator, setting machine id, poll interval, optional registry-load/persist and live-roots callbacks, and initializing the in-memory active/persisted root sets, mtime tracking, and the historical-roots TTL cache. <!--#8ec512a021cfe5cf-->
  - `DaemonAggregator.add_project_root` (method) — The single write-through seam that registers a project root (normalizing worktree paths back to the main repo), best-effort persists it to the durable registry, and invalidates the historical-roots cache only for genuinely new roots. <!--#7a236bc0ac19814c-->
  - `DaemonAggregator.remove_project_root` (method) — Stops polling the given path and invalidates the historical-roots cache. <!--#4138c922e7fea488-->
  - `DaemonAggregator.set_project_roots` (method) — Replaces the entire polled project-root set and invalidates the historical-roots cache. <!--#b0860aaf9c1796da-->
  - `DaemonAggregator._invalidate_hist_roots_cache` (method) — Drops the cached historical-root enumeration so the next `all_project_roots` re-runs the on-disk history walk. <!--#9f1c834431d818f3-->
  - `DaemonAggregator.project_roots` (method) — Returns a sorted snapshot list of the currently registered active project roots. <!--#424a9b11cd59d976-->
  - `DaemonAggregator.has_changes` (method) — Returns whether any tracked `engine.json` mtime changed since the last call, updating the internal mtime cache as a side effect. <!--#0d911f5dc970cb00-->
  - `DaemonAggregator.get_snapshot` (method) — Builds and returns the current MachineStatus by snapshotting every observable root's flow, calls, issues, and supplemental resumable snapshots. <!--#5fdf22f72c529a8f-->
  - `DaemonAggregator._live_roots` (method) — Resolves the normalized set of roots with a live `se3 run` process via the injected provider, used to gate the resumable flag. <!--#42348cabae23a503-->
  - `DaemonAggregator.all_project_roots` (method) — Returns the deduplicated, sorted union of active, registry, and TTL-cached historical roots that drives the New Task dropdown and history index. <!--#96d5c9ebc5b23cc9-->
  - `DaemonAggregator.all_observable_roots` (method) — Returns `all_project_roots` plus active `--worktree` run subdirectories, the root view used for building flow snapshots. <!--#667d4c7077dc12cb-->
  - `DaemonAggregator._active_worktree_run_roots` (method) — Discovers live `se3 run --worktree` isolation subdirectories by scanning each base root's `se3/worktrees/*/` for children whose cached engine.json header marks an `is_worktree_mode` flow, so in-progress worktree runs stay observable. <!--#77ed6c980ea8b816-->
  - `DaemonAggregator._historical_roots` (method) — Returns the on-disk historical roots for a base set, reusing a TTL- and fingerprint-guarded cache to keep the expensive history walk off the hot path. <!--#14abb216427621d8-->
  - `DaemonAggregator.pending_calls_signature` (method) — Returns a cheap, kind-agnostic stat-based fingerprint (name, mtime, size) of every `se3/calls/` file across active and worktree roots, letting the client poll frequently and run the heavy snapshot only when the signature changes. <!--#ebf4a5c56c26e13f-->
  - `DaemonAggregator._merge_project_roots` (method) — Produces the snapshot's `project_roots` field by delegating to `all_project_roots`. <!--#f97c43f045028b11-->
  - `DaemonAggregator._snapshot_for_root` (method) — Builds a per-root FlowSnapshot from the root's active engine.json — deriving status, step progress, filtered pending calls, and a live-process-gated resumable flag — returning None (no card) when no active flow exists so archived roots don't produce empty '(untitled flow)' entries. <!--#5d5c2bf2542c31ee-->
  - `DaemonAggregator._enumerate_resumable_snapshots` (method) — Enumerates `se3/state/resumable/*.json` per-flow snapshots and emits one resumable FlowSnapshot per not-yet-seen, filename-matched, still-resumable flow, skipping duplicates and stale completed snapshots so the WebUI never shows a dead resume entry. <!--#d1f6aa101a840860-->
  - `DaemonAggregator._snapshot_from_resumable` (method) — Builds a resumable-oriented FlowSnapshot from a superseded resumable snapshot dict (same shape as engine.json), deriving progress/step metadata but leaving live-flow-owned fields empty and honestly re-deriving the live-gated resumable flag. <!--#bfbad50cc153b741-->
  - `DaemonAggregator._enumerate_calls` (method) — Lists genuinely-pending human-call files under `se3/calls/`, skipping response files and any call that already has a response sibling. <!--#b1b553058e150ab1-->
  - `DaemonAggregator._filter_calls_for_flow` (method) — Filters a call list to those whose `context.flow_id` matches the given flow, dropping unattributed calls (or returning all when no flow_id is given). <!--#d1420ff6e2ef8337-->
  - `DaemonAggregator._filter_stale_calls` (method) — Drops calls whose owning step the flow has already moved past, with an exemption keeping retry-decision chips visible on a FAILED step. <!--#290a9c80a50fe843-->
  - `DaemonAggregator._dedup_calls_by_step` (method) — Keeps only the newest unanswered call per (flow_id, step_id) so superseded clarification-round leftovers don't pile up as stale chips. <!--#252191d67ed75681-->
  - `DaemonAggregator._parse_call_file` (method) — Builds a PendingCall from one call file, reading its JSON body for display metadata with legacy fallbacks for kind/prompt/flow_id. <!--#8f422e8874df3dbe-->
  - `DaemonAggregator._read_summary` (method) — Returns the most recent `summary-*.json` summary text for a flow, if any. <!--#a4e35352515c5261-->
  - `DaemonAggregator._collect_issues` (method) — Reads open/ and closed/ issue YAML files under a root's se3/issues/ into clipped IssueSnapshots, silently skipping malformed files and worktree-copy roots to avoid double-counting. <!--#b9bfafeedd42500b-->
- `_is_resumable_status` (function) — Returns whether a status string names a resumable flow — everything except `completed` qualifies. <!--#e302c0e8083cfeec-->
- `_normalize_root` (function) — Normalizes a project root to the canonical live-process-gate key by folding worktree copies to their main root and resolving symlinks. <!--#a89e080d5bf58c7b-->
- `_resumable_with_live_gate` (function) — Computes a flow's resumable flag, tightening it to False only for a RUNNING flow whose root still has a live process. <!--#0f5ece84b5759a40-->
- `_safe_mtime` (function) — Returns a path's mtime, or None if it does not exist or is unreadable. <!--#11651aaac368a47d-->
- `_safe_stat` (function) — Returns a path's (mtime, size) tuple, or (0.0, 0) when unreadable, for change-signature fingerprinting. <!--#854c07daef0261c7-->
- `_read_json` (function) — Reads and parses a JSON file, returning None on any OS or parse error. <!--#5d8c043c7c84672b-->
- `_call_step_id` (function) — Resolves the step a PendingCall belongs to, preferring its `step_id` field then `context.step_id`, else None. <!--#6fb85d6e474a8859-->
- `_call_sort_key` (function) — Returns a recency sort key (created_at mtime, then call_id tie-breaker) for a PendingCall. <!--#7c1a397b9866544b-->
- `_current_step` (function) — Resolves a human-readable current-step label from a flow `state` dict. <!--#b7b602ad33735782-->
- `_count_dir` (function) — Counts regular files anywhere under a path (0 if it does not exist). <!--#745c695aa4dafe04-->
- `_count_issues` (function) — Counts open issue YAML records under `se3/issues/` (the open/ subtree). <!--#2150e54506de74da-->

### `src/se3/daemon/client.py` (python) — The daemon's NAT-friendly outbound WebSocket client (DaemonClient) that dials the central server, announces itself with HELLO, pushes periodic STATUS_UPDATE and HISTORY snapshots plus PONG heartbeats, routes inbound server commands (spawn/respond/interject/end-session/issue/history/detail) to their handlers off the event loop, and auto-reconnects with capped exponential backoff, treating the lazily-imported `websockets` library as an optional dependency. <!--#0a92e1ad8b7341ce|bdf58d4c73d9e242-->
- `_format_exc` (function) — Helper returning a guaranteed-non-empty, key-safe one-line description of an exception (falling back to its type name) for recording as the connection's last-error reason. <!--#6bb7dce1e7c8ec76-->
- `_normalize_ws_url` (function) — Helper that normalizes any user-supplied server URL into a canonical `ws(s)://host:port/ws` form, filling in scheme-aware default ports and preserving explicit ports/paths/IPv6 literals. <!--#b5332febe335055e-->
- `DaemonClient` (class) — The daemon's outbound WebSocket client to the central server: it advertises the machine in HELLO, pushes status snapshots and incremental history/index deltas on a dual-cadence loop with keepalive-based traffic reduction, and dispatches inbound server commands (SPAWN_FLOW, RESUME, END_SESSION, RESPOND/INTERJECT, ISSUE and HISTORY/DETAIL requests) to the injected handlers and providers. <!--#a6ffaf0b68eec720-->
  - `DaemonClient.__init__` (method) — Constructs the client from server URL and machine identity plus optional handler/provider callbacks (spawn, ensure, end-session, respond, history, calls-signature) and cadence intervals, initializing wire metrics and the change-gate/signature state. <!--#792a6cd8c3770332-->
  - `DaemonClient.connected` (method) — Property reporting whether an active WebSocket session is currently established. <!--#5831c223727779da-->
  - `DaemonClient.last_error` (method) — Property returning the most recent connection error string, if any. <!--#d8d98d202de9e6d8-->
  - `DaemonClient._next_seq` (method) — Helper that increments and returns a monotonically increasing per-client message sequence number. <!--#f2490b69e1cbed2e-->
  - `DaemonClient.run` (method) — Top-level coroutine that lazily imports `websockets`, then connects/serves/reconnects with capped exponential backoff until the stop event fires or auth is rejected. <!--#11e83456424fefaa-->
  - `DaemonClient._session` (method) — Runs one full WebSocket session — connects with deflate compression, resets per-session state, sends HELLO and primes a full status/history baseline, then races the receive, push, stop, and auth-rejection tasks until the session unwinds. <!--#61afff90f2e3199a-->
  - `DaemonClient._receive_loop` (method) — Reads inbound frames off the socket, decodes them, and dispatches each to its handler until the socket closes or shutdown is requested. <!--#eecbd577cc3ed509-->
  - `DaemonClient._push_loop` (method) — The single coroutine that drives all status and history pushes, waking on the fast tick / fast-push event / shutdown and firing STATUS_UPDATE (heartbeat or on calls-signature change) and HISTORY (on active-flow disk change) with signature scans offloaded to worker threads. <!--#b2c16ff24a256d7a-->
  - `DaemonClient._wait_next_tick` (method) — Waits one fast tick racing the timeout against the stop event and the fast-push event, returning whether a fast-push actually woke the loop. <!--#b0d8ca12e0865a9e-->
  - `DaemonClient._calls_changed` (method) — Returns whether the `se3/calls/` directory fingerprint changed since last check (updating cached signature), so a new/drained interjection triggers an immediate status push. <!--#77712dc7033b695c-->
  - `DaemonClient._trigger_fast_push` (method) — Sets the sticky fast-push event to wake the push loop immediately for an out-of-band STATUS_UPDATE after a local side-effect. <!--#f6a684584badbf4c-->
  - `DaemonClient._history_changed` (method) — Detects whether any active flow's on-disk signature has changed since the last check (updating the cached signature), returning False when no provider is configured and conservatively True on lookup failure so the next push still runs. <!--#c8e42de0c5d5742a-->
  - `DaemonClient._dispatch` (method) — Routes one inbound server message to the appropriate handler by type (ping, welcome, spawn, respond, interject, end-session, issue-command, history requests, detail request). <!--#e6f017f2f9c3e471-->
  - `DaemonClient._handle_welcome` (method) — Processes the server's WELCOME, recording the peer protocol version / traffic-reduction support and, on an accepted=false reject, storing the reason and signalling the session to stop reconnecting. <!--#c6bd447a784035b2-->
  - `DaemonClient._handle_spawn` (method) — Handles a SPAWN_FLOW by branching to resume vs. fresh-spawn, running the ensure/init hook off-thread, and reporting real execution failures back as SPAWN_FAILED. <!--#5dae2c4817efeae1-->
  - `DaemonClient._handle_respond` (method) — Handles a RESPOND_CALL by resolving the project root (from the history index when omitted) and invoking the response-file writer, all off the event loop. <!--#ef5250dde50cf761-->
  - `DaemonClient._handle_interject` (method) — Routes an INTERJECT_FLOW to the interjection-file writer (resolving the project root if absent) then fires a fast push so the pending chip surfaces within ~1s. <!--#4de62f88a34aeb37-->
  - `DaemonClient._resolve_interject_root` (method) — Resolves a flow's project root for an INTERJECT_FLOW lacking one, matching the flow against the machine snapshot and falling back to the history index (both off-thread). <!--#5b01808b0ad25144-->
  - `DaemonClient._resolve_flow_root_from_index` (method) — Resolves a flow_id's project root from the TTL-cached history index so respond/interject/end-session writes match the history-read scope. <!--#925a6b4ab18ff7b0-->
  - `DaemonClient._handle_end_session` (method) — Handles an END_SESSION by resolving the flow's root and dispatching the injected end-session handler off-thread, catching exceptions so a bad request never drops the connection. <!--#718f9f629603a13b-->
  - `DaemonClient._handle_issue_command` (method) — Validates and executes a server ISSUE_COMMAND against a registered project via IssueManager (off-thread), replying with an ISSUE_RESULT ack and triggering a fast push. <!--#97331081843b1f9b-->
  - `DaemonClient._execute_issue_operation` (method) — Synchronous dispatcher mapping create/edit/close/reopen issue operations to the corresponding IssueManager method and returning the affected issue ID. <!--#5883f40a7a7e6a85-->
  - `DaemonClient._handle_history_request` (method) — Answers a server HISTORY_REQUEST by reading the requested flow's records off disk in a worker thread (full snapshot or cursor-based delta) and replying with a HISTORY_DATA frame. <!--#c1eb14de1b93567e-->
  - `DaemonClient._handle_history_index_request` (method) — Forces a fresh rebuild and re-push of the full history index when a browser enters the history view, bypassing the change debounce. <!--#8960fe7c8bb23353-->
  - `DaemonClient._handle_detail_request` (method) — Answers a server DETAIL_REQUEST by reading the untruncated issue/call artifact off disk in a worker thread and replying with DETAIL_DATA, always degrading failures to ok=false rather than tearing down the connection. <!--#9c6dd69352cfbf0a-->
  - `DaemonClient._detail_root_candidates` (method) — Builds the ordered list of project roots to search for a detail artifact, trying the request's supplied root first then the last STATUS_UPDATE's known roots as fallback. <!--#d33881a1d5f81030-->
  - `DaemonClient._read_detail` (method) — Off-thread dispatcher that reads one full-text detail artifact from disk by kind, delegating to the issue or call reader and returning None when unlocatable. <!--#acac1e292c8f45e0-->
  - `DaemonClient._read_issue_detail` (method) — Loads an issue's untruncated record via IssueManager, trying each candidate root until the issue is found and returning its to_dict (or None). <!--#1650cebc04fa1fae-->
  - `DaemonClient._read_call_detail` (method) — Reads a pending call's full file body from se3/calls/ by matching call_id stem, normalizing the full text under a canonical prompt key (falling back to legacy message/question fields). <!--#e438353c4ff068ae-->
  - `DaemonClient._send` (method) — JSON-encodes and sends a message over the socket, then meters its byte length against its type in WireMetrics only after the send succeeds. <!--#889d1f5bc2c2bea9-->
  - `DaemonClient._peer_supports_traffic_reduction` (method) — Returns whether the connected server understands revision-3 lean frames, degrading pre-WELCOME/legacy peers to False so no keepalive is ever emitted to a peer that would reject it. <!--#313eab67d3ffd219-->
  - `DaemonClient._push_status` (method) — Builds the machine snapshot (off-thread) and either ships a full STATUS_UPDATE or, when unchanged and the peer supports it and force is off, a tiny signature-only KEEPALIVE, advancing the change-gate baseline only after a successful send. <!--#c9710c62352529ed-->
  - `DaemonClient._push_history` (method) — Pushes the history index (as a delta, or a full baseline on reconnect/force/legacy peers) plus incremental record batches for active flows, committing each flow's cursor only after its frame is actually sent so a failed send is re-read and re-delivered rather than silently lost. <!--#b0a96ec0290f994f-->
  - `DaemonClient._push_history_index` (method) — Sends the history index as a full HISTORY_INDEX baseline (on force/unprimed/legacy peer, debounced to real changes) or otherwise as a HISTORY_INDEX_DELTA of only changed/removed rows, advancing the by-flow baseline only after a successful send. <!--#e9a6aea091f5b686-->
  - `DaemonClient._compute_index_delta` (method) — Pure diff of current meta rows against the last-pushed baseline returning (upserts, removed), holding back updated_at-only liveness changes on non-status ticks without mutating the baseline. <!--#cfcd9340a9a5b3a0-->
  - `DaemonClient._resumable_flow_ids` (method) — Returns the set of flow_ids still resumable from disk (live engine.json flows) via the provider, so a final-flushed FAILED flow's cursor is retained. <!--#d0588d10991a6ff5-->
- `_status_signature` (function) — Module helper returning a stable SHA-256 content hash of a status snapshot (excluding the always-moving generated_at stamp) so the push loop can detect unchanged state and send a keepalive instead of a full snapshot. <!--#c80d850c963f31b0-->
- `_default_respond_handler` (function) — Default handler that atomically writes a `<call_id>.response.json` file into `<project_root>/se3/calls/` to feed a server response back into a paused flow. <!--#3cc084bfe323f24e-->
- `_default_interject_handler` (function) — Default handler that writes a mid-flow interjection request file into `se3/calls/` for the running `se3 run` process to drain at its next step boundary. <!--#7bf411ef69f626a3-->

### `src/se3/daemon/daemon.py` (python) — Defines the resident SE3 daemon: a long-lived asyncio control-plane process (Daemon) with its DaemonConfig, that composes supervisor/spawner/aggregator/history-reader to discover and aggregate flow state, expose remote spawn/resume/end-session/respond control surfaces, and run periodic polling and worktree-GC loops with pidfile/status/signal lifecycle management. <!--#d0374e22c275b79c|e4e711008d0e53fd-->
- `_configure_daemon_logging` (function) — Installs a single idempotent, timestamped log handler for the daemon process so its log lines are attributable across detached and foreground modes. <!--#9280268fece7609c-->
- `_default_pid_dir` (function) — Returns the directory for daemon runtime files (pidfile/status/log), defaulting to ~/.se3 but overridable via the SE3_DAEMON_DIR env var for test isolation. <!--#64e9a9b21d5ed8cd-->
- `DaemonConfig` (class) — A dataclass holding all tunable settings for a Daemon instance (server URL, daemon credential, pidfile/status/log/registry directory, poll and GC cadences, machine id, project roots, shutdown grace) with derived path properties for each on-disk file. <!--#edabbbdcb37e3833-->
  - `DaemonConfig.__post_init__` (method) — Coerces the configured pid_dir into a Path after dataclass construction. <!--#c8319b96022c643e-->
  - `DaemonConfig.pid_file` (method) — Property giving the pidfile path under pid_dir. <!--#db80f9021d5529bf-->
  - `DaemonConfig.status_file` (method) — Property giving the status-file path under pid_dir. <!--#1d551dccb5cefe59-->
  - `DaemonConfig.log_file` (method) — Property giving the daemon log-file path under pid_dir. <!--#1ad7ba864a0ad3ee-->
  - `DaemonConfig.project_roots_file` (method) — Property giving the persistent project-roots registry file path under pid_dir. <!--#bd196da4c4c0757e-->
- `Daemon` (class) — The resident control-plane process that owns the supervisor, spawner, aggregator, history reader, and machine-local project-root registry, exposing request_spawn/request_resume as remote entry points to start or resume `se3 run` flows and driving the poll loop, worktree GC, and outbound WebSocket client to the central server. <!--#244497510ce5437e-->
  - `Daemon.__init__` (method) — Constructs the daemon's collaborators (supervisor, spawner, aggregator with project-root registry callbacks, history reader) from its config and initializes the run/stop/client/last-GC state. <!--#85bcbef5d343027a-->
  - `Daemon.request_spawn` (method) — Spawns a new `se3 run` flow (optionally discovery/worktree/from-issue) and registers its project root with the aggregator. <!--#2bbb2d056b412ce6-->
  - `Daemon.request_resume` (method) — Remote entry point that resumes a non-COMPLETED flow by locating it via the active engine.json header or its per-flow resumable snapshot, rejecting mismatched/COMPLETED flows and refusing when a live process still occupies the project root. <!--#bd2074a98906f6d7-->
  - `Daemon.request_end_session` (method) — Terminates and archives a supervised (or dangling worktree) flow by dispatching an `se3 end-session` subprocess so grace-waits and archival stay off the event loop. <!--#80a7f53b17992e5a-->
  - `Daemon._live_project_roots` (method) — Returns the set of project roots that currently have a live `se3 run` process, using the same supervisor/is_alive view as the resume double-spawn guard, to gate the RUNNING-flow resumable flag. <!--#7f1555c5a2eb317e-->
  - `Daemon.snapshot` (method) — Returns a fresh MachineStatus aggregation snapshot from the aggregator. <!--#18881f0b4dc950ac-->
  - `Daemon.stop` (method) — Signals the running event loop to shut down gracefully by setting the stop event. <!--#8c421937c52e8b71-->
  - `Daemon.run_forever` (method) — Foreground entry point that configures daemon logging and runs the async serve loop until interrupted. <!--#28c8017c1d0d57e6-->
  - `Daemon.serve` (method) — The async main that writes the pidfile, installs signal handlers, and runs the poll loop plus optional outbound server client concurrently on one event loop before shutting down. <!--#c99097a39e82fbf1-->
  - `Daemon._start_server_client` (method) — Lazily creates the outbound DaemonClient asyncio task (wiring snapshot/spawn/resume/end-session/respond/history handlers) only when a server_url is configured. <!--#266d6b30d3d101a2-->
  - `Daemon._handle_spawn_request` (method) — Adapts an inbound server SPAWN_FLOW message into a request_spawn call. <!--#4fb879526798f301-->
  - `Daemon._handle_resume_request` (method) — Adapts an inbound server SPAWN_FLOW-with-resume_flow_id message into a request_resume call. <!--#a1397f1fc3be07ee-->
  - `Daemon._handle_end_session_request` (method) — Adapts an inbound server END_SESSION message into a request_end_session call. <!--#785f8ebae74029dc-->
  - `Daemon._handle_ensure_request` (method) — Pre-spawn hook that runs `se3 init` on a target directory if needed and registers the freshly-initialized root with the aggregator. <!--#73697a39cd470777-->
  - `Daemon._handle_respond_request` (method) — Adapts a server RESPOND_CALL by writing the response file to se3/calls and then re-spawning the now-answerable PAUSED flow with --resume. <!--#dd2ea42bc295b24b-->
  - `Daemon._resume_paused_flow` (method) — Best-effort helper that re-spawns a project's flow with --resume only when its engine.json reports PAUSED status and no live process is already running in that root. <!--#ee49b520be17efa6-->
  - `Daemon._poll_loop` (method) — The async loop that runs a local-state aggregation poll (and a gated GC check) each poll_interval until the stop event fires, isolating per-iteration failures. <!--#271c693afd1b47e7-->
  - `Daemon._poll_once` (method) — A single aggregation tick that discovers flows, registers their roots, reaps dead processes, and builds a status snapshot — offloading every disk-JSON-parsing step to worker threads to keep the event loop free. <!--#77a27d446cca2ea3-->
  - `Daemon._register_discovered_roots` (method) — Worker-thread helper that registers each discovered flow's project root with the aggregator, resolving worktree-copy roots back to their main project so isolation worktrees never register as standalone projects. <!--#7b2b3770f939b1df-->
  - `Daemon._maybe_run_gc` (method) — Gates the worktree-GC sweep to fire at most once per gc_interval (or never if disabled), stamping the timestamp before offloading the actual sweep to a worker thread. <!--#daba86981c6025aa-->
  - `Daemon._gc_once` (method) — Worker-thread routine that sweeps each tracked project root for leaked worktree runs via gc_worktree_runs, isolating per-root failures and logging each sweep's report. <!--#222ba97fc36b37e3-->
  - `Daemon._log_gc_report` (method) — Emits a GC sweep's outcome to the daemon log, raising retained-unmerged branches to WARNING as operator-actionable signals while logging reclamations and errors. <!--#1934263e345da6b8-->
  - `Daemon._install_signal_handlers` (method) — Wires SIGTERM/SIGINT to a graceful stop on the event loop, falling back to signal.signal on platforms without loop signal handlers. <!--#49b2ae2f6678bb85-->
  - `Daemon._shutdown` (method) — Terminates any spawned flows within the grace period and removes the status/pid runtime files on shutdown. <!--#943e2b7baa719500-->
