  - `Daemon._write_pidfile` (method) — Writes the daemon pidfile (pid/start time/server/machine id), refusing to start if another live daemon already holds it. <!--#4e6caf9c4c17a9d6-->
  - `Daemon._write_status` (method) — Persists the latest machine snapshot, tracked flows, and real outbound-client connection state (connected/last_error/per-message wire metrics, or unconfigured markers when no server_url is set) to the status file for `se3 daemon status` to read. <!--#2c1c4f46f522b912-->
- `DaemonAlreadyRunning` (class) — RuntimeError subclass raised when a daemon is started while another instance is alive, carrying the conflicting pid. <!--#da58834df4e58342-->
  - `DaemonAlreadyRunning.__init__` (method) — Initializes the error with a message and stores the conflicting pid. <!--#75516beb68cdd4c3-->
- `_se3_version` (function) — Best-effort lookup of the installed SE3 version string, returning 'unknown' on failure. <!--#4b1a40eeb2d1b705-->
- `_read_pidfile` (function) — Reads and JSON-parses a daemon pid/status file, returning None if absent or corrupt. <!--#5aa376cf77d5cd0f-->
- `_pid_alive` (function) — Returns whether an int-like pid names a live process via os.kill(pid, 0), treating permission errors as alive. <!--#166d012dcd6de729-->
- `_atomic_write_json` (function) — Atomically writes a payload as JSON to a path using a temp-file-plus-rename. <!--#dcff051d0bc329f1-->
- `_read_project_roots_raw` (function) — Reads the persisted project-roots JSON registry verbatim (no existence filtering, empty on missing/corrupt), providing the raw on-disk view that the sanitize/self-heal logic compares against. <!--#d0dc15ff0a431b5b-->
- `_read_project_roots` (function) — Returns the live project roots by reading the raw registry and dropping any root whose directory no longer exists on disk, so consumers never see a since-deleted project. <!--#9273ec53a134058c-->
- `_append_project_root` (function) — Appends a new project root to the registry (realpath-deduplicated, worktree-copy folded back to its main root), rewriting the file atomically only for a genuinely new live root while pruning stale/deleted entries in the same write. <!--#d7f17f19d7eecf99-->
- `_sanitize_project_roots` (function) — One-time fault-tolerant startup cleanup that scans the raw registry and atomically rewrites it—only when something changed—to drop worktree-copy and no-longer-existent roots that would otherwise resurface indefinitely. <!--#302ab2c30f2afd76-->
- `start_daemon` (function) — Public entry point that starts the daemon foreground (blocking) or fully detached via double-fork/subprocess, raising DaemonAlreadyRunning if one is already live. <!--#856f4e1148be83db-->
- `_start_detached_fork` (function) — Detaches the daemon via a classic double-fork (reparenting the real daemon onto init) and polls the pidfile before returning to the launcher. <!--#e621687e3abf6b96-->
- `_detach_streams` (function) — Redirects the detached daemon's stdin/stdout/stderr to /dev/null and the log file. <!--#02d4194e10a76e4a-->
- `_start_detached_subprocess` (function) — Fallback detach path for platforms without os.fork, launching `se3 daemon start --foreground` as a new-session subprocess and passing the daemon key via the environment. <!--#64cf11f07fad0ba3-->
- `stop_daemon` (function) — Signals a running daemon to shut down via SIGTERM and waits for it to exit, reporting stopped/not_running/stop_timeout. <!--#def767d191f88bfb-->
- `daemon_status` (function) — Reports whether the daemon is running plus its tracked flows, snapshot, and real outbound-connection state read from the pid/status files. <!--#472f7d019b97062f-->

### `src/se3/daemon/disk_json_cache.py` (python) — A unified, thread-safe disk-JSON parse cache for the daemon control plane that parses each on-disk artifact (engine.json, archived snapshots, resumable/_meta.json) at most once per real content change—keying immutable snapshots by (path, mtime, size) and re-validating the live engine.json with a whole-content hash—plus a bounded head+tail regex scan (read_engine_header/_degraded_header) that reads just the top-level header of oversized files without ever fully parsing them, eliminating the #243 event-loop freeze and executor saturation. <!--#2b4aa0be7d4f2093|fcb07a662f43a4c9-->
- `clear_cache` (function) — Test-isolation helper that drops all cached parses and the degraded-warning dedup set under their locks. <!--#d10abadbb5bb703f-->
- `_store` (function) — Lock-held helper that inserts/refreshes a cache entry as most-recently-used and evicts the oldest entries once the LRU cap is exceeded. <!--#1f90857dea1c197c-->
- `_drop_entry` (function) — Removes a cached entry whose backing path no longer stats, so a deleted worktree/archive file's parsed dict isn't pinned for the daemon's lifetime. <!--#b0e78e317fb71c07-->
- `cached_content_digest` (function) — Accessor that returns the cached whole-content digest from a path's last active engine.json read (or None if unavailable), letting the change-detection signature fold in content changes to catch same-(mtime,size) in-place rewrites without a second read or hash. <!--#f1c3197761855712-->
- `_warn_once_degraded` (function) — Emits a once-per-path warning that degraded header extraction failed for an oversized file, deduplicated so a persistently broken file doesn't flood the log. <!--#bf9238330491dc5d-->
- `_safe_stat` (function) — Helper that stats a path and returns an integer-based (st_mtime_ns, st_size) cache key, or None if the file is inaccessible. <!--#2b2346a3ef96b23f-->
- `_read_active_content` (function) — Reads the whole (size-guarded) content of the live engine.json as bytes to back the content-hash freshness check, catching middle-of-file rewrites a windowed hash would miss. <!--#3387ba37f0d9faef-->
- `_json_loads` (function) — Thin, separately-patchable json.loads wrapper serving as the innermost GIL-bound decode seam for parse-counting tests. <!--#2998e22c3d77cbf7-->
- `_parse_json` (function) — Parses whole-file JSON text into a top-level dict (or None), routing the decode through the patchable _json_loads seam. <!--#dd3d34f8d9787ed3-->
- `_parse_json_file` (function) — Reads a file's text and parses it into a dict (or None), the outer parse seam that regression tests patch to count full-file parses. <!--#4f108527de729a80-->
- `read_json_cached` (function) — The daemon's unified JSON read/parse cache: keys immutable snapshots by (path, mtime, size) and re-validates the live engine.json with a whole-content hash so each file is parsed at most once per real content change. <!--#6ec91ffd5406eef0-->
- `read_engine_header` (function) — Returns just the small top-level header of an engine.json/snapshot, using the cache for at/under-guard files (verify_content when active) and a bounded head+tail scan for oversized files so giant active runs stay visible without ever fully parsing them. <!--#1cf11754bf92b769-->
- `_join_head_tail` (function) — Joins bounded head and tail windows into scannable text, dropping the tail's truncated first line so only genuine top-level keys can be matched. <!--#7b1bfd11987d6e6d-->
- `_degraded_header` (function) — Extracts top-level header keys from an oversized indent=2 JSON file via a bounded head+tail regex scan (never a full parse), warning once and returning None if flow_id can't be found. <!--#6c3a84424823ceb6-->

### `src/se3/daemon/history.py` (python) — Read-only history layer for the SE3 daemon: `DaemonHistoryReader` enumerates each tracked project root's `se3/state/engine.json`, `se3/state/archive/engine_*.json` and `se3/history/<flow_id>/` artifacts into a `SessionMeta` session index for the web UI, and serves per-flow `jsonl` conversation records via `read_flow` as either a `full` snapshot or an `append` delta driven by a per-file line cursor, with a running whole-prefix hash to detect in-place rewrites/retries, `MAX_RECORDS_PER_REPORT` truncation, and once-per-path warnings for unreadable files. <!--#bd4d13dbca8c0f0d|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/se3/daemon/protocol.py` (python) — The single-source-of-truth wire protocol module for the daemon↔server WebSocket link, defining the JSON frame format via the Message dataclass (with encode/decode and ProtocolError), a version-gated traffic-reduction predicate, and per-type make_* constructors for every daemon↔server message (hello/welcome, status/keepalive, calls, spawn/interject/end-session, issue commands, ping/pong, and history/detail requests and data). <!--#362f90329e6209cc|dfc9966cf17cade2-->
- `supports_traffic_reduction` (function) — Predicate that decides, per peer, whether its advertised protocol version is recent enough (>= the revision-3 threshold) to safely receive the lean traffic-reduction messages, degrading to False for missing/non-numeric versions. <!--#4bafdcc6c4ebfe54-->
- `ProtocolError` (class) — A ValueError subclass raised when a wire frame cannot be parsed as a valid protocol message. <!--#8844b8e7e818cf89-->
- `Message` (class) — A dataclass representing one protocol frame (type, payload, seq, timestamp) with serialization/parsing helpers to and from JSON dicts and strings. <!--#6d471563b76576f9-->
  - `Message.to_dict` (method) — Returns the JSON-friendly dict form of the message with its four canonical top-level keys. <!--#759de46712e4b25b-->
  - `Message.to_json` (method) — Serializes the message to a compact JSON string. <!--#4ea1594e9d498330-->
  - `Message.from_dict` (method) — Classmethod that validates and builds a Message from a decoded JSON object, raising ProtocolError on a malformed or unknown-type frame. <!--#fc4a7b6821d1c6ea-->
  - `Message.from_json` (method) — Classmethod that parses a JSON string into a validated Message, raising ProtocolError on bad JSON or an invalid frame. <!--#e82ebe85cf35c624-->
- `encode` (function) — Builds a Message of the given type/payload/seq and returns it JSON-encoded in one call. <!--#3f319ca1e3054bfe-->
- `decode` (function) — Parses a raw JSON wire string into a validated Message. <!--#c008cfff05ac0ddc-->
- `make_hello` (function) — Constructs the daemon→server HELLO message announcing a daemon's machine identity, version, and optional secret owner key. <!--#e11c4df49538cc4c-->
- `make_welcome` (function) — Constructs the server→daemon WELCOME message acknowledging a HELLO with server version and acceptance status. <!--#a9085ee42f4fc840-->
- `make_status_update` (function) — Constructs the daemon→server STATUS_UPDATE message carrying an aggregated machine-status snapshot. <!--#7525f2e92673100b-->
- `make_call_notification` (function) — Constructs the daemon→server CALL_NOTIFICATION message reporting a freshly-detected pending human call. <!--#677dd0e2384a7f58-->
- `make_spawn_flow` (function) — Constructs the server→daemon SPAWN_FLOW message instructing a daemon to spawn, resume, or issue-spawn an se3 run flow (with optional discover/worktree flags). <!--#7f6c7841d5e5bfc9-->
- `make_spawn_failed` (function) — Constructs the daemon→server SPAWN_FAILED message reporting that a dispatched spawn/resume/project-init failed after the server already replied 202. <!--#1b569585789302df-->
- `make_respond_call` (function) — Constructs the server→daemon RESPOND_CALL message delivering a human response for a pending call. <!--#8aaa1c0ac739b1bf-->
- `make_interject_flow` (function) — Constructs the server→daemon INTERJECT_FLOW message delivering a mid-flow user interjection to be folded into a running flow. <!--#150211d4be0cc211-->
- `make_end_session` (function) — Constructs the server→daemon END_SESSION message instructing the daemon to terminate and archive a given flow. <!--#5db85a6d8a2b3c14-->
- `make_issue_command` (function) — Constructs the server→daemon ISSUE_COMMAND message requesting an issue write operation (create/edit/close/reopen) with operation-specific fields. <!--#ea7e983f451ab580-->
- `make_issue_result` (function) — Constructs the daemon→server ISSUE_RESULT message acknowledging an issue write command, correlated by request_id. <!--#81cd9f6eebb1d8f3-->
- `make_ping` (function) — Constructs the server→daemon PING heartbeat-probe message. <!--#b2c7fb1f30e8011c-->
- `make_pong` (function) — Constructs the daemon→server PONG heartbeat-reply message. <!--#2b41c9ace39e5f99-->
- `make_history_index` (function) — Constructs the daemon→server HISTORY_INDEX message reporting the list of known history-session metadata. <!--#fa0245e46e8a3b42-->
- `make_history_index_request` (function) — Constructs the payload-less server→daemon HISTORY_INDEX_REQUEST message forcing a fresh rebuild and re-push of the history index. <!--#946e3b425098a9e1-->
- `make_history_request` (function) — Constructs the server→daemon HISTORY_REQUEST message pulling a flow's history records, optionally with a per-step cursor for incremental fetch. <!--#b51051e6cfa89ccd-->
- `make_history_data` (function) — Constructs the daemon→server MSG_HISTORY_DATA message carrying a flow's history records in either full-snapshot or append mode, along with the updated per-file cursor and the optional cursor_base marking the start of the window the frame covers, raising ProtocolError on an unrecognized mode. <!--#dc3d34f8b8a054f2-->
- `make_keepalive` (function) — Builds the minimal daemon→server heartbeat Message sent in place of a full STATUS_UPDATE when the status snapshot's content signature is unchanged, keeping the server's liveness timer alive without re-sending the snapshot. <!--#2bd0ff4e380f4c1b-->
- `make_history_index_delta` (function) — Builds a daemon→server incremental history-index Message carrying only upserted SessionMeta dicts and removed flow_ids, so index traffic scales with changed flows instead of the total flow count. <!--#39b955ee1b6fb00e-->
- `make_detail_request` (function) — Builds a server→daemon Message requesting the full untruncated text of one issue or pending call (by kind and target_id, optionally scoped by project_root and correlated by request_id), raising ProtocolError on an unrecognised detail kind. <!--#3f067d241441dfd1-->
- `make_detail_data` (function) — Builds the daemon→server reply Message delivering the requested full-text detail (or an error when ok is False), echoing request_id and kind and raising ProtocolError on an unrecognised detail kind. <!--#056bc8a670d10b31-->

### `src/se3/daemon/spawner.py` (python) — Module implementing the SE3 daemon's process spawner, whose DaemonSpawner class launches, tracks, polls, tails (via NDJSON log files), and terminates `se3 run`/`init`/`end-session` child processes as independent Popen subprocesses, with helpers for login-shell PATH recovery, se3-CLI resolution, and SE3-project initialization. <!--#2abc526d74899ce2|c6c39984755248ef-->
- `resolve_login_shell_path` (function) — Probes `$SHELL -lc 'echo $PATH'` once at startup to recover the full login-shell PATH, returning it as a string or `None` on any failure without raising. <!--#5a7b63a33cc7dea2-->
- `merge_path_env` (function) — Combines a login-shell PATH ahead of the current PATH, deduplicating entries while preserving order, so spawned children inherit the richer PATH idempotently. <!--#97a7fecfa2117609-->
- `SpawnedProcess` (class) — Dataclass wrapping a spawned `se3 run` child's Popen handle plus metadata (project root, task, argv, start time, log files) with convenience properties and a JSON-serializable `to_dict`. <!--#685faf708e7f87df-->
  - `SpawnedProcess.pid` (method) — Property returning the child process's PID. <!--#723aab9ae510a1e7-->
  - `SpawnedProcess.returncode` (method) — Property returning the child's exit code, or `None` while it is still running. <!--#2ae567e522946e10-->
  - `SpawnedProcess.is_running` (method) — Property giving a non-blocking boolean probe of whether the child is still executing. <!--#46892e7692d315b1-->
  - `SpawnedProcess.to_dict` (method) — Returns a JSON-serializable dict of the process's PID, root, task, status, start time, and log paths. <!--#2405a3194bc0f30a-->
- `_resolve_se3_command` (function) — Resolves the argv prefix that invokes the `se3` CLI using same-interpreter-first fallbacks (sibling console script → `-m se3` → `shutil.which`) to avoid picking up a foreign environment's `se3`. <!--#be84eeb3635a4409-->
- `EnsureResult` (class) — Dataclass reporting the outcome of `ensure_se3_project` — whether init ran, any error to short-circuit on, and captured stdout/stderr. <!--#8ece94eff8859192-->
- `_is_se3_project` (function) — Returns whether a directory is already an SE3 project by checking for the durable `se3/charter.md` marker file. <!--#3a5427bfb36e813c-->
- `DaemonSpawner` (class) — The core class that starts, tracks, polls, tails, and terminates `se3 run` child flows for the daemon, caching login-shell PATH and optionally registering with a supervisor. <!--#c03d438af558dcf8-->
  - `DaemonSpawner.__init__` (method) — Constructs the spawner, wiring optional supervisor and spawn/exit callbacks and resolving/caching the login-shell PATH (unless overridden) once at startup. <!--#7eb90569d833fc11-->
  - `DaemonSpawner.ensure_se3_project` (method) — Ensures a directory is SE3-initialized, returning a no-op when the charter marker exists or otherwise spawning `se3 init -p <root>` and surfacing failures as an error result. <!--#f6d3b4fcbdfc5885-->
  - `DaemonSpawner.spawn` (method) — Builds the argv for a new `se3 run` flow (task or `--from-issue`, with optional `--discover`/`--worktree`) and launches it as a tracked child. <!--#8dcf15f1b32b3ed0-->
  - `DaemonSpawner.resume` (method) — Relaunches a paused flow by spawning `se3 run --resume --flow-id <id>` so it continues from persisted state after a human-call answer. <!--#986ef1903d45f4d3-->
  - `DaemonSpawner.end_session` (method) — Spawns `se3 end-session <flow_id>` (optionally with a `--pid` hint) to gracefully terminate and archive a flow off the daemon's event loop. <!--#eae1bede7b559482-->
  - `DaemonSpawner._launch` (method) — Shared launcher that builds the child env with merged PATH, opens per-flow log files, starts the Popen child, then tracks it and fires supervisor registration and the on-spawn callback. <!--#c47ee0388e45bb8a-->
  - `DaemonSpawner._allocate_log_paths` (method) — Computes timestamped stdout (`.ndjson`) and stderr log paths under `<root>/se3/logs/daemon/`, returning `(None, None)` if the directory can't be created. <!--#2972143c96485bbf-->
  - `DaemonSpawner._open_log_targets` (method) — Opens the stdout/stderr log files for Popen redirection (falling back to DEVNULL on failure) and returns the targets plus handles for the caller to close. <!--#f4e9be468f03f95c-->
  - `DaemonSpawner.get` (method) — Returns the tracked `SpawnedProcess` for a given PID, or `None`. <!--#afe4d346453eb0a2-->
  - `DaemonSpawner.processes` (method) — Returns a snapshot list of all currently tracked spawned processes. <!--#98f0b6899e671ee8-->
  - `DaemonSpawner.poll` (method) — Non-blocking exit-code probe for a tracked PID, returning `None` while it runs or is untracked. <!--#9ddea01204faba20-->
  - `DaemonSpawner.wait` (method) — Blocks up to a timeout for a tracked PID to exit and returns its code, raising `TimeoutExpired` if still running. <!--#1e54bd90cc51f142-->
  - `DaemonSpawner.iter_events` (method) — Tails a child's stdout log file, yielding each line parsed as an NDJSON event dict and stopping once the child has exited and the log is drained. <!--#b4e8468ca8557bde-->
  - `DaemonSpawner.terminate` (method) — Gracefully stops a tracked PID via SIGTERM, waits the grace period, then escalates to SIGKILL, returning the exit code. <!--#a3530ad10bca19d0-->
  - `DaemonSpawner.terminate_all` (method) — Gracefully terminates every still-running tracked process. <!--#2c13b58e7138e052-->
  - `DaemonSpawner.orphans` (method) — Returns the tracked processes still running that would be orphaned if the daemon exited. <!--#b330fd95d71db3f9-->
  - `DaemonSpawner.reap` (method) — Drops tracking for finished children, firing supervisor de-registration and the on-exit callback, and returns the reaped processes. <!--#e777ee62d549b294-->

### `src/se3/daemon/supervisor.py` (python) — Thread-safe SE3-daemon module that discovers, registers, tracks liveness of, and reaps local `se3 run` flow processes—via a PID→FlowRecord map fed by daemon-spawned flows and best-effort psutil-based external scans—firing exit callbacks when tracked processes die. <!--#f1968c24ed1c8a7d|364622291f8163f9-->
- `_proc_opted_out_of_scan` (function) — Best-effort helper that reads a process's environment and returns whether it carries the SE3_EXTERNAL_SCAN_IGNORE opt-out marker, treating any read failure as 'not opted out' so real se3 runs are never hidden. <!--#1504ef8ee147251a-->
- `FlowRecord` (class) — Dataclass holding metadata for one supervised `se3 run` process (pid, project root, flow id, task, origin, start time). <!--#c0bf1436f2eb3589-->
  - `FlowRecord.to_dict` (method) — Returns a JSON-serializable dict of the record's fields. <!--#db07055256e060a1-->
- `_is_alive` (function) — Returns whether a pid names a live process using `os.kill(pid, 0)`, treating permission errors as alive. <!--#cefb5946976f093c-->
- `resolve_worktree_main_root` (function) — Maps a `<main>/se3/worktrees/<name>` isolation-sandbox path back to its main project root (or None if the path isn't such a worktree), so worktree copies aren't registered as standalone projects. <!--#abf7cf1fc461bcce-->
- `is_worktree_copy_root` (function) — Returns whether a path is an se3 worktree isolation copy directory, i.e. whether resolve_worktree_main_root would attribute it back to a main root. <!--#3d0c3c74dfc13264-->
- `_read_flow_id` (function) — Best-effort helper that reads just the top-level `flow_id` from a project's live `engine.json` via the size-guarded, active (same-stat-window verified) header read, so registering a spawned/discovered flow never fully parses a giant file nor misattributes a just-swapped flow to the previous flow_id. <!--#e11068735ef345c7-->
- `DaemonSupervisor` (class) — Thread-safe supervisor that registers, tracks liveness of, reaps, and externally discovers local `se3 run` flow processes, notifying exit callbacks when tracked processes die. <!--#2397be024e2d4e4c-->
  - `DaemonSupervisor.__init__` (method) — Initializes the supervisor's pid→FlowRecord map, reentrant lock, exit-callback list, and the include_scan_ignored flag that controls whether opt-out-marked processes are surfaced during external discovery. <!--#a913c2ebb3712f97-->
  - `DaemonSupervisor.register` (method) — Tracks a pid as a supervised flow (updating metadata in place if already known) and returns its FlowRecord. <!--#553d17a1289ca485-->
  - `DaemonSupervisor.unregister` (method) — Stops tracking a pid, returning its record if it was tracked. <!--#974100ca92149eb8-->
  - `DaemonSupervisor.on_exit` (method) — Registers a callback invoked once per process found dead during reaping. <!--#bf51ed3636e3c140-->
  - `DaemonSupervisor.is_alive` (method) — Static wrapper exposing `_is_alive` to report whether a pid is a live process. <!--#92412c191d795dea-->
  - `DaemonSupervisor.reap` (method) — Prunes records for exited processes, firing exit callbacks (errors swallowed) and returning the reaped records. <!--#e3b14bf6bd4807b3-->
  - `DaemonSupervisor.discover_flows` (method) — Reaps dead processes, optionally scans for external `se3 run` processes, and returns all tracked flows sorted by start time. <!--#8c7c75225573f74f-->
  - `DaemonSupervisor._scan_external` (method) — Uses psutil to iterate running processes, matching externally-started `se3 run` flows (skipping self and opt-out-marked ones) and registering them under their resolved main project root as 'discovered'. <!--#b13d531b6c8fc4fc-->
  - `DaemonSupervisor.get` (method) — Returns the FlowRecord for a pid, or None if untracked. <!--#8e9bd7dae72840c9-->
  - `DaemonSupervisor.flows` (method) — Property returning a snapshot list of all tracked records. <!--#e98310c8ea90711a-->
  - `DaemonSupervisor.count` (method) — Property returning the number of currently-tracked records. <!--#7a98b600786cd252-->
- `_cmdline_is_se3_run` (function) — A structural predicate that inspects a process's psutil-observed argv to decide whether it is a genuine `se3 run` invocation, matching only the console-script (`se3 run`) and module (`python -m se3 run`) launch shapes where `run` immediately follows the se3 program/module token, while excluding Python inline `-c` stubs and unrelated subcommands to prevent false-positive WebUI aggregation. <!--#176b92a5d4a3ad4a-->

### `src/se3/daemon/wire_metrics.py` (python) — A dependency-free, stdlib-only module providing WireMetrics, a thread-safe per-message-type sent-byte/frame accumulator held at each end of the daemon↔server↔WebUI link to make wire-traffic-by-message-type verifiable at runtime and guard against traffic-reduction regressions. <!--#964b4dbede2b3604|81efb6cfe5411c03-->
- `WireMetrics` (class) — A thread-safe, in-process accumulator that tallies sent bytes and frame counts per WebSocket message type, with one instance held at each end (daemon client and server relay) to report which link/message type dominates wire traffic. <!--#087dde7db7931df8-->
  - `WireMetrics.__init__` (method) — Initializes the accumulator with a threading lock and empty per-message-type byte and count dictionaries. <!--#ee5f8f65e32594fa-->
  - `WireMetrics.record` (method) — Adds a frame's byte length (and one to the frame count) to the running total for a message type under the lock, defensively coercing bad/negative sizes to zero so accounting can never crash the real send path. <!--#71fe02f3289d22e7-->
  - `WireMetrics.snapshot` (method) — Returns a fresh point-in-time copy of per-type {bytes, count} counters plus a synthetic '__total__' roll-up, so callers can report both the breakdown and grand total without mutating internal state. <!--#0220956e757e3bf0-->
  - `WireMetrics.reset` (method) — Clears all byte and count counters under the lock, mainly for tests and per-window sampling. <!--#67395f01807f54d0-->

## `src/se3/engine/` — The SE3 flow engine package — the state-machine-driven workflow core — bundling the per-step handlers (analyze, plan, discovery, implement, commit, merge, fix-loop guards), the LLM prompt/context assembly and JSON-response parsing layer, supporting subsystems for charter, chat history, code-index building/rendering, fix-loop adjudication and baseline-fix memory, a DAG scheduler for parallel task-group execution across worktrees, output formatters, and the LLM-assisted sequential branch-merge engine. <!--#299006863b4d0907|eb3ee7f2ebf6bbf4-->

### `src/se3/engine/__init__.py` (python) — Package initializer for the SE3 flow engine — the state-machine-driven workflow core — that re-exports its public API (flow models, StateMachine, PersistenceManager, LLMCaller, schemas, structured logging, event stream, and sinks) and aliases EventEmitter as EventStream. <!--#bdee0c4d523b5958|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/se3/engine/adjudication.py` (python) — The pure, LLM-free core of the se3 fix-loop adjudication ("警察") mechanism: it normalizes issue fingerprints, maintains an append-only cross-round issue ledger on flow context, and applies three structural triggers (oscillation, contradiction, reproduction) plus a periodic backstop to decide when ADJUDICATE must run and convergence must be suppressed, leaving actual truth-determination to the ADJUDICATE LLM. <!--#aab826176cbf70b6|c5c74f9cdef9d6f9-->
- `_normalize_for_quote_match` (function) — Symmetric string normalizer (literal-newline unescape → NFKC → smart-quote replacement → whitespace collapse), deliberately duplicated from the self_check step to keep this pure module import-cycle-free while guaranteeing ledger keys and source-pool checks normalize identically. <!--#9810f5963a6c10cd-->
- `relaxed_quote_candidates` (function) — Single source of truth generating relaxed substring variants of a normalized quote (trimmed trailing ellipsis, stripped bullet/id prefix) so that source-pool validation and dead-clause abolition accept the same set of re-quotes. <!--#f77b5de029d4e1c1-->
- `_pk_quote` (function) — Extracts the normalized-quote component from a position_key string, returning empty when the key carries no quote. <!--#c6dee106c5a3e6d1-->
- `_issue_file` (function) — Derives an issue's fingerprint file-path component, preferring the first evidence line (with its trailing :N line number stripped) and falling back to the first missing_in path. <!--#195a3bda23d126ce-->
- `_issue_quote` (function) — Returns an issue's normalized verbatim expectation-source quote, or empty if absent. <!--#18dc6bcac691d7e8-->
- `_issue_expected` (function) — Returns an issue's normalized expected_behavior text. <!--#122306771b268131-->
- `position_key` (function) — Builds a location identity key from file path plus normalized quote (deliberately excluding expected content so disagreements at a shared position surface as oscillation/contradiction signals). <!--#a0ab61724e4d692b-->
- `fingerprint` (function) — Builds the full finding identity (file + normalized quote + normalized expected) used for reproduction counting, where a shared position but differing expected yields distinct fingerprints but the same position key. <!--#794ee82d97c609d1-->
- `_ensure_ledger` (function) — Returns (initializing if absent) the ctx ledger sub-tree with its append-only observation/resolution lists and counters, tolerating legacy ledger-less engine state and remaining idempotent on re-invocation. <!--#9aa4dae7f004f60c-->
- `_observation_from_issue` (function) — Constructs a single ledger observation record (round, file, quote, expected, position key, fingerprint, abolished flag) from an issue dict. <!--#181c6347e4b04084-->
- `record_self_check_round` (function) — Appends one SELF_CHECK round's issues as observations to the ledger, collapsing intra-round duplicate fingerprints, returning the assigned round index, and skipping replays that reuse a prior round_id token. <!--#6e9e5625d69d4c0d-->
- `record_fix_resolutions` (function) — Appends a fix round's previous_issue_resolution verdicts to the ledger, normalizing each into a fingerprint/position record and anchoring 'fixed' verdicts to the latest prior observation round so trigger (b)/(c) counting stays correct. <!--#57e0817ee5910623-->
- `mark_abolished` (function) — Flags (but retains) all ledger observations and resolutions whose fingerprint is in the given set so they stop driving triggers after an adjudication overrides their grounding clause, returning the count flagged. <!--#5e5be73c64f95acd-->
- `record_rejected_candidates` (function) — Records position keys the ADJUDICATE LLM ruled non-contradictions so they are permanently excluded from trigger (a) and never re-fire the adjudicator. <!--#eaf6ef6e95143091-->
- `AdjudicationDecision` (class) — Dataclass holding the trigger layer's structural verdict — whether ADJUDICATE should run, which triggers fired, the triggering positions/fingerprints, and whether convergence must be suppressed. <!--#bb634298bda7e1d8-->
  - `AdjudicationDecision.suppress_convergence` (method) — Property that is True whenever any signal trigger (a/b/c) fired, indicating convergence must yield to adjudication (the periodic backstop alone does not suppress). <!--#d82f9ae3758eefa2-->
- `_active_observations` (function) — Returns the ledger observations that are not abolished and therefore still count toward triggers. <!--#41c1adef493d761c-->
- `_current_round_index` (function) — Returns the index of the most recently recorded round (round_count − 1), the 'current' round given recording precedes trigger evaluation. <!--#0265ccca0b075e96-->
- `_detect_oscillation` (function) — Trigger (a): flags quote-anchored, non-rejected positions that were flagged in a prior round demanding a materially different expected than this round's, using set-difference so genuine A/B flips survive even self-contradicting earlier rounds. <!--#6e4cc932716bd02c-->
- `_detect_contradiction` (function) — Trigger (b) '打脸': flags any current quote-anchored, non-rejected position that carries a live 'fixed' resolution yet still shows a current fingerprint, firing immediately since a re-flagged or opposite finding conflicts with the resolved claim. <!--#1139e32d33fab517-->
- `_detect_reproduction` (function) — Trigger (c): flags full fingerprints that reappear at least the reproduction threshold (3) times strictly after their earliest declared-fixed round, skipping rejected and quoteless fingerprints to avoid livelocks. <!--#790d5a04b352c9b9-->
- `evaluate_triggers` (function) — Aggregates the three structural detectors plus the periodic backstop over the current round's issues into an AdjudicationDecision, doing purely structural judgement and leaving truth-determination to the ADJUDICATE LLM. <!--#ee8ae6aa71554754-->
- `note_adjudication_ran` (function) — Resets the ledger's periodic-backstop baseline to the current fix iteration so the next periodic sweep is measured from the last adjudication rather than flow start. <!--#440ca23de70e6f61-->
- `should_suppress_convergence` (function) — Convergence-guard helper that returns True when any trigger (including a due periodic backstop) is active, so the self_check convergence shortcut yields to a REVISION_NEEDED round and the state machine can insert ADJUDICATE. <!--#1f3cfb36a6c1d3f2-->

### `src/se3/engine/baseline_fix_memory.py` (python) — A cross-flow persistent store (schema-versioned JSON at se3/state/baseline_fix_attempts.json, written atomically and LRU-bounded, read corruption-tolerantly) that records which inherited/baseline test failures a fix loop has given up on so subsequent flows skip re-attempting the same un-fixable failures. <!--#c501d64f879331ae|4b4720d265c83075-->
- `memory_path` (function) — Returns the path to the baseline-fix memory JSON file (se3/state/baseline_fix_attempts.json) under a given project root. <!--#9eec86eaec770cfb-->
- `_read_entries` (function) — Corruption-tolerant reader that loads the memory's entries map, returning an empty dict on any missing/corrupt/schema-mismatched file rather than raising. <!--#d3d6de9e35eb54ba-->
- `load_given_up` (function) — Returns the set of test ids already given up on, reading an empty set when the store is missing or corrupt. <!--#27086faf5a83f3a9-->
- `load_given_up_details` (function) — Returns the full per-test_id metadata map (attempts/reason) so callers can surface why a baseline failure was abandoned. <!--#62d3a0c6091dc142-->
- `record_given_up` (function) — Atomically marks test ids as given-up, accumulating attempt counts and latest reason while LRU-trimming the store to MAX_ENTRIES. <!--#e31f6cbd4ec5c077-->

### `src/se3/engine/charter.py` (python) — Side-effect-free, stdlib-only module for the project charter (se3/charter.md, the shrunk successor to the base spec that is injected in full into every run step): it locates, loads, and template-renders the charter and implements the 'altitude gate' admission check plus the LLM prompt builder for the charter_freshness auto-update loop, where a non-blocking byte-size 'monitoring light' and a normative admission standard guard against low-level content leaking into the high-level charter. <!--#915741f939f2d947|b7b14d4357355953-->
- `AdmissionResult` (class) — Dataclass capturing the outcome of the charter altitude gate: byte size, threshold, advisory over-threshold flag, the normative admission-standard text, and an optional monitoring-light warning. <!--#254a712e6734b8f1-->
- `charter_path` (function) — Returns the absolute path to se3/charter.md for a given project root. <!--#65a9fce46453f1c5-->
- `load_charter` (function) — Reads the full charter text for whole-text injection, degrading to an empty string (never raising) when the file is missing or unreadable. <!--#dfbea1c686094d59-->
- `load_charter_template` (function) — Returns the raw packaged charter.md template text without any placeholder substitution. <!--#14e46cbcc4abd4d3-->
- `render_charter_template` (function) — Renders the packaged charter template by literal-replacing {key} placeholders, leaving incidental braces untouched, for use by init/migrate. <!--#30f6fa7d05c57c78-->
- `_changed_paths_touch_charter` (function) — Helper that returns True iff se3/charter.md appears among the changed files, matching on the path tail to tolerate relative/absolute and Windows-separator forms. <!--#44ee47271579de1f-->
- `admission_check_for_changes` (function) — Trigger point that runs the altitude gate only when the charter was actually changed, returning the AdmissionResult or None when the charter is untouched. <!--#82c6810331ea6f27-->
- `build_admission_gate_prompt` (function) — Assembles (pure string, no I/O or LLM call) the binding admission-gate prompt for a proposed charter update, injecting the admission standard, the full candidate charter, verbatim removed/rewritten passages (or a pure-insertion notice), an optional triggering diff summary, and the removal-weakening question, and instructs the LLM to return a JSON verdict of `admitted`/`violations`/`weakened_removals`. <!--#c703412ef9cd2ed7-->
- `check_admission` (function) — Runs the charter altitude gate against given text, computing a non-blocking monitoring-light warning when the UTF-8 byte size exceeds the threshold and attaching the normative admission standard. <!--#d2630d46b30139ac-->

### `src/se3/engine/chat_history.py` (python) — Chat-history subsystem that records per-step LLM prompts and responses as JSONL ChatMessage records under se3/history/{flow_id}/{step_id}.jsonl, tracking token usage, agent/model metadata, and fix-loop iterations to support retry-context injection and human-readable conversation browsing. <!--#98495f7a54cb418b|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/se3/engine/code_index.py` (python) — The core module that builds the deterministic code-index structure map: it enumerates the project tree, extracts within-file symbols per language (Python AST, markdown/YAML/JSON keys, or degraded chunks) into Fingerprint/Symbol/FileEntry/CodeIndex dataclasses, computes recursive and mechanical 'list' fingerprints so only changed nodes are re-summarised while human corrections are preserved, and atomically renders/reparses the authoritative fingerprint-embedded `se3/code-index.md` under an advisory build lock. <!--#9a49282cc43765e6|0d15b6b6f30c1992-->
- `Fingerprint` (class) — A dataclass holding one file's content fingerprint — cheap mtime/size signals plus the authoritative sha256 prefix used as the change signal. <!--#9451c48c84db3103-->
- `Symbol` (class) — Dataclass for one within-file node (class/function/method, structural unit, or degraded chunk) carrying its id, kind, location, hash, summary, and optional verbatim content. <!--#a009f18727b02756-->
- `FileEntry` (class) — Dataclass holding one enumerated file's path, kind, fingerprints (whole-file plus a direct-symbol-roster 'list' fingerprint that gates reuse without cascading on body edits), summary, and extracted child symbols. <!--#c08141b42a516794-->
  - `FileEntry.symbol_id` (method) — Returns a symbol's full id by joining the file's relpath and the symbol's local id with '::'. <!--#c3974e13d18e0fdf-->
- `CodeIndex` (class) — Dataclass representing the in-memory structure map — a relpath→FileEntry table plus per-directory summaries, recursive content fingerprints, and direct-child list fingerprints — and able to reconstruct a render-only instance from the authoritative md via from_md. <!--#45de87d959de8cc5-->
  - `CodeIndex.from_md` (method) — Classmethod that rebuilds a render-sufficient CodeIndex by parsing directory headings, file headings, and symbol bullets out of the authoritative md, capturing only structure and summaries (fingerprints left zeroed). <!--#1ad25495637898a3-->
- `_split_fp` (function) — Helper that strips an md line's embedded fingerprint comment, returning the bare line plus its parsed content-fp and (optional) list-fp before any heading/bullet regex runs. <!--#fca7095dc35bd53e-->
- `_fp_comment` (function) — Helper that renders the trailing fingerprint HTML comment for an md line, emitting the legacy single-fp shape or the dual content|list shape when a list-fp is supplied. <!--#af268880669ba2d9-->
- `SummaryTarget` (class) — A dataclass describing one node (symbol, file, or directory) that needs an LLM summary, carrying its id, owning path, kind, name, and content to summarise. <!--#784c7c0812cd97aa-->
- `_sha256_prefix` (function) — Returns a hex sha256 of the given bytes truncated to a configurable prefix length. <!--#4a3d0b21f35268a9-->
- `_sha256_text` (function) — Hashes a string by UTF-8 encoding it and delegating to _sha256_prefix. <!--#4f7607d84cf5f60a-->
- `_fp` (function) — Helper that truncates a node's sha256 to the first `_FP_LEN` hex chars for embedding in the md. <!--#7dc034e8bbda50ba-->
- `_slice_lines` (function) — Returns the 1-based inclusive line range of a list of lines joined by newlines, clamping out-of-range bounds. <!--#b6d736c0ae3a5c02-->
- `_extract_python` (function) — Extracts top-level classes/functions and class methods from Python source via AST, stopping at the function/method level. <!--#8977c5a354cfcd6a-->
- `_extract_markdown` (function) — Extracts markdown headings (ignoring fenced code blocks) as structural units, each spanning to the next heading. <!--#e78a2c67046c83eb-->
- `_line_of_top_key` (function) — Best-effort lookup of the 1-based line number where a top-level YAML/key declaration appears. <!--#cf55f29734a6211c-->
- `_extract_yaml` (function) — Extracts top-level YAML mapping keys as symbols, carrying each key's serialized value as content. <!--#03759e3e86c28e59-->
- `_extract_json` (function) — Extracts top-level JSON object keys as symbols, carrying each key's serialized value as content. <!--#915a274e73e1db64-->
- `_extract_structure` (function) — Dispatches structural extraction to the right per-extension extractor, returning [] when none applies or none is found. <!--#25e24dfeb6fb8a76-->
- `_file_kind` (function) — Classifies a file as python/markdown/yaml/json/text by its extension. <!--#8090ae4dd5164009-->
- `is_degrade_eligible` (function) — Returns whether a file qualifies for last-resort chunk degradation by requiring all three conditions: text, no structure, and over a size threshold. <!--#08b26f76b777e5f6-->
- `_chunk_degraded` (function) — Splits a structure-less oversized file into line/byte-bounded chunks, each emitted as one degraded symbol. <!--#93818e7aaf52f59e-->
- `_index_file` (function) — Builds a structural FileEntry for one path (no summaries) — handling binary/unreadable files, structural symbol extraction, oversized-file collapsing, and structure-less degradation to chunks. <!--#d4b21d66db7f2546-->
- `md_path` (function) — Returns the path to the authoritative se3/code-index.md under the project root. <!--#f147cb0ac2d3f6ee-->
- `lock_path` (function) — Returns the path of the advisory build-lock file under the gitignored `se3/cache/` directory. <!--#d9a84f9915e55bf2-->
- `_build_lock` (function) — Context manager holding an exclusive advisory flock across a build's load→enumerate→write critical section to serialize concurrent rebuilds, falling back to unlocked when fcntl is unavailable. <!--#bfdd14e1fa8107ed-->
- `_atomic_write_text` (function) — Writes text to a path atomically via a unique per-write temp file plus os.replace, so concurrent writers never clobber each other. <!--#b1565ce44f841b76-->
- `_dir_of` (function) — Returns the directory key of a file's immediate parent directory. <!--#29c094ab2953dd41-->
- `_parent_dir` (function) — Returns the parent directory key of a directory key (None for the root). <!--#a3be6ae8fa72d759-->
- `_depth` (function) — Returns the nesting depth of a directory key (root = 0). <!--#106ed76edc8752c9-->
- `_all_dir_keys` (function) — Computes the set of every directory key in the tree — every ancestor of every file plus the root. <!--#a754c18a54352d82-->
- `_child_files` (function) — Returns the sorted relpaths of files whose immediate parent directory is the given directory key. <!--#a60e7ddda26ff7ca-->
- `_child_dirs` (function) — Returns the sorted directory keys whose immediate parent is the given directory key. <!--#336d66009c59273a-->
- `_compute_dir_fps` (function) — Computes a recursive per-directory content fingerprint bottom-up so any change in a subtree propagates up and re-summarises every ancestor while untouched siblings reuse cached summaries. <!--#eb5bf3ca6ead4260-->
- `_compute_file_list_fp` (function) — Computes a file's mechanical 'list' fingerprint by hashing only its direct symbols' sorted (kind, name) roster — ignoring bodies, summaries, position, and order — so body-only edits don't change it. <!--#06db726193d7e3a4-->
- `_compute_dir_list_fps` (function) — Computes each directory's non-recursive 'list' fingerprint by hashing only its direct child names (immediate files and subdirs), so a deep edit never bubbles up and each level reuses independently. <!--#51135b8b8c0187f7-->
- `render_full` (function) — Renders the complete authoritative md map — every directory level, file, and symbol — embedding each node's content (and list) fingerprint only when it already has a real summary so partial flushes stay safe resume points. <!--#4b2fc507f56d93d1-->
- `_write_md` (function) — Atomically writes the rendered authoritative md for an index to its md path. <!--#e0d9f93ae34e6f6a-->
- `_parse_md` (function) — Parses the authoritative md into three node-id-keyed maps (reusable summaries, content fingerprints, and migrated file/dir list fingerprints), reading everything from the committed md with no out-of-band cache. <!--#75f859777f45cf86-->
- `_parse_md_summaries` (function) — Convenience wrapper returning just the `{id: summary}` map from the parsed md. <!--#7b2c20ea52847695-->
- `_flatten_summary` (function) — Collapses an LLM summary's whitespace (including newlines) to a single physical line so the one-node-per-line md format isn't corrupted. <!--#ab4fda75898c4eba-->
- `_heuristic_summary` (function) — Produces a deterministic placeholder summary used when no LLM is available or a call fails, keeping builds from crashing. <!--#5e95c0cfd0580e7b-->
- `_make_llm_summarizer` (function) — Factory that builds the default LLM-backed summariser for the code index, batching targets into one LLM call per owning path, running those per-path groups concurrently (each with its own LLMCaller instance for thread safety), firing an optional per-group progress callback, and falling back to heuristic summaries whenever a call fails. <!--#be8e06fa18f9393c-->
- `_make_target` (function) — Builds the summary target for a symbol (using its own content or a line slice) or, as a fallback, a file node from its own source. <!--#3bcb90fc368a7d51-->
- `_make_file_target` (function) — Builds a file's summary target bottom-up — from a digest of its symbols' one-line summaries, or its own source when it has no symbols. <!--#303ef86543b2fdf0-->
- `_make_dir_target` (function) — Builds a directory's summary target bottom-up from its immediate child subdirectory and file summaries. <!--#0490470f87f95416-->
- `_summarize_wave` (function) — Summarises one dependency wave by invoking the summariser and assigning each result onto its dir/symbol/file node, skipping empty waves and firing on_node per assigned target (the progress path used for injected, opaque summarisers). <!--#53c05db5ae43802d-->
- `build_index` (function) — The single (re)build entry point that enumerates the project, extracts structure, summarises changed nodes bottom-up and writes the authoritative md, running the whole critical section under a best-effort exclusive advisory lock. <!--#1e7a8ba29d5f15e1-->
- `_build_index_locked` (function) — The lock-held body of build_index that parses any prior md, enumerates files and directories, computes content and direct-member list fingerprints, and uses per-level list-fp reuse gates to seed unchanged summaries with no LLM before re-summarising only the changed nodes. <!--#bf34cf54fa4f39a5-->
- `load_or_build` (function) — Thin lazy-incremental entry point that delegates to build_index, forwarding force and an optional progress emitter to refresh only changed nodes (or everything under force). <!--#1d7726c26d3419c1-->

### `src/se3/engine/code_index_render.py` (python) — Renders two display views over the authoritative `se3/code-index.md` — a byte-budgeted zoomable adaptive root map and a literal one-level drill-in — plus a flat grep-able line dump, all reconstructed read-only from the md. <!--#465ee04b791e829b|631c387dbec56708-->
- `load_for_display` (function) — Reconstructs a render-only CodeIndex from the authoritative `se3/code-index.md` on disk, returning None when no build has produced that file yet. <!--#efdde682055b6a2a-->
- `_top_of` (function) — Returns the top-level ancestor directory key of a given directory key (or the key itself if already top-level). <!--#42c3cefff4559ca3-->
- `_auto_primary_roots` (function) — Auto-detects the code-bearing top-level directories to treat as primary expansion roots, falling back to all top-level dirs when none contain code. <!--#6ea444b4ecf816de-->
- `_subtree_file_counts` (function) — Computes, in one pass, the number of files contained in the subtree of every directory by incrementing each file's ancestor directories. <!--#7afffc3c5eead1ed-->
- `_render_view` (function) — Renders the directory tree as a bulleted markdown map, descending only into the expanded directories and showing files under expanded parents. <!--#ef2c6ecc16fafe5c-->
- `_expansion_costs` (function) — Precomputes the byte cost of expanding each directory (its immediate children block) so the render budget can be checked incrementally in O(1) per candidate. <!--#af7dd118de471c22-->
- `render_adaptive` (function) — Produces the byte-budgeted zoomable root view, expanding frontier directories shallowest-and-densest-first within primary roots until the budget is exhausted. <!--#d164459ab4fc6ed8-->
- `_render_file_detail` (function) — Helper that formats a single file's heading plus its indented function/method symbol tree, marking degraded symbols. <!--#68467cdf328f6577-->
- `_render_one_level` (function) — Renders exactly the immediate children (subdirs and files) of a single directory key as a markdown section. <!--#0ecd37d78e015b3a-->
- `iter_search_lines` (function) — Flattens the entire code index into a sorted list of one grep-able bullet line per item — each directory, file, and in-file symbol (with symbols carrying their owning file's full `relpath::local_id` path) — built from the structured index so lines carry no fingerprint comments. <!--#00c27601d73e1a21-->
- `render_path` (function) — Renders the one-level drill-in view for a given path — root level, a file's full symbol tree, a directory's immediate children, or a not-found note. <!--#e9351a5830007db3-->

### `src/se3/engine/conftest.py` (python) — Pytest fixture module scoped to engine tests that sandboxes the live repo — redirecting chat-history writes into tmp dirs, stubbing out real LLM code-index refreshes, and pinning the UI language to en-US for deterministic assertions. <!--#d248b98832403512|1ec988100dc42efb-->
- `_real_history_roots` (function) — Helper that returns the set of filesystem paths considered the live repo root (the package's top-level parent and the current working directory), used to detect when test writes would leak into the real repository. <!--#6f2232fb1afc6fc6-->
- `_no_chat_history_leak_to_real_repo` (function) — Pytest fixture (twin of the one in tests/conftest.py) that monkeypatches chat_history's `_history_dir` resolver so any engine-test chat-history write targeting a real repo root is redirected into a per-test tmp dir, preventing fake history files from leaking into the committed se3/history/. <!--#9d7557010e9adf76-->
- `_no_real_code_index_refresh` (function) — An autouse-style engine-test fixture that monkeypatches `context_builder.ensure_code_index_fresh` to a no-op, preventing analyze/commit flow steps from triggering a real, flock-serialized LLM code-index rebuild against the live repo during unit tests. <!--#a936702bb02dfe92-->
- `_force_en_us_ui_language` (function) — A pytest fixture that pins the i18n UI language to en-US (via SE3_LANG plus singleton/cache resets, restored afterwards) so engine tests co-located with the source get stable English rendered strings instead of the repo's zh-CN default. <!--#1e1eda4fc59e2147-->

### `src/se3/engine/context.py` (python) — Defines the read-only Context wrapper around workflow State plus the pure effective_task_type resolver, centralizing the logic that surfaces a real task type (feature/bugfix) rather than a run mode like 'discovery' for commit-message, version, and UI display consumers. <!--#452bcd230af5840e|90feb89a44d2ba97-->
- `effective_task_type` (function) — Pure resolver that returns the real task type (feature/bugfix/etc.) for commit-message and version consumers, preferring an explicit --type, then analyze's persisted type, then a sanitized flow fallback, never returning a run mode like 'discovery'. <!--#bcfd3dadd820ea37-->
- `Context` (class) — Read-only wrapper around workflow State that exposes the task description and display-friendly task-type properties, encapsulating the logic that distinguishes resolved task types from run modes and pending state. <!--#81e0e2bc8cdbd3e4-->
  - `Context.__init__` (method) — Constructor storing the original task description and the workflow State reference. <!--#8242df2429226234-->
  - `Context.task_description` (method) — Property returning the original task description string. <!--#9ad8135cc0823e21-->
  - `Context.task_type` (method) — Property that resolves the current task type from state (resolved_type, explicit_type, flow type, or analyzed_type), skipping run modes and returning the 'pending' sentinel when no real type is available yet. <!--#3bb2d6106a2e5b27-->
  - `Context.display_type` (method) — Property returning the display-friendly task type from resolved_type (mapping a run mode to its real analyzed type), or None while the type is still pending. <!--#ad0cf2c8ef999b33-->
  - `Context.is_type_pending` (method) — Returns whether the task type is still unresolved, delegating to State's method when available. <!--#a8174bd77d016406-->
  - `Context.__repr__` (method) — Debug string representation showing the task type and pending status. <!--#ac43d00ede6802c8-->

### `src/se3/engine/context_builder.py` (python) — Central prompt-context assembly module for the run engine: it computes the per-step LLM prompt injections (language/spec-language instructions, runtime-environment capabilities, issue discovery, spec index and charter, code-index root map with lazy refresh, worktree runtime context, plus read-only and spec-write-protection constraints gated by step whitelists), owns `is_step_read_only` as the single source of truth for read-only step enforcement, and builds the review/confirm/adjudicate prompts and display payloads used at LLM-review and human approval gates. <!--#d5199173afc27898|1fd53681f0c44652-->
- `get_step_language_instruction` (function) — Returns the language instruction to append to a run-engine step's prompt, routing spec steps to spec_language, human-facing/confirmed steps to the general language, and everything else to no injection. <!--#69f7354a76473892-->
- `get_spec_language_instruction` (function) — Returns the spec-flavored language instruction string derived from the project's configured `language.spec_language` (empty when unset), so non-state-machine knowledge-asset writers such as the sync_* modules can inject the same wording that the `update_spec` step gets. <!--#204d184923fe2a05-->
- `_load_runtime_environment_markdown` (function) — Reads and process-caches runtime_environment.md, returning empty string with a one-time warning on read failure. <!--#c69d2cc539e7ddc0-->
- `_reset_runtime_environment_cache` (function) — Test-only helper that clears the runtime_environment.md cache so reload paths can be exercised. <!--#8fcfcfa91ac8350c-->
- `get_runtime_environment_injection` (function) — Returns the se3 runtime-environment capability markdown for whitelisted steps (default list overridable via se3.yaml, minus always-forbidden steps). <!--#e2ac12eb9ac7a402-->
- `get_issue_discovery_injection` (function) — Returns the B-class issue-discovery prompt fragment for steps in the configurable whitelist and not in the forbidden set. <!--#bbb89699dda1eaf7-->
- `get_spec_names_injection` (function) — Builds the 'available specifications' injection listing all specs and which are already loaded, instructing the LLM to consult others on demand via the read-only `se3 spec` index commands. <!--#f54620f6f99f8ee6-->
- `get_charter_injection` (function) — Returns the project charter (se3/charter.md) wrapped in a labelled section, injected in full on every step as the authoritative convention channel. <!--#2427642e166932b4-->
- `get_code_index_injection` (function) — Builds the per-step LLM prompt injection that presents the project's adaptive code-index root map (or a not-yet-built notice) plus the drill-down/search protocol, reading only from the authoritative se3/code-index.md without triggering a rebuild. <!--#c531b3ea853b3021-->
- `ensure_code_index_fresh` (function) — Best-effort helper that a flow step calls before injecting the code index to trigger a lazy-incremental rebuild of se3/code-index.md (only re-summarising changed symbols), optionally streaming per-node progress to the web console when a flow/step context is given, gated on the map already existing and swallowing any failure so prompt construction never breaks. <!--#00be438f657b8eda-->
- `is_step_read_only` (function) — Predicate that determines whether a given step type runs under read-only constraints by consulting STEP_POOL attributes plus sync-engine and internal pure-data step sets, serving as the single source of truth for both prompt-level read-only injection and tool-level enforcement. <!--#06ae86fbd04076e4-->
- `get_read_only_injection` (function) — Returns a read-only constraint prompt string forbidding file modifications for read-only steps (or when `force` is set), delegating the read-only determination to `is_step_read_only`. <!--#114d0ac15b71666c-->
- `_is_spec_write_protected_step` (function) — Returns True when a step is a non-read-only LLM step outside `SPEC_WRITE_ALLOWED_STEPS`, marking it for a se3/specs write-protection prompt injection. <!--#ff0b104a83421c39-->
- `get_spec_write_protection_injection` (function) — Returns the spec-file write-protection prompt fragment for spec-write-protected steps, forbidding edits under se3/specs/ while leaving code changes free. <!--#f405841f29eb8970-->
- `get_runtime_context_injection` (function) — When running in a worktree, injects context about gitignored runtime state (open issues, flow state, history) that exists only in the main repository. <!--#40ad7d8911426794-->
- `_detect_main_repo_root` (function) — Detects the main repository root from a worktree path via git's --git-common-dir, returning None if detection fails. <!--#d5041cfe6374379d-->
- `ContextBuilder` (class) — Class providing specs-directory resolution and spec-content loading for the analyze and discovery handlers. <!--#9edf18ec74038306-->
  - `ContextBuilder.__init__` (method) — Initializes the builder with a project root and resolves its specs directory. <!--#7c2a9e8da739c1ae-->
  - `ContextBuilder._resolve_specs_dir` (method) — Static helper resolving the specs directory, preferring se3/specs/ then specs/ then the legacy openspec/specs/. <!--#1d639c614f0c5fc6-->
  - `ContextBuilder._load_spec_content` (method) — Loads a spec's text by name, trying several candidate paths and returning None if none exist. <!--#8cd7e0c8ec088d86-->
- `build_llm_review_prompt` (function) — Builds the structured prompt for LLM-based review of a step's output, formatting the output, optional revision feedback, evaluation criteria, and required JSON response format. <!--#bf66f623e57bd0bb-->
- `build_plan_confirm_prompt` (function) — Builds the always-on plan-confirm review prompt that asks an LLM reviewer to decompose the task's discrete requirements and verify each is covered by at least one task in the plan's task_groups, returning the standard {approved, feedback} contract for the requirement→task half of SE3's two-stage coverage guarantee. <!--#eb93edc45352586e-->
- `build_confirm_prompt` (function) — Returns the one-line human-readable question shown at a CONFIRM approval gate, with a special wording for adjudicate reviews and a generic "review the <step type> output" fallback. <!--#625a3476caf9d1a5-->
- `_display_covered_surfaces` (function) — Defensively sanitizes a ruling's raw `covered_surfaces` value into a list of well-formed {surface, justification} dicts, silently dropping malformed entries so the human-approval display degrades instead of crashing. <!--#7aa129def41bb195-->
- `build_adjudicate_review_context` (function) — Builds the display payload a CONFIRM gate needs to review an ADJUDICATE ruling — rationale, adjudicated description, the pre-ruling baseline description (resolved excluding the reviewed step), and the sanitized covered-surfaces sweep — returning an empty dict for non-adjudicate steps. <!--#fc9df5ee52290489-->

### `src/se3/engine/dag_scheduler.py` (python) — Event-driven parallel scheduler that builds a validated DAG from task-group dependencies and runs groups via a ThreadPoolExecutor, using relay planning (classify_chains/RelayPlan/RelayContext) to reuse, fork, or converge worktree branches while emitting per-group lifecycle status and returning GroupResults. <!--#9f4a305db6d4857c|8e398420b3a80b98-->
- `ConvergenceInfo` (class) — Dataclass capturing, for a node with multiple predecessors, which predecessor's worktree is inherited (primary) and which predecessors' branches are merged in (secondary). <!--#1b7a60866faacf8e-->
- `RelayContext` (class) — Runtime context handed to the executor telling a group how to obtain its worktree — reuse a predecessor's, fork a new branch, or create fresh — plus any convergence branches to merge. <!--#05abe19424a373e2-->
- `RelayPlan` (class) — Dataclass holding the full relay execution strategy (relay map, fork sources, leaf/root nodes, convergence points) produced by classify_chains and consumed by the scheduler. <!--#06c133c34947e5d3-->
- `classify_chains` (function) — Analyzes DAG topology to produce a RelayPlan, deciding per group whether to create a new worktree, relay from a primary predecessor, fork, or merge at a convergence point. <!--#a14041499502d9b6-->
- `_relay_plan_is_linear` (function) — Helper returning True when a RelayPlan describes a single-root, fork-free linear chain, letting callers skip DAG-parallel execution that would yield no parallelism. <!--#195dd89fd4eb9574-->
- `GroupResult` (class) — Dataclass representing the outcome of executing one task group (status, files/tests changed, branch, worktree, completion details) with skipped/failed constructor helpers. <!--#c16bb24282ecaca3-->
  - `GroupResult.skipped` (method) — Classmethod constructing a GroupResult marked as skipped because an upstream dependency failed. <!--#41b078e164946dde-->
  - `GroupResult.failed` (method) — Classmethod constructing a GroupResult marked as failed with the given error message. <!--#fb9f926def640ccf-->
- `DAGScheduler` (class) — Core class that builds a validated DAG from group dependencies and drives parallel execution via ThreadPoolExecutor + Condition, emitting per-group lifecycle status and building relay contexts. <!--#2a8c65cc167d157f-->
  - `DAGScheduler.__init__` (method) — Initializes the scheduler's config and DAG bookkeeping structures and builds the DAG from the supplied groups. <!--#7fbf3b1d94a456b5-->
  - `DAGScheduler._emit_status` (method) — Safely invokes the optional on_group_status callback, swallowing and logging any exception so a faulty status sink cannot disrupt scheduling. <!--#6944feb1a073cafa-->
  - `DAGScheduler._build_dag` (method) — Builds the group map, forward/reverse adjacency, and in-degrees from depends_on edges and validates the graph is acyclic. <!--#1d7fc2a08282d9bd-->
  - `DAGScheduler._kahn_topo_sort` (method) — Computes a topological ordering of groups via Kahn's algorithm, with a short result signaling a cycle. <!--#e8ecf8fb870b4c2b-->
  - `DAGScheduler._build_relay_context` (method) — Constructs a RelayContext for a group from the relay plan and completed predecessor results, resolving worktree reuse, fork source, and convergence merge branches. <!--#50778ecfac8bbe73-->
  - `DAGScheduler.run` (method) — Executes all groups in dependency order, submitting ready groups to a thread pool, propagating failures to downstream groups, and returning their GroupResults. <!--#a61ec96384e2fe46-->
  - `DAGScheduler.get_fallback_leaves` (method) — Returns completed groups whose downstream all failed or were skipped (excluding normal leaves), so their valid work can be merged back as fallback. <!--#516fb66a7a14bfae-->
  - `DAGScheduler.topological_merge_order` (method) — Returns groups in topological order to guide the sequence of branch merges back to the main branch. <!--#277ba115a8b5b1be-->

### `src/se3/engine/display.py` (python) — Rich-based display utilities that render LLM outputs, specs, proposals, designs, code, diffs, markdown, and token-usage summaries as full-content (untruncated) styled terminal blocks via a shared Console singleton. <!--#5ed270e1b794909e|542b7c7ad2425872-->
- `get_console` (function) — Lazily creates and returns the module-global Rich Console singleton. <!--#34af9b63623b3216-->
- `set_console` (function) — Overrides the module-global Console instance, mainly for testing. <!--#3c900a44fe46127f-->
- `_reverse_title` (function) — Builds a reverse-color ` ## Title ` heading as a Rich Text object on a colored background. <!--#548f67b20e68a7ec-->
- `_reverse_footer` (function) — Builds a fixed-width reverse-color whitespace block used as a block's bottom boundary marker. <!--#b3b374c4e5cfae09-->
- `render_block_header` (function) — Public wrapper that prints a reverse-color block title followed by a blank line. <!--#6bc1573d1ddb863c-->
- `render_block_footer` (function) — Public wrapper that prints the fixed-width reverse-color block footer followed by a blank line. <!--#b02ffd2b25f0e7e4-->
- `render_usage_block` (function) — Renders a token/cost summary (input, output, cache, cost) as an aligned two-column reverse-color block, accepting a UsageTotals, its dict form, or None (printing nothing when empty). <!--#8b192ae6d60d9f61-->
- `render_full` (function) — Prints arbitrary content in full without truncation, optionally wrapped in a blue title/footer block. <!--#cc2bafbda92f1b83-->
- `render_proposal` (function) — Formats a proposal dict — summary, files to modify/create with reasons, rationale, plus any extra fields — into styled markup and prints it via render_full. <!--#6d0f1e9bb416f3b6-->
- `render_design` (function) — Formats a design-document dict — overview, components, interfaces, key decisions, and any additional sections — into section-headed styled text rendered via render_full. <!--#d062764c0cce5794-->
- `render_spec_content` (function) — Formats a spec dict — title/version/type metadata header, description, requirements, and extra sections — into styled text rendered via render_full. <!--#bc18d620c9aa9fbd-->
- `render_text` (function) — Renders plain text left-aligned with an optional title block and optional Rich style. <!--#02638b45c952b7be-->
- `render_code` (function) — Renders code with syntax highlighting and line numbers under an optional green title block. <!--#5b51ac6cd6788d16-->
- `render_diff` (function) — Prints a unified diff for a file with red/green/cyan coloring, gutter line numbers derived from hunk headers, and truncation past a max-line limit. <!--#034a49466dfa98af-->
- `render_markdown` (function) — Renders markdown content via Rich's Markdown under an optional magenta title block. <!--#57673343920809b3-->

### `src/se3/engine/docs_updater.py` (python) — Module providing the DocumentationUpdater class (plus a small {{key}}-substituting Template helper and template-path resolvers) that updates a project's README.md version badge/header and inserts or idempotently merges VERSIONS.md changelog entries using configurable, template-driven placeholders. <!--#b4e48d19f90536e8|95d19a05a7460871-->
- `_versions_md_template_path` (function) — Module-level helper returning the path to the packaged versions_md.md template (resolved relative to this module so tests can monkeypatch it). <!--#76ac7c1506576aea-->
- `_versions_entry_template_from_file` (function) — Reads the first ## section of the packaged versions_md.md template and returns it as a fallback entry template only if it contains the required {{version}} and {{changes}} placeholders, else None. <!--#fcd606d5ab77c4ed-->
- `Template` (class) — Simple template holder that substitutes {{key}} placeholders with merged default and context values. <!--#aa02c2559079b161-->
  - `Template.__init__` (method) — Stores the template content string and an optional dict of default placeholder values. <!--#4aeb58f2bd29890e-->
  - `Template.render` (method) — Returns the content with each {{key}} replaced by its value from the merged placeholder/context dictionary. <!--#3ea1ee9e956e5b1b-->
- `DocumentationUpdater` (class) — The core class that updates a project's README.md version badge/header and inserts or merges VERSIONS.md changelog entries using configurable placeholder templates. <!--#bb255f0881fe7061-->
  - `DocumentationUpdater.__init__` (method) — Stores the project root and config, then loads the template set via _load_templates. <!--#bdedeb61dfc386a6-->
  - `DocumentationUpdater._load_templates` (method) — Builds the readme_badge, optional readme_header, and versions_entry templates from config with file/default fallbacks. <!--#92a84c251a5f850e-->
  - `DocumentationUpdater.update_readme` (method) — Reads README.md, replaces its version badge (and header if configured), and writes back only if the content changed; raises if README.md is missing. <!--#04e75a628f5ca34d-->
  - `DocumentationUpdater._build_context` (method) — Constructs the base render context (version, current date, year) merged with any additional context. <!--#df355d4c1e939574-->
  - `DocumentationUpdater._replace_version_badge` (method) — Replaces an existing version badge by regex, or inserts a freshly rendered badge after the title heading (skipping YAML front-matter and leading HTML comments). <!--#b5f47aef81a18505-->
  - `DocumentationUpdater._replace_version_header` (method) — Replaces the first matching version-header line in README content using the configured readme_header template, leaving content unchanged if none exists. <!--#5eba858b38211444-->
  - `DocumentationUpdater.update_versions_md` (method) — Renders a new changelog entry and inserts it into an existing VERSIONS.md (or creates the file with a header if absent). <!--#9d948f317e8bb930-->
  - `DocumentationUpdater._format_changes` (method) — Formats a list of change descriptions into a markdown bullet block, falling back to the 'No changes recorded' placeholder when the list is empty. <!--#6aaf04eb5c1d653b-->
  - `DocumentationUpdater._insert_version_entry` (method) — Inserts a new rendered version entry into VERSIONS.md, or merges its bullets into an existing same-version block, after normalizing head blank lines to avoid duplicate-version data loss. <!--#4a3f9b50baa3328a-->
  - `DocumentationUpdater._versions_entry_header_line` (method) — Returns the version-bearing header line of the effective versions_entry template (the line carrying `{{version}}`) so header detection works for any heading level or non-heading template. <!--#d3dfd87db700bf82-->
  - `DocumentationUpdater._version_header_pattern` (method) — Builds a regex that matches an existing VERSIONS.md block header for a given version, derived from the template's literal prefix/suffix so bracketed, suffixless, and varied header shapes are all recognized for merging. <!--#b67ee467f635bc25-->
  - `DocumentationUpdater._version_header_marker` (method) — Returns the literal `#`-prefix (or non-heading literal) that begins every version block header, used to bound block scans at the correct heading level. <!--#edfbb8461630f2d1-->
  - `DocumentationUpdater._inline_changes_from_header` (method) — Recovers changelog text rendered on the same line as the version (single-line entry templates like `ENTRY {{version}} | {{changes}}`) so those inline bullets participate in dedupe/merge. <!--#36200207e8bbba0e-->
  - `DocumentationUpdater._merge_change_lines` (method) — Merges an entry's new changelog bullets into an existing version block idempotently, deduping against existing bullets, dropping the no-changes placeholder once real bullets exist, and inserting before the block's trailing blanks. <!--#6263d26215adb9b9-->
  - `DocumentationUpdater._normalize_head_blanks` (method) — Idempotently collapses the blank-line run immediately after the VERSIONS.md title heading to a single blank line, leaving title-less or non-title-first files untouched. <!--#6faaa3b0d08c4748-->
  - `DocumentationUpdater._create_new_versions_md` (method) — Returns brand-new VERSIONS.md content with a 'Version History' header followed by the first entry. <!--#1f2a677e05d7bc42-->
  - `DocumentationUpdater.render_template` (method) — Renders a named template with the given context, raising KeyError if the template is not registered. <!--#ed1913f03093bd06-->
  - `DocumentationUpdater.add_template` (method) — Registers a custom named template with optional default placeholders. <!--#a2e403c04c0432e5-->
  - `DocumentationUpdater.update_both` (method) — Convenience method that updates both README.md and VERSIONS.md, returning a dict of per-file success flags and tolerating missing files. <!--#e95fc6040805098f-->

### `src/se3/engine/event_stream.py` (python) — Defines SE3's unified in-memory flow event stream: the EventType lifecycle enum, the serializable Event dataclass with its new_event factory, and an EventEmitter pub/sub hub that fans events out to pluggable sinks (CLI/JSON) with per-sink fault isolation and scoped subscriptions. <!--#bb8c44fc6ab62e7c|a0e685a12504c7b1-->
- `EventType` (class) — A str-backed Enum enumerating every flow-lifecycle event type (flow started/paused/completed/failed, step started/output/completed/failed, interjection/call needed) with JSON-serializable string values. <!--#5042d02dff7f81ca-->
- `Event` (class) — Dataclass representing one structured stream event (type, timestamp, flow/step ids, step type, arbitrary data payload) with dict serialization round-trip helpers. <!--#8025abee4638212c-->
  - `Event.to_dict` (method) — Serializes an Event to a plain JSON-friendly dict, reducing the type enum to its string value and passing data through verbatim. <!--#c81b31aedb4967c2-->
  - `Event.from_dict` (method) — Classmethod that reconstructs an Event from a to_dict payload, supplying defaults for missing optional fields. <!--#e7515b91e274fa52-->
- `new_event` (function) — Convenience factory used by run_flow that builds an Event, collecting keyword payload arguments into its data dict. <!--#3da965c97a496c47-->
- `EventEmitter` (class) — In-memory pub/sub hub holding an ordered list of subscribed sinks and fanning each emitted Event out to them, with isolation against failing sinks and a scoped-subscription context manager. <!--#13f76d85d2b8b4ac-->
  - `EventEmitter.__init__` (method) — Initializes the emitter with an empty subscriber-sink list. <!--#777bfe63b8aa5014-->
  - `EventEmitter.sinks` (method) — Property returning a copy of the currently subscribed sinks in subscription order. <!--#6eaaeda2e99bfed6-->
  - `EventEmitter.subscribe` (method) — Registers a sink to receive future events, ignoring duplicate subscriptions of the same instance. <!--#91dda552eaf06e71-->
  - `EventEmitter.unsubscribe` (method) — Removes a sink from the subscriber list, silently ignoring sinks that aren't subscribed. <!--#7e72619f09833308-->
  - `EventEmitter.emit` (method) — Delivers an event to every subscribed sink in order, swallowing any sink exception so one rendering fault can't break delivery or the flow. <!--#8494582ed4c615e6-->
  - `EventEmitter.scope` (method) — Context manager that snapshots the subscriber list on entry and restores it on exit, so subscriptions made inside the block are automatically undone. <!--#c65503c1b0064a8d-->

### `src/se3/engine/file_enum.py` (python) — Gitignore-respecting file enumeration for the code-index: wraps `git ls-files` (tracked ∪ untracked-non-ignored) as the primary inclusion filter, backstopped by an explicit exclude-pattern guard and per-file binary/size classification, exposing `enumerate_index_files` as the deterministic entry point for the set of files the index should cover. <!--#d6d81694c0b30a0d|7524aebd7fe113ac-->
- `_is_se3_path` (function) — Predicate returning True when a relative path lies inside the always-excluded `se3/` runtime directory. <!--#894fc5809a6f598a-->
- `_git_ls_files_paths` (function) — Runs `git ls-files` to return the index view of every tracked file's relative path, returning empty on git failure. <!--#d5658f06054df9fb-->
- `_git_ls_files_other` (function) — Runs `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` to return untracked-but-not-ignored files so new files are picked up without registration. <!--#056a2ea4677d010d-->
- `matches_exclude` (function) — Secondary glob-based guard testing whether a relative path matches any explicit `code_index.exclude` pattern, with basename and directory-subtree conveniences. <!--#65ebacc0b391b57e-->
- `is_binary` (function) — Sniffs a file's leading bytes to classify it as binary (NUL byte or largely-undecodable UTF-8) so the indexer keeps it at a single file-level line. <!--#25bf9ae9141d17de-->
- `FileSize` (class) — Dataclass holding a text file's cheap size measurement as line count and byte count. <!--#47930e403c8c718f-->
  - `FileSize.from_bytes` (method) — Classmethod constructing a FileSize from already-read content without re-reading the file. <!--#4179f5c88553b475-->
- `measure_file` (function) — Reads a file and returns its FileSize, or None if it cannot be read. <!--#cfe51f3a660821c6-->
- `enumerate_index_files` (function) — Top-level entry point returning the deterministic, sorted set of absolute file paths the code-index should cover (tracked ∪ untracked-non-ignored, minus se3/, excludes, and deleted ghosts). <!--#e76522edfbc770fc-->

### `src/se3/engine/git_tags.py` (python) — Git version-tagging helper module: derives canonical `v`-prefixed tag names, applies the SemVer major/minor policy to decide when a version bump warrants a tag, and creates annotated tags on a commit (using its subject as the message) via git subprocesses that surface failures as `VersionTagError`. <!--#0b7b9e8407c2045e|b81d26127b16a400-->
- `VersionTagError` (class) — A RuntimeError subclass raised when a version tag cannot be created, carrying the tag name, target commit, git stderr, and exit code. <!--#6d7e7d08e14c4ae5-->
  - `VersionTagError.__init__` (method) — Stores the tag/commit/stderr/returncode context and builds a message naming both the tag and its commit so the failure can be recovered manually. <!--#bb1bb3fd1fecbabe-->
- `tag_name_for_version` (function) — Normalizes a version string into the canonical `v`-prefixed git tag name. <!--#33784bcdc0144716-->
- `should_tag_semver_bump` (function) — Returns whether a textual bump type (`major`/`minor`) warrants a tag under the default SemVer policy. <!--#35d0d2832a1ae3e2-->
