- `semver_tag_decision` (function) — Decides tag/no-tag by comparing the major.minor components of the current and new versions, returning None when either version is not SemVer-comparable. <!--#2c580f3b4adb98dd-->
- `semver_advance_requires_tag` (function) — Boolean convenience wrapper over `semver_tag_decision` that treats an undecidable comparison as no tag. <!--#93fd3781902bed28-->
- `_semver_major_minor` (function) — Parses a version string into an integer `(major, minor)` tuple, stripping `v`, build, and pre-release parts, or None if unparseable. <!--#bb5b85c2f4596587-->
- `commit_subject` (function) — Reads a commit's raw message body via git and returns only its first physical line, for use as the tag message. <!--#6bea55ccd663659f-->
- `create_annotated_version_tag` (function) — Creates an annotated version tag on the given commit, using that commit's subject as the tag message, and returns the tag name. <!--#3b89535357ca8b9e-->
- `_run_git` (function) — Runs a git subprocess in the project root, converting timeouts, OS errors, and non-zero exits into `VersionTagError`. <!--#1bcd63c9e89f6246-->
- `_tag_name_from_args` (function) — Recovers the tag name from a `git tag -a <name> …` argument tuple for error reporting, falling back to `<unknown>`. <!--#5435883bc6dfd449-->
- `_decode_output` (function) — Coerces possibly-bytes or None subprocess output into a string, replacing undecodable characters. <!--#c3e2b02481034ff7-->

### `src/se3/engine/interaction_calls.py` (python) — The single producer/consumer helper for SE3's unified `se3/calls/` file channel, reading and writing kind-tagged JSON call files (MCP calls, mid-flow interjections, retry/failure decisions, and CLI confirmations) plus their sibling `.response` answer files, with backward-compatible defaulting of legacy untagged artifacts to a plain `call` kind. <!--#a5f083bbedb83b4b|0634ff752c4ef491-->
- `calls_dir_for` (function) — Returns the `se3/calls/` directory path for a given project root. <!--#652a81f197a424a6-->
- `classify_kind` (function) — Resolves a parsed call dict's interaction kind, defaulting legacy or unrecognized files to `CALL_KIND_CALL` so old artifacts work without migration. <!--#880f7c9758d2615c-->
- `write_call` (function) — Atomically writes a call file of a given kind with prompt/context/options payload, returning its path. <!--#5eb93b7be0ca617f-->
- `read_call` (function) — Parses a call file into a dict (always carrying a `kind` key), returning `None` on any read/parse error. <!--#a51ef169b9c2eacf-->
- `response_path` (function) — Returns the canonical sibling `.response` path for a given call file. <!--#6943622212596f29-->
- `read_response` (function) — Returns the parsed sibling answer file, recognizing both `.response` and `.response.json` variants, or `None` if none exists. <!--#f16ade7359cac25c-->
- `write_response` (function) — Atomically writes a sibling `.response` answer file (wrapping non-dict values) and returns its path. <!--#8d02ff1e8ce9e6d0-->
- `write_interjection_request` (function) — Daemon-side producer that queues a mid-flow interjection as a `CALL_KIND_INTERJECTION` call file for the running `se3 run` to consume. <!--#965c0f08272a7e6a-->
- `drain_interjection_requests` (function) — The `se3 run` consumer that scans for unanswered interjection call files and returns them oldest-first, sealing each via an idempotent write-response-then-delete protocol. <!--#3dedded011a0e8c7-->
- `write_retry_decision_call` (function) — Writes a `CALL_KIND_RETRY_DECISION` call file for a failed step on the no-TTY path, externalizing the Retry/Skip/Abort prompt for a web console to answer. <!--#92af625ef122d099-->
- `write_interaction_call` (function) — A project-root-addressed convenience wrapper around `write_call` that folds extra keywords into the call payload. <!--#c59f01ec4147bea5-->
- `read_interaction_response` (function) — Returns the bare answer value for a call (unwrapping `{response: ...}` envelopes from either `.response.json` or plain `.response`), or `None` when no answer exists yet. <!--#318712f1706b9339-->
- `make_cli_confirm_handler` (function) — Builds an `on_confirm` callback for the agent runner that writes a `cli_confirm` call file, polls for the sibling response while the subprocess lives, and marks orphaned calls consumed if the child exits unanswered. <!--#1f5d19c172a19a06-->

### `src/se3/engine/issue_discovery.py` (python) — Flow-engine module for automatic issue discovery, providing A-class system triggers (fix-loop exhaustion, pre-existing failures), B-class whitelist-based prompt injection and output collection with title-based deduplication via the IssueDiscovery class, plus a scoped executor that applies LLM-emitted create/update/delete issue operations under tracking-set constraints. <!--#370d7905d149a5d6|fbd916824bfc4e68-->
- `_normalize_issue_id` (function) — Helper that strips leading zeros from an issue ID so zero-padded variants like '5' and '005' compare equal in membership checks. <!--#3d9056ee5983eaff-->
- `apply_discovery_issue_operations` (function) — Engine-side executor that runs LLM-emitted create/update/delete issue intents for a discovery step, enforcing the tracking-set scope guarantee and isolating each operation so one failure doesn't abort the batch. <!--#ffeb9af8ec081bdb-->
- `_apply_create` (function) — Creates a new issue with source='human' and adds its ID to the discovery step's tracking set. <!--#3c972612bf74020d-->
- `_apply_update` (function) — Updates a tracked issue's editable fields (title/description/priority/type/tags only), rejecting out-of-scope IDs and dropping malformed non-list tags. <!--#8108bd67f54f0192-->
- `_apply_delete` (function) — Deletes a tracked issue and removes its ID from the tracking set, rejecting out-of-scope IDs. <!--#cebe0d8a0b5000ed-->
- `IssueDiscovery` (class) — Class managing per-flow automatic issue discovery (A-class system triggers and B-class prompt-injection collection) with title-based deduplication. <!--#eef0d8fdc803f19f-->
  - `IssueDiscovery.__init__` (method) — Initializes the discovery instance with an IssueManager, flow ID, and an empty list of created titles for deduplication. <!--#1292078f24c6befe-->
  - `IssueDiscovery.create_from_fix_loop_exhaustion` (method) — A-class trigger that builds and creates a high-priority bug issue (source=system) when the fix loop hits max iterations, embedding flow context, test output, and fix history. <!--#0857f45fd5b99585-->
  - `IssueDiscovery.create_from_pre_existing_failures` (method) — A-class trigger that creates a medium-priority issue documenting inherited baseline test failures not introduced by the current change. <!--#bf9800b8f2e5bb00-->
  - `IssueDiscovery.get_injection_prompt` (method) — Returns the issue-discovery prompt fragment for whitelisted step types (B-class injection), or None otherwise. <!--#2979579ce1738652-->
  - `IssueDiscovery.collect_issues_from_output` (method) — B-class collector that parses a whitelisted step's discovered_issues output and creates deduplicated source=system issues from each valid entry. <!--#2b8bce29a5aede95-->
  - `IssueDiscovery._is_duplicate` (method) — Checks whether a title matches any already-created title in this flow using normalized similarity comparison. <!--#1a096e2f501e6ea8-->
  - `IssueDiscovery._normalize_title` (method) — Normalizes a title for comparison by lowercasing, stripping punctuation, and collapsing whitespace. <!--#28516bc357948272-->
  - `IssueDiscovery._titles_similar` (method) — Determines if two normalized titles are near-duplicates via exact match or >70% token-overlap ratio. <!--#16f9009715e698f8-->

### `src/se3/engine/issue_manager.py` (python) — Module implementing SE3's YAML-based issue tracker — the Issue dataclass/IssueStatus enum plus the IssueManager class that creates, adopts, loads, lists, updates, moves, and deletes issue files across se3/issues/open and closed/, with collision-free ID allocation serialized through a shared fcntl-locked .next_id counter and #NNN reference rewriting on renumber. <!--#24b52b1e78bc2fb1|41f028bbfbcc2c98-->
- `IssueStatus` (class) — Enum of the five issue lifecycle states (open, in-progress, resolved, won't-fix, closed). <!--#decbedd5a7c9f2d6-->
- `Issue` (class) — Dataclass representing a single issue record with serialization helpers and a derived display title. <!--#ff53e1ff54ead2d9-->
  - `Issue.display_title` (method) — Property that returns a human-readable title, falling back from explicit title to the first non-empty description line to "untitled". <!--#1a19b1f1da95d214-->
  - `Issue.to_dict` (method) — Serializes the issue to a YAML-ready dict, including optional fields only when set. <!--#5baf46152d4ccfe9-->
  - `Issue.from_dict` (method) — Classmethod that deserializes an issue from a dict, tolerating missing/legacy fields and parsing timestamps defensively. <!--#1fb4f2a14503faab-->
- `_numeric_id_or_none` (function) — Helper that parses an issue ID into an int (or None if non-numeric), used to decide whether an adopt actually renumbered the issue before invoking the #NNN reference-rewrite/trace primitives. <!--#9b63cfc2f30db776-->
- `_make_slug` (function) — Helper that converts a title into a lowercase, hyphenated URL/filesystem-friendly slug. <!--#0de7a9734d3c82a6-->
- `_derive_slug_for_issue` (function) — Helper that derives a filename slug for an issue using the same title-priority logic as display_title. <!--#f32424f3c00139e5-->
- `IssueManager` (class) — The core class managing the full issue lifecycle — creating, adopting, loading, listing, updating status, and moving YAML issue files between se3/issues/open and closed directories, with all ID allocation serialized through the shared .next_id fcntl lock. <!--#94fbfaeae5078a5f-->
  - `IssueManager.__init__` (method) — Initializes the manager with the project root and resolves the issues, open, and closed directory paths. <!--#072700a6b770b364-->
  - `IssueManager._ensure_dirs` (method) — Creates the open/ and closed/ issue directories if they don't already exist. <!--#8e38a3b44bcd372f-->
  - `IssueManager._next_id` (method) — Allocates the next zero-padded issue ID by delegating to the shared fcntl-locked reserve_next_id primitive, which reconciles the .next_id counter against the on-disk store so a stale counter can never re-mint a number a live issue already owns. <!--#da2971856971a648-->
  - `IssueManager._find_issue_file` (method) — Locates an issue's YAML file by ID across open/ and closed/, tolerating zero-padding differences. <!--#395484abb8bf782f-->
  - `IssueManager.create` (method) — Creates a new open issue from a required description (plus optional metadata), writing its YAML to open/. <!--#fe8f1910d7c1a7a6-->
  - `IssueManager.adopt_issue` (method) — Re-homes an externally-originated issue (e.g. from a merge worktree) under a freshly-allocated collision-free ID, preserving all other fields, writing it to open/ or closed/ by status, and rewriting #<old> references plus appending a renumber trace unless deferred for batch finalization. <!--#ceb588194974ea61-->
  - `IssueManager.append_renumber_trace` (method) — Appends the 'old → new' audit line to an already-written issue file, completing a deferred adopt after the batch bulk reference rewrite so the trace's embedded #<old> is not repointed, returning None if the issue has no file. <!--#fefa502e3904bbaf-->
  - `IssueManager.load` (method) — Loads and returns an issue by ID from open/ or closed/, or None if not found. <!--#020eb18913a1d3ab-->
  - `IssueManager.list_issues` (method) — Lists issues (open by default, optionally closed) with optional type and source filters, sorted by ID. <!--#83ee845dc598e516-->
  - `IssueManager.update_status` (method) — Validates and applies a status transition, updating the YAML and moving the file between open/ and closed/ as needed. <!--#d96cdeb912e9e247-->
  - `IssueManager.reset_to_open` (method) — Resets an in-progress issue back to open, erroring if it is in any other state. <!--#a22f7bfa163b4e22-->
  - `IssueManager.find_open_by_title` (method) — Finds an open issue whose display title case-insensitively matches the given title. <!--#83a2c1627c6282c0-->
  - `IssueManager.close_issue` (method) — Closes an open issue (falling back to resolved when needed) and moves its file to closed/. <!--#77684cefd8dabbd4-->
  - `IssueManager.delete_issue` (method) — Permanently deletes an issue's YAML file by ID with no status transition or file move. <!--#25390c6a0d56a160-->
  - `IssueManager.list_by_tags` (method) — Lists issues that contain all of the specified tags, optionally including closed ones. <!--#a4ef3ff5e8af3ded-->
  - `IssueManager.update_fields` (method) — Updates editable issue fields and renames the YAML file when the derived slug changes. <!--#712c1fc23aaca8f1-->
  - `IssueManager.reopen_issue` (method) — Reopens a closed/resolved/won't-fix issue back to open, moving its file to open/. <!--#53e5b2dd713901f3-->
  - `IssueManager._read_issue` (method) — Reads and parses an issue YAML file into an Issue, returning None on parse failure. <!--#33a506ffef4077af-->
  - `IssueManager._write_issue` (method) — Serializes an issue and writes it as YAML to the given filepath. <!--#26627c78c08ec256-->

### `src/se3/engine/json_extractor.py` (python) — Two-phase JSON extractor that reliably recovers a schema-complete JSON dict from raw LLM output, using a direct-parse fast path first and, on failure, stripping stream-json to assistant text and invoking a lightweight second LLM pass to restructure it. <!--#aaed016a6e055540|1d927ac6d6a985f9-->
- `JSONExtractor` (class) — Class that extracts a JSON dict from raw LLM output, trying a direct parse first and a lightweight second LLM pass as fallback. <!--#16dfa7c498bda86b-->
  - `JSONExtractor.__init__` (method) — Constructor storing the project root (for the LLM caller) and the extraction call timeout. <!--#5c1837782c47b8c5-->
  - `JSONExtractor.extract` (method) — Public entry point that returns parsed JSON via the direct-parse fast path, or delegates to LLM extraction when that fails. <!--#08106d958854572b-->
  - `JSONExtractor._try_direct_parse` (method) — Helper that attempts to parse the raw output directly using the shared json_parser utility without invoking an LLM. <!--#c74809bed98aaa51-->
  - `JSONExtractor._extract_text_from_stream_json` (method) — Helper that parses stream-json (NDJSON) output and concatenates the text content of assistant messages, dropping tool calls and results. <!--#1c3d95c718342e3c-->
  - `JSONExtractor._extract_with_llm` (method) — Fallback that strips stream-json to assistant text, prompts a non-JSON LLMCaller to restructure it into schema-complete JSON, and parses the result. <!--#903e5a4227f7fd73-->
- `extract_json_two_phase` (function) — Module-level convenience function that constructs a JSONExtractor and runs two-phase extraction in one call. <!--#f6b6bb2c3227af8b-->

### `src/se3/engine/json_modes.py` (python) — Defines the JsonMode enum (STRICT, EXTRACT, TWO_PHASE, OFF) of strategies for obtaining structured JSON from LLM calls, plus a get_json_mode helper that resolves the active mode from explicit and legacy parameters via a fixed backward-compatible priority order. <!--#cb3ab8a5a880eec8|92767f0284f446eb-->
- `JsonMode` (class) — Enum enumerating the available JSON extraction strategies (STRICT, EXTRACT, TWO_PHASE, OFF) used to control how an LLM call produces structured output. <!--#3c44b448f5440910-->
- `get_json_mode` (function) — Resolves a JsonMode from a mix of explicit and legacy parameters (json_mode, two_phase_json, require_json), applying a fixed priority order for backward compatibility. <!--#45eacf3bde2932c4-->

### `src/se3/engine/llm_caller.py` (python) — The engine's LLM invocation layer: an `LLMCaller` that builds prompts (with extra-prompt injection, retry-history context, dedup and a post-dedup size cap), runs Claude/agent CLI subprocesses in strict, extract, or two-phase JSON modes, retries with agent rotation on infrastructure errors, and a `StreamJSONTracker` that parses the stream-json NDJSON output to emit progress, capture token usage, and record touched files. <!--#70c601a124ebba0a|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/se3/engine/logging_config.py` (python) — Defines the flow engine's structured logging subsystem — log-level and event-type enums, a serializable StructuredLogEntry value object, and a singleton StructuredLogger that writes JSON-lines daily log files with an in-memory buffer, console output, per-flow/step/LLM timing helpers, and log retrieval/export. <!--#2fb132f11a8b0f4c|7c79a7fcdeb5af16-->
- `LogLevel` (class) — String enum defining the five severity levels (debug through critical) used for log entries and filtering. <!--#0afc90c8e31e38f7-->
- `LogEventType` (class) — String enum enumerating the categories of flow-engine log events across flow, step, LLM, persistence, and tool operations. <!--#e6e9c091fe6eacd7-->
- `StructuredLogEntry` (class) — Value object representing a single structured log event with metadata and serialization to dict/JSON. <!--#b3501160ecd27907-->
  - `StructuredLogEntry.__init__` (method) — Constructs a log entry, stamping the current UTC timestamp and storing event type, level, and optional flow/step/LLM context. <!--#059a51e6b392ac75-->
  - `StructuredLogEntry.to_dict` (method) — Serializes the entry to a dictionary, omitting unset optional fields and rounding the duration. <!--#234f02f7ff69c0bf-->
  - `StructuredLogEntry.to_json` (method) — Serializes the entry to a JSON string via its dict representation. <!--#6f39524c89de5837-->
- `StructuredLogger` (class) — Logger that writes structured entries to a daily JSON-lines file, keeps an in-memory buffer, and optionally prints to the console. <!--#a23456e4a4234c8a-->
  - `StructuredLogger.__init__` (method) — Initializes the logger, setting up the log directory, daily log file, recent-log buffer, and timing trackers. <!--#64bdeda4cd028cef-->
  - `StructuredLogger._get_log_file` (method) — Returns the date-stamped JSON-lines log file path for the current day. <!--#4f29bb52bebeaebd-->
  - `StructuredLogger._should_log` (method) — Determines whether a given level meets the configured minimum threshold. <!--#60722b42c6fbf2cb-->
  - `StructuredLogger._write_log` (method) — Appends an entry to the current log file, updates the bounded in-memory buffer, and emits console output if enabled. <!--#845a6fa3db9a39bb-->
  - `StructuredLogger._console_output` (method) — Prints a human-readable, color-coded one-line summary of an entry to stderr. <!--#3428059cb34f263a-->
  - `StructuredLogger.log` (method) — Core logging method that builds a StructuredLogEntry and writes it if the level passes the threshold. <!--#b5c689d8f1d507d8-->
  - `StructuredLogger.flow_started` (method) — Convenience method logging a flow-started event with the task and task type. <!--#010d617a47430eb6-->
  - `StructuredLogger.flow_completed` (method) — Convenience method logging a successful flow-completion event with its duration. <!--#6334121e6557f6d8-->
  - `StructuredLogger.flow_failed` (method) — Convenience method logging a flow-failure event with the error and optional duration. <!--#19591ad845bb411a-->
  - `StructuredLogger.step_started` (method) — Starts a per-step timer and logs a step-started event. <!--#c898e0b04a6e3713-->
  - `StructuredLogger.step_completed` (method) — Logs a step-completion event with computed duration and optional outputs. <!--#16ba47376084468d-->
  - `StructuredLogger.step_failed` (method) — Logs a step-failure event with duration, error, and retry indication, downgrading severity when a retry will follow. <!--#b8368ebbb9097a76-->
  - `StructuredLogger.llm_call_started` (method) — Starts an LLM-call timer and logs the call-started event with model and prompt size. <!--#0b2900cc5c77e4b3-->
  - `StructuredLogger.llm_call_completed` (method) — Logs an LLM-call-completed event with duration and input/output token counts. <!--#634b0aa95a7ac233-->
  - `StructuredLogger.llm_call_failed` (method) — Logs an LLM-call-failure event with duration, model, and error. <!--#1a7b3576bbc26ef7-->
  - `StructuredLogger.state_saved` (method) — Convenience method logging a state-saved event referencing the persisted state file. <!--#593c9924dc51089d-->
  - `StructuredLogger.get_recent_logs` (method) — Returns recent buffered log entries, optionally filtered by event type and flow ID and capped by a limit. <!--#8c123a66b7b211f9-->
  - `StructuredLogger.export_logs` (method) — Reads all daily log files and exports matching entries (filtered by time and event type) to a JSON file, returning the count. <!--#cbed0084601dd847-->
- `get_logger` (function) — Module-level accessor that lazily creates and returns the singleton StructuredLogger instance. <!--#45e4799fe4cca297-->
- `reset_logger` (function) — Resets the global logger singleton, primarily for testing. <!--#1cb3faeb6146c533-->

### `src/se3/engine/models.py` (python) — Defines the flow engine's core state-machine data models — Step, Transition, State, and FlowInstance dataclasses plus their StepType/StepStatus/FlowStatus enums and STEP_POOL/default-sequence helpers — each supporting both legacy fully-inline and hot/cold-split (header + externalized body) serialization with lazy hydration and data-loss guards. <!--#d9362e7569295383|5372351495de183c-->
- `StepType` (class) — An Enum enumerating every workflow step kind in the engine's step pool (discovery, analyze, plan, implement, test, self-check, commit, etc.), including deprecated planning/spec steps and the merge-side MERGE_INTEGRATE / VERSION_RECONCILE steps appended only to worktree flows. <!--#948d46f7bc525353-->
- `StepStatus` (class) — Enum of a step's execution lifecycle states (pending, running, completed, partial, failed, retrying, paused, revision_needed). <!--#38d6ab911468a93f-->
- `Step` (class) — A dataclass modeling one workflow step — its type, status, timing/retry and LLM-model config, optional cwd override, inputs/outputs/artifacts, error fields, and hot/cold lazy-load bookkeeping — with methods to serialize (full, header-only, cold payload) and materialize its externalized body. <!--#e2d7e5aa1edcf793-->
  - `Step.to_dict` (method) — Serializes a step to a full inline dictionary including all metadata plus the heavy inputs/outputs/artifacts bodies. <!--#257609c083c1358d-->
  - `Step.to_header_dict` (method) — Serializes only the KB-scale status-table fields, omitting the heavy inputs/outputs/artifacts body for the hot/cold-split header. <!--#a632cd902601e663-->
  - `Step.cold_payload` (method) — Returns just the heavy per-step body (inputs/outputs/artifacts) that gets externalized to a cold file. <!--#067d19099d525307-->
  - `Step.apply_cold` (method) — Lazily materializes a header-only step's externalized body, with a data-loss guard that leaves the step unloaded on a failed cold read so an intact file is never overwritten with empty data. <!--#cb38dad39673e591-->
  - `Step.from_dict` (method) — Reconstructs a Step from its dictionary (full inline form), restoring hot/cold provenance markers so a transiently-unreadable cold file is re-emitted rather than overwritten with empty data. <!--#937a996c0e28916b-->
  - `Step.from_header_dict` (method) — Deserializes a header-only step, leaving its body empty and cold_loaded False while retaining the cold_ref for on-demand hydration or unchanged re-emit. <!--#4070520bb875d5c6-->
- `Transition` (class) — Dataclass describing a state-machine transition rule from one step type to another with an optional condition. <!--#7a2689d2166206ee-->
  - `Transition.to_dict` (method) — Serializes a Transition to a dictionary. <!--#4540da1b0410523c-->
  - `Transition.from_dict` (method) — Reconstructs a Transition from its serialized dictionary form. <!--#cdfa73691c44022b-->
- `State` (class) — Dataclass holding the flow engine's execution state (current/history steps, shared context, selected steps, review/fix loops, baseline failures, cumulative token usage) with full and hot/cold-split serialization and helper methods for step lookup and iteration tracking. <!--#f67b40cea4bfa18a-->
  - `State.get_current_step` (method) — Returns the currently active Step, or None if none is set. <!--#918e318297b74364-->
  - `State.add_step` (method) — Registers a Step in the state, auto-generating a sortable human-readable step_id and appending it to history. <!--#8764118b5d041b38-->
  - `State.get_step_to_review` (method) — Finds the step preceding a given confirm step (the one being reviewed) from history. <!--#7a52d05a0edb06c5-->
  - `State.increment_review_iteration` (method) — Increments and returns the review-cycle iteration count for a given step. <!--#7dcf9130950ebe0b-->
  - `State.get_review_iteration` (method) — Returns the current review iteration count for a step (0 if never reviewed). <!--#19414144af977a06-->
  - `State.increment_fix_iteration` (method) — Increments the test-verify-fix loop counter, appends a capped history entry, and mirrors the count into context. <!--#3550ebf4a7e40719-->
  - `State.get_fix_iteration` (method) — Returns the current fix-loop iteration count. <!--#6b71e3bdd412a0bc-->
  - `State.update_task_type` (method) — Stores the analyze-step-resolved task type in the shared context. <!--#a1d6daf59f1e228d-->
  - `State.is_type_pending` (method) — Reports whether the task type has not yet been resolved. <!--#4e7aadf82393a590-->
  - `State.to_dict` (method) — Serializes state to a full dictionary with inline steps and context/fix_history. <!--#a441e44228a5b2ae-->
  - `State.to_header_dict` (method) — Serializes the KB-scale state header — per-step status table with bodies replaced and the unbounded context/fix_history dropped for external cold storage. <!--#243b70e8f3069785-->
  - `State.cold_context` (method) — Returns the shared cold payload (context and fix_history) externalized out of the state header. <!--#613d3836030a3441-->
  - `State.from_header_dict` (method) — Deserializes a header-only state with empty context/fix_history and header-only steps, marking context not-loaded so a failed cold read never masquerades as a genuine empty context. <!--#960710dfd7ff0989-->
  - `State.from_dict` (method) — Deserializes state from a full dict, re-clamping fix_history to the sliding-window cap, keeping context's mirrored copy consistent, and restoring cold-context provenance markers. <!--#b51dde214d9f6b8e-->
- `FlowStatus` (class) — Enum of a flow instance's overall lifecycle status (init, running, paused, completed, failed, recovering). <!--#2e96c050c86ed8d4-->
- `FlowInstance` (class) — The top-level dataclass for a single engine run — holding flow id, status, task/issue metadata, the State machine, timestamps, change tracking, worktree-isolation fields, and lock-wait state — with full/header serialization and deserialization helpers. <!--#ce7aaaada87ca23f-->
  - `FlowInstance.to_dict` (method) — Serializes a flow instance to a full dictionary, emitting the waiting_for_lock key only when actually waiting to stay backward-compatible with old engine.json readers. <!--#39bfc2e2a3eb1289-->
  - `FlowInstance.to_header_dict` (method) — Serializes the KB-scale flow header, identical to to_dict except the heavy state block is replaced by State.to_header_dict. <!--#aa1b15eb1063dcd8-->
  - `FlowInstance.from_header_dict` (method) — Deserializes a header-only flow, reusing from_dict for identity/metadata with an empty state then installing the header-only State via State.from_header_dict. <!--#350e037e5afda9f8-->
  - `FlowInstance.from_dict` (method) — Reconstructs a FlowInstance from its dictionary, reading each metadata/worktree field and defaulting missing legacy keys (like waiting_for_lock) to safe values. <!--#78e16df247ad23b5-->
  - `FlowInstance.get_progress` (method) — Returns flow completion as a (completed_count, total_count) tuple. <!--#382fd14e9da0d282-->
- `get_step_info` (function) — Looks up a step type's metadata entry from the STEP_POOL. <!--#9d66a58a6cd35598-->
- `get_default_step_sequence` (function) — Returns the default ordered list of step types for a given task type (feature, bugfix, review, small, directive, discovery). <!--#79a8090f0e6cd94a-->

### `src/se3/engine/output.py` (python) — A utility module providing helpers to format arbitrary data into strings, log messages at named levels, and format and render errors and success messages (with optional context/details) through the display module. <!--#b44eff3ec94fee91|c0b1b9557353d0db-->
- `format_output` (function) — Converts any data type (string, dict/list as pretty JSON, else str) to a string representation without truncation, ignoring the deprecated truncate flag. <!--#1fb8dc97c460cf5b-->
- `log_output` (function) — Logs a message at a named level via the module logger, used for internal logging output that bypasses the display module. <!--#bcd99a66853b242d-->
- `format_error` (function) — Builds a Rich-markup error string from an exception or message, with an optional context key/value block, using i18n-translated labels. <!--#0eb718e4817745ef-->
- `display_error` (function) — Renders a formatted error message into a full-width error panel via `render_full`. <!--#0a0dbeaf6ce8adfd-->
- `display_success` (function) — Renders a green success message plus optional key/value details into a full-width success panel. <!--#2d9bad1ac7706454-->

### `src/se3/engine/output_formatter.py` (python) — Module providing a name-keyed registry and factory for SE3 output formatters, exposing a lazily-created global FormatterRegistry singleton (seeded with the default 'tasks' TaskFormatter) plus module-level convenience functions to register, retrieve, and list formatters. <!--#4dcdfd93fddf90e8|eca8291d052da2a1-->
- `FormatterRegistry` (class) — Class that maintains a name-to-formatter-class mapping and acts as a factory for instantiating formatters, seeded with default formatters on construction. <!--#059002186071d632-->
  - `FormatterRegistry.__init__` (method) — Initializes the empty formatter mapping and registers the default formatters. <!--#d42322823229516e-->
  - `FormatterRegistry._register_default_formatters` (method) — Registers the built-in default formatters (currently the 'tasks' TaskFormatter). <!--#e0ff2860430fe51d-->
  - `FormatterRegistry.register_formatter` (method) — Stores a formatter class under a given name, warning if it overwrites an existing registration. <!--#8566348c910c841e-->
  - `FormatterRegistry.get_formatter` (method) — Looks up and instantiates a formatter by name with optional constructor kwargs, returning None (and logging) on missing name or instantiation failure. <!--#56a1016d3a6b9cd2-->
  - `FormatterRegistry.list_formatters` (method) — Returns a dict mapping each registered formatter name to its class name. <!--#ad7a2621dacf661f-->
  - `FormatterRegistry.unregister_formatter` (method) — Removes a formatter by name, returning whether it was present. <!--#ec59bc018e1528a2-->
- `get_registry` (function) — Lazily creates and returns the module-level singleton FormatterRegistry. <!--#0450178df4985dc7-->
- `register_formatter` (function) — Module-level convenience that registers a formatter class on the global registry. <!--#defcad979b65f3de-->
- `get_formatter` (function) — Module-level convenience that retrieves a formatter instance from the global registry by name. <!--#f3cc7acf1ada4e92-->
- `list_formatters` (function) — Module-level convenience that lists all formatters registered in the global registry. <!--#cb28e95009c9c96e-->

### `src/se3/engine/persistence.py` (python) — Implements the flow engine's state persistence layer, providing atomic hot/cold-split JSON writes — a KB-scale engine.json header plus per-step/context cold-file partitions — with content-hash-based incremental saves, lazy on-demand step hydration, resumable snapshots, archives, and backward-compatible tolerant load paths. <!--#30bb170dc3adbca4|0d7d364b73373377-->
- `_stringify_keys` (function) — Recursively coerces all dict keys to strings so a mixed-key payload becomes sortable/hashable, used only as the slow-path fallback in canonical JSON encoding. <!--#3513c1be3e3a60f5-->
- `_canonical_json` (function) — Produces a stable, order-independent JSON encoding of a cold payload for content-hashing, falling back to string-coerced keys when mixed key types defeat sort_keys. <!--#385cc592b6ed181a-->
- `_content_hash` (function) — Returns the SHA-256 hex digest of a cold payload's canonical JSON, used to detect whether a cold file's content changed since the last save. <!--#470c812027aa7bb8-->
- `_is_hotcold` (function) — Predicate that returns True when a loaded payload is a new-format hot/cold engine header (identified by an 'hotcold/' engine_format marker). <!--#ebc6f054d1359dc3-->
- `_LazyStepDict` (class) — A step-id→Step dict subclass that hydrates a step's heavy cold body only on keyed access (not on iteration), so header-only resumes don't re-materialize every step. <!--#5d0e314e994c1538-->
  - `_LazyStepDict.__init__` (method) — Constructs the lazy step dict, storing the per-step hydrator callable used to fault in cold bodies. <!--#47266bb613804247-->
  - `_LazyStepDict.__getitem__` (method) — Fetches a step by key and invokes the hydrator to load its cold body before returning it. <!--#70c77a4d5c526ead-->
  - `_LazyStepDict.get` (method) — Dict-style get that hydrates the fetched step (via __getitem__) or returns the default when the key is absent. <!--#e9227ea77353e267-->
  - `_LazyStepDict._hydrate_all` (method) — Forces hydration of every stored step's cold body without triggering the lazy __getitem__ override. <!--#d91d30867698c00f-->
  - `_LazyStepDict.__eq__` (method) — Equality that first hydrates all steps so a header-loaded flow compares equal to the same flow built in memory. <!--#fc47cfe42e28616b-->
- `_split_flow` (function) — Splits a FlowInstance into a KB-scale header (with per-step and context cold_refs), the changed steps' cold payloads, and the shared context payload, skipping unhydrated bodies to avoid re-reading them. <!--#be4821feebe902bf-->
- `PersistenceManager` (class) — Manages atomic, hot/cold-split persistence of flow engine state — engine.json header plus per-flow cold-file partitions, resumable snapshots, archives, and incremental/tolerant load-save paths. <!--#d80394df43affed4-->
  - `PersistenceManager.__init__` (method) — Initializes the manager with the project root and derives all state paths (engine.json, context, resumable snapshots, and the cold-file partition root). <!--#ace690493189830f-->
  - `PersistenceManager.ensure_directories` (method) — Creates the se3/state directory tree if it does not yet exist. <!--#b8a17d8d37aa3ed9-->
  - `PersistenceManager._cold_dir` (method) — Returns the default cold-file partition directory for a flow (steps/<flow_id>/). <!--#776745a3cf542161-->
  - `PersistenceManager._resolve_cold_dir` (method) — Resolves the cold partition directory for a header, honoring a recorded cold_partition override and an alternate steps_root (e.g. archive/steps). <!--#52f97639bbde67ed-->
  - `PersistenceManager._atomic_write_json` (method) — The single write seam that atomically writes data as pretty JSON via a distinct temp-file-plus-rename, cleaning up the temp file on failure. <!--#e044c062ff21a2cd-->
  - `PersistenceManager._prior_cold_hashes` (method) — Reads the per-step and context content hashes recorded by the same flow's previously written header, enabling incremental cold-file writes and safely degrading to 'rewrite everything' on any mismatch or corruption. <!--#fa7ed1e9b8c8083a-->
  - `PersistenceManager._dirty_step_ids` (method) — Computes which step ids need their cold file rewritten — those whose hash changed, plus hash-matching steps whose on-disk cold file went missing. <!--#703eff81ec7cd47f-->
  - `PersistenceManager._write_cold` (method) — Writes only the cold files whose content changed (or whose file vanished) this save, skipping unhydrated header-only steps and never clobbering an intact context file with empty data. <!--#3039890fa634829f-->
  - `PersistenceManager.save_flow` (method) — Atomically persists a flow as a hot/cold split (cold files then header), updates or clears the resumable snapshot by status, and prunes an orphaned prior partition when a new run overwrites engine.json. <!--#a42efa09382d59fd-->
  - `PersistenceManager._read_cold_json` (method) — Reads and parses a cold file, returning None and appending a warning when it is missing or corrupt rather than crashing the flow load. <!--#0e6d61aedfa19466-->
  - `PersistenceManager._reconstruct_full_dict` (method) — Inlines a new-format header's per-step and context cold files back into a full flow dict for FlowInstance.from_dict, tolerating missing/corrupt cold files and preserving load/save provenance markers. <!--#432b6c0d6e272e45-->
  - `PersistenceManager.hydrate_step` (method) — Public on-demand loader that faults in a single header-only step's cold payload in place, no-op on already-loaded steps and tolerant of missing files. <!--#87290adb58e85005-->
  - `PersistenceManager._make_step_hydrator` (method) — Returns a hydrator closure (bound into a _LazyStepDict) that loads a single header-only step's cold body from a resolved partition on first access. <!--#8c09d7c79fe665c3-->
  - `PersistenceManager._build_lazy_flow` (method) — Builds a header-only FlowInstance with lazily-hydrating step bodies while eagerly loading the shared context, returning a legacy inline payload complete and None on undeserializable headers. <!--#0c1b3f376894e953-->
  - `PersistenceManager._peek_active_flow_id` (method) — Cheaply reads (size-guarded) the flow_id currently held by engine.json so the resume path can tell whether a flow came from the live file or a snapshot. <!--#ecc1ca6324ab9450-->
  - `PersistenceManager.save_resumable_snapshot` (method) — Writes a per-flow resumable snapshot sharing the same cold partition as engine.json, reusing save_flow's prebuilt header when given or recomputing the split otherwise. <!--#5790a257d57c8e35-->
  - `PersistenceManager.load_resumable_snapshot` (method) — Loads a flow's resumable snapshot header-only with lazy hydration, rejecting (as not found) a snapshot whose embedded flow_id doesn't match the request. <!--#1cf4cccae1d02172-->
  - `PersistenceManager.clear_resumable_snapshot` (method) — Best-effort removes a flow's resumable snapshot file and then prunes its cold partition if nothing references it any more. <!--#87bc54fe81463e54-->
  - `PersistenceManager._prune_cold_partition_if_orphan` (method) — Deletes a flow's cold partition once neither the live engine.json nor a resumable snapshot references it, preventing multi-MB leaks (best effort, logs on failure). <!--#06c86195f35f61d8-->
  - `PersistenceManager.list_resumable_snapshots` (method) — Enumerates all resumable snapshots header-only with lazy hydration, skipping unreadable ones and those whose embedded flow_id mismatches the filename. <!--#6f6c9741dc787e1d-->
  - `PersistenceManager.load_flow_by_id` (method) — Locates and loads a flow by id (header-only, lazy) preferring the active engine.json then the resumable snapshot, rejecting a snapshot with a mismatched flow_id. <!--#a65f6251e61fe81d-->
  - `PersistenceManager.load_archived_flow_by_id` (method) — Loads an archived flow by id by scanning archive/engine_*.json newest-first (by mtime), reconstructing split-format headers against archive/steps and skipping degraded oversized-legacy headers. <!--#173b9d507e965658-->
  - `PersistenceManager._read_flow_file` (method) — Parses a header/engine/snapshot JSON file into a dict, returning None on read/parse error or a non-dict payload. <!--#c24496b433023d94-->
  - `PersistenceManager.load_flow` (method) — Loads the active flow from engine.json (reconstructing cold files), falling back to the .bak backup on corruption and returning None when neither is usable. <!--#174187f0022f984b-->
  - `PersistenceManager.load_flow_tolerant` (method) — Never-raising loader that tries main then backup files, repairs truncated JSON, and backfills missing fields, returning the flow (or None) plus a list of recovery warnings. <!--#a23096bcdd699b83-->
  - `PersistenceManager._try_repair_json` (method) — Helper that attempts to fix truncated JSON by trimming partial trailing data and closing unbalanced braces/brackets. <!--#45fdbf54c5b23a71-->
  - `PersistenceManager._tolerant_from_dict` (method) — Builds a FlowInstance from a possibly-incomplete dict by filling required flow and state fields with recovery defaults and recording each substitution as a warning. <!--#34a53770123bc174-->
  - `PersistenceManager.create_backup` (method) — Copies the current engine.json to a .bak backup file, returning its path or None on failure. <!--#b7bea4c92cf007e5-->
  - `PersistenceManager.clear_state` (method) — Archives the current flow whole — header plus its entire cold-data directory — into archive/, fail-closed with collision-suffixed names, copying (not moving) cold files when a resumable snapshot still shares the live partition. <!--#344ebda1f16a941d-->
  - `PersistenceManager.list_active_flows` (method) — Returns metadata for the single currently-active flow held in engine.json, if any. <!--#48ea8fd793831682-->
  - `PersistenceManager.list_all_flows` (method) — Combines active, archived (size-guarded header read), and history-only flows into one de-duplicated list of metadata dicts sorted by updated_at descending. <!--#a90c5cbbcba9d86a-->
  - `PersistenceManager.extract_history_summary` (method) — Derives a short task-description title from a history directory's first JSONL file using a three-tier (user-marker / task-block / raw) priority. <!--#4499ec791bdb034d-->
  - `PersistenceManager.save_context` (method) — Atomically writes an AI-consumable context dictionary to context.json for handoff/resumption. <!--#71b404bb79559768-->
  - `PersistenceManager.export_context_from_flow` (method) — Exports a flow's AI context to context.json, first force-hydrating all lazy step bodies so the serialization doesn't emit hollow steps with empty IO. <!--#fc31838cf5dfafaf-->
  - `PersistenceManager.load_context` (method) — Loads the saved context.json, handling both the new direct and old nested formats. <!--#587d5c82f36df771-->
  - `PersistenceManager.export_progress_markdown` (method) — Renders a flow's steps and context as human-readable progress markdown derived from the JSON state. <!--#2d591e3b31f21aa2-->
- `_read_snapshot_header` (function) — Reads a snapshot's top-level header — fully parsing small files but scanning a bounded head+tail window with regex for identity keys on oversized files — returning None if no flow_id is recoverable. <!--#6b0125ab3e7448ce-->

### `src/se3/engine/project_context.py` (python) — Defines ProjectContextCollector, which gathers project-wide context (git status, flow-engine history, backlog items, and spec names) into a structured dict for the flow engine's PROJECT_SUMMARY step and the `se3 summary` CLI. <!--#e9c1f298e9b07b81|0c4f9aaf972f0d55-->
- `ProjectContextCollector` (class) — Class that gathers project-wide context from multiple sources (git, flow engine, backlog, specs) rooted at a project directory. <!--#68f3c4ac3bc2422e-->
  - `ProjectContextCollector.__init__` (method) — Constructor storing the project root path as a Path. <!--#9812ec98f69838a9-->
  - `ProjectContextCollector.collect` (method) — Aggregates git, flow_engine, backlog, and specs context into a single structured dict. <!--#837254f0d8b3e685-->
  - `ProjectContextCollector._collect_git` (method) — Returns git status via the commands/status helper, falling back to an unknown-branch default on error. <!--#acb96af4ae25b142-->
  - `ProjectContextCollector._collect_flow_engine` (method) — Returns flow engine history via the commands/status helper, or None on failure. <!--#056dd30cb3a17c33-->
  - `ProjectContextCollector._collect_backlog` (method) — Scans se3/specs/_backlog/*.md files and returns a list of parsed backlog items. <!--#152900683ae6176d-->
  - `ProjectContextCollector._parse_backlog_item` (method) — Parses a backlog markdown file's first lines to extract title, status, and phase. <!--#512c11b5f66af35a-->
  - `ProjectContextCollector._collect_specs` (method) — Lists available spec names by delegating to ContextBuilder's specs directory. <!--#2d1aaf9b24d7374a-->
- `list_spec_names` (function) — Returns a sorted list of spec subdirectory names, excluding internal dirs prefixed with underscore. <!--#b4e64d015a4eff4f-->

### `src/se3/engine/prompt_dedup.py` (python) — A standalone utility module whose `deduplicate_prompt_lines` function collapses repeated contiguous line-blocks in an LLM prompt string, keeping the first occurrence and replacing later copies with content-hash `[DUPLICATED CONTENT:...]` markers via O(n) fingerprint matching. <!--#14e7b640b0b10a2c|72b2d7612e58296b-->
- `deduplicate_prompt_lines` (function) — Scans a prompt for repeated contiguous line blocks of at least `min_block_lines`, keeping the first occurrence and replacing duplicates with content-hash-based `[DUPLICATED CONTENT:...]` markers via fingerprint-based O(n) matching. <!--#371239b146ce980e-->

### `src/se3/engine/prompt_history.py` (python) — Module that provides prompt_toolkit FileHistory instances for SE3's interactive input, storing prompts at se3/history/prompt_history and truncating the file to the most recent MAX_ENTRIES (500) before use. <!--#5f5aa17c2519ba66|04bd12b146c2d87e-->
- `_truncate_history` (function) — Helper that parses a prompt_toolkit history file and rewrites it to retain only the most recent MAX_ENTRIES entries, failing silently on I/O errors. <!--#2200a06d776996fb-->
- `get_prompt_history` (function) — Returns a FileHistory for the project's se3/history/prompt_history path, creating the directory and truncating the file before use. <!--#9ccd7eb15cdd0929-->

### `src/se3/engine/prompt_markers.py` (python) — Defines the HTML-comment sentinel markers and pure helper functions that delimit the template-prefix / user-content / framework-suffix segments of a step prompt so the web console can render the user's literal input as its own bubble, providing both the preferred three-segment wrapper (wrap_user_section) and its extractor (extract_user_content), a bounded jsonl scanner for the first user-content record (first_user_content), and legacy two-segment compatibility helpers (inject_boundary, wrap_user_content). <!--#4a6d5f8d5b5676be|2ad3dabcf08b54e5-->
- `_strip_edge_newlines` (function) — Helper that strips only leading/trailing CR/LF (preserving other whitespace) from a marker-bounded segment, mirroring the JS console's newline-stripping. <!--#c325d55079417749-->
- `extract_user_content` (function) — Pure function that locates the three markers in canonical order and returns the middle user-content segment, or None when the full three-segment layout is absent or empty. <!--#8530e9db818b2b45-->
- `first_user_content` (function) — Scans a bounded number of jsonl lines forward, skipping event/non-user/empty records, and returns the content of the first genuine user-content record (or None). <!--#2906efc562d20f94-->
- `_marker_pair_present` (function) — Predicate returning True only when text already contains all three markers in canonical order, used to make wrapping idempotent and distinguish the legacy two-marker form. <!--#7264f000ac385a29-->
- `wrap_user_section` (function) — Wraps user_content as an explicitly marked middle segment between prefix and suffix (the preferred three-segment layout), idempotently skipping re-wrapping if markers already exist. <!--#32884d24dfcf9446-->
- `inject_boundary` (function) — Legacy two-segment helper that splices the marker pair into a template just before a given anchor substring, idempotent and defensive when the anchor or markers are absent. <!--#85d4d148f339ac22-->
- `wrap_user_content` (function) — Legacy two-segment helper joining a template prefix and user content with the marker pair (no suffix), with empty-side and idempotency fallbacks. <!--#f94f37a3057dc0f6-->

### `src/se3/engine/retry_context.py` (python) — Neutral shared-constants module defining the retry-history block's marker and separator sentinels plus the env-configurable post-dedup safety limit, exposing this API to both the retry-context producer (chat_history) and consumer (llm_caller) without cross-importing private names. <!--#a5a0cbe752a64910|d1925360b2c56d65-->
- `_load_safety_limit` (function) — Resolves the post-dedup safety limit from the SE3_POST_DEDUP_SAFETY_LIMIT env var, falling back to the built-in default when the value is missing, non-integer, or non-positive. <!--#273086c8defce832-->

### `src/se3/engine/runtime_environment.md` (markdown) — A runtime-context document injected into agent flow steps that classifies se3 CLI commands into read-only ones safe to call proactively (history, issue, and code-index navigation) versus state-mutating ones the agent must not invoke without explicit user request. <!--#6fd2d66e2a583611|2c90375074fd2184-->
  - `se3 Runtime Environment` (heading) — Top-level heading introducing the document and stating that the agent is running inside an se3-managed project with command-safety lists following. <!--#de743451af2ef77e-->
    - `Safe to call proactively (read-only)` (heading) — A documentation section listing read-only SE3 commands an agent may run proactively—for viewing past session history, consulting related issue context, and locating code via the code-index (list/show/index/search)—with trigger phrases and a recommended navigate-then-drill-down workflow for each. <!--#5dba4b58441b4999-->
    - `Do NOT call proactively` (heading) — Section enumerating state-mutating se3 commands (history restore, issue create/reset, salvage, merge, sync, init) that the agent must not invoke unless the user explicitly requests them. <!--#d89cfba2610ed611-->

### `src/se3/engine/schema.py` (python) — Defines the formal TypedDict/Enum schemas and validation values for SE3's two state files — engine.json (flow instance, state, and hot/cold-split steps with cold_ref/context_ref externalization mirroring the models layer's status/type/flow enums) and context.json (the AI-optimized distilled export) — plus the build_context_from_flow transformer and its output-summarizing helpers. <!--#230c5065a15e844c|507a0615e5ea6ecc-->
- `StepStatusValue` (class) — A string Enum enumerating the valid step status values (pending, running, completed, partial, failed, retrying, paused, revision_needed) that mirror se3.engine.models.StepStatus so a valid engine.json passes schema validation. <!--#0ab75e95c1596ecc-->
- `StepTypeValue` (class) — A string Enum enumerating every valid step_type value (including deprecated ones) that engine.json may contain, mirroring models.StepType so valid files aren't rejected by the schema. <!--#9c52e58052b669a2-->
- `FlowStatusValue` (class) — String enum of valid overall flow statuses (init, running, paused, completed, failed, recovering). <!--#39df2b604e1da00c-->
- `ColdRefSchema` (class) — A TypedDict describing a header step's reference (file name + content hash) to its externalized cold-payload file under the hot/cold split (issue #244), enabling incremental rewrites of only changed cold files. <!--#8e6b34a181192ca9-->
- `StepSchema` (class) — A TypedDict describing one step entry in engine.json, accepting both the new hot/cold format (externalized payloads via cold_ref) and the legacy inline format (inputs/outputs/artifacts). <!--#679c1899dc00745f-->
- `ContextRefSchema` (class) — A TypedDict describing the header's reference (file name + hash) to the externalized shared-context cold file (_context.json) holding context and fix_history in the new hot/cold format. <!--#4131282588f0510f-->
- `StateSchema` (class) — A TypedDict for engine.json's state object tracking current step, step history/index, per-step statuses, selected steps, and inline scalar counters/usage, with shared context and fix_history either externalized via context_ref (new) or inlined (legacy). <!--#31df415e3bc63737-->
- `FlowInstanceSchema` (class) — The root TypedDict for engine.json, the top-level container holding a single flow execution's identity, status, task metadata, state, timestamps, worktree fields, and hot/cold format marker. <!--#6bbcf5d2fa70203e-->
- `ContextStepInfo` (class) — TypedDict holding a condensed per-step summary (type, status, timestamps, key outputs) used inside context.json. <!--#44e8c429cad17650-->
- `ContextSchema` (class) — TypedDict for the root context.json object — an AI-optimized, distilled export of flow state for handoff and resumption. <!--#04a6cbdc2923d71f-->
- `build_context_from_flow` (function) — Function that transforms a full flow instance dict into the distilled context.json structure with step summaries, key outputs, and progress. <!--#d5345fcc8d8a18af-->
- `_summarize_outputs` (function) — Helper that selects and truncates the key output fields per step type for inclusion in a context step summary. <!--#8d53669a401b3363-->
- `_extract_key_outputs` (function) — Helper that extracts the most important output values for each step type into the context's key_outputs map. <!--#38f86a01943d8f20-->

### `src/se3/engine/sink.py` (python) — Defines pluggable event-stream sinks that consume unified Event objects and render them as concrete output, with concrete CliSink (Rich CLI rendering), JsonSink (NDJSON for daemon mode), and HistorySink (per-step chat-history persistence for the web console). <!--#b70fee1ecfa89a70|c74fbe7a84cd7382-->
- `Sink` (class) — Abstract base class for an event-stream consumer that subscribes to an EventEmitter and receives every emitted event. <!--#056bd1888e33fe98-->
  - `Sink.consume` (method) — Abstract method each concrete sink overrides to perform its side effect on a single event. <!--#bb2390a15e6f138f-->
- `CliSink` (class) — The CLI-mode event sink that renders step output by delegating to the existing `step_renderers` functions — rendering full reports for terminal step events, usage-only blocks for non-terminal STEP_OUTPUT events, and per-type compact usage footers for confirm/discovery/plan — while treating flow-level lifecycle events as no-ops since the `se3 run` orchestrator already prints those. <!--#a3ab74404c131662-->
  - `CliSink.__init__` (method) — Constructor that optionally installs a supplied Rich Console as the global display console for all delegated renderers. <!--#7670536357cf51e0-->
  - `CliSink.consume` (method) — Dispatches terminal step events to `_render_step` and STEP_OUTPUT events to `_render_step_usage`, ignoring all other event types. <!--#4fb42242ff9754f9-->
  - `CliSink._render_step` (method) — Routes a terminal step event to the step-output renderer, skipping full reports for confirm/discovery/plan but still surfacing their token usage via per-type renderers. <!--#c17bf533ba7cf189-->
  - `CliSink._render_step_usage` (method) — Renders per-step token usage for a non-terminal STEP_OUTPUT event, applying the same per-type (discovery/confirm/default) rules as the terminal path. <!--#02ac269cfbbc8c1d-->
  - `CliSink._render_confirm_usage_footer` (method) — Renders confirm's token usage as a compact dim single-line footer (round equals cumulative since confirm calls the LLM at most once), rendering nothing when usage is empty. <!--#d0d721be80846166-->
  - `CliSink._render_discovery_cumulative_usage` (method) — Renders the discovery step's whole-run cumulative token usage (read from `step.outputs['token_usage']`) as a single dim i18n line via `format_usage_line`, printing nothing when the usage is absent or empty. <!--#ddf32cf5f5ac2d47-->
- `JsonSink` (class) — Sink for daemon mode that serializes each event to one line of JSON (NDJSON, or pretty-indented), degrading non-serializable payloads to their str() form. <!--#b3473271b7b32503-->
  - `JsonSink.__init__` (method) — Constructor selecting the destination text stream (default stdout) and compact-vs-pretty serialization mode. <!--#f494e6176cbf27cf-->
  - `JsonSink.consume` (method) — Serializes an event via `to_dict` and writes it as a newline-terminated JSON line, flushing while swallowing closed/unflushable-stream errors. <!--#620cbdd2cd131156-->
- `HistorySink` (class) — Sink that persists step-lifecycle events (started/completed/failed/output) into per-step chat-history jsonl so the web console can render anchors and report cards, swallowing filesystem failures. <!--#ef6b304ba013539b-->
  - `HistorySink.__init__` (method) — Constructor that records the project root used to locate the per-step history files. <!--#72ade7501cf2da27-->
  - `HistorySink.consume` (method) — Records STEP_STARTED via `_record_started` and persists terminal/output events' full step dict through `record_step_event`, ignoring other event types. <!--#85f85df1bccb1bbe-->
  - `HistorySink._record_started` (method) — Persists a STEP_STARTED event as a state-aware `running` anchor, skipping when a terminal record exists or the last anchor is already running, and re-arming '进行中' when a paused step resumes. <!--#091c894d34c9cc7a-->

### `src/se3/engine/spec_format.py` (python) — Parser and validator for spec-format v1 markdown, exposing parse_spec() to decompose a spec into a ParsedSpec (header plus Requirement items with tags, keywords, and references, while flagging content-loss hazards) and validate() to report format-rule violations as Issues, backed by code-block/table-aware regex helpers. <!--#68fe61c069d82482|ad5f94024bcdb848-->
- `Issue` (class) — Dataclass representing a single validation finding with its severity, message, and source location. <!--#83b25fba29c9c8a5-->
- `Requirement` (class) — Dataclass holding one parsed Requirement item: its name, body, tags, keywords, references, and starting line. <!--#05f4aeb020c89af3-->
- `ParsedSpec` (class) — Dataclass capturing the full parse result — shared header, Requirements, v1 marker flag, and content-loss hazards like orphan H2s, trailing text, and deep headings. <!--#2e1a351c3b5d3bd8-->
- `_find_code_block_ranges` (function) — Helper that locates the character ranges of fenced code blocks so parsing can skip their contents. <!--#be98a62dfece2077-->
- `_is_inside_code_block` (function) — Helper that tests whether a character position falls within any fenced code-block range. <!--#8a533901a897c653-->
- `_is_inside_table_row` (function) — Helper that tests whether a position lies inside a markdown table row. <!--#841d46f55f6d4171-->
- `_split_values` (function) — Helper that splits a comma-separated tags/keywords string into a trimmed list. <!--#0534b827650457a7-->
- `_clean_ref_name` (function) — Helper that truncates an extracted reference name at stop-words or a word limit to avoid over-capturing prose. <!--#8f4a6f0ef4729236-->
- `_extract_refs` (function) — Helper that extracts deduplicated intra-spec and inter-spec references from a Requirement body, skipping code blocks and tables. <!--#2ab0ac5cf93ce57b-->
- `_extract_tags_and_keywords` (function) — Helper that pulls all tags and keywords declared in a Requirement body. <!--#a38457bf73f7ba5f-->
- `parse_spec` (function) — Top-level function that parses raw spec markdown into a ParsedSpec, splitting header from Requirements and detecting orphan/trailing/deep-heading hazards. <!--#76fb3994bd0231e0-->
- `validate` (function) — Top-level function that checks a ParsedSpec against format v1 rules and returns a list of error/warning Issues. <!--#d2b1f64c2542a1f1-->

### `src/se3/engine/spec_governance.py` (python) — The authoritative, side-effect-free source of normative prompt text and small constants (domain-marker syntax, base-spec admission standard, per-Requirement/per-spec writing discipline, and cohesion-first split criteria) that governs spec volume and content, injected into update_spec/se3 sync prompts so every LLM sub-process shares one description of the spec-governance rules while the numeric thresholds live separately in SpecGovernanceConfig. <!--#7667af3fe28bd09e|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/se3/engine/spec_validator.py` (python) — A dependency-free stdlib module that structurally validates spec.md files against the spec-format v1 contract (v1 marker, title heading, non-empty Purpose section, at least one Requirement, and no leading narrative prose) via `validate_spec_structure`, plus an `extract_spec_body` helper that strips sub-agent preamble down to the first structural anchor, backed by small pure line-scanning helpers and used by discovery/engine sync and the `se3 sync --validate-only` CLI. <!--#d5fbca240b1620b9|c04ceb4ce144aea5-->
- `ValidationResult` (class) — Dataclass holding the outcome of a structural validation — a `passed` boolean plus an ordered list of human-readable error strings. <!--#7654e5f86acdea05-->
- `validate_spec_structure` (function) — Top-level validator that runs all five spec-format v1 structural rules (v1 marker, title heading, non-empty Purpose, a Requirement section, no narrative prose) and returns a non-short-circuiting ValidationResult. <!--#d50e58263018def4-->
- `extract_spec_body` (function) — Pure transform that slices the real spec body out of sub-agent output by dropping everything before the first structural anchor (v1 marker, valid title, or any level-1 heading). <!--#0c3fc23b04302c7d-->
- `_line_offset` (function) — Helper returning the character offset of the first line (from keepends-split lines) whose stripped form satisfies a predicate, or None. <!--#8c57691b144ae603-->
- `_first_non_blank` (function) — Helper returning the index of the first non-blank line at or after a start index, or None. <!--#e36c52c1fcb0f668-->
- `_first_non_blank_noncomment` (function) — Helper returning the first non-blank line index that is also not a self-contained HTML comment, used to skip header markers when locating the title. <!--#9cef8bcd96c2a4f2-->
- `_is_valid_title` (function) — Helper deciding whether a line is a valid case-insensitive `# <spec_name> Specification` title, with token-tolerant matching for legacy human-authored titles. <!--#7b638e24391d4985-->
- `_find_heading` (function) — Helper returning the index of the first line exactly matching a given heading string, or None. <!--#027eef02d7887b7c-->
- `_section_has_body` (function) — Helper returning whether the section starting at a heading index has any non-blank, non-heading content before the next heading or EOF. <!--#0c4356cb276e0e77-->
- `_has_requirement` (function) — Helper returning whether any line begins with the `### Requirement:` heading. <!--#ce96c41febce9768-->
- `_first_prose_line` (function) — Helper returning the first non-blank, non-comment, non-heading line's stripped content, or None. <!--#4baaf5be448346e5-->
- `_looks_narrative` (function) — Helper returning whether a line begins with one of the narrative-prose prefixes (English or Chinese) that signal sub-agent prose instead of spec content. <!--#ce5b66df03816acc-->

### `src/se3/engine/spec_write_hook.py` (python) — A stdlib-only, side-effect-free module providing two layers of spec-file write protection: a PreToolUse hook (`main`) that denies any Write/Edit/NotebookEdit targeting `se3/specs/`, and an `ensure_guard_plugin` generator that materializes a minimal controlled Claude plugin so the guard can be injected additively via `--plugin-dir` (avoiding the clobbering-second-`--settings` hazard), plus content-hash and byte-capture helpers (`snapshot_spec_files`, `diff_spec_files`, `capture_spec_contents`, `restore_spec_files`) used by the post-step fallback guard to detect and revert illegal spec writes that bypass the hook. <!--#c124f3842f287b18|d8b45a5cce38fc55-->
- `_specs_dir` (function) — Returns the absolute, normalized se3/specs directory path for a given cwd without checking existence. <!--#820e65f393a68a60-->
- `_resolve_target` (function) — Resolves a possibly-relative file path against cwd into a normalized absolute Path, returning None on empty input or error. <!--#796c32141d866a6c-->
- `_is_spec_target` (function) — Returns True when a given file path resolves to somewhere under the cwd's se3/specs directory. <!--#51c3f95bed41c685-->
- `_emit_deny` (function) — Emits a PreToolUse deny decision (both the structured JSON protocol and an exit-2/stderr backstop) explaining the spec write is rejected, then exits. <!--#15e3859220f183cd-->
- `main` (function) — Hook entry point that reads the stdin payload, denies a write targeting a spec file, and otherwise safely allows the call (failing open on any error). <!--#ff237bb752e3f93f-->
- `_guard_plugin_manifest` (function) — Returns the minimal `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` manifest dict (name/version/description) identifying the SE3 spec-write-guard plugin. <!--#2fcd9b3a8a782d88-->
- `_guard_plugin_hooks_payload` (function) — Builds the plugin's `hooks/hooks.json` payload declaring a single PreToolUse hook that shell-quotes the interpreter path and invokes `se3.engine.spec_write_hook` to intercept Write/Edit/NotebookEdit calls. <!--#861ed0155543d9b9-->
- `_write_if_changed` (function) — Idempotency helper that writes desired content to a path only when it differs from the existing file, avoiding needless mtime churn. <!--#6b00192241849aab-->
- `ensure_guard_plugin` (function) — Materializes (idempotently) the controlled guard plugin — manifest plus PreToolUse hook — under `se3/tmp/spec_write_guard_plugin/` and returns its directory for additive injection via `--plugin-dir` rather than a clobbering second `--settings` flag. <!--#a82cc37a1f20af37-->
- `snapshot_spec_files` (function) — Walks se3/specs recursively and returns a map of project-relative path to sha256 content hash for before/after change detection. <!--#e88c238e08d4ad1f-->
- `diff_spec_files` (function) — Compares two spec snapshot/content maps and returns the sorted list of paths that were added, removed, or modified. <!--#6d7b39d46828be66-->
- `capture_spec_contents` (function) — Byte-level counterpart of snapshot_spec_files, mapping each spec path to its raw bytes so the fallback guard can revert illegal writes. <!--#fe4a82c02e1e6b95-->
- `restore_spec_files` (function) — Reverts each changed spec path to its pre-step bytes (or deletes newly-created ones) and returns paths that could not be restored. <!--#e5e8dd0422656775-->

### `src/se3/engine/stash_utils.py` (python) — Shared no-data-loss recovery helpers for `git stash pop` conflicts—used by both the DAG implement step and the `se3 merge` robust strategy—that label-resolve stashes, archive all recoverable content (tracked and untracked, both sides) to a gitignored archive dir before touching it, classify and resolve conflicts, drop the labeled stash only after recovery is proven, and render an operator-facing audit manifest. <!--#ac82c8cba23a5b1b|9022da602294d82a-->
- `ArchivedEntry` (class) — A dataclass representing one stashed file persisted to the archive directory, tracking its relative path, archive location, blob SHA, conflict class (case 'a' tracked vs 'b' untracked), and which side ('stashed'/theirs or 'head'/ours) it holds for recovery. <!--#37c71d5a84923444-->
- `_resolve_stash_ref` (function) — Resolves the live `stash@{N}` ref whose message exactly matches a given label, by parsing `git stash list`, so concurrent stashes can't be confused for SE3's own (returns None if none match). <!--#d30a07a7548e9662-->
- `pop_stash_by_label` (function) — Performs `git stash pop` on the specific stash entry resolved by label (never a bare pop), returning a synthetic non-zero result if the label doesn't resolve so the no-data-loss recovery path takes over instead of popping an unrelated stash. <!--#eb99645738aef351-->
- `_git_show_bytes` (function) — Returns the raw bytes of `git show <spec>` so binary blobs round-trip intact and hash back to the original git object, or None if the object can't be read. <!--#fbe303964dff7cba-->
- `_sanitize_label` (function) — Replaces filesystem-unsafe characters in a label so an embedded branch-name slash can't spill the archive across directories, making it a single safe path segment. <!--#6067e278401649bd-->
- `_archive_run_rel` (function) — Computes the project-root-relative base directory name (`<timestamp>_<label>`) for a recovery run's archived payload, shared by both the stashed-side and HEAD-side captures. <!--#cf78655932911e32-->
- `_prepare_unique_archive_run` (function) — Atomically claims a fresh, never-reused run directory for a recovery's archived payload (via `mkdir(exist_ok=False)` with `-N` suffix fallback) so same-second repeat recoveries can't overwrite each other's bytes. <!--#ea87c78b56353604-->
- `_archive_blob` (function) — Persists a single git object into the run directory, recording its blob SHA and returning an ArchivedEntry, raising RuntimeError on any read/resolve/write failure so a caller relying on it as recovery proof refuses to drop. <!--#b8140b47f14d554a-->
- `archive_stash_payload` (function) — Persists a live stash's entire recoverable content (untracked files via `^3` and non-deleted tracked changes) to the archive directory and returns the recovery manifest, raising rather than silently skipping so the caller never drops without proven-complete persistence. <!--#beca1d2bea64fe6d-->
- `parse_stashpop_already_exists` (function) — Parses `git stash pop` output to extract file paths reported as 'already exists, no checkout', which git doesn't mark as unmerged. <!--#740f82b591b8253f-->
- `take_ours_for_stashpop` (function) — Resolves stash-pop conflicts by keeping the merged HEAD (ours) version via `checkout --ours`, the default no-resolver fallback for case-a conflicts, safe only because the discarded stashed side was already archived first. <!--#9381e724e451d872-->
- `_archive_case_a_head_side` (function) — Archives the merged HEAD (ours, `:2:<path>`) version of each case-a conflict path into a side-namespaced location before resolution, so both sides of a tracked 3-way conflict are recoverable regardless of which the resolver discards. <!--#8396eab3d118aef2-->
- `StashPopOutcome` (class) — A dataclass holding the result of `resolve_stashpop_safely` — the recovery manifest, whether the stash was dropped, the case-a/case-b file split, an archive-failure flag, and the still-unmerged files that must block reporting a clean merge. <!--#f488a7c7eb37e6be-->
- `resolve_stashpop_safely` (function) — The shared entry point that recovers a stash-pop result without data loss: short-circuits on clean pops, archives all recoverable content first, classifies conflicts (leaving untracked case-b untouched while resolving tracked case-a via an injected resolver or take-ours), and drops the labeled stash only after recovery is proven and the conflict resolved. <!--#bab929a1e4571489-->
- `format_archived_manifest` (function) — Renders an archive manifest into audit-issue body text (path, blob SHA, conflict class, and side) so the operator-facing recovery pointer is identical across both merge paths. <!--#c05204ff2a9f49c5-->

### `src/se3/engine/stashpop_llm_resolver.py` (python) — The LLM-integration layer that builds a case-a stash-pop `conflict_resolver`, sending marker-bearing files to the LLM-as-editor, staging only the paths whose unmerged index entry is provably cleared, and falling back to the deterministic `take_ours_for_stashpop` for everything else so the working tree is left marker-free without data loss. <!--#10f2f5a80f56db1c|e70e458b5fa15562-->
- `_path_is_unmerged` (function) — Returns whether a path still has an unmerged index entry via `git ls-files --unmerged`, treating any git error as still-unmerged so the caller never optimistically drops the stash over an unresolved conflict. <!--#1b9b4d31a66b2af4-->
- `llm_resolve_stashpop_conflicts` (function) — Reconciles case-a stash-pop conflicts by handing each marker-bearing file to the LLM-as-editor, writing and staging the result, and returns only the paths whose unmerged index entry is provably cleared (leaving everything else to the deterministic fallback). <!--#dec44c2d15334150-->
- `make_llm_stashpop_resolver` (function) — Builds the `resolve_stashpop_safely` conflict-resolver callable that tries the LLM resolver first and falls back to the deterministic `take_ours_for_stashpop` for any unresolved files, leaving the working tree marker-free. <!--#60bd80d7d596bc9a-->

### `src/se3/engine/state_machine.py` (python) — Core flow-engine state machine that drives step sequencing and execution — building each step's inputs (including adjudication overrides and effective task descriptions), performing transitions between discovery/fix/revision/merge phases, managing retry-counter semantics, persistence, and token-usage accumulation, and raising the module's StateMachineError family (StepExecutionError, TransitionError, MergeCheckoutResolutionError) when a step or transition cannot proceed. <!--#7d3b2724cecfcdb0|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/se3/engine/step_renderers.py` (python) — Rich-based presentation layer for the SE3 engine: a StepType→renderer registry (with a generic fallback) plus per-step renderers that turn each completed step's outputs — analyze, propose, design, plan, implement, test, spec_gate, self_check, verify_spec, update_spec, summarize, commit, version_analyze/reconcile, merge_integrate — into localized console panels, tables and token-usage blocks. <!--#0b7d1a9506d769b6|5ad5983757ab833a-->
- `step_display_title` (function) — Returns the localized display title for a StepType (falling back to its raw value), exposed publicly so the `se3 run` console and the renderers share one step-title vocabulary. <!--#8832c035e4d7282b-->
- `register_renderer` (function) — Decorator factory that registers a function as the custom renderer for a given StepType in the STEP_RENDERERS registry. <!--#d32f2f04d911965a-->
- `render_step_output` (function) — Main entry point that renders a completed step by dispatching to its registered custom renderer (or the generic fallback) and then appending the step's token-usage block. <!--#0cc6d9917694653b-->
- `render_step_usage` (function) — Renders a step's per-step token-usage panel from `outputs.token_usage`, rendering nothing when the step made no LLM calls; public so CliSink can call it for the interactive steps whose reports it skips. <!--#a9368489b20686e5-->
- `_format_value` (function) — Helper that formats an arbitrary output value into a display string, JSON-encoding dicts/lists and stringifying everything else. <!--#de91dc9da5c3e62f-->
- `_default_render` (function) — Generic fallback renderer that dumps a step's status, each output key/value (truncating long strings to a preview) and any error message into a panel. <!--#15af8e595c77305d-->
- `_render_remaining` (function) — Helper that renders any step.outputs keys a specialized renderer didn't already cover, using the same generic key/value formatting under a "remaining" panel title. <!--#8d4380e5dfe48c4d-->
- `_render_version_analyze` (function) — Renders the version_analyze step as a current→suggested version headline plus bump type, confidence, reasoning and any error. <!--#4460e5c62eda9db3-->
- `_render_merge_integrate` (function) — Renders the merge_integrate step, listing which branches landed on master, flagging escalation to a human, and showing any error. <!--#cf26edeb58f59974-->
- `_render_version_reconcile` (function) — Renders the version_reconcile step as the base→final version derived at merge, plus release channel, reconcile commit, and the clean already-reconciled no-op case. <!--#8e1bbb1b4148f135-->
- `_render_summarize` (function) — Renders the summarize step's `summary` output as markdown. <!--#2d06117faf4f22a8-->
- `_build_test_summary_lines` (function) — Shared helper that turns a `test_results` dict into summary-only lines (overall pass/fail, per-phase results, command) with no raw pytest output. <!--#2db7e1ac1b1d1f59-->
- `_render_test` (function) — Renders the test step's summary lines from `test_results`, falling back to the generic renderer when no results dict is present. <!--#f65f736cef99d027-->
- `_render_spec_gate` (function) — Renders the spec_gate step as a gate conclusion (passed/failed/skipped plus fallback route), fix instructions, and a reused summary-only test-results block. <!--#a0a7d43e41767694-->
- `_render_propose` (function) — Renders the propose step via the shared proposal renderer when a proposal dict is present, then any uncovered outputs; otherwise falls back to the generic renderer. <!--#0f0edcb30f6edf74-->
- `_render_design` (function) — Renders the design step via the shared design renderer when a design dict is present, then any uncovered outputs; otherwise falls back to the generic renderer. <!--#b3afb38e46c172e0-->
- `_render_plan` (function) — Renders the plan step in three sections — proposal, design, and a task-group table (id, name, task count, estimated LOC, dependencies) — plus any remaining outputs. <!--#f2daf4e27212498c-->
- `_group_files_by_directory` (function) — Helper that groups a list of file paths by their top-level directory into a sorted OrderedDict for display. <!--#f9bc34f5641dd2ca-->
- `_render_implement` (function) — Renders the implement step as a status bar (complete/partial/failed with group/file/test counts) followed by summary, files changed grouped by directory, tests added, incomplete tasks, restricted-edit results and errors. <!--#a9f5caa827fe6807-->
- `_render_analyze` (function) — Renders the analyze step as a task-type/complexity/scope status bar plus reasoning and the selected relevant spec items. <!--#dac29330f5fad146-->
- `_render_self_check` (function) — Renders the self_check step's pass/fail/actionable-count status, summary, and issues grouped and colored by severity (with schema compatibility for legacy verify_spec issues). <!--#bf9dee1a5dd7c798-->
- `_render_verify_spec` (function) — Renders the verify_spec step's verified status, summary, issues grouped by in/out-of-scope and colored by priority with suggestions, and recommendations. <!--#4cfa969f07fd1e3c-->
- `_render_update_spec` (function) — Renders the update_spec step's list of updated specs and new capabilities, or a "nothing updated" panel when both are empty. <!--#af36182188d46fa3-->
- `_render_commit` (function) — Renders the commit step as short hash plus optional bumped version and the commit message, showing the "no changes" shortcut only when there is also no error to report. <!--#94a60b13b0bfcd7d-->

### `src/se3/engine/task_description.py` (python) — Owns the canonical rendering of persisted user interjections into an '## Additional Instructions (added during run)' section appended to a step's base task description, shared by all call sites so immediate re-runs and downstream step propagation produce byte-identical output. <!--#5bfbec42e2f34e85|86c2c9cd1e02d20d-->
- `compose_task_description_with_interjections` (function) — Renders a list of interjection dicts into a '## Additional Instructions' section appended to the base task description, skipping empty entries and returning the base unchanged when none are usable. <!--#0330964a0329ae3c-->

### `src/se3/engine/test_adjudicate_step.py` (python) — Unit-test suite for the ADJUDICATE step, covering oscillation-candidate detection on the adjudication ledger, the handler's flat trigger inputs and effective task description/plan resolution, LLM ruling parsing (including null-string coercion and unparseable-response failure), and the staged-then-landed ledger effects (abolishing or rejecting positions, superseding fix instructions) while leaving prior steps' outputs untouched. <!--#67d935cd8489e66d|ab8b42c44b5de921-->
- `_issue` (function) — Test factory that builds a canonical self-check issue dict (severity, expected/actual behavior, verbatim-quote expectation source, evidence lines) with overridable file/line/quote/expected fields. <!--#d96d19b9391b4932-->
