- `_flow_with_ledger` (function) — Test factory that builds a FlowInstance whose adjudication ledger holds one position, optionally seeded with two opposing self-check rounds to make it an oscillation candidate. <!--#3c9817e99a3650e3-->
- `_adj_step` (function) — Test helper that creates an ADJUDICATE Step with the given inputs and appends it to the flow's state. <!--#1db08f9da8fe61a7-->
- `_mock_call` (function) — Test helper returning a fake LLMCaller class whose call() always returns the given payload serialized as JSON. <!--#ac2021013da00311-->
- `test_candidate_positions_picks_oscillating` (function) — Asserts _candidate_positions surfaces an oscillating position and its timeline captures both opposing expectations. <!--#0a034c6dd028cc55-->
- `test_candidate_positions_ignores_single_expectation` (function) — Asserts _candidate_positions returns nothing for a position that carried only a single (non-oscillating) expectation. <!--#ce03340f3db35ec0-->
- `test_candidate_positions_honors_explicit_trigger` (function) — Asserts a single-expectation position is surfaced as a candidate when explicitly passed via the trigger's explicit position list. <!--#c2f68d55612f8d52-->
- `test_candidate_positions_skips_quoteless` (function) — Asserts quoteless (evidence-only) findings that collapse to a per-file position_key are not presented as a bogus A/B oscillation candidate. <!--#d1805d93b5896836-->
- `test_handler_reads_flat_trigger_inputs` (function) — Asserts the handler consumes the flat trigger keys the state machine writes, rendering the real trigger reason and surfacing an explicitly-unioned single-expectation candidate. <!--#e6bcc8b565e14798-->
- `test_effective_task_description_ignores_interjection_composed_input` (function) — Asserts _effective_task_description adjudicates over the pre-interjection base, stripping the interjection-composed '## Additional Instructions' section. <!--#7e84625d83761d5f-->
- `test_effective_task_description_honors_clean_base_input` (function) — Asserts a clean task_description_base input is used verbatim by _effective_task_description. <!--#6eaf3f927012790a-->
- `test_handler_writes_override_to_own_outputs` (function) — Asserts a contradiction ruling writes adjudicated description/plan/rationale/timestamp to the step's own outputs and emits no self_check-style issues. <!--#caab40ec2aec857f-->
- `test_handler_supersedes_fix_instructions` (function) — Asserts the handler stashes and flags any pending fix_instructions as superseded by the new ruling. <!--#b8c217f516672aef-->
- `test_contradiction_verdict_abolishes_position` (function) — Asserts a contradiction verdict only stages position abolition until the ruling lands, after which apply_landed_ledger_effects abolishes the observations and the position stops suppressing convergence. <!--#17aa0ba1d1287545-->
- `test_benign_verdict_records_rejected_candidate` (function) — Asserts a benign verdict stages a rejected candidate that is recorded on the ledger's rejected_positions only after landing, excluding it from future oscillation triggers. <!--#e6d4c8cb7cb7030a-->
- `test_plan_override_accepted_only_as_nonempty_list` (function) — Asserts a non-empty adjudicated_plan list override is accepted while the description override stays None. <!--#8f0cc3f47389ec2f-->
- `test_null_string_override_coerced_to_none` (function) — Verifies that when the LLM emits literal 'null'/'none' strings for a review_divergence ruling, the transparent no-op path never writes the (coerced) description/plan overrides. <!--#b7712e88a9d29ee5-->
- `test_override_without_verdicts_still_abolishes_candidates` (function) — Asserts a description patch with no explicit verdicts still abolishes the flagged candidates whose quoted clause left the adjudicated text. <!--#6bd6eceb9ff213ea-->
- `test_handler_does_not_touch_prior_step_outputs` (function) — Asserts adjudication leaves prior DISCOVERY and PLAN step outputs byte-for-byte unchanged, layering overrides only onto the adjudicate step. <!--#02447fceeb71641c-->
- `test_effective_task_groups_prefers_prior_adjudication` (function) — Asserts _effective_task_groups reads the latest prior adjudicated_plan rather than the raw plan step's task_groups. <!--#afaacfa00e1341c8-->
- `test_handler_threads_revision_feedback_into_prompt` (function) — Asserts a confirmation-gate revision re-run surfaces the reviewer's rejection feedback in the ruling prompt. <!--#135388ae1d329f2f-->
- `test_handler_ignores_revision_feedback_when_not_revision` (function) — Asserts revision_feedback is omitted from the prompt when the step is not flagged as a revision. <!--#3fc782c269419024-->
- `test_handler_fails_gracefully_on_unparseable_llm` (function) — Asserts an unparseable LLM response makes the handler return FAILED with an error message set. <!--#61d82941cc407e1c-->
- `test_multi_generation_rulings_are_each_auditable` (function) — Asserts each ADJUDICATE generation retains its own rationale/timestamp while _latest_adjudicated resolves the effective text to the newest ruling. <!--#3a7b9fd906a92857-->
- `test_ruling_description_drops_dead_clause_issue_via_source_pool` (function) — Asserts the ruling's adjudicated_description becomes the verbatim-quote source pool so a later issue re-quoting the abolished clause is dropped by self_check validation. <!--#efae7616e4579b4d-->
- `test_handler_stages_but_does_not_apply_ledger_effects` (function) — Asserts the handler only stages abolish/reject effects, leaving the persisted ledger clean and abolished_count unwritten until landing. <!--#314120db143bb6af-->
- `test_rejected_ruling_leaves_ledger_untouched` (function) — Asserts a confirmation-rejected ruling and its revision re-run leave no abolish/reject side effects on the ledger since nothing was ever applied. <!--#5e91eb9cbeda40cf-->
- `test_plan_only_override_keeps_live_description_clause_counting` (function) — Asserts a plan-only fix does not abolish a description-grounded position whose quoted clause still lives in the unchanged task description, so it keeps counting toward triggers. <!--#c8528e00249025a8-->
- `test_description_rewrite_abolishes_only_the_removed_clause` (function) — Asserts a description rewrite abolishes only the position whose clause was removed while a preserved hard-constraint clause keeps its history. <!--#c099276c48037401-->
- `test_description_only_ruling_keeps_clause_the_live_plan_still_restates` (function) — Asserts a description-only ruling does not abolish a clause the un-overridden plan still restates, keeping the plan-grounded issue quotable and valid downstream. <!--#f53b64e5049dbfec-->
- `test_noop_contradiction_ruling_fails_after_retries` (function) — Asserts a real-contradiction verdict with no covering override patch is rejected (FAILED) rather than reflowing against an unchanged spec, staging nothing. <!--#85d8ae82307b6579-->
- `test_noop_contradiction_ruling_retries_then_succeeds` (function) — Asserts a first no-op contradiction ruling is re-asked with a strict patch demand and a corrected second ruling lands normally. <!--#c7549f31e1fcd7c3-->
- `test_review_divergence_needs_no_patch` (function) — Asserts that a review_divergence verdict legitimately completes with no override patch, flagging adjudication_noop and leaving description/plan unset. <!--#a358bda30dd8a1bb-->
- `test_review_divergence_blank_rationale_is_rejected` (function) — Asserts a whitespace-only adjudication_rationale is non-actionable, so even a review_divergence ruling retries and FAILS without writing a blank audit or rejected candidates. <!--#09d88aaf99b8c675-->
- `test_review_divergence_without_verdicts_rejects_all_candidates` (function) — Asserts a no-patch review_divergence ruling omitting candidate_verdicts still stages every flagged position as rejected so the oscillation cannot re-trigger. <!--#cf07644616324582-->
- `test_review_divergence_stray_contradiction_verdict_is_rejected` (function) — Asserts a no-patch review_divergence ruling with a stray per-candidate contradiction verdict still rejects the position since there is no patch to abolish against. <!--#04c770bb9254894f-->
- `test_review_divergence_with_patch_discards_override` (function) — Regression test ensuring a review_divergence ruling that also carries an override patch discards the override (no spec rewrite, nothing abolished) and instead stages the candidate as rejected. <!--#ef9c9a3d26a77bce-->
- `test_review_divergence_is_transparent_noop` (function) — Verifies a no-real-contradiction ruling is a transparent no-op: it flags adjudication_noop and records an audit-only verdict plus rejected_positions bookkeeping, but writes none of the supersede/override fields so IMPLEMENT keeps the original fix_instructions. <!--#1c2d3e59f62a712c-->
- `test_real_contradiction_is_not_a_noop` (function) — Confirms a real internal_contradiction takes the patch path — superseding pending fix_instructions and writing the override — and never sets adjudication_noop. <!--#16f9ad04dd1445f3-->
- `test_noop_reruling_clears_rejected_patch_ruling` (function) — Regression test asserting that when a rejected patch ruling re-runs the same ADJUDICATE step in place and the LLM then rules a benign review_divergence (no-op), the handler fully wipes the earlier ruling's adjudicated_description/adjudicated_plan/superseded_fix_instructions/fix_instructions_superseded keys so the never-approved rewrite can't linger as the effective task description. <!--#1dd078998aaa36cd-->
- `test_contradiction_reruling_clears_stale_noop_flag` (function) — Regression test that a re-run following a prior no-op ruling forces adjudication_noop back to False when it now rules a real contradiction, so routing takes the patch/supersede path. <!--#f240956d4d300f1c-->
- `_sequenced_caller` (function) — Test helper that builds a fake LLMCaller class returning a scripted sequence of JSON payloads while appending each prompt it receives to a shared list, so tests can assert on prompt content across retries. <!--#53663eb20cf7c926-->
- `test_prompt_demands_homomorphic_sweep_and_conservatism` (function) — Asserts the adjudication prompt sent to the LLM contains the homomorphic-surfaces sweep instruction, the conservatism ('when in doubt, leave it out' / auto-pass) rule, the rule-in-full demand, and the covered_surfaces schema. <!--#e077e9dd3094fd38-->
- `test_covered_surfaces_persisted_on_patch_path` (function) — Verifies that for a real-contradiction ruling the handler sanitizes (strips whitespace from) the LLM's covered_surfaces entries and persists them into the step's outputs. <!--#ece18460b35de397-->
- `test_covered_surfaces_absent_or_empty_still_actionable` (function) — Checks that an omitted, null, or empty covered_surfaces field is a legitimate outcome — the ruling still completes and outputs an empty list rather than forcing the LLM to invent surfaces. <!--#c041f884594c6117-->
- `test_normalized_covered_surfaces_shapes` (function) — Unit-tests the private `_normalized_covered_surfaces` helper directly, covering the well-formed/absent/empty cases (valid, list returned) and a battery of malformed shapes (invalid flag). <!--#892de7bc12fed5c1-->
- `test_incomplete_covered_surfaces_entry_triggers_semantic_retry` (function) — Confirms that a covered_surfaces entry missing its justification makes the handler re-ask the LLM with the malformed-field reason in the retry prompt, and that the corrected second ruling lands. <!--#2200cf1b8716816b-->
- `test_covered_surfaces_never_valid_fails_with_reason` (function) — Confirms two consecutive malformed covered_surfaces rulings fail the step with an error message naming the gate, leaving nothing written to the outputs. <!--#eaea15e00ad318f0-->
- `test_review_divergence_ignores_malformed_covered_surfaces` (function) — Confirms a no-op (review_divergence) ruling ignores malformed covered_surfaces rather than blocking, and omits the key entirely from its outputs since no boundary clause is written. <!--#e8deeca2120bb88e-->
- `test_noop_rerun_pops_stale_covered_surfaces` (function) — Confirms that when a rejected patch ruling re-runs in place as a no-op review_divergence, the stale covered_surfaces governance claim from the earlier ruling is removed from the step's outputs. <!--#8fbc0d67a039cc35-->

### `src/se3/engine/test_adjudication.py` (python) — Unit tests for the pure adjudication logic — issue fingerprinting and position keys, ledger accumulation/dedup/idempotency, and the mechanical triggers (oscillation, contradiction, reproduction, periodic backstop) plus convergence suppression and abolished/rejected exclusions. <!--#4ad0b3c443e9e123|dafb2c5c49b145fe-->
- `_issue` (function) — Test helper that builds a minimal self_check issue dict with configurable file, line, verbatim quote, and expected behavior. <!--#91b0474f9f5473c0-->
- `test_fingerprint_stable_under_line_drift` (function) — Asserts an issue's fingerprint and position_key stay constant when only its line number shifts after a fix iteration. <!--#ec3c45b08e6f0ef6-->
- `test_fingerprint_differs_on_expected` (function) — Asserts that identical positions with opposing expected behaviors yield different fingerprints but the same position_key. <!--#c2442c47438993a3-->
- `test_normalization_matches_source_pool_semantics` (function) — Verifies quote normalization (NFKC, smart quotes, whitespace, literal \n) collapses semantically-equal quotes to the same position_key. <!--#e1da97afa131e12b-->
- `test_missing_in_fallback_for_unimplemented` (function) — Checks that a wholly-missing task with empty evidence_lines grounds its position via the missing_in file instead. <!--#e14283244ccfa2b0-->
- `test_empty_ledger_on_legacy_context` (function) — Verifies a legacy context lacking the ledger key tolerates evaluation as empty and lazily initializes the ledger. <!--#d6bc73a31814b5c5-->
- `test_record_accumulates_across_rounds_only_grows` (function) — Confirms recording self_check rounds monotonically grows the ledger's round_count and observations, never clearing them. <!--#4808167f9c8eccc2-->
- `test_record_dedupes_within_round` (function) — Asserts identical issues within a single recorded round collapse to one observation. <!--#f7a4bf9831a0fd31-->
- `test_record_idempotent_on_round_id_replay` (function) — Verifies replaying the same round_id (e.g. on --resume) does not double-count rounds or observations. <!--#adecf2322021bc3f-->
- `test_trigger_a_oscillation_fires_on_flipped_expected` (function) — Asserts trigger (a) fires the oscillation reason when the same position flips its expected behavior across rounds. <!--#8ad29b6cfe0648bf-->
- `test_trigger_a_no_fire_when_expected_stable` (function) — Confirms the oscillation trigger stays silent when a position's expectation is stable across rounds. <!--#0c5ec22f9280bb7c-->
- `test_trigger_a_no_fire_first_time_seen` (function) — Confirms the oscillation trigger does not fire on an issue's first appearance. <!--#f8a738b4ca1e5f56-->
- `test_trigger_a_only_structural_not_truth` (function) — Asserts oscillation is a purely structural signal that sets suppress_convergence. <!--#0557ce3d6ba56700-->
- `test_trigger_b_contradiction_reads_previous_resolutions` (function) — Asserts trigger (b) fires contradiction (and suppresses convergence) when a fixed position re-opens with the opposite expectation. <!--#c15c096f431eac3e-->
- `test_trigger_b_fires_when_same_fixed_fingerprint_reopens` (function) — Asserts contradiction fires immediately when a self_check re-flags the exact fingerprint just declared fixed, rather than waiting for reproduction threshold (c). <!--#299f5af7f697bb54-->
- `test_trigger_b_ignores_still_present_resolutions` (function) — Confirms contradiction does not fire when the prior resolution was 'still_present' rather than 'fixed'. <!--#a73cd8deee12ee54-->
- `test_trigger_b_accepts_inlined_resolution_fields` (function) — Verifies contradiction detection works when resolution carries issue fields inline instead of in a nested issue. <!--#3d476a3f2fd7f65f-->
- `test_trigger_c_reproduction_third_appearance_after_fix` (function) — Asserts trigger (c) reproduction fires only on the third genuine post-fix recurrence of a fingerprint, not the second. <!--#5ec3c10e82b621be-->
- `test_trigger_c_no_fire_before_third_or_without_fix` (function) — Confirms reproduction does not fire for a recurring issue that was never declared fixed. <!--#d229b6da597b97f7-->
- `test_trigger_c_pre_fix_flags_do_not_inflate_count` (function) — Verifies pre-fix and at-fix flags are excluded so reproduction is scored strictly from post-fixed recurrences. <!--#abceed5933c6a7c9-->
- `test_trigger_c_quoteless_fingerprint_never_fires` (function) — Asserts a quoteless (regression-type) fingerprint, whose position collapses to per-file identity, is excluded from firing reproduction. <!--#32cbf6e6004385a9-->
- `test_period_backstop_fires_every_n_iterations` (function) — Asserts the periodic backstop fires the period reason at the configured iteration interval without suppressing convergence. <!--#5e09c2f2501dd1ea-->
- `test_period_backstop_measures_from_baseline` (function) — Verifies the periodic backstop counts iterations from the last adjudication baseline rather than absolute iteration zero. <!--#c83633b3f8ebe7c2-->
- `test_abolished_entries_excluded_from_triggers` (function) — Confirms abolished fingerprints are excluded so a would-be oscillation no longer triggers. <!--#3d5fed2e7f519413-->
- `test_abolished_excludes_reproduction` (function) — Confirms marking a fingerprint abolished vetoes an otherwise-firing reproduction trigger. <!--#8296842e146bb5ef-->
- `test_rejected_candidate_position_not_retriggered` (function) — Asserts a previously rejected candidate position no longer re-triggers oscillation. <!--#f172f40ae9b302c2-->
- `test_should_suppress_convergence_true_on_oscillation` (function) — Asserts should_suppress_convergence returns True when an oscillation signal is present. <!--#25bf007754e6a8d8-->
- `test_should_suppress_convergence_false_when_no_signal` (function) — Asserts should_suppress_convergence returns False for a stable issue with no structural signal. <!--#841e39362b392cbd-->
- `test_should_suppress_convergence_true_on_due_periodic_backstop` (function) — Asserts a due periodic backstop suppresses convergence so ADJUDICATE can run before the convergence shortcut short-circuits to COMPLETED. <!--#c0159237fcdd5c33-->
- `test_ledger_survives_dict_round_trip` (function) — Verifies the ledger is plain JSON-serializable so triggers evaluate identically before and after a dict round-trip. <!--#a050b343c8f5d136-->

### `src/se3/engine/test_adjudication_effective.py` (python) — Unit tests for the engine's adjudication effective-text layer, verifying that the latest adjudicated description/plan correctly overrides refined and original task text across `_latest_adjudicated_output`, `_effective_task_description_base`, `_build_step_inputs`, and the self_check `_build_source_pool`, so that self-check issues quoting clauses abolished by adjudication are filtered out while live-clause issues survive. <!--#e317b3be3be42ca6|43ea25f184186d7c-->

- `test_latest_adjudicated_output_ignores_non_completed` (function) — Asserts _latest_adjudicated_output ignores outputs from adjudicate steps that are not COMPLETED. <!--#611aec2c12668a1f-->
- `test_base_original_without_any_override` (function) — Asserts _effective_task_description_base returns the original task text when nothing overrides it. <!--#d035d0e068937e95-->
- `test_base_refined_overrides_original` (function) — Asserts a discovery step's refined_description overrides the original task text in the effective base. <!--#8e7e230a151d5517-->
- `test_base_adjudicated_overrides_refined_and_original` (function) — Asserts an adjudicated_description takes precedence over both refined and original text in the effective base. <!--#445b1569b0badcfd-->
- `test_base_multi_generation_takes_latest_adjudication` (function) — Asserts the effective base uses the latest adjudication generation's description across multiple rulings. <!--#e8d0b9c5089ec22e-->
- `test_base_plan_only_ruling_falls_through_to_refined` (function) — Asserts a ruling that changed only the plan leaves the effective base description at the refined value. <!--#ebe202195a85c064-->
- `_sm` (function) — Test helper that instantiates a StateMachine rooted at a fresh temp directory. <!--#310be166a0b8631d-->
- `test_build_step_inputs_uses_adjudicated_description` (function) — Asserts _build_step_inputs feeds the adjudicated description as task_description into the implement step. <!--#3706b795bca36d67-->
- `test_build_step_inputs_no_adjudication_unchanged` (function) — Asserts _build_step_inputs passes through the original description and plan task_groups when no adjudication exists. <!--#2f5dcc16a6cddff3-->
- `test_build_step_inputs_plan_override` (function) — Asserts an adjudicated_plan overrides the plan step's task_groups in the built inputs. <!--#9693fbc7b3bc34d9-->
- `test_build_step_inputs_self_check_signals_adjudication` (function) — Asserts self_check inputs expose the adjudicated text as both task_description_base and adjudicated_description. <!--#ad5eb229103bef00-->
- `test_transition_to_fix_uses_adjudicated_description` (function) — Asserts re-entering implement on the fix loop composes the adjudicated description into the implement step's inputs. <!--#7da8ff8b193017b1-->
- `test_source_pool_unchanged_without_adjudication` (function) — Asserts _build_source_pool retains both the refined base and canonical original when no adjudication is present. <!--#23fd1d8c12381cf6-->
- `test_source_pool_drops_original_when_adjudicated` (function) — Asserts _build_source_pool drops the superseded original text from the pool once an adjudicated description is in effect. <!--#72003edca75d4ab1-->

### `src/se3/engine/test_baseline.py` (python) — Captures the set of tests already failing at flow start — via a background test-suite subprocess (BaselineCapture) plus a git-HEAD/dirty-hash keyed on-disk cache — so later test/verify_spec steps can tell inherited failures apart from regressions this flow introduced. <!--#458c1e367e315aa7|3a16cb9889dc135e-->
- `compute_baseline_key` (function) — Builds a deterministic cache key from the git HEAD sha plus a working-tree dirty hash, so any commit or content change invalidates a stale baseline. <!--#8dd9a8fe1224c6b5-->
- `_git_head_sha` (function) — Returns the current git HEAD sha, degrading to the literal "no-head" when the directory isn't a git repo or git is unavailable. <!--#6d07afeb323ea303-->
- `_file_content_hash` (function) — Returns the SHA-256 hex digest of a file's bytes, or None if it can't be read. <!--#857a05eb3f930681-->
- `_working_tree_dirty_hash` (function) — Hashes the working tree's dirty state — the raw `git diff HEAD` plus the names and content hashes of untracked non-ignored files — into a content-sensitive digest. <!--#695425e98c6d4c13-->
- `_git_untracked_files` (function) — Returns the sorted relative paths of untracked, non-ignored files via `git ls-files --others`, or an empty list on failure. <!--#64b04d87e8a279d9-->
- `cache_path` (function) — Returns the on-disk path of the baseline cache file (se3/state/test_baseline_cache.json) under a project root. <!--#c7e65d5b0cdc7682-->
- `_read_cache_entries` (function) — Best-effort reader of the cache's `entries` map that returns an empty dict on any problem (missing/corrupt/wrong-shape/schema-mismatch) so a damaged cache reads as a clean miss. <!--#e5a6072715306eca-->
- `load_cached` (function) — Looks up the cached failing-test-id set for a key, returning a (possibly empty) set on a hit or None on any miss. <!--#e3cd6b779c7a8b44-->
- `save_cache` (function) — Atomically persists a failing-set under a key (preserving other keys, LRU-bounded to MAX_CACHE_ENTRIES) via tempfile + os.replace. <!--#5c020aadea086148-->
- `resolve_baseline_timeout` (function) — Resolves the wall-clock bound for a baseline run by reusing `test.timeout` from se3.yaml, falling back to DEFAULT_BASELINE_TIMEOUT on any config error. <!--#cf0c6e1d36901294-->
- `BaselineCapture` (class) — Class that runs the full test suite as a background subprocess and later resolves the failing-id set, returning the None sentinel when the capture itself failed. <!--#575545a1c87e3780-->
  - `BaselineCapture.__init__` (method) — Initializes the capture's project root, optional command override, and the process/result/timeout bookkeeping state. <!--#496945c492d18e32-->
  - `BaselineCapture.launch` (method) — Starts the background test subprocess (with SE3_TEST_RUNNING=1 to prevent recursion), idempotently and without raising, recording any launch failure for later. <!--#e3d786d17860ee0e-->
  - `BaselineCapture.is_ready` (method) — Returns True when `wait` would resolve without blocking — i.e. the subprocess finished, launch failed, or nothing was ever launched. <!--#cf4e7fa49e0f2d9f-->
  - `BaselineCapture.wait` (method) — Blocks until the capture finishes and returns the cached failing-id set, or None on capture failure, raising TimeoutExpired (resumable) if a timeout is given and hit. <!--#e1642a76f1abaa60-->
  - `BaselineCapture.timed_out` (method) — Reports whether the capture was killed for exceeding its time bound, letting the caller skip a synchronous retry that would just hang again. <!--#f66c64ed5690fb8f-->
  - `BaselineCapture.wait_or_kill` (method) — Bounded wait that kills the subprocess on timeout and resolves to the None sentinel (setting timed_out), instead of leaving the capture resumable like `wait`. <!--#58778a3528d13e61-->
  - `BaselineCapture.kill` (method) — Best-effort, idempotent teardown that terminates and reaps the subprocess, cleans up the temp output file, and marks the capture as a failed (None) measurement. <!--#5d1609d8c4dcd876-->
  - `BaselineCapture._resolve_command` (method) — Resolves the test command from se3.yaml or the test step's auto-detection, ensuring a pytest command carries a verbose flag so per-test results are parseable. <!--#a732a2702ddbe0ce-->
  - `BaselineCapture._parse_result` (method) — Parses the captured output into a failing-id set, returning None when a non-zero exit produced no parseable per-test results (a collection/infra error) to signal fallback. <!--#0b6275a2089ff0ef-->
  - `BaselineCapture._close_stdout_file` (method) — Closes the open stdout temp-file handle, swallowing any OSError. <!--#b5e92b79a12c5410-->
  - `BaselineCapture._cleanup_stdout_file` (method) — Closes and deletes the temp stdout file once it has been read, ignoring errors. <!--#59ca266f4db1a002-->

### `src/se3/engine/test_code_index_concurrency.py` (python) — Co-located pytest suite verifying the code-index's concurrent LLM summariser: config validation of max_concurrency, bounded fan-out that reaches but never exceeds the concurrency cap with one caller per group, serial/concurrent output parity, per-group failure isolation, byte-identical and resumable batched Pass-2 rebuilds, concurrent handling of scattered incremental edits, and correct progress-callback firing. <!--#9a135f4f225a72bb|bbfcb101094aeadd-->
- `_ids_in_prompt` (function) — Helper that extracts the list of node ids embedded in a summariser prompt via a module-level regex. <!--#9a8e067c62be815e-->
- `_EchoCaller` (class) — Deterministic stub LLMCaller that echoes each requested id back as `sum:<id>` and records every constructed instance so tests can prove one caller is built per concurrent group. <!--#7d9075dc679adb6e-->
  - `_EchoCaller.__init__` (method) — Registers each new instance on the class's shared instance list under a lock. <!--#5f2e552e2b28f659-->
  - `_EchoCaller.call` (method) — Returns a JSON map of each prompt id to `sum:<id>`. <!--#2b9cdb94e0fbd974-->
  - `_EchoCaller.reset` (method) — Clears the recorded instance list between tests. <!--#5fc86487a4adf402-->
- `_Recorder` (class) — Builds a stub-caller class that uses a shared counter and a Barrier(workers) to deterministically record peak concurrent in-flight calls and each caller instance. <!--#7f7d1605fd927297-->
  - `_Recorder.__init__` (method) — Initialises the lock, in-flight/peak counters, instance list, and a barrier sized to the expected worker count. <!--#119d80ee5b16bebd-->
  - `_Recorder.caller_cls` (method) — Returns a closure-bound `_BarrierCaller` class whose calls bump the peak counter, rendezvous on the barrier, then return empty JSON. <!--#37e41f5f9bac7c87-->
- `_file_targets` (function) — Factory producing `n` distinct file-level SummaryTargets so each becomes an independent by-file summary group. <!--#a98d7d1f8b796af4-->
- `TestMaxConcurrencyConfig` (class) — Tests that CodeIndexConfig's max_concurrency defaults to four, reads valid values, and falls back with a warning on illegal ones. <!--#ce5a7f60f4834d2b-->
  - `TestMaxConcurrencyConfig.test_default_is_four` (method) — Asserts the default max_concurrency (and its constant) is four across constructor and from_dict. <!--#9b6bdbcccd2f808b-->
  - `TestMaxConcurrencyConfig.test_valid_value_read` (method) — Asserts a valid max_concurrency value is read through from_dict unchanged. <!--#e4c6dc2d40c20677-->
  - `TestMaxConcurrencyConfig.test_illegal_value_falls_back_with_warning` (method) — Parametrised test asserting illegal max_concurrency values revert to four and log a warning. <!--#f3f2f842688847f3-->
- `TestConcurrentSummarizer` (class) — Tests that the LLM summariser fans out correctly — reaching but not exceeding max_concurrency, one caller per group, serial/concurrent parity, and per-group failure isolation. <!--#19adeb3dccf5f749-->
  - `TestConcurrentSummarizer.test_reaches_exactly_max_concurrency` (method) — Asserts that with 2×max groups the peak in-flight count exactly equals max_concurrency and each group builds its own distinct caller. <!--#383240f421da8465-->
  - `TestConcurrentSummarizer.test_serial_when_max_concurrency_one` (method) — Asserts a max_concurrency of one runs strictly serially (peak 1) while still building one caller per group. <!--#687c590f568930f4-->
  - `TestConcurrentSummarizer.test_each_group_builds_its_own_caller` (method) — Asserts six groups yield six distinct, never-shared caller instances. <!--#3d146513c4ea7f28-->
  - `TestConcurrentSummarizer.test_results_identical_serial_vs_concurrent` (method) — Asserts the summariser's id→summary output is identical whether built serially or concurrently. <!--#b2cf9c0c721f3f8b-->
  - `TestConcurrentSummarizer.test_single_group_failure_degrades_to_heuristic` (method) — Asserts one group's caller failure degrades only that group to the `<kind> <name>` heuristic while peers succeed and every id is still returned. <!--#4e252eb15785aa72-->
- `_git` (function) — Helper running a git subcommand in a repo root with output captured and errors raised. <!--#881bf8d1b379498d-->
- `_DeterministicSummarizer` (class) — Injected summariser bypassing the LLM path that returns `S:<name>` per target so md differences are attributable to Pass-2 batching alone. <!--#b18c2289df6ead18-->
  - `_DeterministicSummarizer.__call__` (method) — Returns a map of each target id to `S:<name>`. <!--#1d61334eb28ddb92-->
- `project` (function) — Pytest fixture creating a committed git project with a multi-file `pkg` package and README for exercising multi-batch index builds. <!--#aa0f496400eaea29-->
- `TestBatchedPass2` (class) — Tests that batched Pass-2 summarisation yields byte-identical md across concurrency levels and that a partial flush is a valid incremental resume point. <!--#c434e352e4f839a8-->
  - `TestBatchedPass2.test_md_byte_identical_across_concurrency` (method) — Asserts the generated code-index.md is byte-identical whether built with concurrency 1 or 8. <!--#fecf85e9f821daa9-->
  - `TestBatchedPass2.test_partial_flush_is_a_superset_resume_point` (method) — Asserts an unchanged incremental rebuild reuses every already-summarised node and hands the summariser no targets. <!--#61460bd575d9cc6d-->
- `_ScatterRecorder` (class) — Peak-concurrency recorder that gates only the summary calls for a known set of edited files on a barrier, proving scattered incremental edits batch together and run concurrently rather than being serialised. <!--#02a4420e0f199d92-->
  - `_ScatterRecorder.__init__` (method) — Initialises the edited-path set, counters, and a barrier sized to the edited count. <!--#3e05bea13f08f97d-->
  - `_ScatterRecorder.caller_cls` (method) — Returns a caller class that gates prompts matching an edited path on the barrier (tracking peak) and always echoes id summaries. <!--#3067b2d46df01891-->
- `TestIncrementalConcurrency` (class) — Tests that the incremental commit-time rebuild reaches max_concurrency even when edited files are scattered across the sorted file list. <!--#1db1ee18a928e247-->
  - `TestIncrementalConcurrency.test_scattered_incremental_edits_run_concurrently` (method) — Regression test asserting three scattered edited files summarise concurrently (peak equals edit count), which positional batching would have serialised to peak 1. <!--#8da83bb8d9f06ac8-->
- `TestProgressCallback` (class) — Tests the build's progress callback fires once per stale file/dir node, reports body-only edits at file granularity, is a no-op when omitted, and stays silent on fully-reused builds. <!--#12160670cc6faa76-->
  - `TestProgressCallback.test_fires_once_per_file_and_dir_node` (method) — Asserts a forced build fires exactly one monotonic callback per file/dir node with constant total and file phase preceding dir phase. <!--#f632cf62339de46c-->
  - `TestProgressCallback.test_body_only_edit_still_reports_its_file` (method) — Regression test asserting a body-only edit still reports its file at file granularity exactly once even though the file node is reused. <!--#acc26694ab906219-->
  - `TestProgressCallback.test_progress_none_is_noop` (method) — Asserts omitting the progress callback still produces the md file without error. <!--#7827272b623aefb0-->
  - `TestProgressCallback.test_no_callback_for_fully_reused_build` (method) — Asserts a no-change incremental rebuild fires zero progress callbacks. <!--#fe40f1c086abc140-->
- `TestRecordIndexProgress` (class) — Tests the chat_history record_index_progress writer — correct jsonl records, exclusion from step/retry history, soft no-op on missing ids, and swallowed OSErrors. <!--#22d68fd86aba06a9-->
  - `TestRecordIndexProgress.test_write_and_history_retry_skip` (method) — Asserts index_progress records are written to jsonl but skipped by step-history and retry-context reads. <!--#c2a47334e492305d-->
  - `TestRecordIndexProgress.test_missing_ids_soft_noop` (method) — Asserts recording progress with empty flow/step ids writes nothing. <!--#96298e0389492ff0-->
  - `TestRecordIndexProgress.test_oserror_is_swallowed` (method) — Asserts a write-path OSError is warned-and-swallowed rather than propagated. <!--#63f1b52fc5f6201e-->
- `TestEnsureCodeIndexFreshProgress` (class) — Tests the real ensure_code_index_fresh hook — silent without flow context and emitting index_progress history when given commit flow/step context. <!--#cd5e081cffa9b063-->
  - `TestEnsureCodeIndexFreshProgress._build_with_echo` (method) — Helper that runs a forced build using the _EchoCaller stub. <!--#16f403ade6c3de42-->
  - `TestEnsureCodeIndexFreshProgress.test_no_flow_context_is_noop` (method) — Asserts refreshing without flow/step context writes no history and never raises. <!--#acef2384f7aeb96c-->
  - `TestEnsureCodeIndexFreshProgress.test_commit_context_writes_progress` (method) — Asserts a stale-file refresh under commit context writes well-formed monotonic index_progress records that stay out of the session history. <!--#cc14cd077ce7eb48-->

### `src/se3/engine/test_code_index_degrade.py` (python) — Co-located unit tests pinning the code-index degrade mode: the three-condition (text + structure-less + over-threshold) eligibility gate, line/byte-based chunking into degraded 'chunk' units, and the DEGRADED_MARKER render annotation. <!--#66c3611511c6f6b5|71775928e2399a22-->
- `_small_cfg` (function) — Test helper returning a CodeIndexConfig with tiny line/chunk thresholds so tests can trip degrade with only a few lines. <!--#53bc45df86825aa9-->
- `TestDegradeGate` (class) — Test class covering when a file becomes degrade-eligible — the three-condition gate and independent byte-threshold triggering. <!--#d0d6098b67194f0e-->
  - `TestDegradeGate.test_all_three_conditions_required` (method) — Asserts degrade eligibility requires structure-less AND over-threshold, voided by either having structure or being under threshold. <!--#2199039eeb4e2357-->
  - `TestDegradeGate.test_byte_threshold_trips_independently` (method) — Verifies the byte-size threshold can trip degrade on its own, even for a single-line file under the line threshold. <!--#46459083602a0c70-->
- `TestChunking` (class) — Test class covering chunk production: per-chunk line limits, degraded marking, and file-level vs chunked indexing outcomes including render output. <!--#ed0c09850d45ad3e-->
  - `TestChunking.test_chunks_respect_line_limit_and_mark_degraded` (method) — Checks _chunk_degraded splits text into degraded 'chunk' units that each stay within the configured chunk_lines limit. <!--#e1f3a47db522d4b6-->
  - `TestChunking.test_small_structureless_file_stops_at_file_level` (method) — Verifies a small structure-less file stays a single file-level text entry with no chunk symbols. <!--#6740dfa1b46eb647-->
  - `TestChunking.test_large_structureless_file_degrades_to_chunks` (method) — Verifies a large structure-less file is indexed into degraded chunk symbols. <!--#95e53b825cb305cd-->
  - `TestChunking.test_degraded_marker_in_render` (method) — Confirms the DEGRADED_MARKER appears in the rendered output for a degraded, chunked file. <!--#5fcb0faef565ff1c-->

### `src/se3/engine/test_e2e.py` (python) — End-to-end test suite for the flow engine that drives full task flows (documentation, feature, bugfix) to completion with mocked LLM/subprocess handlers, verifying interruption/resume, error recovery, persistence consistency, and correct wiring of worktree merge steps (merge_integrate + version_reconcile) against both stubbed and real integrate/reconcile libraries. <!--#dc521d517aa531eb|a927f89f92d6fe19-->
- `MockSubprocessResult` (class) — Test double mimicking a subprocess.run result with stdout, stderr, and returncode attributes. <!--#7cd9e8f256499683-->
  - `MockSubprocessResult.__init__` (method) — Initializes the mock subprocess result with given stdout, stderr, and returncode defaults. <!--#a5da8ba30e1e20a5-->
- `create_mock_llm_responses` (function) — Helper returning a dict of canned LLM responses keyed by StepType for a documentation-task flow. <!--#03aedc206121439a-->
- `TestEndToEndSmallTask` (class) — Test class covering a small task's full flow execution and its interruption/resume behavior. <!--#68c4ca59b6e8986c-->
  - `TestEndToEndSmallTask.test_complete_small_flow` (method) — Runs a small documentation flow with mocked subprocess and handlers, asserting it reaches COMPLETED. <!--#c26ddf8f7d77721a-->
  - `TestEndToEndSmallTask.test_flow_with_interruption` (method) — Saves a flow, recreates fresh manager/state-machine instances, and asserts the flow resumes from persistence. <!--#6a17973c7dc1db29-->
- `TestRealWorldScenarios` (class) — Test class exercising realistic feature-request and bugfix flows end to end. <!--#7f1bc8fab797c09f-->
  - `TestRealWorldScenarios.test_feature_request_flow` (method) — Drives a feature-task flow through all steps and asserts completion with at least five steps taken. <!--#9581d9848cdc769c-->
  - `TestRealWorldScenarios.test_bugfix_flow` (method) — Drives a bugfix-task flow to completion using success handlers for every step type. <!--#993335182c66a65a-->
- `TestErrorRecovery` (class) — Test class covering step-failure recovery and state consistency across persistence cycles. <!--#aa6f34f92cacf389-->
  - `TestErrorRecovery.test_recovery_after_step_failure` (method) — Uses a flaky handler that fails once then succeeds to verify a retried step recovers to COMPLETED. <!--#5fa7662358f09216-->
  - `TestErrorRecovery.test_state_consistency_across_persistence` (method) — Progresses and saves a flow, then reloads in fresh instances to assert step outputs and current step survive intact. <!--#dc2c8d56fc423f1f-->
- `TestWorktreeMergeSteps` (class) — End-to-end test suite proving the merge-side steps (merge_integrate + version_reconcile) of a worktree flow are correctly wired into the state machine, mostly with stubbed integrate/reconcile libraries plus one test against the real libraries in a temp git repo. <!--#d4380baf40daa5e8-->
  - `TestWorktreeMergeSteps._register_mock_handlers` (method) — Helper that registers pass-through mock handlers for every step type, optionally keeping the real merge_integrate and version_reconcile handlers so only those two steps do real work. <!--#e2ae0cc40d3b8510-->
  - `TestWorktreeMergeSteps._fake_integrate_result` (method) — Helper returning a canned successful integrate() result namespace for the given branch, used to stub the merge library in wiring tests. <!--#a6689b7c8161b6f4-->
  - `TestWorktreeMergeSteps._fake_reconcile_result` (method) — Helper returning a canned successful ReconcileResult (base 11.12.0 → final 11.13.0, minor bump) used to stub the reconcile library. <!--#65e99a2c0b24f533-->
  - `TestWorktreeMergeSteps._make_worktree_flow` (method) — Fixture that initializes a real git repo at project_root and creates a small worktree-mode flow with mock handlers, returning the state machine and flow. <!--#829ad362f6bf8cfd-->
  - `TestWorktreeMergeSteps._run_to_completion` (method) — Helper that drives the state machine step-by-step until the flow completes, fails, or hits a max-steps cap, returning the number of steps run. <!--#b68412ecd5757fe4-->
  - `TestWorktreeMergeSteps.test_worktree_sequence_appends_merge_steps` (method) — Asserts a worktree flow's step sequence places merge_integrate then version_reconcile immediately after commit (before any post-commit step), while a non-worktree flow gets neither. <!--#7dc69744016e298a-->
  - `TestWorktreeMergeSteps.test_analyze_rederive_preserves_worktree_merge_steps` (method) — Regression test that the analyze step's from-scratch sequence rebuild retains the two worktree merge steps in the post-commit position and still omits them for non-worktree flows. <!--#3dc87d74b39bc2b5-->
  - `TestWorktreeMergeSteps.test_worktree_flow_runs_to_reconcile_on_master` (method) — Drives a worktree flow to completion with stubbed integrate/reconcile, asserting integrate ran once (no delete/lock), reconcile produced the final version, and the reconcile step recorded the expected outputs. <!--#2250ba9a7768fb2d-->
  - `TestWorktreeMergeSteps._git` (method) — Thin helper running a git subcommand in the given repo root with output capture and check=True. <!--#77ab30c76cd20b87-->
  - `TestWorktreeMergeSteps._make_real_git_project` (method) — Fixture building a committed git project plus a feature branch carrying a committed version-intent (changelog bullet + minor hint), mirroring a de-versioned worktree session, returning the default branch name. <!--#bf63be982d86a45b-->
  - `TestWorktreeMergeSteps.test_worktree_merge_steps_land_real_version_on_master` (method) — Integration test driving the merge steps through the REAL integrate/reconcile libraries in a temp git repo, asserting the branch actually lands on master and a real version (11.13.0) with VERSIONS.md entry and session trailer is written. <!--#97f2aeb1d53b8b40-->
  - `TestWorktreeMergeSteps.test_integrate_failure_does_not_reach_reconcile` (method) — Asserts that when integrate() fails (conflict), merge_integrate ends FAILED, version_reconcile is never invoked, and the flow does not complete. <!--#431f1d24cbe3a413-->
  - `TestWorktreeMergeSteps.test_resume_between_merge_steps_only_reruns_reconcile` (method) — Simulates a crash after merge_integrate completes, then resumes in a fresh state machine and asserts integrate is not re-run while only reconcile executes to completion. <!--#667deb626c19445d-->
  - `TestWorktreeMergeSteps.test_per_step_confirm_gates_only_version_decision` (method) — Asserts a per-step human confirmation configured for version_reconcile inserts a CONFIRM step only after version_reconcile, not after the expensive merge_integrate. <!--#632ba3be298b07e5-->

### `src/se3/engine/test_engine.py` (python) — Unit test suite for the flow engine covering data models (Step/FlowInstance serialization and default step sequences), PersistenceManager save/load, StateMachine lifecycle and handler dispatch, crash/mid-step recovery, full state transitions with retries, and post-charter-refactor step routing across all six task types. <!--#72b5360fb7a64104|56405d63d534b602-->
- `TestModels` (class) — Tests the engine's data models — Step/FlowInstance creation, serialization round-trips, progress, and the default step sequences for each task type. <!--#2c8637eed9528cb4-->
  - `TestModels.test_step_creation` (method) — Asserts a freshly created Step has the given type, PENDING status, and a string step_id. <!--#03395a96573ee1e6-->
  - `TestModels.test_step_serialization` (method) — Verifies a Step survives a to_dict/from_dict round-trip with type, status, inputs, and outputs intact. <!--#847efa99565cc90a-->
  - `TestModels.test_flow_instance_creation` (method) — Checks a new FlowInstance gets a well-formed dated flow_id, INIT status, and the supplied task description. <!--#bbbccfb954c27a8e-->
  - `TestModels.test_flow_progress` (method) — Confirms get_progress reports completed-over-total counts as steps are added and completed. <!--#5a57696221608554-->
  - `TestModels.test_flow_serialization` (method) — Verifies a FlowInstance with a step survives a to_dict/from_dict round-trip preserving its fields and steps. <!--#b4bbc96f9e25d2e2-->
  - `TestModels.test_default_step_sequences` (method) — Sanity-checks that feature/bugfix/small default sequences contain (or omit) the expected step types and relative lengths. <!--#6f246bdfcbcd5390-->
  - `TestModels.test_charter_refactor_sequences_exact` (method) — Pins each task type's default step sequence to its exact post-charter-refactor ordering. <!--#8023d8e832c3ea50-->
  - `TestModels.test_retired_spec_steps_absent_from_all_sequences` (method) — Asserts the retired spec-governance step types appear in no default sequence. <!--#016a1658f709e362-->
  - `TestModels.test_invariant_check_placement` (method) — Verifies INVARIANT_CHECK and CHARTER_FRESHNESS sit at the correct positions relative to SELF_CHECK and VERSION_ANALYZE across task types. <!--#71c5713dc899cdd2-->
  - `TestModels.test_default_sequences_end_with_summarize` (method) — Asserts SUMMARIZE is the single final step of every default sequence (right after COMMIT for non-review types) and that the unknown-type fallback matches feature. <!--#8be39b0610d798b8-->
- `TestPersistence` (class) — Tests the PersistenceManager — saving/loading flows, atomic writes, listing active flows, and context file round-trips. <!--#4bbcf88fcd7adab4-->
  - `TestPersistence.test_save_and_load` (method) — Verifies a saved flow can be reloaded with its flow_id and task description preserved. <!--#3a7087926038fa1e-->
  - `TestPersistence.test_atomic_write` (method) — Confirms save_flow produces a state file containing valid JSON with the flow_id. <!--#0f06ae9a3d0f3632-->
  - `TestPersistence.test_list_active_flows` (method) — Checks list_active_flows returns the saved flow's metadata. <!--#01e519333ee00894-->
  - `TestPersistence.test_context_save_load` (method) — Verifies an se3_context dict survives save_context/load_context unchanged. <!--#1d9f448bcf942230-->
- `TestStateMachine` (class) — Tests StateMachine flow lifecycle — create, load-or-create/resume, step transitions, handler dispatch, and on_running callback timing. <!--#e8a8b124e6e68691-->
  - `TestStateMachine.test_create_flow` (method) — Asserts create_flow seeds a flow with the task fields, INIT status, selected steps, and a current step id. <!--#b91b112b6d75210c-->
  - `TestStateMachine.test_load_or_create_new` (method) — Confirms load_or_create_flow creates a fresh flow when none exists (not resumed). <!--#e32b5e7e0542ec9b-->
  - `TestStateMachine.test_load_or_create_resume` (method) — Confirms load_or_create_flow resumes a previously persisted flow by id. <!--#0a45052783b903ee-->
  - `TestStateMachine.test_transition_to_next` (method) — Verifies completing the current step advances the state machine to a different next step. <!--#ffd1afc71976d503-->
  - `TestStateMachine.test_run_step_with_handler` (method) — Checks a registered handler runs, sets outputs, and returns COMPLETED. <!--#5e6c1ac4b9d43d26-->
  - `TestStateMachine.test_run_step_no_handler` (method) — Confirms a step with no registered handler fails gracefully with an explanatory error message. <!--#8c9a60b7097ad62a-->
  - `TestStateMachine.test_run_step_on_running_called_after_running` (method) — Verifies on_running fires exactly once, after the step enters RUNNING and before the handler executes. <!--#9e3d591a85955740-->
  - `TestStateMachine.test_run_step_on_running_not_called_without_handler` (method) — Confirms on_running is never invoked when a step fails before entering RUNNING due to a missing handler. <!--#bd686d879e5dbd5b-->
- `TestRecovery` (class) — Tests interrupt/crash recovery — resuming flows after a simulated crash, mid-step interruption, and scanning for multiple persisted flows. <!--#54dd5e46dc1d60b5-->
  - `TestRecovery.test_recovery_after_crash` (method) — Verifies a new StateMachine resumes a persisted flow and restores the current step after a simulated crash. <!--#706a66871174803d-->
  - `TestRecovery.test_recovery_mid_step` (method) — Confirms a flow interrupted with a RUNNING step reloads with that step's status and type intact. <!--#fa1a380956ed7259-->
  - `TestRecovery.test_multiple_flow_recovery` (method) — Checks that saved flow state files can be discovered by scanning the state directory. <!--#eb6761daf283ad9f-->
- `TestStateTransitions` (class) — Tests full-flow state transitions — driving to completion, the completion step-index semantics, resuming a completed flow, failure handling, and retries. <!--#e6f4f99f9adb1214-->
  - `TestStateTransitions.test_complete_flow_transitions` (method) — Drives a small flow through every step with mock handlers and asserts it reaches COMPLETED. <!--#370ba5bbabad6678-->
  - `TestStateTransitions.test_completion_advances_step_index_to_total` (method) — Verifies completion advances current_step_index to the total step count for unified total/total progress reporting. <!--#3e7c9a2d219c8fbc-->
  - `TestStateTransitions.test_resume_completed_flow_does_not_raise` (method) — Confirms transition_to_next on an already-completed flow self-heals the out-of-range index instead of raising. <!--#b5fed906e3c98d54-->
  - `TestStateTransitions.test_failed_step_handling` (method) — Checks a failing handler yields FAILED with its error message preserved. <!--#aa0be9352513d1c1-->
  - `TestStateTransitions.test_retry_mechanism` (method) — Verifies a flaky handler fails first then succeeds on retry after incrementing retry_count. <!--#3ba498c0505da1cb-->
- `TestCharterRefactorRouting` (class) — G6 routing tests — all six task sequences run to completion, INVARIANT_CHECK joins the implement fix loop (sharing the iteration bound), CHARTER_FRESHNESS stays non-blocking, and invariant anchors freeze once. <!--#94923d3210bb6f78-->
  - `TestCharterRefactorRouting._run_to_completion` (method) — Helper that drives a flow through run_step/transition_to_next until it leaves RUNNING or hits a step cap. <!--#14cd253743bf4b15-->
  - `TestCharterRefactorRouting.test_all_six_sequences_run_through` (method) — Asserts every task type's default sequence drives to COMPLETED with mock handlers. <!--#6be306d739d495d7-->
  - `TestCharterRefactorRouting.test_invariant_check_revision_routes_to_implement_fix_loop` (method) — Verifies an INVARIANT_CHECK REVISION_NEEDED routes back to IMPLEMENT, bumps the fix iteration, and re-runs to completion. <!--#95614723fa7eb6b7-->
  - `TestCharterRefactorRouting.test_invariant_check_shares_max_fix_iterations_exhaustion` (method) — Confirms an always-failing INVARIANT_CHECK exhausts the shared fix-iteration bound and fails the flow. <!--#8e19b6d57a6af023-->
  - `TestCharterRefactorRouting.test_charter_freshness_is_non_blocking` (method) — Verifies CHARTER_FRESHNESS advisory output never diverts the flow into a fix loop. <!--#b1bab9680a232e89-->
  - `TestCharterRefactorRouting.test_freeze_invariant_anchors_idempotent` (method) — Confirms invariant anchors are frozen once at flow start and not re-read on a subsequent init. <!--#005ac88de9bbd6e7-->
- `TestKnowledgeGuardIntegration` (class) — End-to-end, state-machine-level integration test class (G6) exercising the two knowledge guards (charter_freshness closed loop and invariant_check WHY-comment guard) through real routing across feature/small task-type sequences. <!--#bd2a3394077b5a14-->
  - `TestKnowledgeGuardIntegration._write_charter` (method) — Helper that writes the given charter text to `se3/charter.md` under a temp root, creating the `se3` dir as needed. <!--#7a33974ce77c7a9c-->
  - `TestKnowledgeGuardIntegration._install_fake_caller` (method) — Helper that monkeypatches charter_freshness's LLMCaller with a queued-response fake, returning a state dict recording prompts, remaining responses, and call count. <!--#b40ebb8b515a0a76-->
  - `TestKnowledgeGuardIntegration._propose` (method) — Helper building the JSON string for charter_freshness's propose-stage LLM response (whether an update is needed plus the patch/reason/suggestion). <!--#1ebb5829bfe8d635-->
  - `TestKnowledgeGuardIntegration._gate` (method) — Helper building the JSON string for charter_freshness's gate-stage LLM response (admitted flag plus any violations/weakened removals). <!--#6e7ec8a4873af7de-->
  - `TestKnowledgeGuardIntegration._register_recording_mocks` (method) — Helper that registers a COMPLETED-returning mock handler for every StepType, with IMPLEMENT publishing `files_changed` so charter_freshness receives a non-empty diff. <!--#67f029d7899ba1e1-->
  - `TestKnowledgeGuardIntegration._drive` (method) — Helper that runs a flow to a terminal status, appending each executed step's type (including fix-loop re-runs) to an order list and returning the step count. <!--#1d543338d16611ff-->
  - `TestKnowledgeGuardIntegration._make_flow` (method) — Helper that creates and initializes a flow for a given task type, pinning change_path/project_root to tmp_path and skipping the pre-implement baseline subprocess. <!--#7391d7dc5fecf711-->
  - `TestKnowledgeGuardIntegration._charter_step` (method) — Helper that finds and returns the CHARTER_FRESHNESS step object within a flow's state. <!--#b67ffd33fefd2658-->
  - `TestKnowledgeGuardIntegration.test_charter_auto_update_does_not_reflow_completed_review_steps` (method) — Test asserting a passing charter_freshness gate rewrites the on-disk charter and advances straight to version_analyze→commit→summarize without re-running any completed review step or bumping the fix counter. <!--#b9a15f761819aaa3-->
  - `TestKnowledgeGuardIntegration.test_charter_freshness_stays_advisory_without_invariant_check_in_sequence` (method) — Test asserting that in the 'small' sequence (no invariant_check) charter_freshness stays advisory — one propose call, no gate, disk unchanged, degraded_reason set — yet the flow still completes. <!--#62cadaccec039782-->
  - `TestKnowledgeGuardIntegration.test_why_comment_deletion_routes_shared_fix_loop_and_coexists_with_charter_update` (method) — Test asserting a WHY-comment-deletion REVISION_NEEDED from invariant_check rides the shared implement fix loop (re-running implement/invariant, bumping fix_iteration) and then coexists with a successful charter auto-update in one completing flow. <!--#95d4b87a9da8d022-->
  - `TestKnowledgeGuardIntegration.test_why_comment_deletion_respects_shared_max_fix_iterations_bound` (method) — Test asserting an always-failing WHY-deletion invariant_check exhausts the shared max_fix_iterations bound and FAILs the flow before charter_freshness runs, leaving no LLM call and the charter untouched. <!--#cd43aa7606490351-->
- `TestStreamProgressHistory` (class) — Tests chat-history streaming — recording partial stream_progress lines, skipping them in step-history/retry reads, tolerating truncated tails, and the daemon reader's incremental cursor. <!--#a363e783bac8dd94-->
  - `TestStreamProgressHistory._step` (method) — Helper returning a jsonl step id following the NN_<step_type>_<hash> naming convention. <!--#b2fbb608bc784187-->

  - `TestStreamProgressHistory.test_get_step_history_skips_stream_progress` (method) — Confirms get_step_history keeps only the prompt and final assistant turn, dropping partial stream_progress lines. <!--#f9ee72edeaa284b2-->
  - `TestStreamProgressHistory.test_format_history_for_retry_skips_stream_progress` (method) — Confirms retry-history formatting excludes partial stream_progress content. <!--#c1f8e3d6efdcd154-->
  - `TestStreamProgressHistory.test_truncated_last_line_does_not_break_reads` (method) — Verifies a half-written final jsonl line is skipped while earlier valid lines still parse. <!--#f5d4718ca082e024-->
  - `TestStreamProgressHistory.test_read_flow_incremental_cursor_over_progress` (method) — Tests the daemon reader advancing its per-file cursor across progress lines in full then append mode without losing or duplicating records. <!--#cca0aa5c5f344548-->
- `TestStreamJSONTrackerUsage` (class) — Tests StreamJSONTracker capturing token usage and cost from result NDJSON lines, ignoring non-result/malformed input, and folding into the step accumulator. <!--#7710f60803b78ce3-->
  - `TestStreamJSONTrackerUsage._tracker` (method) — Helper constructing a StreamJSONTracker with no flow/step ids for usage inspection only. <!--#73cf77f02be4a2ce-->
  - `TestStreamJSONTrackerUsage.test_usage_starts_empty` (method) — Asserts a fresh tracker's usage is empty. <!--#e1a4ebf237f4a732-->
  - `TestStreamJSONTrackerUsage.test_capture_nested_message_usage_and_top_cost` (method) — Verifies the tracker captures nested message usage fields plus the top-level cost. <!--#354c29ee4f024f8e-->
  - `TestStreamJSONTrackerUsage.test_capture_top_level_usage` (method) — Confirms the tracker reads usage from a top-level usage object. <!--#6f17822ee8d28bae-->
  - `TestStreamJSONTrackerUsage.test_result_without_usage_stays_zero` (method) — Checks a result line lacking usage leaves the tracker empty. <!--#b991e5b85866e059-->
  - `TestStreamJSONTrackerUsage.test_result_partial_usage_fields_default_zero` (method) — Verifies missing usage subfields default to zero while present ones are captured. <!--#e8a9c46bbba779ca-->
  - `TestStreamJSONTrackerUsage.test_malformed_usage_does_not_raise` (method) — Confirms a non-dict usage payload is swallowed without error, leaving usage empty. <!--#875205ac5b9566cd-->
  - `TestStreamJSONTrackerUsage.test_non_result_lines_do_not_set_usage` (method) — Asserts non-result (e.g. assistant) lines never populate usage. <!--#e7854b203b319e93-->
  - `TestStreamJSONTrackerUsage.test_invalid_json_silently_skipped` (method) — Confirms invalid JSON input is silently ignored, leaving usage empty. <!--#fff839677424149a-->
  - `TestStreamJSONTrackerUsage.test_capture_integrates_with_step_accumulator` (method) — Verifies tracker usage folds into a step scope via add_call_usage, summing across repeated calls. <!--#64a3acc4b5683ba7-->
- `TestSessionTokenUsageModel` (class) — Tests State.session_token_usage — default emptiness, serialization round-trip as a primitive dict, backward compatibility with old engine.json, and non-interference with other fields. <!--#4596b53ce8081225-->
  - `TestSessionTokenUsageModel.test_default_session_usage_is_empty` (method) — Asserts a default State has empty session token usage. <!--#c8def32349991da0-->
  - `TestSessionTokenUsageModel.test_session_usage_round_trips` (method) — Verifies session_token_usage survives a FlowInstance to_dict/from_dict round-trip across all fields. <!--#e314c7685cc50e1a-->
  - `TestSessionTokenUsageModel.test_session_usage_serializes_as_primitive_dict` (method) — Confirms session_token_usage serializes to a JSON-primitive dict that survives a json round-trip. <!--#51fd2f84c0b404f5-->
  - `TestSessionTokenUsageModel.test_old_engine_json_without_field_loads_empty` (method) — Checks loading an older engine.json lacking the field yields empty session usage. <!--#61bf693011e6f93d-->
  - `TestSessionTokenUsageModel.test_other_state_fields_unaffected_by_round_trip` (method) — Verifies fix_iterations and baseline_failures survive a round-trip alongside session usage. <!--#a28fb1946aae9a31-->
- `TestRunStepTokenAggregation` (class) — Tests run_step folding per-step token usage into step.outputs and session totals, including multi-call merges, no-call cases, exceptions, and non-terminal (paused/revision) carry-over without double-counting. <!--#c2a8a9257880d762-->
  - `TestRunStepTokenAggregation._make_usage` (method) — Helper constructing a UsageTotals from keyword fields. <!--#61d9bd91f9c0d33a-->
  - `TestRunStepTokenAggregation.test_single_step_merges_multiple_calls` (method) — Verifies two calls within one step merge into the step's token_usage and the session total. <!--#c39903bd03e6bf4d-->
  - `TestRunStepTokenAggregation.test_no_call_step_writes_no_usage_field` (method) — Confirms a step making no LLM call writes no token_usage field and leaves the session total empty. <!--#f7afd427ad3b2dbf-->
  - `TestRunStepTokenAggregation.test_multi_step_session_accumulation` (method) — Verifies the session total equals the sum of usage across multiple separately-run steps. <!--#d0f0e4c88a4e0921-->
  - `TestRunStepTokenAggregation.test_exception_step_still_aggregates_and_resets_scope` (method) — Confirms a raising handler still records usage gathered before the raise and resets the step scope (no contextvar leak). <!--#498168edce99d8ce-->
  - `TestRunStepTokenAggregation.test_paused_run_usage_carried_into_next_emitted_record` (method) — Verifies paused rounds publish both token_usage and carried_token_usage, the final round sums all rounds and clears the carry, and the session total stays consistent. <!--#2a522c6d2150f888-->
  - `TestRunStepTokenAggregation.test_aggregated_usage_survives_persistence` (method) — Confirms both step-level and session token usage round-trip through engine.json persistence. <!--#e87aadc8e5ee2ef4-->
  - `TestRunStepTokenAggregation.test_revision_needed_step_publishes_visible_token_usage` (method) — Verifies a REVISION_NEEDED step publishes visible token_usage (the G2 fix) alongside carried_token_usage. <!--#23c0cc57791d6903-->
  - `TestRunStepTokenAggregation.test_non_terminal_then_terminal_usage_equals_sum_of_rounds` (method) — Confirms after a revision then a completion round the terminal token_usage and session total equal the sum of both rounds' increments. <!--#a6bfda3a51da181c-->
  - `TestRunStepTokenAggregation.test_session_usage_not_duplicated_by_combined_totals` (method) — Verifies the session total sums each round's per-round increment rather than combined carry totals, avoiding double-counting across re-entries. <!--#5fd1b8051bd165b1-->

### `src/se3/engine/test_steps.py` (python) — Integration test suite (with mocked LLM/git/subprocess) for the flow engine's step handlers — analyze classification, pass/fail TEST runs, and commit — with heavy coverage of the de-versioning behaviour where worktree flows emit provisional VersionIntent files and bump-decorated messages while synchronous flows keep authoritative versions and Version: lines, plus a commit in-lock race guard that re-analyzes on concurrent version drift. <!--#99b3e6da37376ce3|be2ca97423c25743-->
- `TestAnalyzeStep` (class) — Test suite for the analyze step handler's classification output and error handling. <!--#e870f470662e8935-->
  - `TestAnalyzeStep.test_analyze_success` (method) — Asserts a successful analyze produces task_type/scope/complexity classification plus empty retired spec-selection outputs and never the legacy selected_specs key. <!--#3c0c7d552674801d-->
  - `TestAnalyzeStep.test_analyze_invalid_json` (method) — Asserts analyze fails (with an error message) when the LLM returns unparseable JSON. <!--#da519831bd138dbe-->
  - `TestAnalyzeStep.test_analyze_llm_error` (method) — Asserts analyze fails when the LLM call itself raises an LLMCallError. <!--#9b9696993d33a034-->
- `TestTestStep` (class) — Test class verifying the TEST step handler's pass/fail behavior, including a fixture that pre-warms the git-probe cache and clears SE3_TEST_RUNNING so the tests work in isolation and under self-invocation. <!--#a89bc65d365d4e41-->
  - `TestTestStep._warm_main_repo_root_cache` (method) — Autouse fixture that pre-warms the main-repo-root lru_cache before subprocess.Popen is patched and clears the SE3_TEST_RUNNING sentinel so the test step exercises its real path. <!--#03bbcfc0e5740790-->
  - `TestTestStep.test_test_success` (method) — Asserts a zero-exit pytest run completes the test step and records test_results. <!--#9549f65cd5ea7dcc-->
  - `TestTestStep.test_test_failure` (method) — Asserts an unparseable non-zero pytest failure is treated as introduced (blocking) and returns REVISION_NEEDED. <!--#b51593f06f5def18-->
- `TestCommitStep` (class) — Test class for the COMMIT step handler, covering a successful commit on the pure-git path (version bumping disabled) and the no-changes case. <!--#ebbda85c20f34607-->
  - `TestCommitStep.test_commit_success` (method) — Verifies commit_handler returns COMPLETED by mocking git calls dispatched by subcommand with version bumping disabled. <!--#5acc02711e1bcd11-->
  - `TestCommitStep.test_commit_no_changes` (method) — Asserts the commit handler completes successfully even when git reports no changes. <!--#441ea7bef6ef446b-->
- `TestVersionAnalyzeDeVersioning` (class) — Test class verifying that in worktree mode version_analyze emits a provisional VersionIntent file rather than an authoritative suggested_version, while synchronous (non-worktree) flows retain their old authoritative-version behaviour. <!--#5c99e02d4e2c12c4-->
  - `TestVersionAnalyzeDeVersioning._run` (method) — Helper that runs version_analyze_handler with a mocked LLMCaller against a temp-dir flow (worktree toggle) and returns the flow, step, and result. <!--#95560f58ab1b9ec5-->
  - `TestVersionAnalyzeDeVersioning.test_worktree_flow_emits_intent_and_no_authoritative_version` (method) — Asserts a worktree flow persists a VersionIntent (provisional version, bump hint, baseline, changelog, non-empty change_summary) and exposes no authoritative suggested_version. <!--#02e984308b107795-->
  - `TestVersionAnalyzeDeVersioning.test_worktree_intent_body_complete_without_usable_bump_type` (method) — Asserts that even when the LLM omits bump_type (custom versioning scheme), the intent's substance—change_summary and versions_changes—remains complete. <!--#6ee852488f0317dc-->
  - `TestVersionAnalyzeDeVersioning.test_synchronous_flow_keeps_authoritative_version` (method) — Asserts a non-worktree flow still exposes the authoritative suggested_version and writes no VersionIntent file. <!--#54d6f86f33083468-->
- `TestCommitDeVersioning` (class) — Test class verifying the commit step's de-versioning behavior: worktree flows only decorate the message with bump-intent (e.g. "(minor bump)") while skipping any version-file write or "Version:" line, synchronous flows keep the version line, and discovery flows are prefixed with the real analyzed type rather than "discovery:". <!--#876296f85fd9697a-->
  - `TestCommitDeVersioning._fake_git` (method) — Helper returning a fake subprocess.run side-effect that stubs git status/commit/rev-parse and captures the commit message. <!--#41664d63231a0f0d-->
  - `TestCommitDeVersioning.test_worktree_commit_skips_version_and_docs` (method) — Asserts that with version bumping enabled but in worktree mode, the commit never touches the version file and stamps no Version: line, only the bump decoration. <!--#7d18d60756c6bec6-->
  - `TestCommitDeVersioning.test_worktree_commit_message_has_no_version_line` (method) — Unit-tests _generate_commit_message with new_version=None (worktree path) to confirm the bump decoration appears but no Version: line. <!--#7182fc4b4c03de94-->
  - `TestCommitDeVersioning.test_synchronous_commit_message_keeps_version_line` (method) — Contrast unit test confirming _generate_commit_message with a written version still includes the Version: line for synchronous flows. <!--#8d22481f45e51b90-->
  - `TestCommitDeVersioning.test_discovery_flow_commit_prefix_uses_real_analyzed_type` (method) — Asserts that a discovery flow with an `analyzed_type` of "feature" in state context produces a commit message prefixed "feature:" via effective_task_type, never "discovery:". <!--#f4a777db8a1128be-->
  - `TestCommitDeVersioning.test_discovery_flow_without_analyzed_type_falls_back_to_feature` (method) — Asserts that a discovery flow lacking any `analyzed_type` still avoids a "discovery:" prefix and degrades gracefully to a "feature:" commit-subject prefix. <!--#e37d3fde0bc9dc38-->
- `TestCommitVersionRaceGuard` (class) — Tests the commit step's in-lock version race guard: when the on-disk version has drifted past the version version_analyze observed (a concurrent flow bumped first), version_analyze is re-run against the drifted baseline so the stale suggested version is never written, while an undrifted disk writes the resolved target unchanged. <!--#f40a35a58b4ff071-->
  - `TestCommitVersionRaceGuard._fake_git` (method) — Helper returning a fake subprocess.run side-effect stubbing git status/commit/rev-parse and capturing the commit message. <!--#ff5591844863b501-->
  - `TestCommitVersionRaceGuard._make_flow_with_version_analyze` (method) — Helper building a non-worktree flow carrying a completed version_analyze step with configurable observed current_version and baseline. <!--#6d93bf332c9e07ce-->
  - `TestCommitVersionRaceGuard._make_commit_step` (method) — Helper building a COMMIT step preloaded with a suggested version, pre-session baseline, and patch bump_type. <!--#0f81df148bbf4e20-->
  - `TestCommitVersionRaceGuard.test_drift_triggers_reanalyze_and_avoids_collision` (method) — Asserts that when disk drifted past the baseline (concurrent bump), the stale suggested_version is discarded and version_analyze re-runs against the drifted baseline to write a non-colliding version. <!--#153cb98227a7ff38-->
  - `TestCommitVersionRaceGuard.test_no_drift_writes_target_unchanged` (method) — Asserts that when the disk version still equals the baseline (no concurrent bump), version_analyze is not re-run and the resolved target is written verbatim. <!--#23c58e9348e1dba0-->
  - `TestCommitVersionRaceGuard.test_own_session_advance_is_not_drift` (method) — Asserts that a version file advanced by this flow's own session commits (disk == observed current_version but > baseline) is not treated as drift, discriminating the guard's operand from pre_session_version. <!--#1500673daabe5691-->
  - `TestCommitVersionRaceGuard.test_drift_reanalyze_failure_halts_commit` (method) — Asserts the commit halts with FAILED (never writing the stale colliding target) when the drift re-analysis fails to produce a version. <!--#b5007fbf516e519c-->
  - `TestCommitVersionRaceGuard.test_crash_resume_uncommitted_own_write_kept` (method) — Asserts that a crash-resume drift (disk written but HEAD blob still pre-crash, i.e. head != disk) is recognized as the flow's own uncommitted residue and the target is kept/re-written rather than re-analysed. <!--#21fe007a74b62463-->
  - `TestCommitVersionRaceGuard.test_concurrent_drift_committed_head_triggers_reanalyze` (method) — Asserts the inverse of crash-resume: a committed drift (HEAD blob == disk) is a concurrent bump, so self-heal must not fire and version_analyze is re-run against the drifted baseline. <!--#752cb45cd645f0e4-->
  - `TestCommitVersionRaceGuard.test_drift_reanalyze_regression_halts_commit` (method) — Asserts the commit halts with FAILED when drift re-analysis hallucinates a version lower than the drifted disk version, blocking a monotonicity-violating regression. <!--#e63ac36b62538d39-->
- `TestStepHandlers` (class) — Test suite verifying the STEP_HANDLERS registry covers all non-retired step types with callable handlers. <!--#8076771bd49382b1-->
  - `TestStepHandlers.test_all_step_types_have_handlers` (method) — Asserts every step type except the retired spec steps has a registered handler. <!--#3250f8784dac9d41-->

- `TestLLMCallerIntegration` (class) — Tests LLMCaller's retry behaviour against a mocked ClaudeCodeRunner with agent rotation pinned off, covering both eventual success after failures and LLMCallError on retry exhaustion. <!--#7f8ba4321acb880d-->
  - `TestLLMCallerIntegration.test_llm_retry_success` (method) — Asserts LLMCaller.call retries a failing runner and returns the output once a later attempt succeeds, after exactly the expected number of invocations. <!--#b39dce2720d96457-->
  - `TestLLMCallerIntegration.test_llm_retry_exhausted` (method) — Asserts LLMCaller.call raises LLMCallError once max_retries attempts have all failed, without exceeding the retry budget. <!--#81190593d694e9fe-->

- `TestFormatRoundUsageFooter` (class) — Unit tests for `token_usage.format_round_usage_footer`, asserting the compact "This round … · Total …" string uses comma thousands separators, shows only input/output tokens (no cache or cost), renders zeros, and degrades `None` inputs to zeros instead of raising. <!--#4a5e4a0f4db5f27b-->

### `src/se3/engine/test_version_intent.py` (python) — Unit tests for the version-intent module, covering VersionIntent serialization and disk round-trips, collect_intents gathering/filtering, idempotent consumed-marking, the gitignore guard on write_intent, and git-trailer-based reconcile-commit detection. <!--#9614ee2e3bf03d64|3631e0ddc217275d-->

### `src/se3/engine/token_usage.py` (python) — The single source of truth for se3's token/cost accounting, defining the additive UsageTotals tally (field-wise merge, tolerant JSON round-tripping), a ContextVar-based step-scoped accumulator that best-effort folds each LLM call's usage into the in-scope step, and formatting helpers that render labelled usage/cost strings for the CLI and WebUI display ends. <!--#deecb225fd093d50|a60fafda9217ec4b-->
- `_coerce_int` (function) — Best-effort coerces any value to an int, returning 0 for None/missing/unparseable input so malformed usage payloads never raise. <!--#c97b0fddc8bb6dee-->
- `_coerce_float` (function) — Best-effort coerces any value to a float, returning 0.0 for None/missing/bad input. <!--#9a7b6843df4c055e-->
- `UsageTotals` (class) — Additive dataclass holding the four token counts plus USD cost for a step or session, with field-wise merging and tolerant JSON round-tripping. <!--#375cd06ef41c59d1-->
  - `UsageTotals.add` (method) — Folds another UsageTotals into self field-by-field (ignoring None) and returns self, the merge primitive for combining many LLM calls or steps. <!--#fdfadb75f6c63a01-->
  - `UsageTotals.total_tokens` (method) — Property returning the sum of all four token counts (input + output + both cache kinds). <!--#7b66453eb3751841-->
  - `UsageTotals.is_empty` (method) — Returns True when every token field and the cost are (near) zero, used by display to suppress an empty usage block. <!--#418f023efc3e6d45-->
  - `UsageTotals.to_dict` (method) — Serializes the tally to a stable-keyed JSON-primitive dict for persistence and read-back by both display ends. <!--#8a5404e456cc4012-->
  - `UsageTotals.from_dict` (method) — Classmethod reconstructing a UsageTotals from a possibly-partial/None mapping, defaulting missing fields to zero via the coerce helpers. <!--#0886740f6509abf2-->
- `accumulate_step_usage` (function) — Context manager that opens a fresh step-scoped accumulator (via ContextVar) for its body and yields it so the caller can read the merged step total afterward. <!--#cc56e3c1d6f5a823-->
- `current_step_usage` (function) — Returns the currently in-scope step accumulator, or None when no step scope is active. <!--#7fd09ce3743acedc-->
- `use_step_usage` (function) — Context manager that re-binds a given existing accumulator into the current context, used to carry a parent step's scope across ThreadPoolExecutor thread boundaries (no-op for None). <!--#3dbb8ce677b8dd31-->
- `add_call_usage` (function) — Best-effort folds one LLM call's usage (UsageTotals or raw dict) into the in-scope step accumulator under a lock, a safe no-op outside any scope and on any error. <!--#638e1c5fbd6b3f82-->
- `format_cost` (function) — Renders a USD cost as a 4-decimal-place string (e.g. $0.0123), tolerant of None/non-numeric input. <!--#1d2dadbbbc3b7703-->
- `_format_tokens` (function) — Renders a token count with thousands separators (e.g. 12,345). <!--#6ac1c2bfe7972253-->
- `format_round_usage_footer` (function) — Renders the compact one-line per-round token usage footer (this round's in/out plus the running cumulative in/out) used at the tail of interactive CLI step output, with localized labels and None inputs degrading to zeros. <!--#9084375cfda31011-->
- `format_usage_line` (function) — Renders a compact single-line labelled usage summary (input, output, cache read/write tokens and cost) with localized labels, tolerating None/empty tallies by showing zeros. <!--#14ff2b3fc01f8d95-->

### `src/se3/engine/tool_formatters.py` (python) — A registry-based formatting module that renders tool_use and tool_result calls (Edit, Write, Read, Bash, Grep, Glob, plus generic fallbacks) into single-line previews, merged success/failure chip headers, unified diffs, and JSON-safe structured detail payloads for CLI stream output and web chip panels. <!--#c54dd61994655562|91e7162fb2ba2d74-->
- `set_project_root` (function) — Sets the module-level project root used for relative-path truncation. <!--#dfcc75f6b64065c1-->
- `get_project_root` (function) — Returns the currently configured module-level project root. <!--#7154a7b54664f7dd-->
- `truncate_path` (function) — Shortens a file path by converting to project-relative and abbreviating middle segments while always preserving the filename. <!--#af68e886ed526bb5-->
- `truncate_preview` (function) — Collapses text to a single line and truncates it to a max length with an ellipsis. <!--#430e41a2779956b6-->
- `_generic_tool_use_preview` (function) — Fallback formatter rendering a tool name plus up to three key=value input parameters. <!--#5381c07435a555b6-->
- `_generic_tool_result_preview` (function) — Fallback formatter producing a short preview of an arbitrary tool result, handling errors, dicts, lists, and strings. <!--#48f2fbefea36c20f-->
- `_format_edit_use` (function) — Formats an Edit tool_use preview showing the path and old→new line counts. <!--#f71eb442b30a57a8-->
- `_format_edit_result` (function) — Formats an Edit tool_result preview with a success/failure check mark. <!--#85c9245a8efa4b63-->
- `_format_write_use` (function) — Formats a Write tool_use preview showing the path and content line count. <!--#cbf2c6850db84c36-->
- `_format_write_result` (function) — Formats a Write tool_result preview with a success check mark. <!--#bb864e49ebf169af-->
- `_format_read_use` (function) — Formats a Read tool_use preview showing the path and optional offset/limit line range. <!--#033bed8e51562302-->
- `_format_read_result` (function) — Formats a Read tool_result preview reporting the number of lines read. <!--#64139de5213892f1-->
- `_format_bash_use` (function) — Formats a Bash tool_use preview showing a truncated command string. <!--#1d81716ea4607e32-->
