- `_format_bash_result` (function) — Formats a Bash tool_result preview reporting the output line count. <!--#cadb1cac2322ffa6-->
- `_format_grep_use` (function) — Formats a Grep tool_use preview showing the pattern and search path. <!--#f358d0cddd652f2f-->
- `_format_grep_result` (function) — Formats a Grep tool_result preview reporting the number of matches. <!--#db18d2ecd441d75f-->
- `_format_glob_use` (function) — Formats a Glob tool_use preview showing the pattern and search path. <!--#a5fb2a263b26c807-->
- `_format_glob_result` (function) — Formats a Glob tool_result preview reporting the number of matched files. <!--#15d57808a43d6f30-->
- `_extract_text` (function) — Normalizes a tool result of varied shapes (string, dict, content-block list) into plain text. <!--#9ccecf462228bddd-->
- `format_tool_use_preview` (function) — Public entry point that routes a tool_use to its registered formatter or the generic fallback. <!--#384bca508e74b524-->
- `format_tool_result_preview` (function) — Public entry point that routes a tool_result to its registered formatter or the generic fallback. <!--#be3e1b30f642fff2-->
- `generate_edit_diff` (function) — Produces unified-diff lines from an Edit tool's old and new strings. <!--#12314b9f4beec6e1-->
- `format_tool_chip_in_flight_header` (function) — Returns the chip header string for an in-flight (not-yet-settled) tool call. <!--#1f543073fd4bdc05-->
- `_error_preview` (function) — Extracts a short error description from a failed tool_result payload. <!--#355770af1dbe4956-->
- `_success_combined_edit` (function) — Builds the merged success-chip body for an Edit call (path plus line-count delta). <!--#c1da397fa166012e-->
- `_success_combined_write` (function) — Builds the merged success-chip body for a Write call (path plus line count). <!--#dd4ee8b0ac44b368-->
- `_success_combined_read` (function) — Builds the merged success-chip body for a Read call (path, range, and lines read). <!--#8301d4b64ec2f5f6-->
- `_success_combined_bash` (function) — Builds the merged success-chip body for a Bash call (command plus output line count). <!--#7244951a7d393507-->
- `_success_combined_grep` (function) — Builds the merged success-chip body for a Grep call (pattern, path, and match count). <!--#2cf5893c148f574d-->
- `_success_combined_glob` (function) — Builds the merged success-chip body for a Glob call (pattern, path, and file count). <!--#a0ffe282c52331a7-->
- `_failure_use_body` (function) — Returns the use-side summary body for a chip with the tool-name prefix stripped off. <!--#42b4af467d9e996a-->
- `format_tool_chip_header` (function) — Builds the merged success (✓) or failure (✗) chip header combining input and result/error summaries for a settled tool call. <!--#0289b350323d1bb4-->
- `_parse_first_hunk_start` (function) — Parses the first hunk's old/new starting line numbers from unified-diff lines. <!--#9423216a302e5b77-->
- `_maybe_truncate_text` (function) — Tail-truncates text to a max character count, returning the text and a truncation flag. <!--#ec5a2a60e03451e2-->
- `_maybe_truncate_lines` (function) — Truncates a list of lines to a max item count, returning the list and a truncation flag. <!--#2fbed4dc3f10a384-->
- `_build_edit_detail` (function) — Builds the structured edit_diff detail payload (diff text and hunk line numbers) for an Edit call. <!--#5af5b189f4951526-->
- `_build_write_detail` (function) — Builds the write_full or write_diff detail payload for a Write call depending on whether prior content existed. <!--#5ef63ac28351f7e8-->
- `_build_read_detail` (function) — Builds the read_text detail payload (file text and start line) for a Read call. <!--#0cd9954a4b3a9156-->
- `_build_bash_detail` (function) — Builds the bash_output detail payload (command, stdout, stderr) for a Bash call. <!--#92b7bb8c3d4fd9bf-->
- `_build_grep_detail` (function) — Builds the grep_matches detail payload (pattern, path, match lines) for a Grep call. <!--#f8f884afae6d79fa-->
- `_build_glob_detail` (function) — Builds the glob_matches detail payload (pattern, path, file list) for a Glob call. <!--#f5ce9cb5e0ed9cdc-->
- `_build_generic_text_detail` (function) — Builds the fallback kind="text" detail payload from extracted result text for unregistered tools. <!--#4d3ee4f1226cb7d4-->
- `build_tool_detail_payload` (function) — Public entry point producing a JSON-safe structured detail dict (with a kind discriminator) for the web chip's expandable panel. <!--#343f99f9c9ff70ee-->
- `format_tool_diff` (function) — Renders unified-diff or created-file output to the console for Edit/Write tools, no-op for others. <!--#17b73d59cfd2d12c-->

### `src/se3/engine/transitive_reduction.py` (python) — Performs transitive reduction on a task-group dependency DAG, returning a deep copy in which each redundant direct `depends_on` edge (one also reachable via a longer intermediate path, detected by a BFS helper) is removed while the input is left unmutated. <!--#e9031a4a3db90475|0f08cb4ec581ddce-->
- `transitive_reduce` (function) — Public function returning a deep copy of the input groups with each redundant direct dependency (one reachable via a longer path) removed from its `depends_on` list, leaving the originals untouched. <!--#41aca8aef443ed63-->
- `_has_long_path` (function) — Internal BFS helper that reports whether the adjacency graph has an indirect path of length ≥ 2 from source to target, ignoring the direct source→target edge. <!--#d3ec927b055eff6d-->

### `src/se3/engine/truncation.py` (python) — Central module defining the shared character-limit constants for tail-truncating stdout/stderr, test-history output, failure sections, plan summaries, and web tool-detail payloads that get fed into LLM prompts, keeping truncation behavior consistent across the test, self_check, and verify_spec step handlers. <!--#ef740dc558517a20|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/se3/engine/version_bumper.py` (python) — Version-management module providing a SemVer 2.0.0 `Version` value object (parse, compare, bump) plus pluggable format-specific version-file handlers (JSON/TOML/Python/setup.py) and a `VersionDetector` that identifies a project's type and locates, reads, and updates its version file. <!--#f10ee1578849d135|febbe367307b6b96-->
- `ProjectType` (class) — Enum of supported project types (Python, Node.js, Unknown) used to drive version-file detection. <!--#2c6662747efb04b7-->
- `BumpType` (class) — Enum naming the three semantic-versioning bump kinds: major, minor, and patch. <!--#da8d688705155657-->
- `Version` (class) — Immutable SemVer 2.0.0 value object that parses, validates, stringifies, compares, and bumps version components. <!--#6343759176871ea6-->
  - `Version.parse` (method) — Classmethod that parses a SemVer string into a Version, raising ValueError on empty or malformed input. <!--#96dad270505dc81c-->
  - `Version.validate` (method) — Classmethod returning True if a string is a valid SemVer version (parse succeeds), else False. <!--#a520043f7f23f28d-->
  - `Version.__str__` (method) — Renders the Version back to its canonical MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH[-prerelease][+build] string form. <!--#ba5738e57d5afb3e-->
  - `Version.bump_major` (method) — Returns a new Version with major incremented and minor/patch reset to zero. <!--#f3339b07dd8dfb40-->
  - `Version.bump_minor` (method) — Returns a new Version with minor incremented and patch reset to zero. <!--#3d59389e3f5867ab-->
  - `Version.bump_patch` (method) — Returns a new Version with patch incremented. <!--#ddc46dd1a9d0bc33-->
  - `Version.with_prerelease` (method) — Returns a copy of the Version with the prerelease identifier replaced. <!--#6da00fb8dfe0907e-->
  - `Version.with_build` (method) — Returns a copy of the Version with the build metadata replaced. <!--#c78c75cdc85a37d8-->
  - `Version.bump` (method) — Dispatches to bump_major/minor/patch based on the given BumpType. <!--#1621340211520461-->
  - `Version.__eq__` (method) — Equality comparison against another Version (ignoring build metadata) or a 3-tuple of numbers. <!--#60b50cf04371f68a-->
  - `Version.__hash__` (method) — Hashes the Version on its numeric components and prerelease, excluding build metadata. <!--#0d62c0a2d0e94ec0-->
  - `Version.__lt__` (method) — Implements SemVer precedence ordering, including prerelease identifier comparison rules. <!--#08963aa698cc60d5-->
  - `Version.__le__` (method) — Less-than-or-equal comparison derived from __eq__ and __lt__. <!--#abc20a7cc2141ee0-->
  - `Version.__gt__` (method) — Greater-than comparison derived from __le__. <!--#00451315f65f92a1-->
  - `Version.__ge__` (method) — Greater-than-or-equal comparison derived from __lt__. <!--#24ebfdfd27ae87fc-->
- `VersionInfo` (class) — Dataclass bundling detected project type, version-file path, raw version string, and parsed Version. <!--#802e8ec3419df566-->
- `VersionFileHandler` (class) — Abstract base class defining the read/write/ensure/create interface for format-specific version file handlers. <!--#a07b8f65236b1ffc-->
  - `VersionFileHandler.can_handle` (method) — Abstract predicate indicating whether the handler supports a given file path/format. <!--#db58566b8a10520b-->
  - `VersionFileHandler.read_version` (method) — Abstract method to read and return the version string from a file. <!--#5035056e002230d5-->
  - `VersionFileHandler.write_version` (method) — Abstract method to write a new version string into the file. <!--#a475c00f546c0bb6-->
  - `VersionFileHandler.ensure_version` (method) — Optional hook (default unsupported) that idempotently inserts a version field if one is missing. <!--#c9a4431ce5153943-->
  - `VersionFileHandler.create_version_file` (method) — Optional hook (default unsupported) that creates a new version file with an initial version. <!--#6a4f7c21938ff82f-->
- `JsonVersionHandler` (class) — Version file handler for JSON files like package.json, reading/writing the top-level version field. <!--#ce928dc45bec4d5f-->
  - `JsonVersionHandler.can_handle` (method) — Returns True for .json files or files named package.json. <!--#2bf682d38aefb50b-->
  - `JsonVersionHandler.read_version` (method) — Loads the JSON and returns its version field, raising if absent. <!--#83346fccd78f5315-->
  - `JsonVersionHandler.write_version` (method) — Updates the JSON version field and rewrites the file with 2-space indentation. <!--#de1b95612151f94f-->
  - `JsonVersionHandler.create_version_file` (method) — Creates a minimal package.json with name/version/description fields, erroring if one already exists. <!--#a274cb9243bcc633-->
- `TomlVersionHandler` (class) — Version file handler for TOML files like pyproject.toml, supporting PEP 621 and Poetry version fields. <!--#6fe3d2c4bfecb0f0-->
  - `TomlVersionHandler.can_handle` (method) — Returns True for .toml files or files named pyproject.toml. <!--#cf5108c660cb6332-->
  - `TomlVersionHandler.read_version` (method) — Parses the TOML and returns project.version or tool.poetry.version, raising if neither is present. <!--#09f2a22b558ba011-->
  - `TomlVersionHandler.write_version` (method) — Regex-replaces the version string in the [project] or [tool.poetry] section while preserving formatting. <!--#1992edca58aa8de2-->
  - `TomlVersionHandler.ensure_version` (method) — Adds a version field under [project] (creating the section if needed) when none exists. <!--#ae9fafd9dd9ff935-->
  - `TomlVersionHandler.create_version_file` (method) — Creates a minimal PEP 621 pyproject.toml with build-system and project sections. <!--#5ecc875d7ab5fac3-->
- `PythonVersionHandler` (class) — Version file handler for .py files exposing __version__, version, or VERSION assignments. <!--#16a991b3b7e0ddb0-->
  - `PythonVersionHandler.can_handle` (method) — Returns True for any .py file. <!--#b096d66b4d0a6776-->
  - `PythonVersionHandler.read_version` (method) — Regex-extracts the version from __version__, version, or VERSION assignments. <!--#20c1d195b1aab75d-->
  - `PythonVersionHandler.write_version` (method) — Regex-replaces the version in __version__, version, or VERSION assignments. <!--#d549e76c5f9c361d-->
  - `PythonVersionHandler.ensure_version` (method) — Prepends a __version__ assignment to the file if no version is found. <!--#6dfb4e1ab685ea1d-->
  - `PythonVersionHandler.create_version_file` (method) — Creates a version.py with __version__ inside the detected package or src/ directory. <!--#ad58a4cb4acc90dd-->
- `SetupPyHandler` (class) — Version file handler for setup.py that reads/writes the version keyword of the setup() call via AST. <!--#b8ea17a61702ecba-->
  - `SetupPyHandler.can_handle` (method) — Returns True only for files named setup.py. <!--#faafe99ad3e31b2c-->
  - `SetupPyHandler.read_version` (method) — Walks the AST to locate the setup() call's version keyword and returns its constant value. <!--#a7cd71c89280a9c8-->
  - `SetupPyHandler._get_func_name` (method) — Helper extracting a callable's name from an AST Name or Attribute node. <!--#bec71767409a06e2-->
  - `SetupPyHandler.write_version` (method) — Locates the version argument via AST positions and replaces its string, falling back to regex for multi-line cases. <!--#a009ee54b96ba372-->
  - `SetupPyHandler.create_version_file` (method) — Creates a minimal setup.py invoking setuptools.setup() with name and version. <!--#f241b6ce5dd61c41-->
- `VersionDetector` (class) — Detects a project's type and locates/reads its version file by checking known markers and file locations in priority order. <!--#4fea9be4e65f2ddf-->
  - `VersionDetector.__init__` (method) — Initializes the detector with its ordered list of TOML/JSON/Python/setup.py handlers. <!--#48f8b1a48b142f73-->
  - `VersionDetector.detect_project_type` (method) — Classifies the project as Python, Node.js, or Unknown by checking characteristic marker files. <!--#d0ebb06157a824d2-->
  - `VersionDetector.detect_project_type_without_version_file` (method) — Classifies project type from language/framework markers and source structure when no version file exists yet. <!--#54ca047bc8b24a52-->
  - `VersionDetector.get_version_file_path` (method) — Returns the first known version-file location that both matches a handler and yields a readable version. <!--#3714d693e64ea4a4-->
  - `VersionDetector.read_version` (method) — Reads a version string from a path by delegating to the first capable handler. <!--#d4769f408e454856-->
  - `VersionDetector.detect` (method) — Main entry point that detects project type, finds the version file, and returns a populated VersionInfo. <!--#4a30496f59d5ac93-->
- `VersionConfig` (class) — Configuration dataclass controlling whether bumping is enabled, an explicit version-file path, and commit-message inclusion. <!--#014d4efef42053a3-->
  - `VersionConfig.validate` (method) — Returns a list of validation errors, e.g. when the configured version file path does not exist. <!--#9d8ace4382297af9-->
- `VersionBumper` (class) — High-level orchestrator that detects, reads, bumps, sets, and rolls back versions via file handlers or an optional version script. <!--#511ac50dd45ecfd1-->
  - `VersionBumper.__init__` (method) — Initializes the bumper with config, handler list, detector, backup state, and script-mode flags. <!--#987a05dfe1c3fdb4-->
  - `VersionBumper.register_handler` (method) — Appends a custom version file handler to the bumper's handler list. <!--#32122fd9d619e3d1-->
  - `VersionBumper.detect_version_file` (method) — Locates the version file, preferring a version script, then an explicit config path, then auto-detection. <!--#16c556251b1d2a5c-->
  - `VersionBumper._find_and_init_script` (method) — Searches for a version script and, if found, switches the bumper into script mode with a VersionScriptRunner. <!--#adc59518a3995bb0-->
  - `VersionBumper.initialize_version_system` (method) — Bootstraps versioning for a project by generating a version script or creating/updating an appropriate version file. <!--#f85719e10f4d362b-->
  - `VersionBumper._get_handler_for_new_file` (method) — Returns a handler capable of creating a new file with the given suffix. <!--#2ab4976ca4b6c6d7-->
  - `VersionBumper.detect_project_type` (method) — Delegates to the detector to classify the project's type. <!--#aec769c16a3c72d1-->
  - `VersionBumper._get_handler` (method) — Returns the first registered handler that can process the given file path, raising if none apply. <!--#c46fafc4e8a5aaa4-->
  - `VersionBumper.read_version` (method) — Reads the current version via the script runner in script mode, otherwise via the detected file's handler. <!--#fe3a2746035c133f-->
  - `VersionBumper.parse_version` (method) — Static convenience wrapper delegating to Version.parse. <!--#55545ad66a6934ff-->
  - `VersionBumper.validate_semver` (method) — Static convenience wrapper delegating to Version.validate. <!--#b4dfccabd4c8fb35-->
  - `VersionBumper.bump_version_string` (method) — Static helper that parses a version string, applies a bump, and returns the new string. <!--#5a9b2633882efb56-->
  - `VersionBumper.bump_version` (method) — Bumps the version in the file or script, capturing a backup for rollback and returning the new version. <!--#53f37d782d5be3e5-->
  - `VersionBumper.set_version` (method) — Validates and writes an explicit version directly (no bump computation), capturing a rollback backup. <!--#b2acecbc992d2fa9-->
  - `VersionBumper.save_original_version` (method) — Records the current version and its path as a backup for potential rollback. <!--#58bfbb0699c085d9-->
  - `VersionBumper.rollback` (method) — Restores the backed-up version via handler or script, then clears the backup state. <!--#059becaee9ad1190-->
  - `VersionBumper.clear_backup` (method) — Discards the saved backup so the last bump becomes permanent, typically after a successful commit. <!--#a854889561986177-->
  - `VersionBumper.atomic_bump` (method) — Context manager that applies a bump and yields the new version, auto-rolling back on exception and clearing the backup on success. <!--#8520e55a31d36db5-->

### `src/se3/engine/version_intent.py` (python) — Defines the branch-committed VersionIntent metadata and its read/write/collect/idempotency helpers, moving the version-bump decision from each worktree session to a single merge-side reconcile that derives the final version once from all merged-in branches' intents. <!--#704d87e4a4d55265|43bfc961d0fb3ce7-->
- `IntentReadError` (class) — A RuntimeError signalling that a git ref's version intents could not be read (infrastructure fault), kept distinct from a genuine 'no intents' so the merge CLI never treats a git failure as an empty version-bump scope. <!--#41470ddc83654816-->
- `VersionIntentIgnoredError` (class) — An OSError raised at intent write time when the intent path is gitignored, surfacing the .gitignore root cause early instead of as a misleading merge-side failure. <!--#aaee15b22aecb21c-->
- `VersionIntent` (class) — A serializable dataclass capturing a worktree session's version-bump intent (change summary, changelog bullets, optional SemVer hint and tag flag, baseline/provisional version, and consumption markers) that travels with the flow branch as committed JSON for the merge-side reconcile step. <!--#7aa5924d53c58943-->
  - `VersionIntent.to_dict` (method) — Serializes the VersionIntent into a plain JSON-safe dict via dataclasses.asdict. <!--#ce32cc6f66e77914-->
  - `VersionIntent.from_dict` (method) — Classmethod that rebuilds a VersionIntent from a dict, validating that a non-empty flow_id is present while tolerantly ignoring unknown keys and defaulting missing ones for forward/backward compatibility. <!--#5f4f1945e7766aae-->
- `_normalize_optional_str` (function) — Helper that coerces a value to a stripped string, mapping None and empty strings to None so absent and blank hints read identically. <!--#da1f215e25acc584-->
- `intent_path` (function) — Returns the committed file path for a flow's intent JSON, using flow_id as the stem so distinct flows' files coexist in a merged tree. <!--#433a74b6d2477c1b-->
- `write_intent` (function) — Atomically persists an intent to its committed path (creating the dir), first asserting the path isn't gitignored so it will actually travel with the branch. <!--#1916316ba4a154de-->
- `_assert_intent_path_not_ignored` (function) — Best-effort guard that raises VersionIntentIgnoredError only when `git check-ignore` definitively reports the intent path as ignored, letting probe/non-repo faults fall through to the write. <!--#8bbd8f1b012ef898-->
- `read_intent` (function) — Reads a flow's intent from the working tree by path, returning None if absent. <!--#a4ea9ca56ca36de0-->
- `read_intent_file` (function) — Parses a single intent file, returning None (with a warning) on missing, corrupt, or invalid content so one damaged intent doesn't abort collecting the rest. <!--#6238dde42b5c20bc-->
- `collect_intents` (function) — Scans the merged master tree's intents directory and returns all readable VersionIntents (optionally including consumed ones), sorted deterministically by flow_id. <!--#e26b838ec25dd2b9-->
- `intent_flow_ids_at_ref` (function) — Returns the set of intent flow_ids committed under the intents dir at a given git ref, raising IntentReadError on git infrastructure faults rather than degrading them to an empty set. <!--#6762c7ed445f6423-->
- `_merge_base` (function) — Returns the merge-base sha of two refs, None when there is no common ancestor, and raises IntentReadError on a git infrastructure fault. <!--#314c8d98b3a586fc-->
- `_is_ancestor` (function) — Returns whether ref_a is an ancestor of ref_b via `git merge-base --is-ancestor`, raising IntentReadError on any non-0/1 exit or subprocess fault. <!--#739718bf0dd269ac-->
- `intent_flow_ids_introduced` (function) — Computes the intent flow_ids a branch actually contributes to a merge (its own intents minus those inherited at the fork point), with a rerun-recovery carve-out that reconstructs the pre-integration baseline from the --no-ff merge commit. <!--#c13307aeb46f1e8a-->
- `_integration_baseline_ids` (function) — Rerun-recovery helper that reconstructs the intents a branch inherited by locating its --no-ff integration merge, finding the fork point against the merge's other parent(s), and returning those baseline flow_ids (or None if no merge is found). <!--#e87894c73356e464-->
- `mark_consumed` (function) — Idempotently rewrites a flow's on-disk intent with consumed=True (and the reconcile commit sha), returning whether a marking write actually occurred. <!--#7acec8900631ac4f-->
- `is_consumed` (function) — Reports whether a flow's intent has been reconciled, defaulting to the git-durable reconcile-commit signal (with a test-only flag-based opt-out) rather than the bare on-disk consumed flag. <!--#10a211365c643f51-->
- `reconcile_commit_exists` (function) — Authoritative idempotency check that searches commits under a ref for the exact `Version-Reconcile-Session: <flow_id>` trailer line, retrying once and raising IntentReadError on persistent probe faults so it never falsely reports absent. <!--#915e68152c18da13-->
- `_atomic_write_text` (function) — Writes text to a path atomically via a temp file plus os.replace, refusing to overwrite a destination symlink to prevent redirect-onto-tracked-file attacks. <!--#fa39f8a5ed909e57-->

### `src/se3/engine/version_script_interface.py` (python) — Module providing a subprocess-based version-script interface for SE3, exposing a VersionScriptRunner that delegates get/bump/set version operations to a project's version script, plus helpers to locate, validate, and LLM-generate that script from the project structure. <!--#0e53153b3b79a7fc|c410e6e037c8df3a-->
- `VersionScriptRunner` (class) — Class that runs a version script's get/bump/set subcommands via subprocess and returns parsed Version objects. <!--#98b4f61a5c96e0ff-->
  - `VersionScriptRunner.__init__` (method) — Initializes the runner with a script path and project root (used as cwd), raising FileNotFoundError if the script is missing. <!--#0928b5697a4b7343-->
  - `VersionScriptRunner._run_script` (method) — Invokes the version script (via python/bash/direct) with given args and a timeout, returning stripped stdout or raising RuntimeError on failure. <!--#dea2c93f7c197c77-->
  - `VersionScriptRunner.get_version` (method) — Calls the script's 'get' command and returns the parsed current Version. <!--#f9aaac75f0d15371-->
  - `VersionScriptRunner.bump_version` (method) — Calls the script's 'bump' command with the given bump type and returns the new Version. <!--#f094221c393e8096-->
  - `VersionScriptRunner.set_version` (method) — Calls the script's 'set' command to explicitly set a version string and returns the resulting Version. <!--#2e00806c0b7fe690-->
- `find_version_script` (function) — Locates the project's version script, checking a configured path first then the default se3/scripts locations, returning its Path or None. <!--#dffe245a479cd4ad-->
- `validate_script` (function) — Validates a version script by running its 'get' command, returning a (is_valid, error_message) tuple. <!--#98058fd72961d58c-->
- `generate_version_script` (function) — Uses an LLM to generate a version script tailored to the project structure, writing it to disk, validating it, and making it executable. <!--#4042aeeaa878b170-->
- `_validate_generated_script` (function) — Checks that the LLM-written script exists, is non-empty, has valid Python syntax, and contains a read_version() function. <!--#16d30943aaff6188-->
- `_scan_project_for_generation` (function) — Scans the project to detect its type, candidate version files, and current version to inform script generation. <!--#de357e474966dba1-->
- `_load_template` (function) — Loads the bundled version script template from the templates directory, or a placeholder if absent. <!--#4965c6c93641fa49-->
- `_build_generation_prompt` (function) — Constructs the LLM prompt instructing it to write a version script to the target path based on project info and the template. <!--#3a98ca7c38f412ef-->

### `src/se3/engine/worktree.py` (python) — Provides generic git worktree lifecycle primitives for SE3 branch isolation—creating/forking worktrees, resiliently cleaning them up, querying repository and merge state, and LLM-assisted merge-conflict resolution—shared by the parallel implement DAG and the `se3 run --worktree` isolation mode. <!--#c4d85ecb353d3b4c|dc4c498fcd3567b3-->
- `_run_git` (function) — Internal helper that runs a git subcommand in a given project root via subprocess, with configurable error-checking and timeout. <!--#fde166d981df8704-->
- `has_commits` (function) — Returns whether the repository has at least one commit by checking if HEAD resolves. <!--#eedc238ff332a101-->
- `get_current_branch` (function) — Resolves the current branch name, working on both populated and empty repos via symbolic-ref with a rev-parse fallback. <!--#2e6f604688447f87-->
- `_branch_safe_name` (function) — Converts a branch name into a filesystem-safe directory name by replacing slashes with hyphens. <!--#cc8e98cb43f0ac71-->
- `create_worktree` (function) — Creates a git worktree for a branch under se3/worktrees/, with pruning and timeout-doubling retries. <!--#46f06f633b1f8f67-->
- `fork_worktree` (function) — Creates a new branch from a source branch and sets up a worktree for it (used by the relay strategy). <!--#f48d9ef83b40d95d-->
- `remove_worktree` (function) — Removes a git worktree resiliently, handling already-deleted directories, locked worktrees (double-force), and stale metadata via pruning. <!--#1829e020bd67d3d9-->
- `_force_remove_if_still_registered` (function) — Force-removes a worktree entry when git still tracks it after pruning, by inspecting porcelain worktree-list output. <!--#89eb514629084d02-->
- `_cleanup_git_worktree_metadata` (function) — Last-resort helper that directly deletes the internal .git/worktrees/<safe_name> metadata directory. <!--#5b0e5d350a7da2a3-->
- `force_cleanup_worktree` (function) — Forcefully and fault-tolerantly removes a branch's worktree through a six-step sequence (unlock, remove, rmtree, prune, metadata cleanup, verify) for inconsistent-state recovery. <!--#c7aba362e1be00dd-->
- `delete_branch` (function) — Deletes a local branch, first force-cleaning any worktree still registered for it. <!--#eef8cbd9d7138774-->
- `has_new_commits` (function) — Returns whether a branch has any commits ahead of a given base branch. <!--#f4edc123aabe5a25-->
- `exists_for_branch` (function) — Returns whether a worktree is already registered for a given branch by parsing porcelain worktree-list output. <!--#74103a50bb9fc065-->
- `get_conflicting_files` (function) — Returns the list of files with merge conflicts via a worktree-vs-index unmerged diff. <!--#3f1832ae28ca0082-->
- `detect_unmerged_paths` (function) — Returns deduped paths in unmerged-index state by reading the index directly (catching modify/delete cases that get_conflicting_files misses). <!--#e556cc1055c95525-->
- `merge_in_progress` (function) — Returns whether a real git merge/cherry-pick/rebase/revert is mid-flight by checking for marker files in the resolved git directory. <!--#9ced3782cc2dca53-->
- `recover_stale_unmerged_paths` (function) — Auto-resolves stale unmerged-index entries left by a prior failure when safe (working tree matches HEAD), returning resolved and human-needing-attention path lists. <!--#50f627f74a09fbdd-->
- `get_diff_stat` (function) — Returns the `git diff --stat` summary string between a branch and a base branch. <!--#d14c134710526000-->
- `resolve_merge_conflicts_with_context` (function) — Resolves merge conflicts via the LLM using full task/group/spec context, verifying marker-free output and retrying without falling back to --theirs. <!--#8b1d0c0949972df5-->
- `WorktreeContext` (class) — Context manager providing exception-safe worktree lifecycle—creating one on enter and removing it (but preserving the branch) on exit. <!--#bd0659262faa940f-->
  - `WorktreeContext.__init__` (method) — Initializes the context manager with project root, branch, and an empty worktree-path slot. <!--#bc42ff0de12cc5de-->
  - `WorktreeContext.__enter__` (method) — Validates no existing worktree for the branch, creates one, and returns its path. <!--#a4162b03623770c5-->
  - `WorktreeContext.__exit__` (method) — Removes the created worktree on exit (including on exceptions), logging the cleanup. <!--#0c7666626a47f293-->

## `src/se3/engine/formatters/` — Package of SE3 engine output formatters, currently housing the task-formatting subsystem that validates plan_tasks data (dependency/cycle checks) and renders task groups into rich human-readable views (tree, table, detail, summary, dependency map, and implementation plan with execution waves and statistics), re-exported via its __init__ public API. <!--#1b4c84e5ed9a1175|2ce50dddb72b1f1f-->

### `src/se3/engine/formatters/__init__.py` (python) — Package init for SE3 engine output formatters that re-exports the task formatting public API (TaskFormatter, TaskDataValidator, TaskValidationError, and format_task_groups) from the task_formatter module. <!--#22f9c3569771702b|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/se3/engine/formatters/task_formatter.py` (python) — Rich-based formatter module that validates/normalizes plan_tasks output (via TaskDataValidator with dependency and cycle checks) and renders task groups into human-readable tree, table, detail, summary, dependency-map, and implementation-plan views (including topological execution waves, DAG topology, complexity, and LOC statistics). <!--#795b2307acac071e|50c6e24d6bc0f0be-->
- `_md_heading` (function) — Helper that builds a reverse-color block heading Text via _reverse_title. <!--#f1f52807a66af571-->
- `_heading_group` (function) — Helper that wraps body renderables with a reverse-color heading and matching footer into a Rich Group. <!--#9d666073ce164827-->
- `TaskValidationError` (class) — Exception type raised when task-data validation fails. <!--#868e99ba0adf3b5e-->
- `TaskDataValidator` (class) — Class that validates and normalizes task-list structure, including required fields, complexity, and dependency integrity. <!--#dff249dc1c22b374-->
  - `TaskDataValidator.validate` (method) — Validates a full task list, normalizing each task, rejecting duplicate IDs, and checking dependencies. <!--#2f2a9aad43fa2dc0-->
  - `TaskDataValidator._validate_task` (method) — Validates one task dict, enforcing required fields and filling optional fields with defaults. <!--#e9a09cff2880eb69-->
  - `TaskDataValidator._validate_dependencies` (method) — Checks that dependency/depends_on fields are lists of known task IDs and triggers cycle detection. <!--#ab8aa6e10809309e-->
  - `TaskDataValidator._check_circular_dependencies` (method) — Detects circular dependencies among tasks via a three-color DFS over the dependency graph. <!--#849b5c958fd28e7d-->
- `TaskFormatter` (class) — Main formatter class that renders task groups into Rich tree, table, detail, summary, dependency, and implementation-plan views. <!--#626f5a864fa11b3e-->
  - `TaskFormatter.__init__` (method) — Initializes the formatter with a Rich console and a TaskDataValidator instance. <!--#d4734cdcc8d08064-->
  - `TaskFormatter.format_tasks` (method) — Dispatches task-group formatting to tree or table view based on the requested mode. <!--#f39588af93915899-->
  - `TaskFormatter._format_tree_view` (method) — Renders task groups as a hierarchical Rich Tree with complexity badges, files, dependencies, and a summary line. <!--#9291f474a280033f-->
  - `TaskFormatter._format_table_view` (method) — Renders task groups as a flat Rich Table with ID, group, description, complexity, and dependency/criteria counts. <!--#31203a0e9b8178cf-->
  - `TaskFormatter.format_task_detail` (method) — Renders a detailed single-task view as a key/value table under a per-task heading with complexity icon. <!--#18fe44ea3fef9117-->
  - `TaskFormatter.format_summary` (method) — Renders aggregate statistics (group/task counts, complexity breakdown, deps, criteria, effort estimate) as a summary table. <!--#79e56750824aa7e5-->
  - `TaskFormatter._calculate_avg_complexity` (method) — Computes the weighted average complexity score across tasks (small=1, medium=2, large=3). <!--#2ac50f195b62aa79-->
  - `TaskFormatter._estimate_effort` (method) — Derives a human-readable effort estimate (hours/days/weeks) from task count and average complexity. <!--#732f9190234d3afd-->
  - `TaskFormatter.format_implement_plan` (method) — Renders the implement-step plan with execution-strategy summary, task tree, optional DAG topology, and LOC statistics. <!--#6003cca7d82a7f66-->
  - `TaskFormatter._format_strategy_line` (method) — Builds the execution-strategy summary line (single/dag_parallel/sequential) with icon, LOC context, and optional reason. <!--#709f0931b93fee7d-->
  - `TaskFormatter._build_implement_tree` (method) — Builds a Rich Tree of task groups for the implement plan, annotating tasks with complexity, estimated LOC, and files. <!--#4f9b3fb564ea37ce-->
  - `TaskFormatter._compute_topo_waves` (method) — Computes topological execution waves of parallelizable groups via Kahn's algorithm, ordered by group_order. <!--#60000bbf915c98d5-->
  - `TaskFormatter._build_dag_topology` (method) — Builds a layered DAG topology diagram showing waves, LLM call numbering, and relay/fork/merge annotations from a RelayPlan. <!--#85583c02477a7016-->
  - `TaskFormatter._format_loc_summary` (method) — Builds the total and per-group LOC statistics line for the implement plan. <!--#90bd438f64d33add-->
  - `TaskFormatter.format_dependencies` (method) — Renders a dependency map table listing each task's dependencies and computed dependents across all groups. <!--#a264942af6747829-->
- `format_task_groups` (function) — Module-level convenience function combining task, summary, and dependency sections into a single renderable view. <!--#1a59b24466bca805-->

## `src/se3/engine/merge/` — The SE3 sequential branch-merge engine package, orchestrating LLM-assisted `se3 merge` runs — driving per-branch git merges through deterministic-then-LLM conflict resolution (with three-way conflict-context building and safe/strict/fast strategy decisions), then applying spec-integrity guardrails and LLM guardrail-repair, human-call escalation, issue-ID renumbering, tier-A runtime sync, version aggregation/reconciliation, and merged-branch/leaked-worktree cleanup and GC. <!--#3a8019a83fc84b87|f2c42960375a3c6f-->

### `src/se3/engine/merge/__init__.py` (python) — Public API facade for the SE3 merge engine package, re-exporting the merge orchestrator, conflict-context/resolver, guardrails, issue-renumbering, runtime sync, reconcile, version aggregation, and worktree-GC/cleanup symbols for sequential LLM-assisted branch merging. <!--#5f18c25e6daa30f2|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/se3/engine/merge/cleanup.py` (python) — The cleanup manager for `se3 merge --delete-merged`, whose `CleanupManager` safely deletes fully-merged branches after archiving/removing their bound worktrees and promoting each worktree's terminal engine.json (including hot/cold cold partitions) into the main archive, while skipping protected, current, dirty, or unmerged branches and recording every outcome in a `CleanupReport`, with locale-pinned git calls and hardened porcelain parsing for reliable, recoverable behavior. <!--#56ce1d79f9b2319f|fc27539159886176-->
- `_read_init_default_branch` (function) — Reads git's `init.defaultBranch` config value (or None) so a repo's custom integration branch can be auto-added to the protected set. <!--#c6d785bb210037c8-->
- `_load_protected_branches` (function) — Builds the effective protected-branch set by combining the hardcoded baseline, git's `init.defaultBranch`, and `merge.protected_branches` from se3.yaml, falling back to the baseline on any config-load error. <!--#186e605ef95b66ac-->
- `_build_locale_env` (function) — Returns a copy of the environment with `LC_ALL`/`LANG` pinned to C (and `LANGUAGE` cleared) so git stderr stays English for reliable keyword matching (J2). <!--#695fbdcf800c9c55-->
- `_run_git_locale` (function) — Wrapper that runs a git command against a project root in the locale-pinned C environment with captured output and DEVNULL stdin (J2). <!--#fa3542eba6c79592-->
- `CleanupReport` (class) — Dataclass tallying the outcome of a cleanup run — deleted branches plus per-reason skip lists, archived worktree paths, and promoted terminal-state snapshots. <!--#d678524803e55ce2-->
- `_WorktreeRecord` (class) — Dataclass holding one parsed `git worktree list --porcelain` entry (path, head, branch, detached/bare flags, and a non-local-ref flag for J7). <!--#28d19ef401ec29c8-->
- `_parse_worktree_porcelain` (function) — Parses `git worktree list --porcelain` output block-by-block into validated `_WorktreeRecord`s, logging and dropping malformed blocks instead of silently skipping them (J1, J7). <!--#9922630aafe049fa-->
- `_get_worktree_path_for_branch` (function) — Returns the filesystem path of the local-branch worktree bound to a given branch (or None), skipping non-local-ref records (J7). <!--#2906c7bf2f8b62fe-->
- `_archive_worktree` (function) — Copies a soon-to-be-deleted git worktree into an ignored `se3/worktrees/.archive/<slug>-<ts>/` directory (excluding `.git`, keeping WIP) and writes recovery metadata, so branch/worktree deletion during merge cleanup is safely reversible. <!--#e8b35beff84b04b5-->
- `_promote_completed_engine_state` (function) — Copies a worktree flow's terminal engine.json (COMPLETED-only by default, or any status when force=True for end-session) into the main project's state archive before the worktree is destroyed, preserving the active→completed→history lifecycle including any hot/cold cold partition. <!--#019382e0430eca55-->
- `_is_hotcold_header` (function) — Predicate returning True when engine.json data is a new-format hot/cold-split header, detected by its format key beginning with 'hotcold/'. <!--#a0c233c1502caf71-->
- `_promote_cold_partition` (function) — Copies a new-format flow's per-step cold partition from the worktree into the main archive (routing to a suffixed partition on flow_id collision and failing closed on copy errors) so the promoted header's cold_ref entries still resolve after the worktree is deleted. <!--#ba8c58039ae70c96-->
- `_is_worktree_clean` (function) — Returns whether a worktree has no uncommitted or untracked changes (treating a missing dir as clean and an unreadable one as dirty) so `git worktree remove` can run without `--force`. <!--#13fcb50dbcbbb210-->
- `_is_branch_ancestor_of_head` (function) — Returns True/False/None for whether a branch is an ancestor of HEAD via `merge-base --is-ancestor`, with None meaning undecidable and treated by callers as do-not-delete (J4). <!--#b716a8e760161657-->
- `CleanupManager` (class) — Class that orchestrates safe deletion of merged branches and their worktrees, exposing a partial report for recovery if the run raises mid-way. <!--#283ba581e89bbe65-->
  - `CleanupManager.__init__` (method) — Stores the project root and initializes the `_current_report` field that exposes in-progress cleanup state to callers' exception handlers. <!--#80bf35838fa3650d-->
  - `CleanupManager.delete_merged_branches` (method) — Main routine that, per branch, skips protected/current/unmerged branches, archives and removes clean bound worktrees, promotes completed state, and runs `git branch -d`, recording each outcome in the CleanupReport. <!--#aa451a3bf03434ef-->

### `src/se3/engine/merge/conflict_context.py` (python) — A read-only builder module that gathers a git merge's full three-way conflict context — branch names, merge-base and HEAD SHAs/messages, oneline logs, and each conflicting file's four versions (base/ours/theirs/working) with binary/spec classification, text decoding, and parsed hunk ranges — packaged as a ConflictContext for downstream LLM conflict resolution. <!--#19ef5218619ec0d0|3f4381af5c45f195-->
- `ShaResolutionError` (class) — Exception raised when a git ref cannot be resolved to a commit SHA, so the merge halts visibly instead of silently continuing with an empty SHA. <!--#14181aca2a4ac79d-->
- `ConflictHunk` (class) — Dataclass holding the 1-based start/end line range of a single `<<<<<<<`...`>>>>>>>` conflict block. <!--#bd6d9147dc8b0d55-->
- `ConflictFile` (class) — Dataclass capturing all per-file conflict data: the four content versions, existence flags, hunks, spec/binary classification, and decoding (encoding/lossy) status. <!--#741937ea92d50ab0-->
- `ConflictContext` (class) — Top-level dataclass aggregating one merge's full context — branch names, merge-base, head SHAs/messages, oneline logs, and the list of conflicting files. <!--#efc05225f8fefe19-->
- `_git_show_bytes` (function) — Runs `git show <ref>` (including `:N:<path>` index stages) and returns the raw bytes plus an existence flag, handling timeouts and errors gracefully. <!--#46008387dee37aaf-->
- `_decode_text` (function) — Decodes bytes to text by detecting UTF-32/16/8 BOMs and falling back to lossy UTF-8 replacement, returning the text, encoding name, and a lossy flag. <!--#bc0a2e7c3743390d-->
- `_decode_lossy` (function) — Backwards-compatible wrapper around `_decode_text` that returns only the decoded text for external callers. <!--#b45b47dcee7b2866-->
- `_looks_binary` (function) — Heuristic that classifies bytes as binary by matching known magic-byte signatures (at offset 0 and within the first 512 bytes) or detecting NUL bytes. <!--#a9ab25300ea6b325-->
- `_read_gitattributes_binary_paths` (function) — Parses the project's `.gitattributes` to return glob patterns explicitly marked binary (`binary`/`-text`/`-diff`). <!--#ee82061393628243-->
- `_path_matches_binary_pattern` (function) — Returns whether a relative path matches any of the given binary glob patterns, testing both the full path and the bare basename. <!--#ae169f13c2436b9c-->
- `_is_spec_path` (function) — Returns whether a path matches the `se3/specs/**/spec.md` spec-file pattern. <!--#52ac92675013ccc1-->
- `_parse_hunks` (function) — Scans conflict-marker text to find `<<<<<<<`...`>>>>>>>` blocks and return their line ranges, tolerating diff3 markers and unmatched starts. <!--#b2f42f8ef9ca0ce8-->
- `_read_working_tree` (function) — Reads the working-tree version of a file as bytes, returning an existence flag and handling missing/unreadable files. <!--#a833da06d43a858d-->
- `_resolve_sha` (function) — Resolves a ref to a full commit SHA via `git rev-parse`, raising `ShaResolutionError` on any failure or empty result. <!--#ca2413026b4efe5f-->
- `_commit_message` (function) — Returns the full commit message (subject + body) for a ref, or an empty string on failure. <!--#e964eb7f6f75ff78-->
- `_merge_base` (function) — Returns the merge-base commit SHA between two refs, raising `ValueError` on empty input arguments. <!--#14f71f9b25b208c8-->
- `_oneline_log` (function) — Returns the `git log <base>..<head> --oneline` commits (up to a limit) as a list of strings. <!--#19cd724550e13c5d-->
- `_build_conflict_file` (function) — Collects and assembles a complete `ConflictFile` for one path — fetching all four versions, classifying binary/spec, decoding text, and parsing hunks. <!--#73182d7958538926-->
- `build` (function) — Public entry point that builds a full `ConflictContext` for an in-progress merge by resolving SHAs, logs, and per-file conflict data (read-only). <!--#6ebd8dd8afc3bc7e-->

### `src/se3/engine/merge/conflict_resolver.py` (python) — Defines the ConflictResolver and its supporting dataclasses/enums (MergeStrategy, HunkResolution, FileResolution, LLMResolution, BatchResolveOutcome) plus conflict-marker detection helpers, resolving merge conflicts by iteratively prompting an LLM to edit working-tree files in place and rescanning for residual markers until resolved or a max-iterations cap forces escalation. <!--#5c8d2e6e15042b4a|2b9ebe4a720c4c46-->
- `_normalize_unicode_whitespace_for_marker_detection` (function) — Helper that maps a set of Unicode whitespace prefix characters (NBSP, zero-width, BOM, etc.) to ASCII spaces for marker detection only, so disguised conflict markers can't evade the regexes. <!--#b53f346f2ca1d839-->
- `_has_conflict_markers` (function) — Returns whether a text blob still contains git conflict markers, tolerating up to 7 leading spaces/tabs and normalized Unicode whitespace, and also catching a stray ======= divider. <!--#917d39cfa8592ae6-->
- `_has_any_conflict_marker` (function) — Reads the file at a path and reports whether it still has conflict markers, treating a missing file as resolved and a read error as unresolved. <!--#ff273679e9eaf157-->
- `_scan_unresolved` (function) — Filters a list of paths down to those whose files still contain conflict markers, preserving input order. <!--#4914e931eee5f132-->
- `_load_max_conflict_resolve_iterations` (function) — Reads the configured max conflict-resolution iteration count from project config, falling back to 10 on any error. <!--#71204d72e0685063-->
- `_preview` (function) — Trims a string to a short truncated preview (with a remaining-char suffix) for storing on outcome records. <!--#a08e37d395298bcd-->
- `HunkValidationError` (class) — Exception raised when a HunkResolution payload (e.g. line numbers) is malformed. <!--#fdd34bd771c38197-->
- `ResolvedContentTooLargeError` (class) — Exception raised when an LLM resolution's content exceeds the configured size cap. <!--#d03720d1f58c1128-->
- `Confidence` (class) — String enum of resolution confidence levels (HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW). <!--#dc02a14650d6e871-->
- `MergeStrategy` (class) — A string enum defining the three merge conflict-resolution tiers — `fast` (LLM-only, aborts on failure), `safe` (LLM with human-MCP fallback), and `strict` (always human) — plus a strict parser that rejects the removed legacy names. <!--#7d7496e6923c746d-->
  - `MergeStrategy.from_str` (method) — Classmethod that parses a case-insensitive strategy name into a `MergeStrategy`, raising migration-friendly errors for the retired `default`/`robust` names and a list of allowed values for anything else unrecognized. <!--#75614be5e330bb36-->
- `HunkResolution` (class) — Dataclass holding the resolution result for a single conflict hunk (validated 1-based line range, confidence, reasoning). <!--#b764faf99e100832-->
  - `HunkResolution.__post_init__` (method) — Validates the hunk's start/end line numbers and enforces end_line >= start_line, raising HunkValidationError on bad values. <!--#1014dae11a150b03-->
  - `HunkResolution._validate_line` (method) — Classmethod that coerces/validates a line-number field to a positive bounded int, rejecting None, bools, non-ASCII numerals, and out-of-range values. <!--#472cc527f6b2bbe5-->
- `FileResolution` (class) — Dataclass holding the resolution result for a single file (path, resolved content, hunks, confidence, flags, spec marker). <!--#3177741ae28eddb2-->
- `LLMResolution` (class) — Dataclass aggregating the complete LLM resolution result across all conflict files, with overall confidence, flags, and raw response/parse-error fields. <!--#43b3a064635d1b4c-->
- `BatchContext` (class) — Dataclass carrying merge-level metadata (branches, SHAs, logs, strategy) for a resolve_batch call, decoupled from the per-file list. <!--#ff3a9ad8b2a2f3ca-->
- `IterationFailure` (class) — Dataclass recording one iteration's failure mode and affected files, fed back into the next iteration's prompt instead of triggering take-theirs. <!--#0bfe4e4812133b90-->
- `BatchResolveOutcome` (class) — Dataclass summarizing a resolve_batch run: resolved/unresolved paths, iterations used, escalation reason, failure history, timing, and prompt/response previews. <!--#29444bc8647cbf34-->
  - `BatchResolveOutcome.success` (method) — Property returning True when no escalation occurred and no files remain unresolved. <!--#0d36d6f331e2183b-->
- `ConflictResolver` (class) — LLM-as-editor merge conflict resolver: given a three-way ConflictContext it drives bounded iterative LLM edit rounds over the working tree (via resolve_batch), judging success purely on whether conflict markers remain, and synthesises the result back into an LLMResolution that flags unresolved files for human review. <!--#6e37e277612675fa-->
  - `ConflictResolver.__init__` (method) — Constructs the resolver with a project root, optional shared LLMCaller/trace, and a positive resolved-content byte cap. <!--#24d0499556e2b012-->
  - `ConflictResolver.resolve` (method) — Thin wrapper that builds a BatchContext from a ConflictContext, runs resolve_batch, and synthesizes the result into an LLMResolution. <!--#a46441d349a1f254-->
  - `ConflictResolver._synthesize_resolution_from_outcome` (method) — Translates a BatchResolveOutcome into an LLMResolution, reading back on-disk content for cleared files and flagging unresolved or unreadable files for human review. <!--#1ffbb06151dfa253-->
  - `ConflictResolver.resolve_batch` (method) — Core iteration loop that repeatedly builds an editor prompt, calls the LLM, and rescans files for markers until resolved or max_iterations is hit, returning a BatchResolveOutcome with the appropriate escalation reason. <!--#009706a6d1f4d769-->
  - `ConflictResolver._build_editor_prompt` (method) — Builds the per-iteration LLM-as-editor prompt, assembling merge metadata, commit logs, spec-guardrail warnings, prior-iteration failure history, and per-file conflict hunk locations (paths only, never inlined file contents, to keep prompt size bounded). <!--#8c4c09b424ce42c0-->
  - `ConflictResolver._call_llm` (method) — Sends a prompt to the (shared or lazily-built) LLMCaller and optionally records a timed, redacted entry to the LLM trace. <!--#e893a70c18916891-->

### `src/se3/engine/merge/deterministic_resolvers.py` (python) — Defines the mechanical merge-conflict resolvers (code-index md entry-wise merge, `.next_id` max-counter) behind a `DeterministicResolver` protocol, plus the `resolve_deterministic` entry point that applies and stages what it can and hands the rest back to the LLM fallback. <!--#6aee0063cf97ef61|91a18b49771c6d4e-->
- `DeterministicResolver` (class) — Protocol defining a mechanical merge rule: a named resolver that claims some conflicting paths via `matches` and produces their merged content via `resolve`. <!--#479c430dab88c580-->
  - `DeterministicResolver.matches` (method) — Predicate stating whether this resolver owns the given repo-relative path. <!--#0710e1696ccd2fa0-->
  - `DeterministicResolver.resolve` (method) — Returns the merged content for a path (empty string means delete; raising means defer to the LLM). <!--#af369647c5627c88-->
- `DeterministicOutcome` (class) — Dataclass partitioning a conflict list into mechanically `resolved` paths, `remaining` ones left for the LLM, and per-path `failures`. <!--#d94121d2a12528a9-->
- `_git_show_stage` (function) — Reads a conflicted path's blob at a given merge stage as UTF-8 text, returning None when that stage is legitimately absent while letting git invocation errors propagate. <!--#f83f3331fee76e19-->
- `_git_add` (function) — Stages a path with `git add`, raising on failure. <!--#8bec845a81c24051-->
- `_git_rm` (function) — Removes and stages the deletion of a path with `git rm -f`, raising on failure. <!--#a0954d5a4eba66e4-->
- `FileBlock` (class) — Dataclass holding one code-index md entry — a file heading plus its symbol bullets and fingerprints — treated as the atomic, never-split unit of the index merge. <!--#d1b274542a59855a-->
- `_parse_md_blocks` (function) — Parses a rendered code-index md into its directory headings and per-file blocks, keeping lines verbatim so a parse→render round trip is byte-identical. <!--#47c54eb8fe12e873-->
- `_render` (function) — Rebuilds a full code-index md from directory headings and file blocks in `render_full`'s deterministic sorted order. <!--#15a81765fe17e8e0-->
- `_actual_content_fp` (function) — Recomputes the content fingerprint of a post-merge working-tree file (None if unreadable), used to adjudicate which side's index entry is current. <!--#3e68b3682946bf0d-->
- `CodeIndexResolver` (class) — Resolver that merges the two regenerated `se3/code-index.md` sides entry by entry, breaking ties by hashing the real post-merge file and defaulting to theirs rather than failing. <!--#2b79ac89f211c8d7-->
  - `CodeIndexResolver.matches` (method) — Claims exactly the code-index md path. <!--#998c18c440d85a04-->
  - `CodeIndexResolver.resolve` (method) — Parses both index sides, drops entries for files the merge deleted, adjudicates each surviving entry, and re-renders the merged index. <!--#2b0b6dfc8172a6ef-->
  - `CodeIndexResolver._pick` (method) — Chooses the winning FileBlock for one entry (and a reason string), preferring whichever side's fingerprint matches the working tree and otherwise falling back to theirs. <!--#8a47f64a5df8f74c-->
- `_parse_counter` (function) — Parses one side of the `.next_id` counter into an int, returning None when the side is absent or malformed. <!--#fac5586bf30c119c-->
- `NextIdResolver` (class) — Resolver that merges `se3/issues/.next_id` to the larger of the two counters so no already-allocated issue ID is reissued. <!--#f5fa3298b8e860ea-->
  - `NextIdResolver.matches` (method) — Claims exactly the `.next_id` path. <!--#6c227fc040fa8d8a-->
  - `NextIdResolver.resolve` (method) — Returns the maximum of the two readable counter sides, raising when neither side yields a usable value. <!--#5b04a1df110529a0-->
- `_find_resolver` (function) — Returns the first registered resolver claiming the path, or None. <!--#d0b1a44823e3efa8-->
- `resolve_deterministic` (function) — Public entry point that runs each conflict path through its registered resolver, staging what it can and returning the resolved/remaining/failures partition for the LLM fallback. <!--#224789a18bf1b44e-->
- `_apply` (function) — Writes and stages a resolver's output atomically — deleting on empty output, rejecting conflict markers, and restoring the original working-tree state if staging fails. <!--#0055c2fa4d5fd43a-->

### `src/se3/engine/merge/guardrail_repair.py` (python) — Module implementing GuardrailRepairer, which drives LLM-based repair of fast-mode spec guardrail violations by building a repair prompt from violations and spec contents, parsing the corrected JSON response, writing fixes back to se3/specs/**/spec.md, committing (fix-up or safely-amended) and re-verifying guardrails, with a strict amend/rollback safety contract, test-mode gating, and dedicated result/error types (RepairResult, parse-error, and inconsistent-state exceptions). <!--#dbb48c0557ca91b9|778140db357c6e4b-->
- `RepairResult` (class) — Dataclass holding the outcome of a repair attempt: success flag, repaired files, error text, whether amend was used, and files skipped for missing content. <!--#8a4277828d8b3791-->
- `_is_test_environment` (function) — Helper that detects whether code is running under a test harness via the PYTEST_CURRENT_TEST or SE3_GUARDRAIL_REPAIR_TEST_MODE env vars. <!--#1a59ca252d7b649f-->
- `GuardrailRepairResponseParseError` (class) — ValueError subclass marking that the LLM responded but its output could not be parsed as JSON, distinct from transport errors. <!--#5b0723fa04585374-->
- `GuardrailRepairInconsistentState` (class) — RuntimeError raised when rollback cannot be performed safely, carrying an INCONSISTENT_REPAIR_STATE failure reason to hard-stop the merge sequence. <!--#759538f0ae2a61a2-->
  - `GuardrailRepairInconsistentState.__init__` (method) — Constructor that sets the message and attaches the INCONSISTENT_REPAIR_STATE failure_reason enum. <!--#04d331b235aac86d-->
- `GuardrailRepairer` (class) — Main class that orchestrates LLM repair of spec guardrail violations—building prompts, writing corrections back, committing, and re-verifying—with test_mode safety gating. <!--#393d4bab6122927f-->
  - `GuardrailRepairer.__init__` (method) — Initializer storing project root, optional shared LLM caller and trace, and validating that test_mode is only enabled inside a real test environment. <!--#bd408905c6a97528-->
  - `GuardrailRepairer.repair_violations` (method) — Entry-point method that sends violations and spec contents to the LLM, validates the response, writes corrected files back, commits, and re-checks guardrails. <!--#47a45121494ff4e9-->
  - `GuardrailRepairer._probe_branch_verifiable` (method) — Helper that checks whether a branch is a verifiable git ref, treating timeouts and git failures as unverifiable so the silent-loss check fires conservatively. <!--#e085aa5ae817e2c5-->
  - `GuardrailRepairer._amend_preserved_merge_topology` (method) — Helper verifying an amended HEAD retains the original merge commit's parent set, distinguishing real topology violations from transient git failures. <!--#83a5eea5de34a7a7-->
  - `GuardrailRepairer._format_violations` (method) — Helper that renders the violation list (with evidence such as strong/weak lines, deleted clauses, and topology) into prompt text. <!--#f94d2d94be695007-->
  - `GuardrailRepairer._format_spec_contents` (method) — Helper that formats a path-to-content spec dict into a labeled text block for the repair prompt. <!--#84016bcd9d96a331-->
  - `GuardrailRepairer._restore_merged_content` (method) — Cleanup helper that best-effort restores merged spec content (or removes hallucinated tracked files) after a failed repair, re-raising the first restore error. <!--#429fea1c9124eae9-->
  - `GuardrailRepairer._rollback_commit` (method) — Helper that rolls back a repair commit by soft-resetting to the captured pre-repair SHA, refusing to use HEAD~1 and raising inconsistent-state when no safe target exists. <!--#b80f76abf1f4ffd9-->
  - `GuardrailRepairer._call_llm` (method) — Helper that invokes the LLM caller with the repair prompt, optionally records a trace, and extracts/validates the JSON response. <!--#6ced7b4774497bce-->
  - `GuardrailRepairer._parse_response` (method) — Helper that normalizes the LLM response (dict or string) into a parsed JSON dict containing a 'files' key, or None on failure. <!--#addb6af6de17705e-->

### `src/se3/engine/merge/guardrails.py` (python) — The merge-time spec-integrity guardrail module that detects deleted requirements, weakened SHALL/MUST language, and weakened quantifiers in changed `se3/specs/**/spec.md` files, exposing pure diff/size-check functions plus the `MergeGuardrailsCheck` orchestrator that validates merge topology and returns a fail-closed report. <!--#e28bd859f5ba97d0|b1a37a332205ddf6-->
- `_evidence_dict` (function) — Helper that builds a violation evidence dict via EvidenceRecord so unknown keys fail fast with a TypeError. <!--#eaa7ac8fdd6d88a4-->
- `GuardrailViolation` (class) — Dataclass representing a single guardrail violation with its file path, type, message, and diagnostic evidence. <!--#f07c968360073291-->
- `GuardrailReport` (class) — Dataclass holding the overall result of a guardrails check (passed flag, violations list, and fail-closed incomplete flag). <!--#f8059de2a6f52afd-->
- `_tokenize_for_pairing` (function) — Tokenizer that strips role words and stop words to extract content tokens for strong↔weak line similarity comparison. <!--#934ca71c228fe4c9-->
- `_tokenize_for_deduplication` (function) — Tokenizer that keeps role words (but drops stop words) so a strong line can be distinguished from its weakened variant during deduplication. <!--#cf6567000bdaf281-->
- `_jaccard_similarity` (function) — Computes Jaccard similarity between two token sets, returning 0.0 when either set is empty. <!--#b593fcbb81531c9e-->
- `_pair_strong_weak_lines` (function) — Greedily pairs missing strong lines with new weak lines by descending Jaccard similarity above a threshold, each line used at most once. <!--#66341ebe0796c5be-->
- `_extract_weak_role_word` (function) — Extracts the weak role keyword (e.g. SHOULD/MAY) from a line, or None if none is present. <!--#ac436197e33bb640-->
- `_weak_line_is_new` (function) — Determines whether a weak-only line is genuinely new (not a pre-existing or whitespace-only variant), treating a changed weak role word as new. <!--#f4d445ef165be61a-->
- `_precompute_orig_data` (function) — Precomputes stripped strings and both token-set variants for original lines to avoid re-tokenizing across pattern checks. <!--#04754242eadc2a13-->
- `_compute_pairing_evidence` (function) — Builds evidence for a strong→weak transition by pairing a disappeared strong line with a new weak-only (or optionally mixed) line via token similarity. <!--#3f633a92b160dd36-->
- `_first_missing_strong_line` (function) — Returns the first strong line that disappeared and its line number, used as minimal evidence for DELETE violations. <!--#8263d772aeedefff-->
- `_normalize_message` (function) — Normalizes a violation message for stable hashing by stripping line numbers, attempt counters, and SHA-like tokens while preserving counts. <!--#89507c9bc0b6dcf7-->
- `_stable_hash_short` (function) — Returns a short deterministic SHA-256 hex digest of text for sentinel keys. <!--#5c8683f0a1767008-->
- `_stable_key_from_violation` (function) — Derives a stable, format-insensitive hash key from a violation's evidence (strong/deleted/WHEN-clause lines), falling back to the normalized message. <!--#b16564cfe3c8a4d7-->
- `_normalize_for_comparison` (function) — Normalizes text into a sorted role/stop-word-free token string for identity comparison so role-word or punctuation differences collapse. <!--#01bfe89cc9fe74fd-->
- `violation_set_hash` (function) — Computes an order-independent stable hash over a set of violations from their file path, type, and evidence-derived stable key. <!--#8498b3f3ca3361dd-->
- `check_spec_diff` (function) — Core pure function that compares two spec versions and returns all weakening, quantifier-weakening, and deletion violations using two-layer detection. <!--#c35d13da507651d2-->
- `_rel_spec_path` (function) — Best-effort conversion of a spec path to a posix path relative to the project root. <!--#6f104b491084f943-->
- `check_spec_sizes` (function) — Pure, LLM-free check that walks every spec file and reports size-budget violations for base spec, per-file, and per-Requirement byte limits. <!--#0b377d27a9f7d4a0-->
- `_next_non_blank_line` (function) — Advances to the next non-blank line from a start index, raising StopIteration at end-of-file. <!--#3f4a6c956a546a12-->
- `_extract_when_clauses` (function) — Extracts WHEN clauses from spec lines, joining reflowed indented continuation lines to avoid spurious deletion detection. <!--#44a3d34afd8833b4-->
- `_normalize_when_clause` (function) — Normalizes a WHEN clause for identity comparison, preserving short tokens and role/stop words unlike the general normalizer. <!--#21c5f6075c9dd681-->
- `_is_spec_path` (function) — Canonical predicate returning True when a path matches `se3/specs/**/spec.md`, rejecting empty intermediate segments. <!--#faf60cbfd38edafb-->
- `ChangedSpecFilesIncomplete` (class) — Exception raised when the git diff for changed spec files fails, so callers fail closed instead of assuming no changes. <!--#31e4a8dbb4724810-->
- `_get_changed_spec_files` (function) — Returns the spec files changed between two git refs, distinguishing a real empty diff from a failed diff by raising ChangedSpecFilesIncomplete. <!--#54d50811dd02db3d-->
- `_read_file_from_ref` (function) — Reads a file's content from a git ref via `git show`, returning None when unavailable. <!--#858bd66e15a18942-->
- `_check_spec_file_against_ref` (function) — Compares a single spec file between an old and new ref (or worktree), emitting DELETE/CHECK_INCOMPLETE markers and delegating content checks to check_spec_diff. <!--#eb639d60c4d88238-->
- `_check_merge_topology` (function) — Validates that the post-merge commit is a descendant of the pre-merge HEAD and is a real merge commit (with opt-in fix-up tolerance), returning topology violations. <!--#ef56fdec0d6f393c-->
- `MergeGuardrailsCheck` (class) — Class orchestrating guardrail checks over the spec files touched by a merge between two commits, including merge-topology validation. <!--#b500f2c5e16d6cfa-->
  - `MergeGuardrailsCheck.__init__` (method) — Initializes the check with the project root path. <!--#fc13bde9d61f7a1d-->
  - `MergeGuardrailsCheck.check` (method) — Deprecated backward-compatible entry point that delegates to check_merge_result. <!--#3b0761d4bf0d92b5-->
  - `MergeGuardrailsCheck.check_merge_result` (method) — Lists changed spec files between two commits, validates merge topology, runs spec-diff checks on each, and returns a fail-closed GuardrailReport. <!--#ed91003073421d48-->

### `src/se3/engine/merge/human_call.py` (python) — Module providing the HumanCallWriter class and supporting helpers that write structured MCP human-call files (with collision-resistant names, atomic JSON writes, and orphan/guardrail evidence) to se3/calls/ when a merge conflict or post-merge guardrail violation requires human review. <!--#a64f40b367ffa284|76047dd2fafeb843-->
- `_reset_call_seq_after_fork_in_child` (function) — os.register_at_fork child handler that reinitializes the process-level call-sequence counter and its lock so a forked child cannot reuse the parent's seq values. <!--#93f0ed501bc55d98-->
- `_generate_call_filename` (function) — Builds a collision-resistant call filename from prefix, UTC microsecond timestamp, pid, an atomic sequence number, an 8-char SHA, and a sanitized branch label. <!--#c8159a35d9364bee-->
- `_atomic_write_json` (function) — Atomically writes call JSON via a temp file plus os.replace with fsync, symlink-refusal protection, and original-mode/0o644 permission preservation. <!--#b6cfa9d212432913-->
- `_read_original_for_orphan` (function) — Fetches a file's original content from base_ref (falling back to HEAD) via `git show` to support orphan guardrail diffing, returning None if absent. <!--#1a3016dadf670813-->
- `_is_spec_path` (function) — Thin delegator to guardrails._is_spec_path so spec-path detection (se3/specs/**/spec.md) stays canonical across the merge subsystem. <!--#85efc2ce33848333-->
- `_scan_orphan_content_for_evidence` (function) — Scans a rejected orphan file's resolved content for suspicious patterns (conflict markers, smuggled spec keywords, oversize, spec-like paths) and returns structured evidence for the reviewer. <!--#23ec339de6d50e50-->
- `HumanCallWriter` (class) — Class that writes MCP human-call files for merge conflicts and post-merge guardrail violations under a project's se3/calls/ directory. <!--#499a0803273b63c6-->
  - `HumanCallWriter.__init__` (method) — Stores the project_root path used to locate the se3/calls/ output directory. <!--#fc13bde9d61f7a1d-->
  - `HumanCallWriter.write_call` (method) — Assembles per-file conflict context plus LLM resolution proposals, validates orphan files against guardrails, and writes a merge-conflict human-call file. <!--#5b1a005995de8417-->
  - `HumanCallWriter.write_guardrail_call` (method) — Writes a human-call file for guardrail violations detected after a merge, validating violation dicts and embedding rollback/repair instructions. <!--#0e938f6d349fbff9-->
  - `HumanCallWriter.print_instructions` (method) — Reads a call file and prints user-facing instructions, response format, and a summary of violations/next steps to the console. <!--#1d1be8ad87b70e5b-->

### `src/se3/engine/merge/issue_renumber.py` (python) — Shared collection of pure primitives used by both `se3 merge` issue channels to renumber colliding issue IDs while preserving cross-references — rewriting standalone `#<old>`→`#<new>` reference tokens (individually, in order-independent bulk, or only on merge-added lines), scanning/allocating/advancing the fcntl-locked `.next_id` counter to keep IDs collision-free, and recording durable renumber-trace and ambiguous-reference audit notes that dedup logic can later parse, strip, or mask. <!--#084e5b101fc60458|4b27dd25df9bc4bb-->
- `_norm_id` (function) — Helper that coerces an issue ID given as a zero-padded string or int into its plain integer value. <!--#c0fe01f0b823bc4e-->
- `_issue_files` (function) — Generator yielding every `*.yaml` file under `se3/issues/{open,closed}/` in sorted (deterministic) order. <!--#da4d2cd801d7b63c-->
- `rewrite_issue_references` (function) — Rewrites standalone `#<old_id>` cross-reference tokens to a zero-padded `#<new_id>` within a scoped set of incoming-side issue files (matching by integer value), returning the count of references moved. <!--#34f281ccaada1eed-->
- `rewrite_issue_references_bulk` (function) — Applies a whole batch of `#<old>`→`#<new>` reference rewrites in one order-independent pass so chained pairs (e.g. 005→010, 010→011) don't cascade, returning the total references rewritten. <!--#454c84f1232614d5-->
- `_string_lines` (function) — Recursively yields every logical line of every string value nested inside a dict/list/str YAML node. <!--#f6fc170e8f103cba-->
- `count_reference_tokens` (function) — Counts standalone `#<digits>` tokens in a text string whose integer value equals a target ID, using the same boundary/zero-padding rules as the rewriters. <!--#686c93555aee3b3d-->
- `live_reference_count` (function) — Counts *live* `#<target_id>` references in an issue file, first stripping renumber-trace/ambiguity audit lines from the parsed YAML string values so historical records aren't miscounted. <!--#1f4efb96691e716c-->
- `rewrite_references_in_added_lines` (function) — For the committed-merge channel, rewrites `#<old>`→`#<new>` only on logical YAML lines the merged branch ADDED (per-occurrence membership against the pre-merge baseline), leaving pre-existing kept-side references intact, with a dry-run count mode. <!--#016ea1d58a8fd685-->
- `scan_max_issue_id` (function) — Returns the highest numeric issue ID present in the store, considering both each file's `NNN_` filename prefix and its parsed YAML `id` field. <!--#ada6637710240d46-->
- `resolve_issue_numeric_id` (function) — Resolves a single issue file's numeric identity, preferring the parsed YAML `id` field and falling back to the filename prefix, returning None if neither is present. <!--#9e9970c053f9c781-->
- `find_issue_id_owner` (function) — Scans the issue store for the file whose resolved numeric identity equals a target ID (skipping excluded files), used to detect a kept-side owner that must not be repointed. <!--#96416b36b0f0a141-->
- `reserve_next_id` (function) — The single atomic ID-allocation primitive: under the `.next_id` fcntl lock it reserves `max(counter, on-disk max+1)` and advances the counter, keeping all concurrent allocators (CLI/webui/discovery/merge) collision-free. <!--#6efcb28f40d7f798-->
- `advance_next_id_to_max` (function) — Monotonically pushes the `.next_id` counter up to at least `max(existing ID)+1` under the fcntl lock (never lowering an ahead reservation), so future allocations can't re-mint a renumbered file's number. <!--#a7927599059f4a29-->
- `format_renumber_trace` (function) — Renders the appended audit line (`旧号 #old → 新号 #new (se3 merge)`) recording an issue's old-to-new renumbering. <!--#052b50117286ac70-->
- `format_ambiguous_reference_note` (function) — Renders the durable Chinese-language note (`歧义引用 #005 → 候选 #011 / #012 (se3 merge)`) recording an unresolvable `#<old>` reference that had multiple renumber candidates. <!--#4df58f1b66be4165-->
- `append_description_note` (function) — Appends a note as a trailing line of an issue file's YAML `description` (leaving non-mapping files untouched) so it never shifts the title-deriving first line. <!--#72e70d953cfb5b7f-->
- `strip_renumber_traces` (function) — Removes every merge-machinery audit line (renumber traces and ambiguity notes) from a description so content-signature dedup stays match-stable across re-runs. <!--#e2b980dcd6ca5727-->
- `parse_renumber_traces` (function) — Extracts the recorded `(old, new)` renumber pairs from a description's trace lines so dedup can confirm that a digit change was an actual recorded renumber. <!--#9060d9f01f82ccb2-->
- `mask_issue_references` (function) — Replaces every standalone `#<digits>` token with a fixed `#REF` placeholder to give a rewrite-invariant (but coarse) signature key for shortlisting dedup candidates. <!--#eeacb0031c213645-->

### `src/se3/engine/merge/orchestrator.py` (python) — MergeOrchestrator module that sequentially merges branches into the current branch — driving git merge per branch, handling clean/conflict/failure outcomes via deterministic and LLM conflict resolvers, strategy decisions, runtime sync, issue renumbering, version aggregation, guardrail checks/repair and human-call escalation — plus helpers for the self-managed dirty-path whitelist (se3/issues/, se3/code-index.md) used in the pre-flight sync commit and an atomic file-write utility, returning a structured MergeReport to callers. <!--#b7eaf367ae19b68c|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/se3/engine/merge/reconcile.py` (python) — Merge-side version reconciliation core: collects the version intents emitted by worktree sessions and derives the final project version once at merge time against master's current version — via a deterministic max-bump channel, or an LLM channel when se3/version-rules.md exists — guarding against regressions/collisions, writing the changelog and reconcile commit, tagging, and marking intents consumed so re-entry never double-bumps. <!--#469dfbebdd7603d6|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/se3/engine/merge/runtime_sync.py` (python) — Post-merge synchronizer that copies git-ignored tier-A runtime content from a source branch's worktree into the current branch's se3/ directory, with hardened atomic writes (renameat2/RENAME_NOREPLACE to close symlink-swap TOCTOU windows), bounded per-file I/O caps, and issue-reference renumbering. <!--#7bc7eb9a0ed69189|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/se3/engine/merge/strategy.py` (python) — Defines the StrategyDecider and its DecisionAction/StrategyDecision types, encoding the safe/strict/fast decision matrix that translates an LLM conflict resolution's confidence and spec-guardrail signals into an accept, reject, or escalate-to-human outcome across both the legacy single-resolution and newer batch resolve-and-decide paths. <!--#a81da339556b94d6|fd94ea476199f009-->
- `DecisionAction` (class) — String enum of the three terminal decisions a strategy can reach: ACCEPT, HUMAN_CALL, or REJECT. <!--#bc263ff5be2b5d9d-->
- `StrategyDecision` (class) — Dataclass bundling a strategy's chosen action, a human-readable reason, and optional batch outcome / unresolved-file details for downstream orchestration. <!--#5a5765bc74c70683-->
- `StrategyDecider` (class) — Class that decides whether to accept, reject, or escalate a conflict resolution, dispatching across the safe/strict/fast merge strategies. <!--#28e18589511ef908-->
  - `StrategyDecider.decide` (method) — Legacy single-resolution entry point that routes an LLMResolution to the safe/strict/fast decision method based on the merge strategy. <!--#f9aaf33cc2ed29ae-->
  - `StrategyDecider._decide_safe` (method) — Safe-strategy logic that accepts a resolution unless explicit requires_human_review or spec_guardrail_concern flags (global or per-file) demand a human call. <!--#c9297b94ee3d7092-->
  - `StrategyDecider._decide_strict` (method) — Fallback strict-strategy logic requiring every hunk and overall confidence to be HIGH with no guardrail flags, else escalating to a human call. <!--#240c886d0f935bbd-->
  - `StrategyDecider._decide_fast` (method) — Fast-strategy logic that aggressively accepts non-spec files but rejects spec files on human-review or low-confidence signals, never calling a human. <!--#5e80c2888b04a526-->
  - `StrategyDecider.resolve_and_decide` (method) — Newer batch entry point that runs the resolver and dispatches to the per-strategy *_batch deciders, translating the outcome into a StrategyDecision. <!--#ea291ee351b07a3d-->
  - `StrategyDecider._run_resolver` (method) — Helper that drives ConflictResolver.resolve, builds a ConflictContext, and derives a BatchResolveOutcome (preferring an attached outcome or re-scanning for unresolved markers). <!--#c9c0ce846deffd61-->
  - `StrategyDecider._decide_fast_batch` (method) — Fast batch decider that ACCEPTs when all markers clear (subject to fast flag gates) and REJECTs on iteration exhaustion, never escalating to a human. <!--#0e356fb39af47485-->
  - `StrategyDecider._decide_safe_batch` (method) — Safe batch decider that ACCEPTs when all markers clear (subject to safe flag gates) and escalates to HUMAN_CALL on iteration exhaustion. <!--#3bb1d80eec3d777c-->
  - `StrategyDecider._decide_strict_batch` (method) — Strict batch decider that short-circuits the resolver and routes every conflict file straight to a human MCP call without invoking the LLM. <!--#49e4c40caceb9a2d-->

### `src/se3/engine/merge/version_aggregator.py` (python) — Computes each merged branch's SemVer bump by comparing pyproject.toml versions at merge-base versus branch tip, takes the maximum bump, and atomically rewrites the version while amending the last merge commit—with section/triple-quote-aware TOML parsing and fail-loud rollback handling for no-op, corrupt, and write/git-failure paths. <!--#61210775f690c3eb|d5342d20e0b318f0-->
- `VersionNotAdvanced` (class) — Documentation-only RuntimeError describing the fail-loud 'on-disk version already at or above target' condition that callers may raise instead of accepting a false success. <!--#147a2fa2febe45c7-->
  - `VersionNotAdvanced.__init__` (method) — Stores the pre-merge, current, and target version strings and builds the explanatory 'no bump applied' message. <!--#b12259069490d4d2-->
- `_slice_to_next_section` (function) — Returns TOML content from a section start up to the next line-anchored section header, skipping over triple-quoted strings. <!--#199ed868d02d591f-->
