- `_strip_triple_quoted_strings` (function) — Returns the content with all triple-quoted string blocks removed so embedded version-like literals aren't matched. <!--#f9d97057fabebb37-->
- `_find_triple_quoted_regions` (function) — Returns half-open (start, end) offset ranges of every triple-quoted block in the content. <!--#c934417522f7a342-->
- `_find_version_match_in_section` (function) — Returns the first `version = "..."` regex match that lies outside any triple-quoted region, or None. <!--#bfaf31411e2b9cdc-->
- `_parse_pyproject_version` (function) — Extracts the version string from pyproject.toml content, preferring [project] over [tool.poetry] with section and triple-quote awareness. <!--#a1708031992d7430-->
- `read_version_at_ref` (function) — Reads and parses pyproject.toml's version as it existed at a given git ref, returning None when absent or unparseable. <!--#dfc1c3ff78c29e16-->
- `_diff_bump` (function) — Returns the BumpType (MAJOR/MINOR/PATCH) going from a base Version to a branch Version, treating prerelease→release as PATCH and None when not advanced. <!--#0a2cdd1198ba4f38-->
- `InferResult` (class) — Dataclass pairing an inferred bump type (or None) with a human-readable reason string. <!--#4a852784336bceba-->
- `infer_branch_bump` (function) — Infers a branch's SemVer bump by comparing pyproject versions at the merge-base and branch tip, returning None (with a reason) on missing/unreadable/non-advancing versions. <!--#607a0a1cb38faaad-->
- `max_bump` (function) — Returns the highest-priority bump from a list, defaulting to PATCH for an empty list. <!--#ae0a425b7d47d771-->
- `AggregateResult` (class) — Dataclass capturing the outcome of aggregate_and_apply, including success, before/after versions, bump type, error, and the already-at/higher-than-target anomaly flags. <!--#5a2fc7e603d44e55-->
- `_atomic_write_text` (function) — Writes text to a path atomically via temp-file + fsync + os.replace, preserving mode, guarding against destination symlinks, and flushing the parent directory. <!--#a93e22e5d1af0a4a-->
- `_safe_write_version` (function) — Locates the version field's byte offset and rewrites pyproject.toml's version atomically, optionally reusing a caller-supplied content snapshot to avoid cross-read drift. <!--#fad8303d4e307893-->
- `_reset_staged_pyproject` (function) — Runs `git reset HEAD pyproject.toml`, logging and returning an error string on timeout/OSError/non-zero exit so a failed amend leaves no stale staged change. <!--#49cd07058d20978d-->
- `aggregate_and_apply` (function) — Top-level entry point that computes and applies the aggregated bump to pyproject.toml and amends the last merge commit, with rollback and fail-loud handling for no-op, corrupt, and write/git failure paths. <!--#496f8f107da329c8-->

### `src/se3/engine/merge/worktree_gc.py` (python) — Standalone garbage collector for leaked isolation-worktree (`se3 run --worktree`) runs that escape the normal finalize/merge cleanup — it enumerates terminal, over-age worktree runs and, per run, archives (a hard gate), promotes engine state, removes the directory, and deletes only provably-merged branches while always retaining and surfacing unmerged ones, returning a WorktreeGCReport and reusing the hardened cleanup primitives shared by the CLI and daemon triggers. <!--#69f39a587ecf88f9|7d405a8ae20dbbb6-->
- `WorktreeGCReport` (class) — A dataclass capturing the outcome of one worktree-GC sweep, recording what was archived, which unmerged branches were deliberately retained, bytes reclaimed, and runs skipped or errored. <!--#600549b447894cc5-->
- `_dir_size` (function) — Best-effort helper that totals the byte size of a directory tree (0 if missing), stat-ing symlinks without following them and skipping per-entry errors, for the reclaimed-space report. <!--#a78bc9d7c8d25026-->
- `_branch_is_merged` (function) — Fail-closed safety check that returns whether a branch is provably merged into its recorded original base, retaining the branch on any ambiguity and never falling back to HEAD. <!--#5ccdca4db8de2ca4-->
- `_load_worktree_header` (function) — Safely reads a worktree engine.json header dict, returning None (never raising) for corrupt/unreadable/non-object files so one bad state file can't abort the sweep. <!--#d353e352eaa27e5f-->
- `find_stale_worktree_runs` (function) — Enumerates terminal, over-age isolation-worktree runs eligible for GC by globbing worktree engine.json files and filtering on worktree-mode, terminal status, and mtime age. <!--#e13ded98fe332b32-->
- `gc_worktree_runs` (function) — The main GC entry point that reclaims leaked terminal worktree runs — archiving each (a hard gate), promoting its engine state, removing the directory, and deleting only provably-merged branches — returning a WorktreeGCReport, with a no-op dry-run mode. <!--#2884a8581498d1ab-->

## `src/se3/engine/steps/` — The flow-engine's step-handler package, which registers one handler per StepType (analyze, plan/plan_tasks, discovery, implement, commit, confirm, merge_integrate, project_summary, plus fix-loop guards adjudicate/invariant_check/charter_freshness) and their shared prompt/fix-context helpers, providing the concrete per-step logic — LLM prompt assembly, context injection, and COMPLETED/REVISION_NEEDED/PAUSED/FAILED routing — that drives a task from analysis through planning, implementation, review, and commit/merge. <!--#9992691038b146fc|f3da4e825e3e8a9d-->

### `src/se3/engine/steps/__init__.py` (python) — The step-handlers package init that imports every flow-engine step handler, assembles the STEP_HANDLERS registry mapping each StepType to its handler, and defines backward-compatibility stubs that forward deprecated PROPOSE/DESIGN/PROJECT_SUMMARY step types to their unified replacements so old persisted flows can still resume. <!--#9862f33d3a1e7c74|4b179c6ca8599baf-->
- `propose_stub_handler` (function) — Backward-compatibility stub for the deprecated PROPOSE step type that logs a warning and forwards to plan_handler so old persisted flows can resume. <!--#6fb89b174cba579c-->
- `design_stub_handler` (function) — Backward-compatibility stub for the deprecated DESIGN step type that logs a warning and forwards to plan_handler so old persisted flows can resume. <!--#ab925d0e54c6959b-->
- `project_summary_stub_handler` (function) — Backward-compatibility stub for the deprecated PROJECT_SUMMARY step type (now merged into ANALYZE) that logs a warning and forwards to project_summary_handler so old persisted flows can resume. <!--#0ddfcccc8427c3ad-->

### `src/se3/engine/steps/_fix_context.py` (python) — Shared helper module that renders the fix-loop context block for step LLM prompts, providing schema-tolerant extraction of issue display fields (severity/description/location), compact iteration-count formatting, and the multi-line fix-context prompt builder that deliberately omits fix_history to avoid biasing reviewers. <!--#879eff276f120e3b|e1e167a8536068b1-->
- `format_fix_iteration_display` (function) — Formats a fix iteration and cap as a compact `<n>/<cap>` (or `<n>/unlimited`) string for log lines. <!--#20f94d99307f7201-->
- `extract_issue_display_fields` (function) — Schema-tolerant reader that pulls (severity, description, location) out of an issue dict whether it uses the new self_check schema or the legacy verify_spec one, defaulting missing fields to empty strings. <!--#7c6be96c5a8cbcf4-->
- `render_fix_context` (function) — Builds the multi-line fix-context prompt block for a step (initial-pass message, iteration count, final-attempt warning, and previously-reported issues), deliberately omitting fix_history to avoid biasing reviewers. <!--#8395e1ce73d6743f-->

### `src/se3/engine/steps/adjudicate.py` (python) — Implements the ADJUDICATE step: it mines the cross-round contradiction ledger for oscillating/triggered/fixed-then-reopened quote positions, builds a ruling prompt from them plus the currently-effective task description, plan and charter, runs a bounded semantic-retry LLM loop until the ruling is actionable (rationale plus a covering override patch with well-formed covered surfaces), then writes the verdict and override into the step outputs and stages the abolish/reject ledger effects that are applied only once the ruling lands. <!--#c97fc2a0c2c4fe75|20fc08fcd2fb5c0d-->
- `_ledger` (function) — Returns the read-only cross-round ledger sub-tree from the flow's context, tolerating an absent/malformed ledger by yielding an empty dict. <!--#a23000ada9ea4ced-->
- `_active_nonrejected_observations` (function) — Filters the ledger's observations down to those still counting toward triggers — neither abolished nor at a position the adjudicator already ruled benign. <!--#6bd8662db445556a-->
- `_candidate_positions` (function) — Builds the prompt's candidate-contradiction list from quote-anchored positions showing ≥2 materially different expected behaviors (oscillation) unioned with explicit trigger positions, each carrying its per-round expected-behavior timeline. <!--#df54c70c6026d38e-->
- `_fixed_then_reopened` (function) — Collects positions the ledger declared 'fixed' yet flagged again (打脸), surfaced in the prompt as extra evidence of a real contradiction. <!--#e65ca03f02fe1187-->
- `_position_fingerprints` (function) — Returns all still-active fingerprints at the given positions so a ruling can abolish every ledger entry grounded on a clause it removed. <!--#204675b35520fea5-->
- `_latest_adjudicated_output` (function) — Walks a flow's step_history in reverse to return the most recent completed/partial ADJUDICATE step's non-empty outputs[key], optionally skipping one step to fetch the pre-ruling baseline value in effect before a given ruling. <!--#93446a9bdc495a63-->
- `_latest_adjudicated` (function) — Thin no-exclusion wrapper over _latest_adjudicated_output that returns the latest completed ADJUDICATE step's value for a given output key. <!--#a25efebee83b3080-->
- `_effective_task_description` (function) — Resolves the currently-effective pre-interjection base task_description (injected base, else the flow's recomputed effective base) so the LLM's corrected description installs cleanly at the base layer without duplicating interjections. <!--#b126a5ee450237a1-->
- `_effective_task_groups` (function) — Resolves the currently-effective plan task_groups for the ruling prompt, preferring injected inputs then prior adjudicated plan then the latest completed PLAN step's output. <!--#2fc438efc803e1be-->
- `_format_task_groups` (function) — Pretty-prints the plan task_groups as indented JSON (or a placeholder when empty) for inclusion in the prompt. <!--#230849a8084b858a-->
- `_format_candidates` (function) — Renders the candidate-contradiction list into human-readable prompt sections showing each candidate's file, quoted clause, and per-round expected-behavior timeline. <!--#57c3fe9b552bef33-->
- `_format_fixed_reopened` (function) — Renders the fixed-then-reopened rows into prompt bullets showing each location's quote and the behavior it was previously fixed as. <!--#9eba39a5beb13b74-->
- `_build_prompt` (function) — Assembles the full adjudication prompt by filling the template with trigger reasons, task description, task groups, candidates, and fixed-reopened rows, then best-effort appends the charter for hard-constraint conflict detection. <!--#c3d4c4fde16ef386-->
- `_normalized_covered_surfaces` (function) — Sanitizes an LLM ruling's optional `covered_surfaces` field into a stripped list plus a validity flag, treating absent/empty as valid but rejecting any malformed entry that lacks a non-blank `surface` or `justification`. <!--#ae4211ea6a12b908-->
- `_ruling_rejection_reason` (function) — Returns a human-readable string of why an adjudication ruling cannot land (missing rationale, missing covering override patch, malformed covered_surfaces) or None when it is actionable, and is the single source of truth reused in re-prompts and FAILED messages. <!--#fb808b08ca3e17e8-->
- `_normalized_overrides` (function) — Coerces and type-validates the ruling's two override fields into (description, plan), accepting only a non-empty string and a non-empty list respectively, else None. <!--#c4ed0a1f83c7869f-->
- `_ruling_is_actionable` (function) — Thin boolean wrapper over `_ruling_rejection_reason` telling whether a ruling is safe to land — every ruling needs a rationale, and any non-`review_divergence` verdict also needs a covering override patch with well-formed covered surfaces. <!--#070ee1eb2ae30e8e-->
- `_effective_source_pool` (function) — Builds the source-pool entries (task description plus each plan task's description and acceptance_criteria) that the adjudicated spec exposes to quote validation, mirroring self_check's composition. <!--#46089a1c99dd124e-->
- `_positions_with_dead_clause` (function) — Filters positions to only those whose quoted clause (via relaxed variants matching self_check) no longer appears in the now-effective source pool, so a preserved clause's oscillation history is not wrongly cleared. <!--#6e6fed5cdd78386d-->
- `adjudicate_handler` (function) — The ADJUDICATE step handler: builds a ruling prompt from the contradiction ledger and effective spec, calls the LLM with a bounded semantic-retry loop until the ruling is actionable (failing the step otherwise), then applies the ruling to the step's outputs. <!--#c541cf9cdf3bcc00-->
- `_coerce_override` (function) — Normalizes a nullable override field, treating empty or literal 'null'/'none' strings as absent so the effective-text layer falls through to the prior generation. <!--#3c6b688bb8a3aa34-->
- `_apply_ruling` (function) — Writes the LLM ruling into `step.outputs` and stages (but does not commit) its ledger side effects — taking a transparent no-op path for `review_divergence` verdicts and otherwise recording the override patch, rationale, covered surfaces, superseded fix instructions, and per-candidate contradiction/benign verdicts. <!--#0438bc10118c6a8d-->
- `apply_landed_ledger_effects` (function) — Idempotently applies a ruling's staged abolish/reject ledger effects to the persisted ledger, called by the state machine only once the ruling has landed (confirmed or免确认). <!--#5c06f6163813815e-->

### `src/se3/engine/steps/analyze.py` (python) — The ANALYZE workflow step handler that programmatically gathers project context and injects the charter plus a freshly-refreshed code-index map, makes a single LLM call to classify the task's type/scope/complexity, sanitizes and resolves the resulting task type (honoring --type and --discover overrides while coercing run-mode/invalid values to 'feature'), and persists it while re-deriving the flow's full step sequence. <!--#748c005274408868|f533634d2fb71b53-->
- `analyze_handler` (function) — The analyze step handler that collects programmatic project context, injects the charter and freshly-refreshed code-index map, makes a single LLM call to classify the task (type/scope/complexity), then resolves and persists the task type into flow state and step outputs. <!--#fbe46ff534197f3e-->
- `_extract_task_type` (function) — Extracts and validates the task_type from the LLM output, downgrading 'discovery' to 'feature' unless the --discover flag was explicitly set and defaulting invalid values to 'feature'. <!--#4b0f5f2da387e239-->
- `_sanitize_analyzed_type` (function) — Helper that extracts the LLM's real task type from the analyze output and coerces any run-mode value (e.g. 'discovery') or invalid value to 'feature', so the persisted analyzed_type is always a clean domain type. <!--#6204b5464e894ca4-->
- `_handle_type_conflict` (function) — Returns the explicit --type flag value when set, overriding the task type the LLM analysis resolved. <!--#581b4b10d216bb7d-->
- `_collect_project_summary` (function) — Gathers structured project context (git status, active flows, backlog, specs) via ProjectContextCollector and formats it into a concise text block, replacing the former PROJECT_SUMMARY LLM step. <!--#b083896bf9f5f700-->
- `_update_flow_steps` (function) — Rebuilds a flow's selected step sequence from the task type's default sequence, layering in configured optional steps, worktree merge steps, and confirmation steps so ANALYZE-time re-derivation preserves the full pipeline. <!--#c912381d1cdf7fa0-->

### `src/se3/engine/steps/charter_freshness.py` (python) — A never-blocking flow-end step handler that detects whether a diff touched the charter's three content classes and, only after a COMPLETED invariant_check, runs a self-contained propose→gate→apply closed loop (mechanical anchored-patch validation plus an admission size/altitude LLM gate) to auto-write se3/charter.md via an atomic temp-file rename, degrading fail-safe to advisory-only (charter untouched) on any failure while also firing the human-amendment monitoring trigger. <!--#8fec6c8bda8575e4|dd74b1d1d7f2a98f-->
- `_changed_files` (function) — Helper that extracts a flat list of changed file paths from the `changes_made` payload, tolerating both string and dict `files_changed` entry shapes. <!--#8b6c4d2c442424e0-->
- `_format_changes` (function) — Helper that renders the diff's changed-files list (with actions and explanations) into a human-readable string for the freshness prompt. <!--#63fed8bbe4faa206-->
- `_resolve_edits` (function) — Resolves a validated anchored-patch op list into concrete (start, end, replacement) spans against the text, mapping insert_after to a zero-width span after the anchor and replace to the span covering the quoted old text. <!--#ebae0c706a3c4db2-->
- `_validate_anchored_patch` (function) — Mechanically validates an anchored patch against the on-disk charter text — enforcing op/char bounds, verbatim-unique anchors and quoted deletions, and non-overlapping edits — returning (ok, human-feedable reason). <!--#e3a2b68097fb95e3-->
- `_apply_patch` (function) — Applies an already-validated anchored patch to the text in a single order-independent left-to-right pass, returning the candidate charter (unchanged for an empty patch). <!--#b78987f3e6bef80c-->
- `_atomic_write_charter` (function) — Atomically writes text to se3/charter.md via a same-directory temp file plus os.replace, so a crash never leaves a partially-written charter and no rollback machinery is needed. <!--#a34e9d9a77df07e2-->
- `_unified_charter_diff` (function) — Returns a unified diff of the charter (old -> new) for inclusion in the step outputs. <!--#c47d9ef3c0cb8701-->
- `_invariant_check_completed` (function) — Returns True iff the flow contains a COMPLETED invariant_check step, the precondition certifying the code change already passed review before an auto-update. <!--#d6aa1d92f36f9e30-->
- `_run_admission_trigger` (function) — Runs the non-blocking human-amendment monitoring gate (admission size check) when the diff directly edited se3/charter.md, annotating step.outputs with any monitoring-light warning. <!--#cee62ee094a8618e-->
- `_run_gate` (function) — Runs the two-part auto-update gate over the in-memory candidate — mechanical anchored-patch check, gating admission size red light, then the admission LLM gate for altitude/content-class and removal-weakening — returning (ok, candidate, verdicts, reason). <!--#153b3d3fa0568d07-->
- `_record_advisory` (function) — Records the advisory freshness output fields (charter_update_needed, touched_classes, reason, suggested_update) on the step from the propose response, defaulting them when no proposal exists. <!--#bee2ecd9ee971400-->
- `charter_freshness_handler` (function) — Non-blocking step handler that checks whether a flow's code diff touches the charter's content classes and, when an invariant_check has certified the diff, runs an LLM propose → gate → apply loop to auto-patch se3/charter.md — degrading to advisory-only output (and always returning COMPLETED) on empty diffs, missing preconditions, gate rejection, or LLM/parse errors. <!--#6003e77949e49488-->

### `src/se3/engine/steps/commit.py` (python) — Implements the flow engine's commit step: it stages and commits the flow's changes with a generated message, strips se3 runtime-leak paths, and for release-point flows writes the authoritative version, README badge and VERSIONS.md entry under a race guard that detects concurrent version drift and its own replays, plus fallback summary generation. <!--#deab156397ccf508|f4ec726d2e8c6583-->
- `_detect_runtime_leaks` (function) — Pure path-signature predicate that returns which staged paths carry an se3 runtime signature (a top-level `.se3/`, or a nested `se3`/`.se3` followed by a known runtime-subtree name) outside the legitimate top-level `se3/` root. <!--#c5e4e71e671d9029-->
- `_strip_runtime_leaks` (function) — Fault-tolerant backstop run between `git add` and `git commit` that unstages detected runtime-leak paths and warns, never failing the commit, returning whether any leak was found. <!--#2effffb256a8aef8-->
- `_index_has_staged_changes` (function) — Checks whether anything remains staged after leak-stripping, returning True (assume committable) on any git error so it never short-circuits a legitimate commit. <!--#4ef01544d2b8b91f-->
- `_root_deny_excludes` (function) — Helper that uses `git check-ignore -v` to confirm whether a given path is ignored specifically by the root `/*` default-deny rule (versus some ordinary gitignore rule), returning False fault-tolerantly on any subprocess error. <!--#114ca63636e40293-->
- `_detect_root_whitelist_exclusions` (function) — Diagnostic-only backstop run between `git add -A` and commit that enumerates top-level untracked paths swept up by the root `/*` whitelist rule and logs a single WARNING listing them, without modifying .gitignore, staging, or commit control flow. <!--#905992454b796cf0-->
- `commit_handler` (function) — The commit step's entry point: detects changes, and for release-point (non-worktree) flows writes the authoritative version, VERSIONS.md entry and Version: message line under a race guard, while worktree flows commit de-versioned with only bump-intent decoration. <!--#cee08ee190feb664-->
- `_load_version_config` (function) — Thin wrapper that lazily imports and loads the project's VersionConfig to avoid circular imports. <!--#4c9c3fe4b832d2e3-->
- `_resolve_target_version` (function) — Resolves the authoritative target version from the version_analyze step's suggested_version, raising RuntimeError (halting the commit) if that step failed or produced none. <!--#7106e85fbee3d03f-->
- `_normalize_version` (function) — Helper that canonicalizes a version string for equality checks by trimming whitespace and a leading v/V prefix, collapsing non-strings to an empty string that never matches a real version. <!--#b4d44c3588ab5143-->
- `_resolve_analyze_baseline` (function) — Resolves the disk-version reference the race guard compares against — version_analyze's observed current_version (which already includes this flow's own commits), falling back to the pre-session baseline and ignoring 'unknown' sentinels. <!--#072849081914d207-->
- `_version_at_commit` (function) — Reads and parses the version recorded in a version file at a given git commit (via git show of the blob through the same handler), returning None on any fault so callers never treat failure as a match. <!--#02c99b05464bcd10-->
- `_record_flow_committed_version` (function) — Best-effort persistence of the version this flow just committed onto durable flow state, so a re-entered commit step can later recognise its own already-landed bump even in script mode or when the Version: message trailer is absent. <!--#8a25545f1c7b008a-->
- `_flow_wrote_version` (function) — Determines whether this flow's own earlier commit already stamped a given version by matching commits carrying its Flow: trailer against the version-file blob (with a Version:-line grep fallback), distinguishing a legitimate replay/resume from concurrent drift. <!--#2a02d51857b6cb2a-->
- `_version_commit_already_landed` (function) — Decides, before this call commits anything, whether an earlier invocation of the same flow already committed the target version (via the durable flow marker or a git-durable Flow: trailer plus version-file blob probe), so the tag block knows if it is re-entering. <!--#8c921cf520cba0ae-->
- `_guard_version_race` (function) — Core race guard that returns the version to write: keeps the resolved target when the in-lock disk version matches version_analyze's observed baseline or is recognisably this flow's own replay/uncommitted-crash residue, and otherwise re-runs version_analyze against the drifted baseline to avoid colliding with a concurrent flow's bump. <!--#e5a3bd5f32bf478d-->
- `_reanalyze_version_with_baseline` (function) — Re-runs version_analyze against a drifted on-disk baseline and returns the recomputed version, forwarding the refreshed bump type, commit message, changelog entry and tag decision onto the commit step, or raising to halt rather than write a colliding version. <!--#240fba630f6287d0-->
- `_stage_file` (function) — Stages a single file via `git add`, resolving it relative to the project root and raising RuntimeError on failure. <!--#23f43a7c6b6b7a0b-->
- `_update_docs` (function) — Best-effort mechanical update of the README.md badge and VERSIONS.md changelog via DocumentationUpdater, staging both, swallowing any failure so docs never abort the commit. <!--#56d644ab0a00578e-->
- `_rollback_version` (function) — Restores the version file to its original value via VersionBumper.rollback, re-raising if the rollback itself fails. <!--#25140dabaebd94dc-->
- `_has_changes` (function) — Determines whether there is anything to commit, diffing a baseline commit against HEAD when available and falling back to `git status --porcelain`. <!--#c3879be18295377b-->
- `_generate_commit_message` (function) — Builds a git commit message string from flow/step context, choosing the subject line via a priority chain (version_analyze commit_message, plan proposal summary, implement summary, then a task-description template) prefixed with the real analyzed task type, and appending bump-type, changed files, incomplete tasks, version, and flow-id sections. <!--#6f8b772486c1b2ad-->
- `_read_head_commit` (function) — Reads HEAD's commit hash via git rev-parse, returning (hash, "") on success or (None, stderr) when unreadable so the caller decides whether that is benign or fatal. <!--#3a3c602382b7b733-->
- `_describe_head_location` (function) — Best-effort human-readable locator for HEAD (its branch name, or an honest "could not be determined") used in messages when HEAD's hash cannot be read. <!--#8e5ea0e472345a00-->
- `_generate_template_summary` (function) — Writes a Markdown work-summary document (task, type, commit hash, version, reasoning, commit message, changed files, and test results) to se3/state/summary-{flow_id}.md without an LLM call, as a fallback when no summarize step is present in the flow. <!--#a463772f2410045f-->
- `_collect_changes_from_flow` (function) — Gathers the list of changed file paths from all implement-step outputs in the flow history. <!--#9eb8c57d96e672be-->
- `_collect_test_results_from_flow` (function) — Returns the most recent test step's test_results dict from the flow history, or an empty dict if none exists. <!--#dc428ebd61d1ef28-->

### `src/se3/engine/steps/confirm.py` (python) — CONFIRM step handler that gates a prior step's output through either a synchronous LLM review (with iteration-cap auto-approval) or an asynchronous human review flow via call/response sidecar files, returning COMPLETED, REVISION_NEEDED, or PAUSED. <!--#1f485fff6f356940|ebc50be1da48293f-->
- `TimeoutError` (class) — Custom exception raised when polling for a human review response exceeds the allotted time. <!--#a6c6b7f03a421c70-->
- `_check_existing_response` (function) — Reads a `.response` sidecar file (if present) for a given call file and returns the parsed approval/feedback dict, used to detect human responses on resume. <!--#9723ee1681b75054-->
- `_wait_for_human_response` (function) — Blocks by polling for a human response file at a fixed interval, returning the response or raising TimeoutError when a timeout elapses. <!--#2d3854fcd84f716d-->
- `_create_call_file` (function) — Writes a timestamped JSON call file under se3/calls/ describing a CONFIRM step's pending human approval (flow/step ids, reviewed step type/id, prompt, CALL_KIND_CONFIRM discriminant, and for adjudicate reviews the extra ruling/diff/covered-surfaces context) and returns its path. <!--#0ccdc1d6e27d7fbc-->
- `_llm_review` (function) — Handler for a CONFIRM step that runs an LLM-based review of a prior step's output: it enforces a cross-revision iteration cap (auto-approving when exceeded), builds a plan-specific or generic review prompt, calls the LLM via LLMCaller, and returns a (StepStatus, review_result) tuple indicating approval or a request for revision. <!--#8631516078165616-->
- `confirm_handler` (function) — Top-level CONFIRM dispatcher that routes to synchronous LLM review or the human call-file/response flow, returning COMPLETED, REVISION_NEEDED, or PAUSED. <!--#8c46893f0eb1f6cb-->

### `src/se3/engine/steps/conftest.py` (python) — A pytest conftest that sets collect_ignore to exclude the step-handler implementation modules test.py and test_with_fail_loop.py, preventing pytest from mistaking their test-prefixed names for actual test modules/functions. <!--#93a55fa5e88f5424|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/se3/engine/steps/discovery.py` (python) — Implements the SE3 discovery step: a multi-turn, PAUSED-driven requirement-clarification conversation with the LLM that gathers project/recency context, asks clarifying questions, executes proposed issue operations, renders each round to the console, and ends at a programmatic confirmation gate (response "1") on the refined task description before the flow advances to analyze. <!--#d2497154d15a691c|796978823c2265e8-->
- `discovery_confirm_hint` (function) — Returns the i18n-rendered textual fallback hint ("type 1 to confirm") that accompanies the GUI confirm button at the discovery confirmation gate. <!--#ac0801c43937e9ce-->
- `discovery_confirm_metadata` (function) — Builds the (prompt, options) display metadata — a Markdown prompt carrying the proposed refined description plus a single one-click confirm option whose value is the normative "1" — for pausing a non-interactive discovery step at the programmatic confirmation gate. <!--#6cf5f054c946c924-->
- `_gather_project_context` (function) — Detects and formats basic project context (project type/name, test framework, git remote and branch) from files in the project root for inclusion in the discovery prompt. <!--#2efc5e2fb07052a6-->
- `_summary_recency_key` (function) — Computes a comparable epoch-float sort key for a `summary-*.md` file, parsing the filename's `YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS` timestamp as local time when present and otherwise falling back to file mtime so recency comparisons stay on a single numeric scale. <!--#cf902648d5769663-->
- `_collect_session_summaries` (function) — Reads the most recent `se3/state/summary-*.md` files (recency-ordered) and returns up to `limit` compact, capped excerpts (Task line + first body paragraph) in a best-effort, read-only manner for discovery's round-0 context. <!--#5992735f893dee56-->
- `_collect_recent_commits` (function) — Returns subject lines of the most recent non-merge git commits via `git log`, best-effort and read-only with a timeout, yielding an empty list on any failure. <!--#89f42ded4fd71f5c-->
- `_gather_recency_context` (function) — Combines recent session summaries and recent commits into a single titled Markdown "Recent Activity Context" block for round-0 discovery, returning "" when both sources are empty. <!--#63d5bacc3853f06b-->
- `discovery_handler` (function) — The discovery step handler: drives the multi-turn requirement-clarification conversation with the LLM (pausing via PAUSED between user turns), tracks round/history state, executes any LLM-proposed issue operations, and completes once the refined description is confirmed. <!--#17a38e550e914169-->
- `_run_discovery_round` (function) — Builds and sends one discovery-round prompt to the LLM (assembling history, round-0 recency, charter/code-index/language/runtime injections), then parses, validates against emptiness, and returns the structured result plus raw response text. <!--#4656dcdec2db4e27-->
- `_format_conversation_history` (function) — Formats the accumulated conversation history list into a plain ROLE: content text block for prompt inclusion. <!--#ce6ad351fc217e64-->
- `_format_issue_op_engine_note` (function) — Builds an engine note summarizing this round's executed issue operations and the current set of in-scope tracked issue IDs, to append to the conversation history for the LLM. <!--#15b7d36de96e91b3-->
- `_generate_summary` (function) — Produces a short summary string counting assistant rounds and user inputs from the discovery conversation history. <!--#3e9395a1b38195a0-->
- `_extract_narrative_from_raw` (function) — Strips fenced and bare JSON blocks out of the raw LLM result text to recover any surrounding narrative prose for display. <!--#951c0061d894ad35-->
- `_proposed_description_block` (function) — Wraps the LLM's proposed refined description in a nested cyan se3 reverse-color block (title, Markdown body, footer) so it has clear visual boundaries inside the Discovery output. <!--#fa9ca2df0d140335-->
- `_display_discovery_message` (function) — Renders a discovery round to the console as a Rich group — narrative, content, proposed-description block, questions, issue-operation summary, and a token-usage footer — varying layout by question / synthesis / confirmation mode. <!--#7ca3c569c79fdd8e-->

### `src/se3/engine/steps/implement.py` (python) — The implement step handler that drives LLM-based (claude -p, TWO_PHASE JSON) code generation for task groups across a dependency DAG, handling worktree creation/merging, stash conflict resolution, disaster-recovery pruning of completed groups, and the test-verify-fix loop, subject to version-file and why-comment prompt guardrails. <!--#721f3e74bac0c3c6|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/se3/engine/steps/invariant_check.py` (python) — Implements the anchored INVARIANT_CHECK step handler, which audits a flow's diff against an explicitly-recorded, flow-start-frozen anchor set (task text, charter, and the touched code's why-comments), cheap-passing when there is no diff or no anchors, raising REVISION_NEEDED for surviving verbatim-grounded violations plus hard-guarded deletions/rewrites of MARKED (WHY:/INVARIANT:) comments, and advisorily LLM-triaging unmarked comment losses into step outputs without spinning the fix loop. <!--#be59c3b06c6f460b|2295e0f6fd3f3363-->
- `_is_marked_why_comment` (function) — Predicate that returns true when a marker-stripped comment body carries an explicit WHY:/INVARIANT: tag (case-insensitive, colon required), marking it as machine-protected. <!--#3f87b85f4e531865-->
- `_extract_comments` (function) — Best-effort textual harvest returning the bodies of single-line `#`/`//` comments from a block of text. <!--#90739f6db8d26015-->
- `_read_baseline_file` (function) — Reads a file's original pre-implementation content at the flow's frozen baseline commit via `git show`, returning None when there is no baseline or the file is unavailable. <!--#2e17a8cbfdf0c653-->
- `_harvest_why_comments` (function) — Collects colocated why-comments from each touched file, merging baseline and working-tree content so original invariant-documenting comments survive even if the diff deleted or rewrote them. <!--#d9851e8426c286b3-->
- `_deleted_comments_by_file` (function) — Best-effort per-file multiset diff of colocated comments between the frozen baseline commit and the working tree, returning comments present at baseline but now deleted or rewritten. <!--#faba99f56dee4fa3-->
- `_marked_comments_with_pos` (function) — Extracts each MARKED (WHY:/INVARIANT:) comment from text as (line_index, body) tuples, without inspecting surrounding code, for use in positional pairing. <!--#685db2c13a1cd060-->
- `_rewritten_marked_exemptions` (function) — Computes per-file counts of deleted marked comments that are exempt from the hard guard because they pair one-to-one (by text similarity then proximity) with a newly added/rewritten marked comment in the SAME file. <!--#a892ed9438e81979-->
- `_build_why_comment_guard_issues` (function) — Synthesizes anchored REVISION_NEEDED issues for each deleted/rewritten marked WHY:/INVARIANT: comment, minus those covered by same-file re-declaration exemptions (缺口二 hard guard). <!--#a50d5679d32c8e02-->
- `_build_anchor_inputs` (function) — Assembles the synthetic step_inputs (task text, charter, why-comments, changed files) that drive self_check's validators, sourcing anchors from frozen step inputs with on-disk/harvest fallbacks. <!--#69b66727417e5344-->
- `_anchor_pool_is_empty` (function) — Returns True when the frozen anchor set normalizes to no usable text, signaling the anchor-less case where the check must be refused. <!--#1bdb8c1632821713-->
- `_format_deleted_comments_block` (function) — Renders unmarked deleted comments grouped by file into a markdown block for the advisory LLM re-judge prompt. <!--#7fdccd42842a50bc-->
- `_rejudge_why_losses` (function) — Advisory-only, never-raising LLM triage that filters unmarked comment deletions down to meaningful why/intent losses destined for step.outputs only (never the fix loop). <!--#a58118bb188c7f23-->
- `_has_changed_files` (function) — Returns True iff the `changes_made` payload reports at least one changed file/path. <!--#cbe8e49e3e236b70-->
- `_format_changes` (function) — Renders the diff's changed-file list into prompt text mirroring self_check's view. <!--#68b655da37aa3b06-->
- `invariant_check_handler` (function) — Top-level step handler that audits the diff against recorded anchors (charter/why-comments/task), returning COMPLETED on cheap passes or clean audits and REVISION_NEEDED on surviving violations or guarded marked-comment deletions. <!--#e2129c98943b616e-->
- `_build_fix_outputs` (function) — Populates the step's fix-loop outputs (issues, fix instructions, iteration counts) from validated invariant violations and returns REVISION_NEEDED, mirroring self_check's fix output shape. <!--#259888a25e114e3e-->

### `src/se3/engine/steps/merge_integrate.py` (python) — Step handler that performs the integration half of a worktree flow — resolving the main checkout (fail-loud if the isolation worktree would be used by mistake), delegating the actual branch-into-master merge to se3.engine.merge.integrate under the already-held lock with deletion deferred, and mapping success to COMPLETED and failure/human-escalation to FAILED so version_reconcile never runs for work that didn't land. <!--#964eb2b72946be21|b156ff6df3aed18c-->
- `_resolve_merge_root` (function) — Resolves the main-checkout root a merge step operates on, preferring the step's `cwd` override and otherwise strictly probing the main repo, failing loud with `MergeCheckoutResolutionError` rather than silently degrading to the isolation worktree. <!--#21523518f4d5d095-->
- `merge_integrate_handler` (function) — Step handler that integrates the flow's isolation branch into master by delegating to `se3.engine.merge.integrate` (with the lock already held and deletion deferred), records the structured result on the step, and maps success to COMPLETED and failure/human-escalation to FAILED so `version_reconcile` never runs for unmerged work. <!--#b9f16e3228224e48-->
- `_summarize_result` (function) — Helper that extracts a JSON-safe dict summary of a `MergeResult`'s key fields (coercing enums/paths to strings) for storage on step outputs and history. <!--#b71352e034b521c0-->

### `src/se3/engine/steps/plan.py` (python) — The unified 'plan' step handler module that, in a single depth-adapted LLM call (depth chosen from task_type), builds a prompt composing proposal/design/task-group sections plus the matching JSON schema — with charter, code-index, language, issue, and runtime injections — then parses and stores the resulting plan (proposal, design, task groups) on the step outputs and renders it to the console via Rich formatters. <!--#031b209098efad7d|a8c2aea47989b8ff-->
- `_get_prompt_depth` (function) — Maps a task_type string to a prompt-depth level ('full' for feature/discovery, 'medium' for bugfix, 'shallow' otherwise). <!--#ce8cd3dfad9063df-->
- `_build_prompt` (function) — Assembles the final plan prompt by composing the header with proposal/design/tasks sections and the matching JSON schema according to the chosen depth. <!--#739f8fa1c96d7334-->
- `plan_handler` (function) — The handler for the unified 'plan' step that, in a single depth-adapted LLM call (with charter/code-index/issue/language/runtime injections), generates and stores the full plan (proposal, design, task groups) on the step outputs, returning COMPLETED on success or FAILED on missing input or errors. <!--#ddca62978c2788fc-->
- `_display_plan` (function) — Renders the generated proposal, design, and task groups to the console using Rich formatters for human-readable output. <!--#4d18d096d6926809-->

### `src/se3/engine/steps/plan_tasks.py` (python) — Flow-step module that breaks an implementation into logical, verifiable task groups: its handler assembles a design/proposal/spec prompt (augmented with charter, code-index, discovery, and revision injections), calls the LLM, and stores the parsed task groups and complexity estimates, with helpers that render the design doc and proposal into prompt text. <!--#ca86700f219dd22f|082d773d725c8833-->
- `plan_tasks_handler` (function) — The handler for the plan_tasks flow step: it assembles a prompt from the design doc, proposal, and spec content (synthesizing a minimal design when the DESIGN step was skipped), augments it with charter/code-index/issue-discovery/revision injections, calls the LLM to break the work into task groups, and stores the parsed task groups and complexity estimates as step outputs. <!--#a255324e82e7a76c-->
- `_format_design_doc` (function) — Helper that renders a design-document dict into a readable prompt string covering overview, key decisions, components, and implementation plan. <!--#408d2cc21b753960-->
- `_format_proposal` (function) — Helper that renders a proposal dict into a prompt string summarizing the proposal and the files to modify and create. <!--#8f0ab84037ee5337-->

### `src/se3/engine/steps/project_summary.py` (python) — Defines the PROJECT_SUMMARY flow step, which collects raw project context (git status, flow engine state, backlog, specs) via ProjectContextCollector and calls the LLM to produce a concise natural-language project summary that downstream steps and the `se3 summary` CLI command reuse. <!--#87a77e1e3755f333|90d3d47590cc5270-->
- `generate_project_summary` (function) — Shared core function that collects raw project context, formats it into the summary prompt, and calls the LLM to return a natural-language project summary. <!--#574424aa7919551e-->
- `project_summary_handler` (function) — Step executor that runs the project summary generation for a flow, stores the result in step outputs, and returns COMPLETED or FAILED. <!--#4b56d7159393f684-->

### `src/se3/engine/steps/self_check.py` (python) — Implements the SE3 self_check flow step: after tests pass, it builds an LLM code-review prompt from the changes, test results, specs, plan task groups, charter, and code-index, then structurally validates each returned issue (verbatim-quote source-pool matching, evidence grounding, out-of-scope/regression handling) and deduplicates, tracks fix-loop convergence, and emits COMPLETED when clean or REVISION_NEEDED with consolidated fix instructions when grounded logic/robustness/test-coverage issues remain. <!--#7bfe118d1d7b545f|aaf392b54f735593-->
- `_normalize_for_quote_match` (function) — Symmetrically normalizes a string (literal-\n expansion, NFKC, smart-quote folding, whitespace collapse) so an LLM's verbatim_quote can be substring-matched against the source pool despite cosmetic drift. <!--#8db8997a3a87e3a5-->
- `_build_source_pool` (function) — Assembles the list of source strings (effective/base task description, non-superseded original, user interjections, project spec content, and per-plan-task text) against which self-check issues' verbatim_quote is validated, dropping original and abolished-clause-restating entries when an adjudication ruling is in effect. <!--#0a8de7726397d558-->
- `_changed_paths` (function) — Extracts the set of changed file paths from changes_made.files_changed, tolerating string or dict entries and malformed input. <!--#8ff815377519db66-->
- `_validate_evidence` (function) — Returns True when a self-check issue carries usable grounding — a well-formed `path:N` line in a changed file, or (unless require_changed_line is set for regressions) a non-empty `missing_in` entry. <!--#639d2bbd6eb53a6b-->
- `_describe_issue` (function) — Renders a kept issue as a single bullet line (location plus actual/expected/divergence) for the fix_instructions output. <!--#3a2af65715d0ea40-->
- `_validate_and_filter_issues` (function) — Runs each raw LLM issue through the structural validation pipeline (out-of-scope drop, verbatim-quote presence and source-pool substring match, evidence grounding, non-empty behavior fields), exempting regression issues from quote checks, and returns the kept issues plus per-rejection-reason stats. <!--#9818379abdb208fd-->
- `_count_tasks` (function) — Counts well-formed (dict) tasks across all plan task_groups, used for sharing the rendering character budget. <!--#610c0f458e29ace2-->
- `_render_task_groups` (function) — Renders task_groups as a Markdown summary at a selectable detail level, optionally including acceptance criteria and capping each description to a character limit. <!--#ac7f3e94a00efea7-->
- `_format_task_groups` (function) — Produces the task_groups Markdown section for the prompt, degrading detail (drop acceptance criteria, then cap descriptions) under the char budget rather than ever hiding a whole task from the per-task audit. <!--#3389c51d1a5b2a9d-->
- `_build_task_groups_section` (function) — Wraps the task-groups Markdown summary in its `## Plan Task Groups` prompt section, or returns empty string to avoid an orphan heading. <!--#fd3b5a4b04262bff-->
- `self_check_handler` (function) — The self_check step entry point that builds the review prompt (changes, tests, specs, plan tasks, charter, code-index) and calls the LLM to find logic/robustness/test-coverage issues, returning COMPLETED when clean or REVISION_NEEDED when issues remain. <!--#7c6643585304802d-->
- `_normalize_description` (function) — Normalizes a free-text issue description (lowercase, strip punctuation, drop stopwords, sort tokens) so paraphrased issues compare equal during convergence detection. <!--#37733267f0004aa3-->
- `_issue_signature` (function) — Computes a set of (location, normalized-description) signatures for a list of issues, handling both new and legacy schemas, for dedup and convergence detection. <!--#d3cc36127f3969cb-->
- `_merge_dedup_issues` (function) — Merges incoming issues into an existing list, dropping mechanical duplicates by signature while keeping signature-less issues. <!--#764d50d7676ea599-->
- `_has_critical_or_high` (function) — Returns True if any issue in the list is of critical or high severity (case-insensitive). <!--#a3574497faf32b13-->
- `_build_fix_outputs` (function) — Populates the step's consolidated fix-loop outputs (fix_instructions, issues, iteration counters) from the accumulated issue set and returns REVISION_NEEDED. <!--#13a9625d04f948ee-->
- `_identity_tokens` (function) — Returns the set of lowercased, deduplicated word tokens (length > 2) of a text, used as the substantive-word signal for summary↔issue overlap scoring. <!--#dcb01860855ff330-->
- `_issue_identity_tokens` (function) — Extracts the discriminating identity tokens of a previous issue from its quote, expected/actual behavior, divergence, and evidence file paths so a resolution summary can be content-matched to the correct prior issue. <!--#1ab08d617d9501a4-->
- `_pair_resolutions_with_prev` (function) — Pairs each LLM previous_issue_resolution verdict with the prior issue it refers to via ordered positional matching guarded by token-overlap content scoring, only when counts match and the positional partner is a (co-)best match, so reordered or drifted resolutions don't stamp verdicts onto the wrong issue's fingerprint. <!--#2028939d3ee43f98-->
- `_issues_converged` (function) — Returns True when the current issues largely repeat the previous set (by signature subset or shared locations), signaling the fix loop has stalled. <!--#b28509e30f468b66-->
- `_format_changes` (function) — Formats the changes_made dict into a human-readable bulleted list of changed files for the prompt. <!--#2f76c452cbec9dff-->
- `_format_test_results` (function) — Formats test_results (phased or flat) into a prompt-ready text summary including pass/fail status and truncated stdout/stderr tails. <!--#094f63f9a19ee178-->
- `_format_spec_content` (function) — Formats spec_content (string or name→content dict) into a Markdown-sectioned block for the prompt. <!--#5b2f381c19897610-->
- `_format_fix_context` (function) — Thin wrapper delegating fix-context rendering to the shared render_fix_context helper, inlining previous issues for the self_check prompt. <!--#ac764dd7d21d35f4-->

### `src/se3/engine/steps/summarize.py` (python) — The summarize step handler that generates an end-of-session report by gathering prior-step results (changes, test/verification verdicts, and knowledge-guard outputs), building an LLM prompt, calling the LLM to produce a natural-language summary saved under se3/state/, and falling back to a deterministic basic summary on failure—while never claiming completion for unverified work. <!--#51f1045991ef70d8|d02b02e93bc09f76-->
- `summarize_handler` (function) — The summarize step's entry point: gathers prior-step results, builds an LLM prompt (with completion status, verification verdict, and knowledge-guard section), calls the LLM to generate a session summary, saves it, and falls back to a deterministic basic summary on any failure while still marking the step COMPLETED. <!--#a43a3143a13c8121-->
- `_format_changes` (function) — Renders the changes_made dict into a Markdown bullet list of modified files, tolerating both plain-string paths and structured change dicts. <!--#e9f2222313255a7b-->
- `_gated_tests_passed` (function) — Returns the gated test pass/fail verdict, preferring critical-acceptance-gated `overall_passed` over the legacy raw `passed` key so skipped critical tests aren't reported green. <!--#b3909e825e66b5f8-->
- `_format_test_results` (function) — Formats test results into a one-line 'Tests passed: <bool>' string using the gated verdict. <!--#fc3da81113dda393-->
- `_format_verification` (function) — Formats the verification_result dict into prompt text covering the verified flag, summary, and issue/error counts. <!--#d8353e5d6198d067-->
- `_collect_knowledge_guard_outputs` (function) — Scans the flow's completed steps to pull charter_freshness outputs and invariant_check why-comment losses (last-occurrence wins), returning them as a tuple so summarize can report knowledge-artifact guard results self-contained. <!--#6ef47fbaa7333440-->
- `_format_why_loss` (function) — Renders a single removed/rewritten why-comment advisory entry (file, comment, why-it-matters) as one markdown line. <!--#68efd30d25c0c676-->
- `_format_knowledge_guards` (function) — Builds the flow-level 'Knowledge Guards' markdown section covering charter auto-updates, charter update advisories, and why-comment losses, returning an empty string when nothing occurred. <!--#ffea6eacea1f0f3e-->
- `_resolve_verified` (function) — Extracts the authoritative boolean `verified` verdict from verification_result, returning None when no verify_spec step ran. <!--#f1b90fb72a3da192-->
- `_verification_gate_lines` (function) — Returns prompt instruction lines forbidding 'complete/all-green' claims, but only when verification explicitly failed (verified is False). <!--#77b6a8199fa1459e-->
- `_build_completion_section` (function) — Assembles the optional completion-status prompt section (incomplete tasks, restricted edits, and the verification gate), returning empty for the clean complete-and-verified case. <!--#7577870ce91e6575-->
- `_create_basic_summary_text` (function) — Constructs a deterministic fallback Markdown summary (status, changed files, incomplete tasks, testing status, handoff, and knowledge guards) used when LLM summary generation fails or returns empty, honoring the verification verdict so unverified work is not claimed complete. <!--#35166e333a1d36d3-->
- `_save_summary` (function) — Writes the summary text to `se3/state/summary-{flow_id}.md` with header metadata, logging a warning on failure. <!--#c990539ad0295730-->

### `src/se3/engine/steps/test.py` (python) — The non-LLM test step handler that auto-detects/runs the configured test command and phases, classifies results into new-test vs regression and inherited (baseline) vs introduced failures, applies critical-acceptance and dynamic-timeout gating with a bounded baseline fix loop, and returns a shared TestVerdict consumed identically by both the test step and the SPEC_GATE. <!--#9fa6638633d29442|e04201ea4a2400cc-->
- `TestVerdict` (class) — Dataclass capturing the classified result of one test-suite run (results dict, pass flag, fix trigger, fix guidance/context, inherited failures), shared so the test step and SPEC_GATE consume one identical verdict. <!--#2fe28d757ce5a9dd-->
- `_extract_failures_section` (function) — Extracts the pytest FAILURES/ERRORS diagnostic section from stdout, per-block-truncating it to fit a character budget while preserving assertions and traceback tails. <!--#48ac6719f45bd66e-->
- `_parse_test_summary_counts` (function) — Best-effort parses aggregate passed/failed counts from a runner's summary line (pytest/cargo/jest) when per-test lines are unavailable, summing across multiple summary lines. <!--#268b30edce88f897-->
- `_summarize_passed_phase_output` (function) — Builds a compact archive summary (count line plus output tail) for a PASSED phase's otherwise-noisy verbose stdout/stderr, using a three-tier count fallback. <!--#1659723ff3b743eb-->
- `_slim_passed_phase_archive` (function) — Mutates a test_results dict in place to replace each passed phase's (and the top-level) stored stdout/stderr with the slimmed summary, leaving failed phases intact. <!--#c54a963da6a47643-->
- `_render_estimate` (function) — Formats an estimated_test_duration value for display, rendering whole floats as ints and None as 'not set'. <!--#ab9da39a8180758d-->
- `test_handler` (function) — The test step entry point: a thin shell that loads config, runs+classifies via run_and_classify_tests, then writes outputs, records history, files the once-per-flow inherited-failure issue, and maps the verdict to a StepStatus. <!--#4e502bca496a33cc-->
- `run_and_classify_tests` (function) — The shared core that runs the primary command plus configured phases with dynamic timeout, applies the critical-acceptance gate, splits inherited vs introduced failures, applies bounded baseline looping, and returns a TestVerdict. <!--#15856b5e490f16e0-->
- `_build_baseline_fix_section` (function) — Constructs the prepended fix-instruction text (mechanism B) listing active baseline failures the fix loop must also repair, with a tightly-scoped relaxation of focus limits. <!--#89d08ebc963cfce8-->
- `_extract_failure_reason` (function) — Extracts a brief failure reason string for a given test id from pytest's short summary output, falling back to a generic message. <!--#8b7946881d8e5999-->
- `_report_pre_existing_issues` (function) — Files inherited (pre-implement baseline) test failures as a single medium-priority A-class discovery issue, relying on the caller for the once-per-flow guard. <!--#11f4592b36f9fb6f-->
- `_is_timeout_result` (function) — Classifies a command result as a timeout-class failure via the structured flag, stderr marker, or -1 returncode sentinel, short-circuiting to False for any passing run. <!--#5cf69f14034df1cf-->
- `_run_command_with_timeout_retry` (function) — Runs a command and, on a timeout-class failure only, retries it once in place (without incrementing the fix iteration), returning the result and whether a retry occurred. <!--#118ae307f8169959-->
- `_run_command` (function) — Runs a test command as a subprocess in the given working directory with a live dot-progress indicator, guarding against recursive se3-invoked test runs via the SE3_TEST_RUNNING sentinel env var, and returns a result dict (command/returncode/stdout/stderr/passed/timed_out) using distinct sentinel return codes for timeout (-1) versus spawn failure (-2). <!--#daf630ebf436dcf0-->
- `_classify_results` (function) — Splits parsed test ids into new_tests vs regression buckets (passed/failed) based on whether each id matches the implement step's added test files. <!--#1198d5758658cb17-->
- `_parse_test_ids` (function) — Parses individual (test_id, passed) tuples from pytest/jest/go/cargo runner stdout, trying each format in turn. <!--#b0d7d24039c585c4-->
- `_parse_skipped_test_ids` (function) — Parses deduplicated SKIPPED test ids from pytest verbose per-test output (ignoring the -rs short-summary form that lacks the file::test form). <!--#aff2a440b23db006-->
- `_critical_pattern_matches` (function) — Returns whether a critical-test pattern matches a test id by substring (covering exact and prefix forms). <!--#ec1772ef7be60c0f-->
- `_detect_critical_failures` (function) — Detects critical acceptance tests that were skipped or silently un-collected/missing (which would otherwise exit 0 falsely green), returning the skipped and missing lists. <!--#37c95ee988a1a3c4-->
- `_is_pytest_command` (function) — Heuristic check for whether a command invokes pytest (bare, path-suffixed, or via python -m pytest). <!--#daec89699f707a0a-->
- `_ensure_verbose_pytest` (function) — Appends -v to a pytest command when critical tests are configured but no verbose flag is present, so per-test SKIPPED lines become parseable (warning if the command isn't pytest). <!--#a56631f4701dbfd3-->
- `_resolve_cwd` (function) — Resolves a phase's optional cwd to an absolute path relative to the project root. <!--#df0454357359e938-->
- `_detect_test_command` (function) — Auto-detects the test command from project marker files (pyproject/pytest.ini → pytest, package.json → npm, Cargo.toml → cargo, go.mod → go), defaulting to pytest. <!--#2ffafee5e990e5d8-->
- `_record_test_history` (function) — Records the test execution as synthetic prompt/response entries in the chat-history system so results persist across worktree isolation and fix-loop iterations. <!--#f051597e9473e28c-->

### `src/se3/engine/steps/test_version_reconcile.py` (python) — Test suite for the version-reconcile merge step, covering the deterministic, custom-rules (LLM), and no-op channels along with annotated-tag creation, changelog merging into VERSIONS.md, no-regression/anti-collision validation, and error paths such as git timeouts, tag failures, and unreadable reconcile commits. <!--#ac15a4c2375749b6|3dab93d7b9401761-->
- `_git` (function) — Test helper that runs a git subcommand against a given repo root and returns the completed process. <!--#9f1bc200ef078687-->

- `test_deterministic_no_bump_no_substance_leaves_version_unchanged` (function) — Verifies an intent with no bump and no changelog substance leaves the version unchanged yet still consumes the intent and creates a reconcile commit. <!--#0f950607343703d2-->
- `test_deterministic_changelog_substance_without_bump_hint_forces_patch` (function) — Regression guard that an intent carrying a changelog note but no bump_type still forces a patch bump so the note is filed rather than silently dropped. <!--#2c7df6a37a279ccd-->

- `test_deterministic_major_creates_tag` (function) — Asserts a major bump produces the next major version and an annotated tag pointing at the reconcile commit. <!--#25a1d95045d02543-->
- `test_deterministic_patch_does_not_create_tag` (function) — Asserts a patch bump raises the version but creates no tag. <!--#ded5f524bbb893af-->
- `test_changelog_entries_merged_under_final` (function) — Asserts changelog bullets from multiple intents are merged under the single final version in VERSIONS.md. <!--#f237e4a16bf56a7c-->
- `test_operator_edit_survives_residue_reset_timeout` (function) — Verifies an operator's uncommitted edit is replayed via the finally-block reattach even when a git timeout stalls the crash-residue reset. <!--#b20a017e481ee564-->
- `test_reattach_git_timeout_surfaces_as_reconcile_error` (function) — Verifies a git timeout inside the finally-block reattach (git merge-file) surfaces as a typed ReconcileError rather than a raw TimeoutExpired. <!--#e9eb4553ca5c8064-->
- `test_prepass_git_timeout_surfaces_as_reconcile_error` (function) — Verifies a git timeout in the read-only replayability pre-pass is also mapped to a typed ReconcileError. <!--#7cc03f83cb54d5d7-->
- `test_empty_changelog_still_recorded_in_versions_md` (function) — Asserts a reconcile with no changelog bullets still records the released version header so the anti-collision historical set includes it. <!--#ca096198545d3075-->
- `test_custom_rules_channel_uses_llm_output` (function) — Asserts that when se3/version-rules.md exists, reconcile takes the custom-rules channel, prompts the LLM with the rules and change substance, and adopts the LLM's version and tag decision. <!--#52042e6f8ddfb119-->
- `test_custom_rules_is_tag_false_does_not_create_tag` (function) — Asserts the custom-rules channel honors an LLM `is_tag: false` verdict by skipping tag creation. <!--#bf367c952a745ee7-->
- `test_tag_failure_raises_reconcile_error` (function) — Asserts a VersionTagError from tag creation surfaces as a ReconcileError naming the failed tag. <!--#2a08b8643e78e4bf-->
- `test_noop_after_tag_failure_does_not_create_missing_tag` (function) — Asserts that after a tag failure, a later re-run reports the no-op/already-reconciled channel and does not self-heal by retroactively creating the missing tag. <!--#5e29af3041dffbdc-->

- `test_validate_rejects_no_advance` (function) — Asserts validate_no_regression rejects a final version equal to the current when a bump was declared. <!--#1e3d5ea47ec31515-->

- `test_validate_custom_rules_rejects_unchanged` (function) — Asserts validate_no_regression rejects an unchanged version even under the custom-rules channel. <!--#80a989d1bc501ca4-->

- `test_validate_default_channel_still_rejects_build_metadata_only` (function) — Asserts the default SemVer channel still rejects a build-metadata-only change as a non-advance. <!--#6e3a78128a851894-->

### `src/se3/engine/steps/test_with_fail_loop.py` (python) — A test-only step handler module that deliberately injects a bug into a target project's calculator on the first test run (tracked via a persisted run-count file) so tests fail, then runs pytest normally on later runs to exercise and verify the engine's fix-loop mechanism. <!--#c94ccfc50f81af48|8fff20a98050d566-->
- `test_handler_with_fail_loop` (function) — Step handler that introduces an intentional bug on the first run before running pytest, then runs tests normally on later runs, to force the fix loop to trigger. <!--#576bd7d1fef5b377-->
- `_get_run_count` (function) — Reads the persisted run count from the tracker JSON file, returning 0 if missing or unreadable. <!--#7a98a6120b25eac3-->
- `_increment_run_count` (function) — Increments the run count and writes it back to the tracker file, returning the new count. <!--#bc0552dcc5f0422e-->
- `_introduce_temporary_bug` (function) — Edits the target project's calculator.py to replace addition with subtraction, deliberately breaking tests on the first run. <!--#46937d61991f40e5-->
- `_run_pytest` (function) — Runs `pytest -v` in the project root via subprocess and returns the completed process result. <!--#675f6b2ee4815506-->
- `reset_test_tracker` (function) — Deletes the run-count tracker file to reset state before starting a new test. <!--#da1a842a593e2517-->

### `src/se3/engine/steps/version_analyze.py` (python) — The version_analyze step handler that runs an LLM over a session's implementation, spec, and verification changes to decide a SemVer bump — emitting an authoritative suggested_version in synchronous flows or persisting a provisional VersionIntent on the flow branch for the merge-side reconcile step in worktree flows, with helpers to gather current version/rules, format each prompt section, and parse/validate the LLM's response. <!--#868d66d7235fbd32|1e404fd54114b1d2-->
- `version_analyze_handler` (function) — Step handler that asks an LLM (with optional project version-rules) to decide the next version from the session's changes, emitting an authoritative `suggested_version` for synchronous flows or a branch-committed VersionIntent for worktree flows. <!--#abc007da8521caaa-->
- `_emit_version_intent` (function) — Builds a VersionIntent from the analysis and persists it under `se3/version-intents/` for the merge-side `version_reconcile` step, exposing only a provisional (non-authoritative) version and letting write failures propagate. <!--#c4b9a2b9db110d96-->
- `_build_change_summary` (function) — Composes the free-form intent digest by concatenating the already-formatted Changes/Spec/Verification prompt sections, dropping empty ones, so the merge side sees exactly what drove the bump decision. <!--#d8e20ac9e34291f1-->
- `_read_version_rules_file` (function) — Reads the optional `se3/version-rules.md` project rules file (size-capped, error-swallowing) for verbatim injection into the prompt, returning None when absent or unreadable. <!--#3979c0847245e97e-->
- `_version_bumping_enabled` (function) — Returns whether the project has version bumping enabled by mirroring the commit step's version_config.enabled gate, defaulting to enabled on any config-load fault. <!--#c2b12563eb3d7b45-->
- `_get_current_version` (function) — Detects the project's current version string via the configured VersionBumper, returning an "unknown" sentinel when disabled or no version file is found. <!--#0a9d200f2ca8c0e8-->
- `_format_changes` (function) — Renders the implement step's changed-files and implementation-group data into a markdown block for the prompt's "Changes Made" section. <!--#6c7938dd04d95393-->
- `_format_spec_changes` (function) — Renders update_spec's spec/API-change data (dict or list forms) into a markdown block highlighting API-contract changes for the prompt. <!--#5d210c649f528bc0-->
- `_format_session_commits` (function) — Renders implement-stage commits already landed on the main branch as a capped, file-folded markdown list so the prompt can treat them as the baseline-excluded session changes. <!--#916117384c2b9364-->
- `_format_verification` (function) — Renders the verification step's pass/summary/issue results into a markdown block for the prompt's "Verification Results" section. <!--#2ae548847100d2c2-->
- `_parse_response` (function) — Extracts the JSON object from the raw LLM response, requiring a `suggested_version` key, and hands it to `_validate_result`. <!--#402c4b4db481597b-->
- `_validate_result` (function) — Validates and normalizes the parsed LLM payload — requiring `suggested_version`, defaulting `bump_type`/`confidence`, cleaning changelog bullets, and deciding `is_tag` via custom rules or the SemVer tag policy. <!--#ec59dcf0ef5133f8-->
- `_fallback_commit_message` (function) — Builds a fallback commit-subject line from the task type and description (first sentence, 72-char capped) when the LLM omits or fails to produce one. <!--#8502a2c669ba9cb5-->

### `src/se3/engine/steps/version_reconcile.py` (python) — The second merge-side step handler of a worktree flow: a thin adapter over the reconcile() library that re-derives and applies the flow's final project version at merge time against master's current version, resolving the main-checkout root strictly, handling the by-design no-intent, human-review revision-undo, missing-intent, and version-disabled cases while recording ReconcileResult on step.outputs and mapping faults to a resumable FAILED. <!--#0e5184be860f18e8|91f78548c8bea3cb-->
- `_resolve_merge_root` (function) — Resolves the main-checkout root that reconcile writes to, returning step.cwd if set and otherwise strictly probing the main repo from the flow's project_root, raising MergeCheckoutResolutionError rather than silently degrading to the isolation worktree. <!--#4442023c0c711f99-->
- `version_reconcile_handler` (function) — Step handler that derives and applies the project's final version at merge time by delegating to se3.engine.merge.reconcile against the main checkout, short-circuiting as a no-op for flows that never emit a version intent, undoing a prior reconcile commit on human-review revision re-runs, and recording the ReconcileResult on step.outputs before returning COMPLETED or FAILED. <!--#fe2fd68c8d6a6e84-->

## `src/se3/engine/utils/` — The engine's utils subpackage, providing shared low-level helpers—currently a robust JSON parser that extracts and repairs JSON payloads from varied LLM response formats (stream-json/NDJSON, markdown-fenced, embedded) before validating required keys. <!--#7ead5ec392afa505|97edfdb0427111b2-->

### `src/se3/engine/utils/__init__.py` (python) — Empty package initializer marking `src/se3/engine/utils/` as the utils subpackage of the engine. <!--#e3b0c44298fc1c14|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/se3/engine/utils/json_parser.py` (python) — A robust JSON parser for LLM responses that handles stream-json/NDJSON, markdown-fenced, and embedded JSON, extracting the payload and running it through a repair chain (trailing commas, unescaped quotes, single quotes, truncation-closing) before validating required keys, and exposes lenient looks_like_json predicates. <!--#41772d21d16224bb|d655d5bc22787606-->
- `parse_json_response` (function) — Public entry point that parses JSON from an LLM response, collecting text from stream-json assistant messages when multi-line, otherwise parsing the response directly. <!--#bfc1ed6667139fbc-->
- `_extract_and_parse_json` (function) — Helper that extracts a JSON string from text, parses it through the repair chain, and validates that required keys are present. <!--#70254293e3b33aea-->
- `_extract_json_string` (function) — Locates the JSON payload within text by stripping tool-preview lines, unwrapping markdown code blocks, and falling back to first-brace-to-last-brace or trailing-object extraction. <!--#20dcab890ff12010-->
- `_extract_trailing_json_string` (function) — Walks backwards from the last '}' to find its matching '{' (respecting strings and escaped quotes) to extract the rightmost complete JSON object. <!--#ad42bc21e87f46a3-->
- `_count_unescaped_quotes` (function) — Utility that counts unescaped double quotes in a string, skipping backslash-escaped characters. <!--#8be78ab15a58c787-->
- `_repair_unescaped_quotes` (function) — Iteratively escapes unescaped interior double quotes in JSON string values using json.loads error positions to fix LLM quoting mistakes. <!--#c7f178fd4cf6cc12-->
- `_repair_json` (function) — Repairs common LLM JSON errors by removing trailing commas, converting single quotes to double quotes, and closing truncated structures. <!--#fedcf1c86d1564bc-->
- `_close_truncated_json` (function) — Attempts to make length-truncated JSON parseable by closing open strings and balancing unclosed objects and arrays. <!--#cfd0092566cd7de7-->
- `_validate_keys` (function) — Checks that the parsed data is a dict containing all required keys (trivially true when no keys are required). <!--#a69714e9aba6d385-->
- `_try_parse_with_repairs` (function) — Shared parsing core that tries strict json.loads then escalates through the structural and quote repair chain, returning the parsed object or None. <!--#2529ab7af10ffe44-->
- `looks_like_json_object` (function) — Lenient predicate returning whether text parses as a JSON dict after the full repair chain, mirroring parse_json_response's dict-only semantics. <!--#5fa87d39d7511b7c-->
- `looks_like_json` (function) — Lenient predicate returning whether text parses as any valid JSON value via the repair chain, with a strict fallback to distinguish literal `null` from failure. <!--#9155397a29d59ee8-->

## `src/se3/i18n/` — The CLI's internationalization package: it resolves the active UI language via the SE3_LANG → config → system-locale → en-US precedence chain, exposes the `t()` translation helper (plus status-token key normalization), and backs it with a loader that discovers, caches, and fail-safe reads the flat dot-keyed JSON catalogs under `locales/`, so adding a language is a pure data drop-in. <!--#014238b532eb6e71|cce6ea0a9790d67b-->

### `src/se3/i18n/__init__.py` (python) — Public i18n entry point that resolves the active UI language through the SE3_LANG → config → system-locale → en-US precedence chain (with set/get/bind/reset seams) and exposes the `t` translation helper plus status-token key normalization and translation. <!--#fe265c61d8c9da27|d32ddf1b66a7afbb-->
- `_decide_explicit` (function) — Resolves an explicitly-set se3 language request (env var or config value), returning None only when truly unset so resolution falls through, and en-US when set but unsupported. <!--#1f50cf093fb201f7-->
- `_safe_cwd` (function) — Returns the process working directory, or None if it cannot be read (e.g. deleted worktree), so language resolution never raises. <!--#cae38b9c8441a6ba-->
- `resolve_language` (function) — Resolves the effective UI language via the precedence chain SE3_LANG → project/global config → system locale → en-US. <!--#4394f4c329d94838-->
- `set_language` (function) — Explicitly sets the active UI language (unknown/None falls back to en-US) and returns the effective code. <!--#d718115194fcaba5-->
- `get_language` (function) — Returns the active UI language, lazily resolving it on first access. <!--#384ce0f141f206ed-->
- `bind_project_root` (function) — Re-runs language resolution against a command's actual project root, correcting the language cached at import time from the cwd. <!--#44a90f6ef691f7ef-->
- `reset_language` (function) — Test seam that clears the cached language so the next access re-resolves the chain. <!--#5373fe42094abcd5-->
- `t` (function) — Translates a catalog key into the active language with kwargs formatting, falling back through en-US to the raw key and never raising. <!--#c4a5b1943393acaa-->
- `status_key` (function) — Normalizes a status token or Enum into a canonical `status.<snake_case>` catalog key shared by issue, flow and step vocabularies. <!--#23076fd178cdec6f-->
- `t_status` (function) — Translates a status token for display, falling back to the raw token (not the key) when no catalog entry exists. <!--#74736fec0b8d97f9-->

### `src/se3/i18n/loader.py` (python) — Backing store for the i18n layer: discovers `<code>.json` locale catalogs in the sibling `locales/` directory via `importlib.resources` (with a filesystem fallback), loads/caches them fail-safe as flat `key -> str` maps, normalizes arbitrary config or system locale codes (`zh_CN.UTF-8`, bare `zh`, non-string YAML scalars) to a supported code, and defines `en-US` as the base fallback language — so adding a language is a pure data drop-in. <!--#a3c588a0551173ca|f2a438a9e2fc75d6-->
- `_iter_locale_resources` (function) — Generator that discovers every `<code>.json` under the package's `locales/` directory, yielding `(code, traversable)` pairs via `importlib.resources.files` with a filesystem-glob fallback so it works from both a wheel and a source tree. <!--#152fd5ea9ae6ef8d-->
- `supported_languages` (function) — Returns the sorted, deliberately uncached list of locale codes found in `locales/`, so dropping in a new language file takes effect without a restart. <!--#5e90534f30a2aa79-->
- `load_catalog` (function) — Loads and caches the flat `key -> str` translation catalog for a locale code, returning `{}` (never raising) when the file is missing, unreadable, or not a JSON object. <!--#de53c8f88213788d-->
- `normalize_language` (function) — Normalizes an arbitrary config or system locale value (e.g. `zh_CN.UTF-8`, `ZH-cn`, bare `zh`, or a non-string YAML scalar) to a supported locale code, or `None` if unsupported. <!--#b36db2217038eae3-->
- `clear_caches` (function) — Test seam that clears the cached catalogs so locale-file mutations are picked up. <!--#7b1436e83f936825-->

## `src/se3/i18n/locales/` — The CLI's translation catalog package, holding the flat dot-keyed JSON message catalogs for each supported locale (en-US as default, zh-CN as its mirror) plus an `__init__.py` package marker that lets the i18n loader read them via `importlib.resources`. <!--#70e05450331367ed|1c3428669e73e94f-->

### `src/se3/i18n/locales/__init__.py` (python) — An intentionally empty-of-code package marker whose sole purpose is to make the locales directory a regular (non-namespace) package so that `importlib.resources.files("se3.i18n.locales")` can load the `<code>.json` CLI translation catalogs on Python 3.9. <!--#c2036bfd857ee105|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/se3/i18n/locales/en-US.json` (json) — The English (en-US) locale bundle for the se3 CLI, mapping dotted message keys (cli.common.*, cli.run.*, cli.error.*, including run banners, resume/interrupt prompts, choice menus, and confirmation/adjudication gate text) to their user-facing English strings with `{placeholder}` interpolation slots. <!--#9d1f0c39b402b67c|bdc93c8f53940ae7-->

### `src/se3/i18n/locales/zh-CN.json` (json) — Simplified-Chinese translation catalog for the se3 CLI, a nested JSON tree of message keys covering shared labels (done/cancelled/error/yes/no), run lifecycle notices, interactive choice and confirmation-gate prompts (including adjudicate covered-surface listings), flow resume prompts, Ctrl+C interjection dialogs, and discovery pause/resume messages, many with interpolation placeholders and Rich markup. <!--#6fb7afcf7596cd6a|3e3dd140f4e1fe33-->
- `cli.common.done` (json-key) — Shared CLI label for the word "done" (完成). <!--#493dc211a2941efa-->
- `cli.common.cancelled` (json-key) — Shared CLI label for a cancelled action (已取消). <!--#9199f6d2dd14865b-->
- `cli.common.error` (json-key) — Shared CLI label for the word "error" (错误). <!--#fdd635d7c5cbb2fb-->
- `cli.common.warning` (json-key) — Shared CLI label for the word "warning" (警告). <!--#0759a42085198ea4-->
- `cli.common.yes` (json-key) — Shared CLI label for an affirmative answer (是). <!--#54735afd6c0386ef-->
- `cli.common.no` (json-key) — Shared CLI label for a negative answer (否). <!--#3e844d96300ac538-->
- `cli.run.starting` (json-key) — Message announcing the start of a run, interpolating the task description. <!--#48afa1831398d3e0-->
