## `src/se3/templates/` — SE3's template collection housing the project-scaffolding assets emitted by `se3 init`/`se3 migrate` — the charter, base-spec, README, VERSIONS, and standalone version-management CLI templates plus the `CHARTER_TEMPLATE` constant exported from `__init__.py` — alongside a `prompts/` subdirectory of step prompt templates (e.g. the doc-sync consistency pass), together codifying project identity, conventions, and SemVer-based version management. <!--#8160cf3e132b8065|2231a8ebe8aa0d05-->

### `src/se3/templates/__init__.py` (python) — Package initializer for SE3's project-initialization templates (charter, legacy base_spec, README, VERSIONS, version-script), exposing the canonical `CHARTER_TEMPLATE` filename constant for the charter template rendered by `se3 init`/`se3 migrate`. <!--#c244c02c91dc2554|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/se3/templates/base_spec.md` (markdown) — The `se3 init`-generated base specification template that, with placeholders for project identity/structure/conventions/constraints, establishes a project's baseline spec auto-loaded into every run, and codifies a SemVer 2.0.0 version-management policy driven by `version_analyze`'s authoritative suggested version with no silent patch-bump fallback. <!--#00d742d6e9b0c964|a3af382958bb3a94-->
- `{project_name} — Base Specification` (heading) — Top-level document title parameterized by the project name. <!--#d111501fa2c349b2-->
  - `Purpose` (heading) — States that this spec captures the project's base conventions and is generated by `se3 init` then auto-loaded in all runs. <!--#89c4e90a8f22c56c-->
  - `Requirements` (heading) — Container heading grouping all the requirement subsections of the spec. <!--#d8416f1863ce5290-->
    - `Requirement: Project Identity` (heading) — Records the project's name, description, and primary languages/frameworks via placeholders. <!--#8f8680697bd5dba4-->
    - `Requirement: Directory Structure` (heading) — Placeholder requirement describing the project's directory layout. <!--#fda3fd8b0889a9d0-->
    - `Requirement: Coding Conventions` (heading) — Placeholder requirement capturing the project's coding style conventions. <!--#c4a2c6cbe902bea6-->
    - `Requirement: Key Constraints` (heading) — Placeholder requirement listing the project's key constraints. <!--#224404c163fbb0c3-->
    - `Requirement: Workflow Conventions` (heading) — Placeholder requirement describing the project's workflow conventions. <!--#ccc10176db969929-->
    - `Requirement: Version Management` (heading) — Defines the SemVer 2.0.0 versioning policy, the single-source version file per project type, and the `version_analyze`→`commit` decision model with no silent patch-bump fallback. <!--#d362c5fe36acb63d-->
      - `Scenario: 版本自动更新` (heading) — Example scenario where completing a feature task auto-bumps the version (1.2.3→1.3.0) and syncs README/VERSIONS during commit. <!--#819f03a8342b11e0-->
      - `Scenario: 手动版本控制` (heading) — Example scenario where disabling `version.enabled` skips auto-bumping and requires manual version updates. <!--#e32e0fdc9402eb4c-->

### `src/se3/templates/charter.md` (markdown) — Jinja-style template for a project's charter document — the high-level, cross-cutting conventions channel (project identity, top-level architecture, coding conventions, key constraints, workflow conventions, and SemVer-based version management) that se3 injects verbatim into every run step, deliberately excluding per-module location detail owned by code-index. <!--#8588351519c858d3|a25ae194c9b872cd-->
- `{project_name} — Charter` (heading) — Top-level title heading naming the charter for the interpolated project. <!--#5fec8c4721218303-->
  - `Purpose` (heading) — Explains that the charter is unconditionally injected into every step and serves as the sandbox subprocess's conventions channel, holding only high-level cross-cutting content (not per-module location info, which belongs to code-index). <!--#013d4260326cc74e-->
  - `Requirements` (heading) — Container heading grouping the charter's requirement subsections. <!--#d8416f1863ce5290-->
    - `Requirement: Project Identity` (heading) — Records the project's name, description, and primary languages/frameworks via placeholders. <!--#8f8680697bd5dba4-->
    - `Requirement: Top-Level Architecture` (heading) — Captures the global architectural picture and subsystem-grouping rationale, explicitly excluding mechanical per-module location info (delegated to code-index). <!--#fa7a503fd6769af5-->
    - `Requirement: Coding Conventions` (heading) — Holds project-wide, cross-cutting coding conventions every step should follow. <!--#9d68141915bc34f0-->
    - `Requirement: Key Constraints` (heading) — Lists hard project-level constraints whose violation is treated as an error. <!--#d6e0ccfe4259b72e-->
    - `Requirement: Workflow Conventions` (heading) — Placeholder section for project workflow conventions. <!--#ccc10176db969929-->
    - `Requirement: Version Management` (heading) — Charter section mandating SemVer 2.0.0 versioning, defining the single-source version file per project type, the version-number format, and the version-decision model where version_analyze's suggested_version is the sole authority (optionally guided by se3/version-rules.md) that commit writes verbatim with no silent patch-bump fallback, plus README/VERSIONS doc-update requirements. <!--#7d849389d954389d-->

### `src/se3/templates/readme_md.md` (markdown) — A README scaffold template for SE3-generated projects, with placeholder tokens for project name/description/overview and static sections covering quick-start, directory structure, documentation links, and version. <!--#55c8d680b6a802c7|a110ba4f79dab588-->
- `{project_name}` (heading) — Top-level title heading carrying the project name placeholder, a version badge, and the project description token. <!--#516e411a1b099380-->
  - `Overview` (heading) — Overview section holding the {project_overview} placeholder for a longer project description. <!--#00ae69c98f86a6da-->
  - `Quick Start` (heading) — Quick Start section with a bash code block stubbed for install and run commands. <!--#358b911d25baaa6b-->
  - `Project Structure` (heading) — Project Structure section showing the expected directory layout (se3/, src/, tests/, and config files) of a generated project. <!--#057b89a8a6c416e8-->
  - `Documentation` (heading) — Documentation section with a table linking key files like VERSIONS.md and the base spec to their purposes. <!--#5336c849bd171379-->
  - `Version` (heading) — Version section stating the project's current version (0.1.0). <!--#2caa1c9bf3aee798-->

### `src/se3/templates/version_script.py.tmpl` (text) — A project-scaffolding template for a standalone version-management CLI (get/bump/set commands over major/minor/patch semver) with the version bump/parse logic implemented but the project-specific read_version()/write_version() left as NotImplementedError stubs for users to fill in. <!--#997ccfab37134d45|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/se3/templates/versions_md.md` (markdown) — A template for the project's VERSIONS.md changelog file, providing the version-history heading, an auto-maintenance note (se3's version_analyze + commit steps), and a seed 0.1.0 initial-release entry with placeholders for project name and date. <!--#a107f82d29b594b9|8f7146410aeb657b-->
- `Version History` (heading) — The top-level heading and intro line stating the file tracks version history, auto-maintained by se3's version_analyze and commit steps. <!--#382dba47091f371f-->
  - `0.1.0 - {date}` (heading) — The initial changelog entry template for version 0.1.0, marking the project's first release. <!--#e10dcc90f8cf1864-->

## `src/se3/templates/prompts/` — Directory holding SE3's step prompt templates — currently the doc-sync prompt that drives the documentation-consistency pass, instructing the agent to reconcile all already-published user-facing docs (README, localized variants, and any docs tree) against the current CLI, specs, structure, and version while only reporting undocumented surfaces as gaps and never authoring new files or bumping the version. <!--#e04f71f39eef32eb|69c10d0919ed52ea-->

### `src/se3/templates/prompts/doc-sync.md` (markdown) — The prompt template for SE3's documentation-sync step, instructing the agent to reconcile all published docs (README plus any docs tree and localized variants) against the CLI, specs, structure, and version, while reporting undocumented surfaces as gaps rather than authoring new files and never bumping the version. <!--#7a847c4bd60f1f36|8e0db45353f552da-->
  - `Scope` (heading) — Defines what counts as in-scope documentation — every doc the project actually publishes (README always, plus any docs tree if present) — rather than a fixed required path. <!--#f1b304b8bedd824d-->
    - `README reconciliation (baseline — preserved in full)` (heading) — Specifies the baseline README contract: aligning it item-by-item with the CLI/public interface, specs, project structure, and displayed version. <!--#b042efe5d3ee0a7b-->
    - `Reporting documentation gaps (report only — never create)` (heading) — Directs the agent to report undocumented user-facing surfaces as gaps for human triage rather than authoring new doc files to fill them. <!--#9c9e901db2527ddb-->
  - `Localized documentation alignment` (heading) — Requires language variants of a document to stay structurally parallel and faithfully translated, following the dotted BCP 47 naming convention (e.g. README.zh.md). <!--#9b42e96a14a53f00-->
  - `Constraints (scope discipline)` (heading) — Lists scope guardrails: edit only documentation, never bump the version or create new doc files, and preserve existing rationale prose unless factually wrong. <!--#c209a5d5196bb9cb-->

## `tests/` — The repository's full pytest/Node test suite for SE3, organized into subpackages for the CLI command layer, core utilities, the daemon (history cursor/push semantics), the engine (state machine, steps, prompts, LLM caller, merge/docs/version handling), the web-console server API, and a browser-stub frontend suite for app.js, alongside root-level fixtures (conftest.py, _authsrv.py), full-stack integration and regression tests (adjudication, active-flow signatures, WebUI live-chat freeze), and diagnosis/verification write-ups plus a standalone repro harness for the issue-#209 WebUI freeze. <!--#aba71d46e44b0585|2dd501bcfd4a5bfd-->

### `tests/DISCOVERY_ANALYZE_BOUNDARY_VERIFICATION.md` (markdown) — Verification write-up documenting two fixed WebUI live-chat delivery bugs — the issue #260 discovery→analyze WebSocket freeze (stale daemon cache read) and the issue #278 worktree multi-round discovery chat loss (daemon read-path identity collision) — each with reproduced symptom, root cause, layered daemon/server/frontend fixes, automated acceptance and full-suite results, and manual browser checklists. <!--#03c1be9b951a9f81|e8b4a5b2189b8ada-->
- `Discovery→Analyze WS-Freeze — Root Cause, Fix & Verification (issue #260)` (heading) — Top-level verification write-up for issue #260 documenting the reproduced discovery→analyze WebSocket freeze, its confirmed root cause, the daemon/server/frontend fixes that landed, and the acceptance/manual-check results (status: FIXED). <!--#af46afb9cee62cab-->
  - `Symptom (as reported)` (heading) — Describes the reported bug: crossing the discovery→analyze boundary stopped an open WebUI chat from receiving live `/ws/ui` content, with the prior 5s progression-grace fallback (8a128eb3) surfacing only a lone `analyze` label and scrolling up, requiring chat re-entry to recover. <!--#81bb01c5ff4e79d6-->
  - `Harness & five-hop instrumentation` (heading) — Documents the reproduction harness (`test_discovery_analyze_ws_delivery.py`) driving the real daemon reader, signature-gated push loop, and real server broadcast to a subscribed `_UiWS` client, plus five-hop DEBUG (`hist-diag`) instrumentation for end-to-end tracing. <!--#4e52c8a8a0356a54-->
  - `Final root cause — the freeze hop` (heading) — Identifies the freeze as a daemon-side stale read during the dense steps-first-write rewrite window (stale `disk_json_cache` head+tail-window parse, missing forced-fresh fallback in `_is_still_active`, and a server `requires_full` stuck-state that made the freeze persist). <!--#11eda9ca1a58663a-->
  - `Fixes that landed` (heading) — Summarizes the four fixes: whole-content hashing + `force_fresh` in `disk_json_cache` (G2), a forced-fresh drop-path rescue in `_is_still_active` (G2), a one-shot recovery full-pull on discarded appends in the server relay (G3), and self-re-arming periodic frontend fallback (G4) plus bottom-follow scroll intent (G5). <!--#0c9b2064571f8f7c-->
  - `Script-level acceptance results` (heading) — Lists the passing acceptance suites (boundary e2e, daemon cache/transition, server relay self-heal, frontend fallback and scroll) and the clean full-suite integration run (7327 passed, 1 skipped, 1 deselected in ~278s). <!--#30c4a24f3d412523-->
  - `Manual browser verification (not an automated gate)` (heading) — Documents the by-hand WebUI checklist for the #260 discovery→analyze boundary fix (incremental analyze rendering, scroll anchoring, append-seq growth, WS-severed fallback), performed manually because this host lacks libnspr4.so for the Chromium e2e. <!--#42d4c1e033c9aae6-->
- `Worktree Multi-Round Discovery — Live Chat Loss After Round 1 (issue #278)` (heading) — Introduces issue #278 (now FIXED): in `se3 run --worktree` flows, discovery chat records after round 1 vanished from the live web console and were only reachable via the show-details adjudication affordance. <!--#88ebffce5e77ad3b-->
  - `Symptom (as reported)#2` (heading) — Quotes the original user report (in Chinese) that in worktree tasks all discovery chat after round 1 disappeared, visible only through the adjudication show-details view. <!--#81464b9f74e8bb2a-->
  - `Root cause — an identity collision in the daemon read path` (heading) — Explains the root cause as a daemon read-path identity collision: multiple physical files folded under one step_id produced duplicate stepId#ordinal keys, reinforced by largest-copy-wins selection thrash desyncing the by-name cursor and a server cache self-heal that never re-queried the daemon. <!--#65972d2de8e837c1-->
  - `Fixes that landed (G1 daemon · G2 server · G3 frontend)` (heading) — Summarizes the three-layer fix: G1 gives each physical file its own stable frontend step id, prefers the worktree copy, and cleanly re-reads on copy switches; G2 relays the disambiguated identity verbatim and adds a running-worktree self-heal re-pull; G3 makes the frontend recordKey consume the disambiguated id and de-dup only byte-identical discovery records. <!--#130e49efe798db2f-->
  - `End-to-end acceptance (G4)` (heading) — Lists the automated acceptance coverage per hop (daemon read-path, server relay, frontend reconcile test suites) plus the new G4 end-to-end seam test chaining the real daemon reader, real server relay, and a faithful app.js reconcile port to prove every multi-round discovery round reaches the frontend losslessly. <!--#035778dee1a5abf3-->
  - `Full-suite regression run` (heading) — Records the full-suite regression result (7923 passed, 1 deselected, exit 0 in ~355s) confirming no #260 regression, with the deselected Chromium e2e and known environment-conditional failures explained as pre-existing. <!--#8090998ed34fc747-->
  - `Manual browser verification (not an automated gate)#2` (heading) — Documents the manual WebUI checklist for #278: run a real worktree discovery flow across several rounds and confirm every round's chat renders live (no show-details needed), the verdict appears as a normal bubble, and no round is doubled. <!--#64757af654f652c4-->

### `tests/ISSUE_209_FREEZE_DIAGNOSIS.md` (markdown) — G1 diagnosis document for issue #209 (WebUI conversation freeze on discovery→analyze and retry boundaries) that, grounded in a full-stack reproduction, localizes the root cause to the daemon's `_push_loop` being starved under large/busy roots by per-tick synchronous `engine.json` parsing and heavy awaited reads, then records candidate G2 fixes, G3 regression hooks, and the gated `SE3_HISTORY_DIAG` instrumentation G4 should remove. <!--#ce31c8fcf5960605|937cf4d0e4488f7a-->
- `issue #209 — WebUI console freeze on discovery→analyze / retry — G1 diagnosis` (heading) — Title/intro section stating the diagnosis is grounded in real reproduction and localizing the bug to the daemon push side rather than the frontend or server cache. <!--#5570eb393f47dc39-->
  - `Symptom (recap)` (heading) — Describes the observed symptom: the polled status bar keeps advancing while the WS-pushed conversation freezes until the session is exited and re-entered. <!--#c7aa4c30e5d9233d-->
  - `How it was坐实ed (reproductions, in order)` (heading) — Walks through the ordered chain of real reproductions and instrumentation proving each layer except the daemon push is correct. <!--#61b108926b1ebca6-->
  - `Root cause` (heading) — States the root cause: the daemon's `_push_loop` is starved under large/busy roots by per-tick synchronous engine.json parsing and per-iteration heavy awaited reads. <!--#124f112be7c6ef89-->
    - `Why specifically discovery→analyze and retry` (heading) — Explains why these two pause→resume boundaries manifest the freeze — the loaded daemon falls behind during the pause so the one post-resume incremental push never lands. <!--#4d5ac9e1a5a2edb3-->
  - `Trigger boundaries (the two the task asks to distinguish)` (heading) — Distinguishes the two triggers (new analyze jsonl vs. retry append to same jsonl) and notes a latent truncate/rewrite bug in `read_flow` not actually exercised by #209. <!--#c5a827852a521f2d-->
  - `Implications for G2 (fix) — recorded, not implemented here` (heading) — Lists candidate fix directions for the G2 group (cheapen per-tick change detection, decouple per-flow pushes, or a frontend poll-triggered reload workaround). <!--#12ed624429be8ce5-->
  - `Reproduction / regression hooks for G3` (heading) — Points to the repro script and fixtures G3 can use as before/after regression guards for the fix. <!--#faaf39a73b7ae25d-->
  - `Temporary instrumentation added in G1 (remove / demote in G4)` (heading) — Inventories the gated `SE3_HISTORY_DIAG` Python and frontend diagnostic logging added in G1 that G4 should remove or demote. <!--#fd95ca978ebdd59f-->

### `tests/_authsrv.py` (python) — Shared test helpers for authenticating against the multi-tenant, fail-closed se3 server: seeding an admin owner with an issued daemon key, logging a TestClient in via the login endpoint, and building authenticated daemon HELLO messages. <!--#a83029560578def6|138ae9367e119030-->
- `authed_app` (function) — Builds a server app pre-seeded with an admin owner and an issued daemon key, exposing them via app.state for tests. <!--#9d67901a372cc811-->
- `login` (function) — Logs a TestClient in as the seeded admin via the login endpoint, persisting the session cookie in the client's jar. <!--#98934d9f117043f0-->
- `authed_hello` (function) — Constructs an authenticated daemon HELLO message carrying the app's issued daemon key as JSON. <!--#3e0b56b990c9a04f-->

### `tests/conftest.py` (python) — Root pytest configuration for the test suite, providing autouse fixtures that isolate tests from the real environment — pinning the UI language to en-US, clearing config warning dedup state, stubbing out code-index refreshes, redirecting chat-history writes and the daemon home to temp dirs — plus browser-library path wiring for the headless-browser test. <!--#3d2e0180761c44f8|23b804b5a1e9546a-->
- `_wire_browser_test_libs` (function) — Prepends the gitignored `.browser-libs/lib` directory to `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` (when present) so a child Chromium process can find userspace-installed system libraries during the headless-browser test. <!--#2fe4dfbf7269486e-->
- `_force_en_us_ui_language` (function) — Autouse pytest fixture that pins the i18n UI language to en-US (via SE3_LANG plus a singleton/cache reset before and after each test) so rendered text assertions stay deterministic despite the repo's zh-CN se3.yaml. <!--#1e40da6e79a87579-->
- `_reset_config_warning_dedup_sets` (function) — Autouse fixture that dynamically clears all `_warned_*_for` dedup sets in `se3.config` before and after each test so warning-related caplog assertions stay order-independent. <!--#56a91681465d8a59-->
- `_pin_ui_language_en` (function) — Pytest fixture that sets the process-wide i18n language singleton to en-US for the test and resets it afterwards, keeping CLI output assertions stable without touching SE3_LANG/locale env vars. <!--#7b69cf84e5dd148a-->
- `_no_real_code_index_refresh` (function) — An autouse pytest fixture that monkeypatches `ensure_code_index_fresh` to a no-op so unit tests never trigger a real, flock-taking, LLM-spawning code-index rebuild against the live repo (which previously hung the suite). <!--#dcbaa1968a2bf2b9-->
- `_real_history_roots` (function) — Returns the set of real repository/CWD root paths that chat-history writes must never leak into, used as the reroute trigger for the history guard. <!--#ab53de7897d04069-->
- `_install_chat_history_guard` (function) — Monkeypatches chat_history._history_dir (and state_machine's import-bound copy) so any history write whose resolved project_root matches a real repo root is redirected into a per-test tmp dir, preventing committed se3/history/ leaks across all record_* writers. <!--#bd39968b3f2a9dae-->
- `_no_chat_history_leak_to_real_repo` (function) — Suite-wide fixture that installs the chat-history guard for every test, redirecting live-repo history writes into a tmp directory (twin of the engine-conftest fixture). <!--#3e464e53b943a9cb-->
- `_isolate_se3_daemon_home` (function) — Suite-wide fixture that redirects the daemon's SE3 home via SE3_DAEMON_DIR and sets SE3_EXTERNAL_SCAN_IGNORE so tests and their subprocesses never read or pollute the real ~/.se3/ registry. <!--#89fc7d2cc88e9ed1-->

### `tests/repro_issue_209_freeze.py` (python) — A standalone, self-run acceptance harness (not collected by pytest) that reproduces the issue-#209 WebUI freeze by standing up a real isolated se3 server/daemon/project/fake-agent plus a /ws/ui WebSocket client, driving the discovery→analyze transition under selectable daemon load (--clean/--loaded/--heavy-root), and asserting whether the analyze append reaches the browser to prove the freeze is daemon push-loop starvation under load. <!--#c5433d68e0db0d67|886835cc487d4d30-->
- `_free_port` (function) — Helper that grabs an unused TCP port by binding to port 0 and returning the OS-assigned number. <!--#171e93bcd41a6242-->
- `_poll` (function) — Generic retry helper that repeatedly calls a function until it returns truthy or attempts are exhausted, swallowing exceptions between tries. <!--#e08f25e336db03f8-->
- `_synth_heavy_root` (function) — Builds a synthetic 'heavy' se3 project root (large engine.json, busy active flow, hundreds of history dirs) to simulate the daemon load that starves the push loop. <!--#3f3002f1b5415543-->
- `run` (function) — Core driver that provisions the isolated instance (server, daemon, project, fake agent, WS client), drives the discovery→analyze transition, and asserts whether the analyze append crosses the /ws/ui wire. <!--#b8c826a6ee87b3e5-->
- `main` (function) — CLI entry point that parses --clean/--loaded/--heavy-root/--wait-after flags and invokes run() with the chosen daemon-load configuration. <!--#745c2467c7705ab4-->

### `tests/test_active_flow_signature_group_status.py` (python) — End-to-end tests verifying that appending a group_status NDJSON line to a flow's per-step history jsonl shifts DaemonHistoryReader.active_flow_signature's change-detection token (via the byte-size component of its (name, mtime, size) fingerprint) for active flows but not terminal ones, locking in the behavior that drives live per-group status pushes to the web console. <!--#4c95c37a4ca33dce|796bce7e264dcc62-->
- `_make_reader` (function) — Helper that constructs a DaemonHistoryReader whose project-roots provider yields the given test root. <!--#642397a307e5d24c-->
- `_write_active_engine` (function) — Helper that writes a minimal engine.json under se3/state so a flow is seen as active with the given status. <!--#5ba06c47d08c913d-->
- `_seed_step_jsonl` (function) — Helper that seeds a per-step history jsonl with one chat line and returns its path. <!--#d52bbbca9ebbecb3-->
- `test_group_status_append_shifts_active_flow_signature` (function) — Asserts that recording a group_status line changes the active flow's signature token. <!--#9df023d23d7f3597-->
- `test_group_status_shifts_signature_via_size_even_without_mtime_change` (function) — Asserts the signature still moves on a group_status append when mtime is pinned back, proving the byte-size fingerprint component alone shifts the token. <!--#bbf0217bbee97ef4-->
- `test_first_group_status_creates_jsonl_and_shifts_signature` (function) — Asserts that the first group_status line creating a brand-new step jsonl shifts the signature from its file-absent state. <!--#7ea955e7725f045f-->
- `test_terminal_flow_excluded_from_signature` (function) — Asserts a terminal (COMPLETED) flow is excluded from the signature, documenting that live-status pushes only apply to active flows. <!--#8b76e41afd914635-->

### `tests/test_adjudicate_integration.py` (python) — End-to-end integration tests for the fix-loop adjudication ("警察") mechanism, driving the real state machine and the real SELF_CHECK/ADJUDICATE handlers (only the LLM mocked) to prove that self-contradictory task descriptions oscillate into ADJUDICATE within two rounds, that the opt-in human confirmation gate lands or rejects a ruling's staged description/plan/ledger effects and reflows to a converging SELF_CHECK, that benign rulings are transparent no-ops, that the fingerprint ledger survives a --resume State round-trip, that the periodic backstop forces adjudication every N iterations, and that one ruling's covered_surfaces sweep resolves homomorphic sister surfaces at once while leaving uncovered surfaces to trigger their own adjudication. <!--#e1d845ba7a387735|183576cf2494e76c-->
- `_clear_test_running_env` (function) — Pytest fixture that pops SE3_TEST_RUNNING for the duration of a test and restores it afterward, honoring the recursion-guard convention for failure-asserting flows. <!--#6d9e285d42211f37-->
- `_cfg` (function) — Helper that builds a WorkflowConfig tuned for adjudication tests (defer-off, immediate fix) with optional field overrides. <!--#c999c4979f32a059-->
- `_make_sm` (function) — Helper that constructs a StateMachine with PersistenceManager patched out and its workflow-config/self-check-passes accessors stubbed. <!--#fc84d21c127bb235-->
- `_make_flow` (function) — Helper that builds a RUNNING FlowInstance parked just past a COMPLETED IMPLEMENT+TEST and ready for SELF_CHECK, returning the flow and those two steps. <!--#a237c9e492503f7f-->
- `_issue` (function) — Helper that builds a SELF_CHECK issue dict (severity, expected/actual behavior, verbatim task-description quote, evidence lines) for driving oscillation scenarios. <!--#ada8f1bd38022c9b-->
- `_new_self_check` (function) — Helper that assembles a fresh PENDING SELF_CHECK step via the real input assembler, injects the changed-file set, and makes it the flow's current step. <!--#2a81a3987e666df4-->
- `_run_self_check` (function) — Helper that runs the real self_check_handler with the LLMCaller mocked to return given issues/resolutions, then writes the returned status back onto the step. <!--#2200a0ed194cf3a1-->
- `_run_adjudicate` (function) — Helper that runs the real adjudicate_handler with the LLMCaller mocked to return a given ruling, writing the returned status back onto the step. <!--#48eff3323633207e-->
- `TestConfirmationGate` (class) — Integration test class asserting that when adjudicate is not registered under `confirmation.steps` (resolve_confirm_inputs → None), even a description-rewriting ruling auto-passes with no CONFIRM gate and reflows straight to SELF_CHECK against the adjudicated text. <!--#c68394a4100cce9d-->
  - `TestConfirmationGate._drive_to_desc_ruling` (method) — Helper that drives the state machine through two oscillating SELF_CHECK rounds into ADJUDICATE, applies a description-rewrite ruling, and returns the COMPLETED ADJUDICATE step with its gate still unresolved. <!--#a594e861e96a87f0-->
  - `TestConfirmationGate.test_unregistered_adjudicate_auto_passes_without_confirm` (method) — Test proving that an unregistered adjudicate step auto-passes without inserting any CONFIRM, reflowing to SELF_CHECK pass #1 with the adjudicated description in force and the ruling's staged ledger effects applied. <!--#80988950642e8e09-->
- `TestContradictionConverges` (class) — Integration test class verifying that two-round SELF_CHECK oscillation on the same clause routes to ADJUDICATE and the flow converges cleanly to terminal COMPLETED. <!--#fa92b2e665984067-->
  - `TestContradictionConverges.test_oscillation_triggers_adjudicate_within_two_rounds_and_converges` (method) — End-to-end test that oscillating reviewer expectations trigger ADJUDICATE within two rounds, a human-approved CONFIRM applies the staged abolition and reflows to SELF_CHECK, and the flow then advances through COMMIT to terminal COMPLETED without re-entering the fix loop or a spurious adjudication. <!--#e22887e79d1c2dab-->
  - `TestContradictionConverges.test_still_valid_issue_after_ruling_stays_in_fix_loop` (method) — Test that a post-ruling issue grounded on the surviving clause drives a normal IMPLEMENT→TEST→SELF_CHECK fix cycle without re-entering a spurious ADJUDICATE, proving the inserted ADJUDICATE/CONFIRM slots were stripped on landing. <!--#6f31beebc577a401-->
  - `TestContradictionConverges.test_rejected_ruling_does_not_land_ledger_effects` (method) — Test that a human rejection re-runs the same ADJUDICATE without applying its abolition to the ledger, and only the subsequently approved ruling lands its staged side effects. <!--#437bed976f56d906-->
- `TestResumeContinuity` (class) — Test class verifying the cross-round adjudication ledger survives a --resume State serialization boundary. <!--#0d6d56621780c6b3-->
  - `TestResumeContinuity.test_ledger_accumulates_across_resume_boundary` (method) — Test that records one oscillation round, round-trips State through to_dict/from_dict, and confirms a second post-resume round at the same position still trips the adjudicator with round_count==2. <!--#48dbc4077dd5760e-->
- `TestPeriodicBackstop` (class) — Test class covering the every-N-iteration periodic backstop that forces ADJUDICATE (and the below-period case that does not). <!--#d8bf9e7e38b6cb48-->
  - `TestPeriodicBackstop.test_backstop_forces_adjudicate_every_n_iterations` (method) — Test that with no oscillation signal but the fix-iteration counter at the configured period, a SELF_CHECK REVISION_NEEDED routes to ADJUDICATE and rebases the period baseline. <!--#5447c195fd67a736-->
  - `TestPeriodicBackstop.test_below_period_stays_on_fix_loop` (method) — Test that below the configured adjudicate period a single non-oscillating issue stays on the normal IMPLEMENT fix loop without inserting ADJUDICATE. <!--#ee98d61d6bfc7c28-->
- `TestBenignNoop` (class) — End-to-end integration test class verifying that when an oscillation trips ADJUDICATE but the LLM rules the flagged position benign (a review_divergence, not a real spec contradiction), ADJUDICATE acts as a transparent no-op that passes the triggering round's fix_instructions untouched into IMPLEMENT. <!--#92e237cea93403ce-->
  - `TestBenignNoop.test_oscillation_then_benign_ruling_passes_through_to_implement` (method) — Drives a two-round self-check oscillation into ADJUDICATE and asserts that a benign ruling leaves the flow as if ADJUDICATE never ran — pending fix_instructions flow straight to IMPLEMENT, no extra fix iteration, issue left intact, supersede/override outputs absent — with only two mechanical effects surviving: the ADJUDICATE slot is stripped and the benign position lands in the ledger's rejected_positions (baseline reset unchanged). <!--#585657a88d42690a-->
- `_make_cold_flow` (function) — Test helper that builds a RUNNING FlowInstance on the hot/cold-split task, pre-populated with COMPLETED PLAN/IMPLEMENT/TEST steps so it sits parked in the fix loop just before SELF_CHECK. <!--#fa6cb58254fd5353-->
- `_new_cold_self_check` (function) — Test helper that constructs and registers a fresh PENDING SELF_CHECK step (built via the state machine's step inputs) whose changed-file set spans all three contended surfaces, making it the flow's current step. <!--#3758df24250ec945-->
- `_complete_implement` (function) — Test helper that marks an IMPLEMENT step COMPLETED with all surface files listed as changed. <!--#83aef1ba116ca7c7-->
- `_adjudicate_steps` (function) — Test helper returning every ADJUDICATE step recorded in a flow's state, used to assert how many rulings were actually inserted. <!--#701d566b053e4e5d-->
- `TestHomomorphicSurfaceSweep` (class) — Integration test suite verifying the homomorphic surface sweep: a single adjudication ruling covers every surface its boundary clause claims (so sister surfaces never re-trigger), while surfaces it does not claim keep their ordinary independent trigger and patch/no-op paths. <!--#a66ce7ce237e9a6f-->
  - `TestHomomorphicSurfaceSweep._oscillate_cold_surface` (method) — Suite helper that drives two SELF_CHECK rounds with opposing issues on the cold-step-file surface to provoke — and return — the resulting ADJUDICATE step. <!--#ffb049f75094499a-->
  - `TestHomomorphicSurfaceSweep.test_one_ruling_covers_both_surfaces_and_sister_never_retriggers` (method) — Asserts that one swept ruling patches description and plan together, records both covered surfaces with justifications, and makes later contradicting issues on the sister surface ungrounded so the flow converges to COMMIT with exactly one adjudication. <!--#c9c282e860c192ad-->
  - `TestHomomorphicSurfaceSweep.test_uncovered_surface_still_triggers_its_own_adjudication` (method) — Asserts the sweep's conservatism is self-healing: a surface the first ruling did not claim still oscillates through the normal trigger path into a second, independent ADJUDICATE that lands via the unchanged patch/auto-pass flow. <!--#ba1cd8fa5cd85106-->
  - `TestHomomorphicSurfaceSweep.test_uncovered_surface_benign_ruling_passes_through` (method) — Asserts the no-op branch of that self-healing path: when the un-swept surface's second ruling is a review divergence, it claims no surfaces, forwards the pending fix instructions into IMPLEMENT, records the rejected position, and leaves the first ruling's patch intact. <!--#ebd911d53fcad708-->

### `tests/test_agent_config.py` (python) — Unit tests for se3.config's agent-configuration loading, covering load_agents() resolution of built-in defaults, the agents registry, legacy claude_commands migration, project-over-global precedence, ordering/priority deprecation, and the backward-compatible load_claude_commands() shim. <!--#b893466c42c84728|f6494d298abfc18b-->

  - `TestLoadAgents.test_agents_takes_priority_over_claude_commands` (method) — Confirms the agents registry wins over claude_commands when both are present. <!--#1f73e7108ad1699e-->
  - `TestLoadAgents.test_project_overrides_global` (method) — Verifies project-level defaults fully replace global defaults rather than merging. <!--#a89d304c586b32e4-->

  - `TestLoadAgents.test_registry_without_defaults_uses_built_in` (method) — Asserts that an agents registry with no llm_caller.defaults and no legacy claude_commands falls back to the PATH-available built-in candidates rather than the registry entries. <!--#e1a918deb07353e2-->
  - `TestLoadAgents.test_unknown_name_in_defaults_raises` (method) — Asserts an unknown agent name in llm_caller.defaults raises a ValueError naming the bad entry. <!--#d13d05fdf6acc790-->

### `tests/test_breakglass_bootstrap.py` (python) — Tests for the break-glass bootstrap escape hatch (`se3.server.bootstrap` and the `se3-server bootstrap-token` CLI), covering one-time/reissuable/TTL'd token issuance that persists only the hash, the security baseline that the plaintext never reaches disk or logs, dependency isolation so the command works on a core-only install without the `[server]` extra, and the end-to-end seam where a CLI-minted token is consumed by a live server on the same sqlite file. <!--#10a96aecd8ef763a|2122393ba9c40629-->
- `test_issue_returns_plaintext_and_persists_only_the_hash` (function) — Asserts issuance returns a `bg_`-prefixed plaintext plus id while storing only the hash, verified by consuming via the hash of the plaintext. <!--#60127117962037ca-->
- `test_issued_token_is_one_time` (function) — Asserts a token consumes successfully once and is rejected on replay. <!--#bccb5e6a317d68e8-->
- `test_issue_is_reissuable_with_distinct_tokens` (function) — Asserts repeated issuance yields distinct plaintexts/ids that remain independently consumable (re-issue does not revoke prior tokens). <!--#f3e8600a8526c4ec-->
- `test_issue_honours_ttl_expiry` (function) — Asserts a token with a past (negative) TTL is rejected by consume while a generously-TTL'd token is accepted. <!--#d7417d2f903eb507-->
- `test_print_reveals_token_once_to_the_stream` (function) — Asserts `print_breakglass_token` reveals the real, consumable secret exactly once on the provided console stream. <!--#256e30385ee1d555-->
- `test_plaintext_token_never_written_to_the_store_file` (function) — Asserts the plaintext token never appears in any sqlite artifact (db/WAL/SHM) on disk — only its SHA-256 hash. <!--#fd7f66b43c1af758-->
- `test_issuance_never_logs_the_plaintext` (function) — Asserts the plaintext reaches the console stream but never the logging output at DEBUG level. <!--#f3653838c1c5f487-->
- `test_cli_bootstrap_token_prints_token_and_exits_zero` (function) — Asserts the `bootstrap-token` CLI subcommand prints a token, exits 0, and that the printed token is consumable from the same store file. <!--#f555bdbb6f6776df-->
- `test_cli_bootstrap_token_is_reissuable` (function) — Asserts running the `bootstrap-token` CLI twice yields two distinct, independently consumable tokens. <!--#5d8638473d74b4da-->
- `_run_python` (function) — Helper that runs a Python snippet in a fresh subprocess with this worktree's `src` prepended to `PYTHONPATH`, capturing output. <!--#7c663f38919d0739-->
- `test_bootstrap_token_works_without_server_extra` (function) — Asserts `bootstrap-token` mints a token in a simulated core-only install where fastapi/uvicorn/argon2/bcrypt imports are blocked, confirming it's intercepted before the `[server]` extra import. <!--#21e1f146bd82e3ef-->
- `test_server_version_works_without_server_extra` (function) — Asserts `se3-server --version` prints the version and exits 0 even when fastapi/uvicorn imports are blocked (handled before the extra import). <!--#5748f539edaa0267-->
- `test_core_modules_import_clean` (function) — Parametrized test asserting core modules (e.g. se3.cli / se3.daemon) import cleanly with no server extra present. <!--#781ce35f32a3cb16-->
- `test_cli_token_is_consumable_by_a_server_on_the_same_db` (function) — End-to-end test that a CLI-minted token is accepted by a live server (via `POST /api/auth/breakglass`) opened on the same db, mints an admin session, and is rejected on replay. <!--#695855b6de03e738-->

### `tests/test_builtin_default_chain.py` (python) — Unit tests for se3.config's built-in agent-chain fallback, verifying that the default chain is built by probing PATH for supported agent commands (with priority renumbering, declared ordering, an informative error when none are installed, and exclusion of the opt-in claude-interactive variant), that probing never filters explicitly configured agents, and that the legacy claude-commands view never surfaces a non-Claude binary from the built-in chain. <!--#54bd8a9073178a9d|d65ac39d0b99fdbc-->
- `_reset_module_caches` (function) — Test helper that clears se3.config's module-level 'already warned' caches so each test sees fresh deprecation/unknown-key warnings. <!--#0d4baf75d508c40f-->
- `_which_only` (function) — Test helper returning a patch of shutil.which that pretends only the named commands exist on PATH. <!--#46d87c9af166983d-->
- `_no_global` (function) — Test helper that patches Path.home() to a tmp dir so global user config never leaks into a test. <!--#200c86f71d189eaf-->
- `TestBuiltinDefaultChain` (class) — Tests that the built-in agent chain is derived from which-probing the supported agent commands, with correct priority renumbering, declared ordering, a helpful error when none are installed, and exclusion of the opt-in claude-interactive variant. <!--#715c39904ffe5765-->
  - `TestBuiltinDefaultChain.test_only_claude_available` (method) — Asserts that with only claude on PATH the built-in chain is a single claude-code agent at priority 0. <!--#9835d69bb1dea6dd-->
  - `TestBuiltinDefaultChain.test_only_codex_available` (method) — Asserts a lone second-ranked candidate (codex) is renumbered to priority 0 rather than keeping its declared priority 1. <!--#c73ee991d4320f71-->
  - `TestBuiltinDefaultChain.test_both_available_preserves_declared_order` (method) — Asserts that when both commands exist the chain keeps declared order claude-then-codex with priorities 0 and 1. <!--#12263a63d39d6bf3-->
  - `TestBuiltinDefaultChain.test_none_available_raises_listing_supported_agents` (method) — Asserts that with no agent command on PATH the chain raises a ValueError naming every supported agent and both escape hatches (install, or configure llm_caller.defaults). <!--#cf822fa6e7310402-->
  - `TestBuiltinDefaultChain.test_interactive_variant_is_not_a_builtin_candidate` (method) — Asserts claude-interactive is absent from the built-in candidate list because it needs a PTY and must be opted into explicitly. <!--#eb62b051d4165322-->
- `TestProbeAppliesToBuiltinBranchOnly` (class) — Tests the invariant that PATH-probing only filters the built-in fallback chain and never touches explicitly configured agents. <!--#e68bdb2c783cbe85-->
  - `TestProbeAppliesToBuiltinBranchOnly.test_no_config_falls_through_to_probed_builtin` (method) — Asserts that with an empty agents config load_agents falls through to the built-in chain and reflects whatever commands are on PATH. <!--#660d7d40a44e3af0-->
  - `TestProbeAppliesToBuiltinBranchOnly.test_explicit_defaults_are_never_probe_filtered` (method) — Asserts an agent named in llm_caller.defaults is returned verbatim even when its command is missing from PATH, so se3 never silently substitutes a different agent. <!--#dab544e5272b07f3-->
- `TestLegacyClaudeCommandsNeverGetANonClaudeAgent` (class) — Tests that the legacy Claude-CLI-only load_claude_commands view never surfaces a non-Claude binary from the built-in chain, while still passing explicitly configured agents through unchanged. <!--#646f4abe0179092b-->
  - `TestLegacyClaudeCommandsNeverGetANonClaudeAgent.test_builtin_codex_only_yields_no_claude_command` (method) — Asserts a built-in chain containing only codex yields an empty legacy claude-commands list even though load_agents still returns codex. <!--#2f96c942ec21e4fb-->
  - `TestLegacyClaudeCommandsNeverGetANonClaudeAgent.test_builtin_both_available_yields_claude_only` (method) — Asserts that when both commands are on PATH the legacy view keeps only the claude command at priority 0. <!--#f020bb3d179695b3-->
  - `TestLegacyClaudeCommandsNeverGetANonClaudeAgent.test_explicit_codex_default_still_passes_through` (method) — Asserts an explicitly configured codex default is passed through verbatim by the legacy view, since config levels 1-3 are taken as written. <!--#8a3ef031783b8b42-->

### `tests/test_charter_anchored_patch.py` (python) — A unit-test matrix exercising the pure anchored-patch validator and applier in charter_freshness, covering accept paths (empty, unique replace, insert_after, multi-op, order-independence) and rejection paths (non-verbatim/ambiguous quotes, missing anchors, unknown ops, budget/removal/op-count bounds, overlaps, and type errors). <!--#d12cdac5c28786f9|4f50bd375f8eb715-->
- `test_empty_patch_is_valid_and_candidate_equals_original` (function) — Asserts an empty op list validates successfully and applying it returns the charter unchanged. <!--#44369af0a82ecb5c-->
- `test_unique_replace_generates_candidate` (function) — Verifies a single unique-match replace op swaps the target line while leaving all other charter text intact. <!--#642de5288bef3b4e-->
- `test_insert_after_pure_insertion` (function) — Checks that an insert_after op anchored on the last line purely appends new text without removing any original content. <!--#06ea48cb20e30664-->
- `test_multiple_nonoverlapping_ops_apply_in_one_pass` (function) — Confirms multiple non-overlapping replace and insert ops all apply correctly in a single validation/apply pass. <!--#658daaba504b1283-->
- `test_apply_patch_is_order_independent_for_adjacent_insert_and_replace` (function) — Regression test ensuring a zero-width insert adjacent to a same-start replace yields identical output regardless of op order and never duplicates the removed span. <!--#bd1415b3ec022ade-->
- `test_replace_quote_not_on_disk_is_rejected` (function) — Ensures a replace whose old_text is absent from the charter is rejected with a verbatim-quote error. <!--#be43e4fcf937fde6-->
- `test_replace_quote_matching_multiple_places_is_rejected` (function) — Ensures a replace whose old_text matches more than one location is rejected for non-uniqueness. <!--#30ab01e6f74c4aa5-->
- `test_insert_after_anchor_not_found_is_rejected` (function) — Ensures an insert_after op whose anchor text does not exist is rejected with an anchor error. <!--#6f5c71ea852d79c2-->
- `test_insert_after_ambiguous_anchor_is_rejected` (function) — Ensures an insert_after op whose anchor matches multiple places is rejected for non-uniqueness. <!--#e2030ef3813af834-->
- `test_unknown_op_kind_is_rejected` (function) — Ensures an op with an unrecognized kind (e.g. 'delete') is rejected as an unknown op. <!--#aeb2c0a04b1f3e85-->
- `test_missing_old_text_on_replace_is_rejected` (function) — Ensures a replace op lacking the required old_text field is rejected. <!--#8f8c2e9ec8748e18-->
- `test_over_char_budget_is_rejected` (function) — Ensures new_text exceeding the maximum added-character budget is rejected for adding too much text. <!--#f8d9e121644547dc-->
- `test_mass_removal_behind_short_replacement_is_rejected` (function) — Ensures a replace that deletes a huge region behind a tiny replacement is caught by the removed-character bound. <!--#20d47c5711869e53-->
- `test_too_many_ops_is_rejected` (function) — Ensures a patch exceeding the maximum allowed number of operations is rejected. <!--#e8360f98d6d7a928-->
- `test_overlapping_ops_are_rejected` (function) — Ensures two ops whose target spans overlap the same region are rejected. <!--#019a9ac99c61fa7a-->
- `test_patch_not_a_list_is_rejected` (function) — Ensures a patch passed as a non-list (e.g. a dict) is rejected with a list-type error. <!--#4fed5007aaf77d53-->
- `test_non_string_new_text_is_rejected` (function) — Ensures an op whose new_text is not a string is rejected with a new_text type error. <!--#4531435007134309-->

### `tests/test_charter_freshness.py` (python) — Test suite for the CHARTER_FRESHNESS flow-end advisory step, covering the cheap no-diff pass, non-blocking LLM verdicts and failures, the oversize-admission monitoring trigger, the admission-gate prompt builder and in-memory check_admission path, the propose→gate→apply closed-loop write path with its preconditions/retries/fail-closed guards, and summarize's aggregation of charter and why-comment guard results. <!--#a12be84bc0f1f075|606037d329b4f717-->
- `_make_flow` (function) — Test helper that builds a FlowInstance with a given task and a change_path under the project root. <!--#32ffecb7d316c431-->
- `_make_step` (function) — Test helper that constructs a CHARTER_FRESHNESS Step from a given inputs dict. <!--#b10efb4585914365-->
- `_install_fake_caller` (function) — Test helper that monkeypatches charter_freshness.LLMCaller with a fake that records prompts/init kwargs and pops scripted responses (raising on unexpected extra calls), returning the shared state dict. <!--#72f9911297cf1ca5-->
- `_with_completed_invariant_check` (function) — Helper that attaches a COMPLETED invariant_check step to a flow so the closed-loop charter-update precondition is satisfied. <!--#4f3505ea448782a6-->
- `_propose` (function) — Helper that builds a JSON propose-stage LLM response encoding whether a charter update is needed, the touched classes, reason, suggested text, and patch. <!--#174db0cef10d9d7e-->
- `_gate` (function) — Helper that builds a JSON admission-gate LLM verdict encoding admitted plus optional violations and weakened_removals. <!--#693a8a5e996879e1-->
- `_write_charter` (function) — Test helper that writes given text to se3/charter.md under the project root, creating the se3 directory. <!--#eb2499a1aa852241-->
- `test_no_diff_passes_cheap_without_llm` (function) — Asserts an empty diff completes with no LLM call, charter_update_needed=False, and skipped_reason='no_diff'. <!--#d25c71c8982fd47a-->
- `test_untouched_charter_completes_without_prompt` (function) — Asserts a diff the LLM deems charter-irrelevant completes with one LLM call, no update needed, and empty touched_classes. <!--#731d97a0c6aaeee6-->
- `test_touched_charter_surfaces_update_prompt` (function) — Asserts a charter-relevant diff completes non-blocking while surfacing charter_update_needed, touched_classes, and a suggested_update. <!--#afbf594051ce604f-->
- `test_llm_failure_is_non_blocking` (function) — Asserts an LLM exception degrades to a non-blocking COMPLETED with charter_update_needed=False and skipped_reason='llm_error'. <!--#5b4ca1b6951c2bbc-->
- `test_unparsable_response_is_non_blocking` (function) — Asserts an unparsable LLM response degrades to a non-blocking COMPLETED with skipped_reason='parse_error'. <!--#9a1f867c66ad9a13-->
- `test_admission_check_not_run_when_charter_untouched` (function) — Asserts the admission check is skipped (no admission_checked output) when the diff does not edit se3/charter.md. <!--#98dd57850b8a2af7-->
- `test_admission_check_runs_and_warns_when_charter_oversized` (function) — Asserts that editing an oversized charter.md triggers the admission check and surfaces a non-blocking over-threshold monitoring warning. <!--#55c36aab44b85557-->
- `test_admission_check_runs_no_warn_when_charter_small` (function) — Asserts that editing a small charter.md runs the admission check but reports under-threshold with no admission_warning. <!--#3dc839bf64ba5887-->
- `test_admission_gate_prompt_includes_standard_and_removal_question` (function) — Asserts build_admission_gate_prompt embeds the full admission standard, the removal-weakening question, the candidate text, diff summary, and JSON verdict schema keys. <!--#0f2b02c4cc1f4d0f-->
- `test_admission_gate_prompt_pure_insertion_states_no_removal` (function) — Asserts an empty/None replaced_texts (pure-insertion patch) yields prompt wording of 'PURE INSERTION' with no verbatim replaced-passage block. <!--#a0d4c8dd179e6cff-->
- `test_admission_gate_prompt_lists_each_replaced_text_verbatim` (function) — Asserts each removed passage is rendered verbatim and numbered ('replaced passage #1/#2') so the gate can judge removals individually. <!--#9f6d2516c8c83cb3-->
- `test_admission_gate_prompt_filters_blank_replaced_entries` (function) — Asserts blank/non-string replaced entries are dropped, degrading the prompt to pure-insertion wording when none survive. <!--#ca81b7bcc0ed36a6-->
- `test_check_admission_in_memory_candidate_under_threshold` (function) — Asserts check_admission accepts an in-memory candidate string and reports over_threshold False (with no warning, correct byte size, standard) for a small candidate. <!--#7c24255c26e8c237-->
- `test_check_admission_in_memory_candidate_over_threshold` (function) — Asserts an oversized candidate sets over_threshold True with a monitoring warning and correct byte size, without raising or blocking. <!--#8e95a05f27749d8c-->
- `test_check_admission_respects_custom_threshold_for_candidate` (function) — Asserts a tiny custom threshold_bytes flips a normally-small candidate to over_threshold, confirming the in-memory path honours the threshold argument. <!--#9ef35f9ff11badae-->
- `test_precondition_missing_stays_advisory_and_never_writes` (function) — Asserts that without a COMPLETED invariant_check the handler stays advisory-only — one propose call, no gate, disk unchanged, and degraded_reason 'invariant_check_not_completed'. <!--#dc6b75be4b17d34d-->
- `test_gate_pass_writes_charter_atomically_with_diff` (function) — Asserts a passing propose+gate round writes the charter atomically, records the diff and gate verdicts, keeps LLM sub-calls read-only, and updates disk content. <!--#548d4c99f4f4328f-->
- `test_gate_reject_twice_degrades_without_writing` (function) — Asserts two consecutive gate rejections degrade to a no-op (llm_admitted False, degraded_reason set) leaving the charter byte-for-byte unchanged. <!--#8ba596ada9b9a24e-->
- `test_gate_malformed_response_fails_closed_without_writing` (function) — Asserts a gate response with string-typed fields fails closed (llm_malformed) rather than coercing to a pass, so the charter stays unchanged. <!--#4961fdc84d81ec8c-->
- `test_gate_reject_then_retry_succeeds` (function) — Asserts a first-round gate rejection feeds back into the retry prompt (carrying 'REJECTED') and the corrected second-round patch passes and is applied. <!--#3372a6f432af33ee-->
- `test_mechanical_reject_then_retry_succeeds_without_extra_gate_call` (function) — Asserts a patch quoting off-disk text fails the mechanical check with no LLM gate call, and the retried valid patch is applied. <!--#d5f8871958864cb2-->
- `test_size_red_light_is_gating_and_blocks_write` (function) — Asserts the admission size check is gating on this path — an over-threshold candidate is blocked (size_over_threshold True) with no LLM gate call and no write. <!--#52226bfa7a016aa6-->
- `test_resume_reentry_is_idempotent` (function) — Asserts that on resume, with the charter already updated, propose judges the on-disk text fresh and nothing is written (propose only, no gate). <!--#ee065574409374bd-->
- `test_propose_prompt_uses_on_disk_charter_not_frozen_anchor` (function) — Asserts the propose base is the on-disk charter text, never the frozen invariant anchor passed via step.inputs['charter']. <!--#344c79225b5f1f8e-->
- `test_closed_loop_llm_failure_is_non_blocking` (function) — Asserts a propose LLM exception degrades to a soft no-op (still COMPLETED, skipped_reason 'llm_error', charter untouched) even with the precondition satisfied. <!--#b0d4fd9121b58dac-->
- `_flow_with_guard_steps` (function) — Helper that builds a flow with optional COMPLETED charter_freshness and/or invariant_check steps carrying given outputs, for exercising the summarize aggregation. <!--#173a8ad421680167-->
- `test_summarize_aggregates_charter_auto_update` (function) — Asserts the summarize knowledge-guards section and deterministic fallback report both surface a 'Charter Auto-Update' entry with the embedded diff excerpt. <!--#93f2a99c723d8fd5-->
- `test_summarize_aggregates_charter_advisory_and_reason` (function) — Asserts the summarize section reports a 'Charter Update Advisory' with the suggested update text and the degraded reason when auto-update was declined. <!--#86722fe43ecd7109-->
- `test_summarize_aggregates_why_comment_losses` (function) — Asserts the summarize section surfaces 'Why-Comment Losses' from invariant_check outputs, including the comment text and file. <!--#f913f8414a44343f-->
- `test_summarize_no_guard_activity_adds_nothing` (function) — Asserts that with a fresh charter and no why-comment losses the knowledge-guards section is empty and the base report omits 'Knowledge Guards'. <!--#d4b7cc4e08a188a1-->

### `tests/test_claude_interactive_runner.py` (python) — Unit test suite for ClaudeInteractiveRunner, the PTY-based interactive `claude` AgentRunner adapter, using a fake pexpect PTY stub and monkeypatching to exercise its class contract, interactive-mode flag translation in build_call_args, PTY driving primitives (feed/await-ready/drain), process-group SIGTERM→SIGKILL termination, and run lifecycle including double timeouts and guaranteed reclamation without spawning a real process. <!--#9aa215770033cf4a|77664b0af72825c0-->
- `FakePty` (class) — Minimal fake stand-in for pexpect.spawn that yields preset chunks then either stays alive (TIMEOUT) or dies (EOF), recording sent input and close/terminate calls. <!--#a3141a517a82d97e-->
  - `FakePty.__init__` (method) — Initializes the fake PTY with queued chunks, death behavior, exit/signal status, pid, and empty sent/closed tracking state. <!--#7496fca132b41784-->
  - `FakePty.isalive` (method) — Reports whether the fake process is still alive. <!--#0e3dde0c98502e77-->
  - `FakePty.read_nonblocking` (method) — Pops the next queued chunk, or raises pexpect.EOF (die) or pexpect.TIMEOUT (stay alive) when exhausted. <!--#68ce5ea45ab2fa7d-->
  - `FakePty.send` (method) — Records sent text and returns its length, mimicking pexpect's send. <!--#a2820cc4c5b2be54-->
  - `FakePty.sendline` (method) — Records sent text plus a newline and returns its length, mimicking pexpect's sendline. <!--#2392030e03661acd-->
  - `FakePty.close` (method) — Marks the fake PTY as closed and dead. <!--#3a14be3524904ca9-->
  - `FakePty.terminate` (method) — Marks the fake process dead and returns True. <!--#9bcccaae01d66223-->
- `_make_runner` (function) — Helper that constructs a ClaudeInteractiveRunner with a default 'claude' command. <!--#219383a5bcb60303-->
- `no_kill` (function) — Pytest fixture that monkeypatches os.getpgid/os.killpg to record process-group signals instead of sending them to real PIDs. <!--#7d4c2761f1c14d6a-->
- `TestContract` (class) — Tests the runner's class contract: AgentRunner subclassing, pexpect-free construction, and legacy commands-list view. <!--#a2990995793db8cb-->
  - `TestContract.test_is_agent_runner_subclass` (method) — Asserts ClaudeInteractiveRunner is a subclass of AgentRunner. <!--#37522825bb6796df-->
  - `TestContract.test_instantiable_without_pexpect_import` (method) — Asserts the runner constructs without needing pexpect/config and exposes the expected command and setting_sources. <!--#6caf941a61772322-->
  - `TestContract.test_legacy_commands_list_view` (method) — Asserts a runner built from a legacy commands list exposes both the first command and the full list. <!--#31e38e6a71e4d153-->
- `TestBuildCallArgs` (class) — Tests build_call_args / _build_full_cmd translation of intent into interactive-mode flags (read-only tools, no print flags, stashed prompt, context dirs, prefix, session id). <!--#e715b89d18796dcb-->
  - `TestBuildCallArgs.test_read_only_adds_disallowed_tools` (method) — Asserts read-only mode appends --disallowedTools with Write/Edit/NotebookEdit/AskUserQuestion. <!--#58cdccc6a587b61c-->
  - `TestBuildCallArgs.test_writable_omits_disallowed_tools` (method) — Asserts writable mode omits the --disallowedTools flag. <!--#ddc85dc0b24b1ec4-->
  - `TestBuildCallArgs.test_no_print_only_flags` (method) — Asserts interactive args never contain print-mode flags like --output-format or -p. <!--#860a2c51759d7767-->
  - `TestBuildCallArgs.test_prompt_stashed_not_in_argv` (method) — Asserts the prompt is stashed in _pending_prompt for PTY feeding rather than placed in argv. <!--#2fe79a2ca5eb0c2d-->
  - `TestBuildCallArgs.test_context_files_translated_to_add_dir` (method) — Asserts context files are translated into deduplicated --add-dir parent-directory flags. <!--#094fc80bf51b3d49-->
  - `TestBuildCallArgs.test_nonexistent_context_files_skipped` (method) — Asserts nonexistent context files produce no --add-dir flag. <!--#a068de4526beec9e-->
  - `TestBuildCallArgs.test_full_cmd_injects_prefix` (method) — Asserts _build_full_cmd injects the claude command, --dangerously-skip-permissions, and --setting-sources user prefix. <!--#996537fdc517f85c-->
  - `TestBuildCallArgs.test_full_cmd_omits_session_id_when_unset` (method) — Asserts no --session-id flag is emitted before a session id is assigned. <!--#04c9f7071e8f9954-->
  - `TestBuildCallArgs.test_full_cmd_injects_session_id_when_set` (method) — Asserts a set _session_id is emitted as a --session-id flag. <!--#29ad66f6c2a1d9d4-->
- `TestPtyDriving` (class) — Tests PTY driving primitives: _feed_prompt bracketed-paste submission, _await_input_ready readiness gating, and _drain_pty reading/activity. <!--#bd9d1df3b40d4997-->
  - `TestPtyDriving.test_feed_prompt_sends_text_and_enter` (method) — Asserts _feed_prompt wraps the prompt in bracketed paste and submits with a trailing carriage return. <!--#7e6609ec0d7b9175-->
  - `TestPtyDriving.test_feed_prompt_multiline_uses_bracketed_paste` (method) — Asserts a multi-line prompt is delivered as one bracketed-paste payload with newlines intact, then a single submit. <!--#b63600aedea92404-->
  - `TestPtyDriving.test_await_input_ready_returns_after_output_settles` (method) — Asserts _await_input_ready returns promptly once existing PTY output has settled. <!--#54d82b9cf8664bdf-->
  - `TestPtyDriving.test_await_input_ready_waits_for_first_output` (method) — Asserts _await_input_ready waits for the first PTY output to appear before returning. <!--#ae2dedece199f5ca-->
  - `TestPtyDriving.test_await_input_ready_caps_at_timeout_without_output` (method) — Asserts _await_input_ready proceeds best-effort once the readiness timeout elapses without any output. <!--#824dd6088f1d7e09-->
  - `TestPtyDriving.test_feed_prompt_swallows_errors` (method) — Asserts _feed_prompt swallows exceptions raised while sending to a broken PTY. <!--#673e846519d35010-->
  - `TestPtyDriving.test_drain_pty_reads_until_eof_and_updates_activity` (method) — Asserts _drain_pty reads all chunks to EOF, accumulates the buffer, invokes on_output, and bumps the activity clock. <!--#377bea60a453b109-->
  - `TestPtyDriving.test_drain_pty_stops_on_stop_event` (method) — Asserts _drain_pty terminates its loop when the stop event is set even on a never-dying PTY. <!--#ee3b6bc9fb5264b9-->
- `TestTerminate` (class) — Tests _terminate's process-group SIGTERM→SIGKILL escalation, close, and tolerance of None and lookup errors. <!--#60e5fb6695ccae64-->
  - `TestTerminate.test_terminate_kills_group_and_closes` (method) — Asserts _terminate sends SIGTERM then SIGKILL to the process group and closes the PTY. <!--#89db074eae552cb6-->
  - `TestTerminate.test_terminate_none_is_noop` (method) — Asserts _terminate(None) is a safe no-op. <!--#b29cd57cd7fdd23c-->
  - `TestTerminate.test_terminate_swallows_lookup_error` (method) — Asserts _terminate still closes the PTY when getpgid raises ProcessLookupError. <!--#03237224542ce44b-->
- `TestLifecycle` (class) — Tests run_with_monitor/run lifecycle: normal exit capture, wall/inactivity timeouts (124), spawn-failure reclamation, thread cleanup, and KeyboardInterrupt handling. <!--#e5530a148e1c63f8-->
  - `TestLifecycle.test_normal_exit_captures_output` (method) — Asserts a normal exit yields returncode 0, success, captured output with the command header, and PTY reclamation. <!--#7c1941bae894cd9a-->
  - `TestLifecycle.test_wall_timeout_kills_and_returns_124` (method) — Asserts a never-finishing process trips the wall timeout, returning 124 with a 'Wall timeout' message and closed PTY. <!--#3033f68b43b91a07-->
  - `TestLifecycle.test_inactivity_timeout_kills_and_returns_124` (method) — Asserts a silent alive process trips the inactivity timeout, returning 124 with an 'inactivity timeout' message. <!--#d06ca88c810c9805-->
  - `TestLifecycle.test_finally_reclaims_on_spawn_failure` (method) — Asserts a spawn failure returns 127/failure with reclamation guaranteed by the finally block. <!--#a21902ce4b5feade-->
  - `TestLifecycle.test_threads_joined_no_leak` (method) — Asserts no claude-interactive I/O threads leak after a monitored run completes. <!--#1dd2824dbb541882-->
  - `TestLifecycle.test_keyboard_interrupt_preserves_partial_output` (method) — Asserts a KeyboardInterrupt from the supervisor marks the result interrupted with returncode -2 and closes the PTY. <!--#5e26d74d6e331f6a-->
  - `TestLifecycle.test_run_returns_completed_process` (method) — Asserts run() returns a CompletedProcess-like result with the exit code and captured stdout. <!--#7c89220478e0077a-->
- `_SpinnerPty` (class) — FakePty subclass that re-renders a cosmetic spinner/footer forever, simulating TUI noise that must not keep the inactivity clock fresh. <!--#fffd9f69d3859ead-->
  - `_SpinnerPty.__init__` (method) — Initializes the spinner PTY as alive-forever with a frame index counter. <!--#769a595a4d89f717-->
  - `_SpinnerPty.read_nonblocking` (method) — Returns an ever-changing spinner footer line (glyph plus volatile second/token counters) on every read. <!--#43dce2fba0065277-->
- `TestMeaningfulContentTracker` (class) — Tests _normalize_pty_lines and _MeaningfulContentTracker that distinguish genuine new output from cosmetic re-renders for the inactivity clock. <!--#f2293b30e2c416a6-->
  - `TestMeaningfulContentTracker.test_normalize_strips_ansi_and_collapses_digits` (method) — Asserts normalization strips ANSI codes and collapses volatile digit runs to '#'. <!--#fe3fe09bce4adfbf-->
  - `TestMeaningfulContentTracker.test_blank_and_pure_ansi_lines_dropped` (method) — Asserts blank and pure-ANSI lines are dropped during normalization. <!--#1f4f14ee0f54d54d-->

  - `TestMeaningfulContentTracker.test_partial_line_held_until_terminator` (method) — Asserts a fragment without a line terminator is held back until completed before counting as activity. <!--#7625113821745e82-->
  - `TestMeaningfulContentTracker.test_degraded_inactivity_fires_despite_cosmetic_rerenders` (method) — Regression test asserting the inactivity timeout still fires in degraded (no-watcher) mode despite a forever-spinning TUI. <!--#14549ce478fcbe2e-->

### `tests/test_claude_runner.py` (python) — Unit test suite for the Claude Code agent runner, covering `load_claude_commands` config resolution (built-in default, project-over-global precedence, legacy entry normalization), `ClaudeCodeRunner` identity/construction and its `ClaudeRunner` alias, infra-error detection (usage limits, exit-code-124 timeouts), synchronous `run()` behavior, and the command index/traversal helpers. <!--#246663bd534dfd89|f8e52fc38515c03d-->
- `_argv_after_skip_perms` (function) — Test helper returning the argv slice following --dangerously-skip-permissions so tests can assert flag adjacency without hard-coded indexes. <!--#b87c144882017c0c-->
- `TestLoadClaudeCommands` (class) — Test class covering `load_claude_commands` config resolution: built-in PATH-probed default, project-over-global override precedence, legacy entry normalization/ordering, and preservation of explicitly named non-claude agents. <!--#a80fe3a9145ba254-->
  - `TestLoadClaudeCommands.test_default_when_no_config` (method) — Asserts that with no config files present and only `claude` on PATH, `load_claude_commands` returns the single built-in `claude` entry at priority 0. <!--#0ba68e9d382297a8-->
  - `TestLoadClaudeCommands.test_project_config_overrides` (method) — Asserts a project se3.yaml config takes precedence over the global config. <!--#02cb57142485b362-->
  - `TestLoadClaudeCommands.test_global_used_when_no_project_config` (method) — Asserts the global config is used when no project config is present. <!--#f4f08e72a5ec60c5-->
  - `TestLoadClaudeCommands.test_legacy_commands_preserve_written_order` (method) — Asserts legacy claude_commands keep their written order and ignore the deprecated priority field. <!--#7ba308ef78d78127-->
  - `TestLoadClaudeCommands.test_string_entries_normalized` (method) — Asserts bare string command entries are normalized into dicts with cmd and priority keys. <!--#c8c02ca5f8e73d82-->
  - `TestLoadClaudeCommands.test_missing_priority_defaults_to_zero` (method) — Asserts a command entry lacking a priority defaults to priority 0. <!--#2d6b73b4f0f662cc-->
  - `TestLoadClaudeCommands.test_no_project_root_uses_global_only` (method) — Asserts that with no project root only the global config is consulted. <!--#1ac62780fc680336-->
  - `TestLoadClaudeCommands.test_explicit_codex_default_is_never_dropped` (method) — Asserts that a user-declared codex agent listed in `llm_caller.defaults` survives legacy conversion verbatim instead of being silently replaced. <!--#cf60014a14a5acda-->

### `tests/test_cleanup_history_leak.py` (python) — Test suite locking in cleanup_history_leak.py's classification logic so the one-time cleanup only deletes leak directories (empty, bare-.jsonl, residue-named) and stray root files while provably preserving real flow-id/recovered_/multi-step directories, covering dry-run safety, deletion targeting, per-category report counts, and content-independent bare-.jsonl leak detection. <!--#73168d281e3a09f3|7dbc5faf13def541-->

- `test_dry_run_removes_nothing` (function) — Asserts a dry-run cleanup deletes nothing, returns 0, and prints a DRY-RUN notice. <!--#d1323918d6e76cef-->
- `test_deletes_only_leaks` (function) — Asserts a real cleanup removes all leak dirs while leaving exactly the three real flow directories. <!--#14c0f48c7f85d28f-->
- `test_flow_id_and_recovered_protected` (function) — Asserts classify_dir returns None (preserve) for flow-id, recovered_, and multi-step uuid-style directories holding real content. <!--#526c630dd122d747-->
- `test_bare_jsonl_leak_removed_regardless_of_content` (function) — Asserts a directory whose sole file is a bare .jsonl is classified as an 'only_jsonl' leak regardless of that file's (non-signature or empty) content. <!--#2dfe7cbd9d7c3587-->
- `test_multistep_flow_with_real_step_file_preserved` (function) — Asserts a dir with a real named <step_id>.jsonl file is preserved (classify_dir returns None), not mistaken for a bare-.jsonl leak. <!--#453a010489ca3737-->
- `test_prompt_history_dir_is_residue` (function) — Asserts a multi-file prompt_history* directory is classified as 'residue_name' purely by name rather than by content criteria. <!--#1a9ebb4f4cbdd2e4-->
- `test_report_counts` (function) — Asserts the cleanup summary output reports the expected per-category counts (empty, single-.jsonl, residue-name dirs, and residue root files). <!--#6f3f29b8adfb1e45-->

### `tests/test_cleanup_project_roots.py` (python) — Unit tests for the one-time `scripts/cleanup_project_roots.py` registry-cleanup script, dynamically importing it to lock in its decision boundary: pytest-tempdir residue detection is anchored to `/tmp` and `/var/tmp` prefixes (not substring matches on real roots), `cleanup` removes residue while preserving genuine roots, `--dry-run` and no-op cases leave the registry byte-for-byte unchanged with no leftover `.tmp` sidecar, `--prune-missing` drops vanished non-residue roots, and the `main` CLI honours `--registry`. <!--#e8e485443058b40e|6e483719f18fa585-->
- `_write_registry` (function) — Test helper that writes a project-roots registry JSON file with the given list of root paths under a "project_roots" key. <!--#b5cfb59017b986ce-->
- `_read_roots` (function) — Test helper that reads a registry JSON file and returns its "project_roots" list. <!--#0e847833ce4c93bc-->
- `test_pytest_residue_matches_tmp_and_var_tmp_prefixes` (function) — Asserts that `_is_pytest_residue` recognizes pytest tempdir paths under both `/tmp` and `/var/tmp` prefixes. <!--#e194a8f70d2f5e43-->
- `test_pytest_residue_is_anchored_not_substring` (function) — Asserts that `_is_pytest_residue` is anchored to the OS tempdir prefix and does not flag real project roots that merely contain a `pytest-of-*` path segment. <!--#d43a2805fab1fd8d-->
- `test_cleanup_removes_pytest_residue_keeps_real_roots` (function) — Verifies that `cleanup` removes pytest-residue roots while preserving genuine project roots. <!--#65fce18006d643cd-->
- `test_cleanup_preserves_non_pytest_missing_root_without_prune` (function) — Verifies that without `prune_missing`, `cleanup` keeps a non-existent but non-residue root. <!--#4461dabbed3059f3-->
- `test_dry_run_does_not_modify_registry` (function) — Verifies that a dry-run `cleanup` leaves the registry file byte-for-byte unchanged. <!--#4848a1a147824900-->
- `test_prune_missing_drops_vanished_roots_keeps_existing` (function) — Verifies that `cleanup` with `prune_missing` drops non-existent non-residue roots while keeping existing ones. <!--#88ed8e2f8d7c3f98-->
- `test_prune_missing_dry_run_does_not_write` (function) — Verifies that `prune_missing` combined with dry-run does not write to the registry file. <!--#d798b5d10815049f-->
- `test_no_removals_leaves_file_untouched` (function) — Verifies that when nothing needs removing, `cleanup` leaves the registry file byte-for-byte identical (no rewrite). <!--#0484482c07789e5a-->
- `test_missing_registry_is_noop` (function) — Verifies that `cleanup` on a non-existent registry is a no-op returning success without creating the file. <!--#66042b63d37b59df-->
- `test_atomic_rewrite_leaves_no_tmp_file` (function) — Verifies that the atomic rewrite in `cleanup` leaves no leftover `.tmp` sidecar file after `os.replace`. <!--#432f1fcfc619b2e2-->
- `test_main_honours_registry_flag` (function) — Verifies that the `main` CLI entry point honours the `--registry` flag and cleans the specified registry. <!--#ed0950a7b67f97ba-->

### `tests/test_cli_confirm.py` (python) — Test module for CLI-subprocess confirmation prompts, covering detect_confirmation_prompt pattern matching (English and Chinese), the interaction_calls call-file writer/response reader, make_cli_confirm_handler's flow_id/step_id context placement, and on_confirm wiring through run_with_monitor so prompts are answered via stdin without hanging. <!--#3b063bdfcf6be598|c10d91fd5933f66e-->
- `TestDetectConfirmationPrompt` (class) — Test class validating that detect_confirmation_prompt matches known confirm prompts (including Chinese), ignores non-prompts, and extracts enumerated options. <!--#75471fb4b360a5be-->
  - `TestDetectConfirmationPrompt.test_known_prompts_detected` (method) — Asserts each known confirmation line (English and Chinese) is detected, returning the stripped prompt and an options list. <!--#74e1d1a2d4e66e07-->
