- `test_is_still_active_rejects_stale_flow_when_different_flow_is_active` (function) — Asserts _is_still_active returns False for a stale meta whose flow_id no longer matches the engine.json's active flow, and True only for the current flow. <!--#d78a01fee66f5d76-->
- `test_is_still_active_returns_false_for_non_active_source` (function) — Asserts _is_still_active never re-checks archived/history-only metas as active. <!--#762a82f09c02f03a-->
- `test_is_still_active_returns_false_when_engine_json_missing` (function) — Asserts _is_still_active returns False when the project's engine.json is absent. <!--#f5d0a20e41fff33e-->
- `test_read_active_flows_drops_stale_flow_after_flow_change` (function) — Asserts read_active_flows reports the newly started flow and drops the completed prior flow after a flow change in the same root. <!--#a44828f62d5ee0c8-->
- `test_all_project_roots_historical_walk_bounded_per_ttl` (function) — Asserts the aggregator's all_project_roots runs historical-root enumeration at most once per HISTORICAL_ROOTS_TTL window despite many calls. <!--#4b2c44773174313a-->
- `test_combined_poll_push_cadence_bounded` (function) — Simulates the combined poll and push loops over many ticks and asserts disk enumerations and index rebuilds stay bounded rather than growing per tick. <!--#38706c36e60ef929-->

### `tests/test_daemon_history.py` (python) — Pytest suite for the daemon-side history reader (se3.daemon.history), covering flow-index construction across active/archived/history sources, incremental cursor-based jsonl reads, active-flow change signatures (including same-(mtime,size) rewrite hardening), terminal step-event streaming, and project-root enumeration. <!--#9dd7e73da5a54a4d|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `tests/test_daemon_history_index_delta.py` (python) — A pytest suite locking the daemon client's incremental HISTORY_INDEX traffic-reduction contract, verifying that full index frames are sent only as reconciliation baselines (connect/request/legacy peer) while steady-state changes ship per-flow delta upserts/removals, that updated_at-only 'liveness' ticks are throttled to the status heartbeat, and that index deltas coexist with metered incremental HISTORY_DATA cursor pushes. <!--#83735118223e3f1e|bb3082123d434a96-->
- `_FakeWS` (class) — A minimal async WebSocket stand-in that captures and decodes every protocol frame the daemon client sends, for assertion in tests. <!--#419a56ffe2a5b3eb-->
  - `_FakeWS.__init__` (method) — Initializes the fake WebSocket with an empty `sent` list to accumulate captured frames. <!--#b8b92aad379d234c-->
  - `_FakeWS.send` (method) — Async send override that decodes the outgoing frame and appends it to the captured `sent` list. <!--#7d44362527b3e749-->
- `_IndexProvider` (class) — A stub history provider whose returned session index and active-flow reads are set per test to drive the client's history-push logic. <!--#02665c0bc7fb68f4-->
  - `_IndexProvider.__init__` (method) — Initializes the provider with empty `metas` (index) and `reads` (active flows) lists. <!--#45e87bde89ae83e5-->
  - `_IndexProvider.build_index` (method) — Returns a copy of the configured session-meta list as the current history index. <!--#474a9aa1feea4e55-->
  - `_IndexProvider.read_active_flows` (method) — Returns a copy of the configured active-flow reads, ignoring the passed cursors. <!--#3ee216e300d899fd-->
  - `_IndexProvider.active_flow_signature` (method) — Returns an empty signature dict, stubbing out active-flow change detection. <!--#d5e6eba440e59874-->
- `_make_client` (function) — Factory that builds a DaemonClient wired to a given provider and forces the peer-reduction flag to simulate a rev-3 (or legacy) server. <!--#a6dfa0b04e6b7ea0-->
- `_meta` (function) — Helper that constructs a SessionMeta with overridable flow_id, updated_at, status, and step_count for building test index entries. <!--#859733252d6e0a39-->
- `_frames` (function) — Helper that filters a fake WebSocket's captured frames down to those of a given message type. <!--#3070312c78e68fc4-->
- `test_meta_change_is_throttleable_updated_at_only` (function) — Asserts that a meta change touching only `updated_at` is classified as throttleable. <!--#3e8ec2ce613c30de-->
- `test_meta_change_is_throttleable_substantive_change_is_not` (function) — Asserts that a meta change including a status change (alongside updated_at) is not throttleable. <!--#daf3c15f016520ff-->
- `test_meta_change_is_throttleable_identical_is_false` (function) — Asserts that identical metas (no delta) are reported as not throttleable since there is nothing to throttle. <!--#35fb7e51ff1b4314-->
- `test_force_index_sends_full_baseline_and_primes` (function) — Verifies that a forced push emits a single full HISTORY_INDEX baseline with all flows, primes the client, and emits no delta frame. <!--#214193799c1917ee-->
- `test_single_flow_change_emits_only_that_flow_upsert` (function) — Verifies that after a baseline, a substantive change to one flow emits a delta containing only that flow's upsert and no full re-push or removals. <!--#13ac22e5adc09f0a-->
- `test_vanished_flow_emits_removal` (function) — Verifies that a flow disappearing from the index produces a delta frame with an empty upserts list and the flow id in `removed`. <!--#3e1697f16f94aa1b-->
- `test_unchanged_index_emits_no_frame` (function) — Verifies that a push with no index change since the baseline emits neither a HISTORY_INDEX nor a delta frame. <!--#e2001dcc93e70275-->
- `test_history_index_request_resends_full_baseline` (function) — Verifies that a HISTORY_INDEX_REQUEST forces a full baseline re-push (never a delta) even for a reduction-capable peer. <!--#a71bec7c8031630f-->
- `test_updated_at_only_change_is_throttled_off_heartbeat` (function) — Verifies that an updated_at-only change is held back on a non-heartbeat tick and flushed as a delta on the next status heartbeat. <!--#7ab1804f0e892a44-->
- `test_substantive_change_is_not_throttled_off_heartbeat` (function) — Verifies that a substantive (status) change is delivered as a delta immediately even on a fast non-heartbeat tick. <!--#68b19830c48e9480-->
- `test_legacy_peer_always_gets_full_index_not_delta` (function) — Verifies that for a legacy (non-reduction) peer a change re-pushes a full HISTORY_INDEX rather than a delta frame. <!--#69ddaf46bff14f88-->
- `test_index_push_frames_are_metered_by_type` (function) — Verifies that full-baseline and delta index frames are each counted and byte-metered under distinct message-type keys, with the delta smaller than the baseline. <!--#1a343682734689bf-->
- `test_active_flow_cursor_push_coexists_with_index_delta` (function) — Verifies that when a flow's meta changes and it emits new records, both an index delta and an incremental HISTORY_DATA frame go out and cursors advance. <!--#985589a95f95cdae-->

### `tests/test_daemon_history_ordinal.py` (python) — Test suite pinning the DaemonHistoryReader's stable per-record `ordinal` (the 0-based physical line index used as `step_id#ordinal` identity) — verifying ordinals are per-step not global, survive full→append deltas unchanged, re-map to new content across equal-length/grown/shrunk retry rewrites, and stay distinct for empty marker records. <!--#b46acd89df6d0020|350e42b5980942cf-->
- `_write_jsonl` (function) — Test helper that writes a list of dicts as a newline-terminated jsonl file, creating parent directories as needed. <!--#de06c26baee321d6-->
- `_make_reader` (function) — Test helper that constructs a DaemonHistoryReader whose project-roots provider returns the given root paths. <!--#808724bfc5456a05-->
- `test_records_carry_zero_based_ordinal` (function) — Asserts each read record's ordinal equals its 0-based physical line index within the step file. <!--#a331dac2efced82f-->
- `test_ordinal_is_per_step_not_global` (function) — Verifies ordinals restart at 0 for each step file rather than continuing globally across steps. <!--#e4cf1fb1e62bdfe8-->
- `test_marker_records_with_empty_content_get_distinct_ordinals` (function) — Confirms empty-content marker records stay individually addressable via distinct ordinals instead of collapsing under the old content+timestamp key. <!--#9a3cfd792e7d254e-->
- `test_same_logical_line_same_ordinal_across_full_and_append` (function) — Checks that an append delta assigns new lines the same physical ordinals a fresh full read would, returning only the appended lines. <!--#7493bb6f4ca570f0-->
- `test_retry_equal_length_rewrite_maps_ordinal_to_new_content` (function) — Verifies an equal-length in-place step rewrite is detected and re-maps each ordinal to the new line's content. <!--#9e7f30ce19a999b0-->
- `test_retry_grown_rewrite_maps_ordinal_to_new_content` (function) — Verifies a rewrite that grows the file re-maps every consumed ordinal, including the newly added line. <!--#90d2c9e7730b6dd9-->
- `test_retry_shrunk_rewrite_maps_ordinal_to_new_content` (function) — Verifies a shrinking rewrite re-maps surviving ordinals and leaks no stale high-ordinal survivors from the old batch. <!--#cbc9dbd8d649cae8-->
- `test_ordinal_stable_across_repeated_discovery_rewrites` (function) — Simulates repeated PAUSE/resume discovery rewrites and asserts each ordinal reflects the latest round's content. <!--#f3940ffbfa5d2603-->

### `tests/test_daemon_history_readpath_cache.py` (python) — A regression-lock test module for the daemon history read-path disk-JSON cache (#243/#260/#209) that verifies oversized legacy engine archives are recovered via bounded head+tail degraded reads without ever being fully parsed, unchanged files are full-parsed at most once via stat- and whole-content-hash-keyed caching (including catching same-(mtime,size) middle rewrites and honoring force_fresh), and unextractable degraded reads are warn-once skipped rather than fatal. <!--#5c959aa758c34c61|d7f583776e13951f-->
- `_isolate_module_state` (function) — A fixture that clears the process-wide disk JSON cache and history warn-dedup set before and after each test so caches never leak across tests. <!--#dff4b11ad2fe0def-->
- `_count_full_parses` (function) — A helper that monkeypatches the disk cache's whole-file `_parse_json` seam with a counting wrapper, returning a dict that tracks how many full-file JSON parses occur. <!--#00fd47cb56c9c1ed-->
- `_write_oversized_archive` (function) — A helper that writes a legacy-format, >5 MiB `engine_*.json` archive with hot keys at the head, a multi-MB `state` blob in the middle, and legacy `is_worktree_mode`/`project_root` keys in the tail, to exercise bounded head+tail degraded reads. <!--#97c4b66551ab32bc-->
- `test_oversized_archive_never_fully_parsed_but_project_root_extracted` (function) — Asserts that enumerating historical roots over a giant legacy archive recovers its tail-positioned `project_root` via degraded head+tail reads while never fully parsing the file (parse count stays 0). <!--#cce24dce3556f744-->
- `test_oversized_archive_degraded_read_recovers_legacy_tail_key` (function) — A direct-call test that `read_engine_header` on an oversized archive scans the tail window and recovers all head and legacy-tail keys including `is_worktree_mode` without full parsing. <!--#bb13928d2f2278af-->
- `test_unchanged_meta_json_parsed_once_across_enumerations` (function) — Asserts that an unchanged `_meta.json` is fully parsed only once across two back-to-back enumerations because the second read is a stat-keyed cache hit. <!--#3c68706c4afbcad0-->
- `test_degraded_extraction_failure_is_skipped_and_warned` (function) — Asserts that an oversized file yielding no extractable hot keys is skipped with a warn-once WARNING (not fatal, never fully parsed), and enumeration still returns the artifact-bearing root without re-warning on repeat. <!--#1199c9e6594a6349-->
- `_build_large_engine` (function) — Test helper that builds a >128 KiB indent=2 engine.json whose only varying bytes are a marker buried in the true middle of a 3000-entry steps table—outside the former 64 KiB head and tail windows—so a same-size middle rewrite is undetectable to a head+tail-only freshness check. <!--#80f0681ed72bafa1-->
- `test_active_engine_middle_rewrite_same_stat_returns_fresh_parse` (function) — Regression test that a middle-only rewrite of a large active engine.json sharing an identical (mtime, size) is caught by the whole-content freshness hash, so read_engine_header(active=True) returns the fresh middle rather than a stale parse (the #260 primary daemon-side fix). <!--#92328b631e759c09-->
- `test_active_engine_unchanged_parsed_once_across_ticks` (function) — Test that an unchanged >128 KiB active engine.json read ten times is fully json-parsed exactly once—the content hash matches each tick, bounding cost to a read + digest and preventing re-introduction of the #209 per-tick parse sink. <!--#d4f77411aeb833d3-->
- `test_active_engine_small_file_middle_rewrite_returns_fresh_parse` (function) — Test that the under-128 KiB small-file path still catches a same-(mtime, size) middle rewrite, locking that the whole-content hash preserves the pre-existing whole-file-read correctness for the degenerate small case. <!--#f3af2f40b151f92e-->
- `test_oversized_active_engine_degrades_unchanged` (function) — Test that an oversized (> MAX_PARSE_BYTES guard) active engine.json is never fully parsed—the size guard runs before the verify path, forcing the always-fresh degraded head+tail scan regardless of active=True, unchanged by the whole-content freshness fix (the #209 guard). <!--#4a5bd4ffa87a8c6d-->
- `test_force_fresh_bypasses_stale_same_stat_cache` (function) — Test that force_fresh=True re-reads and re-parses disk truth even on a (mtime, size) + content-hash cache hit—verified by pre-seeding the cache then hiding a same-stat middle rewrite—backing the active-flow drop decision's true-value fallback. <!--#bc21c1da86be296b-->

- `test_per_file_cursor_first_full_then_append_no_loss_no_dup` (function) — Verifies per-file byte cursors give a new file a full first read while existing files append, so the union of deltas equals one full read with no loss or duplication. <!--#cc73b490a4c94793-->

- `test_retry_rewrite_equal_size_delivers_new_records` (function) — Asserts an in-place retry rewriting the step jsonl to the same byte size but different content is detected via fingerprint and delivers the full replacement instead of seeing 'no new bytes' (issue #209). <!--#89361356232f3890-->
- `test_retry_rewrite_equal_size_preserved_boundary_delivers_new_records` (function) — Asserts an equal-size rewrite that changes an earlier record while keeping the trailing boundary record identical is still detected by whole-prefix fingerprinting (issue #209 iteration 5). <!--#c291d05f80ce3edd-->

- `test_retry_rewrite_larger_size_delivers_full_replacement` (function) — Asserts an in-place retry rewriting the step jsonl larger than the old offset delivers the full replacement from the start rather than a stale-offset partial suffix slice (issue #209). <!--#14202aaa3eef0362-->
- `test_retry_rewrite_larger_size_preserved_head_delivers_full_replacement` (function) — Asserts a grow-case rewrite that preserves the leading head record still falls through to whole-prefix fingerprinting and delivers the full replacement rather than a suffix-only slice (issue #209 iteration 7). <!--#b59092b2be527bb9-->
- `test_retry_rewrite_larger_size_preserved_head_and_boundary_delivers_full_replacement` (function) — Asserts a grow-case rewrite preserving both the head and boundary windows but changing a middle record is caught by whole-prefix fingerprinting, defeating two-bounded-window detection (issue #209 iteration 8). <!--#2c5f3e84199de126-->

- `test_push_history_resend_is_append_not_full_reread` (function) — End-to-end test through DaemonClient._push_history asserting a retry resend ships an APPEND frame carrying only the new record, with no duplicate re-read of the prior attempt. <!--#e700ca281f2f7ded-->

- `test_is_still_active_genuine_terminal_drop_pays_no_extra_read` (function) — Verifies that a cleanly terminal (COMPLETED) flow is dropped on the cached read alone, without triggering the forced-fresh re-confirm fallback. <!--#7ac95be5116d3570-->
- `test_read_active_flows_advances_cursor_on_steps_first_write_and_new_jsonl` (function) — End-to-end boundary test proving read_active_flows still delivers the analyze increment and advances the per-file cursor when a steps-table first-write coincides with a same-(mtime,size) engine rewrite and a newly-created analyze jsonl. <!--#d4e9ccf9edfc9780-->

### `tests/test_daemon_readpath_cache.py` (python) — Regression-lock test suite for the issue #243 (group G2) daemon read-path hardening, asserting that the stat-keyed `disk_json_cache` parses each unchanged active/worktree/resumable engine.json at most once per push tick, that all such parses are offloaded off the event-loop thread to prevent the WebUI freeze, and that oversized (>5 MiB) engine.json files fall back to a degraded head+tail header scan that still keeps runs visible without full-parsing. <!--#a8395bbb3064be04|8863b7d4b5eabefd-->

- `_count_djc_parses` (function) — Test helper that monkeypatches `disk_json_cache._json_loads` to record every actual JSON parse, so tests can count the expensive parse operations the read-path fix collapses. <!--#01672804ecbef6b9-->
- `test_unchanged_engine_json_parsed_once_across_push_ticks` (function) — Asserts that active, worktree, and resumable engine.json files are each parsed at most once across ten unchanged push-tick rounds, proving the stat-keyed cache eliminates per-tick re-parsing. <!--#b9717e8b87f39cf0-->
- `test_changed_engine_json_is_reparsed` (function) — Verifies the `(path, mtime, size)` cache serves unchanged reads without re-parsing but re-parses after a genuine engine.json rewrite so stale content is never returned. <!--#83cc91ecce5df4cb-->
- `_patch_all_parse_seams` (function) — Test helper that patches the unified disk_json_cache parse seams (`_json_loads` and `_parse_json_file`) to record the calling thread ident on every daemon disk-JSON parse. <!--#ca43e023250819ed-->
- `test_signature_checks_are_genuine_disk_parse_points` (function) — Pins the premise that the client's `_calls_changed`/`_history_changed` signature checks really do trigger disk JSON parses, so the off-loading guarantee isn't tested vacuously. <!--#0a2093d8b2614603-->
- `test_push_loop_never_parses_json_on_event_loop_thread` (function) — Runs the real `DaemonClient._push_loop` for several ticks and asserts no disk JSON parse ever occurs on the event-loop thread, locking the fix that offloads parses to worker threads and prevents the WebUI freeze. <!--#5ee9866fc0d0d94a-->
- `_write_oversized_engine` (function) — Test helper that writes a >5 MiB indent=2 `engine.json` with head keys (flow_id/status) and a tail key (is_worktree_mode) around a giant `state`, exercising the degraded head+tail scan. <!--#b6a1ca3d1af5bbcd-->
- `test_oversized_engine_json_uses_degraded_scan_no_full_parse` (function) — Asserts a >5 MiB engine.json's hot keys are recovered via head+tail scan without ever full-parsing (`_json_loads`) or caching the file. <!--#7657881b9a1ac7d5-->
- `test_oversized_worktree_run_stays_visible_via_degraded_scan` (function) — Verifies the aggregator's worktree scan still discovers an active worktree run whose engine.json is oversized, so degrading (not skipping) keeps the run visible in the WebUI. <!--#7349b9682c60378c-->
- `test_oversized_unextractable_file_warns_once_and_skips` (function) — Verifies a giant file yielding no extractable header keys is skipped by `read_engine_header` (returns None) with exactly one degraded-scan warning. <!--#39e2eb675b5d1d98-->

### `tests/test_daemon_spawner_path.py` (python) — Test module for the daemon spawner's login-shell PATH handling, unit-testing the pure merge_path_env and resolve_login_shell_path helpers and integration-testing that DaemonSpawner-spawned (and resumed) children inherit the merged PATH while degrading gracefully on resolution failures. <!--#583538c3dba6c1ff|923f7bdb83c0c5d8-->

  - `TestMergePathEnv.test_current_empty_returns_login` (method) — Asserts an empty current PATH yields the login PATH unchanged. <!--#57f513eaf526b4fe-->
  - `TestMergePathEnv.test_both_none_returns_none` (method) — Asserts merging two None PATHs returns None. <!--#f951c31d6258ee32-->
  - `TestMergePathEnv.test_both_empty_returns_none` (method) — Asserts merging two empty PATHs returns None. <!--#2de7f0e4b37a1996-->
  - `TestMergePathEnv.test_single_entry_each` (method) — Asserts merging single-entry login and current PATHs places current first. <!--#9321d0b4df0ab3d6-->
  - `TestMergePathEnv.test_preserves_order_within_login` (method) — Asserts login entries retain their original relative order in the merged result. <!--#f7e2ca0fee642cd6-->
  - `TestMergePathEnv.test_preserves_order_within_current` (method) — Asserts current entries retain their original relative order after the login entries. <!--#c1d07f3a98391665-->

  - `TestResolveLoginShellPath._write_shell` (method) — Helper that writes an executable fake shell script to tmp_path and returns its path. <!--#fc1efdf9c232f226-->
  - `TestResolveLoginShellPath.test_success_with_normal_output` (method) — Asserts a valid PATH is parsed from shell output even when preceded by noise lines. <!--#cb79ed06cbc9811f-->
  - `TestResolveLoginShellPath.test_success_takes_last_pathsep_line` (method) — Asserts the last output line containing os.pathsep is chosen as the PATH. <!--#398d20f013584224-->

  - `TestResolveLoginShellPath.test_timeout_returns_none` (method) — Asserts a shell that hangs past the timeout causes resolution to return None. <!--#bd39f3c32fd13db8-->
  - `TestResolveLoginShellPath.test_empty_output_returns_none` (method) — Asserts empty shell output causes resolution to return None. <!--#969f25c9f6b707ba-->
  - `TestResolveLoginShellPath.test_output_without_pathsep_returns_none` (method) — Asserts shell output lacking a path separator causes resolution to return None. <!--#c0faf97151dc02be-->
  - `TestResolveLoginShellPath.test_missing_shell_env_falls_back_to_bash` (method) — Asserts that with $SHELL unset, resolution falls back to /bin/bash and returns a string or None without crashing. <!--#7aab126988fa6193-->
  - `TestResolveLoginShellPath.test_nonexistent_shell_returns_none` (method) — Asserts a $SHELL pointing to a missing binary causes resolution to return None. <!--#1e79ddd07c205949-->

### `tests/test_daemon_status_gating.py` (python) — A test module locking the daemon's G6 traffic-reduction contract: it uses an in-memory fake WebSocket and a hand-configured DaemonClient to verify that unchanged ticks collapse to keepalives (only for rev-3 lean peers, never legacy), changed or force-pushed ticks send full STATUS_UPDATEs, per-message-type byte metrics accumulate, and aggregated snapshots are thinned by clipping issue descriptions and pending-call prompts to the shared `_DESC_CLIP` (200) standard. <!--#a97f1be46bc8faf4|224f12d8f1a116e8-->
- `_FakeWS` (class) — A minimal in-memory WebSocket stand-in that decodes and records every frame the daemon client sends, letting tests inspect the message stream. <!--#c3ad43269d7be7e8-->
  - `_FakeWS.__init__` (method) — Initializes the fake WebSocket with an empty `sent` list to accumulate captured frames. <!--#b8b92aad379d234c-->
  - `_FakeWS.send` (method) — Async send override that decodes the outgoing frame via `protocol.decode` and appends it to the captured `sent` list. <!--#7d44362527b3e749-->
- `_client` (function) — Test helper that builds a `DaemonClient` around a snapshot provider and directly sets its learned peer protocol version to model a rev-3 (lean) or legacy peer without a full handshake. <!--#f804c2648e99bfd6-->
- `_types` (function) — Helper returning the list of message types from a fake WebSocket's captured frames for concise assertions. <!--#1847dfb55e9608b9-->
- `test_unchanged_tick_collapses_to_keepalive` (function) — Asserts that two identical snapshots (differing only in the excluded `generated_at` stamp) produce one full STATUS_UPDATE then a KEEPALIVE carrying the same content signature the gate matched on. <!--#c898c1355579076c-->
- `test_changed_tick_sends_full_status_update` (function) — Asserts that a substantive content change (adding an issue) between ticks yields a fresh full STATUS_UPDATE rather than gating to a keepalive. <!--#64560a4ecf7d3d22-->
- `test_legacy_peer_never_gets_a_keepalive` (function) — Asserts that a pre-rev-3 peer always receives full STATUS_UPDATEs even on unchanged ticks, since it would reject the revision-3 keepalive frame. <!--#4fe5f05411039296-->
- `test_force_bypasses_the_gate` (function) — Asserts that an event-driven `force=True` push sends a full STATUS_UPDATE even when the content is unchanged and would otherwise gate to a keepalive. <!--#bbd9767523dca862-->
- `test_metrics_accumulate_per_message_type` (function) — Asserts that each sent frame is metered per message type in `client.metrics`, that a keepalive costs fewer bytes than a full update, and that the synthetic `__total__` roll-up sums both frames. <!--#f5cd4f5c5863b2f9-->
- `test_desc_clip_standard_is_200` (function) — Pins that the snapshot's description clip standard `_DESC_CLIP` equals the shared history value of 200. <!--#da6c8b9cc69871e8-->
- `test_collected_issue_description_is_clipped` (function) — Asserts that `DaemonAggregator._collect_issues` truncates each issue's description to `_DESC_CLIP` chars plus an ellipsis so full bodies are fetched on demand rather than inlined. <!--#289efb2ef33f83ec-->
- `test_issue_snapshot_to_dict_is_a_summary` (function) — Asserts that `IssueSnapshot.to_dict` emits exactly the webui summary field set and nothing more. <!--#52a079e5c5ff833a-->
- `test_machine_wide_pending_call_prompt_is_clipped` (function) — Asserts that `PendingCall.to_dict(clip_prompt=True)` clips the prompt to `_DESC_CLIP` while the parameter defaults to emitting the verbatim body. <!--#9909a9c8eb7b7c42-->

### `tests/test_daemon_traffic_reduction.py` (python) — Test suite locking the G2 daemon traffic-reduction contract: aggregator clipping of issue descriptions and machine-wide call prompts, signature-gated keepalive-vs-full STATUS_UPDATE pushing (including legacy-peer and force cases), on-demand DETAIL_REQUEST fetch of untruncated text with graceful error replies, and per-frame wire-byte metering, using in-memory WebSocket and client fakes. <!--#34b834ccd05bcf08|7381946786761b5d-->
- `_FakeWS` (class) — A minimal in-memory WebSocket stand-in that decodes and records every frame the client sends so tests can assert on the wire output. <!--#e6c82bc92db5d9fa-->
  - `_FakeWS.__init__` (method) — Initializes the fake WebSocket with an empty `sent` list to accumulate captured frames. <!--#ce393d52044e73f0-->
  - `_FakeWS.send` (method) — Async send stub that decodes the outgoing payload via `protocol.decode` and appends it to the `sent` list. <!--#154edf553e8ef4d4-->
- `_make_client` (function) — Test factory that builds a `DaemonClient` with canned identity/version fields and a default snapshot provider, allowing per-test overrides. <!--#f3137c441b7b6c4e-->
- `_write_issue` (function) — Helper that writes a YAML issue file (with a `NNN_slug` filename) into a temp `se3/issues/open` dir so the aggregator can collect it. <!--#b1f1f48eb614488c-->
- `test_issue_snapshot_description_clipped` (function) — Asserts the aggregator clips an overlong issue description to `_DESC_CLIP` plus a `...` ellipsis, consistently in the object and its `to_dict`. <!--#dbef1c95b0289db5-->
- `test_short_issue_description_untouched` (function) — Verifies a short issue description passes through the aggregator unchanged (no clipping). <!--#1e3cb26d244d5bf5-->
- `test_status_update_pending_call_prompts_clipped_on_both_surfaces` (function) — Checks that a long pending-call prompt is clipped on both the machine-wide and flow-own `to_dict` surfaces while the raw `call.to_dict()` still returns the verbatim body. <!--#790b6c4ebd1c15c2-->
- `test_status_signature_ignores_generated_at` (function) — Confirms `_status_signature` ignores the `generated_at` timestamp but changes when the flow content changes. <!--#9b2855228c77e7c1-->
- `test_unchanged_snapshot_sends_keepalive_when_peer_supports` (function) — Verifies that an unchanged snapshot sends a full baseline first then a lean keepalive (carrying the matched signature) when the peer speaks revision 3. <!--#7007c7e2aba72a13-->
- `test_changed_snapshot_sends_full_update` (function) — Verifies that a changing snapshot yields two full STATUS_UPDATE frames rather than a keepalive. <!--#a31730ecd4bae1ec-->
- `test_legacy_peer_never_gets_keepalive` (function) — Verifies a legacy (revision-2) peer always receives full STATUS_UPDATE frames and never lean keepalives. <!--#5aee5d5470255ca2-->
- `test_force_bypasses_keepalive_gate` (function) — Verifies that `force=True` on `_push_status` sends a full update even when the snapshot is unchanged. <!--#d57744a4fb5847b0-->
- `test_detail_request_returns_full_issue` (function) — Verifies a DETAIL_REQUEST for an issue returns a successful DETAIL_DATA reply with the untruncated description and echoed request id. <!--#8f5c19136426c050-->
- `test_detail_request_returns_full_call_prompt` (function) — Verifies a DETAIL_REQUEST for a call returns the full untruncated prompt and correct call id. <!--#8661e2c5e509c15b-->
- `test_detail_request_normalizes_legacy_call_fields` (function) — Verifies legacy call bodies storing text under `message`/`question` are normalized so the full text surfaces under the canonical `prompt` key. <!--#13cdb9d7c5d47912-->
- `test_detail_request_missing_target_replies_error` (function) — Verifies a DETAIL_REQUEST for a nonexistent target returns an `ok=false` DETAIL_DATA error reply with no `detail` body rather than dropping. <!--#91d967fe656dcd93-->
- `test_detail_request_resolves_via_known_roots` (function) — Verifies a DETAIL_REQUEST lacking a `project_root` falls back to the client's last-known roots to locate and return the full issue. <!--#c7124c3794952c94-->
- `test_send_accrues_wire_metrics` (function) — Verifies every `_send` accrues per-type and total frame counts and byte totals into the client's `metrics`. <!--#f4451eb935e75f4b-->
- `test_session_dials_with_permessage_deflate` (function) — Verifies `_session` pins `compression="deflate"` and `max_size=MAX_WS_MESSAGE_BYTES` on the websockets connect call, using a stub that aborts at `__aenter__`. <!--#467fcf58aa2d63d2-->

### `tests/test_daemon_worktree_discovery_multiround.py` (python) — Test module exercising DaemonHistoryReader's multi-round worktree discovery-file handling — verifying that incremental appends, from-scratch full reads, late worktree-copy appearance, cross-root merge selection, and post-merge primary/sidecar streams all yield stable, globally unique (step_id, ordinal) keys so frontend reconciliation never drops or duplicates records. <!--#02b1fe3228c88f72|a60dd48ce2db6247-->
- `_write_jsonl` (function) — Helper that creates parent directories and writes a list of dicts to a file as JSONL lines. <!--#f321072562a278a4-->

- `_make_reader` (function) — Helper that constructs a DaemonHistoryReader whose project-roots provider yields the given root paths. <!--#f5fb70620f9f4765-->

- `_make_worktree` (function) — Helper that creates and returns a named worktree directory under the main root's se3/worktrees. <!--#b329f4718dc5d89d-->
- `_keys` (function) — Helper that extracts the (step_id, ordinal) identity pairs the frontend reconciles records by. <!--#4b068bb00274497d-->
- `test_live_worktree_discovery_all_rounds_unique_and_stable` (function) — Verifies that a growing worktree discovery file read via one full snapshot plus incremental appends delivers every round exactly once with globally unique, stable (step_id, ordinal) keys. <!--#1f23f622991a4500-->
- `test_full_read_reproduces_append_ordinals` (function) — Verifies that a fresh from-scratch full read assigns each line the same (step_id, ordinal) identity that the earlier incremental append path produced. <!--#6baa8acb3b823db7-->
- `test_late_worktree_copy_switch_reemits_all_rounds` (function) — Verifies that when the worktree copy of a discovery file appears after the main-repo copy was already read, the reader re-reads it from line 0 so later rounds arrive and re-emitted early lines keep their original keys for idempotent reconciliation. <!--#70821b78bb531d22-->
- `test_merge_selection_sticks_to_worktree_copy` (function) — Verifies that cross-root merge selection consistently picks the worktree copy over the same-named main copy regardless of which file is transiently larger. <!--#d947a699af2bc7f8-->
- `test_live_worktree_reads_stay_incremental_no_reemit` (function) — Verifies that with a stable worktree selection, successive reads of a growing live flow stay in append mode and never re-emit round 1, despite a stale same-named main copy existing throughout. <!--#544a85d8cbebb3a4-->
- `test_post_merge_primary_and_sidecar_distinct_streams` (function) — Verifies that after merge-back both the primary discovery file and its from-worktree sidecar are read as distinct streams with different display step_ids so their per-file ordinals never collide. <!--#989fb7460917c1d1-->
- `test_pre_fix_collision_would_lose_sidecar_records` (function) — Documents the fixed bug by simulating the frontend's key-based reconcile and asserting the sidecar's ordinal-0 record no longer shares a key with (and thus is not dropped by) the primary's. <!--#7d0a99c6358707f4-->

### `tests/test_daemon_worktree_gc.py` (python) — Unit tests for the Daemon's periodic worktree-GC tick, verifying that _maybe_run_gc fires _gc_once at most once per (positive) gc_interval, that _gc_once sweeps every tracked project root via a mocked gc_worktree_runs while forwarding max-age and tolerating per-root failures, and that retained completed-but-unmerged branches are surfaced as WARNING log records. <!--#ba7358536a0bda54|2c8d7251ba59e07f-->
- `_make_daemon` (function) — Test helper that constructs a Daemon with an isolated pid_dir and configurable GC interval/max-age, optionally seeding one project root, returning the daemon and its root. <!--#5b6e0c9342e73b4b-->
- `_run` (function) — Tiny helper that runs a coroutine to completion via asyncio.run for the synchronous test bodies. <!--#48a8d32a4a8529d2-->
- `test_gc_config_defaults` (function) — Asserts DaemonConfig defaults the GC interval to 3600s and max age to 86400s. <!--#89d0629c99c8ff0a-->
- `test_maybe_run_gc_fires_on_first_poll` (function) — Verifies _maybe_run_gc invokes _gc_once once and records _last_gc_at on the very first poll. <!--#a228b3bbf5eb1bb4-->
- `test_maybe_run_gc_skips_within_interval` (function) — Verifies a second immediate _maybe_run_gc call is skipped because it falls inside the GC interval. <!--#c13fd965a64257ba-->
- `test_maybe_run_gc_reruns_after_interval` (function) — Verifies _maybe_run_gc runs _gc_once again once the simulated last-sweep time is more than one interval in the past. <!--#8ad9f44160f9ec67-->
- `test_maybe_run_gc_disabled_when_interval_nonpositive` (function) — Verifies a non-positive gc_interval fully disables the GC tick, leaving _gc_once uncalled and _last_gc_at unset. <!--#e0fb8cfc1ce0cf57-->
- `test_gc_once_sweeps_each_root_with_max_age` (function) — Verifies _gc_once calls gc_worktree_runs once per tracked (realpath'd) project root, forwarding gc_max_age_seconds and dry_run=False. <!--#a15cda739b55045a-->
- `test_gc_once_survives_one_root_failure` (function) — Verifies _gc_once swallows (rather than propagates) an exception raised while sweeping a single root. <!--#4f8f0cf140e08ccd-->
- `test_retained_unmerged_branch_warns` (function) — Verifies a report with a retained completed-but-unmerged worktree branch triggers a WARNING naming the branch. <!--#6e2f5c08634049e0-->
- `test_clean_report_emits_no_warning` (function) — Verifies a clean (empty) GC report produces no WARNING-level log records. <!--#173fa385598e99e4-->

### `tests/test_dag_scheduler.py` (python) — Unit tests for the DAG scheduler module, covering the GroupResult dataclass, graph construction/validation, parallel and dependency-ordered run() execution, execute_fn deps passing, failure propagation as skips, topological merge ordering, results ordering, and the relay-planning dataclasses/helpers. <!--#73d4613e8f52fa64|ddb09565c7235fcb-->

### `tests/test_dag_scheduler_status.py` (python) — Unit tests for the DAGScheduler's optional `on_group_status` lifecycle callback, verifying the correct ordered emission of per-group statuses (queued → running → completed/failed/skipped) for success, failure, and downstream-skip cases, and that the scheduler tolerates an absent or exception-raising callback. <!--#aab236ae60a4e7a5|880dc3b1d2bca17d-->
- `_completed` (function) — Helper that builds a GroupResult with status 'completed' for a given group id. <!--#41873e858830f33d-->
- `_Collector` (class) — Thread-safe callable test double that records (group_id, status) emissions in order for later assertions. <!--#ae385767a50dab48-->
  - `_Collector.__init__` (method) — Initializes the collector's lock and empty events list. <!--#4bebd83e05c532d5-->
  - `_Collector.__call__` (method) — Records a (group_id, status) emission under the lock when invoked as the status callback. <!--#3a497bd42468aa2c-->
  - `_Collector.statuses_for` (method) — Returns the ordered list of statuses recorded for a specific group id. <!--#5bacaefcb0c1be69-->
- `TestStatusEmission` (class) — Test group asserting the correct sequence and uniqueness of emitted status transitions for success, failure, and downstream-skip cases. <!--#1b5132450013bd4b-->
  - `TestStatusEmission.test_success_chain_queued_running_completed` (method) — Asserts a successful group emits queued → running → completed in order. <!--#c35caa842780c760-->
  - `TestStatusEmission.test_terminal_status_emitted_once_per_group` (method) — Asserts each lifecycle status is emitted exactly once per group. <!--#8d45c7a3fd6f25c2-->
  - `TestStatusEmission.test_failure_emits_failed_and_downstream_skipped` (method) — Asserts an upstream exception emits 'failed' and transitively skips downstream groups (queued → skipped). <!--#9f978d13064c1998-->
  - `TestStatusEmission.test_returned_failed_status_emits_failed` (method) — Asserts a returned GroupResult.failed() (no exception raised) still emits 'failed' and skips downstream. <!--#bd21e69b4115b468-->
- `TestCallbackRobustness` (class) — Test group verifying the scheduler tolerates an absent or exception-raising status callback. <!--#71a5196b52f6ee45-->
  - `TestCallbackRobustness.test_no_callback_is_default` (method) — Asserts omitting on_group_status preserves normal scheduling and results. <!--#3429da429c108f87-->
  - `TestCallbackRobustness.test_callback_exception_does_not_break_run` (method) — Asserts a callback that raises never disrupts scheduling or the returned results. <!--#c78c11e50cb830a5-->

### `tests/test_discovery_analyze_ws_delivery.py` (python) — End-to-end boundary regression suite for issue #260 that drives the real DaemonHistoryReader over a scripted on-disk engine.json/jsonl evolution mimicking the discovery→analyze transition — replaying the daemon's signature-gated push loop through the real server cache and /ws/ui fanout — to prove every disk append streams incrementally with no loss, duplication, or freeze, and to lock the fix where a same-(mtime,size) middle rewrite of a large active engine.json must yield a fresh parse and shift the active-flow signature. <!--#263de51657e9ab1d|d770d978f3bf56f5-->
- `_UiWS` (class) — A minimal UI-WebSocket stand-in that records every decoded frame sent to it and can filter captured `history_data` frames by flow id. <!--#7ad41ce10c30c033-->
  - `_UiWS.__init__` (method) — Initializes the stub's `sent` list that accumulates received frames. <!--#d14bbb740fc91394-->
  - `_UiWS.send_text` (method) — Async send hook that JSON-decodes each outgoing text frame and appends it to the capture list. <!--#015e8192c9e42ee8-->
  - `_UiWS.history_frames` (method) — Returns the captured `history_data` frames, optionally narrowed to a single flow id. <!--#bf1df282dc320385-->
- `_write_engine` (function) — Test helper that writes a realistic `engine.json` with a given status, steps table, and current step index for a flow. <!--#33a1ccb4f132c580-->
- `_hist` (function) — Returns the on-disk history directory path for a given flow id under the test root. <!--#315a508136847fa4-->
- `_write_jsonl` (function) — Writes a list of records as a fresh JSONL file, creating parent directories. <!--#4f3e9d9b8f5030ea-->
- `_append_jsonl` (function) — Appends a list of records as JSONL lines to an existing file. <!--#50fd55bc5ca4ef54-->
- `_chat` (function) — Builds a chat-message record dict with role, content, and timestamp. <!--#653f232ec7903ab1-->
- `_started` (function) — Builds a `step_started` record dict for the given step id and type. <!--#ebbba86f08b85fb3-->
- `_completed` (function) — Builds a `step_completed` record dict wrapping the finished step's data. <!--#7aa09ab2396593b4-->
- `_boundary_mutations` (function) — Returns an ordered list of mutation callables that replay the discovery→analyze boundary (empty-steps discovery, pause/resume, first steps-table write with PAUSED→RUNNING flip, new analyze jsonl, and mid-step appends), each returning the labels it wrote. <!--#eccdc279506015fb-->
- `_normal_step_mutations` (function) — Returns a control sequence of mutation callables for an ordinary analyze→plan boundary (steps table already present, index simply increments) to guard against regression. <!--#2315f8ce06d69b90-->
- `_GatedBoundaryDriver` (class) — A test driver that reproduces `DaemonClient`'s per-tick push loop — computing the active-flow signature debounce gate and reading+broadcasting deltas through the real reader, server cache, and `/ws/ui` fanout. <!--#cc8f703904eac054-->
  - `_GatedBoundaryDriver.__init__` (method) — Wires up the driver's real reader, server state, UI hub, stub WebSocket, request registry, and per-tick signature/cursor tracking maps. <!--#21228bf34e67c0de-->
  - `_GatedBoundaryDriver.setup` (method) — Registers the test machine with the server state and subscribes the stub UI WebSocket to the hub under the owner id. <!--#23c02f78d7a08db2-->
  - `_GatedBoundaryDriver.tick` (method) — Runs one push-loop tick: debounces when the active-flow signature is unchanged, else reads active-flow deltas, rebuilds cursors (retaining live terminal flows), and broadcasts each increment via the real message handler. <!--#c6ccf804ffd74a5f-->
  - `_GatedBoundaryDriver.ui_bodies` (method) — Returns, in order, every conversation content body that actually reached the live UI for a given flow. <!--#28ea0806d4a04a3f-->

- `test_boundary_each_disk_append_delivered_via_gated_push` (function) — Core #260 test asserting every disk append across the discovery→analyze boundary is delivered incrementally over the live `/ws/ui` stream with no mid-stream full reload. <!--#cf448f6af31fc189-->
- `test_boundary_streamed_records_equal_full_snapshot_no_loss_no_dup` (function) — Asserts that concatenating all broadcast frames exactly equals the authoritative full snapshot across the boundary — nothing lost and nothing duplicated. <!--#49681e4f97b44c27-->
- `test_normal_step_boundary_not_regressed` (function) — Control test locking that an ordinary analyze→plan boundary still streams every append through the same gated harness. <!--#d167405e6fe0004b-->
- `_build_large_engine` (function) — Constructs a >128 KiB `engine.json` whose only varying bytes are a marker buried in the true middle of the steps table, outside the head+tail verify windows. <!--#6d883d0aa6eb1d04-->
- `test_active_engine_json_middle_rewrite_returns_fresh_parse` (function) — Locks the #260 primary fix: a same-(mtime,size) rewrite differing only in the file's middle must return the fresh parse rather than the stale cached one. <!--#51dc102375135d56-->
- `test_active_flow_signature_moves_on_engine_middle_rewrite` (function) — A regression test asserting that `DaemonHistoryReader.active_flow_signature` folds in the engine.json whole-content digest so a same-(mtime,size) middle-only rewrite still shifts the signature, closing the frame-delay where an engine-only PAUSE→resume tick used to be debounced by the old raw-stat-only signature. <!--#9db6da4b51febc2a-->
- `_build_large_worktree_engine` (function) — Like `_build_large_engine` but produces a `--worktree`-mode `engine.json` with worktree tail keys trailing the giant steps table. <!--#f6625d89c059e4bd-->
- `test_worktree_engine_middle_rewrite_fresh_and_tail_keys_preserved` (function) — Worktree non-regression test verifying the whole-content freshness hash catches a middle rewrite while still surfacing the worktree tail keys on the live read. <!--#9573777a0b903b45-->

### `tests/test_discovery_interactive_pause.py` (python) — Test module exercising the interactive discovery-pause dual-path wait in se3.commands.run, verifying that terminal question/confirm pauses mirror themselves to se3/calls/ call files answerable from the web console, that whichever of the terminal or web response answers first drives the same live process forward while keeping the flow RUNNING (or persists PAUSED on cancel) with correct file cleanup, and that the DaemonAggregator deduplicates multiple call files per (flow, step). <!--#cd0fc3903ca5a6ea|fd2424055c942019-->

- `test_interactive_confirm_pause_writes_discovery_confirm_call` (function) — Verifies that the interactive discovery confirmation gate writes a `discovery_confirm` call file (with the refined description, a single one-click option value '1', and flow/step context), marks the step confirmed when the user types '1', and removes the call file afterwards. <!--#4f2d3fd0acaee306-->

- `test_cancel_saves_flow_and_cleans_up_call` (function) — Verifies that a Ctrl+C/EOF cancel (no terminal or web answer) persists the PAUSED flow and removes the mirrored call file. <!--#ab3a3a4b1e1fc71d-->

- `test_dedup_keeps_newest_call_per_step` (function) — Verifies DaemonAggregator._dedup_calls_by_step collapses multiple unanswered calls for one (flow, step) to the one with the highest created_at. <!--#73fa923f30bbeaab-->
- `test_dedup_independent_steps_are_all_kept` (function) — Verifies dedup never collapses calls belonging to different (flow, step) keys. <!--#688e34438efdd66f-->

### `tests/test_disk_json_cache.py` (python) — Unit tests for the unified daemon disk-JSON parse cache (#243/#260/#209), asserting via json.loads-seam counting that unchanged files parse at most once across many ticks, real changes (including same-(mtime,size) mid-file rewrites and size/mtime-preserving flow swaps) trigger exactly one re-parse, active engine.json is content-hashed but never re-parsed while unchanged, and oversized files are never full-parsed but have their header keys recovered by a bounded degraded head+tail read with warn-once on failure and no cache pollution. <!--#2fd7be6d04fbc98d|61a0cdd424f5e251-->
- `_clean_cache` (function) — Autouse pytest fixture that clears the module-level parse cache and warn-once set before and after each test. <!--#f901622b842eabe8-->
- `_count_parses` (function) — Test helper that monkeypatches `_parse_json` to count full-file JSON parses and returns the counter dict. <!--#1aa04823ea8aa141-->
- `_engine_json` (function) — Test helper building an indent=2 engine.json string with the real head/state/tail key ordering emitted by FlowInstance.to_dict, to exercise the degraded head+tail scan. <!--#f5d9ce7bafcb4cb8-->
- `test_unchanged_file_parsed_once_across_many_calls` (function) — Asserts an unchanged file is parsed exactly once despite 21 cached reads returning identical results. <!--#9c8b30dc3d49a80e-->
- `test_reparsed_after_content_change` (function) — Asserts a genuine rewrite (new mtime/size) triggers exactly one re-parse and no further parses while unchanged. <!--#0baac5a282dd8071-->
- `_count_file_parses` (function) — Test helper that monkeypatches `_parse_json_file` to count whole-file read+parse calls, which the active path must not repeat for an unchanged file. <!--#09e6098abfd6d331-->
- `test_active_unchanged_not_reparsed` (function) — Asserts that an unchanged active engine.json (verify_content=True) is re-read and re-hashed each poll but never re-parsed via json.loads, keeping the #260 fix off the #209 parse sink. <!--#e1d556ae4aa00395-->
- `test_active_large_underguard_parsed_once_but_middle_rewrite_caught` (function) — Verifies the #260 core trade on a ~1 MiB under-guard file: unchanged polls parse zero times, yet a same-(mtime,size) rewrite buried in the middle state block is still detected (exactly one re-parse) because the hash covers the whole file rather than the old head+tail window. <!--#b7728239acf811ba-->
- `test_active_same_size_same_mtime_swap_detected` (function) — Confirms a completed→new-flow swap that preserves both size and mtime is still caught by the whole-content hash, so the daemon never reports the stale superseded flow. <!--#a400ea85df1facb5-->
- `test_active_underguard_midfile_change_is_reparsed` (function) — Checks that an under-guard file changed only in its middle state block is reparsed via the advanced (mtime,size) stat key (mtime forced forward here), complementing the same-(mtime,size) middle case locked by the large-underguard test. <!--#e144a28927c00842-->
- `test_active_reparses_after_real_change` (function) — Asserts a genuine rewrite (new mtime/size) is re-parsed in active verify_content mode. <!--#fa9c3d5f5408bbd3-->
- `test_parse_failure_returns_none_and_is_not_reparsed` (function) — Asserts invalid JSON returns None once and a corrupt-but-unchanged file is not re-parsed on every tick. <!--#132f471a7699d925-->
- `test_missing_file_returns_none` (function) — Asserts both read_json_cached and read_engine_header return None for a nonexistent file. <!--#8e3d262c0603c9f1-->
- `test_small_engine_header_uses_full_cached_parse` (function) — Asserts an under-threshold engine.json header is served via a single cached full parse routed through `_parse_json`. <!--#73ffc9bb08f0a1eb-->
- `_write_oversized` (function) — Test helper writing a well-formed engine.json larger than SIZE_GUARD_BYTES with a padding blob in `state` so the degraded head+tail read must straddle it. <!--#d32b4ea46b5a0049-->
- `test_oversized_file_never_full_parsed_but_header_extracted` (function) — Asserts an oversized file is never full-parsed yet its head- and tail-cluster header keys (including is_worktree_mode) are extracted, with no cache pollution. <!--#179d3f23062ee673-->
- `test_oversized_extraction_failure_warns_once` (function) — Asserts an oversized file with no recoverable flow_id returns None, warns exactly once across repeated ticks, is never full-parsed, and leaves the cache empty. <!--#054d26d6a0d68d44-->

### `tests/test_docs_updater.py` (python) — Boundary/unit test suite for DocumentationUpdater covering VERSIONS.md entry insertion and same-version merging (empty file, no title, duplicate/prefix-collision, custom and file-fallback templates), README badge placement around front-matter, independent update_both error handling, and Template placeholder rendering. <!--#a0a878c845614342|ab3d6cccb6811daa-->
- `TestEmptyVersionsFile` (class) — Tests that an empty VERSIONS.md file correctly receives a freshly inserted version entry. <!--#8d74e2522a708f58-->
  - `TestEmptyVersionsFile.test_empty_file_gets_entry` (method) — Asserts that updating an empty VERSIONS.md (with the default entry template forced) inserts the version heading and change bullet. <!--#5020936fc130a710-->
- `TestVersionsWithoutTitle` (class) — Tests insertion behavior when VERSIONS.md lacks a `# Version History` title. <!--#65faa944a931adf3-->

- `TestDuplicateVersionMerge` (class) — Test class verifying DocumentationUpdater.update_versions_md merges new changelog entries into an already-present version block instead of duplicating headers, across suffixed, suffixless, custom-template, and prefix-collision cases. <!--#fd63daa3003f5243-->
  - `TestDuplicateVersionMerge.test_existing_version_header_not_duplicated` (method) — Asserts a distinct entry for an already-present version is merged into the single existing header rather than swallowed or duplicated. <!--#f42302829edd3cc2-->
  - `TestDuplicateVersionMerge.test_verbatim_rewrite_is_noop` (method) — Asserts re-writing an identical bullet for an existing version is idempotent and adds no duplicate line. <!--#f2b84cd194c77196-->
  - `TestDuplicateVersionMerge.test_suffixless_custom_template_header_is_merged` (method) — Asserts a second update merges into a suffixless `## {{version}}` custom-template header instead of inserting a duplicate. <!--#ae1c1e6692b55fab-->
  - `TestDuplicateVersionMerge.test_suffixless_header_merged_under_default_template` (method) — Asserts a bare `## 1.2.3` header (no date tail) is recognised and merged into even when the effective template is the default suffixed one. <!--#fa0d7dcbaecf332c-->
  - `TestDuplicateVersionMerge.test_prefix_version_not_matched_as_duplicate` (method) — Anti-prefix guard asserting version `11.13` creates a new header rather than being mis-merged into an existing `## 11.13.1` block. <!--#2725e50e69f420d1-->
- `TestReadmeFrontMatter` (class) — Tests README badge placement across leading YAML front-matter, HTML-comment headers, and heading-less files. <!--#e6d2aabc8dfe9f3c-->
  - `TestReadmeFrontMatter.test_badge_inserted_after_heading_not_breaking_front_matter` (method) — Asserts the version badge is placed after the heading and after intact YAML front-matter, before body content. <!--#b70585e97cb48ccb-->
  - `TestReadmeFrontMatter.test_html_comment_header_is_skipped` (method) — Asserts a leading HTML comment is preserved and the badge is inserted after the heading that follows it. <!--#f4b31a0ea0bef416-->
  - `TestReadmeFrontMatter.test_no_heading_prepends_badge` (method) — Asserts the badge is prepended to the file when README.md has no heading at all. <!--#f04486d700104338-->
- `TestConfigCustomEntryTemplate` (class) — Test class verifying DocumentationUpdater honors a configured `versions_entry_template`, rendering with it and still detecting/merging same-version entries for non-heading templates. <!--#4967db2072cf4c36-->
  - `TestConfigCustomEntryTemplate.test_custom_entry_template_used` (method) — Asserts the custom entry template is stored and renders the version and changes into VERSIONS.md as configured. <!--#2a384d33f0504f57-->
  - `TestConfigCustomEntryTemplate.test_non_heading_template_merges_same_version` (method) — Asserts a non-heading custom entry template still merges repeated same-version updates, stays idempotent on identical rewrites, and keeps different versions as distinct entries. <!--#4a82cb66ebc5caf8-->
- `TestVersionsTemplateFileFallback` (class) — Tests fallback selection of the versions_entry template from the packaged versions_md.md file versus config and the built-in default. <!--#4098f347e903b010-->
  - `TestVersionsTemplateFileFallback.test_fallback_reads_first_section_block` (method) — Asserts a placeholder-bearing first `##` block in versions_md.md is adopted as the entry template and substitutes real version/changes. <!--#446edf1e64c44ef4-->
  - `TestVersionsTemplateFileFallback.test_concrete_first_block_rejected_falls_back_to_default` (method) — Asserts a concrete (non-placeholder) first block is rejected, falling back to the DEFAULT template so the real version/changes are written. <!--#d8000cb90e87b9d2-->
  - `TestVersionsTemplateFileFallback.test_fallback_to_default_when_file_absent` (method) — Asserts that a missing versions_md.md yields None from the file helper and the updater uses the built-in DEFAULT entry template. <!--#e8346f1eeda91920-->
  - `TestVersionsTemplateFileFallback.test_config_template_wins_over_file` (method) — Asserts a config-supplied entry template takes precedence over the versions_md.md file template. <!--#872e4fe24c10ef6b-->
- `TestUpdateBothIndependentErrors` (class) — Tests that update_both handles README and VERSIONS failures independently. <!--#226389aca3d08c7a-->

  - `TestUpdateBothIndependentErrors.test_both_sides_succeed` (method) — Asserts update_both returns True for both when valid README.md and VERSIONS.md exist. <!--#8ca38bff64dd47d8-->
- `TestTemplateRendering` (class) — Unit tests for the Template placeholder-substitution rendering behavior. <!--#30867f09179f990a-->

### `tests/test_end_session_cmd.py` (python) — Test suite for the `end-session` command, verifying that worktree and main-branch sessions are correctly archived (state promotion, history sync, snapshot clearing, branch/worktree cleanup), that live `se3 run` processes are discovered and terminated (SIGTERM/SIGKILL escalation, process-tree kills, pidfile/descendant-cwd discovery), and that error and mismatch cases skip destructive cleanup while exiting non-zero. <!--#0a7beb2a19d289cb|74818f5d65e9a38d-->
- `_init_repo` (function) — Helper that initializes a git repo at the given path with a configured user and an initial committed README. <!--#1635ad85954c81ae-->
- `_branch_exists` (function) — Helper that returns whether a given git branch exists in the repo via `git rev-parse --verify`. <!--#fe856a428f75db97-->
- `_write_fake_se3` (function) — Test helper that writes an executable `se3` shebang script running a given body, so spawning it makes psutil observe the real console-script `[interpreter, /path/se3, run, ...]` argv shape that the tightened `_cmdline_is_se3_run` predicate matches. <!--#314d535317f2db8b-->
- `_make_worktree_session` (function) — Helper that builds a real git worktree session with engine.json, a resumable snapshot, and a history file for use as test fixtures. <!--#045b7a74f370c155-->
- `_make_main_session` (function) — Helper that creates a main-branch (non-worktree) session by writing engine.json and a resumable snapshot under main/se3/state. <!--#7db44937b4a1cbc4-->
- `test_worktree_session_is_archived` (function) — Verifies a worktree session is fully archived: worktree dir archived, terminal state promoted with project_root stamped, history synced to main, and branch/worktree cleaned up. <!--#2156c0f536fdc296-->
- `test_worktree_session_history_collision_uses_sidecar` (function) — Verifies that when a worktree history file collides with an existing main history file, the original is preserved and the copy lands as a `.from-<branch>` sidecar. <!--#cad015fac8b425c9-->
- `test_main_branch_session_is_archived` (function) — Verifies a main-branch session is archived: engine.json moved into archive/ and the resumable snapshot cleared. <!--#f519675a65ef9f1d-->
- `test_flow_id_resolved_from_main_engine` (function) — Verifies that when flow_id is omitted, end-session reads it from the main engine.json and archives that session. <!--#03c5521b1b361121-->
- `test_terminate_by_pid_sigterm` (function) — Verifies that end-session with `--pid` terminates a live long-running child process via SIGTERM. <!--#03b178844d9667b7-->
- `test_terminate_sigkill_escalation` (function) — Verifies that a process ignoring SIGTERM is escalated to SIGKILL after the grace period. <!--#7b9aee7aa64c72ad-->
- `test_terminate_kills_child_subprocess` (function) — Verifies that ending a session kills the whole process tree, not just the parent, so agent/test child subprocesses are not orphaned. <!--#08581e7e7cf1d8e7-->
- `test_worktree_without_branch_is_still_cleaned_up` (function) — Verifies a worktree session whose engine.json lacks worktree_branch is still cleaned up by inferring the branch from git's worktree metadata. <!--#a21bbb579ae81065-->
- `test_stale_unregistered_worktree_dir_is_removed` (function) — Verifies a stale, unregistered worktree dir with no branch is archived and fully removed via the remove-by-path fallback. <!--#1ab8ec7b239a80af-->
- `test_discovers_live_worktree_parent_by_descendant_cwd` (function) — Verifies that a live `se3 run --worktree` parent (which keeps cwd at main_root) is discovered for its flow via a descendant agent subprocess whose cwd is inside the worktree path. <!--#602105da0154f4de-->
- `test_discovers_live_worktree_parent_via_pidfile` (function) — Verifies that a live `se3 run --worktree` parent with no worktree-resident descendant is still discovered through the pid recorded in the worktree's `run.pid` marker, so the worktree isn't archived under a still-live process. <!--#7d8697af7cf82b1b-->
- `test_stale_pidfile_is_ignored` (function) — Verifies a `run.pid` pointing at a dead pid is not reported as a live process by discovery. <!--#a7650edbddf5d986-->
- `test_no_live_process_still_archives` (function) — Verifies a PAUSED worktree with no live process is still archived cleanly and its branch removed. <!--#840509fe5b1a1647-->
- `test_unkillable_process_skips_destructive_archive` (function) — Verifies that if the target process cannot be killed, the destructive archive is skipped, the worktree/branch survive, and the command exits non-zero. <!--#8689e85dd9589d5e-->
- `test_missing_worktree_degrades_to_main_archive` (function) — Verifies that with no worktree found, end-session falls back to the main-branch archival path without error. <!--#04b51133a080e5f7-->
- `test_mismatched_main_flow_is_not_archived` (function) — Verifies that ending flow A does not archive an unrelated active flow B whose engine.json occupies the main project. <!--#16bb8115fc54e639-->
- `test_unreadable_main_flow_is_not_archived` (function) — Verifies that when the main engine.json carries no readable flow_id, the destructive clear is skipped to avoid ending the wrong session. <!--#8ff6e340ec7f42a9-->
- `test_archive_failure_preserves_worktree_and_branch` (function) — Verifies that a failed worktree-archive step skips destructive cleanup, preserving the branch and worktree, and exits non-zero. <!--#64a8e5845d594a8e-->
- `test_step_failure_does_not_abort_and_exit_nonzero` (function) — Verifies that a raising sub-step (e.g. promotion) is recorded and exits non-zero but does not abort later cleanup steps. <!--#11541efbd2e030bb-->
- `test_unresolvable_root_returns_one` (function) — Verifies that an unresolvable project root causes end_session to return exit code 1. <!--#a6b850b8cf6bf46e-->

- `test_app_js_end_flow_handles_all_receipts` (function) — Verifies the endFlow function POSTs to /end, branches on 404/409/503 responses, and debounces via endSessionRequests. <!--#5a6dca2a7fb3ab57-->
- `test_index_html_has_end_session_modal` (function) — Confirms index.html contains the end-session confirmation modal's elements and that the modal defaults to hidden. <!--#c1821487f8bd258d-->

### `tests/test_end_session_protocol_daemon.py` (python) — Unit tests for the END_SESSION control-plane path (feature group G2), covering the daemon protocol's MSG_END_SESSION registration/make_end_session round-trip, the spawner's end-session argv assembly, the daemon's request_end_session flow lookup with worktree-to-main folding and error cases, and the DaemonClient's END_SESSION dispatch/routing including empty-flow ignore, project_root reverse-resolution, and handler-exception containment. <!--#a5df225af2a7f2f5|0f7ee9ebf8749172-->
- `test_msg_end_session_is_server_to_daemon` (function) — Asserts MSG_END_SESSION has the right name and is registered as a server→daemon message in the correct protocol sets. <!--#576fc568a0cafaa3-->
- `test_protocol_version_current` (function) — Pins the daemon protocol's PROTOCOL_VERSION constant to the current value "3", guarding against unintended version drift after the END_SESSION and traffic-reduction message additions. <!--#f4323a76965a9c2b-->
- `test_make_end_session_roundtrip` (function) — Checks a fully-populated make_end_session message survives a JSON encode/decode round-trip with all fields intact. <!--#d371965e5bb78e55-->
- `test_make_end_session_omits_empty_optionals` (function) — Verifies empty optional fields (project_root, reason) are dropped from the wire payload while a defaulted reason is kept. <!--#a68acc0ddbb54efa-->
- `_capturing_spawner` (function) — Test helper that builds a DaemonSpawner whose _launch is patched to capture argv/cwd/label instead of spawning a subprocess. <!--#ea42f4def5dd3040-->
- `test_end_session_builds_argv` (function) — Asserts spawner.end_session assembles the expected `se3 end-session <flow_id> -p ... --pid ...` argv and task label. <!--#be8e5197fb7efd8d-->
- `test_end_session_omits_pid_when_none` (function) — Verifies the --pid flag is omitted from the argv when no pid is supplied. <!--#305ab835fde3e1b6-->
- `test_end_session_uses_resolved_se3_command` (function) — Confirms the argv prefix comes from _resolve_se3_command() rather than a hardcoded 'se3' literal. <!--#6daf8a8de0efb5a5-->
- `_StubSpawner` (class) — Test double standing in for the spawner that records end_session calls without launching a real subprocess. <!--#60e232d13b47e345-->
  - `_StubSpawner.__init__` (method) — Initializes the stub spawner's empty calls-recording list. <!--#052d7032db4d16d0-->
  - `_StubSpawner.end_session` (method) — Records each (flow_id, project_root, pid) invocation and returns a placeholder object. <!--#c4b856cbe3382914-->
- `test_request_end_session_locates_flow_and_spawns` (function) — Verifies request_end_session looks up a supervised flow and dispatches end_session with its resolved root and pid. <!--#ae5e672bfab5d383-->
- `test_request_end_session_prefers_supplied_root` (function) — Asserts a server-supplied project_root overrides the supervisor's registered root. <!--#a1a318767822f163-->
- `test_request_end_session_folds_worktree_root_to_main` (function) — Verifies a worktree project_root is normalized back to its main repo root (with no pid) so end-session runs against main. <!--#8a99d1cd086e92de-->
- `test_request_end_session_unknown_flow_raises` (function) — Asserts request_end_session raises ValueError and never spawns when the flow is unknown and no root is given. <!--#5aab9260ef552cbe-->
- `test_request_end_session_unsupervised_flow_with_root_dispatches` (function) — Verifies a dangling (non-live) flow still dispatches end_session—with no pid hint—when the server supplies a root. <!--#d45b06b0ec1eea3e-->
- `test_request_end_session_empty_flow_raises` (function) — Asserts request_end_session raises ValueError on an empty flow_id. <!--#ddca5db47319cda1-->
- `_make_client` (function) — Test helper that constructs a DaemonClient with default identity/snapshot args and overridable handlers. <!--#2166366244481ca6-->
- `test_dispatch_end_session_routes_to_handler` (function) — Verifies the client's async _dispatch routes a decoded END_SESSION message to the configured handler with flow/root/reason. <!--#497088df98906f11-->

- `test_handle_end_session_resolves_root_from_index` (function) — Verifies that when project_root is missing, _handle_end_session reverse-resolves it from the history provider's index and forwards it (with the default reason) to the handler. <!--#522ca82a96c92415-->
- `test_handle_end_session_without_handler_is_noop` (function) — Verifies _handle_end_session is a safe no-op that raises nothing when no end_session_handler is configured on the client. <!--#e293a7271a63eea8-->
- `test_handle_end_session_swallows_handler_exception` (function) — Verifies _handle_end_session catches and logs a handler exception so the daemon connection survives rather than propagating the error. <!--#0e4f5e8e51f73015-->

### `tests/test_end_session_server.py` (python) — Test suite for the POST /api/flows/{id}/end REST endpoint, verifying its honest-receipt branches — 404 (unknown/cross-owner), 409 (already completed), 503 (daemon disconnected), and 202 (dispatched) — and that the 202 path dispatches MSG_END_SESSION carrying the flow's project_root and reason, including default-reason and dangling-worktree cases. <!--#e949ea8183164e3e|a9e6f953651aedd3-->

- `_report_flow` (function) — Helper that sends HELLO + STATUS_UPDATE over a websocket for one flow and polls until the server reports it visible. <!--#a9a61c0de5fcb9f9-->
- `test_end_flow_unknown_returns_404` (function) — Asserts ending an unknown flow_id returns 404 and leaks nothing. <!--#75e7bb681254ccf1-->
- `test_end_flow_cross_owner_returns_404` (function) — Asserts a flow owned by another owner reads as absent (404) and is never controllable across owners, while its own owner can end it (202). <!--#8f309a624caf502a-->

- `test_end_flow_completed_worktree_dispatches` (function) — Asserts a COMPLETED but dangling worktree session stays endable (202 + MSG_END_SESSION) so the orphaned worktree can be archived. <!--#05337129c169e521-->
- `test_end_flow_daemon_disconnected_returns_503` (function) — Asserts a still-visible flow whose owning daemon has disconnected returns 503. <!--#b4b7567524e79b33-->
- `test_end_flow_dispatches_end_session` (function) — Asserts a non-completed flow on a connected daemon returns 202 and dispatches MSG_END_SESSION carrying the flow's project_root and reason. <!--#983a70d31a7aeb91-->
- `test_end_flow_default_reason_when_body_omitted` (function) — Asserts omitting the request body still dispatches MSG_END_SESSION with the default reason 'user terminated'. <!--#c03b08bb5443a02d-->

### `tests/test_engine_hot_cold_split.py` (python) — Write-path test suite for the engine.json hot/cold split (issue #244/G5), verifying that the persisted header stays KB-scale and hotcold-formatted, that each save rewrites only the cold files whose step or context content actually changed, that resumable snapshots share the cold partition without bloating with payload size, and that content-hash keying plus save/load round-trips preserve payloads correctly. <!--#ef85b3f906c1f511|ec32135b80eb06ea-->
- `pm` (function) — Pytest fixture returning a PersistenceManager rooted at a temporary directory. <!--#2f092c27109e7260-->
- `_big_step` (function) — Helper that builds a single completed Step whose inputs and outputs each carry a ~payload_kb KiB blob. <!--#4af4ea8b472836c5-->
- `_flow_with_steps` (function) — Helper that constructs a RUNNING FlowInstance with n_steps heavy steps and a large shared context for exercising the hot/cold split. <!--#d3a569982b3199c1-->
- `_WriteSpy` (class) — Test double that monkeypatches PersistenceManager._atomic_write_json to record the basenames of every file a persist touched, enabling write-amplification assertions. <!--#f12c27015d2c69dc-->
  - `_WriteSpy.__init__` (method) — Installs the monkeypatch that wraps _atomic_write_json to log each written path's name while delegating to the original. <!--#72eb0ef7a5b20b5f-->
  - `_WriteSpy.reset` (method) — Clears the recorded list of written filenames between assertions. <!--#5c2e6bd0ec5341f4-->
  - `_WriteSpy.written` (method) — Property exposing the recorded write names as a set for membership assertions. <!--#1883677d8dbeefab-->
- `test_header_is_hotcold_format` (function) — Asserts a saved flow's header uses the hotcold/1 format with per-step cold_ref entries and an externalized context_ref rather than inlined payloads. <!--#1dfd5f0522557b4b-->
- `test_header_under_100kb_with_large_payloads` (function) — Verifies the header stays under 100 KB even when steps and context hold >800 KiB of cold data actually written to the cold directory. <!--#ee30f497d507ad7d-->
- `test_header_size_independent_of_step_count` (function) — Confirms header size scales only with the small per-step status table, staying under budget regardless of step count or payload size. <!--#d790e4f3e1a53fb6-->
- `test_first_save_writes_all_cold_files` (function) — Checks that the initial save writes the engine.json header plus every step's cold file and the context cold file. <!--#f54b660fd5bc9e0a-->
- `test_single_step_change_touches_only_that_cold_file` (function) — Verifies that changing one step re-writes only that step's cold file (plus the two headers), leaving other steps' and the context's cold files untouched. <!--#ce372093e6d5db2a-->
- `test_no_change_rewrites_only_headers` (function) — Ensures an unchanged re-save rewrites only the headers, touching no step or context cold files. <!--#b10809e1c3103bbe-->
- `test_context_change_touches_only_context_cold_file` (function) — Verifies mutating the shared context re-writes only the context cold file and no step cold files. <!--#3d69805973857fff-->
- `test_resumable_snapshot_is_split_and_small` (function) — Asserts the resumable snapshot is itself a hotcold-format header under 100 KB rather than a copy of the megabytes of payload. <!--#5b25a304d7378db1-->
- `test_resumable_snapshot_shares_cold_partition` (function) — Confirms the snapshot reuses the single steps/<flow_id>/ cold partition, writing each cold file exactly once instead of duplicating it. <!--#d59f239fa81cd8d3-->
- `test_resumable_snapshot_does_not_grow_with_payload` (function) — Verifies the in-flight snapshot header size tracks the header, not the payload, staying nearly constant across a 200×-larger payload. <!--#a1cbf853ae1278ef-->
- `test_roundtrip_preserves_payloads_and_context` (function) — Round-trips a flow through save/load and asserts status, context, per-step inputs/outputs, and artifacts are preserved. <!--#6b102bce68cb965b-->
- `test_content_hash_is_key_order_independent` (function) — Asserts _canonical_json and _content_hash ignore dict key ordering so unchanged steps are not spuriously re-flagged dirty. <!--#d0769590066c4dd9-->
- `test_content_hash_is_stable_across_repeated_serialization` (function) — Verifies hashing the same payload twice yields an identical digest, proving no hidden serialization state. <!--#b69b5a15a4fb7df2-->
- `test_content_hash_coerces_non_json_native_like_the_writer` (function) — Confirms _content_hash uses default=str like the writer so Path values hash the same as their string forms. <!--#cec5c5b85b0be74d-->
- `test_deleted_cold_file_is_rewritten_on_next_save` (function) — Verifies that a hash-matching step whose cold file was deleted is regenerated on the next save via an on-disk existence check and reloads correctly. <!--#bf3cc10cad8be7d1-->
- `test_resumable_roundtrip` (function) — Round-trips a flow through the resumable snapshot and asserts per-step outputs are restored. <!--#a9eac16ef5dd41d5-->
