### `tests/test_history_head_truncation_interlock.py` (python) — Regression test module that reproduces the confirmed #287 head-truncation chain end-to-end over the real `DaemonHistoryReader` plus `ServerState` (empty `full` frame, a lost frame whose cursor was wrongly committed, then a late `append`), with jsonl-flush/state helpers, asserting the empty bundle is never installed, the truncating append is refused, and the recovery pull restores the complete history. <!--#0c2061d90e8e523b|cab2113bc492e430-->
- `_flush` (function) — Test helper that appends `count` synthetic jsonl discovery-step records (starting at ordinal `start`) to the flow's history file under `<root>/se3/history/<FLOW>/`, simulating a live flush to disk. <!--#f2d6e6bbd2c2e83f-->
- `_mark_active_worktree_flow` (function) — Test helper that registers the flow with `ServerState` as a running flow rooted at the given worktree path, so the server treats it as an active worktree flow (the condition that scopes the empty-full guard). <!--#bdcb4644b1910410-->
- `_apply` (function) — Test helper that feeds a `DaemonHistoryReader` read result into `ServerState.apply_history_frame` as if it had arrived over the wire from the daemon. <!--#1a31ee67fae1a1fb-->
- `_ordinals` (function) — Test helper that extracts the list of record ordinals currently held in `ServerState`'s cached history bundle for the flow, returning `[]` when no bundle exists. <!--#5270d67182955825-->
- `test_lost_frame_then_empty_full_still_yields_complete_history` (function) — End-to-end regression test driving the real daemon reader plus server state through the confirmed #287 trigger chain (empty `full` frame, then a lost frame whose cursor was wrongly committed, then a late `append`), asserting the empty bundle is never installed, the head-truncating append is refused, the recovery pull self-heals, and the full history survives. <!--#a6d4afc5612db181-->

### `tests/test_history_sink_step_started.py` (python) — Unit/integration test suite for the step_started/step_status event-chain that persists lightweight running/paused anchor lines into per-step history jsonl, verifying record_step_started/record_step_status writers, has_step_started/status_event detection, get_step_history's skipping of these non-chat anchors, and HistorySink plus full run_flow behavior around idempotent, re-armed-after-pause, terminal-suppressed, and deduped lifecycle anchors for non-LLM steps. <!--#c6ba6c1a38b12cc6|b17f0c81b9dfe564-->
- `_step_path` (function) — Helper that builds the per-step jsonl path (se3/history/<flow>/<step>.jsonl) under a project root. <!--#957e6c7aeb46a4cb-->
- `_read_lines` (function) — Helper that reads a jsonl file and returns its non-blank lines parsed as a list of dicts (empty list if absent). <!--#3a7c0ef3252423a1-->
- `test_record_step_started_writes_running_record` (function) — Asserts record_step_started writes a single well-shaped step_started/running record with an ISO timestamp and no chat role field. <!--#725de4ed5b9c57f3-->
- `test_record_step_started_default_timestamp_is_iso_string` (function) — Asserts that record_step_started defaults the timestamp to a non-empty ISO string when none is supplied. <!--#d13f94ced1b36b69-->
- `test_has_step_started_event_detection` (function) — Asserts has_step_started_event returns False for absent/other steps and True only once a step's started anchor exists. <!--#0483c6793b34831d-->
- `test_get_step_history_skips_step_started` (function) — Asserts get_step_history ignores step_started lines, returning None for a started-only file and only real chat messages otherwise. <!--#b9613bca7665992f-->
- `_make_event` (function) — Helper that constructs an engine event of a given type with default flow/step/step_type fields for HistorySink tests. <!--#adcce4c55ea8b382-->
- `test_history_sink_persists_step_started` (function) — Asserts HistorySink.consume of a STEP_STARTED event persists one step_started/running anchor to the step jsonl. <!--#acb6143c8b556d43-->
- `test_history_sink_step_started_is_idempotent_while_running` (function) — Asserts repeated STEP_STARTED events while already running do not stack duplicate started anchors. <!--#43e42e3033c96e6f-->
- `test_history_sink_step_started_rearms_after_pause` (function) — Asserts a resumed (previously paused) step re-arms a fresh running anchor while still not stacking subsequent running events. <!--#f879bf7525c82bfb-->
- `test_history_sink_step_started_skipped_after_terminal` (function) — Asserts a late STEP_STARTED arriving after a terminal step_completed is a no-op, never adding a running anchor to a finished step. <!--#114a85102fdb9ceb-->
- `test_history_sink_terminal_events_unchanged` (function) — Regression guard asserting STEP_COMPLETED/STEP_FAILED/STEP_OUTPUT still persist their full step record unchanged. <!--#a3e7005ad019090b-->
- `_build_flow` (function) — Helper that constructs a single-step RUNNING FlowInstance of a given step type for run_flow integration tests. <!--#21d5b5b1ef5abf2a-->
- `_run_single_step` (function) — Test helper that drives `run_flow` with mocked PersistenceManager and StateMachine (whose `run_step` invokes the `on_running` callback to emit STEP_STARTED before returning a supplied StepStatus) so tests can exercise the orchestrator's callback-driven step_started persistence for a single completed step. <!--#2501cdf272e9dfbc-->
- `test_run_flow_emits_step_started_for_non_llm_step` (function) — Asserts a non-LLM TEST step gets one running step_started anchor at entry alongside its terminal step_completed through the full run_flow chain. <!--#eea698beb03f259d-->
- `test_run_flow_resume_after_pause_rearms_running_then_completes` (function) — Asserts running a step PAUSED then COMPLETED re-arms a second running anchor after the paused row and still lands its completion. <!--#e53666bca47fbd82-->
- `test_record_step_status_writes_status_record` (function) — Asserts record_step_status writes a step_status record carrying the given status, step_type, and ISO timestamp with no chat role. <!--#df644a53efa97e99-->
- `test_has_step_status_event_is_status_specific` (function) — Asserts has_step_status_event matches only the specific status token (case-insensitively) and not others. <!--#374e259994ed35c9-->
- `test_get_step_history_skips_step_status` (function) — Asserts get_step_history skips step_status lines, surfacing only real chat messages. <!--#6382f5e0fc7fd013-->
- `_run_discovery_pause` (function) — Test helper that drives `run_flow` for a DISCOVERY step whose mocked `run_step` fires `on_running` then returns PAUSED, with the interactive pause handler stubbed to simulate the user exiting, so tests can verify step_status persistence around a paused discovery step. <!--#75adfc4e13f70f6c-->
- `test_run_flow_persists_step_status_on_pause` (function) — Asserts a DISCOVERY step returning PAUSED persists a single paused step_status anchor alongside its running step_started anchor. <!--#78f13b15452f47e8-->
- `test_run_flow_step_status_records_paused_after_running_rearm` (function) — Asserts a multi-round running→paused→running→paused step records the second paused (after the running re-arm) so the latest persisted lifecycle status is correctly paused. <!--#1701383174e5c514-->
- `test_run_flow_step_status_dedups_back_to_back_paused` (function) — Asserts that without an intervening running anchor a re-recorded paused status is deduplicated, preventing two identical stacked status rows. <!--#fba88a107a5c51ac-->

### `tests/test_history_summary_extraction.py` (python) — Unit test suite verifying that history-title extraction stays aligned across the marker-level parser (extract_user_content), the CLI extractor (100-char clip), and the daemon extractor (untruncated), asserting they share the same three-tier priority (USER_CONTENT markers → Task-description regex → raw-content fallback) and identical extraction source while each keeps its own truncation contract. <!--#68312e0db255f6d7|1735fdca01ccda6f-->

- `test_extract_user_content_strips_edge_newlines` (function) — Asserts extract_user_content strips surrounding newlines but preserves interior spaces of the extracted user content. <!--#29b38f382a95ab60-->
- `test_extract_user_content_missing_markers` (function) — Asserts extract_user_content returns None when the body contains no markers. <!--#811f5b297c2d7bd1-->
- `test_extract_user_content_two_segment_returns_none` (function) — Asserts a two-segment body (BEGIN without END) yields None since the tail is framework-injected rather than user input. <!--#db80ad8d2acad804-->
- `test_extract_user_content_empty_middle_returns_none` (function) — Asserts extract_user_content returns None when the marker-enclosed middle is effectively empty. <!--#6138357c44aa1564-->
- `test_extract_user_content_non_string` (function) — Asserts extract_user_content returns None for non-string and empty-string inputs. <!--#83f91e1b426e7884-->
- `test_extract_user_content_begin_before_template_end_is_none` (function) — Asserts extract_user_content returns None when markers appear out of canonical order (BEGIN before the template prefix end). <!--#161d4db56fc6847c-->
- `_write_first_line` (function) — Fixture helper that creates a flow directory and writes a single first-line JSONL user record to drive the extractor tests. <!--#b5d6bdb1154e1e3e-->
- `_build_cases` (function) — Helper returning a labeled matrix of prompt-body inputs paired with their expected untruncated extraction source across all three priority tiers. <!--#ab79ca9dc7ef17ff-->
- `test_cli_and_daemon_share_extraction_source` (function) — Parametrized test asserting the daemon returns the untruncated extraction source while the CLI applies the 100-char clip, both from the same source. <!--#7085829d7ab011de-->
- `test_three_segment_marker_takes_priority_over_regex` (function) — Asserts that when a body contains both USER_CONTENT markers and a Task description block, the marker-level content wins for both extractors. <!--#693c52b84afdda38-->
- `test_content_as_text_block_list` (function) — Asserts both extractors handle a JSONL record whose content is a list of text blocks rather than a plain string. <!--#d03e01122f11ca9c-->
- `test_no_jsonl_returns_no_history_data` (function) — Asserts both extractors return the '(no history data)' sentinel when the flow directory contains no JSONL file. <!--#689d081a8f1bfdc6-->
- `test_corrupt_json_returns_no_state_data` (function) — Asserts both extractors return the '(no state data)' sentinel when the first JSONL line is malformed JSON. <!--#cc7236afd112c939-->
- `test_plain_text_fallback_matches_pre_change_behavior` (function) — Regression test ensuring a marker-less plain-text first line yields the raw content (clipped to 100 chars for the CLI, untruncated for the daemon). <!--#2b24e6f312e28f5e-->

### `tests/test_history_summary_scan.py` (python) — Regression tests asserting both the daemon and CLI history-only title extractors do a bounded forward scan past no-content `step_started` event records to recover the real user prompt, exercising the tiered marker/task-block/raw-content extraction, empty/unparseable-record skipping, CLI 100-char clipping, and the no-user-record and no-jsonl fallback sentinels. <!--#c00e115813875d8a|44c16148d74ddf9b-->

- `test_list_content_first_text_block` (function) — Asserts block-array user content reduces to its first text block before extraction. <!--#8f173886b49b1d5f-->
- `test_no_user_record_returns_fallback` (function) — Asserts a flow with no user-content record returns the `(no state data)` fallback rather than an empty title. <!--#5d039f785c5a26a1-->

### `tests/test_human_call.py` (python) — Regression test suite for merge/human_call.py defects F1–F5, covering collision-resistant call-filename generation, atomic JSON writes, orphan-file guardrail re-checks, violation-dict validation, and the `__`-for-slash naming convention. <!--#ebd260e209973fa0|edc440af6bf1fd25-->

### `tests/test_i18n.py` (python) — Unit test suite for the se3.i18n layer, covering locale-catalog discovery and auto-registration, t()'s fault-tolerant lookup with per-key en-US fallback and placeholder degradation, language-code normalization, the five-tier resolution precedence chain (SE3_LANG env → project se3.yaml → global ~/.se3 config → system locale → en-US base), and the lazy language singleton's reset seam — all with the process-wide i18n state and the developer's real home config/locale env isolated per test. <!--#6338e1550357b4bf|27944e28cf16e5d5-->
- `_reset_i18n` (function) — Autouse fixture that resets the process-wide i18n language/catalog singletons and isolates each test from the real home config and host locale env vars. <!--#eba138c1c2d5cbdd-->

  - `TestCatalogLoading.test_unknown_code_loads_empty_catalog` (method) — Asserts loading an unknown language code yields an empty catalog rather than raising. <!--#cbee43f1f6a193f5-->
  - `TestCatalogLoading.test_new_language_file_autoregistered` (method) — Asserts a new <code>.json dropped into locales/ becomes a supported language with no code change, by faking the locale resource iterator. <!--#49ae41a7a3ca5b02-->
- `TestTranslate` (class) — Tests t()'s lookup semantics: selected-language strings, en-US fallback, key echo when missing everywhere, and never raising on bad keys, missing kwargs, or malformed templates. <!--#35bfff9ba5dc8d9a-->
  - `TestTranslate.test_returns_selected_language_string` (method) — Asserts t() returns the active language's translation for a known key. <!--#802fc32bae8c0454-->
  - `TestTranslate.test_missing_key_falls_back_to_en_us` (method) — Asserts a key absent from the active catalog falls back to the en-US string. <!--#e7f5ca940302590d-->
  - `TestTranslate.test_missing_everywhere_returns_key` (method) — Asserts a key missing from every catalog renders as the key itself. <!--#73fac6a19e12c755-->
  - `TestTranslate.test_unknown_language_uses_en_us` (method) — Asserts selecting an unsupported language code falls back to the base en-US language. <!--#d20f13e0ebb45236-->
  - `TestTranslate.test_placeholder_rendered` (method) — Asserts t() formats template placeholders from keyword arguments. <!--#1d6785964878ca5e-->
  - `TestTranslate.test_missing_placeholder_returns_unformatted_template` (method) — Asserts a missing format kwarg degrades to the raw template instead of raising KeyError. <!--#fbcfd8447ed9676c-->
  - `TestTranslate.test_extra_placeholder_kwargs_ignored` (method) — Asserts unused keyword arguments passed to t() are harmlessly ignored. <!--#49dd6bf4b1dd7f2a-->
  - `TestTranslate.test_never_raises_on_any_input` (method) — Smoke-asserts t() never raises across empty, known, unknown, and placeholder-bearing keys. <!--#16fb9a7168a18901-->
  - `TestTranslate.test_bad_field_access_in_template_returns_template` (method) — Asserts translator-authored templates using attribute/subscript/positional field access degrade to the raw template instead of crashing t(). <!--#be304b0243f9d2b4-->
- `TestNormalization` (class) — Tests normalize_language()'s mapping of raw locale strings to supported codes and its safe None result for unknown or non-string inputs. <!--#3c390ca3d31bffc9-->
  - `TestNormalization.test_normalizes_to_supported` (method) — Parametrized check that locale variants (case, underscores, encodings, bare language tags) normalize to the canonical supported codes. <!--#55f2ee9540f7d90d-->
  - `TestNormalization.test_unknown_returns_none` (method) — Asserts empty, blank, None, and unsupported locale strings normalize to None. <!--#e66739b8f0749d98-->

  - `TestNormalization.test_set_language_with_non_string_selects_base` (method) — Asserts set_language() with a non-string argument selects the base en-US language. <!--#ddf90e4133e939ad-->
- `TestResolveLanguageChain` (class) — Tests the language resolution precedence chain — SE3_LANG env, project se3.yaml, global ~/.se3 config, system locale, en-US base — including how set-but-unsupported values fall back. <!--#434e4248f11fca3d-->
  - `TestResolveLanguageChain._write_project` (method) — Helper writing a project se3.yaml with a given language setting. <!--#0d30f6d21ed4740c-->

  - `TestResolveLanguageChain.test_unsupported_project_falls_back_to_base_not_locale` (method) — Asserts a set-but-unsupported project language resolves to en-US instead of falling through to the system locale. <!--#8ae72733d4e022cf-->
  - `TestResolveLanguageChain.test_non_string_project_language_falls_back_to_base_not_locale` (method) — Asserts a YAML-boolean project language (e.g. `language: NO`) is treated as explicit-but-invalid and resolves to en-US. <!--#b4642bda55a9952d-->
  - `TestResolveLanguageChain.test_unsupported_locale_passes_through_to_base` (method) — Asserts an unsupported system locale, being only an OS hint, falls through to the en-US base language. <!--#a0270f8efd1c17b1-->
- `TestLazySingleton` (class) — Tests the module-level language singleton: import is side-effect free, get_language() resolves lazily from cwd, and set/reset control re-resolution. <!--#c87c4f7fe0eb38a1-->

### `tests/test_interaction_calls.py` (python) — Test suite for the unified interaction-call channel, exercising the three layers that turn every human-in-the-loop flow interaction into a JSON call file under se3/calls/: the daemon protocol (MSG_INTERJECT_FLOW, CALL_KIND constants, decode backward-compat), the DaemonAggregator parsing of every call kind including legacy files, and the interaction_calls engine module for writing calls, reading response siblings, draining queued interjections, and handling retry-decision and CLI-confirm flows. <!--#e2d4b38784eabaef|02aebbef3381c520-->
- `test_make_interject_flow_payload_and_direction` (function) — Asserts make_interject_flow builds the correct payload and that MSG_INTERJECT_FLOW is registered as a server→daemon (not daemon→server) message type. <!--#ce856c65ac66617e-->
- `test_interject_flow_round_trips_through_decode` (function) — Verifies an interject-flow message survives JSON encode/decode with its text preserved and project_root defaulting to empty string. <!--#ac2793896657f29a-->
- `test_call_kind_constants_are_complete_and_distinct` (function) — Asserts that the protocol's CALL_KINDS set contains exactly the six expected CALL_KIND_* constants (call, interjection, retry-decision, cli-confirm, discovery-confirm, confirm) and that all six are distinct string literals. <!--#2a6d703f03d1a0b1-->
- `test_decode_still_rejects_unknown_types` (function) — Ensures decode raises ProtocolError on a genuinely unknown message type despite newly added known types. <!--#398349aec6b9786b-->
- `test_decode_tolerates_interject_without_optional_fields` (function) — Confirms a minimal interject frame carrying only the required type decodes successfully with an empty payload. <!--#2ebdd7b6b0959937-->
- `_write` (function) — Test helper that JSON-serializes a payload to a file, creating parent directories as needed. <!--#65d03e595cacafc0-->
- `test_aggregator_parses_every_call_kind` (function) — Verifies the aggregator enumerates call files of each kind and preserves enriched retry-decision fields (options/context) through to_dict serialization. <!--#fb5596513692123a-->
- `test_aggregator_legacy_call_file_without_kind` (function) — Backward-compat test that a pre-feature, metadata-less call file is parsed as a plain 'call' rather than dropped. <!--#816888c6e4addb9e-->
- `test_aggregator_unknown_kind_falls_back_to_call` (function) — Asserts both an unrecognized kind and a non-object JSON body degrade gracefully to the 'call' kind. <!--#aed450fd47b2a708-->
- `test_write_and_read_call_round_trip` (function) — Checks write_call persists kind/prompt/context/options to the expected filename and read_call returns them intact. <!--#c4957825936af17d-->
- `test_write_call_rejects_unknown_kind` (function) — Confirms write_call raises ValueError when given an invalid call kind. <!--#b2d6f3ee06a79507-->
- `test_read_call_legacy_file_defaults_kind` (function) — Verifies a kind-less call file reads back as 'call' and classify_kind agrees. <!--#eb1b544ce1d51add-->
- `test_read_call_handles_missing_and_malformed` (function) — Asserts read_call returns None for a missing file and for malformed JSON. <!--#687b30bb968163c8-->
- `test_classify_kind_defensive` (function) — Checks classify_kind defensively returns 'call' for None/empty/unknown inputs and the correct kind for valid ones. <!--#092af2612a47bc38-->
- `test_write_response_round_trip` (function) — Verifies write_response/read_response round-trip a response payload for a call, with read returning None before any response exists. <!--#c4912300dcbd4448-->
- `test_read_response_accepts_daemon_response_json` (function) — Confirms read_response also accepts the daemon client's '<stem>.response.json' sibling format. <!--#50dd437fd5042d9b-->
- `test_drain_interjection_requests_consumes_and_is_idempotent` (function) — Verifies draining queued interjection requests returns them in order and that a second drain returns nothing. <!--#a32f71b7e056faf0-->
- `test_drain_ignores_non_interjection_kinds` (function) — Asserts drain_interjection_requests returns only interjection calls, ignoring plain and retry-decision calls. <!--#b906f288ae57a804-->
- `test_drain_skips_empty_text_requests` (function) — Checks a whitespace-only interjection is silently consumed (marked served) but not returned. <!--#927ebea7703ff2f7-->
- `test_drain_missing_calls_dir_returns_empty` (function) — Confirms draining when the calls directory does not exist returns an empty list. <!--#cb65df987afe9643-->
- `test_drain_unlinks_call_file_and_writes_served_sibling` (function) — Verifies drain seals each consumed call by writing a '.response' sibling (consumed/served_by/served_at) then unlinking the call file. <!--#d16e259cffce6b1c-->
- `test_drain_returns_step_id_and_step_type_when_present` (function) — Asserts drained interjection entries surface step_id/step_type from the call context plus a created_at timestamp. <!--#b32bbc00a76a8e25-->
- `test_drain_legacy_call_without_context_step_fields_empty` (function) — Confirms legacy interjection calls lacking context step fields still drain with empty step_id/step_type. <!--#e6965d334fcce5af-->
- `test_drain_second_pass_is_idempotent_after_unlink` (function) — Verifies a second drain pass finds nothing because the first unlinked the consumed call file. <!--#37022ed4194067f0-->
- `test_write_retry_decision_call_shape` (function) — Checks write_retry_decision_call derives a step-based filename and writes the retry kind, retry/skip/abort options, and context/prompt fields. <!--#8cc0d13c846f142c-->
- `test_cli_confirm_handler_returns_answer_when_response_arrives` (function) — Tests the CLI-confirm handler returns the answer once a response file appears while the child reports alive. <!--#ed27129230cab3d0-->
- `test_cli_confirm_handler_marks_orphan_consumed_when_child_exits` (function) — Verifies the CLI-confirm handler returns None and marks the orphaned call file consumed (skipped=subprocess_exited) when the child exits before answering. <!--#cd2f283da836695c-->

- `test_status_update_broadcasts_interjection_event_to_ui_clients` (function) — End-to-end test that a daemon STATUS_UPDATE introducing an interjection chip broadcasts an interjection_event on the live /ws/ui channel. <!--#bad4be5dbea5501d-->
- `test_tracker_handles_malformed_snapshots_gracefully` (function) — Verifies the tracker returns no events and never raises on missing-key or malformed snapshot inputs. <!--#847b4a02b5780a69-->
- `test_pending_calls_signature_includes_worktree_run_calls` (function) — Confirms the fast call signature also covers call files written under a --worktree isolation run's directory. <!--#7a68a7a15ed3b2a6-->
- `test_history_relay_preserves_step_id_and_ordinal_identity` (function) — Verifies that ServerState.append_history relays records verbatim to the history snapshot, preserving distinct per-file step_ids and duplicate ordinals from worktree sidecar streams without rewriting or collapsing them. <!--#9751ffddf3e54742-->
- `test_history_append_does_not_dedupe_same_ordinal_records` (function) — Verifies that an APPEND-mode history push extends the bundle without dedup, so a record sharing an ordinal with an existing record under a different step_id is kept rather than dropped as a duplicate. <!--#aaee0fdb953dc569-->
- `test_reconcile_full_pull_respects_existing_throttle` (function) — Verifies that ServerState's full-pull throttle reports throttled immediately after mark_full_pull, gating the self-heal reconcile on the same throttle as the cache-miss path so idle polls can't trigger a daemon pull per tick. <!--#af515eb49a926eb9-->

### `tests/test_invariant_check.py` (python) — Test suite for the INVARIANT_CHECK step (the anchored replacement for the retired spec_gate), verifying that only violations grounded in a verbatim charter/why-comment quote whose evidence points at a changed file survive to REVISION_NEEDED while ungrounded nits are filtered, that no-diff and no-anchor cases pass cheaply without an LLM call, that deleted why-comments are recovered from the git baseline, and that unparsable LLM responses fail. <!--#750a3cf6d1af4b3c|af7782bb68ee9b16-->
- `_make_flow` (function) — Helper that builds a feature FlowInstance with a given task description and a change_path under the test's project root. <!--#ffc7ea4176dbfbe2-->
- `_make_step` (function) — Helper that constructs an INVARIANT_CHECK Step from a given inputs dict. <!--#3e4d116d5efe7203-->
- `_install_fake_caller` (function) — Helper that monkeypatches the step's LLMCaller with a scripted fake recording prompts/call counts and returning queued responses. <!--#48f66cdee783b441-->
- `_grounded_issue` (function) — Helper that builds a well-formed issue dict citing a verbatim charter quote and evidence lines in a given file path. <!--#75be8afa7a516dbd-->
- `test_no_diff_passes_cheap_without_llm` (function) — Asserts that an invariant_check with no changed files passes as COMPLETED with skipped_reason 'no_diff' and makes no LLM call. <!--#5cc2d026d2acee1f-->
- `test_no_anchors_refuses_anchorless_check` (function) — Asserts that a diff with zero recorded anchors yields a cheap COMPLETED pass (skipped_reason 'no_anchors') rather than inventing an invariant. <!--#27e66bb91cab2036-->
- `test_ungrounded_nit_is_filtered` (function) — Asserts that an issue whose verbatim_quote is absent from the anchor pool is dropped, leaving the step COMPLETED and counting it in quote_not_in_source_count. <!--#caf367740954be0b-->
- `test_grounded_violation_routes_to_fix` (function) — Asserts that a violation quoting the charter verbatim with evidence in a changed file survives to REVISION_NEEDED with fix outputs populated. <!--#49d21b341c9eecf2-->
- `test_evidence_must_point_at_changed_file` (function) — Asserts the two-sided anchoring: a valid charter quote whose evidence path is not among the changed files is dropped and counted in bad_evidence_count. <!--#b76a319f2c06bd08-->
- `test_why_comment_anchor_is_harvested_from_changed_file` (function) — Asserts that a why-comment present in a changed file enters the anchor pool, so a violation quoting it survives to REVISION_NEEDED. <!--#1eecbca80eae666d-->
- `_git` (function) — Helper that runs a git subcommand in a given working directory, raising on failure. <!--#eae0deaeea597400-->
- `test_deleted_why_comment_invariant_recovered_from_baseline` (function) — Regression test verifying that a why-comment documenting a binding invariant stays anchorable even when the violating diff deletes it, by confirming the harvest recovers the original comment from the flow-start baseline (via git show) and still yields exactly one hard, anchored violation while treating the unmarked deletion as advisory-only. <!--#c458c7c31dc01e07-->
- `test_unparsable_llm_response_fails` (function) — Asserts that a non-JSON LLM response makes the step return FAILED with an error message set. <!--#c00d17d5f8570232-->

### `tests/test_issue209_live_append_regression.py` (python) — Regression lock for issue #209 that replays the real captured frame sequence (on-disk jsonl fixtures + recorded daemon_frames.json) through DaemonHistoryReader to prove the discovery→analyze transition and step-error retry surface as no-loss/no-dup/no-truncation append deltas, and that the ~1 MB active engine.json is parsed at most once per actual change (verifying the daemon push-loop starvation fix). <!--#85edb7797c4bca90|aa69f71a45017b3d-->
- `_load_fixture_lines` (function) — Helper that reads each real fixture jsonl file and returns its raw newline-kept lines keyed by file name. <!--#211d170bf7b36abd-->
- `_load_captured_frames` (function) — Helper that loads the recorded daemon frame sequence (the expected per-tick read output) from daemon_frames.json. <!--#1438223a67f62bae-->
- `_ondisk_messages` (function) — Helper that returns every on-disk fixture record in file-then-line order as the no-loss ground-truth message sequence. <!--#d97b6673519977bb-->
- `_write_active_engine` (function) — Helper that writes a RUNNING active engine.json, optionally inflated with blob steps to mimic the ~1 MB parse that starved the push loop. <!--#3bfc215376d44fef-->
- `_replay_real_frames` (function) — Helper that drives the reader through the captured tick sequence, growing the on-disk jsonl files to each frame's cursor and returning the per-tick FlowRead lists produced. <!--#9f360f95e17b879c-->
- `test_real_frame_sequence_matches_captured_daemon_frames` (function) — Test asserting that replaying the real records reproduces the captured frames' mode/record-count/cursor at every tick and that analyze/plan records surface only as a final append delta. <!--#285d1e7441ec3dfd-->
- `test_real_frame_replay_no_loss_no_dup_no_truncation` (function) — Test asserting the records delivered across all replay ticks equal, item-for-item and in order, the 20 on-disk fixture records. <!--#59eb4809ac43d4fc-->
- `test_retry_after_error_same_jsonl_append_surfaces` (function) — Test asserting that retry records appended to the same plan jsonl after a step failure surface as a fresh append delta with no re-delivery of prior records and a correctly advanced cursor. <!--#b01e474d93b89856-->
- `_count_engine_parses` (function) — Test helper that clears the disk-JSON cache and monkeypatches `disk_json_cache._parse_json` to count full parses of the active engine.json, isolating the exact GIL-bound seam the #209 fix collapses so tests can assert per-tick re-parses are eliminated. <!--#f650ce0ea068dc3e-->
- `test_real_frame_replay_parses_active_engine_json_once_per_change` (function) — Test asserting that across the unchanged-engine.json replay the ~1 MB file is parsed at most once despite all four per-tick readers touching it each tick. <!--#1f86aee91f8e0bd9-->
- `test_active_engine_json_reparsed_on_transition_and_retry` (function) — Test asserting the content-keyed parse cache serves repeats without re-parsing but re-parses when a genuine engine.json rewrite (transition/retry) changes the content, avoiding stale state. <!--#70d262a1d58807db-->

### `tests/test_issue243_disk_json_cache.py` (python) — Regression test suite for issue #243's disk-JSON read-path cache, verifying that unchanged engine.json files are fully parsed only once (keyed by path/mtime/size), reparse on change, and that over-guard oversized files are never fully parsed nor cached while head+tail scanning still yields hot keys, plus daemon aggregator scans of giant/new-format engine.json files avoid full parses. <!--#580d34c8265fd2c0|1eecf4bb0b8af53b-->
- `_clear_cache` (function) — Autouse pytest fixture that clears the disk-JSON cache before and after each test to isolate cache state. <!--#06929c6a0cd57978-->
- `_count_full_parses` (function) — Helper that monkeypatches the single `_parse_json_file` seam to count full-file JSON parses, returning a mutable counter dict. <!--#6459d0ca4d566bad-->
- `_write_engine` (function) — Helper that writes an `indent=2` engine.json with head hot keys (flow_id/status), an inflatable middle `state` blob, and tail keys (is_worktree_mode/worktree_branch), mimicking persistence's on-disk layout. <!--#55e2fe7c5eae3bd1-->
- `test_unchanged_file_parsed_once` (function) — Asserts an unchanged engine.json is fully parsed only once across ten reads, cached by (path, mtime, size). <!--#6cfe3caedc4ee5a2-->
- `test_reparse_on_change` (function) — Asserts rewriting the engine.json with different content/size invalidates the cache key and triggers exactly one reparse. <!--#c52e3e418f2c91e7-->
- `test_oversized_file_never_fully_parsed` (function) — Asserts an over-guard (>MAX_PARSE_BYTES) engine.json is never fully parsed yet still yields head and tail hot keys via head+tail scanning. <!--#44f70d26f2b54037-->
- `test_oversized_file_not_cached` (function) — Asserts `read_json_cached` refuses to store or return over-guard files, returning None as a memory guard. <!--#ad8d45935e5bdbfc-->
- `test_degraded_extraction_failure_warns_once` (function) — Asserts an over-guard file with no recognizable top-level flow_id degrades to None and logs a warning only once, not per read. <!--#a0b12a5ddab98a7d-->
- `_make_worktree_run` (function) — Helper that builds a worktree run directory tree with a (optionally giant) engine.json for daemon-scan tests. <!--#7cdc9f2a88d30549-->
- `test_worktree_scan_no_full_parse_on_giant_files` (function) — Asserts the daemon aggregator's active-worktree scan performs zero full parses on two giant legacy engine.json files while both runs remain observable. <!--#0f4d0fd56041d78e-->
- `test_snapshot_for_root_reads_new_format_header_only` (function) — Asserts the aggregator's `_snapshot_for_root` reads flow_id/status/step-count from a new-format hot header without touching cold files. <!--#aba13c2c4179472d-->

### `tests/test_issue244_split_format.py` (python) — Regression test suite for issue #244's engine.json hot/cold split (Part B / G7 B4/B5), verifying that saving/loading round-trips equal with per-step inputs/outputs and shared context externalized to bounded cold files, that legacy inline formats still load, that persistence and lazy hydration touch only changed/requested cold files, that missing/corrupt/truncated cold data degrades gracefully, and that clear_state archives header plus cold partition together while handling archive-name collisions and preserving surviving resumable snapshots. <!--#2a36fe3da23f34a0|dafbdf1fa62ecb3f-->
- `_make_flow` (function) — Test helper that builds a FlowInstance with N steps carrying large (payload_size) inputs/outputs plus big shared context and fix-iteration data, optionally in worktree mode, to mimic a real 50MB-scale flow for exercising the hot/cold split format. <!--#f10e3512c292a4e9-->
- `test_new_format_save_load_roundtrip_equal` (function) — Verifies a saved flow uses the ENGINE_FORMAT_HOTCOLD header that externalizes per-step inputs/outputs and shared context to cold files (referenced by cold_ref/context_ref), and that loading it round-trips back to an equal flow. <!--#188bec6ea1111bbc-->
- `test_resumable_snapshot_roundtrip_equal` (function) — Checks that saving a non-completed (paused) flow also writes a resumable snapshot that round-trips equal via both load_resumable_snapshot and load_flow_by_id. <!--#54eaed83e44148fe-->
- `test_legacy_inline_engine_json_loads` (function) — Confirms backward compatibility by loading a legacy full-inline engine.json (no engine_format marker, no cold files) verbatim into an equal flow. <!--#19081da7c2eff558-->
- `test_legacy_inline_resumable_snapshot_loads` (function) — Confirms a legacy full-inline resumable snapshot JSON still loads to an equal flow via load_resumable_snapshot. <!--#9ee9fcd42117786c-->
- `test_header_bounded_under_100kb` (function) — Asserts the engine.json header stays under 100KB even for a 31-step flow with ~700KB payloads per step, proving payloads are externalized rather than inlined. <!--#2333ee55c46b3b12-->
- `test_per_step_persistence_touches_only_changed_cold_file` (function) — Verifies that mutating one step's outputs and re-saving rewrites only that step's cold file, with the other steps' cold files and _context.json skipped by the sha1 change guard. <!--#0037fde7592aace1-->
- `test_missing_cold_step_file_degrades_gracefully` (function) — Ensures a deleted or corrupt cold step file degrades that step to empty inputs/outputs on load without crashing, while intact steps survive. <!--#2b28de41eb10980e-->
- `test_missing_cold_context_degrades_gracefully` (function) — Ensures a missing shared _context.json cold file loads as empty context rather than crashing the flow load. <!--#0e1f92d11ee9693f-->
- `test_resume_partial_flow_reloads_full_fidelity` (function) — Verifies a mid-flow paused new-format flow reloads at full fidelity (current_step_id/index preserved, equal to original) via a fresh manager, and re-saving keeps the hot/cold split format without re-inlining. <!--#c23bfbd35fc9ebea-->
- `test_load_flow_by_id_defers_step_cold_files` (function) — Tests the B4 lazy-load: load_flow_by_id reads only the shared context cold file up front and faults in each step's cold body exactly once, on demand, when fetched by id. <!--#43b510e60ec9a4c0-->
- `test_hydrate_step_loads_only_requested_cold_file` (function) — Verifies hydrate_step on a from_header_dict flow materializes only the requested step's cold file (others stay empty) and is idempotent, never re-reading or clobbering already-loaded step data. <!--#b7be7b168522878d-->
- `test_clear_state_archives_header_and_cold_files` (function) — Confirms clear_state archives the hot/cold header plus its full cold-file partition (steps + _context.json) together into archive/, preserving format and identity, and removes the live cold directory. <!--#15f164d213684ae4-->
- `test_clear_state_same_second_archives_do_not_collide` (function) — Verifies the B5 fix that two flows archived within the same second get uniquely-named archive headers (not clobbered), keeping both flows recoverable via list_all_flows with intact distinct cold partitions. <!--#f2a0ca36f98c9cb1-->
- `test_load_resumable_snapshot_defers_step_cold_files` (function) — Tests that load_resumable_snapshot lazily reads only the shared context up front and faults in each paused-flow step's cold body exactly once on first fetch. <!--#3d40a32e5a26d89e-->
- `test_list_resumable_snapshots_defers_step_cold_files` (function) — Verifies enumerating multiple paused/failed resumable snapshots consults only header (and possibly context) data, never reading any per-step cold body up front. <!--#db6fb9a9e57990f2-->
- `test_clear_state_archive_collision_stays_reference_consistent` (function) — Verifies that when archive/steps/<flow_id> already exists, clear_state moves this flow's cold files to a suffixed partition recorded in the header's cold_partition, leaving the pre-existing sibling untouched and keeping the archived header's references consistent with its own payloads. <!--#744c2e34b9c7259e-->
- `test_clear_state_archive_double_collision_does_not_abort` (function) — Verifies that when both the primary and first timestamp-suffixed archive partitions are already occupied, clear_state probes past them to a numeric-suffixed partition rather than aborting, leaving both pre-existing archives intact and keeping references consistent. <!--#107835a3b6bcb899-->
- `test_list_all_flows_mixed_formats` (function) — Confirms list_all_flows enumerates both a new hot/cold archived flow and a legacy inline archived snapshot in the same archive directory. <!--#ca1aca71392b2059-->
- `test_export_context_and_progress_on_new_format` (function) — Checks that export_context_from_flow and export_progress_markdown work on a loaded new-format flow, producing non-empty structured context and a progress markdown containing the flow id and steps section. <!--#287d4abc59e3159f-->
- `test_export_context_hydrates_lazy_loaded_flow` (function) — Regression test (fix iteration 6) ensuring export_context_from_flow first hydrates cold bodies of a lazily-loaded flow so real step inputs/outputs reach the exported context instead of empty payloads from un-hydrated _LazyStepDict iteration. <!--#db66aa2f9c8d7274-->
- `test_clear_state_preserves_surviving_resumable_snapshot_fidelity` (function) — Verifies clear_state on a non-completed flow copies (rather than moves) its cold partition to the archive, leaving the live partition in place so the still-advertised resumable snapshot resumes at full fidelity while the archive keeps a complete copy. <!--#d2456f9bb517618d-->
- `test_load_flow_tolerant_recovers_truncated_hotcold_header` (function) — Verifies load_flow_tolerant salvages a crash-truncated hot/cold header (created_at onward lost) by relying on the leading engine_format marker to still resolve intact cold step files and shared context, reporting recovery via warnings instead of dropping the flow or emptying payloads. <!--#b09747181653dfb7-->

### `tests/test_issue_209_push_starvation.py` (python) — Regression-lock test module for issue #209 (daemon push-loop starvation): it proves DaemonHistoryReader parses the large active engine.json at most once per actual change via a stat-keyed cache, while verifying discovery→analyze and retry live-append deltas still stream incrementally. <!--#e838266acc909a2a|b7392309b695ff4e-->

- `_write_jsonl` (function) — Test helper that writes a per-step history jsonl file containing n simple assistant-message records. <!--#bb20aacf8e3df4bc-->
- `_count_engine_parses` (function) — Test helper that monkeypatches `disk_json_cache._parse_json` to count full engine.json parses (the GIL-bound `json.loads` seam the #209 fix collapses), returning a mutable counter after clearing the module cache so the test can assert parses happen once per actual change rather than once per reader-call per push tick. <!--#bcc5c8ff141c8d88-->
- `test_active_engine_json_parsed_once_per_change_across_readers` (function) — Test asserting the active engine.json is parsed at most once across 10 unchanged ticks driving all four per-tick readers (the starvation regression lock). <!--#f8a6d13239e9ae5e-->
- `test_active_engine_json_reparsed_after_change` (function) — Test asserting the stat-keyed parse cache serves unchanged reads but re-parses once when engine.json is genuinely rewritten. <!--#4f8b51caff277baf-->
- `test_discovery_to_analyze_transition_surfaces_via_read_active_flows` (function) — Correctness test asserting the discovery→analyze new-step append still streams incrementally as an append-mode delta with the parse cache enabled. <!--#fc4a182050c46166-->
- `test_retry_after_error_append_surfaces_via_read_active_flows` (function) — Correctness test asserting retry records appended to the same step's jsonl still surface incrementally with the parse cache enabled. <!--#31f65854c7ea14aa-->

### `tests/test_issue_manager.py` (python) — Unit tests for SE3's YAML-based IssueManager and its Issue dataclass, covering serialization round-trips, legacy/retired-field handling, display-title derivation, slug generation, and create/load behavior (ID assignment, directory creation, open/closed lookup). <!--#2e9e04002faade28|4c2c2200a7cf8d3a-->
- `TestIssueModel` (class) — Tests Issue dataclass serialization round-tripping through to_dict/from_dict, including defaults, legacy compatibility, and retired-field handling. <!--#d62b9ec3cc635737-->
  - `TestIssueModel.test_to_dict_roundtrip` (method) — Verifies a fully-populated Issue survives a to_dict/from_dict round-trip with all fields intact. <!--#c561404c8ddb686a-->
  - `TestIssueModel.test_from_dict_defaults` (method) — Checks from_dict applies correct defaults (open status, system source, empty tags, None optionals) for a minimal dict. <!--#447b188a70081047-->
  - `TestIssueModel.test_from_dict_missing_description_degrades` (method) — Confirms YAML lacking a description loads with description="" and derives display_title from the title. <!--#901c5337ac8b6338-->
  - `TestIssueModel.test_from_dict_empty_description_degrades` (method) — Confirms an empty-string description loads as "" rather than erroring. <!--#45b08875436ff7fb-->
  - `TestIssueModel.test_from_dict_whitespace_description_degrades` (method) — Confirms a whitespace-only description degrades to "" on load. <!--#0de17a6571765616-->

  - `TestIssueModel.test_from_dict_missing_source_defaults_system` (method) — Verifies pre-source legacy YAML (no source field) loads as source=system. <!--#9466400ad6158456-->
  - `TestIssueModel.test_from_dict_explicit_source` (method) — Verifies an explicit source field (human) is preserved on load. <!--#db832807b052916f-->
  - `TestIssueModel.test_from_dict_ignores_legacy_scope_key` (method) — Confirms a retired scope key loads without error, leaves no scope attribute, and is never re-serialized. <!--#c1f9865c5712cace-->
  - `TestIssueModel.test_to_dict_never_emits_scope` (method) — Asserts the fully-retired scope key never appears in serialized output. <!--#260d5d72d8b2946b-->
  - `TestIssueModel.test_to_dict_omits_none_optional_fields` (method) — Verifies title/priority/type are omitted from the dict when None. <!--#4cbd000dca163d04-->
  - `TestIssueModel.test_to_dict_includes_set_optional_fields` (method) — Verifies set optional fields (title/priority/type/source) appear in the serialized dict. <!--#85cf4c9d87721199-->
  - `TestIssueModel.test_roundtrip_with_none_optional_fields` (method) — Confirms an Issue with None optional fields survives a to_dict/from_dict round-trip. <!--#bed60d3eabf1710d-->
  - `TestIssueModel.test_from_dict_invalid_datetime_falls_back` (method) — Checks unparseable datetime strings fall back to now() instead of raising. <!--#f144f373c2240647-->

  - `TestApplyDiscoveryIssueOperations.test_create_marks_source_human_and_tracks_id` (method) — Verifies a discovery create marks source=human, applies fields, and tracks the new ID. <!--#cd033347cd1dd41b-->
  - `TestApplyDiscoveryIssueOperations.test_update_within_scope_applies` (method) — Verifies an update to a tracked (in-scope) issue is applied and stays tracked. <!--#edc32f6b5d615219-->
  - `TestApplyDiscoveryIssueOperations.test_update_out_of_scope_rejected_without_calling_backend` (method) — Verifies updating an out-of-scope historical issue is rejected without invoking the backend. <!--#6937f502027d3eb6-->
  - `TestApplyDiscoveryIssueOperations.test_delete_within_scope_removes_and_untracks` (method) — Verifies deleting an in-scope issue removes it and drops it from the tracked set. <!--#0aac2e3b2c25b29e-->
  - `TestApplyDiscoveryIssueOperations.test_delete_out_of_scope_rejected_without_calling_backend` (method) — Verifies deleting an out-of-scope issue is rejected without invoking the backend. <!--#08db3dc2fbc1acbb-->

### `tests/test_issue_renumber_helper.py` (python) — Unit tests for the shared issue_renumber merge primitives — token-precise `#NNN` reference rewriting (single/bulk/added-lines/masking), `.next_id` counter advancement to max ID, issue-ID ownership resolution, and renumber-trace/ambiguity-note formatting — that both se3 merge channels reuse to renumber colliding issues. <!--#b0fd314c6835fed0|3242e8a90e5b9bf2-->
- `_write_issue` (function) — Test helper that writes a minimal issue YAML with an explicit ID into the manager's open/ or closed/ directory and returns its path. <!--#bb5e01423c8462ed-->
- `_read_next_id` (function) — Test helper that reads and returns the integer value from the project's se3/issues/.next_id counter file. <!--#15781186357ab14f-->
- `test_rewrite_leaves_non_reference_hashnumbers_untouched` (function) — Asserts reference rewriting is token-precise, changing a standalone `#123` while leaving superstrings like `#1234` and leading-alnum tokens like `abc#123` untouched. <!--#1528cb022d95d2e7-->
- `test_rewrite_leaves_trailing_alnum_tokens_untouched` (function) — Asserts rewrite_issue_references treats `#123abc` as prose and rewrites only the standalone `#123` token. <!--#797fb7c055b94094-->
- `test_rewrite_treats_zero_padding_as_equivalent` (function) — Asserts zero-padding variants (`#14`, `#014`, `#0014`) all denote the same issue and are all rewritten to the new ID. <!--#4d8e4147365745d6-->
- `test_rewrite_counts_across_open_and_closed` (function) — Asserts a rewrite spans both open/ and closed/ issues and returns the total number of references replaced. <!--#d1e051cc68657f99-->
- `test_rewrite_confined_to_issues_dir` (function) — Asserts reference rewriting never touches files outside se3/issues/, leaving stray mentions elsewhere unchanged. <!--#81dadcb2c59c6d62-->
- `test_rewrite_new_id_is_zero_padded` (function) — Asserts the replacement reference token is zero-padded to at least three digits (e.g. `#7` becomes `#007`). <!--#14a16b30094067df-->
- `test_bulk_rewrite_does_not_chain_through_overlapping_pairs` (function) — Verifies rewrite_issue_references_bulk resolves each token against the original text so overlapping pairs (005→010, 010→011) don't chain. <!--#43839b01665610c9-->
- `test_bulk_rewrite_ignores_identity_pairs_and_scopes` (function) — Checks bulk rewrite skips identity pairs (007→007) and only touches files within the given scope_files. <!--#a5fd4b46f90e44e2-->
- `test_mask_replaces_only_standalone_reference_tokens` (function) — Confirms mask_issue_references replaces standalone `#NNN` tokens with `#REF` while leaving leading-alnum forms like `abc#123` intact. <!--#44cbb9ef8c5d416c-->
- `test_mask_makes_rewritten_reference_sign_equal` (function) — Asserts masking renders two bodies differing only in reference numbers identically, so pre/post-renumber texts compare equal. <!--#da743f71ba56ffb6-->
- `test_advance_from_missing_counter` (function) — Asserts a missing .next_id counter is created at max(existing ID)+1. <!--#53beb5370d29d6de-->
- `test_advance_from_lagging_counter` (function) — Asserts a counter lagging behind the true max ID is pushed forward to max+1. <!--#067db10a4725e2d3-->
- `test_advance_from_garbage_counter` (function) — Asserts a corrupt/non-numeric counter value is discarded and recomputed from the issue files. <!--#0afb0161f1a10dcf-->
- `test_advance_with_no_issues` (function) — Asserts that with an empty issue store the counter initializes to 1 (max of 0, plus 1). <!--#e44420b4a93c07a4-->
- `test_advance_counts_parsed_id_not_just_filename` (function) — Verifies advance_next_id_to_max counts a parsed `id` field that exceeds its filename prefix, advancing the counter past it. <!--#cca9dde48b61c8ec-->
- `test_find_issue_id_owner_prefers_parsed_id_over_filename` (function) — Checks find_issue_id_owner / resolve_issue_numeric_id resolve ownership by the parsed `id`, not the filename prefix. <!--#dbc76a8b55615a5c-->
- `test_find_issue_id_owner_excludes_given_files` (function) — Verifies find_issue_id_owner honors exclude_files and falls back to filename prefix when a body lacks a parseable id. <!--#75eb80c27a28b379-->
- `test_advance_never_lowers_ahead_counter` (function) — Asserts advance_next_id_to_max is monotonic, leaving a `.next_id` counter already ahead of the scanned max untouched to protect live reservations. <!--#120198bb56c8b07f-->
- `test_added_lines_rewrite_only_touches_new_lines` (function) — Confirms rewrite_references_in_added_lines renumbers references only on merge-added lines, leaving baseline references intact. <!--#28bbb2b52bc959be-->
- `test_added_lines_rewrite_is_token_precise` (function) — Checks added-line rewriting respects `#NNN` token boundaries, ignoring `#1234` and `abc#123` while rewriting standalone `#123`. <!--#d925aa5155377a58-->
- `test_added_lines_rewrite_no_hits_leaves_file_untouched` (function) — Verifies a file whose added lines carry no matching reference returns zero hits and is left byte-identical. <!--#b6afcbb9910e8355-->
- `test_added_lines_rewrite_survives_yaml_quote_style_shift` (function) — Ensures added-line detection compares parsed YAML logical lines, so appending a description line doesn't misclassify a shifted quote-boundary line as added. <!--#38be5c4783cd8b0a-->
- `test_added_duplicate_of_existing_line_still_follows_renumber` (function) — Verifies baseline membership is counted per occurrence so an appended duplicate of an existing YAML line still follows the renumber. <!--#1f862887578f73b3-->
- `test_added_duplicate_line_raw_fallback_still_follows_renumber` (function) — Checks the non-YAML physical-line fallback path also counts baseline lines per occurrence for duplicate added lines. <!--#198110940a910233-->
- `test_trace_contains_old_and_new_ids` (function) — Asserts the formatted renumber trace string contains both the old and new issue IDs. <!--#9fac3d3751279c32-->
- `test_trace_normalizes_and_zero_pads` (function) — Asserts the renumber trace zero-pads both IDs to three digits regardless of input padding or type, producing the expected annotated string. <!--#a78488f080432450-->
- `test_trace_appended_preserves_display_title` (function) — Asserts appending the renumber trace at the tail of a description leaves the issue's display_title (first non-empty line) derivation intact. <!--#29877799ca9b6224-->
- `test_ambiguous_note_lists_all_candidates_zero_padded` (function) — Asserts format_ambiguous_reference_note renders a zero-padded ambiguity note listing all candidate IDs. <!--#84b58fc3d82e4f8e-->
- `test_strip_removes_traces_and_ambiguity_notes` (function) — Verifies strip_renumber_traces removes both renumber-trace and ambiguity audit lines while preserving live text verbatim. <!--#ab86f083289582bf-->
- `test_count_reference_tokens_is_token_precise` (function) — Checks count_reference_tokens counts standalone tokens precisely, absorbing zero-padding and ignoring superstring/leading-alnum prose forms. <!--#ecf1d3e8dc466a2e-->
- `test_live_reference_count_ignores_audit_lines` (function) — Verifies live_reference_count counts genuine references but ignores historical `#NNN` mentions inside audit/trace lines. <!--#ed5c53030ea2a3ed-->
- `test_append_description_note_preserves_title_and_parses` (function) — Confirms append_description_note appends a note while preserving the issue title and keeping the YAML parseable. <!--#28a0f5c90681ff12-->
- `test_added_lines_dry_run_counts_without_writing` (function) — Asserts rewrite_references_in_added_lines dry_run reports would-be hits while leaving the file byte-identical. <!--#b7cc4c41c1f1ddbd-->

### `tests/test_json_parser.py` (python) — Unit and integration tests for se3.engine.utils.json_parser, exercising unescaped-quote repair, JSON extraction/parsing, the shared repair chain, and the dict-only/lenient JSON detectors for consistency with parse_json_response. <!--#023d18321b65857f|392b6f8fa4fd9043-->

  - `TestExtractAndParseJsonWithQuoteRepair.test_raw_json_with_unescaped_quotes` (method) — Asserts raw (unfenced) JSON with unescaped interior quotes is extracted and parsed. <!--#c1589a339f0bc5b1-->

  - `TestExtractAndParseJsonWithQuoteRepair.test_trailing_json_with_escaped_quotes` (method) — Asserts the backward boundary walker selects the trailing JSON object even when it contains escaped quotes. <!--#db097c853bade56f-->
- `TestTryParseWithRepairs` (class) — Test class for _try_parse_with_repairs, the shared repair-chain helper, covering valid input, repairs, non-JSON, and consistency with _extract_and_parse_json. <!--#1a43f4aa55140eee-->
  - `TestTryParseWithRepairs.test_valid_json_object` (method) — Asserts a valid JSON object parses to the expected dict. <!--#781509bb30103ee9-->
  - `TestTryParseWithRepairs.test_valid_json_array` (method) — Asserts a valid JSON array parses to the expected list. <!--#6a28d32d8f3540d9-->

### `tests/test_language_config.py` (python) — Test suite for SE3's language configuration layer, covering LanguageConfig.load()'s parsing of the se3.yaml language section (present, missing, null, malformed) and its per-field project-over-global merge with ~/.se3/config.yaml, plus get_language_instruction()/get_step_language_instruction() behavior determining which pipeline steps receive general-language, spec-language, or no language injection. <!--#d2eb13ee55493b3a|f6e54c093c882331-->
- `_isolated_global_home` (function) — Autouse fixture that redirects `Path.home()` to a fresh temp directory so a developer's real `~/.se3/config.yaml` language setting can't leak into these tests. <!--#b6529ca67d0c52b0-->
- `global_home` (function) — Fixture exposing the isolated fake home directory so a test can write its own `~/.se3/config.yaml` global tier. <!--#f7773c64e7b85831-->
- `_write_global_language` (function) — Helper that writes a minimal `~/.se3/config.yaml` under the given home with the requested `language` / `spec_language` values (or explicit nulls). <!--#a2c3b18e89db90c2-->
- `TestLanguageConfigLoad` (class) — Test class verifying LanguageConfig.load() and load_language_config() parse the se3.yaml language section across present, missing, null, and malformed cases. <!--#550d01ccd4a51cb0-->
  - `TestLanguageConfigLoad.test_defaults_when_no_file` (method) — Asserts both language fields default to None when no se3.yaml exists. <!--#08988d719e459a62-->
  - `TestLanguageConfigLoad.test_defaults_when_no_language_section` (method) — Asserts both fields default to None when se3.yaml lacks a language section. <!--#1d8738f31b7d33b7-->
  - `TestLanguageConfigLoad.test_defaults_when_null_values` (method) — Asserts both fields are None when explicitly set to null in config. <!--#948ab471e2f23742-->
  - `TestLanguageConfigLoad.test_both_set` (method) — Asserts language and spec_language are both loaded when set. <!--#bdde42e09da98667-->
  - `TestLanguageConfigLoad.test_only_language_set` (method) — Asserts language loads and spec_language defaults to None when only language is set. <!--#c1cdb5abf4c9b667-->
  - `TestLanguageConfigLoad.test_only_spec_language_set` (method) — Asserts spec_language loads and language defaults to None when only spec_language is set. <!--#269c01ef67d7dbf1-->
  - `TestLanguageConfigLoad.test_load_language_config_convenience` (method) — Verifies the load_language_config() convenience wrapper loads both fields. <!--#460cf028b5caad9c-->
  - `TestLanguageConfigLoad.test_invalid_yaml` (method) — Asserts malformed YAML is handled gracefully, yielding None fields. <!--#3f86be637028740c-->
  - `TestLanguageConfigLoad.test_language_section_not_dict` (method) — Asserts a scalar (non-dict) language section is handled gracefully as None fields. <!--#e434d78cf6c25682-->
- `TestLanguageConfigGlobalMerge` (class) — Test class covering `LanguageConfig.load`'s per-field project-over-global merge of the language section, including global-only, partial-project, both-unset, and explicit-project-null cases. <!--#b3d910d74c30875c-->

  - `TestLanguageConfigGlobalMerge.test_global_only` (method) — Asserts that with no project `se3.yaml`, the global config's language values are used. <!--#600da28068afd120-->

  - `TestLanguageConfigGlobalMerge.test_project_null_falls_through_to_global` (method) — Asserts an explicit `null` in the project config does not mask a set global value but falls through to it. <!--#8afb1d7a89a4b1f1-->

### `tests/test_llm_caller.py` (python) — Unit test suite for LLMCaller covering the two-phase JSON fast-path/required-keys fallback, forwarding of required_keys and project_root, read-only step enforcement via --disallowedTools, and the force_read_only override that locks a writable step at both the prompt-constraint and runner-tool levels. <!--#79583598d902db82|5129fe005cf50cd5-->

  - `TestCallTwoPhaseRequiredKeys.test_fast_path_with_matching_required_keys` (method) — Asserts that when Phase 1 JSON already contains the required keys, Phase 2 is skipped (only one _call_with_retry). <!--#f0e671f6aedbb0c0-->
  - `TestCallTwoPhaseRequiredKeys.test_fast_path_missing_required_keys_falls_back_to_phase2` (method) — Asserts that valid-but-incomplete Phase 1 JSON triggers a second extraction pass on the same caller's _call_with_retry (two calls), not a separate JSONExtractor LLMCaller. <!--#1d189b9b064ab2f9-->
  - `TestCallTwoPhaseRequiredKeys.test_fast_path_with_none_required_keys` (method) — Asserts backward-compatible behavior: with required_keys=None any valid JSON satisfies the fast path and Phase 2 is skipped. <!--#f13d8be437160bd6-->
- `TestCallPassesRequiredKeys` (class) — Test class verifying call() forwards required_keys into _call_two_phase. <!--#821b322efa876976-->
  - `TestCallPassesRequiredKeys.test_call_passes_required_keys_to_two_phase` (method) — Asserts call() with json_mode='two_phase' passes the required_keys argument through to _call_two_phase. <!--#f891263d91df07f0-->
- `TestCreateRunnerForwardsProjectRoot` (class) — Regression test class ensuring project_root is forwarded so se3.yaml's claude_subprocess.setting_sources reaches the runner. <!--#8911b355a413b103-->
  - `TestCreateRunnerForwardsProjectRoot.test_project_root_forwarded_so_yaml_setting_sources_takes_effect` (method) — Asserts that a project se3.yaml setting setting_sources to [user, project] is reflected on the constructed runner. <!--#6e3e2c997c8f8c38-->
  - `TestCreateRunnerForwardsProjectRoot.test_default_setting_sources_when_no_yaml` (method) — Asserts the runner falls back to the default ['user'] setting_sources when no project YAML is present. <!--#9c9bde4b84d3c47a-->
- `_FakeResult` (class) — Minimal fake runner-result object (success/output/interrupted) stand-in used by _call_with_retry in tests. <!--#e5bad293c6e3a5e1-->

  - `_ArgsCapturingRunner.run_with_monitor` (method) — Records the passed args and returns an empty _FakeResult. <!--#03ab16e216fcd671-->

- `TestForceReadOnlyOverride` (class) — Test suite verifying that `LLMCaller(force_read_only=True)` holds a single LLM sub-call read-only (both prompt-constraint injection and runner tool-lock) on an otherwise-writable step like charter_freshness, without mutating the step's registry read_only. <!--#5d20fe4f364b9d6c-->

  - `TestForceReadOnlyOverride.test_force_read_only_injects_prompt_constraint` (method) — Asserts enforcement point 2: force_read_only=True injects the READ-ONLY STEP CONSTRAINT block into the retry-call prompt. <!--#1e6bc6910662567a-->
  - `TestForceReadOnlyOverride.test_default_no_force_no_prompt_constraint` (method) — Asserts the default force_read_only=False leaves a writable step's prompt free of the READ-ONLY STEP CONSTRAINT block, matching pre-override behavior. <!--#ba119edf9d115fb9-->

### `tests/test_llm_caller_stream_progress_chip.py` (python) — Pytest module verifying StreamJSONTracker's single-chip stream_progress protocol, asserting each tool call emits an in-flight and a terminal chip with correct structured tool_detail payloads (read_text, edit_diff with hunk lines, bash_output, is_error flags), preserves emoji-prefixed CLI stdout, keeps narrative-text jsonl records byte-identical to the legacy schema, and round-trips the new chip fields (tool_use_id, is_error, tool_detail) into the jsonl record. <!--#5bc2a231f430a845|221fa544b849b6f5-->

- `test_read_success_emits_in_flight_and_terminal` (function) — Test asserting a successful Read produces an in-flight chip (no is_error/tool_detail) and a terminal '[Read ✓' chip with a read_text detail payload including file_path, start_line, and text. <!--#0de6e67ca0273f62-->
- `test_edit_success_terminal_has_edit_diff_detail_with_hunk_start` (function) — Test asserting a successful Edit yields an in-flight '[Edit' chip plus a terminal '[Edit ✓' chip carrying an edit_diff detail with parsed hunk start line numbers and a '@@' diff. <!--#3c04faf806769ee2-->
- `test_bash_failure_emits_terminal_with_is_error_true` (function) — Test asserting a failed Bash command produces a terminal '[Bash ✗' chip with is_error True and a bash_output detail echoing the command. <!--#116e96fdb40405e1-->
- `test_cli_stdout_emoji_lines_preserved` (function) — Test verifying the tracker prints emoji-prefixed CLI stdout lines ('🔧 Read:' on start and '✅ Read' on completion) to stdout. <!--#128ea4fd4ce8fdba-->
- `test_narrative_text_progress_jsonl_byte_identical_to_legacy` (function) — Test asserting a narrative-text progress write produces a jsonl record whose key set exactly matches the pre-extension legacy schema with no extra chip keys leaking through. <!--#abcc6d2644f83b03-->
- `test_record_stream_progress_writes_new_chip_fields_when_provided` (function) — Test asserting that when tool_use_id, is_error, and tool_detail are passed, they round-trip into the jsonl record for the daemon reader to forward to the frontend. <!--#8e517db2a718def9-->

### `tests/test_llm_trace_fsync_batching.py` (python) — Unit tests covering two merge-subsystem concerns: that the LLMTrace writer batches/throttles fsync (firing on count/time thresholds, stop/exit, and rotation rather than per-record) while keeping the jsonl stream complete and readable, and that the leaf-merge guard rejects a missing target branch ref diagnosably before ever invoking git merge. <!--#e7bdfb543696079f|7e2a479aae727a88-->
- `fsync_counter` (function) — Pytest fixture that monkeypatches os.fsync in the llm_trace module with a no-op recorder so tests can count when fsync is invoked. <!--#2f60a6b8c6fdac6f-->
- `TestFsyncThrottling` (class) — Test class asserting LLMTrace fsyncs on count/interval thresholds, on stop/rotation, and per-record when disabled, rather than on every write. <!--#9297bb467922118d-->
  - `TestFsyncThrottling.test_no_fsync_under_thresholds` (method) — Asserts no fsync fires while records are written when both the count and time thresholds remain unmet. <!--#8b61fdce063fcfe3-->
  - `TestFsyncThrottling.test_fsync_fires_every_n_records` (method) — Asserts fsync fires exactly once per N records, with the batch counter resetting after each flush. <!--#d3743d17c52837f8-->
  - `TestFsyncThrottling.test_per_record_fsync_when_every_n_nonpositive` (method) — Asserts a non-positive fsync_every_n restores per-record fsync semantics. <!--#1caa0572e1f01e50-->
  - `TestFsyncThrottling.test_stop_forces_tail_fsync` (method) — Asserts stop/__exit__ fsyncs the tail even when the batch threshold was never reached, ensuring trailing records are durable. <!--#a7cdebb1b46dea89-->
  - `TestFsyncThrottling.test_rotation_forces_fsync` (method) — Asserts a file rotation fsyncs and completes the rotated-out file before opening the next one. <!--#bf371111c88e3a1d-->
- `TestRecordsRemainComplete` (class) — Test class verifying every record stays flushed, ordered, and readable even when fsync is throttled away until close. <!--#7d1bf62947363aa6-->
  - `TestRecordsRemainComplete.test_no_tail_loss_with_batched_fsync` (method) — Asserts all 50 records are written in sequence with the tail intact despite fsync being throttled to never fire mid-run. <!--#ee1914f3fb80b1cb-->
  - `TestRecordsRemainComplete.test_records_readable_mid_run_before_fsync` (method) — Asserts a record is readable from the file before any fsync occurs because each line is flushed to the OS page cache. <!--#bb6828f14f0646b6-->
- `_git` (function) — Helper that runs a git subcommand inside a given repo path and returns the completed process. <!--#9bef257c44286ed8-->
- `repo` (function) — Pytest fixture that initializes a fresh git repo with an initial commit on the main branch. <!--#d27143b094612b5a-->
- `TestLeafMergeRefValidation` (class) — Test class verifying the leaf-merge guard fails diagnosably on a missing target ref and proceeds to a clean merge when the ref exists. <!--#59a13e887901aa84-->
  - `TestLeafMergeRefValidation.test_missing_ref_fails_safely` (method) — Asserts a non-existent leaf branch ref returns False with a diagnosable log and no leftover MERGE_HEAD before any merge is attempted. <!--#1ec994f08480c7d3-->
  - `TestLeafMergeRefValidation.test_existing_ref_proceeds_to_merge` (method) — Asserts that when the leaf ref exists the guard passes and a non-conflicting merge succeeds, bringing in the new file. <!--#a8aee8f187e14f3a-->

### `tests/test_merge_committed_issue_collision.py` (python) — Test suite for the git three-way-merge channel of `se3 merge` issue-ID reconciliation, driving `MergeOrchestrator._reconcile_committed_issue_ids` after real merges to verify that when two branches commit different issue files parsing to the same numeric ID, the merge-introduced side is renumbered via the shared G1 primitives (rename, trace, reference rewrite, `.next_id` advance) and landed as a fix-up commit — while covering keeper selection among pre-fork/branch survivors, parsed-id-vs-filename detection, ambiguous multi-candidate references left annotated rather than guessed, byte-identical no-op merges, the LLM-conflict resolution path, non-mapping bodies, and surgical rollback that preserves unrelated drafts and never rewinds the monotonic counter. <!--#d3688ccc4f70afdf|ca17b0a5d3e88e38-->
- `_git` (function) — Thin helper that runs a git subcommand inside a given repo path and returns the completed process, asserting success. <!--#cf40306ebf6a3046-->
- `_init_repo` (function) — Initializes a test git repo whose se3/issues store is tracked while the rest of se3/ runtime (locks, logs) is gitignored, seeded with a README and initial commit. <!--#90ae45c0d23b6e1d-->
- `_head` (function) — Returns the current HEAD commit SHA of the given repo. <!--#3fcb38d33f4242ff-->
- `_parent` (function) — Returns the SHA of the first parent of the given ref. <!--#522753588e085378-->
- `_commits_since` (function) — Counts how many commits are reachable from HEAD but not from the given base ref. <!--#a9bc96d07fa3961e-->
- `_working_tree_clean` (function) — Reports whether the repo's tracked files have no uncommitted changes (ignoring untracked files). <!--#921f3d316e7e9a28-->
- `_write_issue_file` (function) — Writes a minimal valid issue YAML to se3/issues/<status>/<id>_<slug>.yaml and returns its path. <!--#d2ea0d7c7097eb50-->
- `_set_next_id` (function) — Writes the given value into the issue store's .next_id counter file. <!--#2a8eed27ffe5f8a3-->
- `_read_next_id` (function) — Reads and returns the issue store's .next_id counter as an int. <!--#d939226ced0fa0ed-->
- `_open_issue_ids` (function) — Returns the sorted list of numeric IDs parsed from the filenames of all open issue YAMLs. <!--#b3d76787ec4c08a9-->
- `_find_issue_by_slug` (function) — Returns the path of the first issue file matching a given slug under a status directory, or None. <!--#306c989b0dbe9141-->
- `test_committed_id_collision_is_renumbered_and_committed` (function) — Verifies that when two branches each commit a different issue #005, the merge reconciler renumbers the incoming one to the global max+1, rewrites its self-reference and trace, leaves the kept side's references untouched, advances .next_id, and records the change as one fix-up commit plus a report record. <!--#45e2e2f1d54a6351-->
- `test_references_added_to_preexisting_files_follow_the_renumber` (function) — Checks that a #old reference the branch newly added to a pre-existing issue file follows the renumber while the file's original #old stays, and pins that the new number is allocated via the shared .next_id primitive (max(counter, on-disk max+1)) so an ahead-of-store counter of 100 is consumed rather than a bare on-disk max+1. <!--#498aaacdc2a19b3d-->
- `_write_issue_file_with_id` (function) — Test helper that writes an issue YAML whose filename prefix and stored `id` field intentionally differ, returning the file path. <!--#d1b362953f68f1a9-->
- `test_collision_detected_by_parsed_id_not_filename_prefix` (function) — Confirms collisions are detected from each file's parsed `id` field rather than its filename prefix, so two files with mismatched prefixes but the same stored id 007 are recognized as colliding and the incoming one is renumbered past the parsed-id global max. <!--#e1d1f5b2a9319cfe-->
- `test_multiple_incoming_files_sharing_old_id_keep_ambiguous_references` (function) — Verifies that when the merge brings in two distinct files both carrying #005, each #005 token is ambiguous and is left unrewritten with a durable candidate-listing note in each holder and in the report, while both files get fresh IDs and pre-existing branch references stay put. <!--#1336c882af2f01bb-->
- `test_incoming_keeper_keeps_group_ambiguous` (function) — Ensures that when main never had a 005 and the branch commits two colliding 005 files, the lexicographically-first branch file becomes the fallback keeper (retaining 005) yet #005 references stay ambiguous — the kept number appears on the recorded candidate list rather than being read as a single-loser case. <!--#13ffdc0a08949fb4-->
- `test_preexisting_keeper_on_branch_keeps_references_ambiguous` (function) — Checks that a keeper inherited from before the fork, colliding with a branch-added 005, makes the branch's #005 references ambiguous — tokens keep their digits with a durable note listing the keeper's kept number as a candidate rather than being repointed to the single renumbered loser. <!--#14ce661ccd816c74-->
- `test_ambiguous_incoming_reference_is_recorded_not_guessed` (function) — Verifies that a merge-added reference to a shared old id (with two colliding candidate files) is annotated with a durable ambiguity note and surfaced in the report for every affected holder rather than being guessed and repointed to either candidate. <!--#05d7b17ef80e2a8a-->
- `test_identical_issue_same_path_is_not_renumbered` (function) — Integration test that when both branches commit byte-identical issue #005 (which git folds into one file), reconciliation detects no collision and leaves the tree, counter, and commit history untouched. <!--#d1d6dfe4010775bd-->
- `test_llm_resolved_conflict_merge_still_reconciles_issue_ids` (function) — Confirms that the LLM-resolved conflict commit path in `_apply_resolution` runs the same committed-issue reconciliation as the clean-merge path, so an issue-ID collision is still renumbered when the merge conflicts on some other file. <!--#76985b506006ce78-->
- `test_non_mapping_colliding_file_is_still_renumbered` (function) — Verifies that a colliding file whose body isn't a YAML mapping is still renamed to restore uniqueness (body left byte-identical), with the skipped in-file rewrite surfaced as a WARNING log and a normal report record. <!--#4323604f79a5d916-->
- `test_keeper_chosen_among_preexisting_survivors` (function) — Ensures that with several pre-merge survivors sharing an ID, the keeper is chosen among the current branch's pre-merge copies (not by min() over all paths), so a lexicographically-smaller merge-introduced file is renumbered rather than keeping the ID. <!--#4f2f2be0c0251ced-->
- `test_reconcile_rollback_preserves_unrelated_uncommitted_issues` (function) — Checks that when the renumber fix-up commit fails, the rollback is surgical — undoing only what the reconcile wrote and fully restoring the loser — while unrelated pre-existing untracked draft issue YAMLs survive intact. <!--#39e754c5582fadb0-->
- `test_reconcile_rollback_never_pulls_next_id_backwards` (function) — Verifies that a failed fix-up commit rolls back the reconcile's file changes without pulling the tracked, strictly-monotonic .next_id counter backwards past a concurrent reservation. <!--#9e4625c2391eb97c-->
- `test_untracked_draft_reference_to_keeper_is_not_corrupted` (function) — Confirms that authorship is read from the git trees (not the dirty working directory), so a main-side untracked draft referencing the keeper's #005 is neither repointed nor swept into the renumber commit while the collision is still repaired. <!--#a448580bfae8ba58-->
- `test_untracked_draft_sharing_id_is_not_a_collision_loser` (function) — Ensures detection is restricted to files tracked at the merge commit, so an untracked draft sharing a number with a merged committed issue is not treated as a collision loser and survives untouched. <!--#d99734cf15b15258-->
- `test_dirty_tracked_id_edit_does_not_fabricate_a_collision` (function) — Verifies that collision detection reads ids from the committed merge tree rather than the dirty working tree, so an uncommitted `id` edit to a tracked file does not fabricate a phantom collision or trigger a renumber and fix-up commit. <!--#8cf5b03a27ee7b06-->
- `_default_branch` (function) — Returns the name of the currently checked-out branch of the given repo. <!--#32a8fa10d61d713c-->

### `tests/test_merge_guardrails.py` (python) — Pytest suite for merge spec guardrails, covering the `check_spec_diff` pure function (detecting requirement weakenings like SHALL→SHOULD, quantifier reductions, and WHEN-clause deletions), `MergeGuardrailsCheck` against real git refs, and orchestrator integration ensuring violations trigger rollback/HUMAN_CALL across default/strict/fast strategies. <!--#fbd6402bcc1bda56|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `tests/test_merge_issue_renumber.py` (python) — Pytest suite exercising cross-worktree issue merging and ID renumbering (IssueManager.adopt_issue and merge_worktree_issues), covering collision-free renumbering, content dedup/idempotency, monotonic .next_id allocation, reference rewriting, retired-number and ambiguous-shared-ID handling, and trace-based recognition on re-run. <!--#5dbbba3cb2abe607|129784483d5dc394-->

- `test_adopt_retired_number_rewrites_store_wide_references` (function) — Verifies that adopting an incoming issue whose old ID is owned by no kept main issue retires that number and repoints existing store-wide `#<old>` references to the new ID. <!--#4aabc45d3057f186-->

- `test_batch_retired_number_rewrites_preexisting_store_reference` (function) — Verifies the batch `merge_worktree_issues` path matches single-shot adopt: an uncollided old number is retired and a pre-existing dependent `#<old>` reference is repointed store-wide. <!--#c4078a5620a19ccd-->
- `test_batch_collision_leaves_kept_owner_reference_scoped` (function) — Verifies that when the incoming number is still owned by a kept main issue, the batch rewrite stays scoped to the adopted file and the dependent `#<old>` keeps pointing at the kept owner. <!--#45f35c15c07ac3af-->
- `test_colliding_old_ids_in_source_leave_own_references_ambiguous` (function) — Verifies that two source issues sharing one old ID are adopted under distinct new IDs with their ambiguous `#<old>` tokens left un-rewritten and a durable ambiguity note recorded in each. <!--#1e11419413f8b316-->

- `test_runtime_sync_ambiguity_surfaced_via_out_param` (function) — Verifies the runtime-sync channel surfaces ambiguous `#old` references to the caller via an `ambiguous_refs_out` list of `{file, old_id, candidates}` entries per affected repo-relative file. <!--#3eba7fabe802908f-->

- `test_issue_differing_only_by_reference_is_not_lost` (function) — Verifies dedup does not collapse two issues that differ only by their referenced number, adopting the genuinely-different worktree issue under a fresh ID. <!--#b10fb269ddbe9583-->
