- `test_adopted_copy_keeping_its_number_still_dedups_on_rerun` (function) — Verifies a same-numbered adopted copy (no trace) whose reference was rewritten by a batch-mate's renumber still dedups on re-run via the batch-mate's worktree-vouched trace. <!--#48c702ff1299c0e4-->
- `test_next_id_matches_max_after_renumber` (function) — Verifies adopt_issue self-heals a lagging or garbage .next_id counter to on-disk max ID + 1 and repoints the adopted issue's forced-collision self-reference to its new ID. <!--#1e869dec0f926363-->
- `test_stale_lagging_counter_cannot_mint_duplicate_id` (function) — Verifies the ID allocator reconciles against the on-disk store before choosing so a stale lagging `.next_id` never mints two files sharing one ID. <!--#8afbe6361ac14c3b-->

### `tests/test_merge_llm_editor_resolver.py` (python) — Regression test suite for the merge package's LLM-as-editor batch conflict resolver, using scripted stub editors (via monkeypatch, no real Claude subprocess) to verify fast-mode single- and multi-file convergence, iteration-exhaustion failure without human escalation, and the excision of the legacy take-theirs fallback path. <!--#f94cc94221f32718|9b176f805e0d442b-->

- `test_fast_multi_file_multi_round_convergence` (function) — Test that fast mode batched over multiple conflicting files converges across successive rounds, recording markers_remaining history for incomplete rounds. <!--#f70fe2a772b9535e-->
- `test_fast_exhausts_iterations_fails_without_human_call` (function) — Test that fast mode failing to converge within max iterations yields a REJECT with reason 'fast_failed' and no human-call escalation. <!--#79fd646b8faadcf4-->

- `test_replay_resolves_via_llm_without_take_theirs` (function) — Test that a previously take-theirs-prone scenario now resolves cleanly via the LLM editor loop on a second round with no take-theirs side effect. <!--#b57f8d064aee8085-->
- `test_synthesis_osfailure_does_not_synthesise_deletion` (function) — Regression test ensuring that an OSError during read-back of a resolved file flags it for human review instead of synthesizing an empty content delete request. <!--#09d66e50a6e833ef-->

### `tests/test_merge_orchestrator.py` (python) — Tests for MergeOrchestrator's sequential branch-merge logic — building throwaway git repos/worktrees with helper functions to verify merge reports, version-intent probing and aggregation, pyproject version bumps, and failure handling. <!--#4cda647c89c94c33|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `tests/test_merge_orchestrator_fast.py` (python) — Focused unit tests for MergeOrchestrator's fast-mode guardrail repair loop, using real git repos for SHA/HEAD management but mocking the repairer and guardrail check to exercise stall, exhaustion, success, side-effect clearance, topology/incomplete short-circuits, missing-SHA errors, rollback failures, and call-file-write failures across both `_run_guardrails` and end-to-end `execute()` escalation paths. <!--#eff902ad2872753f|1bc35259898e1300-->
- `_git` (function) — Helper that runs a `git -C <path>` subprocess command and returns the completed process with captured output. <!--#8dcfd7712386df15-->
- `_init_repo` (function) — Helper that initializes a git repo at the given path and sets a test user name and email. <!--#63bfb3f5ba420316-->

- `TestRunGuardrailsFastRepairLoop` (class) — Test class covering the `_run_guardrails` fast-strategy repair loop behavior (stall, exhaustion, success, rollback, short-circuit) with mocked dependencies. <!--#9fbfe5d311c567a3-->
  - `TestRunGuardrailsFastRepairLoop.test_repair_stalled_same_hash_twice_raises_with_call_file` (method) — Verifies that repeated identical violations cause a GuardrailRepairStalled at iteration 1 with a written call file preserving evidence and a rollback to pre-merge HEAD. <!--#fcc876657dab2337-->
  - `TestRunGuardrailsFastRepairLoop.test_repair_exhausted_max_iterations_raises_with_call_file` (method) — Verifies that ever-changing violation hashes exhaust max iterations, raising with GUARDRAIL_REPAIR_EXHAUSTED, a call file, and rollback to pre-merge HEAD. <!--#31d37e27c78cc294-->
  - `TestRunGuardrailsFastRepairLoop.test_repair_hash_changes_then_exhausts_max_iterations` (method) — Verifies that oscillating (alternating) violation hashes are not detected as a stall within max iterations and instead exhaust, raising GuardrailRepairExhausted. <!--#0d5a80d2058d9290-->
  - `TestRunGuardrailsFastRepairLoop.test_repair_succeeds_at_second_iteration_returns_none` (method) — Verifies that a repair which fails on iteration 1 but succeeds on iteration 2 clears violations and makes `_run_guardrails` return None. <!--#465ae50474ad1bb1-->
  - `TestRunGuardrailsFastRepairLoop.test_repair_failure_but_violations_cleared_by_side_effect` (method) — Verifies that when the repairer reports failure but the re-check passes, `_run_guardrails` accepts the side-effect clearance and returns None. <!--#8785f53151d2bc47-->
  - `TestRunGuardrailsFastRepairLoop.test_repair_stalled_rollback_fails_raises_rollback_error_with_call_file` (method) — Verifies that on a stall where rollback fails, a GuardrailRollbackError is raised while still writing the stalled-type call file. <!--#99aef5786724b50c-->
  - `TestRunGuardrailsFastRepairLoop.test_repair_exhausted_rollback_fails_raises_rollback_error_with_call_file` (method) — Verifies that on exhaustion where rollback fails, a GuardrailRollbackError is raised while still writing the exhausted-type call file. <!--#a0cab1d96e279bb7-->
  - `TestRunGuardrailsFastRepairLoop.test_repair_exhausted_is_exactly_guardrail_repair_exhausted_type` (method) — Verifies the for...else exhaustion path raises the exact GuardrailRepairExhausted subclass (guarding against a stray `break` skipping the else clause). <!--#86388468e479beec-->
  - `TestRunGuardrailsFastRepairLoop.test_topology_violation_fast_short_circuits_to_human_call` (method) — Verifies that CHECK_FAILURE topology violations in fast mode skip the LLM repairer and route directly to rollback plus a human-call file path. <!--#bab72bd91cec0d4f-->
  - `TestRunGuardrailsFastRepairLoop.test_incomplete_short_circuits_for_default_strategy` (method) — Verifies that a CHECK_INCOMPLETE report under the default/safe strategy skips LLM repair and routes to rollback plus a human-call file path. <!--#a04856757f2e499e-->
- `TestExecuteFastStalledEscalation` (class) — Test class covering end-to-end `execute()` routing in fast mode for stall, exhaustion, success, missing-SHA, call-file-write failure, and rollback-failure outcomes. <!--#db4554ef1b9eaff3-->
  - `TestExecuteFastStalledEscalation.test_execute_fast_stalled_sets_pending_human_and_call_file` (method) — Verifies that a stalled fast-mode repair through `execute()` yields a failed report with pending_human, a stalled-type call file, and restored HEAD. <!--#2667308f0d24c8e1-->
  - `TestExecuteFastStalledEscalation.test_execute_fast_hash_changes_exhausts_to_human_call` (method) — Verifies that oscillating hashes through `execute()` exhaust max iterations and escalate to a human call with failure_reason 'guardrail_repair_exhausted'. <!--#723dd63491ef21d4-->
  - `TestExecuteFastStalledEscalation.test_missing_post_sha_fast_raises_guardrail_repair_failed` (method) — Verifies that a missing post_sha in fast mode raises GuardrailRepairFailed with GUARDRAIL_MISSING_POST_SHA and leaves HEAD unchanged. <!--#8355e5a8d2d6e39a-->
  - `TestExecuteFastStalledEscalation.test_missing_pre_sha_fast_raises_guardrail_repair_failed` (method) — Verifies that a missing pre_sha in fast mode raises GuardrailRepairFailed with GUARDRAIL_MISSING_PRE_SHA and attempts no rollback. <!--#3db656da78abcb3a-->
  - `TestExecuteFastStalledEscalation.test_missing_both_shas_fast_raises_guardrail_repair_failed` (method) — Verifies that both SHAs missing in fast mode raises GuardrailRepairFailed with GUARDRAIL_MISSING_PRE_AND_POST_SHA. <!--#dd55c219cecc9a2a-->
  - `TestExecuteFastStalledEscalation.test_execute_fast_repair_success_no_violation` (method) — Verifies that a successful fast-mode repair through `execute()` produces a successful report listing the merged branch with no pending human call and an advanced HEAD. <!--#9a145eaf97f1a543-->
  - `TestExecuteFastStalledEscalation.test_execute_fast_stalled_call_file_write_fails_aborts` (method) — Verifies that when a stalled repair's call-file write fails, `execute()` aborts with 'guardrail_repair_stalled_call_failed', no human call, and restored HEAD. <!--#108acb34bea19807-->
  - `TestExecuteFastStalledEscalation.test_execute_fast_stalled_call_file_keyboard_interrupt_propagates` (method) — Verifies that a KeyboardInterrupt during stalled call-file write propagates uncaught while the working tree is already rolled back. <!--#cb2a7c7c5fcf6bbb-->
  - `TestExecuteFastStalledEscalation.test_execute_fast_max_iterations_exhausted_escalates_to_human` (method) — Verifies that novel-hash exhaustion through `execute()` escalates to a human call (not an outright abort) with an exhausted-type call file and restored HEAD. <!--#82d2e7c76a467c93-->
  - `TestExecuteFastStalledEscalation.test_execute_fast_exhausted_call_file_write_fails_aborts` (method) — Verifies that when an exhausted repair's call-file write fails, `execute()` aborts with 'guardrail_repair_exhausted_call_failed', no human call, and restored HEAD. <!--#a288838286a9b23f-->
  - `TestExecuteFastStalledEscalation.test_execute_fast_stalled_rollback_fails_sets_rollback_failed` (method) — Verifies that a stalled repair whose rollback fails sets rollback_failed with failure_reason 'rollback_failed' while still surfacing a diagnostic human-call file. <!--#3ba4dea300241941-->
  - `TestExecuteFastStalledEscalation.test_execute_fast_exhausted_rollback_fails_sets_rollback_failed` (method) — Verifies that an exhausted repair whose rollback fails sets rollback_failed with failure_reason 'rollback_failed' while still surfacing a diagnostic exhausted-type call file. <!--#8194aded3f64561f-->
- `TestMaxRepairIterationsClamp` (class) — Regression test class pinning the orchestrator's defense-in-depth clamp of `_max_repair_iterations` to at least one so the repair for-loop body always runs. <!--#78b60e43e42258bf-->
  - `TestMaxRepairIterationsClamp.test_orchestrator_clamps_loader_returning_zero` (method) — Verifies the orchestrator re-clamps a loader-returned 0 up to the positive module default for `_max_repair_iterations`. <!--#10a3e595f88621bb-->
  - `TestMaxRepairIterationsClamp.test_orchestrator_clamps_loader_returning_negative` (method) — Verifies the orchestrator clamps a negative loader value to at least one for `_max_repair_iterations`. <!--#c2d2d4f8b82656c4-->
  - `TestMaxRepairIterationsClamp.test_orchestrator_preserves_loader_returning_positive` (method) — Verifies the orchestrator preserves a positive loader value (7) verbatim, applying the clamp only to non-positive values. <!--#c1181171a5547b19-->

### `tests/test_merge_stash_concurrent_repro.py` (python) — End-to-end and unit regression suite proving that both merge call sites (the `se3 merge` fast path and the DAG implement leaf-back merge) route through the shared archive-first stash-pop recovery so concurrent untracked files colliding on stash-pop are preserved in `se3/worktrees/.archive` with an audit issue pointing at them, and that an incomplete/unresolved recovery is surfaced as a merge failure. <!--#14737e646a31b3d3|a0d88f20dbe88a0c-->
- `_git` (function) — Thin helper that runs a git subcommand inside a given repo directory and returns the completed process with captured output. <!--#9bef257c44286ed8-->
- `_init_repo` (function) — Initializes a fresh git repo with test identity and a .gitignore that ignores only the worktree archive sink (keeping concurrent se3/issues artefacts untracked), then returns the default branch name. <!--#d8e7e72f6c928779-->
- `_archived_files` (function) — Walks the archive directory and returns a mapping of each archived file's run-relative path to its recovered content across all archive runs. <!--#afa7fb9228491f88-->
- `_open_issue_texts` (function) — Reads and returns the text of every open audit issue YAML under se3/issues/open in the given repo. <!--#5bd76b6b31f84ec1-->
- `test_fast_merge_path_archives_concurrent_untracked` (function) — End-to-end test asserting the fast `se3 merge` path archives (rather than destroys) concurrent untracked files that collide on stash-pop and files an audit issue pointing at the archive with a blob sha. <!--#1ef243d832fb926b-->
- `test_fast_stash_pop_unit_archives_and_audits` (function) — Unit test driving `_fast_stash_pop` directly to confirm a colliding stashed untracked file is archived while the merged-tree version is preserved and a recovery audit message is recorded. <!--#3e941fbccc2ba600-->
- `test_leaf_merge_path_archives_concurrent_untracked` (function) — End-to-end test verifying the implement leaf-back merge path enforces the same archive-and-audit invariants as the fast path for concurrent untracked collisions. <!--#b11ac0355130c84a-->
- `_incomplete_outcome` (function) — Test fixture building a `StashPopOutcome` representing a case-a recovery that archived both sides but left the index unmerged (archive_failed with unresolved files). <!--#504f64f90546a256-->
- `_stash_with_collision` (function) — Helper that stashes an untracked file then repopulates its path so a subsequent pop is non-clean, returning the stash label to drive recovery over. <!--#dba309ca457bfd4f-->
- `test_fast_stash_pop_signals_incomplete_when_unresolved` (function) — Test patching the resolver to return an incomplete outcome and asserting `_fast_stash_pop` signals non-finalized recovery (returns True) while still recording archive manifest pointers in the audit issue. <!--#c43d3b0a1f805665-->
- `test_run_merge_fast_reports_failure_on_incomplete_stashpop` (function) — Test that the fast `run_merge` path returns a non-zero exit when post-merge stash-pop recovery does not finalize, even though the underlying branch merge succeeded and landed. <!--#2ccb3f62fab51eff-->
- `test_leaf_merge_reports_failure_on_incomplete_stashpop` (function) — Test that the leaf-back merge path returns False (failure) on an incomplete stash-pop recovery so DAG status reflects the unreconciled repo, while confirming the leaf commit still landed and the audit issue carries the manifest pointers. <!--#280a131f29885ef0-->

### `tests/test_merge_strategy_alignment.py` (python) — Test module verifying merge strategy alignment: the fast strategy converges to ACCEPT/REJECT (never HUMAN_CALL), the strict strategy acts as an orchestrator-short-circuited placeholder, and the default/safe strategy remains unchanged. <!--#8f263a60703bd704|8b6b5d995543368a-->
- `_make_resolution` (function) — Test helper that builds a mock LLMResolution with one file/hunk, parameterizing confidence levels, review/guardrail flags, and spec status. <!--#3ac59ed3ebce187f-->
- `TestFastStrategyAcceptOrRejectOnly` (class) — Test class asserting the fast merge strategy never returns HUMAN_CALL, only ACCEPT or REJECT. <!--#382e40374e7076df-->
  - `TestFastStrategyAcceptOrRejectOnly.test_fast_never_returns_human_call_across_various_inputs` (method) — Property test sweeping many confidence/flag/spec combinations to confirm fast mode never emits HUMAN_CALL. <!--#d213267c53583f2c-->
  - `TestFastStrategyAcceptOrRejectOnly.test_fast_regular_low_confidence_accept` (method) — Asserts low confidence on a regular (non-spec) file in fast mode resolves to ACCEPT. <!--#e8511e820cbe33fe-->
  - `TestFastStrategyAcceptOrRejectOnly.test_fast_regular_medium_confidence_accept` (method) — Asserts medium confidence on a regular file in fast mode resolves to ACCEPT. <!--#0a291211f553964c-->
  - `TestFastStrategyAcceptOrRejectOnly.test_fast_regular_requires_human_review_accept` (method) — Asserts a per-file requires_human_review flag on a non-spec file is ignored in fast mode, yielding ACCEPT. <!--#9d985b1a397275fd-->
  - `TestFastStrategyAcceptOrRejectOnly.test_fast_global_requires_human_review_reject` (method) — Asserts a global requires_human_review flag in fast mode forces REJECT with an abort/no-human-call reason. <!--#027b88c33979b200-->
  - `TestFastStrategyAcceptOrRejectOnly.test_fast_spec_guardrail_concern_deferred_accept` (method) — Asserts a spec_guardrail_concern on a high-confidence spec file is deferred to post-merge and still ACCEPTs. <!--#6f33043a74ff6d76-->
  - `TestFastStrategyAcceptOrRejectOnly.test_fast_spec_low_confidence_reject` (method) — Asserts low confidence on a spec file in fast mode forces REJECT. <!--#5955d29c45c81787-->
  - `TestFastStrategyAcceptOrRejectOnly.test_fast_spec_medium_confidence_reject` (method) — Asserts medium confidence on a spec file in fast mode forces REJECT. <!--#f2966310543ec4eb-->
  - `TestFastStrategyAcceptOrRejectOnly.test_fast_spec_requires_human_review_reject` (method) — Asserts a requires_human_review flag on a spec file in fast mode forces REJECT. <!--#12e50930d4ee69c6-->
  - `TestFastStrategyAcceptOrRejectOnly.test_fast_spec_per_file_requires_human_review_reject` (method) — Asserts the safety-critical path where a per-file (not global) requires_human_review on a spec file still triggers REJECT in fast mode. <!--#209df2667d22ab0a-->
  - `TestFastStrategyAcceptOrRejectOnly.test_fast_mixed_regular_and_spec_accept` (method) — Asserts a mix of a low-confidence regular file and a high-confidence spec file in fast mode resolves to ACCEPT. <!--#7472813e82a8d7cd-->
  - `TestFastStrategyAcceptOrRejectOnly.test_fast_mixed_regular_and_spec_low_spec_reject` (method) — Asserts a mix where the spec file has low confidence in fast mode resolves to REJECT regardless of the regular file. <!--#399e996659f8ed0b-->
- `TestStrictStrategyPlaceholder` (class) — Test class covering the strict strategy as a documented fallback that the orchestrator short-circuits. <!--#0b0eb06f2f5e08a2-->
  - `TestStrictStrategyPlaceholder.test_strict_docstring_mentions_orchestrator_short_circuit` (method) — Asserts the _decide_strict docstring documents that the orchestrator short-circuits/placeholders strict handling. <!--#dc43bd68fc8717e5-->
  - `TestStrictStrategyPlaceholder.test_strict_fallback_all_high_accept` (method) — Asserts the strict fallback path ACCEPTs when all confidence is high and no flags are set. <!--#51510bd60deef7a4-->
  - `TestStrictStrategyPlaceholder.test_strict_fallback_low_hunk_human_call` (method) — Asserts the strict fallback path returns HUMAN_CALL (not REJECT) for low hunk confidence. <!--#7b02b9feddf86834-->
  - `TestStrictStrategyPlaceholder.test_strict_fallback_spec_guardrail_human_call` (method) — Asserts the strict fallback path returns HUMAN_CALL when a spec_guardrail_concern is present. <!--#776949c4f58f37aa-->
- `TestDefaultStrategyUnchanged` (class) — Test class confirming the safe/default strategy's behavior is unaffected by the strategy-alignment work. <!--#08bb9aba259b49b6-->
  - `TestDefaultStrategyUnchanged.test_default_high_confidence_accept` (method) — Asserts the safe strategy ACCEPTs a high-confidence resolution. <!--#019150bf7c2cdc64-->
  - `TestDefaultStrategyUnchanged.test_default_low_overall_accepted_without_flags` (method) — Asserts the safe strategy ACCEPTs a low-confidence resolution that carries no review/guardrail flags (confidence is informational). <!--#878de34dd82a63d0-->
  - `TestDefaultStrategyUnchanged.test_default_spec_guardrail_human_call` (method) — Asserts the safe strategy returns HUMAN_CALL when a spec_guardrail_concern flag is set. <!--#87fecb1d8374289d-->
  - `TestDefaultStrategyUnchanged.test_default_requires_human_review_human_call` (method) — Asserts the safe strategy returns HUMAN_CALL when the requires_human_review flag is set. <!--#b5719dbf3e376870-->

### `tests/test_merge_strategy_consolidation.py` (python) — Regression test suite for the merge-strategy consolidation (G7): it uses git/repo and ConflictFile/BatchContext helpers to verify safe mode escalates to a human MCP call after exhausting resolve iterations, strict mode routes conflicts straight to a human without invoking the LLM, the CLI and run_merge default to the 'fast' strategy, and the legacy 'robust'/'default' strategy names are rejected fail-fast both at MergeStrategy.from_str and the CLI. <!--#b15ceb8b07bf34a9|dc1e0c223b3b838a-->
- `_git` (function) — Helper that runs a `git -C <path>` subprocess and returns the completed process with captured text output. <!--#8dcfd7712386df15-->
- `_init_repo` (function) — Helper that initializes a git repo at a path and sets a test user name/email. <!--#63bfb3f5ba420316-->
- `_write_with_markers` (function) — Helper that writes a file containing standard git conflict markers around the given ours/theirs content. <!--#689f68a75494ff1a-->
- `_make_conflict_file` (function) — Helper that builds a non-spec, non-binary ConflictFile fixture from a relative path and working content. <!--#1c3246491dbdea01-->
- `_make_batch_context` (function) — Helper that constructs a BatchContext fixture with placeholder branch/SHA metadata and the given merge strategy. <!--#9f17bf5e6eea3620-->
- `test_safe_exhausts_iterations_escalates_to_human` (function) — Verifies that safe mode, when the LLM never clears markers, escalates to a human call after exhausting iterations while preserving conflict markers on disk. <!--#1d6e43bbb56f484b-->
- `test_strict_skips_llm_and_routes_to_human` (function) — Verifies that strict mode routes conflicts directly to a human call without ever invoking the LLM (zero iterations). <!--#19198f079fd16273-->
- `test_run_merge_default_strategy_is_fast` (function) — Asserts via signature introspection that `run_merge`'s strategy parameter defaults to 'fast'. <!--#a452d805ed6157fd-->
- `test_cli_merge_defaults_to_fast` (function) — Test verifying that invoking `se3 merge feature` without an explicit `--strategy` flag resolves the strategy to 'fast' when calling `run_merge`, by stubbing `run_merge` in a CLI runner and asserting on the captured argument. <!--#3150bd00a9f520cb-->
- `test_legacy_robust_strategy_name_rejected` (function) — Asserts that `MergeStrategy.from_str('robust')` raises ValueError mentioning the legacy name and the 'fast' replacement. <!--#c4b9add2aba39870-->
- `test_legacy_default_strategy_name_rejected` (function) — Asserts that `MergeStrategy.from_str('default')` raises ValueError mentioning the legacy name and the 'safe' replacement. <!--#8cef9c1bf92e2003-->
- `test_cli_rejects_robust_strategy` (function) — CLI test confirming `--strategy robust` fails fast with a non-zero exit and never invokes run_merge. <!--#1973cd073c1ba355-->
- `test_cli_rejects_default_strategy` (function) — CLI test confirming `--strategy default` fails fast with a non-zero exit and never invokes run_merge. <!--#821ebd3e1ef21f88-->

### `tests/test_merge_unlock.py` (python) — Unit and CLI-level tests for the merge-lock subsystem, covering read-only lock inspection (`inspect_lock`), lock file breaking/releasing across missing/stale/dead-PID/corrupt/live-holder states with and without `--force`, unlink-failure handling, and the `se3 merge-unlock` command's reporting and exit codes. <!--#9842c412b9f52ed2|c4bcaa327c7c11d4-->
- `_lock_path` (function) — Helper returning the absolute merge-lock file path (`se3/state/merge.lock`) under a given project root. <!--#db4c4674fe3e9a27-->
- `_write_lock` (function) — Helper that creates the lock file with the given body content and returns its path. <!--#4a20343d55e0ce24-->
- `_dead_pid` (function) — Helper that scans downward from a large number to find a PID confirmed non-existent via `os.kill(pid, 0)` raising ESRCH. <!--#fde38f4d452aeeab-->
- `test_inspect_lock_missing_file` (function) — Asserts `inspect_lock` reports a missing lock as non-existent, holderless, and reclaimable (stale). <!--#8a000da44494f371-->
- `test_inspect_lock_alive_holder` (function) — Asserts `inspect_lock` recognizes a lock held by the live current process as alive and not stale. <!--#06604a0f76c53a6c-->
- `test_inspect_lock_dead_holder` (function) — Asserts `inspect_lock` treats a lock owned by a dead PID as not-alive and stale. <!--#3ea9cee0acd1c667-->
- `test_inspect_lock_empty_file_is_stale` (function) — Asserts an empty lock file is reported as existing but holderless and stale. <!--#9ceaee7d60ac0c2e-->
- `test_inspect_lock_corrupt_record` (function) — Asserts a non-numeric lock body is reported as corrupt, holderless, and stale. <!--#145a85cf4fabd8fd-->
- `test_inspect_lock_does_not_write` (function) — Asserts `inspect_lock` is read-only by verifying the lock file bytes are unchanged after inspection. <!--#f6c84c8238682557-->
- `test_break_lock_file_removes_existing` (function) — Asserts `break_lock_file` deletes an existing lock and returns True. <!--#774a993f5bfb8c9c-->
- `test_break_lock_file_noop_when_absent` (function) — Asserts `break_lock_file` returns False and is a no-op when no lock exists. <!--#0fffa971484c7f9c-->
- `test_release_no_lock` (function) — Asserts `release_merge_lock` returns the `no_lock` outcome with exit code 0 when no lock is present. <!--#da7f3c75b57e39e8-->
- `test_release_stale_dead_pid` (function) — Asserts a stale lock held by a dead PID is released (`released_stale`) without requiring `--force`. <!--#b7dc02044944394d-->
- `test_release_stale_no_pid` (function) — Asserts an empty (holderless) lock is released as stale without force. <!--#b6ad97ef2781937f-->
- `test_release_stale_corrupt` (function) — Asserts a corrupt lock record is released as stale, with the outcome flagging corruption. <!--#795092016b95b8d9-->
- `test_release_refused_when_alive_without_force` (function) — Asserts release is refused (`refused_alive`, nonzero exit, lock preserved) when a live process holds the lock and `--force` is absent. <!--#ecaf17f195d49934-->
- `test_release_force_removes_live_lock` (function) — Asserts `--force` releases a lock held by a live process, yielding `released_force` and removing the file. <!--#219aa438c6f6b448-->
- `_make_unremovable` (function) — Helper that strips write permission from the lock's parent directory so unlinking the file raises PermissionError. <!--#ff724d541bbdd637-->
- `_restore` (function) — Helper that restores normal (0o700) permissions on the lock's parent directory after an unremovable-file test. <!--#b369467d8e93b67e-->
- `test_release_stale_failed_remove_when_unlink_denied` (function) — Asserts a stale lock that cannot be unlinked yields `failed_remove`, nonzero exit, and the file remaining on disk. <!--#0d36005306b6a72c-->
- `test_release_force_failed_remove_when_unlink_denied` (function) — Asserts a forced release whose unlink is denied yields `failed_remove`, nonzero exit, and the file remaining. <!--#5840a05f6d4c480b-->
- `cli_project` (function) — Fixture that monkeypatches `get_project_root` to point the CLI at `tmp_path`. <!--#cb249ba1ae611144-->
- `_run` (function) — Helper that invokes the `se3` Typer app with given args via CliRunner and returns the result. <!--#23b50511ac6e6535-->
- `_flat` (function) — Helper that collapses rich-rendered newlines and spaces so output can be substring-matched. <!--#3f2ff121b29cf474-->
- `test_cli_no_lock_reports_and_exits_zero` (function) — Asserts the CLI reports no lock to release and exits 0 when none exists. <!--#4ba317c686c41159-->
- `test_cli_refuses_live_holder` (function) — Asserts the CLI refuses (nonzero exit) a live-held lock, printing the holder PID and a `--force` hint while preserving the file. <!--#f007af9f69db8fe7-->
- `test_cli_force_flag_releases_live_holder` (function) — Asserts `merge-unlock --force` releases a live-held lock, prints a WARNING, and removes the file. <!--#8dd64165bd391644-->
- `test_cli_short_force_flag` (function) — Asserts the short `-f` flag behaves like `--force` in releasing a live-held lock. <!--#b8716ef7108d0ab2-->
- `test_cli_stale_cleanup_without_force` (function) — Asserts the CLI cleans up a stale (dead-PID) lock without force, reporting "Released stale" and exiting 0. <!--#3a6792b68e9bccc2-->
- `test_cli_failed_remove_reports_error_and_nonzero` (function) — Asserts that when a stale lock cannot be unlinked, the CLI reports an ERROR, exits nonzero, and does not falsely claim the lock was released. <!--#f576f5430fb87325-->

### `tests/test_merge_version_aggregator.py` (python) — Unit tests for the merge orchestrator's SemVer version aggregator, covering max_bump selection, per-diff bump classification (including prerelease/build-metadata precedence rules), end-to-end branch bump inference from pyproject version diffs, and aggregate_and_apply's writing/committing/amending of the new version with rollback on failure, plus git-repo test helpers. <!--#c25334796f6868e7|9025a32a8658039c-->
- `_get_default_branch` (function) — Helper returning the current/default branch name of a git repo via `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD`. <!--#4ba6e6e14ec77ffd-->
- `_init_repo` (function) — Helper that initializes a fresh git repo with test user config and an initial committed README. <!--#1635ad85954c81ae-->
- `_write_pyproject` (function) — Helper that writes a minimal pyproject.toml with the given project version. <!--#983218c378021696-->
- `_commit` (function) — Helper that stages given files (or all) and creates a commit with the supplied message. <!--#71a622e2cf694e9f-->
- `_checkout` (function) — Helper that checks out (optionally creating) a named git branch. <!--#b220fe75daeda1ff-->
- `_read_pyproject_version` (function) — Helper that reads the project version from the working-tree pyproject.toml via regex. <!--#62776360bd464010-->
- `_last_commit_files` (function) — Helper returning the list of files modified in the HEAD commit. <!--#8813dffb71f598b7-->
- `TestMaxBump` (class) — Test class verifying max_bump selects the highest bump level (defaulting to PATCH on empty input). <!--#bbde82e5b6be0dd9-->
  - `TestMaxBump.test_empty_list_returns_patch` (method) — Asserts max_bump of an empty list returns PATCH. <!--#2c6dd3fd43dc1606-->
  - `TestMaxBump.test_single_patch` (method) — Asserts max_bump of a single PATCH returns PATCH. <!--#fe4d3cd4ebfb5e31-->
  - `TestMaxBump.test_patch_plus_patch_plus_minor_returns_minor` (method) — Asserts max_bump of patch+patch+minor returns MINOR. <!--#631d31612562453e-->
  - `TestMaxBump.test_minor_plus_major_returns_major` (method) — Asserts max_bump of minor+major returns MAJOR. <!--#3ff3f9590e1de749-->
  - `TestMaxBump.test_any_with_major_returns_major` (method) — Asserts any bump set containing MAJOR returns MAJOR. <!--#26e49ed0ef7bd477-->
  - `TestMaxBump.test_only_minor` (method) — Asserts max_bump of only MINOR values returns MINOR. <!--#2802fe8d734cbcd8-->
- `TestDiffBump` (class) — Test class for _diff_bump, covering numeric bumps plus SemVer prerelease and build-metadata precedence rules. <!--#7f02399aa7a8ffcb-->
  - `TestDiffBump.test_major` (method) — Asserts a major-version increase yields BumpType.MAJOR. <!--#139663295ba61d03-->
  - `TestDiffBump.test_minor` (method) — Asserts a minor-version increase yields BumpType.MINOR. <!--#eb8632758f770837-->
  - `TestDiffBump.test_patch` (method) — Asserts a patch-version increase yields BumpType.PATCH. <!--#53ca28a17c2ee8f2-->
  - `TestDiffBump.test_no_change_returns_none` (method) — Asserts identical versions yield None (no bump). <!--#83438ebd0fd7663d-->
  - `TestDiffBump.test_backward_returns_none` (method) — Asserts a backward version step yields None. <!--#fa01f570c0964687-->
  - `TestDiffBump.test_prerelease_to_release_returns_patch` (method) — Asserts finalizing a prerelease (4.5.0-alpha → 4.5.0) yields PATCH per SemVer §11. <!--#ab9c3f31b6faa569-->
  - `TestDiffBump.test_release_to_prerelease_returns_none` (method) — Asserts adding a prerelease suffix (a backward precedence step) yields None. <!--#bbe45ce9c947d112-->
  - `TestDiffBump.test_build_metadata_only_returns_none` (method) — Asserts build-metadata-only changes are ignored in precedence and yield None. <!--#1a422d259ad0a864-->
  - `TestDiffBump.test_prerelease_bump_with_numeric_change` (method) — Asserts a numeric minor change dominates a prerelease difference, yielding MINOR. <!--#292d245fb800ffd2-->
- `TestInferResult` (class) — Test class verifying the InferResult dataclass holds a bump (possibly None) and a reason string. <!--#689b8efc432a3531-->
  - `TestInferResult.test_dataclass_fields` (method) — Asserts InferResult stores bump and reason fields. <!--#5379069f21379909-->
  - `TestInferResult.test_none_bump_with_reason` (method) — Asserts InferResult supports a None bump with an explanatory reason. <!--#37916a89b93e34b9-->
- `TestInferBranchBump` (class) — Test class for infer_branch_bump, deriving a branch's bump from the end-to-end pyproject version diff against a base ref across many scenarios. <!--#40030e1b34866b0f-->
  - `TestInferBranchBump.test_patch_bump` (method) — Asserts a branch raising the version 4.4.0→4.4.1 infers PATCH. <!--#f3f06f044003593a-->
  - `TestInferBranchBump.test_minor_bump` (method) — Asserts a branch raising the version 4.4.0→4.5.0 infers MINOR. <!--#8a0b4318baf14b53-->
  - `TestInferBranchBump.test_major_bump` (method) — Asserts a branch raising the version 4.4.0→5.0.0 infers MAJOR. <!--#e238dd897fb34d56-->

  - `TestInferBranchBump.test_no_pyproject_returns_none` (method) — Asserts a repo with no readable version infers None ('no readable version'). <!--#19831748b57c0ee8-->
  - `TestInferBranchBump.test_branch_lower_version_returns_none` (method) — Asserts a branch that lowers the version contributes no bump. <!--#3f09f829b94b303c-->
  - `TestInferBranchBump.test_end_to_end_diff_ignores_intermediate_bumps` (method) — Asserts only the merge-base-to-tip diff matters, ignoring intermediate in-branch bumps. <!--#106be7e155ca162d-->
  - `TestInferBranchBump.test_spec_example_branch_bumps` (method) — Asserts the spec example where branch B infers PATCH and branch C infers MINOR from their end-to-end diffs. <!--#c05e20444440e5b7-->
  - `TestInferBranchBump.test_prerelease_to_release_infers_patch` (method) — Asserts finalizing a prerelease on a branch infers PATCH. <!--#80a9a47ff0abcb30-->
  - `TestInferBranchBump.test_release_to_prerelease_no_bump` (method) — Asserts adding a prerelease suffix on a branch infers no bump. <!--#228bd9164d0bcfb0-->
  - `TestInferBranchBump.test_build_metadata_only_no_bump` (method) — Asserts a build-metadata-only change on a branch infers no bump. <!--#e2b027a6a8337d48-->
- `TestAggregateAndApply` (class) — Test class for aggregate_and_apply, exercising bump aggregation, writing/committing the new version, and rollback on git failures. <!--#e619584f7ffb6ff7-->
  - `TestAggregateAndApply._setup_repo_with_merge_commit` (method) — Helper creating a repo with a versioned pyproject and a merge-like commit available to amend. <!--#80ee109aef93f6fd-->
  - `TestAggregateAndApply.test_patch_patch_minor_bumps_to_4_5_0` (method) — Asserts aggregating patch+patch+minor on 4.4.0 produces and writes 4.5.0. <!--#cb2c1b0d88b26939-->
  - `TestAggregateAndApply.test_minor_major_bumps_to_2_0_0` (method) — Asserts aggregating minor+major on 1.2.3 produces and writes 2.0.0. <!--#8af6b1ce670db730-->

  - `TestAggregateAndApply.test_only_patch_bumps_patch` (method) — Asserts a sole PATCH bump on 4.4.0 yields 4.4.1. <!--#d80c7d6411e21151-->
  - `TestAggregateAndApply.test_empty_bumps_fails` (method) — Asserts an empty bump list fails with a 'no bumps' error. <!--#ba62232c2693a294-->
  - `TestAggregateAndApply.test_invalid_pre_merge_version_fails` (method) — Asserts an unparseable pre-merge version fails with an error. <!--#98dbe9df3f859adf-->
  - `TestAggregateAndApply.test_missing_pyproject_fails_gracefully` (method) — Asserts a missing pyproject.toml fails gracefully with an explanatory error. <!--#7f2e743b62874c92-->

### `tests/test_migrate.py` (python) — Test suite for the `se3 migrate` command and its first spec-to-new-system migrator, covering the migrator registry (register/list/get with duplicate rejection), CLI wiring, and the fault-tolerant migration pipeline that writes the charter exactly once, injects colocated why-comments, builds the authoritative code-index, deletes salvaged specs only after success, and idempotently rewrites .gitignore with default-deny whitelists for tracked top-level paths. <!--#6ff5fef47d2e581b|4ef8b1d225aebcd4-->
- `_git` (function) — Helper that runs a git subcommand in the given project root, raising on failure. <!--#881bf8d1b379498d-->
- `_init_git_project` (function) — Helper that initializes a git repo with a test user identity in the given root. <!--#6aabffa4b0cbf3dc-->
- `FakeSummarizer` (class) — Deterministic stand-in code-index summarizer that maps each target to a fixed `S:<name>` string instead of calling the LLM. <!--#35adba97abbabfe3-->
  - `FakeSummarizer.__call__` (method) — Returns a dict mapping each target's id to a deterministic `S:<name>` summary. <!--#1d61334eb28ddb92-->
- `_make_salvager` (function) — Factory returning a fake salvager callable that ignores its input and yields a fixed `SalvageResult` (charter body + colocations). <!--#59b18ab05a11927b-->
- `project` (function) — Pytest fixture building a committed git project with base/non-base/changelog specs, one source file, and a baseline .gitignore. <!--#5ae2f30166d70517-->
- `test_registry_has_first_migrator` (function) — Asserts the `spec-to-new-system` migrator is registered and bound to `run_spec_to_new_system`. <!--#cd2233b643f97a14-->
- `test_registry_register_and_duplicate_rejection` (function) — Verifies migrators can be registered and that re-registering a duplicate id raises `ValueError`. <!--#c9c23b945b202a87-->
- `test_list_migrators_sorted` (function) — Asserts `list_migrators` returns migrators ordered by id. <!--#a17aab8ec2db6e4a-->
- `test_cli_registers_migrate` (function) — Checks that a `migrate` sub-app is wired into the main CLI's registered groups. <!--#c1033f71af03974e-->
- `test_migrate_list_command_runs` (function) — Asserts `se3 migrate list` exits cleanly and lists the `spec-to-new-system` migrator. <!--#8f51c77c8e15f79b-->
- `test_migrate_run_unknown_id_errors` (function) — Asserts `se3 migrate run` with an unknown migrator id exits with code 1. <!--#880bbbdf3d97f7df-->
- `test_full_migration_happy_path` (function) — End-to-end test asserting that a full spec-to-new-system migration writes the charter, injects colocated why-comments into source (keeping it parseable), builds the authoritative code-index.md with no JSON sidecar, deletes the salvaged specs, and rewrites .gitignore accordingly. <!--#584a226c5fd5333f-->
- `test_charter_written_exactly_once` (function) — Monkeypatches `Path.write_text` to confirm the charter file is written exactly once (no overwrite window). <!--#01ef1f1e95289d30-->
- `test_specs_kept_when_charter_fails` (function) — Asserts that when the salvager raises, the charter step FAILs, spec deletion is SKIPped, and specs survive. <!--#937eb0375baac764-->
- `test_no_delete_specs_flag_keeps_specs` (function) — Asserts the `delete_specs=False` flag skips spec deletion while still succeeding overall. <!--#e89036c22b6ea748-->
- `test_missing_colocation_target_is_skipped` (function) — Asserts an unresolvable colocation target is noted and skipped, causing specs to be kept since salvage is incomplete. <!--#c3cc2aa311ab8102-->
- `test_all_colocations_skipped_keeps_specs` (function) — Asserts that when every colocation target is unresolvable, spec deletion is skipped and the spec corpus survives. <!--#09504023ac28230f-->
- `test_gitignore_rewrite_idempotent` (function) — Asserts the .gitignore rewrite adds the new whitelists/removes the specs negation on first run and is a no-op on the second. <!--#aec71b6978058cf1-->
- `test_gitignore_whitelists_after_se3_anchor` (function) — Asserts the new whitelists are inserted immediately after the `/se3/*` anchor and the specs negation is removed. <!--#ba74095c847c9b48-->
- `_check_ignored` (function) — Test helper that runs `git check-ignore` in a repo and returns whether a given relative path is ignored by the current .gitignore. <!--#dde6b71d331773dd-->
- `legacy_project` (function) — Pytest fixture building a pre-existing git project with tracked top-level files/dirs and a flat (non-default-deny) .gitignore, representing the shape the migrate command must protect. <!--#a8e1ece9a3cc9060-->
- `test_root_deny_protects_tracked_toplevel` (function) — Verifies that rewriting .gitignore to add a `/*` default-deny also whitelists every tracked top-level path (files as `!/name`, dirs as `!/name/`) so none are dropped, while still ignoring stray new root files. <!--#674fa80026608def-->
- `test_root_deny_idempotent` (function) — Verifies that running `_rewrite_gitignore` a second time reports no changes and leaves the .gitignore content byte-identical. <!--#d77ea16c2aa27d1b-->
- `test_root_deny_skipped_when_ls_files_unavailable` (function) — Verifies that when `git ls-files` is unavailable (not a git repo), the rewrite safely skips adding `/*` rather than risking a silent drop, returning None from `_tracked_toplevel_whitelists` and raising nothing. <!--#53193ff71a374a19-->
- `test_root_deny_skipped_when_ls_files_raises` (function) — Verifies that an unexpected subprocess failure during whitelist discovery is swallowed so `/*` is not added and non-git edits still run without raising. <!--#7383a97ffdfd29c4-->
- `test_load_spec_corpus_splits_and_skips` (function) — Asserts `_load_spec_corpus` separates the base spec from non-base specs while skipping the `_changelog` directory. <!--#66260eaf1a1dfab5-->
- `test_colocation_preserves_shebang` (function) — Asserts inserting a why-comment keeps a script's shebang on the first line while still adding the why marker. <!--#8ed6c42f2d73dcf6-->

### `tests/test_plan_confirm_always_on.py` (python) — Unit tests verifying the always-on plan confirmation behavior, asserting that `insert_confirmation_steps` injects exactly one CONFIRM after PLAN regardless of config (without double-confirming) and that `resolve_confirm_inputs` synthesizes a default LLM review chain for unconfigured plans while leaving other steps config-driven. <!--#040c53d2085d7027|027df13b2db69b1c-->
- `isolated_global_home` (function) — Pytest fixture that monkeypatches `Path.home` to a clean temp dir, neutralizing the real `~/.se3/config.yaml` so only the project's se3.yaml affects confirmation resolution. <!--#682c6d8a048215f7-->
- `TestInsertPlanAlwaysOn` (class) — Test class verifying that `insert_confirmation_steps` always injects exactly one CONFIRM after PLAN regardless of config, without double-confirming explicit plan entries or confirming unconfigured non-plan steps. <!--#5dc3749f72544593-->
  - `TestInsertPlanAlwaysOn.test_no_se3_yaml_still_confirms_plan` (method) — Asserts that with no se3.yaml present, a CONFIRM is still inserted right after PLAN exactly once. <!--#da65986ad9f17878-->
  - `TestInsertPlanAlwaysOn.test_empty_steps_dict_still_confirms_plan` (method) — Asserts that an empty `confirmation.steps` config still yields exactly one CONFIRM after PLAN. <!--#4f6e8b38617008ac-->
  - `TestInsertPlanAlwaysOn.test_steps_without_plan_entry_still_confirms_plan` (method) — Asserts that a config confirming only a non-plan step still confirms PLAN plus the configured step, giving two CONFIRMs. <!--#b84797db142404e4-->
  - `TestInsertPlanAlwaysOn.test_explicit_plan_entry_does_not_double_confirm` (method) — Asserts that an explicit `plan` config entry does not stack a second CONFIRM on top of the always-on one. <!--#ac6721a9da36ad37-->
  - `TestInsertPlanAlwaysOn.test_non_plan_step_not_confirmed_when_unconfigured` (method) — Asserts that a sequence with no PLAN and empty config produces no CONFIRM at all. <!--#2fb6f9e4d1d08101-->
- `TestResolvePlanInputs` (class) — Test class verifying `resolve_confirm_inputs` always enables plan-step confirmation — synthesizing a default LLM-chain entry when unconfigured, matching an explicit empty `plan: {}` entry, honoring explicit reviewer/max_iterations overrides, while leaving non-plan steps config-driven (None when unset). <!--#9269ccf5df60524b-->
  - `TestResolvePlanInputs.test_plan_unconfigured_synthesizes_default_llm_entry` (method) — Asserts that with no se3.yaml the plan step resolves to a concrete default — no human reviewer, the builtin agent chain narrowed to whatever is on PATH (stubbed to just `claude`), and the default max_iterations — rather than None. <!--#73455b25ccddcb5d-->
  - `TestResolvePlanInputs.test_plan_unconfigured_matches_empty_plan_entry` (method) — Asserts that the synthesized default for an absent plan entry is identical to an explicit empty `plan: {}` entry. <!--#386f0e59a2b6fcfd-->
  - `TestResolvePlanInputs.test_plan_explicit_reviewer_and_iterations_override` (method) — Asserts that an explicit human reviewer and custom max_iterations on plan are honored over the always-on default. <!--#b8f3c2bf8b0f83c3-->
  - `TestResolvePlanInputs.test_non_plan_unconfigured_returns_none` (method) — Asserts that an unconfigured non-plan step resolves to None, preserving the human-fallback path. <!--#c1ae13841f11fce1-->
  - `TestResolvePlanInputs.test_non_plan_configured_resolves_entry` (method) — Asserts that an explicitly configured non-plan step resolves normally, unaffected by the plan special-casing. <!--#3fefe41f5e6a8d5d-->

### `tests/test_preset_loader.py` (python) — Pytest suite for the dual-layer preset prompt registry (se3.preset_loader), verifying built-in presets are read at runtime from package data (never copied), project-layer presets override same-named built-ins with optional se3.yaml type metadata, error paths for unknown or missing prompt files, and that list_presets enumerates both layers name-sorted. <!--#475dbb2098acea3b|0ed27c66d819ba4d-->
- `project_root` (function) — Pytest fixture returning a fresh tmp_path to stand in as an isolated project root directory. <!--#8cf80cae6e4c6d2a-->
- `_write_project_preset` (function) — Test helper that writes a project-layer preset markdown file (and optionally its se3.yaml metadata) under a given root. <!--#41105beb86c86e5f-->
- `TestBuiltinLayer` (class) — Test class asserting built-in presets are present and read at runtime from package data without being copied into the project. <!--#869ed38e336d8f74-->
  - `TestBuiltinLayer.test_builtin_doc_sync_present` (method) — Asserts the built-in 'doc-sync' preset appears in the loaded registry with the builtin layer and 'feature' type. <!--#dc0db7a70c2ac98b-->
  - `TestBuiltinLayer.test_builtin_read_at_runtime_from_package` (method) — Asserts 'doc-sync' resolves from package data into a clean project without copying any prompts directory in. <!--#e2756eccf82cf6aa-->
- `TestProjectOverride` (class) — Test class verifying project-layer presets override built-ins and honor (or default) their type metadata. <!--#37f385aed94fbd7d-->
  - `TestProjectOverride.test_project_overrides_builtin_same_name` (method) — Asserts a project-level 'doc-sync' file shadows the built-in, resolving to the project layer and its content. <!--#21633430081225e2-->
  - `TestProjectOverride.test_project_preset_without_yaml_uses_default_type` (method) — Asserts a bare project prompt markdown with no se3.yaml still registers, using DEFAULT_PRESET_TYPE. <!--#dca2b450f60f3140-->
  - `TestProjectOverride.test_yaml_type_override` (method) — Asserts se3.yaml metadata overrides a preset's type (e.g. to 'bugfix') at the project layer. <!--#211b464d8d7fffc9-->
- `TestErrors` (class) — Test class covering error paths: unknown preset names and declared-but-missing prompt files. <!--#3dfbd8e449cd5cdb-->
  - `TestErrors.test_unknown_preset_lists_available` (method) — Asserts resolving an unknown preset raises PresetNotFoundError whose message lists available presets including 'doc-sync'. <!--#851b090d61dd5b59-->
  - `TestErrors.test_missing_prompt_file_raises` (method) — Asserts a preset declared in se3.yaml with a nonexistent prompt_file raises PresetError mentioning the name and 'missing'. <!--#4242778ff4bf01db-->
- `TestListPresets` (class) — Test class verifying list_presets enumerates both built-in and project layers in sorted order. <!--#0e86d9b438d77794-->
  - `TestListPresets.test_list_includes_both_layers` (method) — Asserts list_presets returns both the built-in 'doc-sync' and a project-only preset, name-sorted with correct layer tags. <!--#3719eb084e0f2581-->

### `tests/test_prompt_history.py` (python) — Unit tests for se3.engine.prompt_history covering get_prompt_history's creation of the se3/history/ directory and a persistent, idempotent FileHistory, plus _truncate_history's trimming to the most recent MAX_ENTRIES while handling multiline entries and missing/empty files. <!--#8f1bd45df85829f2|458619e1b9722c9e-->
- `test_get_prompt_history_creates_directory_and_returns_file_history` (function) — Asserts get_prompt_history creates the se3/history/ directory and returns a writable FileHistory instance. <!--#75a50ce193f961c0-->

- `test_get_prompt_history_preserves_existing_entries` (function) — Checks that entries previously written to the history file are loaded back by a freshly created FileHistory. <!--#ab53138009f2d1d8-->

- `test_truncate_history_keeps_last_n_entries` (function) — Confirms _truncate_history retains only the most recent max_entries entries and drops older ones. <!--#ef83236fa7ff4bb3-->
- `test_truncate_history_preserves_multiline_entries` (function) — Verifies _truncate_history treats multiline entries as single units when trimming to max_entries. <!--#7fbbe7dee9feb5d1-->
- `test_truncate_history_no_op_on_missing_file` (function) — Ensures _truncate_history does not raise when the target history file does not exist. <!--#e16ec4109387cbaf-->
- `test_truncate_history_no_op_on_empty_file` (function) — Ensures _truncate_history leaves an empty history file unchanged. <!--#d05aedd8d87ed270-->

### `tests/test_protocol_history.py` (python) — Unit tests for the daemon/server wire protocol's revision-3 history messaging: they verify PROTOCOL_VERSION is bumped, that history index/data/request/index-request and issue-command message types are registered in the correct directional tables, that the make_history_*, make_issue_command, and make_spawn_flow (discover/resume_flow_id) constructors round-trip through encode/decode, and that decode rejects unknown message types with a catchable ProtocolError for backward-compatible peer handling. <!--#a302bf8010bc726b|1d3e2d88215101d8-->
- `test_protocol_version_bumped_to_3` (function) — A test asserting that protocol.PROTOCOL_VERSION equals "3", documenting that revision 3 introduced the traffic-reduction messages (keepalive/index-delta/detail) and that the version bump is what lets peers detect legacy versions and fall back to full-frame semantics. <!--#675b086904074517-->
- `test_history_message_types_registered` (function) — Verifies the history index/data/request message types are registered in the correct daemon/server direction tables and the all-types set. <!--#98449cc460ce40f9-->
- `test_history_index_request_type_registered` (function) — Checks the history-index-request type is server-to-daemon only and never sent back to the server. <!--#fe65f847ae6110c0-->
- `test_make_history_index_request_round_trip` (function) — Confirms make_history_index_request produces an empty-payload re-push trigger that survives encode/decode. <!--#ef2bd936d51d230e-->
- `test_make_history_index_round_trip` (function) — Confirms make_history_index serializes a session list and round-trips it through encode/decode unchanged. <!--#64643c014944da17-->
- `test_make_history_request_full_snapshot` (function) — Verifies make_history_request without a cursor yields a full-snapshot request carrying flow_id, project_root, and an empty cursor. <!--#2b4eec0f25eb436d-->
- `test_make_history_request_with_cursor` (function) — Verifies make_history_request preserves a per-stage byte-offset cursor through the round-trip. <!--#f67024e99736f136-->
- `test_make_history_data_full_round_trip` (function) — Confirms make_history_data in FULL mode round-trips flow_id, mode, records, and an empty cursor. <!--#20941efe2e81108b-->
- `test_make_history_data_append_with_cursor` (function) — Confirms make_history_data in APPEND mode round-trips records, the advancing cursor, and the seq number. <!--#f5bca4b43def2be4-->
- `test_make_history_data_rejects_bad_mode` (function) — Asserts make_history_data raises ProtocolError when given an invalid history mode. <!--#eb6b0938307aedd1-->
- `test_decode_unknown_type_raises_protocol_error` (function) — Asserts decode rejects an unrecognized message type with ProtocolError rather than crashing. <!--#6460f879cf60220a-->
- `test_decode_unknown_type_is_catchable` (function) — Shows known frames decode while unknown ones raise a catchable ProtocolError, enabling forward/backward peer tolerance. <!--#4c2d88e7a8fada6b-->
- `test_make_spawn_flow_discover_defaults_false` (function) — Verifies make_spawn_flow sets the discover field to False by default and round-trips it. <!--#4b85f3c1b0ebd829-->
- `test_make_spawn_flow_discover_true` (function) — Verifies make_spawn_flow with discover=True round-trips the discover flag and the task description. <!--#71786b5aac22427d-->
- `test_issue_command_type_registered` (function) — Checks the issue-command message type is registered server-to-daemon only. <!--#2abb8b052ab10a5a-->
- `test_make_issue_command_create_round_trip` (function) — Confirms make_issue_command for a create operation round-trips all issue fields (description, title, priority, type, tags). <!--#91c642d057f72fb0-->
- `test_make_issue_command_edit_round_trip` (function) — Confirms make_issue_command for an edit operation round-trips issue_id and description while omitting empty fields. <!--#020423f3b51e05dd-->

### `tests/test_read_only_injection.py` (python) — Unit tests verifying the read-only step machinery: that every STEP_POOL entry carries a correct read_only boolean, that get_read_only_injection()/is_step_read_only classify analysis steps (discovery, analyze, plan, sync_scan/analyze, and pure-data code_index/migrate sub-agents) as read-only while mutating steps (implement, commit, sync_resolve) are writable, that the injected constraint text forbids Write/Edit and permits Read/Grep/Glob, and that LLMCaller.call() appends this constraint to prompts for read-only steps across strict and two_phase JSON modes. <!--#f109b9f74917c1a1|979bc3b9c9459164-->

  - `TestGetReadOnlyInjection.test_non_read_only_steps_return_empty` (method) — Parametrized test that writable steps yield an empty injection string. <!--#9468c073be0ea5a5-->
  - `TestGetReadOnlyInjection.test_unknown_step_returns_empty` (method) — Asserts unknown or empty step names safely return an empty string. <!--#02f3b1452617bf55-->
  - `TestGetReadOnlyInjection.test_constraint_forbids_write_edit` (method) — Asserts the constraint text explicitly forbids the Write and Edit tools. <!--#7e75f30aa23d3311-->

- `TestSyncStepReadOnly` (class) — Test class verifying read-only step classification: confirms sync_scan/sync_analyze, pool steps (analyze/plan), and pure-data sub-agents (code_index/migrate) are read-only while writable steps (sync_resolve/implement/commit) are not, and that read-only injection text is added accordingly. <!--#10fa077708a72713-->

  - `TestSyncStepReadOnly.test_is_step_read_only_writable_steps_false` (method) — Asserts implement/update_spec/commit are reported as not read-only. <!--#4c7ef27d30ee6fac-->
  - `TestSyncStepReadOnly.test_is_step_read_only_pool_read_only_steps_true` (method) — Asserts pool steps analyze and plan are reported as read-only. <!--#ded051bc19fd85eb-->
  - `TestSyncStepReadOnly.test_is_step_read_only_unknown_step_false` (method) — Asserts unknown or empty step names are reported as not read-only. <!--#a6aafd8571e216e6-->

### `tests/test_relay_plan_linearity_integration.py` (python) — Integration tests feeding realistic DAGs through the full transitive_reduce → classify_chains → _relay_plan_is_linear pipeline that implement_handler uses, verifying that redundant-edge chains stay linear while genuine forks are not flattened, across a range of topology shapes and pipeline invariants. <!--#4d63a4e90aa8f0fc|1e27f06711d57ac8-->
- `_is_linear` (function) — Test helper that runs the complete TR → classify → linearity-check pipeline on a list of group dicts and returns the boolean verdict. <!--#812062e40d5b42d1-->
- `_g` (function) — Compact factory helper that builds a group dict with the given id, order, and dependency list. <!--#0383f1b0979aaf98-->
- `TestRedundantEdgesStillLinear` (class) — Test class asserting that chains carrying redundant transitive edges remain detected as linear while genuine forks are not flattened. <!--#370646d1081282fe-->
  - `TestRedundantEdgesStillLinear.test_redundant_edge_stays_linear` (method) — Verifies the A→B,A→C,B→C redundancy is treated as a convergence rather than a fork, staying linear before and after transitive reduction. <!--#ed6ce66a9c71b33f-->
  - `TestRedundantEdgesStillLinear.test_cascading_redundant_edges_stay_linear` (method) — Verifies a fully transitively-closed chain (A→B→C→D plus all redundant edges) is still recognized as linear. <!--#60d238f7ddcb1553-->
  - `TestRedundantEdgesStillLinear.test_genuine_fork_stays_fork_after_reduction` (method) — Verifies a true fork (A→B, A→C with no B↔C edge) is non-linear and unchanged by transitive reduction. <!--#859340a1a548c020-->
  - `TestRedundantEdgesStillLinear.test_diamond_with_redundant_root_edge` (method) — Verifies a diamond with a redundant root edge stays non-linear because the B/C fork from A is real. <!--#fa26c99d98969f10-->
- `TestExtendedTopologies` (class) — Test class covering topology shapes beyond the unit tests: long chains, wide forks, disconnected components, out-of-order declarations, and trailing/converging forks. <!--#14c0544fd7b8b986-->
  - `TestExtendedTopologies.test_long_linear_chain` (method) — Verifies a 10-node linear chain is detected as linear. <!--#ab7d88be999d89a4-->
  - `TestExtendedTopologies.test_wide_fork_from_single_root` (method) — Verifies a single root with four independent dependents is non-linear. <!--#6d0e6fead8834c19-->
  - `TestExtendedTopologies.test_two_disconnected_linear_chains` (method) — Verifies two independent chains (two roots) are reported as non-linear. <!--#ef94561a36e81d7f-->
  - `TestExtendedTopologies.test_chain_with_out_of_order_declaration` (method) — Verifies that declaring chain nodes in reverse order doesn't affect linearity detection. <!--#d6d702d2db271fda-->
  - `TestExtendedTopologies.test_trailing_fork_off_linear_prefix` (method) — Verifies a fork branching off the tail of an otherwise linear prefix breaks linearity. <!--#0625b96838d54087-->
  - `TestExtendedTopologies.test_converging_two_chains_at_tail` (method) — Verifies two independent chains converging at one tail are non-linear due to having multiple roots. <!--#a195c25304e6123b-->
- `TestPipelineInvariants` (class) — Test class checking structural invariants of the pipeline: return type, input immutability, and single/empty-node edge cases. <!--#3bf88fa7116e5ac6-->
  - `TestPipelineInvariants.test_pipeline_returns_relayplan_instance` (method) — Verifies classify_chains returns a RelayPlan instance even after transitive reduction. <!--#7ac9d81d62dc3d7c-->
  - `TestPipelineInvariants.test_pipeline_does_not_mutate_input` (method) — Verifies transitive_reduce deep-copies so the caller's original group dicts are left unmutated. <!--#b5bf3eafe801dd0c-->
  - `TestPipelineInvariants.test_single_node_pipeline_is_linear` (method) — Verifies a single-node plan passes the pipeline and is reported linear. <!--#621ffc568d8b0171-->
  - `TestPipelineInvariants.test_empty_pipeline_is_not_linear` (method) — Verifies an empty group list yields an empty RelayPlan that is reported non-linear (zero roots). <!--#c0e9a7e90c37ae82-->

### `tests/test_run_lock_lifecycle.py` (python) — Unit tests for the deferred main-worktree lock lifecycle in `se3 run` (via `_ensure_main_lock_for_step`), verifying discovery steps never lock, free/stale locks acquire without a wait state, contended locks persist and stream `waiting_for_lock=True` then clear it on acquire, `--worktree` bodies are no-ops, the flag round-trips through engine.json, and a Ctrl+C while waiting clears the flag before persist and exits 130. <!--#f756bca04f54074c|f6ba42b86a2f993f-->
- `project` (function) — Pytest fixture creating a temp project tree with `se3/state/` and returning its root path. <!--#022223c2707b4436-->
- `_make_flow` (function) — Helper that builds a RUNNING FlowInstance containing a single RUNNING step of the given StepType. <!--#7e690c403fae6b4f-->
- `_read_engine` (function) — Helper that reads and parses the persisted `se3/state/engine.json` into a dict. <!--#a46e0c5f883e7add-->
- `_jsonl_path` (function) — Helper returning the streaming history JSONL path for a given flow and step. <!--#ac9f7e26db328f1e-->
- `test_waiting_for_lock_roundtrips_true` (function) — Asserts a True `waiting_for_lock` flag serializes and round-trips through FlowInstance dict conversion. <!--#9aa058df1ebf86a0-->
- `test_waiting_for_lock_false_omitted_and_reads_false` (function) — Asserts a default-False `waiting_for_lock` is omitted from serialization and legacy files lacking the key read back as False. <!--#f7596474f23d651f-->
- `test_discovery_step_does_not_acquire_lock` (function) — Verifies a discovery step never acquires the main-worktree lock (1a), leaving it genuinely free for another acquirer. <!--#1917614de3187410-->
- `test_free_lock_acquired_without_waiting_state` (function) — Verifies a free lock is acquired immediately with no `waiting_for_lock` flag set and no streaming event written. <!--#c13a70cfc785211d-->
- `test_already_held_lock_is_noop` (function) — Verifies that calling the helper when the lock is already held is a no-op with no waiting state. <!--#fb10b44cff47523b-->
- `test_worktree_body_none_lock_is_noop` (function) — Verifies that a `--worktree` flow body (main_lock is None) is a pure no-op leaving `waiting_for_lock` False. <!--#7e09f0d84a0e9043-->
- `test_busy_lock_surfaces_waiting_state_then_acquires` (function) — Verifies a contended lock persists `waiting_for_lock=True` and writes a streaming event before blocking, then acquires and clears the flag once the holder releases (1b). <!--#cfdeccfc12afffea-->
- `test_stale_lock_reclaimed_without_waiting` (function) — Verifies a stale lock file (dead PID) is silently reclaimed without surfacing any waiting state or event. <!--#4e6c6df81a403dc6-->
- `test_interrupt_while_waiting_clears_flag_before_persist` (function) — Test verifying that when a Ctrl+C KeyboardInterrupt hits `run_flow` while it is blocked marking `waiting_for_lock=True` and awaiting the contended main-worktree lock, the interrupt handler clears the flag before its final persist so the flow exits 130 and is never left persisted as 'waiting', avoiding a dead process appearing stuck on the lock. <!--#a50fa9bb74a3b31b-->

### `tests/test_run_waiting_for_lock_clear.py` (python) — Pytest suite verifying that acquiring a *contended* main-worktree merge lock emits a clearing 'step_status' running anchor (idempotent, skipped from CLI/retry history) to unfreeze the web transcript's '等待锁' row while free/stale acquires write nothing, and refuting the theory that a step error during retry releases the merge lock — showing it stays held until run_flow's finally on flow exit. <!--#60029f61e126ffaa|b83eeb87c86ba534-->

- `test_contended_acquire_emits_lock_acquired_clear_event` (function) — Asserts that when the lock is held by another holder, the run worker writes a 'waiting_for_lock' anchor while blocked and appends a clearing step_status 'running' anchor after acquiring. <!--#3e299eb60193e543-->
- `test_free_acquire_writes_no_clear_event` (function) — Asserts that acquiring a free lock writes no jsonl anchors at all (neither waiting nor clear). <!--#a91f7a2f8e320602-->
- `test_stale_reclaim_writes_no_clear_event` (function) — Asserts that silently reclaiming a stale lock (dead PID) surfaces no wait and writes no jsonl anchors. <!--#f9c1b8eab78d4cbc-->

- `test_merge_lock_held_through_retry_not_released_until_flow_exit` (function) — Refutes the merge-lock-release-causes-freeze theory by showing the lock stays held and uncontendable through a simulated step-error/retry inside _run_flow_impl, released only by run_flow's finally on flow exit. <!--#c4527a045d299cfe-->
