- `_register` (function) — Helper that performs the HELLO + STATUS_UPDATE handshake on a websocket and waits for the given flows to become visible. <!--#274ab3bd8c39b746-->
- `test_interject_endpoint_dispatches` (function) — Asserts a successful interject returns a dispatched response and forwards an INTERJECT_FLOW frame carrying the text to the daemon. <!--#36a505855d448dcf-->
- `test_interject_unknown_flow_returns_404` (function) — Asserts interjecting into an unknown flow id yields HTTP 404. <!--#58386143eda4a8f4-->
- `test_interject_empty_text_returns_422` (function) — Asserts interjecting with blank/whitespace text yields HTTP 422. <!--#54a6d740fb965b9a-->
- `test_interject_offline_machine_returns_503` (function) — Asserts that interjecting into a still-visible flow whose machine has disconnected yields HTTP 503. <!--#f055d27f301656b4-->
- `test_respond_locates_non_call_kind_pending_call` (function) — Asserts `/respond` resolves the first pending call of any kind (e.g. a retry_decision) and emits a RESPOND_CALL frame. <!--#5e00c287d3d0a69c-->
- `_stub_failed_step` (function) — Helper producing a SimpleNamespace stub of a failed step with id, type, and retry count. <!--#89f62f82c7da6bb8-->
- `test_failure_with_tty_races_and_writes_retry_decision_call` (function) — Asserts an interactive-terminal failure returns a `race` action yet still writes a retry_decision call file for webui bystanders. <!--#83cdc4bf1b4614f0-->
- `test_failure_without_tty_writes_retry_decision_call` (function) — Asserts a non-interactive failure pauses and externalises the decision as a deterministically-named retry_decision call file. <!--#5c0045719a6fc97c-->
- `test_failure_without_tty_applies_existing_response` (function) — Asserts a non-interactive retry_decision answered out-of-band resolves on the next pass to that decision action. <!--#3a2e6aa90912da1d-->
- `test_stdin_is_interactive_reflects_isatty` (function) — Asserts `_stdin_is_interactive` mirrors stdin's isatty result and returns False when stdin is None. <!--#ec7f1849da1cf25e-->

### `tests/test_server_persistence.py` (python) — Unit/concurrency test suite for the se3 server's sqlite Store persistence layer and IdentityService, covering owner CRUD with last-admin/break-glass delete-and-demote guards, decoupled provider-identity bindings, hash-only password/daemon-key/break-glass storage with revoke and one-time consume semantics, DB file path/WAL setup and durability, and identity key→owner resolution plus machine binding. <!--#f0e7d955a92a3644|7f63a09291049faa-->
- `store` (function) — Pytest fixture yielding a fresh Store backed by a temp-path sqlite file. <!--#aecd8298b6711b7d-->
- `test_owner_id_is_stable_internal_key` (function) — Verifies create_owner returns a stable internal owner_id string that round-trips through get_owner with its display_name and admin flag. <!--#dd8394298a98ab2b-->
- `test_get_unknown_owner_returns_none` (function) — Asserts get_owner returns None for an unknown owner_id. <!--#a6ea7144dbc09ba5-->
- `test_set_admin_flip_roundtrip` (function) — Checks set_admin toggles an owner's is_admin flag both directions and persists each change. <!--#f2ad3e65c09792bf-->
- `test_set_admin_unknown_owner_returns_false` (function) — Asserts set_admin on an unknown owner returns False and creates no spurious row. <!--#cde36a3b5b1062c6-->
- `test_delete_owner_guarded_unknown_returns_not_found` (function) — Asserts delete_owner_guarded returns 'not_found' for a nonexistent owner. <!--#6399eb3b8328843b-->
- `test_delete_owner_guarded_last_admin_refused` (function) — Verifies the guard refuses deleting the sole admin, returning 'last_admin' and leaving the owner intact. <!--#892f8314ac665780-->
- `test_delete_owner_guarded_non_admin_always_allowed` (function) — Verifies deleting a non-admin owner is always permitted regardless of admin count. <!--#e7e3120358b4d88b-->
- `test_delete_owner_guarded_second_admin_allowed` (function) — Confirms deleting one of two admins succeeds but deleting the remaining last admin is then refused. <!--#55e7134c79b6047c-->
- `test_delete_owner_guarded_breakglass_not_counted_as_headroom` (function) — Verifies a break-glass admin is excluded from the admin count so the sole real admin is still protected from deletion. <!--#77137f18680db18c-->
- `test_set_admin_guarded_unknown_returns_not_found` (function) — Asserts set_admin_guarded returns 'not_found' for an unknown owner. <!--#17d949acc87beb3c-->
- `test_set_admin_guarded_promote_is_unguarded` (function) — Verifies promoting a non-admin to admin via set_admin_guarded is unguarded and returns 'updated'. <!--#c3955e1bd3a7e88b-->
- `test_set_admin_guarded_demote_last_admin_refused` (function) — Verifies demoting the sole admin is refused with 'last_admin' and the flag stays True. <!--#ff9c45d7f82861b2-->
- `test_set_admin_guarded_demote_second_admin_allowed` (function) — Confirms demoting one of two admins succeeds but demoting the remaining last admin is then refused. <!--#f1fb5939ab2cba5c-->
- `test_set_admin_guarded_breakglass_not_counted_as_headroom` (function) — Verifies a break-glass admin is excluded from the count so the sole real admin cannot be demoted. <!--#41b69d2081d8c872-->
- `test_guarded_delete_concurrent_keeps_one_real_admin` (function) — Concurrency test that two threaded deletions of two distinct admins yield exactly one 'deleted' and one 'last_admin', proving the atomic guard prevents a last-admin race. <!--#00d96b0b487da663-->
- `test_owner_decoupled_from_provider_identity_with_many_bindings` (function) — Verifies one owner can hold multiple (provider, external_id) identity bindings that all resolve back to the same owner_id. <!--#e7225b747598713d-->
- `test_create_local_user_atomic_owner_binding_password` (function) — Verifies create_local_user atomically creates the owner, identity binding, and password hash in one transaction. <!--#1e8dbfd2e7fdd9eb-->
- `test_create_local_user_duplicate_raises_and_leaves_no_orphan` (function) — Verifies a duplicate create_local_user raises IdentityAlreadyBound and rolls back, leaving no orphan owner row. <!--#0713ca3c3b10bdfe-->
- `test_resolve_unknown_identity_returns_none` (function) — Asserts resolve_owner_by_identity returns None for an unknown provider/external_id. <!--#78477c357392e475-->
- `test_link_identity_idempotent_same_owner` (function) — Verifies re-linking the same identity to the same owner is idempotent with no duplicate or error. <!--#7982f70e4151137d-->
- `test_link_identity_conflict_different_owner_raises` (function) — Verifies linking an already-bound identity to a different owner raises IdentityAlreadyBound and keeps the original binding. <!--#73c66b49081a8230-->
- `test_password_hash_roundtrip_and_upsert` (function) — Verifies set_password/get_password_hash round-trip and that a second set_password upserts/replaces the stored hash. <!--#69eeae67d92ca564-->
- `test_password_stored_is_hash_not_plaintext` (function) — Asserts stored passwords are hashes (no plaintext) that still verify via crypto.verify_password. <!--#af0ddc464adee2c9-->
- `test_issue_and_resolve_daemon_key_hash_only` (function) — Verifies daemon keys are stored hash-only and resolve back to their owner by key hash. <!--#0d069f0452aaff5f-->
- `test_revoke_daemon_key_then_resolve_fails` (function) — Verifies a revoked daemon key no longer resolves and is listed only when including revoked keys. <!--#21416019f31dd685-->
- `test_revoke_unknown_daemon_key_returns_false` (function) — Asserts revoking an unknown daemon key returns False. <!--#d14cb25b4520bf7a-->
- `test_revoke_is_idempotent` (function) — Verifies revoking an already-revoked daemon key still returns True as a no-op. <!--#d157b9170d877191-->
- `test_breakglass_one_time_consume` (function) — Verifies a break-glass token can be consumed once, with the second consume returning False. <!--#9aa8926803fc9633-->
- `test_breakglass_unknown_token_fails` (function) — Asserts consuming an unknown break-glass token hash returns False. <!--#16c808ea73b94c95-->
- `test_breakglass_expiry` (function) — Verifies break-glass consumption respects expires_at, refusing expired tokens and accepting unexpired ones. <!--#7dfdf1b223dcd990-->
- `test_breakglass_reissue_after_purge` (function) — Verifies purge_breakglass invalidates the old token and a freshly issued token consumes successfully. <!--#6e28adf5b0068756-->
- `test_breakglass_only_hash_stored` (function) — Asserts break-glass tokens are stored hash-only, matchable only by recomputed hash of the presented plaintext. <!--#d932a5c1d2c6d62e-->
- `test_db_path_from_config_and_persists_across_instances` (function) — Verifies the Store auto-creates parent dirs as a single DB file and that a fresh Store on the same path sees durably persisted data. <!--#52082cda4d2d03f4-->
- `test_wal_mode_enabled` (function) — Asserts the sqlite connection uses WAL journal mode. <!--#a02147b3dbc1f846-->
- `test_concurrent_writes_are_safe` (function) — Concurrency test that four threads each creating 20 owners complete without errors and produce all 80 rows. <!--#7ad32fdf606d6931-->
- `test_identity_resolve_owner_for_key_delegates_to_store` (function) — Verifies IdentityService.resolve_owner_for_key resolves a plaintext daemon key to its owner and returns None for empty/None/unknown keys. <!--#db37f759fcc4ea77-->
- `test_identity_revoked_key_no_longer_resolves` (function) — Verifies IdentityService stops resolving a daemon key once it is revoked in the store. <!--#6e52ba3be7f3f1ca-->
- `test_identity_machine_binding` (function) — Verifies IdentityService machine binding: bind/unbind machines to owners and query owner_of_machine and machines_for_owner. <!--#597bf72068d796c0-->
- `test_identity_link_seam_refuses_unverified_blind_merge` (function) — Verifies link_identity_to_owner refuses an unverified cross-provider link (raising UntrustedIdentityLink) but allows it with admin_override or a verified_claim. <!--#91df7eb9865a1458-->
- `test_identity_link_idempotent_and_conflict` (function) — Verifies link_identity_to_owner is idempotent for re-links to the same owner (bypassing the gate) and raises IdentityAlreadyBound when linking to a different owner. <!--#f6055ee11634fc28-->

### `tests/test_server_users.py` (python) — End-to-end FastAPI TestClient tests for the admin user-management REST surface (the four `/api/users` list/delete/password-reset/admin-toggle routes), asserting every security boundary: non-admin 403 / unauthenticated 401 rejection, list-view field whitelisting and break-glass filtering, and the self / last-real-admin / break-glass / local-only guards, plus a password-reset login round-trip. <!--#c6d3afc3997a4069|d7e1feb697fcbe2e-->
- `client_and_app` (function) — Pytest fixture that builds an authenticated app and yields a `(TestClient, app)` pair for tests. <!--#7c0dc10f1bb22800-->
- `_seed_local` (function) — Helper that seeds a local user — owner record, a `(local, username)` identity binding, and a hashed password — returning its owner id. <!--#daa2acd5586f0707-->
- `_seed_oidc` (function) — Helper that seeds a non-local OIDC owner with an `oidc` identity binding and no local credential, returning its owner id. <!--#7e4d5b1aff828151-->
- `_seed_breakglass` (function) — Helper that directly creates the reserved break-glass admin owner in the store, returning its owner id. <!--#0e39491a0ebfc96d-->
- `_login_breakglass` (function) — Helper that mints and consumes a break-glass token so the client holds a break-glass admin session, enabling the last-real-admin guards to be exercised without self-protection firing. <!--#8a769bdae4cd64d9-->
- `test_user_routes_reject_non_admin_403` (function) — Asserts all four user routes return 403 for an authenticated non-admin, with the admin check preceding existence so no owner-id information leaks. <!--#a08a3a0b305732fe-->
- `test_user_routes_require_authentication_401` (function) — Asserts all four user routes return 401 when called by an unauthenticated client. <!--#75e992687ad509bf-->
- `test_list_users_whitelists_fields_and_filters_breakglass` (function) — Verifies GET `/api/users` filters out the break-glass owner, returns exactly the whitelisted fields, reflects provider/can_reset_password flags, and leaks no password hashes. <!--#dc39f88cea97eb56-->
- `test_delete_self_is_forbidden_403` (function) — Asserts an admin cannot delete their own account (403) and that the account survives. <!--#3d30012f94892fe3-->
- `test_delete_unknown_owner_is_404` (function) — Asserts deleting a nonexistent owner returns 404. <!--#654e48ca58b31d98-->
- `test_delete_breakglass_owner_is_404` (function) — Asserts deleting the reserved break-glass owner returns 404 and leaves it intact. <!--#f7814d2d4938178d-->
- `test_delete_last_real_admin_is_409` (function) — Acting as break-glass, asserts deleting the only real admin is blocked with 409 by the last-real-admin guard. <!--#f2cbcedbc16667f9-->
- `test_delete_user_succeeds_and_drops_from_list` (function) — Happy-path delete: a created user is removed (200), cascades to its binding, and disappears from the list. <!--#cf6a03afc9f4362a-->
- `test_reset_password_non_local_owner_is_409` (function) — Asserts resetting the password of a non-local (OIDC) owner returns 409. <!--#d49b596c8ddf9579-->
- `test_reset_password_unknown_or_breakglass_owner_is_404` (function) — Asserts password reset returns 404 for both an unknown owner and the break-glass owner. <!--#8a78af99dca70682-->
- `test_reset_password_empty_is_422` (function) — Asserts an empty password in a reset request is rejected with 422 validation error. <!--#f9f0d3e63222eb16-->
- `test_reset_password_lets_user_login_with_new_password` (function) — End-to-end check that after a reset the user can log in with the new password and the old one is rejected (401). <!--#04efca73d7e0ac77-->
- `test_reset_password_plaintext_not_logged` (function) — Asserts the plaintext password is never emitted to logs during a reset, even at DEBUG level. <!--#96431bc5939f5c6d-->
- `test_demote_self_is_forbidden_403` (function) — Asserts an admin cannot demote themselves (403) and remains admin. <!--#6dbf96791eb80ef5-->
- `test_demote_last_real_admin_is_409` (function) — Acting as break-glass, asserts demoting the only real admin is blocked with 409. <!--#017004218db04221-->
- `test_toggle_admin_on_breakglass_owner_is_404` (function) — Asserts toggling the admin flag on the break-glass owner returns 404. <!--#6713d5708e9318d5-->
- `test_toggle_admin_unknown_owner_is_404` (function) — Asserts toggling the admin flag on an unknown owner returns 404. <!--#ec23ef0d948ee170-->
- `test_promote_then_demote_reflected_in_list` (function) — Verifies promoting then demoting a user succeeds, is reflected in GET results and the store, with demotion allowed once a second real admin exists. <!--#fb4e6944d94653ad-->

### `tests/test_spawn_failed.py` (python) — Tests for the SPAWN_FAILED daemon-to-server feedback channel (G3), covering the protocol message constructor/registration, the daemon client's three failure paths (spawn, ensure-init, and resume) that must report SPAWN_FAILED instead of failing silently, and the server routing an inbound SPAWN_FAILED only to the reporting owner's UI clients. <!--#63efc434a5a935f0|2472fefe739cbb08-->
- `test_make_spawn_failed_payload_and_registration` (function) — Asserts make_spawn_failed builds the correct payload, registers the type as daemon-to-server and known, and round-trips through encode/decode. <!--#83a62a34132b5e25-->
- `test_make_spawn_failed_omits_empty_optionals` (function) — Asserts make_spawn_failed omits unset optional fields (task_description, from_issue_id, resume_flow_id) from the payload. <!--#6d23a9165f4ecc10-->
- `_FakeWS` (class) — Minimal async WebSocket stand-in that decodes and records frames the daemon client sends. <!--#4bcd88a41b8c0413-->
  - `_FakeWS.__init__` (method) — Initializes the fake WebSocket's empty `sent` capture list. <!--#b8b92aad379d234c-->
  - `_FakeWS.send` (method) — Async send that decodes the wire data and appends the resulting message to `sent`. <!--#7d44362527b3e749-->
- `_make_client` (function) — Helper that constructs a DaemonClient with default identity/snapshot args plus per-test handler overrides. <!--#2166366244481ca6-->
- `_spawn_failed_frames` (function) — Helper that filters a fake WS's captured frames down to SPAWN_FAILED messages. <!--#d01cff50f6f9f0cc-->
- `test_fresh_spawn_failure_reports_spawn_failed` (function) — Verifies a raising spawn_handler causes one SPAWN_FAILED frame carrying the project root, error text, and task description. <!--#b72184d0d1a3df3d-->
- `test_ensure_error_reports_spawn_failed_and_skips_spawn` (function) — Verifies an ensure_handler returning an error reports SPAWN_FAILED and never invokes the spawn handler. <!--#ce8addba54557ff6-->
- `test_ensure_exception_reports_spawn_failed` (function) — Verifies an ensure_handler raising an exception is caught and reported as a SPAWN_FAILED frame. <!--#2c4853ad6b426f7d-->
- `test_resume_failure_reports_spawn_failed` (function) — Verifies a raising resume_handler reports SPAWN_FAILED preserving the resume_flow_id and error text. <!--#167f684e5afa5862-->
- `test_successful_spawn_emits_no_spawn_failed` (function) — Verifies a successful spawn emits no SPAWN_FAILED frame. <!--#7c4e8621afe61635-->
- `test_empty_task_does_not_report_spawn_failed` (function) — Verifies that dropping an empty/whitespace task at input validation emits no SPAWN_FAILED frame since nothing was launched. <!--#33d2c675d30ffaa4-->
- `test_handle_message_routes_spawn_failed_to_owner_ui` (function) — Verifies the server's _handle_message routes an inbound SPAWN_FAILED only to the reporting machine owner's UI clients and not to other owners. <!--#d8f6e612fe622d83-->

### `tests/test_spec_governance_config.py` (python) — Test suite for the G1 spec-governance basis, covering SpecGovernanceConfig defaults, YAML overrides, illegal-value fault tolerance, and the stdlib-only spec_governance.py normative-constant source module. <!--#fa62fe41502b6654|10354e2ebc696a37-->
- `TestSpecGovernanceConfigDefaults` (class) — Test class verifying SpecGovernanceConfig's default field values and that from_dict handles empty, None, and non-dict inputs. <!--#123b06f86c0f5002-->
  - `TestSpecGovernanceConfigDefaults.test_dataclass_defaults` (method) — Asserts the SpecGovernanceConfig dataclass has the expected default byte thresholds and a 'warn' size tier. <!--#ad8f39b03c8ffaf0-->
  - `TestSpecGovernanceConfigDefaults.test_default_tier_is_warn` (method) — Asserts the default guardrails_size_tier is 'warn' per the acceptance criterion. <!--#9ad2ee1191216c5f-->
  - `TestSpecGovernanceConfigDefaults.test_module_constants_match_dataclass_defaults` (method) — Asserts the module-level DEFAULT_* constants match the dataclass's default field values. <!--#bb738c2bf507ed1c-->
  - `TestSpecGovernanceConfigDefaults.test_from_dict_empty` (method) — Asserts from_dict({}) returns a default-valued SpecGovernanceConfig. <!--#9c6639877f0dc44c-->
  - `TestSpecGovernanceConfigDefaults.test_from_dict_none` (method) — Asserts from_dict(None) returns a default-valued SpecGovernanceConfig. <!--#484bfea7479a2565-->
  - `TestSpecGovernanceConfigDefaults.test_from_dict_non_dict` (method) — Asserts from_dict with a non-dict argument returns a default-valued SpecGovernanceConfig. <!--#c83773d8841e6810-->
- `TestSpecGovernanceConfigOverride` (class) — Test class verifying YAML-based overrides via SpecGovernanceConfig.load() and the load_spec_governance_config helper. <!--#c6325680c35062c3-->
  - `TestSpecGovernanceConfigOverride.test_load_defaults_when_no_file` (method) — Asserts load() returns defaults when no se3.yaml file exists. <!--#a4e88b8583d8883c-->
  - `TestSpecGovernanceConfigOverride.test_load_defaults_when_no_section` (method) — Asserts load() returns defaults when se3.yaml lacks a spec_governance section. <!--#a771330f47a91652-->
  - `TestSpecGovernanceConfigOverride.test_yaml_override_takes_effect` (method) — Asserts a full spec_governance YAML section overrides every config field. <!--#f28d8e49b529a2b9-->
  - `TestSpecGovernanceConfigOverride.test_partial_override_keeps_other_defaults` (method) — Asserts a partial YAML override changes only the named field and leaves others at defaults. <!--#02014da4227ad909-->
  - `TestSpecGovernanceConfigOverride.test_tier_case_insensitive` (method) — Asserts the guardrails_size_tier value is normalized case-insensitively (e.g. 'ENFORCE' → 'enforce'). <!--#a849c5f468cd3270-->
  - `TestSpecGovernanceConfigOverride.test_load_spec_governance_config_helper` (method) — Asserts the load_spec_governance_config helper function loads overrides from se3.yaml. <!--#14d4ce630ebd254b-->
- `TestSpecGovernanceConfigFaultTolerance` (class) — Test class verifying illegal config values fall back to defaults and never raise. <!--#8f3d40bded8ebaf3-->
  - `TestSpecGovernanceConfigFaultTolerance.test_negative_base_max_bytes_falls_back` (method) — Asserts a negative base_max_bytes value falls back to its default. <!--#6e674962368c1e27-->
  - `TestSpecGovernanceConfigFaultTolerance.test_zero_falls_back` (method) — Asserts a zero requirement_warn_bytes value falls back to its default. <!--#3dc332f1a0bff64e-->
  - `TestSpecGovernanceConfigFaultTolerance.test_non_integer_falls_back` (method) — Asserts a non-integer (string) threshold value falls back to its default. <!--#35b7ab582e0443a0-->
  - `TestSpecGovernanceConfigFaultTolerance.test_bool_falls_back` (method) — Asserts a boolean value (an int subclass) is rejected and falls back to its default. <!--#bbc46fd35d60f9f8-->
  - `TestSpecGovernanceConfigFaultTolerance.test_float_falls_back` (method) — Asserts a float value falls back to its integer default. <!--#e5de30159830b6a8-->
  - `TestSpecGovernanceConfigFaultTolerance.test_invalid_tier_falls_back` (method) — Asserts an unrecognized guardrails_size_tier value falls back to its default. <!--#9e825e9ad2443b23-->
  - `TestSpecGovernanceConfigFaultTolerance.test_invalid_yaml_falls_back_to_defaults` (method) — Asserts malformed YAML in se3.yaml causes load() to return defaults rather than raise. <!--#3f9d770f32d35173-->
  - `TestSpecGovernanceConfigFaultTolerance.test_non_dict_section_falls_back` (method) — Asserts a non-dict spec_governance YAML section causes load() to return defaults. <!--#aebd071730df6490-->
- `TestSpecGovernanceModule` (class) — Test class verifying the se3.engine.spec_governance normative-constant source module's imports, dependencies, and exported constants. <!--#9ca9e57810db9ff8-->
  - `TestSpecGovernanceModule.test_imports_with_no_side_effects` (method) — Asserts the spec_governance module can be freshly imported with no side effects. <!--#2f3f71dd066f67b4-->
  - `TestSpecGovernanceModule.test_only_stdlib_dependencies` (method) — Asserts the spec_governance source imports no se3 or third-party modules, depending only on stdlib. <!--#bfc1e8cc48724a34-->
  - `TestSpecGovernanceModule.test_exports_required_constants` (method) — Asserts the module exports the required normative constants with expected types and marker/group values. <!--#f799f34ee7a898b8-->
  - `TestSpecGovernanceModule.test_admission_standard_mentions_base_and_modules` (method) — Asserts the BASE_ADMISSION_STANDARD text mentions both 'base' and 'module'. <!--#874ac24aefbcfebc-->
  - `TestSpecGovernanceModule.test_writing_discipline_covers_all_four_rules` (method) — Asserts the WRITING_DISCIPLINE text contains all four rule markers (a) through (d). <!--#0fa37b06515970eb-->

### `tests/test_spec_write_fallback.py` (python) — Test module for the hard-fallback spec-write guard in StateMachine.run_step, which snapshots spec-file content hashes before a non-exempt step and diffs afterward to catch Bash/sed/tee writes that bypass the PreToolUse hook — asserting non-exempt IMPLEMENT writes are FAILED (file named, content reverted, new files removed), update_spec and sync steps are exempt, the guard honors the diff_fallback_enabled config toggle, and unrelated handler errors are preserved. <!--#798cb9b0f7a63249|bcfdc05e54ea5417-->
- `_make_project` (function) — Helper that lays down a minimal project with one committed baseline spec file under se3/specs/base/. <!--#de33f0150ce3ce22-->
- `_make_machine` (function) — Helper that constructs a StateMachine rooted at the given tmp_path. <!--#f02d93ff4947f40d-->
- `_make_flow` (function) — Helper that builds a RUNNING FlowInstance with a pre-seeded empty baseline so the IMPLEMENT pre-hook is a no-op. <!--#dd272dc559d3e92d-->
- `_step` (function) — Helper that creates a PENDING Step of the given StepType with empty inputs. <!--#226cb9be0b73ae0c-->
- `TestBashBypassCaught` (class) — Tests that a non-exempt IMPLEMENT step which writes a spec directly is set to FAILED, the illegal write reverted/removed, and the error names the file and guidance. <!--#73e018d9447e67d1-->
  - `TestBashBypassCaught.test_implement_writing_spec_is_failed` (method) — Asserts an IMPLEMENT step tampering with a spec is FAILED, names the file, reverts the content on disk, and mentions 'reverted'. <!--#e6391367a57cf80f-->
  - `TestBashBypassCaught.test_error_message_explains_channel` (method) — Asserts the failure message points the agent at update_spec / spec_changes rather than forbidding behavior change. <!--#af8e40802dd5d9c1-->
  - `TestBashBypassCaught.test_creating_new_spec_file_is_failed` (method) — Asserts creating a brand-new spec file during IMPLEMENT fails the step and the illegal file is removed from disk. <!--#2717a4dbad276118-->
  - `TestBashBypassCaught.test_non_writing_step_passes` (method) — Asserts an IMPLEMENT step touching only a non-spec file is not flagged and completes. <!--#5fe46ff718726927-->
- `TestUpdateSpecExempt` (class) — Tests that an UPDATE_SPEC step writing a spec is exempt from the diff guard. <!--#8a8fc91f72d68e70-->
  - `TestUpdateSpecExempt.test_update_spec_writing_spec_not_flagged` (method) — Asserts an UPDATE_SPEC step mutating a spec completes without being flagged. <!--#4a6541c7778f9c0e-->
- `TestGuardDecisionExemption` (class) — Tests the _spec_diff_guard_enabled decision helper directly, since sync pseudo-steps never reach run_step. <!--#e323cb927c5f0dae-->
  - `TestGuardDecisionExemption.test_exempt_values_disable_guard` (method) — Asserts update_spec and the sync_* step values are in SPEC_WRITE_ALLOWED_STEPS and disable the guard. <!--#92ab6eafffc667bd-->
  - `TestGuardDecisionExemption.test_non_exempt_values_enable_guard` (method) — Asserts non-exempt step values (implement, plan_tasks, test, commit) enable the guard. <!--#97f0c1c61ab37f45-->
- `TestConfigDisable` (class) — Tests that the guard is off when spec_write_protection.diff_fallback_enabled is false in se3.yaml. <!--#ad39cc153192c334-->
  - `TestConfigDisable.test_disabled_guard_does_not_flag_bash_write` (method) — Asserts a spec write during IMPLEMENT completes when config disables the diff fallback. <!--#a119d6a8c0d690fa-->
  - `TestConfigDisable.test_decision_helper_off_when_disabled` (method) — Asserts _spec_diff_guard_enabled returns False for an implement step when config disables the fallback. <!--#331e166221083511-->
- `TestHandlerErrorPreserved` (class) — Tests that a handler failing for an unrelated reason keeps its own error and is not overwritten by the guard. <!--#6b1946184b01aedd-->
  - `TestHandlerErrorPreserved.test_handler_exception_error_not_overwritten` (method) — Asserts a handler that raises (while also touching a spec) keeps its 'boom from handler' error and is not relabeled as an illegal modification. <!--#cccaf6bc2ceda386-->

### `tests/test_spec_write_hook.py` (python) — Test suite for the hard primary layer of spec-write protection, exercising spec_write_hook's PreToolUse deny/allow decisions and defensive input handling, the idempotent guard-plugin generator, the snapshot/diff and capture/restore spec-file helpers, ClaudeCodeRunner.build_call_args' --plugin-dir wiring (never a clobbering second --settings), and LLMCaller._resolve_spec_guard_settings plus SpecWriteProtectionConfig enable/default behavior. <!--#8cc9e00127d98834|832ab33849fb0d2e-->

### `tests/test_stash_archive.py` (python) — Unit/integration test suite for the safe git-stash-pop recovery helpers (_resolve_stash_ref, archive_stash_payload, pop_stash_by_label, resolve_stashpop_safely, and the LLM-aware conflict resolver), verifying that labeled stashes are resolved and dropped precisely, that both tracked and untracked stashed content is archived verbatim before any drop, and that the helper never refuses valid pops nor drops a stash when recovery cannot be proven. <!--#2912be61c6960f63|fe1c669acd248278-->
- `_git_nocheck` (function) — Test helper that runs a git subcommand without `check=True`, used to capture the non-zero exit of a deliberately-failing `git stash pop` as the input under test. <!--#aa07c14b65b63815-->
- `_git` (function) — Test helper that runs a git subcommand in a given repo with `check=True`, capturing output and raising on failure. <!--#c5eee978784b0ec4-->
- `_init_repo` (function) — Test fixture that initializes a fresh git repo with a configured user and a committed `README.md` base file. <!--#eee1c54b05431432-->
- `_hash_object` (function) — Test helper that returns git's blob sha for a file via `git hash-object`, used to assert archived content integrity. <!--#6ef861a24e5b4d63-->
- `test_resolve_stash_ref_matches_label_not_position` (function) — Verifies `_resolve_stash_ref` resolves a stash by its message label rather than by the `stash@{0}` position, returning None for unknown labels. <!--#6cb6c917d9f5604f-->
- `test_archive_stash_payload_untracked_and_tracked` (function) — Asserts `archive_stash_payload` persists both tracked working-tree changes (case 'a') and untracked concurrent files (case 'b') under the gitignored archive dir with correct relative paths, verbatim content, and matching blob shas. <!--#9283aefd678e012d-->
- `test_archive_stash_payload_missing_label_raises` (function) — Verifies `archive_stash_payload` raises RuntimeError when no live stash matches the label, so the caller never drops without recovery proof. <!--#a94aafc4e05162af-->
- `test_archive_stash_payload_untracked_only` (function) — Verifies a stash containing only untracked files archives cleanly without treating the absent tracked diff as an error. <!--#9271e5c7bea64147-->
- `test_archive_stash_payload_skips_stash_deleted_path` (function) — Verifies a path the stash deleted (with no recoverable content) is skipped rather than raising, while still-present content is archived normally. <!--#916da6b8a6a4686a-->
- `test_resolve_stashpop_drops_despite_stash_deleted_tracked_file` (function) — End-to-end test that an uncommitted deletion plus an untracked collision yields a non-clean pop where archival skips the deletion, proves the rest recoverable, and drops the labeled stash without a false data-loss refusal. <!--#6f3b65d872a99353-->
- `test_archive_stash_payload_same_second_does_not_overwrite` (function) — Verifies two recoveries of the same label within one second go into distinct run directories (a `-2` suffix) so neither clobbers the other's recorded bytes. <!--#46b4c868982a8ec5-->
- `test_pop_stash_by_label_pops_labeled_not_top` (function) — Verifies `pop_stash_by_label` resolves and pops the labeled stash even when an unrelated stash sits on top, leaving the unrelated one untouched. <!--#259455fd18ade4b4-->
- `test_pop_stash_by_label_missing_label_returns_nonzero` (function) — Verifies that an unresolvable label yields a synthetic non-zero result (escalation) rather than a bare pop that would consume an unrelated `stash@{0}`. <!--#aa712b7edd8006e2-->
- `test_resolve_stashpop_clean_pop_is_noop` (function) — Verifies `resolve_stashpop_safely` does nothing (archives nothing, drops nothing, creates no archive sink) when given a clean pop result. <!--#b314f071ac0ebd19-->
- `test_resolve_stashpop_case_b_untracked_collision` (function) — Verifies that on an untracked-file collision (case 'b') the stashed content is archived, the merged tree version is left untouched (no take-ours), and the stash is dropped only after recovery is proven. <!--#ea3316774d894b2a-->
- `_setup_case_a` (function) — Test fixture that constructs a real 3-way tracked conflict on `app.py` and returns the failed `git stash pop` result with the stash still live. <!--#a6ebfef5956dd4b0-->
- `test_resolve_stashpop_case_a_default_fallback_take_ours` (function) — Verifies that for a case-a conflict with no resolver, the safe fallback keeps the merged (ours) version in the tree while both the stashed and head sides are archived for recovery. <!--#cd81aff799c10148-->
- `test_resolve_stashpop_case_a_uses_injected_resolver` (function) — Verifies an injected conflict resolver decides the working-tree result while both original conflict sides remain recoverable from the archive manifest. <!--#75cb4b50484ad915-->
- `test_resolve_stashpop_case_a_resolver_keeping_stashed_archives_head` (function) — Regression test that a resolver keeping the stashed side still leaves the discarded merged-HEAD content recoverable from the manifest. <!--#a794e3234b45cc43-->
- `test_resolve_stashpop_case_a_unresolved_keeps_stash` (function) — High-severity regression test that a resolver leaving the index unmerged causes the helper to keep the live stash, flag failure, surface the unresolved file, yet still archive both sides. <!--#4551daaba0c6808b-->
- `test_resolve_stashpop_drops_only_labeled_stash` (function) — Critical regression test that when the labeled stash is not at `stash@{0}`, the helper drops exactly the labeled entry and never the unrelated top stash, which stays intact and recoverable. <!--#c3455aefdb12cd20-->
- `test_resolve_stashpop_refuses_drop_when_archive_unconfirmed` (function) — Verifies the helper refuses to drop (keeps the stash and flags failure) when archival cannot be proven because there is no live stash to read. <!--#993052f216e1e5de-->
- `test_llm_resolver_applies_llm_output_and_stages` (function) — Verifies the LLM-aware resolver sends the conflict-markered buffer to a stubbed LLM and writes back the reconciled, marker-free result as a staged change while archiving both original sides. <!--#e21eee3451138a7f-->
- `test_llm_resolver_falls_back_to_take_ours_on_llm_failure` (function) — Verifies the LLM resolver falls back to deterministic take-ours (merged HEAD) when the LLM raises, leaving no conflict markers and keeping the discarded stashed side recoverable. <!--#38fc00a4b3cd1ced-->

### `tests/test_stream_progress_agent_model.py` (python) — Unit tests verifying agent/model attribution on the stream_progress channel: that record_stream_progress writes optional agent_name/model_name keys only when present (byte-identical to legacy schema otherwise), that the model-name extraction helpers parse init/system metadata and tolerate garbage, and that StreamJSONTracker labels every progress record with its agent from the first fragment, upgrades records to carry the real model once an init line streams, and gives each attempt its own agent across rotation. <!--#7cf1cad79d1a7997|d312d4909f6252cf-->
- `test_extract_model_from_obj_top_level` (function) — Asserts extract_model_name_from_obj reads the model from a top-level 'model' key on an init metadata object. <!--#c8160b5f152a2f13-->
- `test_extract_model_from_obj_system_and_nested_session` (function) — Asserts extract_model_name_from_obj handles 'system' type and a model nested under a 'session' object. <!--#3ec7a5b377f420c7-->
- `test_extract_model_from_obj_non_metadata_returns_none` (function) — Asserts extract_model_name_from_obj returns None for non-metadata types, missing model, non-dict, and None inputs without raising. <!--#fa1343937690de71-->
- `test_extract_model_from_ndjson_multiline_and_single_line` (function) — Asserts extract_model_name_from_ndjson finds the model across multiline NDJSON, single-line, and already-parsed list inputs. <!--#0199e1f68ddfb12e-->
- `test_extract_model_from_ndjson_tolerates_garbage` (function) — Asserts extract_model_name_from_ndjson returns None for empty, non-JSON, and command-banner garbage input. <!--#9df662986cf96d10-->
- `_read_record` (function) — Test helper that reads and JSON-parses the single stream_progress record written to the step's history jsonl file. <!--#604b696c1b2c494f-->
- `test_record_stream_progress_omits_agent_model_when_none` (function) — Asserts record_stream_progress writes a byte-identical legacy schema (no extra keys) when agent/model are both None. <!--#039edbbc7aef219c-->
- `test_record_stream_progress_writes_agent_only` (function) — Asserts record_stream_progress adds agent_name but omits model_name when only the agent is provided. <!--#0174860483ea9b37-->
- `test_record_stream_progress_writes_agent_and_model` (function) — Asserts record_stream_progress writes both agent_name and model_name when both are provided. <!--#b05d5b7372a9d7d2-->
- `_make_capturing_tracker` (function) — Test helper that monkeypatches record_stream_progress to capture calls and builds a StreamJSONTracker with flow context for assertions. <!--#25c4a2cf5f508df2-->
- `test_tracker_stores_agent_name` (function) — Asserts a freshly constructed StreamJSONTracker stores the agent name and leaves model name unset. <!--#69ed932b8cf1368b-->
- `test_emit_agent_identity_seeds_agent_before_any_output` (function) — Asserts emit_agent_identity writes exactly one empty-content record carrying the agent (but no model) before any stream output. <!--#ac7a1cc506d455a9-->
- `test_emit_agent_identity_includes_model_when_known` (function) — Asserts emit_agent_identity includes the model in its seed record when the model is already known. <!--#ee974fa0e9a98575-->
- `test_emit_agent_identity_noop_without_agent` (function) — Asserts emit_agent_identity writes nothing when no agent name is set. <!--#7e626ea4cf9f4e1f-->
- `test_emit_agent_identity_noop_without_flow_context` (function) — Asserts emit_agent_identity is a safe no-op when no flow/step context (progress) is configured. <!--#57ee69439677da3d-->
- `test_call_emits_identity_seed_before_result` (function) — Test asserting that LLMCaller.call() emits an identity-seed stream-progress record (empty content, agent name) at attempt start even when the runner streams no intermediate fragments. <!--#e2cc51c8a04a12ee-->
- `test_tracker_progress_carries_agent_before_model` (function) — Asserts a tool_use fragment streamed before any init line produces a progress record with agent_name but no model_name yet. <!--#396d98e72fb8b4f8-->
- `test_tracker_upgrades_to_model_after_init_line` (function) — Asserts that after an init line streams, subsequent progress records gain the parsed model_name while earlier ones lack it. <!--#f4cbdb183008a25e-->
- `test_tracker_init_line_first_all_records_carry_model` (function) — Asserts that when the init line streams first, every subsequent progress record carries both agent and model. <!--#29d42b4b61d8c43c-->
- `test_init_line_emits_model_upgrade_without_further_fragments` (function) — Asserts the tracker emits an immediate empty-content agent·model upgrade record the moment an init line reveals the model, without waiting for more fragments. <!--#98d9d2dfaf89c4ed-->
- `_FakeResult` (class) — Test double mimicking an agent runner result object with success/output/returncode and related attributes. <!--#92f47d3c98413a64-->
  - `_FakeResult.__init__` (method) — Initializes the fake result with success, output, returncode, and cmd_used, defaulting interrupted and stderr_tail. <!--#44ddd6d191c352dd-->
- `_RotationRunner` (class) — Fake AgentRunner that streams one init line plus one tool_use event then returns a pre-programmed success/failure, so the progress tracker writes exactly one record per attempt. <!--#6137c896a7f3d0fd-->
  - `_RotationRunner.__init__` (method) — Stores whether this runner instance should report success. <!--#3f755d5b9d489032-->
  - `_RotationRunner.build_call_args` (method) — Stub method returning a minimal `-p prompt` argument list for the fake rotation runner. <!--#1cf76e0ed6380c95-->
  - `_RotationRunner.detect_infra_error` (method) — Always reports no infrastructure error for the fake runner. <!--#f574c18c75997991-->
  - `_RotationRunner.run_with_monitor` (method) — Streams an init line and a tool_use via on_output, then returns the preset success/failure result. <!--#b8d4dcc2d83eef65-->
- `test_rotation_progress_records_carry_per_attempt_agent` (function) — Asserts that after agent A fails and rotation falls to B, each attempt's progress records carry its own agent name (A then B), with no stale carryover. <!--#c1a2cf8fd0b0a341-->

### `tests/test_token_usage.py` (python) — Unit tests for the se3.engine.token_usage module, covering the UsageTotals dataclass (field-wise merge, fault-tolerant dict (de)serialization, formatting helpers) and the contextvars-based step-scoped usage accumulator including cross-thread re-binding for DAG-parallel workers. <!--#b801909fd7fe45ab|7906da1c91cf8584-->
- `TestUsageTotals` (class) — Tests for the UsageTotals dataclass: defaults, field-wise merge, total/empty derivation, and fault-tolerant dict (de)serialization. <!--#2ce12dcbd9c5011b-->
  - `TestUsageTotals.test_defaults_are_zero_and_empty` (method) — Verifies a freshly constructed UsageTotals has all-zero fields, zero total_tokens, and reports is_empty(). <!--#8a806c0feaa0da35-->
  - `TestUsageTotals.test_add_merges_field_by_field` (method) — Verifies add() merges another UsageTotals field-by-field in place, returns self, and leaves the operand unchanged. <!--#1cc849570b3058e8-->
  - `TestUsageTotals.test_add_none_is_noop` (method) — Verifies add(None) leaves the receiver's fields unchanged. <!--#5ab6aec1420b3502-->
  - `TestUsageTotals.test_total_tokens_sums_all_four` (method) — Verifies total_tokens sums input, output, and both cache token fields. <!--#1534a966eb1108e8-->
  - `TestUsageTotals.test_is_empty_false_when_only_cost` (method) — Verifies a nonzero cost alone makes is_empty() return False. <!--#5d019dd1d46a2c9b-->
  - `TestUsageTotals.test_is_empty_false_when_only_tokens` (method) — Verifies a nonzero token count alone makes is_empty() return False. <!--#94808f679d609a72-->
  - `TestUsageTotals.test_to_dict_is_json_primitive` (method) — Verifies to_dict() emits the expected key/value map with only JSON-primitive numeric values. <!--#18933039f07692f6-->
  - `TestUsageTotals.test_round_trip` (method) — Verifies from_dict(to_dict(u)) reconstructs an equal UsageTotals. <!--#d86fde01ec57b51d-->
  - `TestUsageTotals.test_from_dict_none` (method) — Verifies from_dict(None) yields a default (empty) UsageTotals. <!--#1ca398c14d2240b8-->
  - `TestUsageTotals.test_from_dict_empty` (method) — Verifies from_dict({}) yields a default (empty) UsageTotals. <!--#d25f321f967c2339-->
  - `TestUsageTotals.test_from_dict_missing_fields_default_zero` (method) — Verifies from_dict fills absent fields with zero while keeping provided ones. <!--#4cf3a7a77c656d5f-->
  - `TestUsageTotals.test_from_dict_none_values_coerce_to_zero` (method) — Verifies from_dict coerces explicit None field values to zero. <!--#618b6bfce55b5d69-->
  - `TestUsageTotals.test_from_dict_bad_values_coerce_to_zero` (method) — Verifies from_dict coerces non-numeric (unparseable) field values to zero. <!--#17dd3ef86ec0b72e-->
  - `TestUsageTotals.test_from_dict_numeric_strings` (method) — Verifies from_dict parses numeric-string field values into their numeric types. <!--#e856df73945b94b9-->
- `TestFormatting` (class) — Tests for the format_cost and format_usage_line display helpers, including their None/bad-input safety. <!--#c34831a354285e26-->
  - `TestFormatting.test_format_cost` (method) — Verifies format_cost renders a USD amount to four decimal places with a dollar sign. <!--#e2cdb4551149c66b-->
  - `TestFormatting.test_format_cost_none_safe` (method) — Verifies format_cost(None) returns the zero-cost string. <!--#2f49f442d343bf75-->
  - `TestFormatting.test_format_cost_bad_value_safe` (method) — Verifies format_cost on an unparseable value returns the zero-cost string. <!--#a0d166a2bb470167-->
  - `TestFormatting.test_format_usage_line_labels_and_units` (method) — Verifies format_usage_line includes in/out labels, thousands separators, cache read/write counts, and cost. <!--#6e83cf86ebbaf72b-->
  - `TestFormatting.test_format_usage_line_none_safe` (method) — Verifies format_usage_line(None) renders a zeroed line without error. <!--#4a3236797cfad026-->
  - `TestFormatting.test_format_usage_line_empty_safe` (method) — Verifies format_usage_line on an empty UsageTotals renders the zero-cost line. <!--#d83460b5e44a1638-->
- `TestStepScopedAccumulator` (class) — Tests for the contextvars-based step usage scope (accumulate_step_usage / add_call_usage / current_step_usage), covering accumulation, nesting, isolation, and restoration. <!--#173ae0abb738c5e9-->
  - `TestStepScopedAccumulator.test_no_scope_current_is_none` (method) — Verifies current_step_usage() is None when no scope is active. <!--#8b770ffd65d213b4-->
  - `TestStepScopedAccumulator.test_add_call_usage_outside_scope_is_noop` (method) — Verifies add_call_usage is a safe no-op when called with no active scope. <!--#cf6e53dc79d69217-->
  - `TestStepScopedAccumulator.test_scope_accumulates_multiple_calls` (method) — Verifies an active scope sums multiple add_call_usage contributions into its accumulator. <!--#ae2a81908169b5bf-->
  - `TestStepScopedAccumulator.test_scope_accepts_dict_usage` (method) — Verifies add_call_usage accepts plain dict/mapping usage payloads within a scope. <!--#99d3b5b792aa2bbf-->
  - `TestStepScopedAccumulator.test_add_call_usage_ignores_none_and_garbage` (method) — Verifies add_call_usage silently ignores None and non-usage values while still folding valid ones. <!--#84ba9869d9645313-->
  - `TestStepScopedAccumulator.test_scope_restored_after_exit` (method) — Verifies the active scope is cleared back to None after the context manager exits. <!--#59fa3846028df6bb-->
  - `TestStepScopedAccumulator.test_nested_scopes_isolated` (method) — Verifies nested scopes are isolated so inner usage does not leak into the outer accumulator. <!--#b664adca4fba95a8-->
  - `TestStepScopedAccumulator.test_scope_restored_on_exception` (method) — Verifies the scope is restored to None even when the body raises an exception. <!--#1fa78021c116e851-->
- `TestUseStepUsageCrossThread` (class) — Tests for use_step_usage re-binding a parent accumulator across thread boundaries, the fix for DAG-parallel workers dropping usage in fresh contextvars contexts. <!--#ac6aae1c28ce9619-->
  - `TestUseStepUsageCrossThread.test_use_step_usage_none_is_noop` (method) — Verifies use_step_usage(None) binds no scope and leaves add_call_usage a no-op. <!--#c6d75453b36fd5ed-->
  - `TestUseStepUsageCrossThread.test_use_step_usage_binds_existing_accumulator` (method) — Verifies use_step_usage binds a given accumulator so contributions fold into it, then unbinds on exit. <!--#e0cabeb598eff632-->
  - `TestUseStepUsageCrossThread.test_worker_thread_without_rebind_does_not_see_scope` (method) — Reproduces the bug where a bare worker thread sees no scope and its usage is discarded. <!--#9c8450d64dfa4818-->
  - `TestUseStepUsageCrossThread.test_worker_thread_with_rebind_folds_into_parent` (method) — Verifies the fix where workers re-bind the captured accumulator via use_step_usage so their usage folds into the parent. <!--#aa468b0a544eab98-->
  - `TestUseStepUsageCrossThread.test_concurrent_folds_are_not_lost` (method) — Verifies many threads concurrently folding into one shared accumulator lose no updates due to serialized read-modify-write. <!--#3f756857e7e807ad-->

### `tests/test_transitive_reduction.py` (python) — Unit test suite for the transitive_reduce algorithm (from se3.engine.transitive_reduction), covering edge cases, non-reducible graphs (chains, diamonds, independent groups), removal of redundant transitive edges, input immutability, and preservation of extra fields and group ordering. <!--#1e7ab994e7cebc6a|869eab9a07c73c40-->
- `TestTransitiveReduceEmpty` (class) — Test class verifying transitive_reduce handles empty, single-group, and missing-depends_on-key inputs gracefully. <!--#7b69b3acd6043798-->
  - `TestTransitiveReduceEmpty.test_empty_groups` (method) — Asserts that reducing an empty list of groups returns an empty list. <!--#1f7509546b6fd20b-->
  - `TestTransitiveReduceEmpty.test_single_group_no_deps` (method) — Asserts a single group with no dependencies passes through unchanged. <!--#e7b5f6f178778cb5-->
  - `TestTransitiveReduceEmpty.test_single_group_missing_depends_on_key` (method) — Asserts a group lacking a depends_on key is preserved without that key being added. <!--#cc36462721d248b0-->
- `TestTransitiveReduceNoChange` (class) — Test class verifying graphs with no redundant edges (linear chains, diamonds, independent groups) are returned unchanged. <!--#d779151c586f3030-->
  - `TestTransitiveReduceNoChange.test_linear_chain_minimal` (method) — Asserts a minimal A→B→C chain with no redundant edges is unchanged. <!--#1bb1243b56655b1f-->
  - `TestTransitiveReduceNoChange.test_diamond_not_reducible` (method) — Asserts a diamond's two independent edges into D are both essential and not reduced. <!--#b9399ca447fc1374-->
  - `TestTransitiveReduceNoChange.test_two_independent_groups` (method) — Asserts two unconnected groups each retain empty dependencies. <!--#d21a215a0b5e578e-->
  - `TestTransitiveReduceNoChange.test_two_groups_single_edge` (method) — Asserts a single non-redundant edge between two groups is preserved. <!--#46378998972ebc74-->
- `TestTransitiveReduceRedundant` (class) — Test class verifying redundant transitive edges are removed across chains, complex DAGs, and multi-root structures. <!--#b78a583848180213-->
  - `TestTransitiveReduceRedundant.test_linear_chain_with_shortcut` (method) — Asserts a direct A→C edge is dropped when C is already reachable via A→B→C. <!--#ec21bdf86bf1c2d6-->
  - `TestTransitiveReduceRedundant.test_longer_chain_with_skip` (method) — Asserts redundant A and B edges into D collapse to just C in a four-node chain. <!--#3e5bccb3bbb3fb56-->
  - `TestTransitiveReduceRedundant.test_complex_dag_multiple_redundancies` (method) — Asserts the redundant A→D shortcut is removed while essential B→D and C→D edges remain. <!--#b48ada9dda1caa02-->
  - `TestTransitiveReduceRedundant.test_wide_fan_in_with_chain` (method) — Asserts both A→D and B→D shortcuts are removed when D is reachable through the C chain. <!--#26683ab239e65f3d-->
  - `TestTransitiveReduceRedundant.test_multiple_roots_with_redundancy` (method) — Asserts redundant root edges (R1, R2) into C are removed, leaving only A and B. <!--#d018e44a6c07a5f0-->
- `TestTransitiveReduceImmutability` (class) — Test class verifying transitive_reduce does not mutate its input and returns fresh objects. <!--#42856ab8b4a25552-->
  - `TestTransitiveReduceImmutability.test_does_not_mutate_input` (method) — Asserts the input groups list is unchanged after reduction by comparing against a deep copy. <!--#f24a0f4ca27664b4-->
  - `TestTransitiveReduceImmutability.test_returned_list_is_new_object` (method) — Asserts the returned list and its group dicts are new objects, not the inputs. <!--#c3748e7d3153390d-->
- `TestTransitiveReducePreservesFields` (class) — Test class verifying extra group fields and input ordering survive reduction. <!--#aea212cd65523f99-->
  - `TestTransitiveReducePreservesFields.test_extra_keys_preserved` (method) — Asserts non-dependency keys like name and tasks are preserved in the reduced output. <!--#31208ba89d2f1b42-->
  - `TestTransitiveReducePreservesFields.test_group_order_preserved` (method) — Asserts the output list preserves the input group order. <!--#ecbe42e4cab7d630-->

### `tests/test_why_comment_guard.py` (python) — Test module for invariant_check's why-comment deletion guard, verifying both the hard channel (deleted/rewritten WHY:/INVARIANT:-marked comments synthesize an anchored violation routing to REVISION_NEEDED, with same-file rewrite/net-count exemptions) and the advisory channel (plain-comment losses go through swallow-on-failure LLM triage into outputs only), plus the no-baseline skip and charter/prompt documentation of the marker and amendment-exemption conventions. <!--#8281c0016cace148|d684febda683edbb-->
- `_clear_recursion_guard` (function) — Fixture helper that unsets SE3_TEST_RUNNING so se3's recursion-guarded command paths aren't short-circuited while this module's tests drive them. <!--#e95495568df3726b-->

- `_install_fake_caller` (function) — Helper that monkeypatches invariant_check.LLMCaller with a scripted fake returning queued responses and recording prompts/call-count. <!--#48f66cdee783b441-->
- `test_helper_reports_deleted_comment` (function) — Asserts _deleted_comments_by_file reports a marked comment that was removed from the working tree relative to baseline. <!--#30876d34f61dd665-->
- `test_helper_reports_rewritten_comment` (function) — Asserts a rewritten marked comment is reported as deleted because its old body no longer appears. <!--#1be207f4f8b628f2-->
- `test_helper_skips_new_file` (function) — Asserts a file that never existed at baseline lost no comments and is silently skipped by the helper. <!--#d7d578da94cd20fd-->
- `test_helper_no_baseline_returns_empty` (function) — Asserts _deleted_comments_by_file returns an empty result when no baseline commit is provided. <!--#72a57724e493dd96-->
- `test_helper_deleted_file_loses_all_comments` (function) — Asserts a file deleted outright is reported as losing every marked comment it carried at baseline. <!--#4f51b9f30611a013-->
- `test_helper_unchanged_comment_not_reported` (function) — Asserts a marked comment that survives verbatim (only surrounding code changed) is not reported as deleted. <!--#3588ef3a41013f25-->
- `test_marked_comment_deletion_triggers_revision` (function) — End-to-end test that deleting a marked WHY comment yields REVISION_NEEDED with a synthesized hard violation anchored on the deleted body and restore/redeclare fix guidance. <!--#7ed6b3a02561dc2e-->
- `test_restored_marked_comment_passes` (function) — Asserts the handler completes cleanly when the marked comment is retained and only the annotated code changed. <!--#8db67bb19d01ff11-->
- `test_rewritten_marked_comment_with_updated_rationale_passes` (function) — Asserts rewriting a marked comment into a new marked comment (declared update) does not block the flow. <!--#7a10b3e6c9bf698d-->
- `test_rewritten_marked_comment_with_wholly_new_rationale_passes` (function) — Regression asserting a marked-comment rewrite with almost no word overlap over the same code slot is still recognized as a re-declaration and passes. <!--#345c2de7f0a00de6-->
- `test_same_file_marked_addition_covers_deletion_one_to_one` (function) — Asserts a same-file marked addition exempts a marked deletion one-to-one (net-count rule), leaving the marked-comment count intact and not blocking. <!--#b2cf421f9f57faca-->
- `test_sibling_marked_comment_in_same_slot_does_not_swallow_deletion` (function) — Regression asserting a verbatim-surviving sibling marked comment does not exempt a genuinely-deleted sibling in the same slot, which still triggers REVISION_NEEDED. <!--#79152e89fe8e251a-->
- `test_both_siblings_rewritten_in_same_slot_are_exempt` (function) — Asserts that when both protected comments over the same code are genuinely rewritten, each old body is exempted by its own replacement. <!--#ba8bdea59ab66bf5-->
- `test_partial_rewrite_in_shared_slot_guards_all_dropped` (function) — Asserts one-to-one pairing exempts only the most-similar deletion when two are dropped but a single new marked comment is added, guarding the unpaired loss. <!--#d44c3dc1aa15a838-->
- `test_rewritten_marked_exemptions_pairs_rewrite_in_place` (function) — Asserts _rewritten_marked_exemptions pairs a deleted marked comment with a new marked comment in the same file, ignoring plain unmarked comments. <!--#ee60f386b03d354e-->
- `test_rewrite_of_comment_and_its_code_together_is_exempt` (function) — Finding-1 regression asserting a marked comment rewritten together with its annotated code is still exempted by same-file pairing. <!--#eb8bd79f70ff479f-->
- `test_eof_marked_comment_rewrite_is_exempt` (function) — Finding-2 regression asserting an end-of-file marked comment with no following code can still be re-declared and exempted. <!--#7e47d2e547e8f30a-->
- `test_cross_file_marked_move_is_not_exempt` (function) — Asserts the same-file-only rule: a marked comment deleted from one file and reappearing in another leaves an unpaired deletion that triggers REVISION_NEEDED. <!--#4667262492202ad6-->
- `test_duplicate_marked_comment_one_rewritten_guards_the_other` (function) — Occurrence-accounting regression asserting two identical dropped marked comments with only one re-declaration exempt exactly one occurrence and guard the other. <!--#355e26734956b956-->
- `test_plain_comment_deletion_is_advisory_only` (function) — Asserts deleting a plain (unmarked) comment routes through an advisory LLM triage recorded in outputs but never becomes a hard violation or fix loop. <!--#7e29f0b4b90596f2-->
- `test_advisory_llm_failure_degrades_silently` (function) — Asserts a crashing advisory re-judge is swallowed and does not disturb the main audit's COMPLETED verdict. <!--#0169d45a8356467e-->
- `test_no_baseline_guard_silently_skips` (function) — Asserts that with no baseline commit the guard cannot diff and silently skips without calling the LLM or blocking. <!--#5b171e62e15a9b86-->
- `test_prompt_carries_amendment_exemption` (function) — Asserts the INVARIANT_CHECK_PROMPT documents the constitutional-amendment exemption scoped to task-directed charter changes. <!--#85a13e269064ea53-->
- `test_charter_declares_marker_prefix_convention` (function) — Asserts se3/charter.md documents the WHY:/INVARIANT: marker-prefix convention and references invariant_check. <!--#4b82d91b19182efa-->

### `tests/test_wire_metrics.py` (python) — Unit tests for the daemon's shared WireMetrics accountant, covering per-message-type byte/frame accumulation with a synthetic '__total__' roll-up, defensive snapshot copies, coercion of bad byte sizes to zero, counter reset, thread-safe concurrent recording, and an AST-based guard enforcing core/server import isolation. <!--#3a142aa197b439a1|cbd6cf441e18950d-->
- `test_record_and_snapshot_accumulate_by_type` (function) — Verifies that WireMetrics.record accumulates bytes and frame counts per message type and that snapshot() exposes a synthetic '__total__' roll-up across all types. <!--#1595c2a1752f867e-->
- `test_snapshot_is_a_copy` (function) — Asserts that snapshot() returns a defensive copy so mutating the returned dict cannot corrupt the accountant's internal state. <!--#5c9d95df602bea98-->
- `test_bad_nbytes_coerced_to_zero` (function) — Checks that invalid byte sizes (negative, None, non-int) are coerced to 0 bytes while still counting the frame. <!--#c5d1609fcb5cf103-->
- `test_reset_clears_counters` (function) — Confirms that reset() clears all per-type counters, leaving only a zeroed '__total__' entry in the snapshot. <!--#741a4bbff2c5173a-->
- `test_concurrent_record_is_thread_safe` (function) — Stress-tests concurrent record() calls from 8 threads to ensure the counters are thread-safe with no lost updates. <!--#cfa97846235431af-->
- `test_no_server_import` (function) — Enforces core/server isolation by AST-parsing the wire_metrics module to assert it never imports anything under se3.server. <!--#50730255ecd56531-->

### `tests/test_worktree_history_sidecar.py` (python) — Tests that DaemonHistoryReader correctly handles worktree sidecar history files (`.from-<branch>` jsonl variants) — folding primary and sidecar files into logical steps for id parsing, enumeration, and counting, while merging their records on read with distinct display step ids, per-physical-file incremental cursors, and safe handling of half-written tails. <!--#df931df6ecea9fc4|54bda54716beaf34-->
- `_write_jsonl` (function) — Test helper that writes a list of dicts as newline-delimited JSON to a file, creating parent directories as needed. <!--#18930ad89d1ea5fb-->
- `_append_jsonl` (function) — Test helper that appends a list of dicts as JSON lines to an existing jsonl file. <!--#b174bd6540498b15-->
- `_msg` (function) — Tiny factory building a `{role, content}` message dict for test records. <!--#67f68ff7e3aa1c72-->
- `_make_reader` (function) — Test helper constructing a `DaemonHistoryReader` whose project-roots provider returns the given roots. <!--#808724bfc5456a05-->
- `_flow_dir` (function) — Test helper that creates and returns the `se3/history/<flow_id>` directory under a root. <!--#2bc670cdd788413e-->
- `test_logical_step_id_strips_sidecar_suffix` (function) — Verifies `_logical_step_id` reduces primary and sidecar file names to the bare logical step id and leaves non-jsonl names unchanged. <!--#ca19f99c1adbf894-->
- `test_display_step_id_keeps_sidecar_marker` (function) — Verifies that _display_step_id strips the .jsonl suffix but preserves the .from-<branch> sidecar marker (including hash-disambiguated ones), so a step's primary file and each sidecar map to distinct frontend-facing step ids. <!--#2b880caf012d6101-->
- `test_parse_step_type_strips_sidecar_suffix` (function) — Verifies `parse_step_type_from_step_id` extracts the step type from logical ids as well as raw primary/sidecar file names. <!--#c8102b38ca7efffe-->
- `test_iter_history_jsonl_includes_sidecars_sorted` (function) — Asserts `_iter_history_jsonl` enumerates both primary files and their sidecars in sorted order. <!--#ea418105857d9ccf-->
- `test_count_jsonl_counts_logical_steps` (function) — Asserts `_count_jsonl` collapses multiple physical files (primary + sidecars) into a count of distinct logical steps. <!--#c43040e8aed2e32d-->
- `test_read_flow_merges_primary_and_sidecar` (function) — Asserts that read_flow returns all records from a step's primary file and its sidecar in order without loss or duplication, with distinct display step ids preventing (step_id, ordinal) collisions and a cursor keyed per physical file. <!--#d49ebe2dd91f7024-->
- `test_read_flow_sidecar_only_step` (function) — Checks that a step whose records exist only in a sidecar file is still fully read, keeping the branch marker in its step id while parsing the folded logical step type. <!--#a0acb25b514509b6-->
- `test_read_flow_incremental_cursor_advances_over_sidecar` (function) — Verifies incremental reads: after appending to a sidecar, a cursor-based re-read returns only the new records in append mode, advances the sidecar's cursor, and a further read with no new writes yields nothing. <!--#a383adfe68c77820-->
- `test_read_flow_multiple_sidecars_for_one_step` (function) — Confirms that a step with multiple hash-disambiguated sidecars reads all files in order, with each physical file emitting a distinct step id, unique (step_id, ordinal) keys, and independent cursor entries. <!--#c0194fab2108cbe7-->
- `test_read_flow_first_record_nonempty_with_midwrite_sidecar_tail` (function) — Verifies a half-written (truncated) sidecar line is held back rather than consumed mid-stream, then read in full once completed, with the cursor never advancing past it prematurely. <!--#b00e44a639a043f4-->

### `tests/test_worktree_paused_history_reconcile.py` (python) — Regression lock for issue #287 (worktree discovery chat going blank): builds a paused `--worktree` flow's real two-root on-disk history, pins `DaemonHistoryReader.read_flow` to distinguish an unresolvable root from a genuinely empty flow, and drives a self-heal reconcile through the real `/api/history/{flow_id}` endpoint with a fake daemon socket to assert that a `full` reconcile frame may only ever add records — never roll the cached bundle back to zero — while still applying frames that bring more. <!--#0150428cda72306c|c813e924ad2de13e-->
- `_line` (function) — Tiny helper that builds a `{role, content}` chat-line dict used as the message payload of a history record. <!--#2b2d6e3857a596de-->
- `_wire` (function) — Wraps a chat line into a wire-shaped discovery history record (`step_id`/`step_type`/`ordinal`/`message`) for ordinal `n`. <!--#e465cae66c0b24f1-->
- `_write_jsonl` (function) — Writes a list of records as a JSONL file at `path`, creating parent directories as needed. <!--#4b264541129f2baf-->
- `_write_engine_json` (function) — Plants a live `se3/state/engine.json` for `FLOW_ID` under a root with the given status, so the reader classifies the flow as `source="active"` rather than history-only. <!--#a5174a6b28775aae-->
- `_build_two_root_history` (function) — Lays out the real on-disk shape of a paused `--worktree` discovery — round 1 in the main repo's history, rounds 1+2 in the worktree's live JSONL — and returns `(main_root, worktree_root)`. <!--#63bd6a34191ff8d9-->
- `test_read_flow_merges_both_roots_for_a_worktree_flow` (function) — Happy path: a cursorless `read_flow` against the authoritative worktree root returns a `full` frame merging both roots (all of round 2). <!--#f5f0b068a4f02dc6-->
- `test_read_flow_unresolvable_root_falls_back_to_the_registry_walk` (function) — Issue #287 hop 1: when the given project root resolves no history directory, `read_flow` must fall back to the registry walk (returning the real records with a warning) instead of emitting a pseudo-empty `full` frame. <!--#7487659303c1cdee-->
- `test_read_flow_truly_unknown_flow_returns_empty_with_a_warning` (function) — The honest-empty case: an unknown flow id yields an empty `full` frame, but only alongside a "no history directory resolved" warning that distinguishes it from a resolution failure. <!--#926385695f021797-->
- `test_read_active_flows_keeps_streaming_a_paused_worktree_flow` (function) — Locks `_is_active_status` so a PAUSED worktree flow stays in `read_active_flows` and later rounds still arrive as append deltas during the pending-reply window. <!--#e2c0bbd6220aceb3-->
- `_FakeDaemon` (class) — Test double for a connected daemon over the real `/ws` socket, serving `HISTORY_REQUEST` replies from a mutable record list on a background thread so a blocking `TestClient.get` can trigger a reconcile. <!--#4e48bad91e46cec7-->
  - `_FakeDaemon.__init__` (method) — Opens the websocket, completes the authenticated HELLO/WELCOME handshake, seeds the reply payload with round 1, and starts the receive-loop thread. <!--#b59289f0fa9a6438-->
  - `_FakeDaemon._serve` (method) — Background receive loop that counts incoming `HISTORY_REQUEST` messages and answers each with a `full` HISTORY_DATA frame built from the current `reply_records`. <!--#f24e6fc5a1143dc5-->
  - `_FakeDaemon.push_full` (method) — Unprompted push of a `full` HISTORY_DATA frame for `FLOW_ID`, simulating the daemon's live history broadcast. <!--#5fdbcf94bf3d80f0-->
  - `_FakeDaemon.report_paused_worktree_flow` (method) — Sends a STATUS_UPDATE putting `FLOW_ID` in the state #287 requires — `paused` under a worktree project root — which is what opens the server's self-heal reconcile window. <!--#2bff15735e3afd91-->
  - `_FakeDaemon.close` (method) — Stops the receive thread and tears down the websocket context. <!--#8425f1499b69c7eb-->
- `client_and_app` (function) — Pytest fixture yielding an authenticated `TestClient` plus its FastAPI app, already logged in, for the endpoint-level reconcile tests. <!--#c78c8fc0ec5446bd-->
- `test_paused_worktree_reconcile_must_not_empty_the_cached_bundle` (function) — The #287 regression lock: driven through the real `/api/history/{flow_id}` endpoint, a self-heal reconcile whose daemon reply is empty must never roll the cached bundle (or its generation) back to zero records. <!--#13ae1ec5bf02530e-->
- `test_reconcile_that_brings_more_records_still_replaces` (function) — The other half of the invariant: a reconcile that brings *more* records (round 2) must still apply and grow the cached bundle, so any #287 fix cannot simply stop honouring reconcile frames. <!--#4071cb8950b17821-->

### `tests/test_worktree_project_exclusion.py` (python) — Test module verifying that a `se3 run --worktree` copy directory is attributed back to its main project root—so it is excluded from project registries/roots and its cloned issues are counted once—across the supervisor's path resolution, external process scan, aggregator/snapshot, live daemon seam, and startup registry sanitize. <!--#ffc2e97dccae4a55|edbb91e3380f410c-->
