### `tests/commands/merge/test_runtime_sync.py` (python) — Regression test suite for the runtime_sync merge-hardening fixes (G6/Tasks 30-33), covering symlink-destination rejection in atomic writes, lenient-vs-strict rollback on unexpected failures, sidecar self-collision filtering for idempotent repeated syncs, and bounded chunked read/write I/O with iteration/byte/duration caps. <!--#a5a653a5851d5b4f|04b4047a774a4cd0-->
- `_make_sync_call` (function) — Test helper that returns a callable invoking sync_branch_runtime with the per-branch worktree lookup stubbed to a fixed source directory. <!--#e2f317124895190d-->
- `TestSymlinkDestinationRejected` (class) — Test class verifying _atomic_write_bytes refuses symlinked destinations (O_NOFOLLOW guard) to block path-takeover/TOCTOU attacks while still allowing normal writes. <!--#e4483b2104f727ee-->
  - `TestSymlinkDestinationRejected.test_planted_symlink_to_external_file_is_rejected` (method) — Asserts a symlink at the destination pointing to an external file causes ELOOP and leaves the external file untouched. <!--#18e14d502404429b-->
  - `TestSymlinkDestinationRejected.test_planted_symlink_to_inside_target_tree_is_rejected` (method) — Asserts even an in-tree symlink destination is uniformly rejected with ELOOP and its target file is left unchanged. <!--#cb791fbdd3ddec7a-->
  - `TestSymlinkDestinationRejected.test_normal_write_still_works` (method) — Regression check that the symlink guard does not break a normal write to a fresh destination. <!--#372990f2b5d8bcbe-->
  - `TestSymlinkDestinationRejected.test_write_overwrite_regular_file_still_works` (method) — Regression check that the symlink guard still permits overwriting an existing regular file. <!--#5b2f690e4f021265-->
  - `TestSymlinkDestinationRejected.test_toctou_post_write_recheck_catches_late_symlink_swap` (method) — Simulates a symlink planted mid-write and asserts the post-write recheck still rejects it with ELOOP, protecting the external file. <!--#c2b78c0c5a281a09-->
- `TestLenientModePreservesSuccess` (class) — Test class verifying that when an unexpected exception escapes per-file handlers, lenient mode preserves already-succeeded work while strict mode still rolls everything back. <!--#f2d7c1598b401941-->
  - `TestLenientModePreservesSuccess.test_already_copied_files_preserved_on_unexpected_failure` (method) — Asserts that in lenient mode a successfully copied file survives a later propagated exception that fires the outer except net. <!--#0bb96c45e49d60c7-->
  - `TestLenientModePreservesSuccess.test_strict_mode_still_rolls_back` (method) — Asserts strict mode keeps its all-or-nothing promise by rolling back the copied file and the se3/ root on a propagated failure. <!--#bb383c7344d6d7d2-->
  - `TestLenientModePreservesSuccess.test_lenient_mode_preserves_already_written_sidecars` (method) — Asserts a sidecar written before an uncaught RuntimeError remains on disk in lenient mode. <!--#fee761d935614a70-->
- `TestSidecarSelfCollisionFiltered` (class) — Test class verifying source-side sidecar-named files are filtered at collection time so repeated syncs stay idempotent without accumulating .from-A.from-B chains. <!--#0e615694b772b8df-->
  - `TestSidecarSelfCollisionFiltered.test_is_sidecar_filename_pattern` (method) — Unit-tests the _is_sidecar_filename regex against positive sidecar shapes (plain, hash-disambiguated, safe-label) and negative non-sidecar names. <!--#1174d91c8a23f631-->
  - `TestSidecarSelfCollisionFiltered.test_source_sidecar_files_are_filtered` (method) — Asserts leftover sidecar files in the source worktree are neither copied nor recorded as skipped, never reaching the destination. <!--#df64f32db9a613a0-->
  - `TestSidecarSelfCollisionFiltered.test_repeated_sync_is_idempotent_no_chain_accumulation` (method) — Asserts running sync three times yields exactly one sidecar with no nested .from-feature.from- chains. <!--#09b64566c9375805-->
  - `TestSidecarSelfCollisionFiltered.test_sidecar_glob_pattern_files_skipped` (method) — Asserts sidecar leftovers under glob-pattern paths (e.g. state/summary-*) are also filtered out. <!--#1995d8aa89b2aca0-->
- `TestBoundedReadAndWrite` (class) — Test class verifying the chunked read/write loops enforce iteration, byte-size, and duration caps so hostile or malformed files cannot hang the merge. <!--#77aaa6c8c16a7675-->
  - `TestBoundedReadAndWrite.test_bounded_read_byte_cap` (method) — Asserts _bounded_read_chunks raises OSError(EFBIG) once the total-byte cap is exceeded. <!--#6a7baa01c6db66ab-->
  - `TestBoundedReadAndWrite.test_bounded_read_iteration_cap` (method) — Asserts the read iteration cap raises EFBIG independently of total bytes read. <!--#ee5b76d24688595d-->
  - `TestBoundedReadAndWrite.test_bounded_read_duration_cap` (method) — Asserts an exceeded read duration deadline raises OSError(ETIMEDOUT). <!--#04a3cc10e9ea7124-->
  - `TestBoundedReadAndWrite.test_bounded_read_returns_full_content_within_caps` (method) — Regression check that bounded reads return the full file content when within all caps. <!--#610f47729155ee41-->
  - `TestBoundedReadAndWrite.test_bounded_write_zero_progress_raises` (method) — Asserts a no-progress os.write (returns 0) raises OSError(EIO) on a single attempt rather than spinning forever. <!--#e9f38eaf63b81e40-->
  - `TestBoundedReadAndWrite.test_bounded_write_duration_cap` (method) — Asserts _bounded_write_all honors the time deadline by raising ETIMEDOUT. <!--#cdb80a3f318f9b88-->
  - `TestBoundedReadAndWrite.test_bounded_write_empty_content_no_op` (method) — Asserts writing empty content is a no-op that returns immediately without touching the fd. <!--#6d59a9ff7ffba05f-->
  - `TestBoundedReadAndWrite.test_symlink_loop_bounded_via_read_caps` (method) — Asserts an oversized source file is skipped (lenient mode absorbs the OSError) so the merge completes without hanging. <!--#380deceb655fb6e7-->
- `TestIdempotentEndToEnd` (class) — Test class with end-to-end sanity checks that the four hardening fixes compose so repeated syncs remain idempotent. <!--#76d8ec44d199c97b-->
  - `TestIdempotentEndToEnd.test_repeated_clean_sync_is_no_op` (method) — Asserts a second sync of identical content is an idempotent skip with no copy, collision, or sidecar. <!--#b1c3dd8fcefd7d67-->
  - `TestIdempotentEndToEnd.test_repeated_collision_sync_idempotent` (method) — Asserts a conflicting-content sync creates one sidecar initially, then registers idempotent bypasses on repeat runs with no chain or hash-suffix accumulation. <!--#a2895185720373bd-->

  - `TestRedactDiff.test_diff_empty` (method) — Asserts redacting an empty diff returns an empty string. <!--#e5a3275de7d5b496-->

- `TestRedactConfig` (class) — Test class verifying the RedactConfig dataclass default field values. <!--#ae428e07fc949da8-->

### `tests/commands/merge/test_version_collision_regression.py` (python) — End-to-end regression suite freezing the G9 version-collision accident (two concurrent worktree sessions off one baseline both baking 11.12.0, one changelog entry lost), asserting through the real se3 merge adapter and reconcile()/commit-guard libraries that concurrent sessions now land distinct monotonic versions, no-op/ancestor merges still reconcile, resume is idempotent, and the non-worktree drift guard recomputes to prevent collisions. <!--#e48274119f9c94cc|b000938cd303a03d-->
- `_git` (function) — Test helper that runs a git subcommand in a given repo root with output captured and check=True. <!--#9f1bc200ef078687-->
- `_make_project` (function) — Builds a git-initialized project fixture with committed pyproject.toml, VERSIONS.md, and README at a chosen baseline version (default 11.11.2). <!--#8b3ac218202f05de-->
- `_default_branch` (function) — Test helper returning the repo's current branch name via git rev-parse. <!--#32a8fa10d61d713c-->
- `_make_feature_with_intent` (function) — Creates a flow branch off a given base carrying a committed code change plus a version-intent file (bullet + bump hint, no number), simulating a de-versioned worktree session. <!--#1a5b2b27ee4e9775-->
- `_pyproject_version` (function) — Test helper reading the project's current version from disk. <!--#326708a226229629-->
- `_versions_text` (function) — Test helper returning the full text of the project's VERSIONS.md changelog. <!--#09d294b01676b405-->
- `TestConcurrentWorktreeCollision` (class) — Regression suite proving two concurrent worktree sessions off one baseline get distinct, monotonic versions with both changelog entries surviving under their own headers. <!--#e843230da0f26d2e-->
  - `TestConcurrentWorktreeCollision.test_two_concurrent_minor_sessions_do_not_share_a_version` (method) — Asserts two sequentially-merged minor sessions off 11.11.2 reconcile to distinct 11.12.0 and 11.13.0 with both bullets and both intents consumed once. <!--#b640dd540167102c-->
  - `TestConcurrentWorktreeCollision.test_changelog_entries_are_filed_under_distinct_versions` (method) — Asserts each session's changelog bullet lands under a different `## <version>` block, proving neither collapsed via version-number dedup. <!--#20f5fbdd8ea49268-->
- `_owning_version_header` (function) — Test helper that walks the changelog top-down to find the `## <version>` header a given bullet line sits under. <!--#6ae25c110d5bf001-->
- `TestNoOpMergeReconcile` (class) — Suite proving reconcile runs unconditionally and bumps from outstanding intents even for already-ancestor/no-merge-commit shapes. <!--#6f2903f2f80ef521-->
  - `TestNoOpMergeReconcile.test_already_ancestor_merge_still_advances_version` (method) — Fast-forwards an unconsumed intent onto master (no merge commit) and asserts se3 merge's reconcile still advances the version to 11.12.0. <!--#6fbdae9be52d9ba0-->
  - `TestNoOpMergeReconcile.test_intent_on_master_with_no_branch_still_reconciles` (method) — Asserts reconcile() derives and applies a version deterministically from an intent already committed on master with no branch to merge. <!--#002f4bd64f6ab859-->
- `TestReconcileResumeIdempotent` (class) — Suite proving a re-entered reconcile never double-bumps, backed by both the consumed flag and a git-durable reconcile-commit trailer. <!--#cae1fb119221b327-->
  - `TestReconcileResumeIdempotent.test_reconcile_twice_does_not_double_bump` (method) — Asserts a second reconcile after a successful one is a clean already-reconciled noop with no further version advance. <!--#4d31ff7d9de3330f-->
  - `TestReconcileResumeIdempotent.test_reconcile_idempotent_even_if_consumed_flag_lost` (method) — Asserts the git-durable reconcile-commit trailer alone short-circuits a re-bump when the on-disk consumed flag is cleared (crash-window simulation). <!--#77e1fb23cd1f91dd-->
- `TestReconcileCommitFailureRecovery` (class) — Suite proving a reconcile whose git commit fails or crashes rolls back / recovers on resume, never leaving a half-applied uncommitted bump. <!--#728a931f8a909a67-->
  - `TestReconcileCommitFailureRecovery.test_failed_commit_rolls_back_and_resume_lands_version` (method) — Injects a failing _commit_reconcile and asserts the first attempt rolls back cleanly while the resume commits and lands the version. <!--#52c54aa26e837951-->
  - `TestReconcileCommitFailureRecovery.test_resume_recovers_consumed_but_uncommitted_intent` (method) — Simulates on-disk writes + consumed flag but no reconcile commit, asserting resume restores to HEAD, recomputes, and commits rather than trusting the uncommitted flag. <!--#da2cffe2105ef9a0-->
  - `TestReconcileCommitFailureRecovery.test_resume_recovers_dirty_version_file_without_consumed_flag` (method) — Simulates only a dirty version-file write (no changelog, no flag) and asserts resume reads its base from committed 11.11.2 and reconciles to 11.12.0 without double-bumping. <!--#8679c2665b3db693-->
- `TestNonWorktreeDriftGuard` (class) — Suite exercising _guard_version_race directly to verify the direct-run commit drift guard recomputes, passes through, or halts on concurrent disk drift. <!--#090c1db3612b4710-->
  - `TestNonWorktreeDriftGuard._make_flow_with_version_analyze` (method) — Fixture builder returning a non-worktree FlowInstance carrying a completed VERSION_ANALYZE step with given current/baseline/suggested versions. <!--#35afed02bcffa06d-->
  - `TestNonWorktreeDriftGuard._commit_step` (method) — Fixture builder returning a COMMIT step seeded with suggested version, baseline, and patch bump inputs. <!--#102f42e4e89815ee-->
  - `TestNonWorktreeDriftGuard.test_drift_recomputes_to_avoid_collision` (method) — Asserts that when disk drifted past the baseline the guard re-runs version_analyze against the drifted version and returns the fresh non-colliding number. <!--#57174ca35d242e2f-->
  - `TestNonWorktreeDriftGuard.test_no_drift_passes_target_through_unchanged` (method) — Asserts the guard is a pure pass-through (no re-analysis) when disk equals the recorded baseline. <!--#5d423d2f5b484891-->
  - `TestNonWorktreeDriftGuard.test_drift_reanalysis_returning_disk_version_halts` (method) — Asserts the guard raises rather than returns when re-analysis against the drifted baseline still yields the colliding disk version. <!--#d325bf87d31faaa1-->
- `TestFlowWroteVersionBlobDetection` (class) — Suite proving own-replay detection uses the Flow-trailer commit's version-file blob rather than an optional Version: commit line. <!--#65e1e620e9af8200-->
  - `TestFlowWroteVersionBlobDetection._git` (method) — Static test helper running a captured, checked git subcommand in a repo root. <!--#3d92d7d8e87ee41d-->
  - `TestFlowWroteVersionBlobDetection.test_own_replay_detected_without_version_commit_line` (method) — Asserts _flow_wrote_version matches the flow's own commit purely from its Flow: trailer and version-file blob, while rejecting other versions and other flow ids. <!--#33562d0c808271b1-->
- `TestNonWorktreeCommitHandlerDriftGuard` (class) — Suite exercising Change D through the real commit_handler wiring against live git repos: in-lock disk re-read, drift detection, recompute, pass-through, and halt. <!--#e2072b82f5da4568-->
  - `TestNonWorktreeCommitHandlerDriftGuard._make_direct_flow` (method) — Fixture builder returning a non-worktree FlowInstance with completed VERSION_ANALYZE and pending COMMIT steps plus the commit step reference. <!--#e31c07603ce2bfbf-->
  - `TestNonWorktreeCommitHandlerDriftGuard.test_commit_handler_recomputes_on_concurrent_disk_drift` (method) — Asserts commit_handler re-reads a concurrently-published 10.7.1, recomputes past it via version_analyze, and lands 10.7.2 on disk. <!--#3470d98a0bd981c7-->
  - `TestNonWorktreeCommitHandlerDriftGuard.test_commit_handler_no_drift_writes_resolved_target` (method) — Asserts commit_handler writes the resolved 10.7.1 without re-analysis when disk still matches version_analyze's observed current_version. <!--#b9f9a12608fc7b4b-->
  - `TestNonWorktreeCommitHandlerDriftGuard.test_commit_handler_own_session_advance_is_not_drift` (method) — Asserts the guard compares disk against version_analyze's observed current_version (not pre_session_version), so own-session advances are not treated as drift and 10.8.0 lands verbatim. <!--#51d7272560078532-->
  - `TestNonWorktreeCommitHandlerDriftGuard.test_commit_handler_halts_when_reanalysis_still_collides` (method) — Asserts commit_handler fails and writes nothing when the in-lock recompute still returns the concurrent flow's released version, leaving the file and HEAD unchanged. <!--#f9b9334944b043cb-->

## `tests/core/` — Test suite for the core-utilities module, currently exercising the `truncate_preview` string helper across passthrough, ellipsis truncation, unicode/newline handling, and custom max_length/ellipsis edge cases. <!--#c56348f261104338|a803a15a966939d0-->

### `tests/core/__init__.py` (python) — Package init marker for the core-utilities test suite, declaring the tests/core directory as a Python package. <!--#ac166613d2af2787|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `tests/core/test_utils.py` (python) — Unit tests for the core `truncate_preview` utility, covering empty/short/exact-length passthrough, ellipsis truncation, unicode handling, custom max_length and ellipsis parameters, and edge cases like ellipsis longer than max_length. <!--#dbba325123f257ec|ac06f7bbf86b6eb6-->
- `TestTruncatePreview` (class) — Test class grouping all cases that verify truncate_preview correctly shortens strings with an ellipsis under various length and parameter conditions. <!--#571f10d0603d279e-->
  - `TestTruncatePreview.test_empty_string_returns_empty` (method) — Asserts that passing an empty string returns an empty string. <!--#b15a98eac9df3ffb-->
  - `TestTruncatePreview.test_shorter_than_limit_returns_unchanged` (method) — Verifies a string shorter than max_length is returned as the same unchanged object. <!--#7c6c7ebe7f3ceaa5-->
  - `TestTruncatePreview.test_exact_length_returns_unchanged` (method) — Verifies a string exactly at the length limit is returned unchanged and uncopied. <!--#2604b68abae5e47d-->
  - `TestTruncatePreview.test_exceeding_limit_truncates_with_ellipsis` (method) — Checks that an over-length string is truncated and suffixed with an ellipsis to exactly max_length. <!--#329ec84906f2f85a-->
  - `TestTruncatePreview.test_unicode_characters_handled_correctly` (method) — Ensures CJK and emoji characters are each counted as one when truncating. <!--#f412c9818111c458-->
  - `TestTruncatePreview.test_custom_max_length_parameter` (method) — Confirms a custom max_length value produces the expected truncated output length. <!--#19a6bd6fe9c9ff9c-->
  - `TestTruncatePreview.test_custom_ellipsis_string` (method) — Confirms a custom ellipsis string is appended in place of the default '...'. <!--#18100df0e1ecfa5e-->
  - `TestTruncatePreview.test_ellipsis_longer_than_max_length` (method) — Edge case verifying the ellipsis itself is truncated when longer than max_length. <!--#9d20b7ca57d104a0-->
  - `TestTruncatePreview.test_max_length_equals_ellipsis_length` (method) — Edge case where max_length equals the ellipsis length, returning just the ellipsis. <!--#b67ddc3e0e43333d-->
  - `TestTruncatePreview.test_single_character_max_length` (method) — Edge case verifying a max_length of 1 returns a single character. <!--#b381c3f0c86af42a-->
  - `TestTruncatePreview.test_newlines_in_text` (method) — Verifies multi-line text is truncated correctly to the exact length with ellipsis. <!--#653d67df336bff9a-->
  - `TestTruncatePreview.test_default_max_length_is_100` (method) — Confirms the default max_length is 100, truncating to 97 chars plus an ellipsis. <!--#4f1b399a237cf8f6-->

## `tests/daemon/` — Test package for the SE3 daemon layer, currently focused on `_push_history` cursor-commit semantics — verifying that history cursors advance only on successful HISTORY_DATA delivery, that dropped batches are re-sent as exact deltas, and that per-flow failures stay isolated within a complete, duplicate-free `ServerState` bundle. <!--#cf69c5f570150f38|85038ace41ff1004-->

### `tests/daemon/__init__.py` (python) — Empty package marker that makes tests/daemon a Python package for the daemon-related test modules. <!--#e3b0c44298fc1c14|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `tests/daemon/test_push_history_cursor_commit.py` (python) — Daemon test module covering `_push_history` cursor-commit semantics: using a real `DaemonHistoryReader`-backed provider stub and a websocket stub that can fail HISTORY_DATA sends, it asserts cursors only advance on successful delivery, dropped batches are re-read and re-sent as exact deltas next round, empty deltas still commit, one flow's failure does not roll back another's cursor, and the resulting `ServerState` bundle stays complete and duplicate-free. <!--#4058bb06d3674a3f|f374423835590228-->
- `_append_records` (function) — Test helper that appends the given message dicts as jsonl lines to `<root>/se3/history/<flow_id>/<step>`, creating the directory as needed. <!--#cd9a0e994164089e-->
- `_msg` (function) — Test helper building a minimal `{role, content}` message dict. <!--#bfbb3b9d14c45ada-->
- `_keys` (function) — Test helper extracting the `(step_id, ordinal)` identity tuples the frontend reconciles records by, used to assert no duplicates. <!--#62a330d402d6f088-->
- `_bodies` (function) — Test helper extracting each record's `message.content` string so assertions can compare frames by their message bodies. <!--#7f2face56564f9c2-->
- `_Provider` (class) — A minimal HistoryProvider stub wrapping a real `DaemonHistoryReader` over a fixed flow-id list, implementing only the three methods `_push_history` calls so tests exercise the active-flow read/send path with genuine cursor-based re-reads. <!--#7ae1a71893c7117b-->
  - `_Provider.__init__` (method) — Stores the real reader, the project root, and the fixed set of flow ids the provider serves. <!--#7ee4b07333ef65a1-->
  - `_Provider.build_index` (method) — Returns an empty index so tests exercise the active-flow path alone. <!--#17a111c8d858317e-->
  - `_Provider.read_active_flows` (method) — Reads each configured flow through the real `read_flow`, passing the per-flow cursor so retained water marks actually drive what is re-read. <!--#0390b9bb231c7169-->
  - `_Provider.live_flow_ids` (method) — Reports the fixed flow ids as the currently live flows. <!--#1ae3dea316cf1bf6-->
- `_StubWS` (class) — A websocket stub that records every sent frame and raises `ConnectionError` on `MSG_HISTORY_DATA` frames for flows listed in `fail_flows`, simulating a socket that dies mid-push. <!--#5e95dee39e9dbe6a-->
  - `_StubWS.__init__` (method) — Initialises the empty `fail_flows` set and the recorded-frames list. <!--#e8ef1ceeb2f5e2f5-->
  - `_StubWS.send` (method) — Parses the outgoing frame, raises `ConnectionError` if it is a HISTORY_DATA frame for a failing flow, and otherwise records it as delivered. <!--#537996454563aa28-->
  - `_StubWS.history_frames` (method) — Returns the payloads of all recorded HISTORY_DATA frames, optionally filtered to one flow id. <!--#057dede3883a820a-->
- `_client` (function) — Test helper constructing a `DaemonClient` wired to the given history provider and a trivial snapshot provider. <!--#3d5c1809b21d73a1-->
- `flow_env` (function) — Pytest fixture yielding a temporary project root plus flow id, step filename, and a `_Provider` over a real reader for a single discovery flow. <!--#215fb61724315b5b-->
- `test_failed_send_does_not_advance_cursor` (function) — Asserts that when the HISTORY_DATA send raises, no frame is delivered and the flow's cursor is not recorded, so the batch is not silently lost. <!--#6b5999180db386dd-->
- `test_failed_batch_is_re_read_and_re_sent_next_round` (function) — Asserts that after a failed send the same records are re-read from the retained water mark and shipped on the next round as the flow's first full frame. <!--#642028348dae1254-->
- `test_mid_flow_send_failure_re_sends_only_the_dropped_delta` (function) — Asserts that a send failure on a later append re-ships exactly that append delta on the next round rather than the whole flow. <!--#c90cac8e8aae5829-->
- `test_empty_delta_commits_and_send_is_skipped` (function) — Asserts that a flow with no new records sends no frame yet still keeps (commits) its cursor, since there is no delivery that could fail. <!--#52c065985165b9d6-->
- `test_successful_flow_cursor_survives_another_flows_failure` (function) — Asserts that a flow already shipped in the same round keeps its cursor when a later flow's send fails, avoiding needless duplicate traffic. <!--#d0a08c4b4344226c-->
- `test_server_bundle_is_complete_and_duplicate_free_after_a_drop` (function) — End-to-end invariant test replaying every delivered frame into a real `ServerState` and asserting the cached bundle is complete, duplicate-free by `(step_id, ordinal)`, and has the expected final cursor after a mid-flight send failure and re-send. <!--#1f442c83e41a385b-->

### `tests/engine/test_baseline_fix_memory.py` (python) — Unit tests for engine/baseline_fix_memory.py verifying that load_given_up tolerates missing/corrupt/schema-mismatched/non-mapping stores by returning an empty set, that record_given_up performs atomic writes and correctly accumulates attempts, preserves reasons, isolates entries, and clamps negatives, and that the store enforces an LRU bound at MAX_ENTRIES that keeps the most-recently-touched ids. <!--#2d432d577e6b4884|9d56640a2bdb373d-->

  - `TestLoadGivenUp.test_non_mapping_reads_empty` (method) — Asserts load_given_up returns an empty set when the store's top-level JSON is not a mapping. <!--#0c0ab6bcf4510ac2-->
- `TestRecordGivenUp` (class) — Test class verifying record_given_up's atomic write, empty-id no-op, attempt accumulation, reason preservation, entry isolation, and negative-attempt clamping. <!--#d301c4f2b80464f6-->
  - `TestRecordGivenUp.test_atomic_write_leaves_no_tempfile` (method) — Asserts record_given_up leaves no temp file behind after its atomic write. <!--#d6ec216aa4b4aa88-->
  - `TestRecordGivenUp.test_empty_ids_is_noop` (method) — Asserts recording an empty id list writes no file and stores nothing. <!--#bf1c73ab868c704a-->
  - `TestRecordGivenUp.test_attempts_accumulate` (method) — Asserts repeated records sum attempt counts and the latest non-null reason wins. <!--#99b2a123cf4f4d63-->
  - `TestRecordGivenUp.test_reason_preserved_when_none_on_rerecord` (method) — Asserts a re-record with reason=None keeps the previously stored reason while still accumulating attempts. <!--#3d2cbc5840bff03e-->
  - `TestRecordGivenUp.test_other_entries_preserved` (method) — Asserts recording a new id does not drop previously recorded entries. <!--#abde7743737cca5f-->
  - `TestRecordGivenUp.test_negative_attempts_clamped_to_zero` (method) — Asserts a negative attempts value is clamped to zero when stored. <!--#b14f44f3650c518d-->
- `TestLruBound` (class) — Test class verifying the store enforces MAX_ENTRIES by evicting least-recently-touched ids, with re-records refreshing recency. <!--#d5ac364cfd31a01f-->
  - `TestLruBound.test_trims_oldest_beyond_cap` (method) — Asserts that exceeding MAX_ENTRIES evicts the oldest ids and keeps the most-recently-added ones. <!--#7f3d8f66cd8d90e6-->
  - `TestLruBound.test_rerecord_refreshes_recency` (method) — Asserts re-recording an existing id refreshes its recency so a later eviction removes a different, now-oldest id. <!--#7d1996effce747e5-->

### `tests/engine/test_baseline_module.py` (python) — Unit-test suite for the engine's test-baseline module, covering baseline-key computation, the on-disk failure cache, the BaselineCapture launch/wait/kill lifecycle, and timeout resolution from se3.yaml. <!--#4c129004d2fa6fbd|b3659dca0fbfbf30-->

- `TestBaselineCache` (class) — Tests the on-disk baseline cache: round-trip, hit/miss semantics, corruption tolerance, bounding, and atomic writes. <!--#f26adb14f46c5b49-->
  - `TestBaselineCache.test_round_trip_hit` (method) — Asserts a saved failure set is read back identically for the same key. <!--#5997ca605e765382-->

### `tests/engine/test_confirm_revision_and_meta.py` (python) — Unit and integration tests for StateMachine confirm/review behavior — covering CONFIRM→REVISION_NEEDED transitions without infinite loops, nested review_result-based already-confirmed detection, the max_iterations-bounded cross-revision review loop, and _write_flow_meta writing se3/python version and creation timestamp into _meta.json. <!--#47de1a3de3f1d5a4|e3a9430cba581803-->
- `TestBugB_ConfirmRevisionNoInfiniteLoop` (class) — Test class verifying that a CONFIRM step returning REVISION_NEEDED transitions back to the reviewed step via transition_to_next rather than looping infinitely on CONFIRM. <!--#071168476dc0aae3-->

  - `TestBugB_ConfirmRevisionNoInfiniteLoop.test_confirm_revision_calls_transition_to_next` (method) — Calls transition_to_next directly on a REVISION_NEEDED confirm and asserts it returns the reviewed PLAN step reset to PENDING for revision. <!--#7cd72b8756552a50-->
- `TestBugC_AlreadyConfirmedDetection` (class) — Test class checking that already-confirmed detection reads the nested review_result structure so CONFIRM selects the correct (un-confirmed) step to review. <!--#6847a2d86522d7aa-->
  - `TestBugC_AlreadyConfirmedDetection.setup_method` (method) — Creates a temp project root with a PersistenceManager and StateMachine before each test. <!--#70bd64e57dffc13b-->
  - `TestBugC_AlreadyConfirmedDetection.teardown_method` (method) — Removes the temp directory after each test. <!--#c34398a3746e8dbf-->
  - `TestBugC_AlreadyConfirmedDetection.test_already_confirmed_detected_with_nested_review_result` (method) — Asserts a second CONFIRM reviews IMPLEMENT rather than the already-approved PLAN, given the prior confirm's nested review_result. <!--#8f68141922ae98aa-->
  - `TestBugC_AlreadyConfirmedDetection.test_rejected_confirm_does_not_mark_step_confirmed` (method) — Regression test that a rejected (approved=False) confirm does not shield its reviewed PLAN, so the next CONFIRM re-reviews PLAN instead of sliding to an unconfigured later step and hitting the human fallback. <!--#1a7ef6a314d09888-->
  - `TestBugC_AlreadyConfirmedDetection.test_not_yet_confirmed_step_is_found` (method) — Asserts that a step with no prior CONFIRM is selected for review by _build_step_inputs. <!--#16992e217f2b5b8b-->
- `TestBoundedCrossRevisionReview` (class) — Test class verifying the LLM review↔revise loop is bounded by max_iterations using the persisted cross-revision counter (flow.state.review_iterations). <!--#2f8c3a1afdd8b1fb-->

  - `TestBoundedCrossRevisionReview.test_integration_revision_loop_is_bounded` (method) — End-to-end test with an always-rejecting mock LLM asserting the loop stops at max_iterations, auto-approves, re-runs plan the expected number of times, and completes the flow. <!--#89385792de63fef5-->

### `tests/engine/test_conflict_resolver_prompt_size.py` (python) — Regression tests asserting that ConflictResolver's editor prompt stays small and content-independent — bounded under 20k chars for huge conflict files, byte-identical across 5 MiB and 50 MiB inputs, stripped of base/ours/theirs/working file contents, while still carrying paths, hunk ranges, the `git show :2:` hint, and the binary-file short-circuit. <!--#c664e86e5e143ca0|580abb47f5accd27-->

- `test_prompt_size_is_independent_of_content_size` (function) — Asserts prompts built from 5 MiB and 50 MiB conflict files are byte-identical, proving content size never leaks into the prompt. <!--#9329f74a5ae396b9-->
- `test_prompt_omits_three_way_contents` (function) — Asserts none of the base/ours/theirs/working sentinel markers appear in the prompt, confirming three-way file contents are excluded. <!--#c50d6fbac60068d8-->
- `test_prompt_keeps_paths_hunks_and_git_show_hint` (function) — Asserts the prompt still carries the actionable metadata — absolute file path, hunk line ranges, and the `git show :2:` retrieval hint. <!--#5208fca8c1531865-->
- `test_binary_file_branch_is_unchanged` (function) — Asserts binary conflict files still render the `[BINARY FILE` marker and short-circuit before the hunk listing. <!--#c35e72ce2d27e5e5-->

### `tests/engine/test_docs_updater.py` (python) — Unit tests for the docs_updater's VERSIONS.md changelog handling, verifying that colliding version blocks are merged rather than swallowed, verbatim rewrites stay idempotent, and head-blank accumulation is drained to a single separator and kept stable across repeated inserts. <!--#b0aebae65414ab47|715abec5e013d908-->
- `_default_updater` (function) — Pytest helper fixture-builder that returns a DocumentationUpdater pinned to the built-in default entry template (by monkeypatching the template path to a nonexistent file) so tests exercise insertion/merge mechanics independent of the packaged versions_md.md. <!--#79a0d56ce8a0483d-->

  - `TestMergeIntoExistingVersion.test_new_entry_merged_not_swallowed` (method) — Asserts a second bullet added to an existing version block is appended after the first (single header, both bullets survive in order), covering concurrent flows landing on the same version. <!--#9241b2e11c1f75b7-->
  - `TestMergeIntoExistingVersion.test_merge_preserves_older_history` (method) — Asserts merging a bullet into the newest version block leaves older version blocks untouched and keeps the merged bullet inside its own block. <!--#eb7474fefe8cabbe-->

- `TestNoBlankAccumulation` (class) — Test class ensuring repeated inserts don't accumulate blank lines in the file head and that any pre-existing blank-line accumulation is drained to a single blank between title and first entry. <!--#366e9f41cd146ff5-->
  - `TestNoBlankAccumulation.test_repeated_inserts_do_not_grow_head` (method) — Asserts five successive inserts keep exactly one blank line after the title and never produce a run of three consecutive blank lines. <!--#60fd0a1b5bc890f7-->
  - `TestNoBlankAccumulation.test_existing_head_accumulation_is_drained` (method) — Asserts an existing ~89-blank-line head is collapsed to a single blank on the next insert while preserving prior entries and avoiding triple blanks. <!--#0b9a392b40511c02-->
- `TestHeadCleanupIdempotent` (class) — Test class checking that head-blank cleanup is stable across repeated inserts and that the _normalize_head_blanks helper is directly idempotent. <!--#911a79c57e3f0f4e-->
  - `TestHeadCleanupIdempotent.test_cleanup_is_stable` (method) — Asserts that after the first insert drains an oversized head, a second no-op insert of the same version and bullet leaves the file byte-stable with a single head blank. <!--#d95281594d64578d-->
  - `TestHeadCleanupIdempotent.test_normalize_head_blanks_directly_idempotent` (method) — Asserts calling _normalize_head_blanks twice yields the same result and collapses the head to title, one blank line, then the first version header. <!--#f49f59bf0ac520bd-->

### `tests/engine/test_git_tags.py` (python) — Unit tests for the git_tags engine module, exercising version-tag naming, semver bump/tag decision helpers, commit-subject extraction, and annotated-tag creation against throwaway git repos, including typed VersionTagError failures that surface the tag, target commit, and git stderr. <!--#8e1225cb3292ca1a|18e07c55ee012336-->

- `test_tag_name_for_version_prefixes_once` (function) — Asserts tag_name_for_version adds the leading 'v' exactly once, whether or not the version string already has it. <!--#602585d1fddae7ae-->
- `test_should_tag_semver_bump` (function) — Parametrised check that should_tag_semver_bump returns the expected boolean for each bump type (including None). <!--#144814fbeccfaf4f-->

- `test_commit_subject_does_not_fold_a_wrapped_first_paragraph` (function) — Regression test that a wrapped subject paragraph yields only its first line, both from commit_subject and in the resulting annotated tag body. <!--#b3cd615c055fbfef-->
- `test_create_annotated_version_tag_uses_commit_subject` (function) — Checks create_annotated_version_tag produces a real annotated tag named 'v<version>', pointing at the target commit, whose message is the commit subject. <!--#76ad762e0c7387b1-->
- `test_existing_tag_raises_typed_error_with_tag_and_stderr` (function) — Asserts re-tagging an existing version raises VersionTagError carrying the tag name and git's 'already exists' stderr. <!--#e297582014bf6911-->
- `test_git_tag_failure_raises_typed_error_with_stderr` (function) — Monkeypatches subprocess.run to fail the `git tag` call and asserts VersionTagError surfaces the tag name and captured stderr. <!--#89c7bc4e9985b320-->
- `test_tag_failure_message_names_the_target_commit` (function) — Asserts a failed tag creation's error message names the tag, the target commit, the exit code, and git's stderr so manual recovery is possible. <!--#e93fb0e0e76f6c1f-->
- `test_semver_advance_requires_tag` (function) — Parametrised check that semver_advance_requires_tag decides correctly for each old/new version pair, including None values. <!--#51a45af6087c677c-->
- `test_semver_tag_decision` (function) — Parametrised check that semver_tag_decision returns True, False, or None for each old/new version pair. <!--#2ea8f76dd173a17d-->

### `tests/engine/test_implement_dispatch_edge_cases.py` (python) — Edge-case tests for implement_handler's execution-strategy dispatch, verifying (via patched _run_dag_parallel/LLMCaller, no real git) the branches that the happy-path sibling omits: linear-detector exceptions, empty-repo fallback, small-LOC single-call precedence, single-group ineligibility, and INFO skip-log emission. <!--#8e70e732df07b797|e8a19b7a11792edd-->

  - `TestLinearChainDetectionExceptionPath.test_linear_chain_detection_raises_falls_through_to_dag` (method) — Asserts a linear chain that normally short-circuits still invokes _run_dag_parallel once when transitive_reduce raises RuntimeError. <!--#bf132b18df6735e4-->
- `TestHasCommitsFalseFallsThroughToSequential` (class) — Test class verifying that an empty repo (has_commits=False) skips DAG and falls through to the sequential group-by-group path even when DAG was selected. <!--#c47354db1e08b9b6-->
  - `TestHasCommitsFalseFallsThroughToSequential.test_empty_repo_skips_dag_and_runs_sequential` (method) — Asserts that with fork groups, use_worktree=True, and has_commits=False, _run_dag_parallel is not called and LLMCaller is invoked once per group sequentially. <!--#77627faf655d2d07-->
- `TestSmallLocPathIgnoresUseWorktree` (class) — Test class verifying that the small-LOC single-call merge path wins before dispatch runs, so use_worktree=False does not change its behavior. <!--#c93ca0e0d5d4aac1-->
  - `TestSmallLocPathIgnoresUseWorktree.test_small_loc_with_use_worktree_false_still_single_call` (method) — Asserts that small total LOC with use_worktree=False invokes _run_single_llm_call once and never reaches _run_dag_parallel. <!--#844643dbc8c3f2c3-->
- `TestSingleGroupNotEligibleForDag` (class) — Test class verifying that single-group inputs bypass DAG parallel regardless of the use_worktree setting. <!--#5ab351c8374c60ab-->
  - `TestSingleGroupNotEligibleForDag.test_single_group_with_use_worktree_true_never_uses_dag` (method) — Asserts that a single group with use_worktree=True takes the single-call path (since len(groups) < 2) and never calls _run_dag_parallel. <!--#4f7516b2ec539ab7-->
- `TestDispatchLogMessages` (class) — Test class verifying that dispatch short-circuits emit visible INFO logs explaining why DAG parallel was skipped, captured via caplog. <!--#c03928eb07d49e72-->
  - `TestDispatchLogMessages.test_use_worktree_false_logs_skip_message` (method) — Asserts an INFO log mentioning 'use_worktree=False' and 'sequential' is emitted when worktrees are disabled. <!--#4c63cb587cbf9b6b-->
  - `TestDispatchLogMessages.test_linear_chain_logs_fallback_message` (method) — Asserts an INFO log mentioning 'linear chain' and 'sequential' is emitted when a linear group chain short-circuits DAG parallel. <!--#f20f53607b796e5a-->

### `tests/engine/test_implement_execution_strategy.py` (python) — Unit tests verifying that implement_handler dispatches to the correct execution path (sequential, DAG-parallel, or single LLM call) based on the implement.use_worktree flag, group topology (fork vs. linear), and total estimated LOC against the group_loc_threshold, using patched _run_dag_parallel/LLMCaller/_run_single_llm_call to assert which path fires. <!--#551f9007a1944547|17b212829a66cf7d-->

  - `TestExecutionStrategyDispatch.test_use_worktree_false_forces_sequential_even_on_dag_eligible_groups` (method) — Asserts that with use_worktree=False, a DAG-eligible fork group above the LOC threshold still runs sequentially (one LLMCaller per group, no DAG call). <!--#82ff1938d841625e-->
  - `TestExecutionStrategyDispatch.test_linear_chain_falls_back_to_sequential` (method) — Asserts that use_worktree=True with a linear group chain above the LOC threshold short-circuits to sequential execution rather than DAG parallel. <!--#eb82a5ee0fa03595-->
  - `TestExecutionStrategyDispatch.test_fork_dag_uses_dag_parallel` (method) — Asserts that use_worktree=True with a fork DAG above the LOC threshold dispatches to _run_dag_parallel exactly once. <!--#86d840f8b6e21973-->
  - `TestExecutionStrategyDispatch.test_small_multi_group_collapses_to_single_call` (method) — Asserts that use_worktree=True with total LOC below the threshold collapses multiple groups into a single LLM call (via _run_single_llm_call) rather than DAG or per-group sequential execution. <!--#647fbce8c13d4d0b-->

  - `TestSequentialReasonPropagation.test_small_loc_merge_no_sequential_reason` (method) — Asserts that a small multi-group plan merges via the 'single' path so no 'sequential' display call (and thus no sequential_reason) is emitted. <!--#65d8e5f77d6abf0b-->

### `tests/engine/test_knowledge_asset_language.py` (python) — Tests that `spec_language` alone (never the human `language` setting) governs language injection into knowledge-asset LLM prompts, verifying that both the charter-freshness propose prompt and the code-index summary prompt gain the respond-in-language directive, preserve-symbols clause, and knowledge-asset framing when it is set, carry zero injection when it is not, and that summaries still honour the single-line contract. <!--#5ac9073e5339f142|502f095fedb976bf-->
- `_isolated_global_home` (function) — An autouse-style fixture that redirects `Path.home()` to a fresh temp directory so the developer's real `~/.se3/config.yaml` language block can't leak into the zero-injection assertions. <!--#f3027ea20d636859-->
- `_write_project_language` (function) — Helper that writes a minimal `se3.yaml` under a project root containing a `language:` section with the given `language`/`spec_language` values (or nulls). <!--#bb4e5b18ebaaf304-->
- `_install_fake_caller` (function) — Helper that monkeypatches `charter_freshness.LLMCaller` with a stub returning a canned response and records every prompt it is called with. <!--#c2f81c724a0eb789-->
- `_make_flow` (function) — Helper that builds a minimal `FlowInstance` whose `change_path` points inside the temp project root, so the handler loads config from that root. <!--#397f11c215a7ea6a-->
- `_make_step` (function) — Helper that builds a CHARTER_FRESHNESS `Step` with a non-empty changed-files diff, which is what forces the propose LLM call instead of the cheap no-LLM path. <!--#2f1e3acf2ce07a17-->
- `_charter_prompt` (function) — Helper that runs the charter-freshness handler against a temp project with the given language settings and returns the captured propose prompt. <!--#4b70dcd4ec92b7e9-->
- `test_charter_prompt_injects_spec_language_when_set` (function) — Asserts that with `spec_language` set the charter prompt gains the respond-in-language directive, the preserve-symbols clause, and knowledge-asset framing, while spec-file/SHALL-MUST wording stays out. <!--#e9c40cc9c2f0afad-->
- `test_charter_prompt_zero_injection_when_spec_language_unset` (function) — Asserts that with no `spec_language` the charter prompt carries no language directive or preserve-symbols clause at all. <!--#6943c3bd342fe065-->
- `test_charter_prompt_ignores_human_language_when_spec_language_unset` (function) — Asserts that the unified human `language` setting alone never drives the charter prompt — only `spec_language` governs a knowledge asset. <!--#5a722ba161fbf5e3-->
- `_install_fake_summary_caller` (function) — Helper that stubs `LLMCaller` on `se3.engine.llm_caller` (where the summarizer's local import resolves it) to return a canned JSON summary map and capture each group's summary prompt. <!--#527c8baeca594d47-->
- `_make_summary_target` (function) — Helper that builds a single symbol-level `SummaryTarget` for a trivial `foo.py::foo` function. <!--#9e712a6aa4ecc5c1-->
- `_code_index_prompt` (function) — Helper that runs the code-index LLM summarizer against a temp project with the given language settings and returns the captured summary prompt. <!--#522b5d5043e8f163-->
- `test_code_index_prompt_injects_spec_language_when_set` (function) — Asserts that with `spec_language` set the code-index summary prompt gains the respond-in-language directive, preserve-symbols clause, and knowledge-asset framing, without spec-file/SHALL-MUST wording. <!--#472112c46c772389-->
- `test_code_index_prompt_zero_injection_when_spec_language_unset` (function) — Asserts that with no `spec_language` the code-index summary prompt contains no language injection. <!--#dbd165258578ceaf-->
- `test_code_index_prompt_ignores_human_language_when_spec_language_unset` (function) — Asserts that the human `language` setting alone never injects into the code-index summary prompt. <!--#4e3348ae559e2dad-->
- `test_code_index_summary_stays_single_line_with_injection` (function) — Asserts that language injection touches only the prompt, so returned summaries are still surfaced verbatim as single lines and the `_flatten_summary` markdown contract holds. <!--#d8476928571fb9e7-->

### `tests/engine/test_llm_caller.py` (python) — Unit tests for the LLM caller module's tool-preview formatters (truncate_preview, format_tool_use_preview, format_tool_result_preview) and stream/caller helpers, covering truncation rules, per-tool vs generic formatting, and value-type handling. <!--#c3c28f1d0eacd903|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `tests/engine/test_llm_caller_agents.py` (python) — Unit tests for LLMCaller's multi-agent management, covering agent-list initialization, runner factory/caching, per-attempt rotation on infra and generic errors, exhaustion, single-agent backward-compat, agent-name attribution in chat history, per-sequence rotation reset, tail-on-last, and two-phase JSON reset semantics. <!--#494c3cff16b4dfb2|8aa4c6408c74ee89-->
- `_make_success_result` (function) — Test helper building a mock MonitoredResult representing a successful agent run with the given output. <!--#255ed86d161fbea7-->
- `_make_fail_result` (function) — Test helper building a mock MonitoredResult representing a failed agent run with a given return code, output, and command. <!--#5af90c7b47c1402e-->
- `_setup_per_agent_runners` (function) — Test helper that pre-populates the caller's runner cache with one scripted MagicMock runner per agent and returns a shared call log recording which agent ran each attempt. <!--#949a6f291319a13d-->
- `_json_ok` (function) — Test helper producing a success result whose output is a valid JSON document. <!--#faa748979be7476b-->
- `TestAgentInitialization` (class) — Test class covering how LLMCaller initializes its agent list from an explicit parameter or from config. <!--#b754082ff7c01a1d-->
  - `TestAgentInitialization.test_explicit_agents_parameter` (method) — Asserts an explicitly passed agents list is used directly with the index starting at zero. <!--#a31ea64677d27078-->
  - `TestAgentInitialization.test_default_loads_from_config` (method) — Asserts that without an agents parameter, the caller loads at least one claude-code agent from config. <!--#10f71ae8083bc081-->
- `TestCreateRunner` (class) — Test class covering the runner factory method, unknown agent types, and runner caching. <!--#e116277bf0670099-->
  - `TestCreateRunner.test_creates_claude_code_runner` (method) — Asserts _create_runner produces a ClaudeCodeRunner configured with the agent's command. <!--#384cdc449a7fd310-->
  - `TestCreateRunner.test_unknown_type_raises` (method) — Asserts constructing an LLMCaller with an unknown agent type raises ValueError. <!--#c98c9fb3ec933d3c-->
  - `TestCreateRunner.test_runner_caching` (method) — Asserts repeated _get_current_runner calls return the same cached runner instance. <!--#67d1a7c9189aad31-->
- `TestRotateAgent` (class) — Test class covering the _rotate_agent index-advancing logic. <!--#67c9e57bdf1b7f9a-->
  - `TestRotateAgent.test_rotate_increments_index` (method) — Asserts rotation advances the current agent index and returns True. <!--#88d936fb86e4a085-->
  - `TestRotateAgent.test_rotate_exhausted_returns_false` (method) — Asserts rotation returns False and leaves the index unchanged when already at the last agent. <!--#b6ba2876a6c99b1a-->
  - `TestRotateAgent.test_single_agent_cannot_rotate` (method) — Asserts rotation returns False when only one agent is configured. <!--#0e954f725787b273-->
- `TestInfraErrorRotation` (class) — Test class verifying that infrastructure errors (usage limit, timeout) trigger rotation to the next agent. <!--#673d7c8962474406-->
  - `TestInfraErrorRotation.test_usage_limit_triggers_rotation` (method) — Asserts a usage-limit infra error rotates to the next agent, which then succeeds. <!--#bcbba194c8955dfc-->
  - `TestInfraErrorRotation.test_timeout_triggers_rotation` (method) — Asserts a timeout infra error rotates to the next agent, which then succeeds. <!--#3424ab3e064dff94-->
- `TestOtherErrorRotation` (class) — Test class verifying that unclassified (NONE) errors also trigger rotation to the next agent. <!--#d887319f31282535-->
  - `TestOtherErrorRotation.test_other_error_rotates_to_next_agent` (method) — Asserts a generic failure classified as NONE still rotates to the next agent. <!--#4f0d52a4ca561cd4-->
  - `TestOtherErrorRotation.test_unknown_certificate_error_triggers_rotation` (method) — Asserts an UNKNOWN_CERTIFICATE_VERIFICATION_ERROR (classified NONE) triggers rotation to the next agent. <!--#82411f85bbca8815-->
- `TestAllAgentsExhausted` (class) — Test class covering the behavior when every agent fails with infrastructure errors. <!--#422110013b255f3b-->
  - `TestAllAgentsExhausted.test_raises_after_exhaustion` (method) — Asserts LLMCallError is raised once all agents are exhausted by infra errors. <!--#2a02b3e9aca4c489-->
- `TestSingleAgentScenario` (class) — Test class covering single-agent (backward-compat) behavior where rotation is impossible and errors fall through to same-agent retries. <!--#6d6bc8f267a5a7a3-->
  - `TestSingleAgentScenario.test_single_agent_success` (method) — Asserts a single agent returning success yields the expected output. <!--#8d052fb7fd35a93b-->
  - `TestSingleAgentScenario.test_single_agent_infra_error_no_rotation` (method) — Asserts a single agent's infra error cannot rotate and falls through to a same-agent retry that succeeds. <!--#32bb1a8428ff9b15-->
  - `TestSingleAgentScenario.test_single_agent_other_error_falls_through` (method) — Asserts a single agent's unclassified error falls through to a same-agent retry that succeeds. <!--#53279fe800e716c8-->
- `TestAgentAttributionInHistory` (class) — Test class verifying that the current agent's name is recorded in chat history for prompts and responses across rotations and retries. <!--#3aae8c4f9f8a817e-->
  - `TestAgentAttributionInHistory.test_record_prompt_gets_agent_name` (method) — Asserts _record_prompt stores the supplied agent name on the recorded message. <!--#d2b8cf1c1b152a58-->
  - `TestAgentAttributionInHistory.test_record_response_gets_agent_name` (method) — Asserts _record_response stores the supplied agent name on the recorded message. <!--#e7b128b7c9c8732f-->
  - `TestAgentAttributionInHistory.test_rotation_records_different_agent_names` (method) — Asserts that after rotation, subsequent recorded messages carry the new agent's name while earlier ones keep the original. <!--#7e47ed8f6f1dbc34-->
  - `TestAgentAttributionInHistory.test_record_failure_does_not_block_call` (method) — Asserts that a failure while recording history does not raise and the call proceeds. <!--#0b6dca932af2399b-->
  - `TestAgentAttributionInHistory.test_call_with_retry_passes_agent_name` (method) — Asserts the full call path snapshots and records the current agent's name on both prompt and response messages. <!--#0c7bf5493e6bb4ba-->
- `TestPerSequenceAgentReset` (class) — Regression test class ensuring each new internal retry sequence restarts rotation from the preferred agent rather than staying pinned to the last one. <!--#92a26445d95f193b-->
  - `TestPerSequenceAgentReset.test_index_starts_at_zero_each_call_when_reused` (method) — Asserts a reused caller resets to the preferred agent on a second call after the first rotated to the last agent. <!--#bf666587a79268a9-->
  - `TestPerSequenceAgentReset.test_reset_refreshes_legacy_runner` (method) — Asserts the entry reset also refreshes the legacy self._runner back to the preferred agent's runner. <!--#5487502383c4654e-->
- `TestTailOnLastWithinSequence` (class) — Test class verifying that when max_retries exceeds the agent count, rotation tails on the last agent (no wrap) before failing. <!--#2cfda631cff66a46-->
  - `TestTailOnLastWithinSequence.test_tail_on_last_then_raises` (method) — Asserts rotation goes a→b→c then repeats on c for surplus attempts and finally raises LLMCallError after the retry cap. <!--#84585ea6d0f302c0-->
- `TestTwoPhasePerPhaseReset` (class) — Test class verifying that in two_phase JSON mode each Phase-1 sequence resets rotation independently and Phase 2 runs verbatim. <!--#0cea97fa439ec081-->
  - `TestTwoPhasePerPhaseReset.test_phase1_resets_each_call` (method) — Asserts each separate two_phase call's Phase 1 starts rotation over from the preferred agent. <!--#29cc1a0e805d6fd0-->
  - `TestTwoPhasePerPhaseReset.test_phase2_starts_from_first_agent` (method) — Asserts that when Phase 1's non-JSON output forces production Phase 2, the extraction sequence resets back to the preferred agent. <!--#130c1bb74a65aade-->
  - `TestTwoPhasePerPhaseReset.test_phase2_runs_extraction_prompt_verbatim_on_step_retry` (method) — Regression test asserting Phase 2's extraction prompt runs verbatim (no continue-mode retry-context injection) even when the step is retried at the state-machine level. <!--#33b6fb31320094d6-->
- `TestJsonContinuationNoReset` (class) — Test class verifying the JSON-continuation recursion stays on the current agent rather than resetting to the preferred one. <!--#e64bef40f9c74fcc-->
  - `TestJsonContinuationNoReset.test_json_retry_keeps_current_agent` (method) — Asserts a non-JSON response triggers a continuation that remains on the same rotated-to agent until it returns valid JSON. <!--#6259ff49e2bd6612-->

### `tests/engine/test_llm_caller_rotation_error.py` (python) — Pytest module that drives LLMCaller with stub always-failing agent runners to verify the LLMCallError raised after retry exhaustion names every attempted agent with its exit code, command, and infra-error label — including rotating attempts, so the message never degrades to a bare 'failed after N attempts'. <!--#591b530e26ce9de0|b6f4e5c1265b9bd6-->
- `_FailingRunner` (class) — Stub AgentRunner used by these tests that always returns a failing result with a fixed exit code and command name, and never reports an infra error. <!--#030161f6b5049c48-->
  - `_FailingRunner.__init__` (method) — Stores the fixed exit code and command string the stub runner will always report. <!--#abba69c15a5887a3-->
  - `_FailingRunner.build_call_args` (method) — Returns a trivial argument list containing just the stub's command name. <!--#bbb319965eb0c43c-->
  - `_FailingRunner.run_with_monitor` (method) — Returns a canned failing _Result carrying the stub's exit code and command. <!--#c77b82924603bf0a-->
  - `_FailingRunner.detect_infra_error` (method) — Always classifies the failure as InfraErrorType.NONE so rotation, not infra handling, drives the test. <!--#ce73a329c5bde7f2-->
- `_Result` (class) — Minimal stand-in for an agent run result, fixed to the failure shape (success False, empty output) with the given exit code and command. <!--#2a5474d4c2e20b6b-->
  - `_Result.__init__` (method) — Initialises the stub result fields to a non-interrupted failure with the supplied returncode and cmd_used. <!--#39159297a3b0fcaf-->
- `make_caller` (function) — Pytest fixture that clears SE3_TEST_RUNNING, patches LLMCaller to hand out the stub runners per agent, and returns a factory building an LLMCaller with a chosen max_retries. <!--#6c92ef0245b1e405-->
- `test_error_names_every_agent_and_exit_code` (function) — Asserts that after exhausting three attempts the raised LLMCallError message names every agent along with its exit code and command, including the rotating attempts that used to be dropped. <!--#a721dae72cc2872d-->
- `test_all_attempts_rotating_still_yields_a_reason` (function) — Asserts that when every attempt ends in a rotation the error message still carries a non-empty reason listing the two agents actually tried, rather than a bare 'failed after N attempts:'. <!--#91dcb0cb175f2331-->
- `test_infra_error_label_is_reported` (function) — Asserts the raised LLMCallError message includes the infra_error label for the failure. <!--#659fbf9e0e7a31e7-->

### `tests/engine/test_llm_caller_step_override.py` (python) — Unit tests for LLMCaller's per-step agent override wiring, verifying that a declared `llm_caller.steps.<step>` override is used verbatim (no default fallback appended), that unoverridden steps fall back to the default agent chain, that exhausting an override chain raises LLMCallError instead of rotating into the default, and that an explicit `agents=` argument takes precedence over both. <!--#eead91a38b92b777|101a184685881979-->
- `_make_fail_result` (function) — Helper building a MagicMock LLM result representing a failed (unsuccessful) agent call, e.g. a usage-limit infra error. <!--#443242c628427894-->
- `_make_success_result` (function) — Helper building a MagicMock LLM result representing a successful agent call. <!--#7cc32192812158d1-->
- `_write_override` (function) — Helper that writes an se3.yaml fixture containing an agents registry plus a per-step override list under `llm_caller.steps.<step>`. <!--#b31feebd82852d49-->
- `TestStepOverrideChain` (class) — Test class verifying LLMCaller's per-step agent-chain override: a step with a declared override uses exactly those agents (no default fallback appended), while a step without one falls back to the built-in default chain. <!--#a40b22ba85a47247-->
  - `TestStepOverrideChain.test_override_used_when_declared` (method) — Asserts a step with an override uses exactly its two override agents with no default 'claude' appended as a fallback tail. <!--#a24a33cbab004d06-->
  - `TestStepOverrideChain.test_other_step_falls_back_to_default_chain` (method) — Asserts that a step with no override declared (here 'plan') resolves to the built-in default chain, with shutil.which patched to only find 'claude' so the result doesn't depend on host-installed agents. <!--#d31b7541ac049de1-->
- `TestExhaustionDoesNotFallBack` (class) — Test class verifying that exhausting an override chain raises rather than rotating into the default chain. <!--#61e4e2809c87dd96-->
  - `TestExhaustionDoesNotFallBack.test_override_exhaustion_raises_without_falling_back` (method) — Asserts that when a single-agent override hits an infra error, the call raises LLMCallError and the agent index stays within the override list instead of falling through to default 'claude'. <!--#3f529f640827f037-->
- `TestExplicitAgentsArgHighestPriority` (class) — Test class verifying that an explicit `agents=` argument takes precedence over both the per-step override and the default chain. <!--#cb0db805cec35ce0-->
  - `TestExplicitAgentsArgHighestPriority.test_explicit_agents_bypasses_override_and_default` (method) — Asserts that passing `agents=` makes the caller use that exact list (identity-equal), bypassing both the override and default chains. <!--#f79f0dbed750fa9f-->

### `tests/engine/test_merge_deterministic_resolvers.py` (python) — Unit tests for the deterministic merge resolvers, covering code-index markdown parse/render round-tripping, per-entry conflict picking against worktree fingerprints, `CodeIndexResolver` and `NextIdResolver` behaviour, and the `resolve_deterministic` staging/degrade-to-LLM path. <!--#664a98ffd4a72398|116abcc31d9c15aa-->
- `_fp_comment` (function) — Test helper that formats the `<!--#content_fp|list_fp-->` fingerprint comment appended to code-index headings. <!--#7ee31e36e855dc69-->
- `_md` (function) — Test helper that assembles a minimal but format-faithful code-index markdown document from a list of pre-rendered entries. <!--#beaf0dbadf66834b-->
- `_entry` (function) — Test helper that renders a single `### relpath (python) — summary <!--#fp-->` code-index file entry plus its symbol bullets. <!--#0d20e841771ca74f-->
- `_block` (function) — Test helper that builds a `FileBlock` for `x.py` with the given fingerprints, summary, and bullets, for driving `_pick` directly. <!--#1f76830d200c5ff3-->
- `test_parse_extracts_fingerprints_and_bullets` (function) — Asserts `_parse_md_blocks` recovers dir headings, content/list fingerprints, summary, and bullet lines from code-index markdown. <!--#771d9e501025dacf-->
- `test_render_is_deterministic_and_marker_free` (function) — Asserts `_render` is idempotent, emits no conflict markers, and orders entries by sorted relpath regardless of input order. <!--#bc30a09839dfaf40-->
- `test_roundtrip_on_repository_index_is_byte_identical` (function) — Guards the parser/renderer against format drift by round-tripping the repository's real `se3/code-index.md` byte-for-byte (skipped if absent). <!--#00987da41258cbcb-->
- `test_pick_keeps_the_only_side_that_has_the_entry` (function) — Asserts `_pick` returns the single present side with reason `only-ours`/`only-theirs` when the other side lacks the entry. <!--#0725c1321695d669-->
- `test_pick_takes_theirs_when_both_sides_are_identical` (function) — Asserts `_pick` reports `identical` and returns theirs when both sides' blocks agree entirely. <!--#8037077e91607b1e-->
- `test_pick_takes_the_side_whose_fingerprint_matches_the_worktree` (function) — Asserts `_pick` resolves a fingerprint disagreement in favour of whichever side matches the post-merge working-tree file. <!--#c7686f3f3bf0cb1d-->
- `test_pick_falls_back_to_theirs_when_neither_side_matches_the_worktree` (function) — Asserts `_pick` deterministically falls back to theirs (reason `neither-matches-worktree`) when the worktree fingerprint matches neither side or is unknown. <!--#dc2f8fbb28e63c24-->
- `test_pick_keeps_theirs_symbols_whole_when_neither_side_matches_the_worktree` (function) — Asserts that when both sides are stale, theirs' bullet list is taken whole rather than merged with ours, keeping the result a pure function of its inputs. <!--#718d18ced6e3e996-->
- `test_pick_takes_the_matching_sides_symbols_whole` (function) — Asserts the worktree-matching side's bullet list is used verbatim, so stale symbols from the losing side are never grafted in. <!--#b900370483417f33-->
- `test_pick_takes_theirs_when_fingerprints_agree_but_summaries_differ` (function) — Asserts a pure wording disagreement over identical content is settled on theirs with reason `same-fp-different-summary`. <!--#2a878a2748bec267-->
- `_stage_stub` (function) — Test helper returning a fake `_git_show_stage` that serves canned ours/theirs blob text per merge stage. <!--#63090386bd661070-->
- `test_resolve_unions_entries_and_drops_those_whose_file_vanished` (function) — Asserts `CodeIndexResolver.resolve` unions both sides' entries, drops entries whose working-tree file is gone, settles disagreements by worktree fingerprint, and emits no conflict markers. <!--#4d754309ce0627ef-->
- `test_resolve_is_deterministic` (function) — Asserts repeated `CodeIndexResolver.resolve` calls on the same inputs produce identical output, falling back to theirs when neither side matches. <!--#a569c4db4e130ee5-->
- `test_resolve_survives_a_missing_side` (function) — Asserts `CodeIndexResolver.resolve` still produces an index when one merge stage has no blob (add/delete-shaped conflict). <!--#0fdb71af0837b465-->
- `test_resolve_raises_when_both_sides_are_missing` (function) — Asserts `CodeIndexResolver.resolve` raises `ValueError` rather than inventing content when neither stage supplies an index. <!--#8ef657d729123add-->
- `test_code_index_resolver_matches_only_its_own_path` (function) — Asserts `CodeIndexResolver.matches` is an exact-path check on `se3/code-index.md` and rejects lookalike paths. <!--#a9514b7124c456f7-->
- `test_next_id_resolver_takes_the_maximum` (function) — Parameterised test that `NextIdResolver` resolves the issue-counter conflict to the larger of the two sides' values. <!--#03713a5a30abbc3d-->
- `test_next_id_resolver_raises_when_no_side_is_usable` (function) — Parameterised test that `NextIdResolver` raises rather than staging a counter value that came from neither side, which would reissue allocated IDs. <!--#d3743988b8b96b6c-->
- `test_next_id_resolver_propagates_git_failure` (function) — Asserts a `git show` failure propagates out of `NextIdResolver` instead of masquerading as an absent side and silently dropping the larger counter. <!--#434b6a353fd8763c-->
- `test_resolve_deterministic_falls_back_when_git_show_fails` (function) — Asserts `resolve_deterministic` records the git error as a failure and leaves the path in `remaining` for the LLM. <!--#f48802ddbc8f1551-->
- `test_registry_holds_two_resolvers_with_disjoint_matches` (function) — Asserts the resolver `REGISTRY` has exactly two entries and that each deterministic path is claimed by exactly one of them. <!--#92ae1adffb669111-->
- `_StubResolver` (class) — Minimal fake resolver that matches one relpath and either returns canned text or raises, used to drive `resolve_deterministic` in isolation. <!--#dcc73293dbc03077-->
  - `_StubResolver.__init__` (method) — Stores the relpath this stub claims and the text (or exception) its `resolve` will produce. <!--#f0ca9a1d39c0d394-->
  - `_StubResolver.matches` (method) — Returns True only for the exact relpath the stub was constructed with. <!--#e1066e19fa5c3c3b-->
  - `_StubResolver.resolve` (method) — Returns the canned output, or raises it if the stub was configured with an exception. <!--#a19580e98867f3d9-->
- `git_calls` (function) — Pytest fixture that patches `_git_add`/`_git_rm` to record staging calls instead of touching git. <!--#ddd9ea21e1443ccb-->
- `test_unmatched_paths_are_left_for_the_llm` (function) — Asserts paths no resolver claims pass through untouched into `remaining` with no git staging. <!--#557a3506f953909d-->
- `test_resolved_path_is_written_and_staged` (function) — Asserts a resolved path has its resolver output written to the working tree and `git add`-ed, while unclaimed paths remain. <!--#ec1d989cd827714e-->
- `test_empty_output_deletes_the_path` (function) — Asserts an empty resolver result means "deleted by the merge" and triggers `git rm` for the path. <!--#00b2bf204b5e06a9-->
- `test_a_raising_resolver_degrades_to_the_llm_without_staging` (function) — Asserts a resolver exception is captured in `failures`, the path degrades to `remaining`, and the conflicted file is left untouched and unstaged. <!--#2460bfb8ea750a52-->
- `test_output_with_conflict_markers_is_never_staged` (function) — Asserts resolver output still containing conflict markers is rejected, recorded as a failure, and never written or staged. <!--#ee868e6f11a0aafa-->
- `test_a_failed_stage_restores_the_conflicted_working_tree` (function) — Asserts a `git add` failure rolls the working-tree file back to its original conflicted content so the LLM inherits the real conflict. <!--#1b6b4972be671175-->
- `test_a_failed_stage_removes_the_file_the_conflict_never_had` (function) — Asserts that when a staging failure follows a conflict with no working-tree copy, the written file is removed rather than left looking already-resolved. <!--#4cbaed83acb42603-->
- `test_resolved_and_remaining_partition_the_input_in_order` (function) — Asserts `resolve_deterministic`'s `resolved` and `remaining` lists exactly partition the input paths while preserving input order. <!--#25d11e1c0a884b25-->
- `_git` (function) — Test helper that runs a `git -C repo …` command and returns its stdout, raising on failure. <!--#4bcee364727a85d9-->
- `_real_fp` (function) — Test helper that computes the true content fingerprint `code_index` would record for a given file text, using the production hashing functions. <!--#d0e4fc19536e4326-->
- `_index_md` (function) — Test helper that renders a full code-index markdown document from `(relpath, summary, content_fp)` triples for the integration fixture. <!--#ec7c9663b6a998b4-->
- `_write` (function) — Test helper that writes text to a repo-relative path, creating parent directories as needed. <!--#f70dcb0dc6f581d0-->
- `conflicted_repo` (function) — Pytest fixture building a real git repo mid-merge in which both `se3/code-index.md` and `se3/issues/.next_id` are genuinely conflicted, reproducing the regenerate-the-whole-index failure shape. <!--#e2bd6ebd0eff666e-->
- `no_llm` (function) — Pytest fixture that patches `LLMCaller.call` to raise, turning any LLM invocation during the test into a failure. <!--#70b3006ee66fbcd0-->
- `test_real_merge_conflict_is_resolved_without_the_llm` (function) — End-to-end test that `resolve_deterministic` clears both deterministic conflicts in a real conflicted repo with no LLM call and nothing left unmerged in git's index. <!--#3756845fb0b0c6ed-->
- `test_resolved_index_unions_entries_and_drops_the_deleted_file` (function) — End-to-end test that the resolved index keeps both sides' new entries, drops the deleted file's entry, prefers the worktree-matching side for edited files, and settles pure wording ties on theirs. <!--#f470b57ff898910c-->
- `test_staged_index_matches_the_working_tree` (function) — Asserts the blob staged in git's index is byte-identical to the resolved `se3/code-index.md` on disk. <!--#416bc920ba6746a0-->
- `test_next_id_takes_the_larger_counter` (function) — End-to-end test that the conflicted `.next_id` counter resolves to the larger of the two branches' values. <!--#f54a27a7e22a3ef6-->
- `test_the_merge_commits_cleanly_after_deterministic_resolution` (function) — Asserts a real two-parent merge commit can be created after deterministic resolution, with both sides' files present and the deleted one gone. <!--#e8671074ff28fa26-->
- `orchestrator_repo` (function) — Pytest fixture wrapping `conflicted_repo` with the LLM, guardrails, and conflict-context builder disarmed so the orchestrator's deterministic short-circuit can be observed. <!--#068e22618daa440e-->
- `_handle_conflict` (function) — Test helper that constructs a `MergeOrchestrator` for the repo and invokes its private `_handle_conflict` against the `feature` branch. <!--#5b1b980127c5b8c8-->
- `test_a_fully_deterministic_conflict_merges_without_the_llm` (function) — Parameterised test that, across strategies (including strict), an all-deterministic conflict short-circuits to a clean two-parent merge commit with no LLM call and no human hand-off. <!--#4c9afab630ef10af-->
- `test_a_leftover_conflict_still_reaches_the_context_builder` (function) — Asserts a single non-deterministic leftover path keeps the LLM path alive and is passed alone as `conflict_files` to the context builder. <!--#0eb257c6b280b1b2-->
- `test_a_broken_deterministic_pass_degrades_to_the_pre_change_behaviour` (function) — Parameterised test that a crash anywhere in the deterministic pass yields `None` and hands `conflict_files=None` to the context builder, leaving the pre-existing LLM path exactly as it was. <!--#7951941a89b469d5-->

### `tests/engine/test_prompt_dedup.py` (python) — Unit test suite for se3.engine.prompt_dedup.deduplicate_prompt_lines(), exhaustively verifying that repeated multi-line blocks in a prompt are collapsed to their first occurrence plus a content-hash marker across edge cases (empty/short input, custom min_block_lines, triple/adjacent/overlapping repeats, pre-existing markers, blank-line handling, and large-prompt performance). <!--#0f5b0eb847d4bc63|a7c86424c88e4fd0-->
- `_expected_marker` (function) — Test helper that computes the expected '[DUPLICATED CONTENT: ...]' marker string (with sha256 hash and truncated first/last lines) for a given block of lines. <!--#0d52f5093d78b812-->
- `TestDeduplicatePromptLines` (class) — Test class grouping all unit tests for the deduplicate_prompt_lines() function. <!--#0eb57bae48ebc839-->

### `tests/engine/test_prompt_markers.py` (python) — Unit tests for the engine's prompt_markers helpers (wrap_user_content, wrap_user_section, inject_boundary, _marker_pair_present), verifying correct marker insertion/ordering, empty-input passthrough, idempotency against pre-existing markers, and that every engine step prompt carries exactly one properly-positioned template-end/user-content boundary separating the system role opener from the user/task content. <!--#9702b20ccdc6680a|20c4806bb0f244db-->
- `test_wrap_user_content_injects_marker_pair` (function) — Asserts wrap_user_content inserts both the template-end and user-content-begin markers in the right order while preserving the original header and task text. <!--#6aa7c18d1165d4e3-->
- `test_wrap_user_content_empty_user_passthrough` (function) — Verifies wrap_user_content returns the system text unchanged when the user content is empty. <!--#15c4e8d227ddfdd6-->
- `test_wrap_user_content_empty_prefix_passthrough` (function) — Verifies wrap_user_content returns the user text unchanged when the prefix is empty. <!--#a0fe7cc86c36cb74-->
- `test_wrap_user_content_idempotent_on_marker_in_prefix` (function) — Checks that re-wrapping already-marked text just appends the new content rather than injecting a second marker pair. <!--#2238ab85bb237da6-->
- `test_wrap_user_section_three_segment_order` (function) — Asserts wrap_user_section emits all three markers exactly once in the strict prefix→template-end→user-begin→user→user-end→suffix order. <!--#4484359185b10ae8-->
- `test_wrap_user_section_idempotent_on_already_wrapped` (function) — Confirms passing an already-wrapped string as the prefix concatenates inputs without injecting a second marker triple. <!--#72de1c722781e98d-->
- `test_wrap_user_section_idempotent_when_markers_in_user_content` (function) — Confirms wrap_user_section does not double-wrap when its user-content argument already contains a marker triple. <!--#84afc7317029f109-->
- `test_wrap_user_section_empty_prefix_and_suffix` (function) — Verifies wrap_user_section still emits the full three-marker record (no stray prefix/suffix) when prefix and suffix are empty. <!--#a929043e404bd6fb-->
- `test_wrap_user_section_empty_user_content_still_wraps` (function) — Verifies an empty middle segment is still wrapped with begin/end markers so the frontend distinguishes an empty bubble from no marker at all. <!--#1b950b27367105f3-->
- `test_marker_pair_present_helper` (function) — Tests _marker_pair_present returns true only for full three-segment text, rejecting empty, marker-less, and legacy two-segment strings. <!--#8d7d5c37165f0a92-->
- `test_wrap_user_section_does_not_affect_legacy_helpers` (function) — Ensures the legacy two-segment helpers (wrap_user_content, inject_boundary) still emit their two markers and never emit USER_CONTENT_END. <!--#9dc17855618a704b-->
- `test_inject_boundary_inserts_before_anchor` (function) — Asserts inject_boundary places the boundary markers immediately before the named anchor heading in the template. <!--#c42f29851b33a6a1-->
- `test_inject_boundary_missing_anchor_is_noop` (function) — Verifies inject_boundary leaves the template unchanged when the anchor text is absent. <!--#96e759f52dfef0e1-->
- `test_inject_boundary_idempotent` (function) — Checks that applying inject_boundary twice with the same anchor yields the same result as applying it once. <!--#38ea4851c588b911-->
- `test_all_step_prompts_have_exactly_one_marker_pair` (function) — Asserts every engine step prompt contains exactly one template-end and one user-content-begin marker in the correct order. <!--#84960131bcc258df-->
- `test_role_opener_is_in_prefix_segment` (function) — Asserts each step prompt's boilerplate role opener ("You are…") sits before the template-end marker so it collapses into the system-prompt chip. <!--#a3aa5e9e5c071832-->
- `test_user_content_anchor_is_in_suffix_segment` (function) — Asserts each step prompt's user/task-content anchor sits after the user-content-begin marker so it renders as an expanded user bubble. <!--#6eac6fa1141dcd64-->

### `tests/engine/test_retry_context_injection.py` (python) — Test module covering retry-context injection paths: that implement (and other) step handlers forward retry_count as external_attempt to LLMCaller, that _get_retry_context logs at WARNING on failure, that format_history_for_retry and extract_conversation_from_ndjson degrade gracefully on malformed NDJSON, that history is filtered by fix_iteration (with 0 as wildcard), and that the record APIs and ChatMessage persist/default the fix_iteration field for backward compatibility. <!--#a113ef4c3c9f7e0c|ee7bd1f525282080-->

  - `TestImplementPassesRetryCount.test_implement_passes_retry_count` (method) — Asserts that a retrying implement step passes its retry_count (2) as external_attempt to LLMCaller. <!--#53c05000adac928c-->
  - `TestImplementPassesRetryCount.test_implement_defaults_retry_count_to_zero` (method) — Asserts external_attempt defaults to 0 when no retry_count is present in step inputs. <!--#232868ae141c9b74-->

- `TestFormatHistoryMalformedNDJSON` (class) — Test class verifying format_history_for_retry degrades gracefully on malformed or partially valid raw_json content. <!--#5c9ff52d1be17030-->
  - `TestFormatHistoryMalformedNDJSON.test_malformed_raw_json_falls_back_to_content` (method) — Asserts that fully malformed raw_json falls back to the message's plain content without crashing. <!--#cd0acaf94c82409f-->
  - `TestFormatHistoryMalformedNDJSON.test_partial_valid_ndjson_returns_partial_context` (method) — Asserts that a mix of valid and malformed raw_json entries still yields the valid entries' text. <!--#5ac6398f2bf6c01c-->
  - `TestFormatHistoryMalformedNDJSON.test_completely_broken_raw_json_falls_back` (method) — Asserts that broken raw_json structure causes a graceful fallback to message content rather than an exception. <!--#124a6e28fffab860-->

  - `TestExtractConversationFromNDJSONResilience.test_handles_items_missing_type` (method) — Asserts dict items lacking a 'type' key are skipped while typed entries are parsed. <!--#33a6fac6748671b8-->
  - `TestExtractConversationFromNDJSONResilience.test_handles_malformed_string_lines` (method) — Asserts malformed/incomplete JSON lines in string input are skipped, keeping valid parsed messages. <!--#64d022247508743d-->
- `TestFormatHistoryFixIterationBoundary` (class) — Test class verifying format_history_for_retry filters messages by current_fix_iteration, with fix_iteration=0 acting as a backward-compat wildcard. <!--#5605a0530e591dbf-->
